According to the statement, Akogun, who is popularly known on Facebook as “Prophet Dr Muyiwa Akogun”, alerted the police after members of the public began reporting fraudulent activities allegedly being carried out in his name. Following the complaint, the Divisional Police Officer in charge of Ilaro Division deployed intelligence and detective operatives to identify and apprehend the alleged impersonator. The command said sustained technological monitoring and intelligence-led analysis led detectives to a village in Ajegunle, along the Ilaro-Ibogun axis, where the suspect was arrested. The police said the suspect allegedly confessed during interrogation to impersonating Akogun on Facebook. The command quoted him as admitting to using the cleric’s identity to “deliver fake prophecies and offer prayer services to vulnerable individuals”, through which victims in Nigeria and the diaspora were allegedly defrauded. The police said preliminary investigation indicated that the suspect allegedly targeted people seeking spiritual assistance through the real prophet’s Facebook platform, gained their confidence and collected money from them. The command put the alleged proceeds of the scheme at more than ₦18 million. The suspect has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department, SCID, Eleweran, Abeokuta, for further investigation. The police said the investigation would determine the full extent of the alleged offences, identify any possible accomplices and establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged transactions before possible prosecution. The Commissioner of Police, Ogun State Command, Bode Ojajuni, commended the Ilaro operatives for their vigilance, tactical discipline and swift response. Ojajuni, according to the statement, reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting residents from cyber-enabled and conventional criminal activities. The police also advised members of the public to exercise caution when interacting with religious leaders, celebrities and other public figures on social media. The command urged residents to verify the authenticity of social media accounts before engaging in financial transactions, particularly where money is requested in exchange for spiritual remedies, prayers or other purported services. The post Police arrest prophet’s son over alleged ₦18m Facebook fraud appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Auchan and Decathlon resume operations at Lavina mall in Kyiv
body:
Auchan Bilichi supermarket and Decathlon sporting goods store have resumed operations at Lavina shopping and entertainment center in Kyiv following the Russian attack on Sept. 26, the retailers said on social media.

According to a Decathlon post on Facebook, the store is currently accessible only from the outside parking lot.

The retailer also reminded customers that the store closes during air alerts.

As reported, Lavina shopping and entertainment center was hit in a Russian attack in late September.

title: Mo Abudu Unveils Cultural Centre, Cinema Dedicated To African Film In London
body: Nigerian producer and media mogul Mo Abudu has realised a “mad dream” by opening a unique cultural centre in London complete with a cinema dedicated to African film and black culture. Close to the Houses of Parliament and its Big Ben clock, a massive concrete facade conceals the venue, which opens to the public this weekend – the first of its kind in Britain and Europe. A small sign reads “EbonyLife Place London”. While the name may mean little to many passers-by, film lovers will recognise the reference to EbonyLife, a leading African production company and a major player in Nollywood, Nigeria’s film industry. Mosunmola “Mo” Abudu, 62, heads a media empire that stretches far beyond Nigeria’s borders. In 2025, Forbes ranked her among the world’s 100 most influential women. “It’s time to tell our own stories,” she told AFP. “I want to showcase the best of who we are, celebrate who we are. Let them see us at our very best.” Abudu, who was born in London, is pursuing that ambition in the British capital through the cultural centre, which she describes as both “literally a blank canvas” and “a bit of a mad dream”. “We have to make the journey because the thing is that we have consumed so much of the world. How much of the world has consumed us?” she asked. She recalled that growing up in England: “I could never go anywhere during my youth and watch a black movie.” So she decided to act. “I’m not waiting anymore for anyone to take a six-hour trip from London to understand what it is to watch a Nigerian film or to see Nigerian fashion and so on. It’s right here in London.” ‘Open to everyone’ The two-storey venue includes a bar, a lounge called “Fẹhinti” — a Yoruba word meaning to lean back and rest — a restaurant and a boutique showcasing designers from Africa and its diaspora. Paintings by artists from across the continent line the walls. Its centrepiece, however, is the new cinema, fitted with red seats, wood panelling and soft lighting. It has been named “Amani”, meaning peace and harmony in Swahili. The project, financed almost entirely by Abudu’s media group, mirrors the upscale lifestyle complex she launched in Lagos in 2019. Abudu, who is widely credited with helping usher in the era of Nollywood blockbusters, said African creatives should stop asking others to make room for them and instead “take responsibility for creating our own spaces”. Describing the centre as a “safe space”, she said it would be a place where “you can shop our fashion, you can view our art, you can listen to our music, and we can tell our stories”. Nigerian film director and media mogul Mo Abudu poses for a portrait for AFP in London on October 1, 2026, ahead of the opening the UK’s first cinema dedicated exclusively to African and Black films. Photo by JUSTIN TALLIS / AFP Access will be through a membership scheme, details of which have yet to be announced. Such systems are common in Britain, particularly among cultural institutions. There will be no ethnic or nationality restrictions. “Membership is open to everyone,” she insisted. The cinema’s programme is still being finalised. But the objective is clear here. “We will have films from all parts of Africa. Everything should be on the table. We would show movies that celebrate black actors, black storytelling; that is why we are here,” Abudu said. Will audiences be able to see films by Senegalese director Ousmane Sembene or by Algerian filmmaker Mohammed Lakhdar-Hamina, the only African director ever to win the Cannes Palme d’Or? Her answer was an emphatic “yes”. The centre will also showcase its own productions and films with black actors, including the next in the “Black Panther” series. Opening week will feature Nigerian filmmakers including Nwani Orire and Ifeyinwa Arinze. And after London? “I would love to do the same thing in Paris, perhaps through a partnership. I’m always open to collaborating with others,” Abudu said. AFP The post Mo Abudu Unveils Cultural Centre, Cinema Dedicated To African Film In London appeared first on Channels Television .

title: LNG exports from Middle East plummet 47% YOY in H1 2026, WTO says
body:
GENEVA, October 8. /TASS/. Liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports from the Middle East fell by about 47% annually during the first six months of 2026, while oil deliveries from the region dropped by about 24%, the World Trade Organization (WTO) said in its global trade prospects report.
"It is estimated that exports of liquefied natural gas from the Middle East fell around 47% in the first half of this year, even though global shipments of LNG only declined minimally, by around -1%," WTO said. Consequences of the energy shock related to the shortfall in supplies from the Middle East was managed to be softened and partly compensated by growing production and deliveries of other exporters, including Malaysia, Norway, and Angola, the organization noted.
According to the report, crude oil exports from the Middle East fell about 24% annually in the first half of this year. "During the same period, other suppliers (including the United States, Norway and Brazil) increased their production and shipments of crude oil, resulting in a global decline in exports of these products of around 6%," WTO added.

title: Russia attacks warehouses in Bucha district: three injured reported – regional administration
body:
Three people were injured in a Russian attack on warehouses in Bucha district of Kyiv region, said Tymur Tkachenko, head of Kyiv Regional Military Administration.

"The enemy attacked warehouses in Bucha district. Three people were injured as a result of the enemy attack," Tkachenko wrote on his Telegram channel on Thursday.

According to him, one person was hospitalized, while the other two received medical assistance at the scene. "Firefighting operations are ongoing. All necessary emergency services have been deployed to deal with the aftermath of the enemy strike," Tkachenko noted.

title: Rubio warns Ukraine conflict could escalate into more dangerous regional war
body:
MADRID, October 8. /TASS/. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned that the fighting in Ukraine could escalate into a "far more dangerous" regional conflict.
"This is a very dangerous war. It's an extremely dangerous war because, frankly, right now it seems to be at a stalemate, and stalemates are very dangerous because stalemates only end one of two ways," he said at a news conference during his visit to Lisbon.
"Number one, you have a negotiated settlement, one in which each side has to give up something in order to get peace <...>. The other way that stalemates end is through escalation. One side or the other, or both, escalate what they are doing in order to try to break the other side and break the stalemate, and that's very dangerous," Rubio said.
He warned that escalation could "turn what is a war between two countries into a much broader and far more dangerous regional conflict." Rubio added that Washington would continue working to facilitate a negotiated settlement and end the conflict.

title: Asaba Massacre: Obasanjo urges forgiveness, reconciliation
body:
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has urged survivors and families of victims of the 1967 Asaba Massacre to embrace forgiveness and reconciliation.
Mr Obasanjo made the call on Wednesday while participating virtually as chairman of the occasion at the 59th anniversary memorial of the massacre in Asaba.
He described the massacre as one of the most painful and terrible aspects of the Nigerian civil war.
Mr Obasanjo said the war was an unfortunate event that should never happen, adding that he wept after receiving documents on the massacre from Chuck Nduka-Eze, the Isama Ajie of Asaba and convener of the Asaba Massacre Memorial.
“To all of you assembled: let us keep one thing in mind, forgiveness, forgiveness, and forgiveness again,” Mr Obasanjo said.
He urged the people of Asaba to forgive and work toward reconciliation, enphasising the need to prevent such tragedies from recurring.
Responding to the appeal, the Asagba of Asaba, Epiphany Azinge, said the people could forgive but would not forget the tragedy.
Mr Azinge, a professor, said there would be no closure or healing until a sitting president publicly apologised to the people of Asaba.
“We may not forget, but certainly, we have to forgive,” Mr Azinge said, adding that former military Head of State, Yakubu Gowon, apologised while out of office.
“We need a sitting president to apologise to Asaba people; that will bring closure,” the traditional ruler said.
He also questioned Mr Obasanjo’s “never again” appeal, recalling that the Odi killings occurred during Obasanjo’s administration as president.
“Coming from him, I was a bit taken aback. How long do we say ‘never again’? But it happened at Odi,” he said.
The Asagba urged Nigerians to continue remembering the victims, saying, “From the going down of the sun till the morning, we will always remember them.”
He said the people had moved on, but stressed that remembrance, justice and reconciliation remained necessary as Asaba prepared for the 60th anniversary of the tragedy.
Despite the demand for a presidential apology, Mr Azinge made a significant reconciliation gesture by publicly proclaiming forgiveness for the family of Ibrahim Taiwo.
“On behalf of the Asaba community, and as the prescribed authority, the Asagba of Asaba, I hereby publicly proclaim that we have forgiven the Taiwo family,” he said.
He said the community had accepted the apology offered by the retired Major-General Ahmed Taiwo, son of Mr Taiwo, who was a colonel in the Nigerian Army during the incident.
Mr Taiwo had expressed regret and apologised on behalf of his father and family for any act, omission or commission that led to the massacre.
Meanwhile, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta State said researchers and community historians estimated that more than 1,000 people died in the massacre.
Represented by the Secretary to the Delta State Government, Kingsley Emu, Mr Oborevwori said, “Let us speak clearly: the killing of unarmed civilians can never be justified.”
The governor pledged continued support for national recognition of the massacre and the establishment of a fitting national memorial.
Also speaking, the Isama Ajie of Asaba and Convener of the Asaba Massacre Memorial, Mr Nduka-Eze, said preparations were underway for the 60th anniversary next year, with efforts intensified to establish a permanent memorial centre.
“The message we’ve been sending about the Asaba Massacre is that Nigerian lives matter,” he said.
He said the 60th anniversary would provide an opportunity to further tell the story of the massacre to Nigeria and the world.
Enotie Ogbebor, son of then-Colonel Paul Ogbebor, who was credited with intervening to save lives during the tragedy, said the massacre should be remembered globally.
He said the proposed memorial site would remind humanity that no innocent life should be lost unfairly for any reason.
The Obi of Onitsha, Nnaemeka Achebe, also spoke on restitution, reconciliation and forgiveness at the memorial.

title: Nine Syrians missing after cargo ship sunk by drone in Black Sea
body: Nine sailors from Syria and one from Egypt are missing after a cargo ship was sunk in the Black Sea, with search-and-rescue operations called off. The Turkish-owned Alfa Watan was hit by a drone off the Bulgarian coast on Tuesday. Russia is suspected of involvement in the latest of several such incidents during the war in Ukraine . Bulgaria said there were “no traces” of the 10 crew members and called off the search on Wednesday. A second ship was damaged on the same day as the Alfa Watan, with all its crew rescued. Syria on Thursday called for an investigation by Bulgaria and the International Maritime Organisation. Mazen Aloush, a director at the Syrian General Authority for Ports and Customs, said it should examine why the search for the Alfa Watan crew was called off before their fate was determined. He said “all available technical means” should be used to reach the wreck and determine what happened. “The file should not be closed before exhausting all available possibilities,” Syrian state media quoted him as saying. Vice Admiral Rumen Nikolov of Bulgaria's Maritime Administration Executive Agency had said a boat, ​three life rafts and parts of the ship's equipment were found before the Alfa Watan search was called off. It was not certain who carried out the attack, which took place off the coastal town of Byala in eastern Bulgaria, but there are growing concerns about attacks by Russia on European Union and Nato countries. “If we look at the nature of the cargo and the direction in which the ships were moving, then logically speaking the result argues in favour of Russia,” Prime Minister Rumen Radev said after a meeting of Bulgaria's National Security Council on Wednesday. “But that does not mean that we can claim that the strike was carried out by Russia without having evidence.” The Russian embassy in Sofia denied involvement, saying the merchant ship was not among targets hit by Russian drones on Tuesday. Ukrainian ⁠President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia and said his country's forces were not operating in that area. Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said the country would invite its Black Sea neighbours Turkey ⁠and Romania for talks on protecting shipping. It may ⁠also ask Nato allies to deploy “additional air and maritime surveillance capabilities and counter-drone systems”, she said. Nato member Bulgaria does not border Russia or Ukraine but lies on the Black Sea, where both countries have major ports and shipping has been caught in the conflict. The ⁠drone attack follows an incident in which Romanian authorities said on Monday two people had died in a fire on a ship in the Black Sea. It also comes in the wake of drone incidents in Poland and Romania, raising fears that Russia is testing Nato's defence posture without waging full-scale war against its members.

title: Russian Attack Warehouses of Auchan, Paper Mill, Publisher, Auto Shop
body:
Russian forces launched a combined drone and missile assault on Ukraine on Oct. 6-7, targeting warehouses belonging to civilian businesses. The attacks hit a new storage facility of the Knygolove book publishing house, warehouses of a cardboard and paper mill, facilities operated by Auchan French supermarket chain and the ATL auto repair network.
Overnight on Oct. 6-7, Russian forces launched a missile attack on a new warehouse of the Ukrainian multi-genre publisher Knygolove. The facility held books that had been restocked following an initial attack in July, which resulted in the loss of nearly 250,000 copies.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Russian attacks in August wiped out about a third of Ukraine’s annual book production. Due to the massive losses and a lack of funds, some publishing houses may not survive the aftermath of the attacks, Vivat Publishing House CEO Yuliya Orlova said on Radio Kultura.
“At this point, we cannot definitively assess the scale of the losses and calculate the number of books that were destroyed or can no longer be restored, but we can say for sure that tens of thousands of books were lost,” the company said on Instagram .
In 2025, the publisher’s revenue grew by 9 percent year-over-year to Hr.85 million ($1.89 million). Net profit for the same period reached Hr.8 million ($178,000), according to Opendatabot data .
That same night, Russian attacks completely destroyed the central warehouse of the ATL auto parts and service chain, which handled the bulk of its motor oils, batteries and automotive goods.
The company had already suffered a Russian attack in May, losing its central office.
“This is yet another painful reminder of how vulnerable Ukrainian civilian businesses remain, forced to operate in conditions where commercial warehouses and civilian infrastructure come under attack. But we have accepted these realities,” the company said on Facebook .
In 2025, the company’s revenue amounted to Hr.811.7 million ($19.23 million). Net profit for the same period reached Hr.25.8 million ($611.115), according to Opendatabot data .
Russian forces hit a fresh food warehouse belonging to Auchan, a French international retail chain specializing in food and everyday consumer goods.
“Most importantly, no employees were injured,” the company said on Facebook .
In 2025, the company’s net sales revenue amounted to Hr.10.03 billion ($229 million).The company ended the reporting period with a net loss of Hr.835.8 million ($18.6 million), according to YouControl data .
The company ended the reporting period with a net loss of Hr.835.8 million ($18.6 million)
Also on Oct. 7, a Russian missile struck the Kyiv Cardboard and Paper Mill, an enterprise in the pulp and paper industry.
“Production has currently been halted. Despite serious material damage, the most important thing for us is that none of our employees were injured,” the company said on Facebook .
This marks the third attack on the mill, following previous attacks in March and April 2026.
In 2025, the company’s revenue amounted to Hr.8.06 billion ($180 million). Net profit for the period reached Hr.419 million ($9.3 million), according to Opendatabot data .

title: Russia’s Defense Ministry proposes establishing rapid response units in military police
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. The Russian Defense Ministry has proposed creating rapid response units within the Russian army’s military police - the relevant draft presidential decree drawn up by the ministry is published on the federal portal of draft normative legal acts.
According to the document, it is proposed to add the term "rapid response unit" to the Charter of the Military Police of the Russian Armed Forces. It specifies that such a unit will consist of two or more military police personnel with an assigned vehicle, "designated in accordance with established procedures to perform, when necessary, duties related to the prompt suppression of crimes, administrative offenses, and/or disciplinary infractions, to detain the perpetrators, to repel attacks on military personnel and civilian staff, on Armed Forces facilities guarded by the military police, as well as to carry out other tasks aimed at ensuring law and order, military discipline, and combating crime among military personnel."
The draft decree also introduces the position of the "patrol duty detail." The patrol duty detail’s duties are planned to include ensuring public order and military discipline within the garrison area and its adjacent territory "within sight and earshot, where military personnel on patrol duty perform their assigned duties around the clock or during a specified period of time."

title: PAC Ranking Member accuses Health Ministry of ‘organised crime’ over GH¢10m outstanding car loans
body: Ranking Member on Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC), Samuel Atta Mills, has criticised the Ministry of Health over the alleged failure to recover about GH¢10 million in car loans, describing the arrangement as “organised crime”. Mr Atta Mills made the remarks when officials of the Ministry of Health appeared before the Public Accounts Committee on October 8 to respond to concerns over vehicles provided to officials under a car loan arrangement. According to the Ranking Member, some beneficiaries who, in his view, did not qualify to drive official vehicles based on their salaries were nevertheless provided with cars under arrangements that allowed them to determine when and how they would repay the loans. “We know these people don’t qualify to drive cars because of their salaries, and then we bypass the system. We give them their cars, and they choose when and how they are going to pay,” he said. He questioned the rationale behind the arrangement and expressed concern over the ministry’s approach to recovering outstanding amounts from beneficiaries. “If this isn’t organised crime, I don’t know what else it is. This is organised crime, being encouraged by the Minister of Health,” Mr Atta Mills said. Questions over retired and deceased beneficiaries The Ranking Member also raised concerns about beneficiaries who have either retired from public service or died without fully settling their car loans. He demanded a comprehensive list of such beneficiaries, suggesting that some vehicles could still be in the possession of relatives despite outstanding payments. ‘Put a stop to it’ Mr Atta Mills called on the Minister of Health to take immediate steps to recover the outstanding vehicles and funds. “This is organised crime, Minister of Health. Put a stop to it,” he said. His concerns centred particularly on the recovery process and the responsibility of the Ministry of Health to ensure that vehicles issued under the arrangement are either fully paid for or recovered where beneficiaries fail to meet the terms of the arrangement. Ranking Member challenges DVLA explanation The PAC Ranking Member also rejected an explanation that the list of beneficiaries or vehicles had been forwarded to the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA). He questioned why the DVLA should be expected to resolve a matter that originated from the Ministry of Health. “Was it DVLA who gave them those cars? Was it DVLA who organised that crime?” he asked. According to Mr Atta Mills, responsibility for recovering the vehicles rests primarily with the institution that provided them. He therefore called for the establishment of a dedicated recovery unit or team within the Ministry to pursue beneficiaries who have failed to honour their obligations. “What you need to do is you need to have a recovery unit, or a recovery team who will go and collect all these cars,” he said. Calls for aggressive recovery Mr Atta Mills argued that the Ministry must take stronger measures to retrieve vehicles where beneficiaries obtained them without meeting the applicable requirements or have failed to repay the associated loans. He suggested that a dedicated recovery team should be empowered to identify vehicles and take steps to retrieve them where necessary. “Somebody who will stop you in the middle of the highway and take the car away from you because you got it fraudulently,” he said. He accused the Ministry of shifting responsibility to other institutions instead of directly addressing the recovery of the vehicles. “You organised this crime, and then you blame everybody else. Whilst you are the criminals,” he added. The confrontation at the Public Accounts Committee highlights concerns over the management and recovery of government-backed vehicle loans, particularly where beneficiaries have retired, died or allegedly failed to meet repayment obligations.

title: Russian oil supplies to India hinder Delhi-Washington trade deal — report
body:
NEW YORK, October 8. /TASS/. US efforts to persuade India to stop purchasing Russian oil and to secure market access for American agricultural products remain the main obstacle to signing a trade agreement between the two nations, according to a report by BMI, a unit of the Fitch international rating agency.
"We expect India and the US eventually to conclude a narrow interim trade deal, although the remaining differences make a near-term breakthrough unlikely," the agency said.
The conflict in the Middle East and difficulties in transporting oil from Persian Gulf nations have reinforced India's incentive to maintain alternative sources of energy supplies, the agency noted.
Despite a narrowing of differences between India and the US, purchasing oil from Russia and importing US agricultural products remain the most politically and commercially sensitive matters for New Delhi. Russian oil accounted for approximately 50.8% of India's oil imports in July 2026. India might potentially allow limited imports of US agricultural goods, but importing American dairy products and genetically modified crops would entail significantly higher political costs.
India's effective tariff rate on US goods currently stands at 13.6%, well below the approximately 35% rate set in February. This implies that the direct benefits of the agreement could be limited unless a deal with the US secures preferential access for Indian goods to commercially significant sectors of the American market.
"India will resist costly concessions unless the US offers it a clear advantage over competing exporters," BMI said.
Trade negotiations between India and the US have also become more complicated due to Washington's efforts to reduce the bilateral goods trade deficit, which stood at $58.42 billion in 2025. India could narrow this gap by increasing purchases of US aircraft, energy products, technology, and weaponry. However, such purchases would not resolve US concerns regarding access to the Indian market.

title: Moldova ready to take in new wave of Ukrainian refugees in winter, Sandu says
body:
Moldovan President Maia Sandu said this at the Moldova Security Forum in Chisinau, Ukrinform reports, citing NewsMaker .
“Since 2022, more than 1 million Ukrainians who fled the war have arrived in Moldova, and about 100,000 have found a home here. If things are as difficult in Ukraine this winter as the whole world expects, we are ready to receive as many people as need safety,” Sandu said.
Former Prime Minister and presidential envoy for development and resilience Dorin Recean said Moldova was also preparing to provide Ukraine with logistical and energy support and to protect its own energy infrastructure.
According to him, the authorities are considering a scenario involving a new influx of Ukrainian refugees and have experience responding to emergencies.
Recean also noted that Moldova’s and Ukraine’s power grids are interconnected, so the country is preparing for possible problems with energy infrastructure as well. At the same time, he said Moldova would not be able to independently supply Ukraine with the necessary volumes of electricity, but electricity from Romania could be supplied through Moldovan territory.
EU representative Dorota Dlouhi-Suliga said the European Union would continue supporting Ukraine’s energy system, including by supplying generators to prevent the worst-case scenario.
According to her, the EU has been helping Moldova strengthen its capacity to receive Ukrainian refugees since 2022. Dlouhi-Suliga did not specify whether the EU was preparing a separate support plan for Moldova and other countries that could receive a new wave of refugees this winter.
As reported by Ukrinform, Sandu said Moldova, Ukraine and Romania should strengthen cooperation on airspace protection amid Russian aggression.

title: GAUA strike disrupts student registration at University of Ghana
body: The ongoing strike by the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) is disrupting administrative services at public universities, with students facing difficulties completing registration and other admission-related processes. GAUA has been on strike for more than two months following failed negotiations with the government over the payment of negotiated and approved allowances. The university administrators are also demanding action to address what they describe as disparities in allowances and other conditions of service. At the University of Ghana, several administrative services, including student, legal, financial and library services, have been affected by the industrial action. The disruption has also affected first-semester registration for the 2026/2027 academic year. A notice from the University of Ghana, signed by Pro Vice-Chancellor Professor Gordon Awandare, informed Level 100 and continuing students that registration had been put on hold due to the ongoing strike by university administrators. “Management of the University of Ghana wishes to apologise to our cherished students, Level 100 and continuing students, for the current challenges with online registration for the first semester of the 2026-2027 academic year, which are caused by the ongoing industrial action by the university administrators,” the notice stated. Checks by JoyNews at the University of Ghana showed that some students are struggling with course registration, accommodation arrangements and access to the university portal. Some parents also said they had been trying to access the portal for several days but had been unable to complete the registration process. The disruption comes as concerns grow over the impact of industrial actions on instructional time and the smooth running of Ghana’s education system. The ongoing teachers’ strike has already affected teaching and learning in some basic and secondary schools, with some pupils reportedly staying home. Parents say the situation is putting additional pressure on families, particularly those who have invested heavily in their children’s education. One parent expressed his frustration. “I have invested a lot for my kids, and honestly speaking, I feel so much sad for this outcome, that after all the investment, my child will not go to school to learn. It is so pathetic for me,” the parent said. The parent urged the authorities to urgently resolve the disputes to prevent students from losing more instructional time.

title: Turkey not to deploy troops abroad for offensive operations — Fidan
body:
ANKARA, October 8. /TASS/. The Mecca Alliance is exclusively defensive, and Turkey will not deploy troops to other countries to participate in offensive operations under the agreement, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said.
"I want to state clearly that this agreement concerns defense only. When a signatory country comes under attack, you must stand by it and defend it. This is not an agreement to launch attacks. Turkey will not deploy troops to another country to carry out an attack," he said at a news conference in Ankara with his Hungarian counterpart Anita Orban.
Fidan added that cooperation under the Mecca agreement "is developing, and military delegations will work together to determine what defensive measures [Saudi Arabia] requires in the operational theater and what contributions Pakistan and Turkey can make."
"Saudi Arabia already has extensive military and technical infrastructure. It possesses a large amount of equipment, weapons and defensive assets acquired over the years. However, joint planning, operations and analysis are also important," Fidan said.
According to the minister, Turkey "is doing everything possible to ensure that the situation is resolved through peace and dialogue." "Saudi Arabia is receiving constructive support in this regard. But I repeat: our agreement is defensive in nature. When a participating country comes under attack, you stand alongside it to defend it," he reiterated.
Fidan added that Turkey views the situation surrounding Saudi Arabia and the Houthi attacks in the broader regional context. "We are trying to understand what we can do politically [to resolve the situation] between the parties at the international level and bring greater peace to the region. There is also Iran, the war Iran is waging with America, and other issues. We are trying to consider all of this as part of the broader picture," he said.
Middle East Eye earlier reported, citing Turkish officials, that Ankara was considering deploying a limited military contingent and equipment to Saudi Arabia to protect critical infrastructure and holy cities from Houthi attacks. According to the publication, the plans do not envisage Turkey’s direct participation in combat operations in Yemen.

title: Tema is regaining its industrial glory days as Ghana’s industrial city – Mahama
body: President John Mahama says Tema is regaining its glory days as Ghana’s industrial city, citing the expansion of the Tema Port, the return of the Tema Oil Refinery and ongoing efforts to revive VALCO. Speaking at the commissioning and inspection of Nestlé Ghana’s expanded evaporated milk production line in Tema, he said the progress and the expansion of industries such as Nestlé is helping to restore Tema’s position as a key industrial centre. “Kwame Nkrumah planned Tema as Ghana’s industrial city, and I am pleased to say that Tema is regaining its glory days”. President Mahama said. He stated that industries operating in the Tema enclave depend on efficient infrastructure, including the port, roads and reliable electricity, to serve markets beyond Ghana. President Mahama said his government accepts the responsibility of providing the infrastructure needed to support industrial expansion. “My government accepts that obligation without reservation, and we are committed to meeting it,” he said. He also urged Nestlé to leverage Ghana’s position as the headquarters of the African Continental Free Trade Area to expand its reach across the continent. “Ghana is the headquarters of the African Continental Free Trade Area, and we must take advantage of this to make Ghana Africa’s production powerhouse,” he said. President Mahama said the expanded Nestlé production line provides the company with the capacity to contribute to that ambition. “This expansion gives Nestlé Ghana the capacity to do exactly that, and I urge the company to seize the opportunity with boldness and carry the words ‘Made in Ghana’ into every market across the length and breadth of Africa,” he said. He also warned that the increased domestic production capacity would come with greater attention to illicit imports and customs evasion. “Having built the capacity to make these cans ourselves, we will take an equally close interest in illicit imports and customs evasion,” President Mahama said. President Mahama declared that Ghana was open for business and outlined measures his administration was taking to improve the business environment. “Ghana is back and Ghana is open for business. Ghana is working again. My government is your partner.” he said. He said government was reforming customs procedures, revising the tax incentive framework and digitising public services to make doing business in Ghana faster, simpler and more predictable. President Mahama assured Ghanaian businesses that his administration would continue to provide the enabling environment, financing and infrastructure needed to support their growth. He said Ghana’s renewed confidence was being built through the work of businesses and workers across the country. “The confidence we are rebuilding today is not borrowed from anyone. It is earned factory by factory and production line by production line through the labour and dedication of Ghanaian workers,” he said.

title: ACF ‘congratulates’ Bwala for admitting Tinubu’s reforms deepen poverty
body: The Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) has sarcastically “congratulated” Daniel Bwala, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, for acknowledging that the administration’s economic reforms have increased poverty and hardship among Nigerians. Professor Tukur Mohammed-Baba, Publicity Secretary of the ACF, made the remark during an interview on Arise Television’s News Day on Thursday. Mohammed-Baba was reacting to Bwala’s comments during an interview on Channels Television on Wednesday, where the presidential aide acknowledged that the government’s economic reforms had contributed to an increase in poverty but argued that the administration had made significant progress since introducing the measures. “Let’s first of all be very happy and congratulate Bwala. Until now, one would expect that whenever he comes on TV or appears on social media, it is to deny, deny, deny,” Mohammed-Baba said. “But I think we are making progress since his admitting fundamentally that the reforms have brought untold hardships on Nigerians. Most especially, he has not denied that poverty has been rising.” The ACF spokesman said multidimensional poverty remained widespread in the country, while criticising attempts by the administration to justify the hardship as a temporary consequence of economic reforms. “As we speak today, the rate of multidimensional poverty is well over 60 per cent in Nigeria,” he said. Mohammed-Baba dismissed claims that the benefits of the reforms would eventually outweigh their immediate effects, describing such assurances as “hallucinations” and drawing a comparison with the structural adjustment programme of the Ibrahim Babangida administration. He said Nigerians were currently struggling with declining purchasing power, rising rents, housing costs, transportation fares and electricity bills, while insecurity had further worsened living conditions. “Look at the purchasing power of the naira. Look at the living conditions of Nigerians. Look at rent. Look at housing materials. Look at transportation. Look at electricity costs,” he said. “See the condition of the roads in Nigeria, and above all, see the level of insecurity that has been pervading this country.” The ACF official, who said he had visited parts of the Northeast, North-Central and Northwest, said insecurity had made basic activities such as farming increasingly difficult. He argued that the Tinubu administration could not continue to shift responsibility for current challenges to previous governments, saying those who sought political power should have assessed the conditions they would inherit before assuming office. “That is precisely why we have a democracy. You identify there are problems, and you think you have the answer. You go out, canvass for votes. You get it, and now you spend reminding us other leaders have faced these problems,” he said. Mohammed-Baba said the administration should accept responsibility for its performance rather than tell Nigerians that it was not responsible for their hardship. “There is no doubt that if the government were to go into the room, look at itself in the mirror, and tell us honestly whether it has performed optimally or near satisfactorily, I am sure the answer will be negative,” he said. The post ACF ‘congratulates’ Bwala for admitting Tinubu’s reforms deepen poverty appeared first on Vanguard News .

Russia has turned everyday movement in frontline Donetsk Oblast into a lethal risk, striking city buses, ambulances, and cars in places its army has not been able to capture. A route bus run turned deadly The attack came at around 10:00, catching two route buses in the impact zone. The prosecutor's office said the attackers likely used a UMPB D-30SN. HUR, Ukraine's military intelligence, describes it as a guided glide bomb that can fly up to 100 km when released from an altitude of 12–15 km and carries a warhead equal to a FAB-250 aerial bomb. 30 people were killed and 18 injured after a Russian bomb hit two passenger buses carrying civilians in Kramatorsk, Donetsk Oblast. title: FBI says more than 130 detained in Ghana over scam operation targeting US victims
body: FBI Director Kash Patel says a scam operation in Ghana has been dismantled as part of the bureau’s global Operation Blackout targeting transnational fraud networks. In a post on X on Thursday, October 8, Patel said the Ghana operation had so far identified nearly US$10 million in losses and 89 victims, while more than 130 people had been arrested or detained. OPERATION BLACKOUT: this FBI’s global scam center fraud demolition. Another takedown this week out of Ghana: -Nearly $10 million in identified losses so far -89 victims identified -130+ individuals arrested or detained (including victims who will be repatriated to home country) -300+ devices seized Investigation is ongoing. These scam compounds target American citizens and destroy lives – and this @FBI is crushing them in every corner of the world. More to come. Operation Blackout totals so far: -Roughly $17 BILLION seized -Hundreds of alleged scammers arrested -Thousands of trafficked workers freed -10,000+ Americans warned before losing their money -$670 MILLION in estimated losses prevented — FBI Director Kash Patel (@FBIDirectorKash) October 8, 2026 He also said more than 300 devices had been seized during the operation. “These scam compounds target American citizens and destroy lives – and this FBI is crushing them in every corner of the world. More to come,” Patel said. The FBI Director said the investigation remains ongoing. According to Patel’s account, some of those detained in Ghana are victims who will be repatriated to their home countries. The identities of those arrested or detained, the locations of the operations and the specific Ghanaian institutions involved have not been disclosed in Patel’s post. It is also not yet clear whether any of those arrested will face prosecution in Ghana or extradition proceedings in the United States. The Ghana operation forms part of Operation Blackout, which the FBI describes as a global effort targeting scam compounds involved in fraud against Americans. Patel has previously said Operation Blackout has resulted in roughly US$17 billion in fraud-related assets being seized. He has also said the initiative has led to hundreds of arrests, the freeing of thousands of trafficked workers and efforts to warn potential victims before they lose money. The FBI’s separate prevention effort, Operation Level Up, has reportedly contacted more than 10,000 potential victims and prevented hundreds of millions of dollars in losses. Patel has described scam compounds targeted by the operation as large, fortified facilities where trafficked workers are allegedly forced to conduct fraud against victims abroad. He has also said criminal networks are increasingly moving their operations towards Africa as law enforcement pressure increases in Southeast Asia and other regions. The announcement comes amid growing cooperation between Ghanaian and US authorities over transnational financial and cybercrime. In July, Ghanaian national Frederick Kumi, popularly known as Abu Trica, was extradited to the United States to face charges over his alleged involvement in a romance-fraud network. The US Department of Justice said Kumi, 31, was accused of being part of a network that targeted more than 80 elderly victims in the United States and allegedly defrauded them of more than US$8 million. Kumi was arrested in Ghana in December 2025 and extradited to the US on July 9, 2026. He faces charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and money laundering conspiracy. The US authorities acknowledged the cooperation of several Ghanaian institutions in securing his arrest and extradition, including the Attorney-General’s Office, Economic and Organised Crime Office, Ghana Police Service, Cyber Security Authority, National Intelligence Bureau and the FBI Legal Attaché Office in Accra. Patel ended his announcement on the Ghana operation by saying “More to come,” suggesting the bureau’s campaign against international scam networks is continuing. The FBI has not provided further details on the identities of those arrested in Ghana or the precise location and nature of the operation.

title: Nigeria at 66: Understanding its politics of the supernatural, By Ayo Akerele
body:
But I must also urge you to remember this: Nigeria’s problems are not only political and economic… They carry deep, far-reaching spiritual dimensions that can only be decisively addressed by a superior spiritual force; one wielded by men and women with an unwavering commitment to righteousness, and above all, to the Lord Jesus Christ. This is where the Nigerian church is most urgently needed.
One of the most unsettling visions I received about Nigeria came during the administration of President Muhammadu Buhari. In it, I watched his presidential motorcade being intercepted, deliberately cut off, by a group of politicians. They produced what appeared to be a document and, under armed supervision, compelled him to sign it. Then the vision ended.
Not long after, something unmistakable began to unfold in the natural realm. Buhari’s most vocal supporters began abandoning him, one by one, consumed by disillusionment as Nigeria descended into a catastrophic spiral of insecurity and economic suffering. What most people did not realise, what they could not see, was that the foundation for that collapse had already been laid in the spirit realm. Agreements had been struck. Bargains had been sealed.
The forces I saw in that vision were not ordinary political actors. They were spiritual powers operating through human vessels, powers determined to use the Buhari administration as a vehicle to entrench the ideology of Jihad in Nigeria; advancing it through the deliberate displacement of ethnic communities and the systematic economic subjugation of non-dominant groups.
This is a truth that must be stated plainly: the spirit controls the natural. It is not primarily politics that determines the direction of a nation, it is the totality of the spiritual climate and the spiritual allegiances of its leadership.
On a separate occasion, I was shown another quick but deeply sobering vision; a map of Nigeria. Before my eyes, it cracked and split apart, from the upper right to the lower left. The vision was brief. But its weight has never left me.
Taken together, these revelations, along with many other messages the Lord has entrusted to me over the years, have driven me to one unavoidable conclusion: Nigeria is in the deliberate plan of God for a strategic shift. But that shift will not come through politics alone, nor through spiritual activity divorced from the realities of governance.
It will require both, the supernatural and the political working in concert.
Politics determines who leads and the policies they pursue. The supernatural determines the environment in which those leaders either rise or fall. One without the other is incomplete.
When the Supernatural and the Political Converge: A Warning From American History
Dr Perry Stone, in his prophetic work on the supernatural dimensions of American politics, documented a striking and sobering pattern in one of his books, Deciphering Endtime Prophetic Codes . Here, he notes an early research done by a prophetic teacher in America, stating that some US presidents elected in years ending in zero died before completing their terms, either through assassination or sudden natural death.
After Kennedy, no president died in office despite the assasination attempt made on Ronald Reagan, elected in 1980, another year ending in zero. But Reagan’s story took a different turn. According to Dr Perry Stone, someone within Ronald Reagan’s inner circle had been made aware of this prophetic pattern in the aftermath of Kennedy’s assassination. Rather than dismiss it, Reagan’s administration responded with urgency: intercessors were mobilised, prayer was organised even within the White House, and the curse was confronted head-on in the spirit realm, and broken.
Reagan survived two full terms. He was even shot, and still he survived. In fact, after he was shot, one of the intercessors who knew about the “curse of the zero” year was so terrified. But their prayers saved the president’s life.
Dr Perry Stone calls this recurring phenomenon the “zero-curse year.”
The implications for Nigeria are direct and sobering. There are spiritual dimensions to the destiny of nations that no amount of political engineering can override. Nigeria is not exempt from this reality. If anything, Nigeria is one of the most contested spiritual territories on earth. Jihadists, US, UK, Russian, and French imperialists, all have strategic interests in the oil and natural resources rich African nation.
As Nigeria marks sixty-six years of independence, there is very little to celebrate when measured against a standard of genuine excellence. And excellence must be the measure. You do not determine greatness by comparing yourself to mediocrity. You measure yourself against the best, and by that standard, Nigeria has not yet arrived.
Nigeria is not simply a political problem. It is a deeply contested spiritual battleground, and it has been for generations.
From the advancing forces of Jihad, to the lingering tendrils of the British imperial system, to other highly organised demonic structures with centuries-old interests in this land, multiple forces are actively competing for the soul of one nation. Every Nigerian with genuine spiritual discernment must therefore direct their energy not only toward political solutions but toward understanding and confronting the spiritual root systems that have made those political solutions perpetually elusive.
Nigeria is a deeply religious nation. Its transformation cannot bypass the role of faith and spiritual values. No nation rises above the ceiling of its dominant spiritual climate. While Nigeria is constitutionally a secular state with deeply polarised religious communities, we need not impose a single religion on the nation. What we must do is rigorously examine the values that each faith tradition brings to the table, and collectively commit to the supernatural belief system that most powerfully advances equity, transparency, and genuine national development. If we solve for the spiritual, the political will begin to yield.
The political instability, the corruption, the ethnic tension; none of it is accidental. To understand Nigeria’s present, we must reckon honestly with its birth.
Let us ask the question plainly: Can you nurture a nation from infancy to adulthood without understanding its spiritual and natural lineage?
You were born from the womb of the British Empire — not out of love, not out of vision for your people, but as the product of economic transactions among greedy imperialists. Your very foundation was constructed on the doctrine of divide-and-rule: the deliberate merging of vastly different ethnic, cultural, and religious peoples into a single state, not to unite them, but to ensure that their divisions would make them permanently manageable and perpetually dependent.
This strategy is not unique in history. It bears a troubling resemblance to the apparatus of Nazi Germany, where division was weaponised as a tool of control. Hitler’s propaganda machinery, led by the notorious Dr Joseph Goebbels, was engineered to create a German society incapable of distinguishing truth from deception. As Dr Erwin Lutzer defines it, propaganda is “the intelligent manipulation of the masses.” Goebbels did not eliminate truth, he buried it beneath layers of orchestrated narrative, sacrificing the welfare of ordinary people to preserve the establishment.
George Orwell captured the same dynamic with devastating precision: “They don’t solve problems, they use them.”
Nigeria’s story is a variation of the same script. Her vast resources have been systematically plundered, first by imperialists, and then by their locally trained successors: the political elite, the entrenched establishment, the corrupt gatekeepers of power who have learnt to profit from the nation’s dysfunction. In this environment, misinformation has become the preferred currency of governance. As Dr Lutzer soberly observed, “The media does not just disseminate information, it alters the consciences of entire generations.”
Nigeria’s media, which should serve as an independent arbiter of truth, has been substantially compromised, leaving ordinary citizens adrift in a sea of competing narratives, unable to locate solid ground.
Sixty-Six Years and Still Waiting to Rise
As Nigeria marks sixty-six years of independence, there is very little to celebrate when measured against a standard of genuine excellence. And excellence must be the measure. You do not determine greatness by comparing yourself to mediocrity. You measure yourself against the best, and by that standard, Nigeria has not yet arrived.
A nation that still cannot guarantee consistent electricity. A nation where clean water is a luxury rather than a right. A nation where the security of life and property remains fragile. A nation where fuel prices, food prices, and housing costs have become unbearable burdens for the average family, such a nation cannot, in good conscience, declare herself great.
She is great in potential. But potential does not fix roads. Potential does not feed children. Sustained, courageous action does.
The battle for Nigeria must be fought on two fronts simultaneously: politically and spiritually. To fight on only one front is to fight with one hand tied behind your back. Nigeria’s redemption is possible. But it will require the full surrender of both our ballot and our altar. Happy 66th birthday to my beloved Nigeria!
There is a passage in Scripture that I believe speaks directly to Nigeria’s past, present, and the promise of its future. It is found in Isaiah 66:7–9:
“Before she was in labour, she gave birth; before her pain came, she delivered a male child. Who has heard such a thing? Who has seen such things? Shall the earth be made to give birth in one day? Or shall a nation be born at once? For as soon as Zion was in labour, she gave birth to her children. Shall I bring to the time of birth, and not cause delivery?” says the Lord. “Shall I who cause delivery shut up the womb?” Says your God.
This is the blueprint, from labour pains to delivery. If God Himself has brought Nigeria to its time of birth, He is fully committed to causing it to deliver. The promise is irrevocable.
But the condition is equally clear: the gods that have entrenched themselves in Nigeria, chief among them the god of greed, which has taken deep root in the hearts of many politicians and far too many religious leaders, must be systematically uprooted. A nation cannot deliver under the authority of a false god.
As followers of Jesus Christ, we carry a responsibility that extends far beyond the walls of our sanctuaries. The Bible is unambiguous: contentment is a virtue; greed is a sin at its root. The church of Christ in Nigeria must therefore lead the spiritual revolution of this nation, not through rhetoric, but through the visible, verifiable modeling of the values of Jesus Christ.
These values must govern how we run our churches, how we conduct our ministries, how Christians engage in politics, how Christian professionals operate in the marketplace, and how church leaders steward the platforms entrusted to them. This is what it truly means to be the light of the world.
When the church operates with this kind of moral authority, she earns the credibility to unite people across divides, to pray with genuine spiritual power, to engage political parties and candidates with discernment, and to advance sound moral values that weaken and subdue the wicked spiritual forces that are actively working for Nigeria’s destruction.
Dr Tony Evans said it precisely: “When conscience dies in a nation, truth becomes the first casualty.”
And we must equally remember: a nation is not great because of the value of its wealth. It is great because of the wealth of its values, values that are both spiritual and natural.
I want to close by honouring every Nigerian, at home and in the diaspora, who has refused to give up on this nation. Those who daily defy threats, intimidation, and danger to lawfully advocate for truth, freedom, fairness, equity, and justice. Your courage is not unseen. It is not unimportant.
But I must also urge you to remember this: Nigeria’s problems are not only political and economic.
They carry deep, far-reaching spiritual dimensions that can only be decisively addressed by a superior spiritual force; one wielded by men and women with an unwavering commitment to righteousness, and above all, to the Lord Jesus Christ. This is where the Nigerian church is most urgently needed.
The battle for Nigeria must be fought on two fronts simultaneously: politically and spiritually. To fight on only one front is to fight with one hand tied behind your back. Nigeria’s redemption is possible. But it will require the full surrender of both our ballot and our altar. Happy 66th birthday to my beloved Nigeria!

title: 'Heroic actions': Magen David Adom mourns first responders who served, were murdered on Oct. 7
body: Magen David Adom mourned its first responders who were murdered during the October 7 massacre earlier this week to mark three years since Hamas terrorists infiltrated Israel and murdered over 1,200 Israelis.According to MDA, 20 members of the emergency services were murdered during the massacre, including seven who were murdered while treating the wounded under fire.Three MDA personnel were abducted into the Gaza Strip. Among them were volunteer Emergency Medical Technicians Ronen Engel from Kibbutz Nir Oz and Lior Rudaeff from Kibbutz Nir Yitzhak, whose remains were returned to Israel for burial in October and November 2025, respectively.MDA said that its ambulances and motorcycles were targeted by terrorists, with 18 ambulances damaged during October 7 and the following days, including eight that were completely destroyed."Tragically, some of those who answered the call to save lives never returned home, losing their own lives in the line of duty," MDA Director-General Eli Bin reflected."Three years later, we remember every member of our MDA family who was lost and honor their courage, dedication, and sacrifice."As reports that morning accumulated of rocket fire, casualties, and terrorist infiltrations into military bases and communities, MDA leadership assembled in the early hours at the National Integrated Dispatch Center.For MDA to mobilize as many available resources as possible, rapid internal decisions were made, such as the initial decision to keep the night shift on duty rather than release personnel as the morning shift arrived.MDA immediately raised its national alert to the highest level, staffed every available ambulance and emergency dispatch position, and deployed armored ambulances from across the country to southern Israel, while maintaining reserve capacity in case of escalation on the northern front.MDA received over 21,600 emergency calls during October 7 massacreMore than 21,600 emergency calls were received by its dispatch centers, approximately five times the daily average, said MDA. Hundreds of MDA ambulances operated in southern Israel, evacuating scores of casualties from the Gaza border communities and their surrounding areas.MDA said that its helicopters also played a critical role in evacuating the wounded. During the morning hours of October 7, MDA said that its helicopters were the only helicopters in the air evacuating wounded people from the affected areas. However, one MDA helicopter was ultimately struck by rocket shrapnel. MDA also coordinated with the Israel Air Force for medical evacuations.MDA Blood Services also played a critical role from the earliest hours of October 7. Blood collection activity was expanded, including at protected donation sites, to increase blood reserves and ensure a continuous supply of blood units to hospitals and the defense system.Since then, they have also "pioneered a whole blood protocol" that has "significantly reduced battlefield deaths," according to MDA.In the days following October 7, thousands of people came forward to donate blood. The Marcus National Blood Services Center, Ramle, enabled MDA to process and distribute blood donations under wartime conditions.Three years after massacre, MDA has greatly expanded emergency response capacityThree years on, MDA honored those it lost while pointing to a major expansion of its emergency response capacity, including a fivefold increase in its armored ambulance fleet.When the October 7 massacre occured, MDA had 20 armored ambulances. Today, it has more than 100 armored ambulances and approximately 2,000 ambulances in total. Its helicopter fleet has also expanded from three helicopters to five.Additionally, MDA has established community-based initiatives, including expanded midwife services and the Magen Project, which has trained over 17,800 civilians to provide immediate first aid when emergency medical teams are cut off. The organization has also reportedly expanded training, blood collection, humanitarian assistance, and emergency preparedness.According to MDA, around 5,000 new volunteers have joined the organization since the war broke out on October 7, and the organization's vehicle fleet and its operational and community capabilities have continued to grow.Since the massacre, MDA has expanded its response capabilities through initiatives designed to strengthen emergency preparedness and bring lifesaving care closer to communities.“October 7 showed the courage, dedication, and leadership of Magen David Adom's medics under circumstances unlike anything we had experienced before,” said Bin.“Our teams went out under heavy fire to treat and evacuate the wounded, putting their own lives at risk while their families sheltered from the attack,” he added.

title: State Customs Service: Bila Tserkva–Sighetu Marmatiei crossing opens with capacity for up to 700 cars and 400 trucks daily
body:
The Bila Tserkva–Sighetu Marmatiei international road crossing on the Ukraine-Romania border has opened, the State Customs Service said Thursday.

The border and customs infrastructure has six passenger-car lanes, two bus lanes and six truck lanes. Daily capacity is up to 700 passenger cars, 60 buses carrying 2,000-3,000 passengers, and 400 trucks.

The service said that, for now, round-the-clock border crossing is available only to passenger cars. Truck traffic without weight restrictions will begin after construction is completed.

title: ARMA Public Control Council formed with representatives of nine NGOs following vote
body:
The National Agency for Asset Recovery and Management (ARMA), following an online ranked voting process held from September 29 through October 2, 2026, has approved the membership of its Public Control Council, the agency said on Thursday.
The newly elected advisory body comprises nine representatives of civic organizations: Yevhen Linnyk (D7 Foundation NGO), Oksana Ihnatenko, Serhiy Verenчuk and Mykola Malukha (all three from the Center for Public Control NGO), Tetiana Yatsyk, Alona Shokarieva and Olena Reznikova (all three from the Ukrainian Legal Society NGO), Andriy Tkachuk (Transparency International Ukraine NGO), and Tetiana Nesterenko (Revival of Ukraine Democracy Development Fund NGO).
The agency said the Public Control Council was established as a mechanism for cooperation between ARMA and civil society. Its powers include public oversight of ARMA's activities, monitoring the exercise of its powers, reviewing the agency's annual report, examining draft regulations and submitting proposals. Council members will also oversee the legality and transparency of the selection of asset managers and the sale of assets, and participate in the work of ARMA's competition and disciplinary commissions.
As reported, the election process was postponed several times due to technical incidents. ARMA previously suspended a similar online vote scheduled for August 10-12, 2026 due to a technical failure, saying this was necessary to preserve confidence in and transparency of the procedure. A new vote was subsequently announced to begin on September 28, but following Russian attacks and damage to technical equipment it was postponed until the following day, September 29. A total of 31 candidates from 17 civic organizations submitted applications, with 27 candidates admitted to the ranked vote.

title: German pilots prepare for CH‑47F fleet with US Army flight simulator
body: A U.S. Army flight simulator at a barracks in Germany stands as a center of critical training for NATO’s aviation community. The U.S. Army Garrison Ansbach’s Stock Barracks in Illesheim houses the Illesheim Flight Simulator Complex, or IFSC, providing one-of-a-kind training opportunities ahead of the German Armed Forces preparing to field CH‑47F Block II Chinook helicopters next fall, according to an Army release . The IFSC, which is operated by U.S. Army Europe and Africa, provides the necessary training needed to prepare German forces to receive 60 of the heavy-lift, tandem-rotor helicopters, the release says. Two German Air Force pilots who will be part of the first cohort to fly the new aircraft once they arrive in fall 2027 recently trained at the IFSC. “In the simulator you can train all the scenarios you do not want to experience while flying a real aircraft,” said Lt. Col. L, a visiting pilot whose name was withheld, as is standard in the German Air Force, or Bundeswehr Luftwaffe. “Emergency procedures, challenging landings and extreme weather operations can all be practiced safely.” “Everything you can do in a real flight, you can also do in a simulator,” the other visiting pilot, Maj. H, said. The fleet will be stationed at two Bundeswehr installations and is meant to boost Germany’s heavy-lift and transport abilities, per the statement. The two German pilots also trained in the U.S. Army Aviation Center of Excellence at Fort Rucker, Alabama. Fort Rucker is the Army’s largest helicopter training institution and trains more than 1,300 U.S. soldiers every year. Beginning in 2028, German Air Force aviators will also trek to Fort Rucker annually for initial helicopter training and complete “track training,” including the CH‑47 qualification. The Army did not say how many German aviators are expected to train at Fort Rucker each year, but the release noted that the German Air Force plans to staff more than 200 trained pilots to operate its future fleet. Germany has already begun sending helicopter pilots for conversion training to the CH‑47 platform, according to the release. Since the IFSC simulator software is tailored to U.S. Army aircraft configurations and not the Bundeswehr’s, the German pilots will need additional learning to transition to their Air Force’s aircraft. Instead of German Air Force pilots needing to travel across the Atlantic for advanced simulator training, the IFSC allows them to drive just three to five hours from their home station. By using the existing U.S. Army facilities in Europe, NATO partners reduce costs by not needing to build their own simulator complex, the announcement says. Even though the IFSC schedule prioritizes U.S. Army soldiers, the complex routinely supports at least five NATO partners’ pilots. “For NATO partners requiring up-to-date, quality aircraft simulation training, USAG Ansbach’s Storck Barracks continues to prove its value: a small installation delivering strategic impact through world‑class training,” the release reads.

title: Ukrainian negotiating team to be in US on Friday, Zelensky says
body:
The Ukrainian President said this during a briefing in Pryluky, according to an Ukrinform correspondent.
“Important moments. Our team is in Europe today, and tomorrow and the day after tomorrow it will be in the United States. I hope that all the necessary signals will be conveyed,” Zelensky said.
He noted that he expects partners to step up sanctions pressure on Russia, particularly following the latest strikes on Pryluky and Kramatorsk, as well as provide Ukraine with additional means of protection, especially air defense, along with financial support.
As reported, Volodymyr Zelensky said several days ago that Ukraine was ready to participate in technical-level talks in the UAE or another country proposed by US representatives, but Russia has yet to respond.

title: EU and GCC to strengthen relations at leaders' summit in Riyadh
body: The European Union hopes to deepen security and energy relations with Gulf countries at the second leaders' summit in Riyadh next month. Since the start of the Iran war on February 28, Europe has cast itself as a solid ally to the Gulf , despite being unable to match superior US military capabilities. “In the current geopolitical context, there is an opportunity for deeper and more ambitious EU-GCC partnerships,” European Council President Antonio Costa said in a letter of invitation to Gulf and EU leaders dated Tuesday and seen by The National . As the closest neighbours geographically, with long historical and cultural ties, and recognising the growing shared challenges we face, I propose that our discussions will focus on key regional issues,” Mr Costa, who will co-chair the summit with Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman, wrote. He called for strengthening co-operation in priority areas such as “peace and security, connectivity, trade, economic co-operation, energy and mobility”. European support The Houthi- Saudi Arabia conflict escalated on Wednesday, with three people killed in attacks by the Yemeni rebels on airports in the kingdom, disrupting flights. Following a major escalation of the Houthi offensive last month, in which the Iran-backed group seized key energy and maritime infrastructure, France and the UK – which is not an EU member – were among the first to send Riyadh military support, including fighter jet-refuelling capabilities and defence systems. This week, Turkey and Pakistan , which signed a defence agreement with Saudi Arabia, said they would send troops. The US, historically a key Saudi ally, has been notably absent from announcements of military aid. The physical presence of the EU's 27 leaders in Riyadh for the EU-GCC Summit on October 24 is likely to represent an important signal of support to Saudi Arabia and more widely to Gulf states affected by regional instability. Early in the war, France and Italy sent air-defence systems to the UAE to help it fend off Iranian drone and missile attacks. “The Riyadh summit can showcase the EU as a reliable and long-term partner to the Gulf countries and unlock shared opportunities,” Mr Costa said in the letter. Cinzia Bianco, a research fellow on Europe and the Gulf at the European Council on Foreign Relations, told The National that Europe's backing did not mean pivoting away from the US. “Europe can offer different things,” Ms Bianco said. “It is about a strategic partnership maturing and showing concrete defensive support is only your entrance ticket, in a way.” The previous EU-GCC Summit took place in Brussels in 2024 and was the first since the signing of the initial EU-GCC co-operation agreement in 1989. The EU is the second-biggest trading partner of the GCC countries: the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman and Qatar. The European Commission said that over the past decade, EU-GCC trade has increased by about 30 per cent, with imports growing about 54 per cent and exports 20 per cent. The key traded good is fuel, accounting for more than 75 per cent of the EU’s imports from GCC countries. In a joint statement issued on Wednesday, nine Southern Mediterranean EU leaders said the summit would provide an opportunity to “strengthen engagement with Gulf partners on regional peace, security and prosperity”. “The EU should continue to work closely with Gulf partners and other partners in the region, using its diplomatic, economic, humanitarian and security instruments to support regional co-operation and peacebuilding,” they said. Reinforcing Aspides? Kaja Kallas, the EU's foreign affairs and security policy chief, has been pushing for months to strengthen Aspides, the bloc's defensive maritime mission. Aspides' mandate covers a wide area including the Bab Al Mandeb strait, the Strait of Hormuz and international waters in the Red Sea. It is currently operating in the Red Sea. “The mandate covers also Hormuz but it needs to be activated, including with more ships,” Ms Bianco said. “This is already happening, to get to the summit in Riyadh in a more credible position.” Ms Kallas' efforts have been backed by Italy, which recently complained in a letter to her that other EU nations were not being supportive enough and suggested they contribute financially instead. Italy and France both have one frigate deployed to the mission, which is under Greek strategic command. Speaking last month in Brussels, Ms Kallas said the quality of vessels was as important as their number. “For example, Aspides does not have a minehunting mandate, which means that you need frigates, you need air-defence support, you need vessels that can do the escorting of the ships,” she said.

title: Germany’s Quantum Systems to supply Kiev with tens of thousands of interceptor drones
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. German defense company Quantum Systems intends to send tens of thousands of SPYS interceptor drones to Ukraine by the end of 2026, Ukrinform news agency quoted Vice President Matthias Lehna as saying.
"An agreement of intent was signed over the weekend on a package for tens of thousands of SPYS," Lehna said at a briefing in Berlin.
Quantum Systems developed the SPYS interceptor drones in collaboration with Ukrainian defense company WIY.
Russia has repeatedly said that arms supplies to the Kiev regime only prolong the conflict in Ukraine.

The GTA VI leaks keep coming — and the latest is almost as long as the game’s official “extended look” on Netflix . Only instead of showing off all the various gameplay details, this one is more of an “extended look” at Jason running around Vice City naked. As Kotaku reports, GTA leaker Cyberleek , who cashed out on a memecoin and seemingly disappeared earlier this year, is back with a new 25-minute video of GTA VI gameplay.
The video suggests players will be able to play through GTA VI with their characters completely unclothed. According to Kotaku , Jason is naked throughout almost the whole video, including while on a motorbike, “at a beach-side coffee store,” and while talking to other characters. Lucia is also mostly naked in a clip at the end of the video, where Cyberleek reportedly briefly shows her from behind.
Some of the leaked footage appears to include light story spoilers, with Kotaku noting that the video opens with a cutscene of Jason and Lucia leading into a dirt bike race for one of the game’s scripted missions. Cyberleek goes on to show some first-person driving footage from Jason, followed by a street race. Kotaku also says Cyberleek “seemingly conjures a tank out of the air” and, of course, uses the video to advertise a crypto coin.
Cyberleek previously shared a slew of other GTA VI clips in the lead up to the game’s Netflix special. Rockstar Games eventually responded, calling the leaks “heartbreaking,” and Take-Two has requested multiple subpoenas as it tries to find the “alleged infringers” leaking the game footage. Before that, a massive collection of videos leaked in 2022 , and the hacker was eventually sentenced to life in hospital prison . Grand Theft Auto VI is available for preorder now and set to launch on November 19th.
