title: Ukrainian actor Serhii Strelnikov enlists in Unmanned Systems Forces
body:
Ukrainian actor Serhii Strelnikov announced on Oct. 8 that he had enlisted in the Unmanned Systems Forces, calling it "an honor to be among these people."
"I am committed to learning, adapting to new conditions, and conscientiously fulfilling the duties entrusted to me," he wrote in an Instagram post.
According to Strelnikov, he has joined the Ferro-6 Unmanned Systems Battalion of the 9th Separate Unmanned Systems Brigade, which he described as "consisting at its core of soldiers with infantry combat experience who now locate and destroy the enemy from the air."
Strelnikov has starred in several critically acclaimed films in recent years, including the lead in the historical drama "Dovbush" (2023). The film is based on Oleksa Dovbush, a legendary 18th-century Ukrainian outlaw who became a folk hero in the Carpathian Mountains during the time of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.
He also played Special Forces Commander "Sova" in the 2026 action thriller " Killhouse ," based on a real-life rescue mission conducted by Ukraine's special forces. The Ukrainian Oscar Committee shortlisted the film as a potential submission for the country at the 2027 Academy Awards.
Many prominent figures from Ukraine's cultural sphere have enlisted in the Armed Forces of Ukraine since the start of the full-scale war to help defend the country against Russian aggression. Strelnikov's "Killhouse" co-star, Denys Kapustin, enlisted in the 3rd Assault Brigade after filming of the action thriller wrapped.

title: GIPA CEO calls for investment to support Ghana’s economic transformation
body: The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), Simon Madjie has called for increased investment, technology and expertise to help turn Ghana’s emerging economic opportunities into productive businesses and sustainable jobs. According to him, the Big Push Infrastructure Programme, 24-Hour Economy and Accelerated Export Development Programme and the New Economy Programme are creating opportunities for investors to participate in infrastructure development, domestic production, industrialisation and export growth. Mr Madjie made the call at the launch of the Invest Ghana Summit 2026 and the 22nd Ghana Club 100 Awards, being organised by GIPA in collaboration with its partners. He said recent improvements in the economy, including stronger growth, declining inflation, rising international reserves and a more stable exchange rate, had provided a stronger foundation for investment. He added that the development of a productive economy required the mobilisation of capital, technology and expertise to support businesses, create jobs and expand exports. Mr. Madjie also highlighted the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority Act, 2026 (Act 1173), saying the new law had removed general minimum foreign capital requirements for joint ventures and wholly foreign-owned enterprises. He further stated that the legislation had also strengthened investor protections and expanded GIPA’s mandate to provide more effective and coordinated support to investors. He opined that the investment environment was therefore being reformed alongside the implementation of programmes designed to expand economic activity.

title: FACTBOX: What is known about approval of EU’s 22nd sanctions package against Russia
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Estonia has asked the European Union to exclude a Russian company--which supplies materials to an Estonian enterprise--and an associated individual from the 22nd sanctions package, Kerstin Lepik, Spokesperson at the Permanent Representation of Estonia to the EU in Brussels, told the ERR national public broadcasting portal.
On October 7, a European source told TASS that EU ambassadors had agreed on the 22nd sanctions package, which will include over 1,500 Russian companies and individuals linked to the defense sector.
TASS has compiled the key details known about the approval process for the new sanctions package.
- EU ambassadors agreed on the 22nd sanctions package, a European source told TASS on October 7.
- According to the source, the package will include over 1,500 Russian companies and individuals linked to the defense sector.
- The source confirmed that the list includes "defense and other" companies and individuals from a number of countries. As the EU claims these companies "produce dual-use goods."
- This package does not include significant new trade or economic restrictions, but it will be the largest since the start of the special military operation in terms of the number of individuals and legal entities simultaneously added to the blacklist.
- To date, under the more than 20 sanctions packages adopted over the past four years, a total of just over 3,000 Russian enterprises and individuals have been included in the EU blacklist.
- The sanctions entail entry bans and asset freezes within the EU. For enterprises, this means asset freezes and a total ban on any joint activities involving EU residents.
- The 22nd package is expected to be approved by the EU Council and enter into force by the end of the week.
- According to Reuters, the new package will add 1,570 legal entities and individuals to the blacklist.
- This package will expand the sanctions list against Russia by nearly 50% but will not include other significant economic measures.
- Estonia has asked the EU to exclude one Russian company and an associated individual from the 22nd sanctions package, Kerstin Lepik, Spokesperson at the Permanent Representation of Estonia to the EU in Brussels, told the national broadcaster ERR.
- According to her, the company supplies materials of strategic importance for Europe to a company based in Estonia.
- Lepik stated that the Estonian company is seeking alternative sources for the materials it currently imports from Russia.
- Estonia will revisit the inclusion of this Russian company and the associated individual on the sanctions list next year, she added.
- Lithuanian authorities propose that the EU ban the transit of Russian food grain through the EU’s territory and impose sanctions on a number of individuals from Russia's agricultural sector, said Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius.

title: Agricultural trade turnover in EAEU up 20% in 7M 2026 — deputy minister
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. The trade volume of agricultural products and foods within the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) increased by 20% in January-July 2026, said Maxim Markovich, the Russian Deputy Minister of Agriculture.
The trade turnover of agricultural products and foods within the union grew by more than 20% in 2025, reaching approximately $18 bln.
"As for the current year, looking at the period from January to July of this year, we also observe a trade turnover growth of about 20%. It is seen that our trade is balanced," Markovich said.
Much attention is currently being paid to the development of such areas of agribusiness as breeding and seed production, increasing the productivity of the livestock sector, and boosting the production of goods with the high added value, the deputy minister said. "Fundamentally, this aligns closely with the areas having priority within the union and the potential cooperative projects that we will implement together," Markovich added.

title: Yemeni army recaptures strategically important area in country’s southwest from Houthis
body:
DOHA, October 8. /TASS/. Yemeni government forces have regained control of the strategically important mountainous area of Kahbub, located near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the Dar al-Watan ("Shield of the Homeland") unit said in a statement posted on its X account.
"The Dar al-Watan forces, the Amalika ("Giants Brigades") and the joint forces [of the Saudi-led coalition] have established full control over the front line in the Kahbub area as part of Operation Yemen’s Dawn," the statement said.
The armed confrontation between government forces and Houthi rebels has been continuing in Yemen since August 2014. The situation deteriorated dramatically this summer. In early August 2026, Ansar Allah launched an offensive in the country’s southwest and took control of the port city of Mokha and territories along the Bab al-Mandeb Strait in western Yemen on September 10-11. Government forces mounted several counterattacks near the strait in the following days. On October 4, government forces began a large-scale military operation to regain control of the country and regained control over Dhubab on October 5.

title: Talks between Tehran, Washington ongoing — Iranian foreign minister
body:
RABAT, October 8. /TASS/. Indirect dialogue between Iranian and US representatives is continuing, with the sides exchanging written messages, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said.
"The negotiating process is continuing, with the sides exchanging messages through intermediaries," the Iranian foreign minister said, as quoted by the Tasnim news agency. Araghchi added that Tehran had "put forward its proposal, the so-called seven-day plan, and Iranian representatives listened to the US side’s views on it."
"We are currently studying the US position, and I believe we will respond within the next few days," Iran’s foreign minister stressed.

title: Zelenskyy: Putin will come to negotiating table when Ukraine dominates the skies
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called on partners to help protect Ukrainian airspace, noting that if Ukraine dominates the skies, it could force Vladimir Putin to the negotiating table.

"We are talking about protection. The USA has the capability. It costs them nothing—absolutely nothing—to help Ukraine. And I say this frankly: help us protect the skies and dominate them. Then Putin will come to the negotiating table. Why? Because he would lose everything," Zelenskyy told reporters in Pryluky on Thursday.

According to the President, there is no need to wait for Chinese representatives to provide Russia with an alternative to Starlink.

He also reported that the Ukrainian side is working on new air defense packages.

"I don't want to go into details, but we know which countries possess these systems, and we have already identified them. I am personally working on this with our team, the government, the Foreign Ministry, and the Defense Ministry," he added.

title: Ukraine Codifies 310-km/h Drone Interceptor as Kyiv Expands Its Counter-Drone Arsenal
body:
Ukraine ’s Defense Ministry has codified the Blade interceptor drone , developed by Ukrainian defense-tech company Phantom Defense, clearing the system for procurement and delivery to the Defense Forces.
The company said the milestone moves the Blade from development and testing toward potential deployment with Ukraine’s military. However, codification does not indicate that the Defense Forces have already placed an order for a specific number of units or that large-scale deliveries have begun.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The Blade is designed to intercept fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles. It has a reported top speed of 310 km/h, an operating range of up to 30 kilometers and can carry a payload of up to 0.5 kilograms.
The interceptor is equipped with vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) capability, allowing it to operate from sites without prepared runways. Optical (daylight) and thermal imaging cameras are intended to enable operations around the clock.
The Blade is not designed as a standalone system. It forms part of Phantom Defense’s broader counter-UAV architecture, which combines detection systems, electronic warfare (EW), kinetic interceptors and software for situational awareness and battle management.
Under this model, a separate sensor can detect an aerial target and transmit information to the control system. Operators can then use electronic warfare or a kinetic interceptor such as the Blade, depending on the threat.
The system includes a ground control station for flight control, telemetry and video transmission. According to the company, the operator uses a portable workstation capable of operating for at least four hours without an external power source.
The company said the Blade will also become available for procurement through the government-backed Brave1 Market.
The codification comes as Ukraine rapidly expands the number of domestically developed unmanned systems cleared for military use.
As of July, the Defense Ministry had codified 413 unmanned aerial systems (UAS) since the beginning of 2026, according to the ministry. Almost all were Ukrainian-made.
The ministry said the number of codified UAS was more than 30% higher than during the same period in 2025 and more than 73% higher than in 2024.
The systems include reconnaissance, strike, FPV, bomber and interceptor drones, as well as signal-relay, target and fiber-optic-controlled systems.
Phantom Defense said it employs more than 850 people and operates production across nine facilities. The company claims an aggregate capacity of more than 100 interceptor drones and 200 EW systems per day, although it has not disclosed how much of that capacity is dedicated specifically to the Blade.
That distinction is important as Ukraine develops defenses against Russia’s large-scale use of strike drones. For interceptor systems, the ability to be produced and deployed in significant numbers can be as important as individual performance characteristics such as speed and range.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Oyo govt expresses relief as abducted corps members regain freedom in Imo
body:
The Oyo State Government has expressed relief over the release of corps members from the state who were abducted in Imo State, describing their freedom as a welcome development.
Commissioner for Information and Civic Orientation, Dotun Oyelade, stated this in a statement issued on Wednesday evening in Ibadan, the state capital, shortly after the report of the release of the 20 prospective corps members.
Mr Oyelade congratulated the Imo and Oyo state governments as well as the federal government on the successful release of the corps members after being held in captivity.
He, however, urged the federal government to intensify efforts to tackle the persistent challenge of kidnapping and banditry across the country.
According to him, the federal government, which has the greatest power and capacity to effectively address the insecurity crisis, must be more proactive and live up to its promise of making Nigerians safer.
The commissioner said the release of the corps members was a development worthy of commendation, while stressing that more needed to be done to prevent similar incidents.
MR Oyelade urged relevant security agencies to intensify intelligence gathering and coordinated operations to rescue those still in captivity and prevent further abductions.
He reiterated the Oyo State government’s commitment to the safety and welfare of its citizens, particularly youths serving the nation under the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) scheme.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) recalls that gunmen ‌‍⁠⁠⁠‍⁠⁠‌⁠⁠⁠‍⁠⁠‌on, 1 October, abducted the 20 prospective corps members, travelling from Ibadan, on the Onitsha-Owerri expressway in Imo State.

title: Crude Oil Production Has Risen To 1.8mb/d — Ojulari
body: State oil company, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited, Thursday said that crude oil production has risen to 1.8 million barrels per day in the last month. The development was revealed by the Group Chief Executive Officer, Bayo Ojulari, at the 2026 Association of Energy Correspondents of Nigeria (NAEC) Conference in Lagos. While speaking on behalf of Ojulari, Chief Communications Officer of the corporation, Andy Odeh, noted that Nigeria’s crude oil production rose to 1.821 million barrels per day (bpd), including condensates, reflecting improved regulations and upstream activities. According to Ojulari, the approach has helped to improve the operating environment and accelerate activities across the upstream sector. “Today, we are doing 1.821 million barrels per day,” he said. “The country has recorded more than 80 per cent success in its efforts to improve production.” The event was themed: ‘Access To Assets: Empowering Players & Driving Growth’. Ojulari’s confirmation of an improved oil production the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), production came few days after the Heineken Lokpobiri, on Tuesday in Abuja at the fifth anniversary commemoration of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), noted that the increase was driven by improved collaboration between the government and industry stakeholders, as well as efforts to remove bottlenecks that had slowed investment. Lokpobiri had also highlighted the increase in drilling activities, saying the number of active rigs had risen from fewer than 10 when the administration assumed office to more than 70 currently. He said sustained drilling activities were critical to increasing production and achieving Nigeria’s target of raising crude output to about three million bpd. According to him, Nigeria’s vast petroleum reserves would only translate into economic value if the government continued to create an enabling environment for investment and issued licences to investors with the requisite financial and technical capacity. Nigeria produced 1, 677,777 barrels of crude oil and condensate per day in the month of August 2026, representing an increase of 0.4 per cent when compared to the month of July. The post Crude Oil Production Has Risen To 1.8mb/d — Ojulari appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Russia's state arms firm puts Nerekhta-E ground robotic system up for sales globally
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Russia’s Rosoboronexport state arms exporter (part of the Rostec state corporation) is launching the Nerekhta-E ground robotic system, which can be used in both field and urban environments, onto the global market, the company reported.
"Rosoboronexport (part of the state corporation Rostec) is introducing the Nerekhta-E ground robotic system, developed and manufactured by the V.A. Degtyarev Plant, to the international market. "The system is designed to increase the effectiveness of combat missions and reduce personnel losses among frontline and reconnaissance units during combined-arms and counterterrorism operations. The system can be deployed in both field and urban environments," Rosoboronexport stated.
The company noted that the new ground robotic system’s armament allows it to engage ground and air targets, including armored vehicles, personnel, reinforced implacements, enemy air defense systems, aircraft, helicopters, and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).
Rosoboronexport CEO Alexander Mikheyev noted that the Nerekhta-E system was designed with modern combat concepts in mind, emphasizing reduced risks for operators, network-centricity, and the use of artificial intelligence. "The system has a number of unique advantages that have been proven in real-world conditions. First and foremost, these are modularity and versatility: depending on tactical requirements, the robot can be equipped with small-arms and grenade launcher modules or anti-tank weapons, and can perform tasks such as transporting the wounded or cargo weighing up to one metric ton," he said.
Rosoboronexport noted that the robot has an armored hull mounted on tracked chassis, and is equipped with a hybrid engine that allows it to reach a maximum speed of 20 km/h. The system can operate continuously for four hours while in motion, and in surveillance mode, it can operate for up to 20 hours.

title: Russia ready to further develop economic ties with Georgia — diplomat
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Moscow is ready to further develop economic relations with Tbilisi and strengthen friendship between the peoples of the two countries, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said at a briefing.
"We have extremely close ties with Georgia. We share a common history and traditions, including religious traditions that bring us together. We are also united by family ties and mutually beneficial cooperation," the diplomat noted, adding that significant progress had been made in trade and tourism in recent years.
"One in four tourists in Georgia comes from Russia. And our large market is the main destination for Georgia’s principal export products, which is also an extremely important factor. We are ready to further develop economic relations and strengthen friendship between our peoples," she said. "And, of course, it is impossible not to notice that the current situation is, you know, like a bone stuck in the throat of outside players seeking to drag Georgia into dangerous adventures of a Russophobic nature. And, in my opinion, Tbilisi has also repeatedly made it very clear, in no uncertain terms, that acting against their own national interests is not part of the Georgian people’s plans. In other words, acting contrary to the goals and objectives of their own development, acting to their own detriment, as they say," Zakharova added.
The diplomat noted that Russia understands Georgia’s efforts "to put up some kind of barrier, to erect an obstacle to these destructive external influences, while maintaining relations with foreign partners on the basis of equality and mutual respect."

title: China nominates health official Song Li to lead WHO
body:
China has nominated health official Song Li to lead the World Health Organization , a Foreign Ministry spokesperson said Thursday, as Beijing seeks to expand its presence in international governing bodies.
The World Health Assembly is set to elect the next WHO head in May. That person will succeed Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus , who is finishing his second five-year term and is barred from running again under WHO rules.
“China’s nomination of Dr. Song Li to run for the position reflects China’s willingness to work with all parties to jointly promote the building of a community of health for all humanity, and demonstrates China’s firm support for multilateralism and the WHO,” spokesperson Mao Ning said.
Song is a senior public health official who has played an active role in crises including the COVID-19 pandemic and SARS . Her areas of expertise include maternal and child healthcare policies and international cooperation, according to an official biography.
China has been seeking greater roles in United Nations institutions in recent years, just as the U.S. under President Donald Trump has pulled out of dozens of international and U.N. bodies.
Chinese nationals have led as many as four U.N. organizations simultaneously, but currently head only one. Qu Dongyu of China heads the Food and Agriculture Organization, based in Rome.
Other candidates for the WHO head position who have been officially announced include Dr. Hanan Mohammed Al-Kuwari of Qatar; Dr. Hanan Balkhy of Saudi Arabia; Dr. Hans Kluge of Belgium; Dr. María Neira of Spain; Indonesian candidate Budi Gunadi Sadikin; and Dr. Gevorg Tamamyan of Botswana.
The deadline for candidacies was Sept. 24, but countries can take time to publicly announce their hopefuls.
The WHO’s executive board, which meets in late January and early February, will winnow down the list to three candidates for consideration by member countries at the World Health Assembly in May, when the next director-general will be elected.

title: Banks to suspend lending to public sector workers under Controller and Accountant General’s payroll
body: Banks have begun moves to suspend lending to public sector workers under the Controller and Accountant-General’s (CAGD) payroll scheme. This has become necessary due to the growing non-performing loans in the banking industry. The Chief Executive of the Ghana Association of Banks, John Awuah, told Journalists at the Association’s Annual General Meeting that the rising default of public sector loans has become a challenge, hence the action. He, therefore, believes that this will impact on the lending rate going forward. According to him, the action follows a marching order to the banks from the Bank of Ghana Governor, Dr. Johnson Asiamah, to reduce non-performing loans to less than 10.0% by next year. “We have begun discussions and in the coming weeks and days we are going to take an action to suspend total lending to public sector workers under the Controller and Accountant Generals payroll. This is serious because we cannot continue to do this to the industry [banking] where salaries are being paid but our loan repayments are not remitted”. “We shall be forced to do this to save the industry and I can assure you that this time, we shall go ahead”, he added. Furthermore, Mr. Awuah said “we have had all the discussions and whatever we need to say has been said but still we don’t get the results. This action was supposed to happen three months ago but few people from higher offices intervene and we had to pause. This time in the next few days or weeks, you’re going to hear from us”, he pointed out. The Association has also been charged to partner the Bank of Ghana in developing a framework for the full implementation of the Lenders and Borrowers Act.

title: Mozambique invites Russia to take part in hydropower plant construction — ambassador
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Mozambique invites Russian companies to take part in construction of hydropower plants, Ambassador of Mozambique to Russia Jose Mateus Muaria Katupha told TASS.
Rosneft and Gazprom are already partnering with Mozambique in the oil and gas sphere, the ambassador said. They cooperate with the Mozambique’s national exploration company Empresa Nacional de Hidrocarbonetos (ENH).
"We look forward to having many more, especially in the area of production of fertilizers. And I know that the area that most Russian companies are interested in, this area of mining, mineral resources, and also in the area of reproduction of energy. And therefore, we are inviting Russian companies to participate in the process of building hydropower energy in Mozambique," he stressed.

title: UK imposes new sanctions on Russia’s oil, shadow fleet, war supply chains
body:
The UK Foreign Office said this in a statement , Ukrinform reports.
The sanctions target 38 legal entities and individuals. In particular, restrictions were imposed on Russian oil companies Zarubezhneft and INK Capital. The UK Foreign Office said Britain had become the first G7 country to impose sanctions on Russia’s four largest oil companies. The latest measures mean that UK sanctions now cover more than 90% of Russia’s oil production capacity.
In addition, 12 more oil tankers were added to the sanctions list, bringing the total number of vessels from Russia’s shadow fleet under UK sanctions to more than 600. According to the Foreign Office, these vessels are used to circumvent sanctions and transport Russian oil, including through deceptive practices and the use of false flags.
The Foreign Office noted that the new sanctions target not only vessels already at sea but also those facilitating the supply chain used to transport Russian oil around the world.
Another 17 legal entities and individuals were sanctioned for supplying Russia with so-called Common High Priority goods. These include machine tools, electronics and materials needed to manufacture ballistic missiles, drones and other military equipment. According to the UK Foreign Office, Russia obtains some of these goods through third countries. The ministry said it was identifying those involved and taking appropriate action against them.
The UK also imposed sanctions on three cryptocurrency exchanges, two payment platforms and a related individual suspected of helping Russia circumvent financial restrictions. According to the Foreign Office, two of these entities processed transactions through the A7 financial network, which is backed by the Kremlin. Last year, it reported processing more than $90 billion in transfers.
“The message is simple: if you help Russia fund or equip this war, you will face the consequences… By sanctioning these companies, we’re not only stemming the flow of Russian oil money, but cutting off the routes used to circumvent our sanctions regime by making it harder for major Russian oil companies to rebadge their oil under the name of an unsanctioned entity,” the UK Foreign Office said.
As reported by Ukrinform, on October 1, the United Kingdom announced a new sweeping package of sanctions against Russia aimed at weakening the Kremlin’s war budget, countering propaganda, and holding accountable those involved in the torture of Ukrainian civilians and the deportation of children.

title: Arctic emergency rescue centers may become base for future bio-ecological settlements
body:
GELENDZHIK /Krasnodar Region/, October 8. /TASS/. Bio-ecological settlements, due to be developed in a number of Russian territories, may be based on a network of Arctic integrated emergency rescue centers of the Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations that already cover the Arctic regions, Acting Head of the Research Institute for Advanced Research and Innovative Life Safety Technologies at the Ministry of Emergency Situations' St. Petersburg University Sergey Ivakhnyuk told the 3rd International Bioprom Forum.
"We propose to eye bio-settlements not just as autonomous residential clusters, but rather as key elements of a risk management system and an integral part of the Russian Emergency Situations Ministry's infrastructure," he said. "This system may be based on the existing network of Arctic integrated emergency rescue centers, which already covers key logistics routes and most important territories of the Arctic Zone. Bio-settlements will act as a risk management framework."
In order to implement this approach, it is necessary to move forward from separate centers to their distributed network as outposts, he continued.
"This is a modular, autonomous solution that, first of all, ensures the settlement's safety, while it is located in the transport accessibility zone off the central hub, serves as its outpost and an additional base for deploying forces and assets in a remote area," he said.
The ministry's reference point in a bio-settlement will become not just a station on duty, but will act as a training ground in Arctic conditions, thus specialists will be able to train personnel right on the spot. Additionally, such a system offers an option to develop the institute of volunteers, involving local residents, and to carry out scientific research.
The project was supported by Mikhail Kovalchuk, President of the Kurchatov Institute National Research Center, who noted it was quite promising given the Northern Sea Route development. However, he suggested to eye the existing settlements along the Northern Sea Route, many of which are currently abandoned. They could be developed to create outposts, since they still have infrastructures. In his opinion, it would be easier to restore such settlements and create bio-ecological settlements on their basis.
The 3rd International Bioprom Forum ran in the Krasnodar Region's Gelendzhik on October 5-6. About 100 companies presented their achievements in biotechnology at the exhibition space of 7,500 square meters.

title: Kyrgyzstan Public Debt Exceeds $10 Billion as Repayment Costs Rise
body: Kyrgyzstan’s public debt reached $10.16 billion by the end of July 2026, with the government expecting to spend about $1.83 billion servicing its external debt between 2027 and 2029. According to Ministry of Finance figures, external debt stood at $5.19 billion as of July 31, while domestic debt totaled $4.96 billion. External borrowing consists mainly of loans from foreign governments and international financial institutions, while domestic debt is raised primarily through government bonds. Total debt was equivalent to about 38% of the government’s projected gross domestic product (GDP) for 2026. At the end of 2025, the debt-to-GDP ratio stood at 39.5%, up from 36.2% a year earlier. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) expects the ratio to reach 41.4% by the end of 2026 . The country’s debt burden is relatively high compared with those of its Central Asian neighbors. IMF figures put Kazakhstan’s public debt at 25.2% of GDP in 2025 , while the equivalent figures were 28.6% for Uzbekistan and a projected 24.7% for Tajikistan . For comparison, United States government debt stood at 123.9% of GDP in 2025 . China remains Kyrgyzstan’s largest foreign creditor . According to Deputy Finance Minister Umutjan Amanbaev, Bishkek owes Beijing about $1.4 billion, equivalent to 27% of its external debt. Much of the remainder is owed to international development banks and financial institutions. Most external loans were obtained on concessional terms, generally carrying low interest rates and long repayment periods. However, the country has also begun taking on more expensive commercial debt. In May 2025, the government issued its first sovereign Eurobonds , raising $700 million through five-year notes carrying an annual interest rate of 7.75%. The bonds, placed on the London Stock Exchange, now account for about 13.5% of external debt. They are due to mature in 2030, when external debt repayments are projected to reach about $1.1 billion , based on the repayment schedule for existing obligations. The draft budget for 2027–2029 , published by the Ministry of Finance, allocates about $606 million to external debt servicing in 2027, $600 million in 2028, and $621 million in 2029. These payments cover principal and interest on existing debt. More than 80% are denominated in U.S. dollars, so a weaker som could increase the budget cost of meeting the same obligations. The government also expects to spend 82.2 billion soms servicing domestic debt. Public debt remains below the government’s benchmark of 70% of GDP. The Ministry of Finance expects debt sustainability to be maintained over the medium term, although exchange-rate fluctuations and economic shocks remain significant risks. The IMF also considers the debt sustainable, while assessing its risk of debt distress as moderate . However, it has warned that growing repayment costs, particularly on domestic and non-concessional borrowing, could place increasing pressure on public finances.

title: Northern Stakeholders Support ACReSAL’s $500m Additional Financing
body: Linus Aleke in Abuja The proposed $500 million additional financing for the Agro-Climatic Resilience in Semi-Arid Landscapes (ACReSAL) project has received broad support from stakeholders across northern Nigeria, according to the Think Nigeria First Initiative (TNFI). Speaking during a press conference in Abuja, the Director General of TNFI, Alhaji Abubakar Tsanni, said governors, traditional rulers, farmers, herders and women’s groups had thrown their weight behind the next phase of the project because of the tangible results recorded in their communities. Tsanni identified the governors of Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Kebbi, Kaduna, Jigawa, Benue and Plateau States as among those who had personally inaugurated, inspected or flagged off ACReSAL interventions. He added that Bauchi State had publicly committed its counterpart funding to the proposed next phase. “Traditional institutions, including the palaces of the Shehu of Borno, Emir of Argungu and Emir of Zazzau, work hand-in-hand with the project. In Wurno, a farmer of 27 years on the irrigation scheme says hope has returned. In Nguru, herders and fishermen have returned to a wetland that was dry for 12 years,” Tsanni said. According to him, women account for 47 per cent of the project’s 4.4 million direct beneficiaries, while university students in Kogi, Kebbi and Plateau States are being trained in modern greenhouse farming on their campuses. He further said the Federal Ministers of Environment, Water Resources and Agriculture had jointly participated in the project’s mid-term review in Kaduna. Tsanni maintained that stakeholders were not seeking charity, but sustainable financing built around continuity, shared responsibility and self-reliance. He disclosed that participating states had so far released N22 billion in counterpart funding, while the $9.5 million Community Revolving Fund disbursed to 381 communities was being repaid and re-lent. He also noted that Benue and Nasarawa States had established state agencies to ensure the sustainability of the project’s assets. The TNFI Director General therefore urged governors, traditional rulers, legislators and community leaders across the north who had witnessed the impact of ACReSAL to “say so publicly, and say so now”. He also called on the Federal Government and the World Bank to conclude the financing arrangement without further delay.

title: US military prepares new options for operations in Iran — media
body:
NEW YORK, October 8. /TASS/. The US military has prepared new options for military operations in Iran for President Donald Trump to consider, NBC News reported, citing sources.
Members of Trump’s national security team discussed US strategy toward Iran and Yemen’s Houthi rebels at a meeting at Camp David last week, according to the report. The military subsequently prepared new options for operations in Iran. No decisions have been made, the sources said.
The Atlantic magazine earlier reported, citing sources, that the White House had instructed the Pentagon to develop options for strikes on Iranian targets that could be carried out before the congressional midterm elections. According to the report, no final decision has been made, but Trump could order strikes before Election Day. The scale and targets of any potential strikes, as well as whether to proceed with them, remain under discussion.

title: Veteran communication scholar Idowu Sobowale dies at 85
body: LAGOS — Professor Idowu Akanbi Sobowale, a renowned communication scholar and veteran member of Nigeria’s media and communication community, has died at the age of 85. Sobowale died on Thursday morning, October 8, 2026, according to a statement by a member of his family, Akinniyi Sowunmi. Sowunmi announced the death in a statement titled, “Transition to Glory,” describing the deceased as a major loss to Nigeria’s communication community, particularly members of the Association of Communication Scholars and Professionals in Nigeria, ACSPN. The statement read in part: “This is a very sad day for us in the Communication Community in Nigeria and especially for us at the Association of Communication Scholars & Professionals in Nigeria. “Our father, Pa Deacon Professor Idowu Akanbi Sobowale, OON, 85, joined the saints triumphant this morning, October 8, 2026.” The family said details of the funeral arrangements would be announced later. Sobowale’s death comes as a loss to Nigeria’s communication and media community, where he was recognised as a veteran scholar and member of the professional community. title: Gazprom's satellites fully serve company's communication in Arctic
body:
ST. PETERSBURG, October 8. /TASS/. The Gazprom Space Systems Company uses three satellites to provide seamlessly a complete communication area for Gazprom companies in the Arctic, the company's First Deputy CEO Pyotr Korviakov said at the OMR 2026 conference.
"Gazprom Space Systems has organized services in the Arctic Region, including along the Northern Sea Route and areas adjacent to the Trans-Arctic Region, where we are using three satellites that form a complete service area for this region and, accordingly, allow for efficient operation with all facilities, both marine and ground infrastructure facilities that ensure the transport corridor's operation, including in the seamless mode," he said.
For this purpose, we have organized a ground-based infrastructure of several control stations and we have a special resource to support this system's operation, he added.
Gazprom's satellites ensure stable communications across the company's entire infrastructure in the Arctic, as well as at other facilities up to Spitsbergen, he said.
Gazprom Space Systems is Gazprom's subsidiary operating in telecommunication and geo-information systems in the interests of the Gazprom Group of Companies and other clients. Gazprom Space Systems has created, operates and develops the Yamal Satellite Communications and Broadcasting System, develops the Smotr Aerospace Monitoring System, and provides telecommunications and geo-information services.

title: Lagos Life game is valued at $1bn — Creator, Shalom Rayhamen
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigerian software developer and creator of the viral Nigerian browser game Lagos Life, Shalom Rayhamen, has said the game is valued at $1 billion, dismissing a reported $100,000 offer for the game as too small. Rayhamen made the disclosure in an interview with Nigerian digital content creator Fisayo Fosudo, shared on his Youtube page on Wednesday. When asked what she thought about people online offering $100,000 to buy Lagos Life and whether she was willing to sell, Rayhamen said the amount was far below the value she places on the game. She said: “A $100,000 is small. Lagos Life is valued at $1 billion, so if they want to buy, they should talk $1 billion. What is a $100,000? I don’t want to say we’ve, like… or something, but what is that?” Lagos Life has become one of the most talked-about Nigerian-made digital games since its launch on October 1, 2026. The browser-based life simulation game allows players to create characters, take jobs, earn virtual naira, rent homes, socialise and explore locations inspired by Lagos. The game is essentially a Lagos-themed take on the life-simulation concept popularised by games such as The Sims, but its appeal comes from its use of familiar Nigerian experiences, locations and culture. Players can navigate different aspects of virtual Lagos, including employment, money, housing, entertainment and social activities. Among the locations featured in the game are Amala Shitta and Quilox, while its wider gameplay draws on familiar Lagos experiences such as transportation, nightlife and food. Lagos Life does not require users to download an application, as it can be played directly through a web browser on phones and computers. The game’s rapid growth has also attracted attention from businesses, with virtual advertising spaces providing a potential commercial model for the platform. However, the money used within the game has no real-world cash value. Players cannot withdraw the virtual naira or convert it into real money. Rayhamen’s $1 billion valuation comes as interest in the game continues to grow, following its rapid rise across social media and its large player base. The game’s success has also placed Nigerian-made browser games in the spotlight, following the viral attention received by Lagos Run, another locally themed game built around the experience of driving a danfo through Lagos. title: I paid N6m for my son’s release, mother of freed NYSC member
body: A mother of one of the freed members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) says she paid N6 million ransom to secure her son’s release. Recall the prospective corps members were abducted on October 1 after gunmen attacked two 18-seater buses travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, along the Owerri-Onitsha expressway. The woman disclosed this in an interview with News Central Television on Wednesday, saying the kidnappers initially demanded N50 million for each victim before eventually accepting N6 million for her son. “Initially, they asked us to pay N50 million per head. We asked whether the amount was for all of them, but they insisted that no, it was for each person. Later, we started begging them to take N500,000. But they said no and started scaring us,” she said in Yoruba. “Three days ago, they called and said we should pay N15 million. We kept begging them that all we had was N5.5 million. They said no and insisted on N6 million. So, it’s that N6 million we paid.” The woman said the abductors asked the parents of the victims to send representatives to meet them in Ibadan as part of arrangements for the ransom payment. “They called all the parents of all the victims. Twenty of them are in the bush. They then asked us to send three persons each to meet with them in Ibadan. My husband and my son’s elder brother went. “When they got to the meeting place, they asked them to send the money to an account and that when they got to Imo state, they should change the money into dollars.” She said her elder son was among those who met the abductors and delivered the ransom. “It is not rumours. They have all been released and sent to us. His brother is among the people who went to meet with the abductors three days ago. They left with the ransom,” she said. “It was the brother who called us this evening to say that they had handed the ransom to the kidnappers and that they had released our son. We also spoke to the boy.” The mother, whose name was not disclosed, said the abduction left her traumatised and unable to sleep throughout the period her son was held captive. “Since he was kidnapped, I have been stooling. I couldn’t sleep either. But I was relieved when I heard they had been released. It was as though the chains all over me were loosened,” she said. title: Kazakhstan Signs Declaration on Human Oversight of AI at Work
body: Kazakhstan’s government, employers, and trade unions signed a declaration on October 7 calling for human oversight of artificial intelligence in the workplace. The declaration was adopted in Astana at the international forum “Digital Labor and Artificial Intelligence.” It states that decisions affecting workers’ rights and interests should involve a human decision-maker rather than be left entirely to AI. Federation of Trade Unions chairman Satybaldy Dauletalin said employers should remain accountable for decisions made using algorithms . Workers should be able to challenge those decisions and request human review, he said. The federation said the signatories agreed to establish a national forum for cooperation on digital labor and AI. Working groups and a monitoring system would support implementation. Some protections already exist under Kazakh law. The country’s AI legislation , which took effect in January 2026, establishes requirements for transparency and human autonomy in AI systems. The Digital Code , effective since July, also gives people the right, under certain conditions, to seek explanations of fully automated decisions and request human review when those decisions affect their rights. The European Union’s 2024 Platform Work Directive sets specific requirements for algorithmic management on digital labor platforms. It requires human oversight of automated systems, including human decisions on the dismissal or suspension of workers. Member states have until December 2026 to implement the directive. Meanwhile, Kazakhstan is already using AI in its public employment services. In the Mangystau and Pavlodar regions, an automated job-matching system sent approximately 59,000 personalized vacancy notifications over two months. Deputy Labor Minister Bakhtiyar Zhazykpayev said about 3,000 people had found employment. Those figures alone do not establish how many found work directly because of the system. The federation’s published account does not explain whether the declaration creates additional enforceable obligations for employers or a new complaints procedure for workers.

title: First Arctic scientific online quiz extended to late November
body:
ARKHANGELSK, October 8. /TASS/. The Arctic: Test Yourself quiz will run online to November 30, the project curator, head of the department for coordinating work of young scientists, specialists and research students at the Northern Arctic Federal University (NArFU) Svetlana Kartseva told TASS. The project participants are invited to answer 20 questions of various difficulty levels about the Arctic.
"The scientific quiz includes solving online tests with closed-ended questions at different levels of difficulty: for school, secondary and higher educational institutions students; for graduate students and young scientists. Anyone may take part in it," she said. "We have extended the project to November 30."
The questions cover topics of nature, climate, the Arctic exploration history, indigenous peoples, current scientific discoveries, and others. Those who complete the quiz, receive personalized electronic certificates. The project's objectives are to promote knowledge about the Arctic as a strategically important region of the Russian Federation; to involve young people in science; and to exchange knowledge and experience about Arctic research.
The project's partners are: the Arkhangelsk Region's Ministry of Education, Ministry of Science, Higher Education and Scientific and Technological Development; the Solovetsky State Historical, Architectural and Natural Museum-Reserve; the Russian Arctic National Park; and the Kenozersky National Park.
More than 9,000 people from across Russia and from more than 20 countries have completed the quiz. The project's offline stage was on October 2. It was attended by about 60 people. The offline stage in Arkhangelsk was part of the national Polyus Forum of Young Scientists.

title: Russia to continue identifying true culprits behind Nord Stream sabotage — diplomat
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Russia intends to continue its efforts on international platforms to identify and punish those truly responsible for organizing the sabotage of the Nord Stream pipelines, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said at a briefing.
"For our part, we will consistently continue our efforts, including on international platforms, to identify and punish not only those who carried out this unprecedented terrorist attack, but also its true masterminds," the diplomat said.
The Foreign Ministry spokeswoman pointed out that European countries that suffered losses from the pipeline explosions had hastily blocked and terminated their national investigations. Only in Germany are law enforcement and judicial authorities continuing to pursue the case, albeit in a highly peculiar manner. According to Zakharova, the Hamburg Higher Regional Court recently refused to allow the Nord Stream operators to participate in the proceedings concerning the pipeline explosions. "Moreover, the court concluded that the damage inflicted on the companies’ interests was not existential, that they could defend their economic interests through civil proceedings, and that they did not require special protection during the criminal hearings scheduled for mid-October," she added.
Zakharova went on to say that a press release issued by the Hamburg court in this connection indicated that the proceedings were limited to determining the degree of culpability of the sole defendant, a certain Sergey K., in complicity in a war crime involving prohibited methods of warfare and an attack on a civilian facility. "Everything else, including a comprehensive examination of the circumstances of the case, falls outside the scope of the hearings," she stated. "It turns out that they are interested only in how this defendant physically committed his crime, while the fact previously established by Germany’s Federal Prosecutor’s Office that he was acting on instructions from Ukrainian government agencies remains outside the purview of the German judiciary."
"We are not surprised by this turn of events. In four years, Germany’s much-vaunted 'impartial' and 'independent' judiciary has shown no interest whatsoever in identifying and bringing to justice the true instigators and masterminds of this terrorist attack. Now the German judicial authorities have also joined efforts to cover up the truth, apparently unwilling to expose the ideological architects of the pipeline explosions, including those based in Ukraine, which the German authorities continue to support with unwavering determination," Zakharova stressed.

title: Russia to give swift response to any unfriendly steps by NATO — representative to OSCE
body:
VIENNA, October 8. /TASS/. Moscow will not wait to respond to any unfriendly actions taken by NATO, said Russia’s Permanent Representative to the OSCE Dmitry Polyansky.
The diplomat said that Russia "does not threaten anyone and has no intention of attacking anyone." However, it "cannot ignore NATO’s development of plans for a direct military confrontation with Russia, or the alliance’s modeling of scenarios involving a military-political blockade of the Kaliningrad Region. Our response to any unfriendly actions will not be long in coming," he told the OSCE Permanent Council.
TASS received a text copy of Polyansky’s speech.
The diplomat also urged Russia’s opponents not to test its patience and not to bring the entire European "continent to the point of no return."

title: Zelenskyy: Russian strike on Kramatorsk won’t go unanswered
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that the Russian strike on Kramatorsk, which killed at least 30 people and injured another 18, would not go unanswered by Ukraine.

"Doctors are now fighting to save the lives of people injured in the Russian strike on Kramatorsk. As of now, 30 people have been confirmed killed, and sadly, that number may rise," Zelenskyy wrote in a post published on Facebook on Thursday.



According to him, a Russian bomb struck two commuter buses. Some of the victims have not yet been identified due to the severity of their injuries.

Zelenskyy noted that a total of 18 people were injured in the strike. Residential buildings and vehicles were also damaged.

"This strike will not go unanswered. Russia is trying to destroy all life in Donbas, and a response from the world is a must. A forceful response – exactly as the Russians deserve for all the deaths they have brought. May all those killed rest in peace," the president emphasized.

title: Umahi dismisses rift with Wike, says ‘we’re one family’
body: Minister of Works, Dave Umahi, has dismissed reports of a strained relationship between him and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, describing the former Rivers State governor as a progressive politician and member of the same political family. Umahi spoke at a press conference in Abuja on Wednesday while reacting to reports of divisions within the All Progressives Congress and speculation over his relationship with Wike. The minister said there was no basis for the reports of a rift, insisting that both men remained connected by their shared political interests. “We need Wike as Wike needs us. So, it’s one family,” Umahi said. He said political differences between him and the FCT minister had been exaggerated by their opponents, stressing that their relationship remained cordial. Umahi also urged politicians to focus on national development rather than allow political disagreements to create divisions among people who share common interests. Wike, who remains a member of the Peoples Democratic Party, has continued to maintain his political relevance while backing President Bola Tinubu’s administration. In January, the FCT minister said his rainbow coalition represented a departure from conventional party politics, describing it as a collective political movement aimed at advancing the interests of Rivers State. His position has, however, come amid concerns within the ruling APC over political alliances that could affect Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. The Progressive Governors Forum has said it would not support any alliance or political arrangement capable of undermining Tinubu’s re-election or the electoral prospects of APC candidates in the 2027 elections. Despite the concerns surrounding political alignments ahead of the 2027 elections, Umahi maintained that his relationship with Wike was not defined by the differences being portrayed by their political opponents. He reiterated that both men remained part of the same political family and should be viewed within the broader context of their shared commitment to national development. title: B.C. Conservatives back in battleground Surrey on election trail
body:
The B.C. Conservatives will spend their second consecutive day campaigning in Surrey, a critical battleground in the provincial election.
The Conservatives say interim leader Lorne Doerkson will be in Surrey to make a policy announcement a day after being in the city to roll out promises for businesses that include eliminating the PST on some equipment.
Surrey is British Columbia’s second-largest municipality and includes 10 of the 93 electoral ridings that are up for grabs when voters go to the polls on Oct. 24.
The region was in the election spotlight in 2024 when Garry Begg won Surrey-Guildford by just 22 votes, securing a one-seat majority in the legislature for the NDP.
NDP Leader David Eby was in Surrey on Wednesday to roll out promises including loans of up to $1 million for small and medium-sized businesses affected by tariffs.
The Conservatives won six of Surrey’s 10 seats in 2024, though one of those legislators, Elenore Sturko, is now on the ballot as leader of the rival CentreBC party.

title: Western intel agencies could use Armenian data center against Russia — official
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. The new data center set up in Armenia could be used in the interests of Western intelligence agencies against Russia, Iran and other countries, Russian Security Council Deputy Secretary Alexey Shevtsov warned.
"Such centers can be used for intelligence activities and analysis in the interests of Western intelligence agencies, particularly against Iran, Russia and the countries of the South Caucasus and Central Asia," he told reporters, commenting on the early August launch of the Firebird AI company’s artificial intelligence data center in the Armenian city of Hrazdan, running on NVIDIA processors.
According to the Russian Security Council deputy secretary, "since the Firebird company is subject to American laws, US intelligence agencies will have access to all of the data processed on its servers." "That means that Armenian government agencies’ data will be available to the United States without the consent of the Armenian authorities," Shevtsov noted.
Armenia doesn't need the data center at all, he emphasised. According to him, "an OVIO data center, belonging to [the Russian provider] Rostelecom has been operating in the country since 2024, which fully covers the needs of commercial and government structures in terms of data storage."
Shevtsov mentioned Firebird’s plans to increase the Hrazdan facility’s capacity to 300 MW by the end of 2027, which "is almost a quarter of Armenia’s winter peak energy load (1.3 GW)." "That said, given these plans, additional energy capacities will be required to keep the center operational," the Russian Security Council deputy secretary stressed. In his view, "Armenia risks facing a major power shortage that will inevitably affect the country’s people."

title: Jackie Chan Highlights Kazakhstan’s Film Potential After ‘Armour of God IV: Ultimatum’ Shoot
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – Filming of the international action film “ Armour of God IV: Ultimatum ,” starring legendary actor Jackie Chan, has concluded in Kazakhstan, showcasing the country’s potential as a destination for major international film productions. Photo credit: Salem Social Media The project, Salem Entertainment’s first international production, was filmed in Almaty and the Almaty and Mangystau Regions, with support from Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Culture and Information and China Film Group Corporation. Photo credit: Ministry of Culture and Information. Speaking at a press conference on Oct. 6, Chan said the idea was first discussed during a meeting with Kazakhstan’s Vice President Erlan Karin in China in 2017 or 2018, when Karin served as State Counselor, Kazinform reported. “I was surprised that the team had already started working on the script and selected a director,” Chan said, noting that the project moved from an initial proposal to production much faster than he had expected. He also praised the shoot’s organization and government support. Kazakh actor and producer Rustem Omarov said Chan sustained a shoulder injury and later fractured a rib during filming. Despite doctors advising him to rest, Chan returned to the set within days. Filming will continue in Shanghai, with the film scheduled for international release in 2027. The project is expected to promote Kazakhstan’s tourism and cultural potential and help attract further international film productions to the country. title: Boy George announces second concert in Israel dedicated to Nova music festival survivors
body: International pop icon Boy George has announced a second concert in Israel titled “We Will Dance Again,” with the entire evening dedicated to the survivors and families of the Nova music festival.The announcement for the November 7 concert comes on the heels of a rapid sell-out of his first scheduled performance on November 4.The British singer-songwriter, who skyrocketed to global fame in the 1980s as the frontman of Culture Club, is expanding his upcoming visit to double down on his public solidarity with the victims of the October 7 tragedy.The performance is a live extension of a tribute Boy George initiated earlier this year. title: Drone attack forces Yandex to shut down its data center on the grounds of a sanctioned Russian machine-tool plant
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); A drone attack overnight on 8 October caused a fire that hit part of Yandex's data center in Sasovo, Ryazan Oblast, about 580 km from Ukraine, and the site is fully stopped, the Russian tech company told Russian media. The data center sits on the grounds of Sasta, a sanctioned machine-tool plant, Russian outlet Astra said , citing Wikimapia data. Astra's OSINT analyst found from eyewitness footage that the fire hit the plant. Since late September, Russia has been striking data centers in Kyiv that keep Ukraine's internet and online services running. Now a drone attack has stopped one of the data centers that Russia's largest tech company relies on. Fires reported at a refinery in Salavat and a machine-tool plant in Sasovo after overnight attacks on 8 October 2026. Map: Euromaidan Press Yandex counts the damage Yandex warned that some services may be unavailable, while its core services kept running and no one was hurt. Ryazan Oblast Governor Pavel Malkov claimed two drones were downed, a roof caught fire at an enterprise in the Sasovo district, and windows were blown out in several homes. The power failure took down a wide range of Yandex Cloud infrastructure, including computing capacity, networks, data storage, databases, Kubernetes, cloud services, AI, and security and monitoring systems, Ukrainian outlet ZN.ua reported , citing Exilenova+. Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+ reported that the plant was hit, without naming an attacker. The channel said Sasta, which claims a place on Russia's register of defense-industry companies, makes computer-controlled machine tools, including five-axis machining centers, and previously supplied the Tactical Missiles Corporation (KTRV) and Roscosmos. The plant's value to the arms industry lies in machines that cut precision parts, not in finished weapons, the channel said. Citing Exilenova+, Militarnyi reported that Ukraine's Defense Forces hit the plant. It also linked Sasta to Iskander missile supply chains. No source has said whether the plant or the data center was the target, and no Ukrainian official has claimed the Sasovo strike. Sasta has been under US sanctions since November 2023, UK sanctions since February 2024, and Ukrainian sanctions since April 2025, a sanctions database shows. Salavat: Kyiv reports a hit Ukrainian forces hit the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat complex in Bashkortostan, about 1,380 km from the front line, causing a fire, Ukraine's General Staff said . It said the complex processes up to 10 million metric tons of hydrocarbons a year and serves Russia's armed forces. Its key unit, the ELOU-AVT-6 primary oil refining unit launched in 2012, can process 6 million metric tons a year, Militarnyi reported . Astra's analyst placed the fire a few kilometers outside Salavat, possibly near the refinery. Salavat oil refinery moment of attack pic.twitter.com/bUxuRshSK1 — Exilenova+ (@Exilenova_plus) October 8, 2026 Salavat Mayor Marat Zagidullin claimed that debris from several drones fell in the industrial zone that morning and started a fire. "The enterprise continues to work," he said. Astra noted earlier hits on the complex on 24 September 2025, on 14 July 2026, when refining fully stopped, and on 13 August 2026. Russia's strikes on Ukraine's data centers Russia has repeatedly hit data centers in Kyiv since 23 September. Strikes hit the COSMONOVA data center twice, the second time knocking it out, and the Parkovyi data center stopped working completely on 1 October after a series of strikes. In early October, Russia destroyed the dline.ua data center in Kyiv.
