title: Pentagon Adds 1,320 Ukrainian F10 Drones to Drone Dominance Order
body:
The US military has ordered 1,320 more F10 strike drones from Ukraine’s F-Drones, extending the first commercial supply of Ukrainian-made combat drones to the Pentagon, Militarnyi reported.
F-Drones told the outlet the drones were ordered under Drone Dominance, a US Department of Defense program worth $1 billion. The program aims to buy small strike drones over the next two years, with plans to acquire more than 200,000 units by 2027.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
According to Militarnyi , the F10 was the first Ukrainian drone to receive official permission to be exported to the US. UDD Tech Corp represents F-Drones on the American market.
By the size of its additional order, F-Drones ranks second among participants in the program’s first phase, the company said. The new order follows a first batch of 2,000 F10 drones, which the US military ordered under the same program and was shipped to the Pentagon in July.
If delivered as planned, the two orders would bring a total of 3,320 drones.
F-Drones must deliver the new batch by the end of November, as the company expects to receive a Ukrainian export permit in time to meet that deadline.
F-Drones also told Militarnyi its production capacity allows it to fill the extra order without disrupting supplies to the front. According to F-Drones CEO Stanislav Khutor, Ukrainian defenders are receiving the company’s drones on time and in full.
In July , Ukraine’s State Export Control Service had issued the country’s first official permit for the export of finished combat drones.
Olena Hrazhdan is the Business Reporter at Kyiv Post, covering Ukraine’s markets, business, and economic policy. While she reports broadly on economic issues, her core focus is banking, finance, monetary and fiscal policy. Olena previously wrote for leading Ukrainian business media and became a Fellow of the International Monetary Fund’s Journalism Fellowship in 2024.

title: Viral video: FCT CP orders probe into N450,000 demand
body: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The Commissioner of Police, FCT Command, CP Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi, has ordered an investigation into allegations that police investigators demanded N450,000 from a content creator before investigating a complaint he brought to the command. The allegation was contained in a video circulating on social media in which the content creator, identified as Tumma Gabriel, claimed that officers at the FCT Police Command Criminal Investigation Department demanded the money as “mobilisation and petition.” The command’s Police Public Relations Officer, SP Josephine Adeh, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday. Adeh said the FCT Police Command was aware of the video and stressed that the police did not mandate or encourage its officers to solicit or demand any form of payment before, during or after investigations. “The Command wishes to state clearly that it does not mandate or encourage its officers to solicit or demand any form of remuneration before, during, or after investigations,” she said. She said the Commissioner of Police had consequently ordered a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the allegation and identify any officer who might be involved. “Any person found liable will be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of the Police Act and Regulations,” Adeh added. The command also urged the complainant to contact it through 08180382808 and visit the Command Headquarters to assist the investigation by providing relevant information that could help identify the officer or officers involved. The police said the investigation was aimed at establishing the facts surrounding the allegation and taking appropriate action where wrongdoing was established. The post Viral video: FCT CP orders probe into N450,000 demand appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: GAUA strike leaves some KNUST administrative offices operating below capacity
body: The ongoing strike by the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) has begun to disrupt administrative services at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), with some students and national service personnel being asked to return at a later date to access services. Some offices, including those responsible for payroll and auditing, have been affected by the strike, while key student-facing units such as the Finance, Registry and Examinations offices remain open, albeit with reduced operational capacity. One of those affected by the disruption told JoyNews on Thursday, 8 October, that she had travelled to the university to have her National Service Scheme (NSS) documentation endorsed but was informed upon arrival that she would have to return later. The delay, he explained, could have financial implications for her because she had travelled to the university without making adequate preparations for a longer wait. She expressed hope that the industrial action would be resolved soon to enable affected personnel to return to work. “I hope that they call it off so that we can resume working.” KNUST GAUA chapter defends strike action The KNUST chapter of GAUA has defended the industrial action, stressing that the association’s members have a right to strike in pursuit of their demands. Speaking on the impact of the strike, the chapter’s General Secretary, Kwadwo Asenso Fanwel, said the association was mindful of the need to maintain its professional and ethical responsibilities even while participating in the industrial action. “We have clearly indicated that a strike is a right of every association or a grouping to press on their demand,” he said. Mr Asenso Fanwel, however, emphasised that GAUA members were not deliberately seeking to sabotage university operations. He explained that the disruption arising from the strike should be understood as passive rather than active. “The disruption here in this case will be passive. We are not going to cause any active disruption, but by virtue of the fact that our people are not going to be in the office to put back services, that is where the effect will be felt,” he explained. Strike intended to demonstrate importance of administrators Mr Asenso Fanwel also acknowledged that the effectiveness of industrial action depends partly on its ability to demonstrate the importance of the workers involved. He said GAUA believed the absence of administrators from their posts would highlight the essential role they play in keeping university systems and services running. For now, the KNUST situation demonstrates the wider role played by university administrators in ensuring that academic institutions function smoothly, even when their work is largely behind the scenes.

title: Jerusalem pharmacy student indicted for plotting mass-casualty attack using poison
body: The State Attorney's Office filed an indictment on Thursday against a 22-year-old pharmacy student from east Jerusalem for allegedly planning a series of terrorist attacks using poisons and explosives against Jewish civilians and security forces.The plans, according to prosecutors, were intended to cause mass casualties and followed a process of ideological radicalization that was fueled in part by the October 7 massacre and the ensuing Israel-Hamas War.The indictment, filed with the Jerusalem District Court against Mohammed Shalbi, charges him with preparation for an act of terrorism constituting murder and receiving training for terrorist purposes.Prosecutors allege that Shalbi regularly consumed material associated with Hamas and ISIS, and decided to use his knowledge and access to chemicals to carry out terrorist attacks.Shalbi was a third-year pharmacy student at Al-Quds University in Abu Dis, and also worked as a pharmacy assistant.Suspect began formulating plan to plant explosive device near where enforcement personnel frequently stoodHe is from the east Jerusalem neighborhood of Beit Hanina. According to the indictment, at the start of 2025, he began formulating a plan to plant an explosive device where enforcement personnel regularly stood, angered by parking tickets issued to worshipers who parked near a mosque in the neighborhood. The plan was never carried out because the enforcement personnel stopped coming to the area.Later, prosecutors allege, he began planning what they described as a large-scale attack in which he wanted to kill “a lot of Jews.”Shalbi joined Telegram groups associated with terrorist organizations, including a group affiliated with ISIS, and downloaded dozens of files. Some contained instructions for making explosive devices, explosives, and lethal poisons. The indictment also alleges that he copied into a notebook two formulas for poisons capable of causing death through contact, inhalation, or ingestion.Soon afterward, according to the indictment, he erased the downloaded files and his search history from his phone in an effort to conceal his actions.On two occasions, he traveled to Ramallah and bought chemicals and equipment, splitting the purchases to avoid suspicion, and stored them in his bedroom. Later, he conducted a chemical experiment in the bathtub of his home, igniting a mixture he had prepared to test the materials.The indictment alleges that, through these actions, Shalbi trained and instructed himself for the purpose of advancing a terrorist offense. The prosecution asked the court to order that he remain in custody until the end of the proceedings against him.

title: Explosions heard in Saudi capital as Middle-East conflict intensifies
body:
Several explosions were heard in the Saudi capital on Thursday, including one at the Riyadh airport that halted flights, a witness said.
The blasts came as Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis have targeted the kingdom’s infrastructure, though there was no word on what had caused the explosions and no claim of responsibility.
A witness says several explosions were heard in Riyadh on Thursday, including a large blast at the city’s international airport.
Fire and ambulance crews were being deployed, and smoke was visible, the witness said.
The witness said that outgoing flights were halted, and that passengers were instructed to evacuate the airport. It was not immediately clear how many flights were disrupted, but the witness said the terminal was crowded with passengers and that people were instructed to leave all checked-in luggage behind.
According to flight tracker Flightradar24, no planes have taken off or landed from Riyadh airport since shortly after noon local time.
The cause of the blasts was not immediately known. But the explosions came at a time when Houthi rebels have been targeting Saudi airports and oil installations.
Saudi authorities did not respond to requests for comment.
The witness spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media.
Britain said it had reached an agreement with Israel’s government to downgrade its consulate in east Jerusalem, and a small team of diplomats will continue to operate in what will now be known as the U.K. Mission.
Israel’s government said last month it would close the consulate in response to the United Kingdom banning trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said in a statement that the consulate had “ceased to function as a consulate.” He said twenty British diplomats will leave Israel, and that the building will continue to operate with seven diplomats engaged in limited activity.
“Israel will no longer turn its cheek to diplomatic attacks against it,” he said.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband denied the building will close and said it will be known as the U.K. Mission. Miliband said the seven diplomats remaining will continue to work with Palestinians, but gave no details. The UK said based on the current agreement, it would not take reciprocal action such as expelling Israeli diplomats from London.
The British military said late Wednesday that several projectiles struck a tanker off the coast of Qatar, causing multiple casualties.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Center said the attack took place in the Persian Gulf, north of Qatar’s city of Madinat ash Shamal. The city is on the northern tip of Qatar.
The U.K. military did not identify the tanker and did not provide any details about the casualties. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack and no comment from Qatar.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s former military secretary has accused the Israeli leader of altering official transcripts of phone calls from the morning of the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks.
The accusations by Maj. Gen. Avi Gil came in a wide-ranging interview with the right-wing Israel Hayom newspaper.
In excerpts of the interview published Thursday, Gil accused Netanyahu of attempting to change records of their phone calls in the first hour of the attack, possibly in an attempt to shift blame for failures that morning from the prime minister to his advisers.
Gil said he reported the attempt, allegedly made by Netanyahu’s chief of staff, to the attorney general. Gil served as military secretary from 2021 to 2024.
In the interview, Gil also confirmed that a senior Egyptian intelligence official had visited Israel shortly before the Oct. 7 attack. Asked whether there had been a warning, Gil said he did not know what message was relayed, but added: “Whoever met with someone or received something is still concealing it today.”
Gil’s full interview is expected to be published over the weekend, and an interview with an Israeli TV channel is also planned.
The report comes as Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, is seeking re-election on Oct. 27. His Likud party told Israel Hayom that Gil’s comments are part of an attempt to oust Netanyahu from power, the paper said.
European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Thursday that the bloc is preparing a “support mission” to train and advise Lebanon’s army and security forces, though that won’t replace U.N. peacekeepers in southern Lebanon whose mandate expires at the end of the year.
Kallas said during a visit to Beirut that Lebanese authorities formally asked the EU for this. She added that she expects the mission to be set up by EU foreign ministers on Monday.
Lebanese officials have previously pushed to extend the mandate of the U.N. force known as UNIFIL, but extension seems unlikely to pass a vote at the U.N. Security Council.
After the latest Israel-Hezbollah war, much of southern Lebanon is now occupied by Israeli forces, and an agreement to transfer control from Israel to the Lebanese army has largely stalled. The exit of U.N. peacekeepers has raised concerns that Israel might extend its occupation and that the Iran-backed Hezbollah militants could exploit the security vacuum.

title: Popular Nigerian rapper Lord of Ajasa becomes US citizen
body: Veteran Nigerian rapper Olusegun Osaniyi, popularly known as Lord of Ajasa, has become a United States citizen, drawing congratulatory messages from fellow artistes, music producers and fans. The pioneer of mainstream Yoruba rap shared photographs and videos of himself celebrating the milestone on his Instagram page, @lordofajasa, on Wednesday. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Olusegun Osaniyi (@lordofajasa) In one of the clips, the rapper was seen holding his American citizenship certificate, while another photograph showed him posing with his wife alongside the United States flag. The development quickly attracted attention from fans and entertainment personalities, with several of Lord of Ajasa’s contemporaries celebrating the milestone in the comment section of his Instagram post. Music producer and Coded Tunes founder, Olumide Ogunade, popularly known as ID Cabasa, wrote, “Congratulations Lord Oshi.” Lord of Ajasa replied, “Thanks Cabasa.” His contemporary, singer Abolore Akande, popularly known as 9ice, also congratulated him, w riting, “Congrats apase” Lord of Ajasa responded, “Thanks Baalè.” The rapper’s citizenship milestone also renewed conversations about his contribution to the development of indigenous Nigerian hip-hop, particularly Yoruba-language rap. Lord of Ajasa emerged as one of the early artistes to bring Yoruba rap into mainstream Nigerian music, predating the rise of later indigenous rap acts such as Dagrin, Olamide and Reminisce. His music has remained influential in conversations about the early years of Yoruba hip-hop, with songs including “Le Fenu So,” “Esha Lo Bade,” and “Mai Lo” still remembered by music lovers. The veteran rapper’s latest milestone has now added a new chapter to his career, as fans and colleagues continue to celebrate his transition to American citizenship. title: Oilpatch profits vastly outpacing spending — at least for now: Deloitte
body:
Canadian oil producers saw a 68 per cent surge in operating profits between the first and second quarters of this year, but capital spending hasn’t kept anywhere near the same pace, says a new report from Deloitte Canada.
The consulting firm notes that crude prices have experienced “considerable volatility” in recent months due to the Middle East war, with the international light benchmark, Brent, fluctuating between US$68 and US$105 per barrel in July and August alone.
High prices have created a windfall for Canada’s oil producers, with that sector the biggest contributor to non-financial industry profits during the second quarter, according to Statistics Canada.
Separate capital expenditure data from StatCan, meanwhile, has shown only modest movement recently, rising about seven per cent to $11 billion in the second quarter versus the first. Citing Baker Hughes rig count data, Deloitte says drilling in Canada was up 17 per cent during the second quarter compared to the same time a year earlier.
“It’s clear that producers are prioritizing drilling programs in plays which offer efficient, short-cycle economics, such as in the Montney, Duvernay and Clearwater, rather than pursue long-cycle, capital-intensive projects,” Deloitte said in the report released Thursday.
“Producers view the current price environment as temporary, or uncertain, rather than rooted in a fundamental supply-demand shift.”
Deloitte is forecasting West Texas Intermediate oil prices — the benchmark for light oil produced from U.S. fields — to average US$76.50 per barrel in 2027, down from a projected 2026 average of US$90.
Andrew Botterill, who leads Deloitte Canada’s oil, gas and chemicals practice, said over the past five to eight years, companies have been under pressure from investors to keep spending and debt in check. The COVID-19 pandemic, and the price collapse that accompanied it, ravaged oilpatch finances when they had barely recovered from the 2014-2015 bust.
But now, Botterill said, there’s a sense of “we could be much more” in the sector. A new million-barrel-per-day export pipeline has been proposed to the British Columbia coast, and Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government has made moves to simplify the regulatory process, roll back Trudeau-era environmental policies and expand investment tax perks.
“We could see significant growth coming from Canada,” Botterill said.
“And I think what we are going to see play out over the coming year is companies are going start to look at, ‘Where are we going to make our bets? Where are we going to start to make bigger capital spends for … the medium and long term?'”
Earlier this week, oilsands giant Cenovus Energy Inc. announced an agreement to buy smaller peer Athabasca Oil Corp. for $5.7 billion. Fellow energy heavyweight Suncor Energy Inc., meanwhile, said it reached a deal to sell some of its Atlantic Canada offshore holdings for $1.2 billion as it focuses on its core oilsands business.
Botterill said those transactions are “preparatory steps” for companies looking at growth over a long time horizon.
“Where would we be more likely to play that capital and let’s make sure we get our portfolio in that direction.”
On the natural gas side, the Deloitte report said prices in Alberta have averaged below an anemic C$2 per thousand cubic feet year-to-date, despite increasing exports from the LNG Canada terminal in Kitimat, B.C., which started up in mid-2025.
Output averaged 20 billion cubic feet per day during the second quarter, about five per cent above the same period in 2025. Companies kept growing production as they chased more valuable natural gas liquids, like propane, which come out of the ground along with dry natural gas.
Botterill said in August and September, typically the weakest time of year for Alberta natural gas, prices did not see sharp declines like they usually do, but stayed relatively steady.
“What that shows you is that there is natural gas demand building in Canada. The ability to export off our West Coast is making a difference,” he said.
“We’re much more structurally sound on the natural gas market than we were say, a year ago.”
Deloitte expects Alberta gas prices to average C$1.75 per thousand cubic feet this year, climbing to $2.15 next year and well above $3 post-2029.
The report also touched on artificial intelligence adoption in the oilpatch, which was detailed in another study Deloitte published in February.
It said 72 per cent of energy, resource and industrial companies use “physical” AI — through machines and control systems — to some extent.
However, many struggle to level up from pilot projects to enterprise-wide use, and only 16 per cent of companies reported using AI extensively.
“Oil and gas companies are used to capital intensive investments, with the oilsands as a prime example of making big bets. Simply put: it’s a business that isn’t afraid of risk,” the report said.
“But to compete with capital that is designated to core operations for development, expansion and optimization projects, the value proposition for AI use cases needs to be well developed.”

title: Rada proposed to introduce Army Volunteer of Security and Defense Forces of Ukraine status
body:
MP Serhiy Hryvko (Servant of the People faction) has proposed that the Verkhovna Rada introduce the status of Army Volunteer of the Security and Defense Forces of Ukraine.
A corresponding bill (No. 16129) on amending certain legislative acts regarding the introduction of the status of volunteers of the Security and Defense Forces of Ukraine has been registered in the Verkhovna Rada, according to the parliament's website.
As noted in the document's explanatory note, the bill does not introduce an alternative "combatant" status or alter the procedure for granting it; rather, it establishes an additional special status for individuals whose voluntary participation in the defense of Ukraine meets specific criteria. The status of Army Volunteer of the Security and Defense Forces of Ukraine is proposed for individuals who already hold combatant status and meet one of the criteria for voluntary participation in Ukraine's defense set out in the bill. These criteria include voluntarily applying to an authorized recruitment body or military unit and entering military service during the Anti-Terrorist Operation (ATO), the effort to repel and deter Russian Federation aggression in Luhansk and Donetsk regions, or the period of martial law.
The bill provides for granting volunteers of the Security and Defence Forces of Ukraine the right to a special award, as well as specific additional social and other guarantees, specifically: seven calendar days of additional paid leave, free access to certain sports, wellness, and cultural-educational services, and priority in being selected for civil service positions in the event of tied competition results.

title: Presidential aide discusses cooperation between Russian, Chinese shipbuilders in Shanghai
body:
SHANGHAI, October 8. /TASS/. Russian Presidential Aide and Maritime Board Chairman Nikolay Patrushev discussed strengthening ties between Russian and Chinese shipbuilding companies in Shanghai, the board’s press service said.
During a visit to the Shanghai Waigaoqiao shipyard, Patrushev and its management discussed "strengthening cooperation between Russian and Chinese shipbuilding companies, as well as opportunities for Chinese shipyards’ engineering departments and Russian shipbuilders’ design bureaus to exchange expertise," the press service said.
Patrushev is on a working visit to China from October 8 to 12. He will hold talks on Russian-Chinese maritime cooperation. The Chinese Foreign Ministry said earlier that Beijing was ready to use Patrushev’s visit as an opportunity to further deepen its strategic dialogue with Russia.

title: President Zelensky, UK Foreign Secretary honor victims of Russian missile strike in Pryluky
body:
This was reported by an Ukrinform correspondent.
“Today is a very tragic day. We had a tragedy here yesterday. We came here to help, to speak with people, and also to visit the hospital, see what people need and what the conditions are, and honor all those who were killed. During this trip, a horrific strike occurred in Kramatorsk, with a large number of people killed,” Zelensky said during a briefing in Pryluky.
He noted that UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband was accompanying him on his trip to Pryluky.
“I certainly want to thank my British counterpart, who came to the capital today, but we invited him to travel with us to Pryluky and see firsthand what is really happening, what these daily strikes look like, and how our people are enduring this struggle,” the President said.
Standing near the destroyed five-story building, Zelensky thanked all the teams that had worked at the site.
“About 500 people worked here, from different teams, from police officers to State Emergency Service personnel. We thank them. They saved 31 lives, 31 people, 15 of whom had been completely buried under the rubble. Unfortunately, the losses are very high: 22 people were killed, including five children, and 54 were injured, including seven children,” the head of state said.
He called on partners, including the UK, to step up assistance to Ukraine, particularly by providing air defense systems.
Zelensky separately stressed the need to intensify the negotiation process.
“Besides air defense, which is in short supply because our country is large and strikes can hit anywhere, we certainly want to draw attention to the negotiating track. In our view, the United States should raise the pressure through sanctions and other measures, as well as through financial assistance and separate assistance to Ukraine with air defense. And through such steps (…) force Putin to sit down at the negotiating table,” the Ukrainian President said.
As reported, 22 people were killed in a Russian missile strike on Pryluky, Chernihiv region, on October 7, including five children.

title: Messi’s farewell: Rohr reveals Benin players were denied photos, shirts
body: Benin head coach Gernot Rohr has criticised the treatment of his players after their international friendly against Argentina, saying they were denied the opportunity to take photographs with Lionel Messi and exchange shirts with the world champions. Argentina defeated Benin 3-0 at the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires on Tuesday in Messi’s final appearance for the national team. Speaking on RMC radio’s Rothen s’enflamme on Wednesday, Rohr said the Benin players attempted to meet Messi and other Argentine players after the match but were prevented from doing so by security personnel. “Yes, it was extremely difficult. We tried. “The only shame is that the Argentines gave us nothing. No photo with Messi, no shirt. They didn’t even let us into the tunnel, nor even the dressing room,” he said. “Security refused to let anyone in. Some players came to swap shirts, so we knew it would be difficult. We tried everything, but we got nothing,” he added. The Benin delegation also tried to present Messi with a bouquet of flowers in the country’s national colours, but Rohr said the gesture did not lead to a meeting with the Argentine captain. “We offered a bouquet of flowers in Benin’s colours, yellow, red and green, but that didn’t work,” the German said. “However, I gave Messi’s 2018 shirt to coach Scaloni, who got him to sign it for me and then returned it to me, but that was all,” he said. Messi marked his farewell after a 21-year international career with Argentina with a goal and two assists, setting up Nicolás Otamendi and Nico Paz before converting a penalty as Argentina secured the victory. He ended his Argentina career as the country’s most capped player and leading goalscorer, with 208 appearances and 126 goals. The post Messi’s farewell: Rohr reveals Benin players were denied photos, shirts appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: EU to establish training and support mission for Lebanese army
body: The European Union will establish a mission to support and train the underfunded Lebanese Armed Forces , the bloc's foreign affairs chief said on Thursday. Kaja Kallas, who was visiting Beirut, said the mission was not a replacement for the UN's peacekeeping mission in south Lebanon (Unifil), whose mandate is set to expire at the end of the year. “It will advise and assist the LAF and Internal Security Forces to strengthen territorial control, border security and also internal security,” she said, alongside Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi. “It's not the Unifil replacement and it will not only focus on southern Lebanon,” Ms Kallas added, saying a continued UN presence remained under discussion. The mission is expected to be formally established on October 12 at a meeting of EU foreign ministers, after a formal invitation from Lebanese authorities. The EU already provides financial, humanitarian and security assistance to Lebanon through a €1 billion ($1.12 billion) support package covering 2024 to 2027. There are fears of a security vacuum in south Lebanon – where Israel occupies about 65 towns and villages and Hezbollah continues to hold influence – as the UN mission prepares to withdraw with no successor formally announced. There have been suggestions that EU member states France and Italy could play a role. “We remain ready to work with Lebanon and UN Security Council members on what comes next,” Ms Kallas said. “There cannot be a security vacuum when Unifil leaves. Lebanon must have full control of its whole territory. That also means moving towards the disarmament of Hezbollah,” she added. Any international force must have a UN mandate, she said. The LAF, which is severely underfunded and relies on international donors, has sought to expand its presence in south Lebanon but has faced intense difficulties amid the latest Israeli occupation. Hezbollah's military arsenal and continued support in parts of Lebanon have raised fears of internal discord or even civil war should disarmament be done by force, amid pressure from the US and Israel to take a firmer stance. Israel's latest war on Lebanon , which was renewed again March against the backdrop of hostilities against Iran, has killed more than 4,300 Lebanese people and led to the destruction of a large number of border towns and villages. It came after Hezbollah fired rockets at Israel following the killing of Iran's supreme leader. Ms Kallas is on a two-day trip to Lebanon, where she also met with President Joseph Aoun among others.

title: Ukrainian forces detonate GPS collar on Russian POW refusing to infiltrate own troops
body:
DONETSK, October 8. /TASS/. Ukrainian troops killed a Russian prisoner of war by blowing up a booby-trapped GPS collar that they had put on him, Russian defense sources told TASS.
The collar was detonated because he refused to go to where Russian troops were stationed and act as a suicide bomber, they added.
Earlier, an escaped Russian POW told TASS that Ukrainian forces had begun using Russian prisoners of war as suicide bombers, sending them toward Russian positions while wearing booby-trapped collars equipped with GPS transmitters. A Ukrainian drone monitors the suicide bomber’s movements, and coordination is carried out via radio. If the prisoner refuses to carry out his mission, the detonator on the collar is remotely activated.
"Ukrainian militants detonated a collar with explosives on a Russian prisoner. The guy became another suicide bomber. It’s obvious that he was sent to infiltrate our positions, but he didn’t go anywhere," the sources said.
TASS has obtained video footage captured by a drone shortly before the soldier’s death. The footage shows the soldier, wearing an unknown device around his neck, sitting motionless in a wooded area.

title: Russian troops liberate Annopolye community in Kharkov Region over past day — top brass
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Russian troops liberated the community of Annopolye in the Kharkov Region over the past 24 hours in the special military operation in Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
"In their operations to expand the outer area of control, Battlegroup North units established control of the settlement of Annopolye in the Kharkov Region in their active advance," the ministry said in a statement.
Before storming Annopolye, Russian forces cleared the sky from enemy attack drones while unmanned systems teams and artillery crews delivered strikes on amassed Ukrainian manpower from a separate motorized infantry brigade, the ministry specified.
After crushing the Ukrainian army’s resistance and gaining their foothold in Annopolye, Battlegroup North forces started to clear buildings, basements and adjacent territory from the remnants of enemy troops, it said.
"Battlegroup North forces are simultaneously advancing in several directions and continue expanding the security belt along the Russian-Ukrainian border in borderline areas of the Sumy and Kharkov Regions. The troops are daily moving forward, edging the enemy out of the state border to ensure the security of civilians," the ministry reported.
The Ukrainian army lost roughly 1,510 troops in battles with Russian forces in all the frontline areas over the past 24 hours, according to the latest data on the special military operation in Ukraine released by Russia’s Defense Ministry.
The latest figures show that the Ukrainian army lost roughly 280 troops and two field artillery guns in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup North, about 210 troops and a US-made multiple rocket launcher in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup West and over 160 troops and three armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup South.
During the last 24-hour period, the Ukrainian army also lost roughly 535 troops and four armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center, about 295 troops and an armored combat vehicle in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup East and more than 30 troops and a US-made howitzer in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup Dnepr, the latest figures show.
Russia’s Battlegroup North forces are fighting for the liberation of six communities in the Kharkov Region and tightening the ring of encirclement of Ukrainian troops in that area, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup North units continue tightening the ring of encirclement in the Kharkov Region and expanding the outer area of control. In the pocket of encirclement, they are fighting for the liberation of the communities of Nikolayevka, Varvarovka, Lukashovo, Reznikovo, Lobanovka and Nefyodovka in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.
During the last 24-hour period, the Ukrainian army lost roughly 40 troops and a field artillery gun in the pocket of encirclement, it specified.
In addition, Battlegroup North units continue battles for taking control of the settlements of Prikolotnoye and Kotovka in the Kharkov Region, it said.
Russia’s Battlegroup North forces inflicted roughly 280 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed two enemy field artillery guns in its areas of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
In the Kharkov direction, Battlegroup North units "inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of a mechanized brigade, two assault regiments of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Chernoglazovka, Mishchenki, Dergachi, Veliky Burluk, Artyomovka and Novy Burluk in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.
In the Sumy direction, Battlegroup North units struck formations of two mechanized brigades of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Kiyanitsa and Grunovka in the Sumy Region and the city of Sumy, it said.
Overall, the Ukrainian army lost an estimated 280 personnel, 19 motor vehicles, two field artillery guns and three electronic warfare stations in the areas of responsibility of Russia’s Battlegroup North over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup West inflicted roughly 210 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed a US-made multiple rocket launcher in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup West units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, an assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements Maliyevka and Chervony Oskol in the Kharkov Region, Volchy Yar, Karpovka and Raigorodok in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 210 personnel, a British-made Snatch armored combat vehicle, a US-made HIMARS multiple rocket launcher, a Gvozdika self-propelled artillery system, 12 motor vehicles and an electronic warfare station in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup South inflicted more than 160 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed three enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup South units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on formations of two mechanized brigades, a mountain assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Krasny Molochar, Belenkoye, Kramatorsk, Gavrilovka, Nikolayevka and Semyonovka in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 160 personnel, three armored combat vehicles, 34 motor vehicles and a counterbattery radar station in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Center forces liberated a sports complex and a stadium in their battles for Dobropolye in the Donetsk People’s Republic over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"In Dobropolye in the Donetsk People’s Republic, assault groups of the 51st Army continued their advance in the town’s central and northern parts. Marine infantry formations seized a sports complex and cleared a stadium and the remaining part of the park zone in their advance in the southwestern direction," the ministry said.
Overall, during the last 24-hour period, Battlegroup Center units liberated 103 buildings and eliminated over 25 Ukrainian troops in Dobropolye, it said.
Russia’s Battlegroup Center inflicted roughly 535 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed four enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Center units inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of three mechanized brigades of the Ukrainian army, a marine infantry brigade and two National Guard brigades in areas near the settlements of Stepanovka, Belozerskoye, Sergeyevka, Roganskoye, Novoyavlenka and Kamyshevakha in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 535 personnel, four armored combat vehicles, 12 motor vehicles, a field artillery gun and a radar system in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup East inflicted roughly 295 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy armored combat vehicle in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup East units continued their advance deep into the enemy’s defenses and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two air assault brigades, two assault regiments of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Orestopol and Velikomikhailovka in the Dnepropetrovsk Region, Krinovka, Mirovka and Zalivnoye in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 295 personnel, an armored combat vehicle, nine motor vehicles and two artillery systems in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Dnepr eliminated more than 30 Ukrainian troops and destroyed a US-made howitzer in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Dnepr units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on formations of two mechanized brigades of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Orekhov and Preobrazhenka in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
"Over 30 Ukrainian military personnel, 20 motor vehicles, a US-made 155mm M777 howitzer and two electronic warfare stations were destroyed," it said.
Russian forces struck Ukrainian missile/artillery armament and ammunition depots and enemy deployment sites over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Operational/tactical aircraft, attack unmanned aerial vehicles, missile troops and artillery of the Russian groups of forces struck workshops producing unmanned aerial vehicles and their storage sites, missile/artillery armament and ammunition depots, and also temporary deployment areas of Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries in 142 locations," the ministry said.
Russian air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 1,062 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and seven smart bombs over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Air defense capabilities shot down seven guided aerial bombs, a rocket of the US-made HIMARS multiple launch rocket system and 1,062 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles," the ministry said.
Russia’s Black Sea Fleet destroyed a Ukrainian naval drone in Black Sea waters over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"The Black Sea Fleet’s forces destroyed an uncrewed boat of the Ukrainian Navy in Black Sea waters," the ministry said.
Overall, the Russian Armed Forces have destroyed 674 Ukrainian combat aircraft, 284 helicopters, 256,490 unmanned aerial vehicles, 672 surface-to-air missile systems, 31,159 tanks and other armored combat vehicles, 1,785 multiple rocket launchers, 36,659 field artillery guns and mortars and 73,965 special military motor vehicles since the start of the special military operation, the ministry reported.

title: Health officials report 74 new measles cases in Pennsylvania
body:
Five people have died in the state so far this year.
Pennsylvania is reporting 74 new measles cases since Monday, the state's health department said Wednesday.
A total of 1,078 cases have been reported in the state so far this year. At least 207 people have been hospitalized and five people have died, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health (DOH) .
"Of the 74 cases added, more than 40 represent individuals who were sick more than two weeks ago and are no longer contagious, but their cases were only recently reported and subsequently confirmed, the DOH said. Wednesday's update "does not reflect a current surge in new infections."
Of the five people who died, two of the deaths were among unvaccinated adults: an 18-year-old and a 40-year-old. The other two deaths were among infants who were too young to have received the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine.
The fifth death occurred in an unvaccinated resident of Lancaster County, in southeastern Pennsylvania, but it is unclear how old the individual is. Lancaster County is the epicenter of the state's outbreak, with 401 cases confirmed so far.
One-third of cases are among those under 18 years old and fewer than 1% of cases are among those fully vaccinated with the MMR shot, according to DOH data.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends that people receive two doses of the MMR vaccine, the first at ages 12 to 15 months and the second between 4 and 6 years old. One dose is 93% effective in preventing measles infection and two doses are 97% effective, the CDC says.
Infants aged 6 to 11 months living in or traveling to high-risk outbreak areas may receive an early third dose of the MMR vaccine.
CDC data, however shows vaccination rates have been lagging in recent years. During the 2025-26 school year, 92.4% of kindergartners received the MMR vaccine, according to data. This is lower than the 95.2% seen in the 2019-20 school year, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.
"State health center staff have administered more than 5,700 MMR vaccinations at 198 pop-up vaccination clinics in the affected communities since the outbreak began in late April," DOH wrote in a press release on Wednesday.
"Dozens of additional vaccine clinics are scheduled for the upcoming weeks and months, based on community interest and need," the press release continued. "In pop-up clinics and at state health centers combined, Department nurses have administered nearly 9,000 MMR vaccine doses to residents across the Commonwealth in 2026."

title: `specialArgs` considered harmful
body:
I'm writing this on my flight from KRK to LYS after Wizz Air fucked me in the ass... I briefly went over this yesterday (and the day before) at NixCon 2026 in my lightning talks (a normal one and a spontaneous one). The purpose of this article is to better articulate myself in addition to my very terrible verbal explanation. This is also related.
I read a lot of code (especially Nix), and I've helped quite some people getting their first NixOS installation working. Normally, users want unified theming across login manager, desktop environment, lock screen, etc., and they would opt to pin a styling dependency in inputs .
To pass them around in NixOS/nix-darwin/home-manager eval context, inputs are usually injected into specialArgs (or extraSpecialArgs , or similar) so that all modules have an inputs argument where additional options can be used (you also get inputs.self fixed point ofc).
Once a config repo gets big enough (10+ machines or some hosts are shared), specialArgs are not only used to pass inputs around module eval context, e.g. custom helper functions, static data, and maybe some other less common arguments are injected as well, making the modules unshareable (or at least making it hard to copy-pasta).
For example (you can copy the code below to a throwaway directory and try it out):
Same idea applies to other arbitrary shareable modules.
This is one of the most common issues with the current "Nix Flakes" ecosystem. Now maybe you are convinced using specialArgs is a bad idea but how can we address this?
There are sooooo many ways to approach this, but the general idea is to apply the special module arguments before lib.evalModules consumes the module implementation.
Yeah now both eval commands above work. But yall will most definitely argue this shit is too ugly blah blah blah.
I thought so too, maybe 2 years ago? I addressed it.
To make it "look prettier", yall should first understand how/why modules computed with lib.evalModules can either have 0 arguments (plain attrset) or 1 argument ( { config, options, pkgs, lib, ... } and some other less used named args):
loadModule calls a module in with "function shape" (again, it should look something like { lib, ... }: { ... } ), through applyModuleArgs with args , which contains standard arguments ( lib , config , options , ...) merged with user specified specialArgs .
If the module is a plain attrset, it will be used as is.
Very informally, the invariant is that, whatever passed to modules list parameter to lib.evalModules has to be a "module". Anything that happened to the "module" shaped file or lambda before lib.evalModules is invisible to the module evaluation context. In this sense, a curried module is nothing more than a function we've already called.
applyModuleArgs is also where the error in the first example comes from:
Every argument in the function's pattern ( functionArgs f ) is looked up in args first (which is where specialArgs is injected into) and then in config._module.args . A module that asks for inputs in args will only works if whoever coded it (or downstream users) put inputs in one of the two.
Moving the curried module to a file and calling import ./version.nix { inherit inputs; } will works as well, but error messages lose the file location, since import only returns the expression. In nixpkgs, we've had lib.modules.importApply to solve this "problem" since nixpkgs#230588 (also in flake-parts ).
Very briefly, importApply imports the module, applies the user passed arguments, and wraps the result so errors point at version.nix .
I don't want to write that call for every module in my config, so my loader scans every file under a module directory with importApplyWithArgs and invoke it with { inherit inputs lib; } , where lib is my extended nixpkgs.lib (see this ).
importApplyWithArgs inspects the outer arguments of each file before module system computation:
This means external consumers (like whoever is mentally unstable enough to use my code) of these modules are never forced to provide arguments they do not define (the injection is structurally invisible to the module system as discussed above).
Using a pattern like this would also solves the same problem as "dendritic pattern" (declaring everything as flake-parts modules) without losing the structural scoping that the module system provides (thanks Matt !).
The module system collects each key once. A module imported by path gets the path as its key, which is why importing ./foo.nix twice is harmless and disabledModules = [ ./foo.nix ] would work. THIS IS VERY IMPORTANT, note that a function or an attrset will get an anonymous key, and the same value imported twice becomes two modules:
In setDefaultModuleLocation (which importApply uses), it sets _file but not key , which leaves every curried module anonymous. Imported twice it is declared twice, and disabledModules cannot name it. Well, this is very bad as you cal already tell from the above REPL snippet...
The foot gun I shot myself with was that, the module system keeps the first module with a given key and never reads the rest:
This is probably why lib.modules.importApply leaves key unset on purpose? If one file applied with different arguments they will be two distinct different modules, and keying both by path would silently drop one of them. In my config however every file goes through modulesFor with the same { inherit inputs lib; } , so in my specific use case the path is enough. If you apply one file with different arguments, DO NOT COPY THIS!
The other way to give modules an argument is _module.args , which is a normal option. It works fine for anything in a module body:
But this might cause issue in some cases as well. Reading an option needs config , and config needs every module's imports first, which means pulling a module out of inputs with it will cause infinite recursion.
Do note that shared module that sets _module.args.inputs for itself collides with every other module doing the same, even with an identical value, since the option type is lazyAttrsOf raw :
Even though lib.mkForce and friends on one of them will make the error go away but by forcefully overriding inputs for every module... bruh...

title: Nearly 11,000 applications submitted for Russia-ASEAN youth summit
body:
VLADIVOSTOK, October 8. /TASS/. Registration has been closed for the 6th Russia-ASEAN Youth Summit, with a total of 10,700 applications submitted from Russia and ASEAN member states, the press service of the Far Eastern Federal University (FEFU) told TASS.
FEFU will host the 6th Youth Summit of Russia and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) from October 21 to 26.
"Registration has been closed for the 6th Russia-ASEAN Youth Summit, which is being held in accordance with the agreements reached at the Russia-ASEAN summit marking its anniversary, attended by Russian President Vladimir Putin. A total of 10,700 applications were submitted for the summit, which will be held at Far Eastern Federal University from October 21 to 26, 2026," the press service said.
The university noted that 4,479 applications from Russian and ASEAN citizens aged 18 to 35 who completed the competition task were admitted for expert evaluation. Each entry was assessed based on five criteria: the candidate’s experience, argumentation, originality, relevance of the proposed youth initiative and quality of development. One in four entries scored 20 or more points out of a possible 25.
The selection results will be announced after the expert evaluation is completed. Summit participants will be provided with tickets, accommodation and meals.

title: Three suspected illegal miners arrested in Tano-Boin Forest Reserve
body: Three men suspected of illegally mining in the Tano-Boin Forest Reserve have been arrested and remanded after allegedly being caught operating along the bank of the Tano River. The suspects were arrested on Friday, October 2, 2026, by members of the Jema Anti-Galamsey Advocacy (JAGA) Watch Committee during an operation in the protected forest reserve. According to JAGA, the suspects were found with a water-pumping machine and a changfang mining raft. One of the suspects allegedly attempted to escape by swimming across the Tano River after the committee members intercepted them. Members of the Watch Committee pursued him into the river and apprehended him. Following the arrests, the three suspects were handed over to the Police at the Jema Police Station and later transferred to the District Police Command at Enchi. However, because the Enchi Magistrate and Circuit Courts currently do not have substantive judicial officers, the suspects were taken to the Assankragwa Magistrate Court, where they were remanded for one week. JAGA commended the Enchi District Police Command, particularly District Commander Chief Superintendent Mensah, for ensuring that the suspects were brought before a court. The organisation said the District and Regional offices of the Forestry Commission at Enchi and Wiawso were immediately informed of the arrests. The Forestry Commission subsequently arranged transportation for the suspects from Jema to Enchi and covered other operational expenses incurred during the operation. JAGA said Forestry Commission officials have assured the organisation that they will follow up on the case to ensure that the suspects are dealt with in accordance with the law. JAGA said the latest case highlights the need for sustained enforcement against illegal mining in protected forest reserves and greater collaboration between community watchdogs and state institutions. The organisation said it expects the relevant law-enforcement and judicial authorities to give the case the necessary attention because of the environmental implications of illegal mining in forest reserves. It also commended the Attorney General and the Chief Justice for initiatives to establish special courts to expedite the prosecution of galamsey-related cases in selected regional capitals, including Sekondi. “When civilians risk their lives to arrest illegal miners to protect their water bodies and forests from destruction, state institutions must support them by enforcing the law,” JAGA said. The organisation maintained that the protection of Ghana’s forests and water bodies requires collaboration among security agencies, the Judiciary, politicians, traditional leaders and local communities. JAGA also appealed to the media and international environmental organisations to follow the case to help ensure that proceedings are handled transparently and in accordance with the law. The organisation contrasted the latest arrests with an earlier case involving two Nigerien nationals who were arrested last year for allegedly mining in the Jema-Assemkrom Forest Reserve. According to JAGA, those suspects were later granted police bail, with the organisation saying it has since seen little progress in the case. JAGA said the latest development reinforces the importance of ensuring that arrests linked to illegal mining proceed through the appropriate legal and judicial channels.

title: Ondo aircraft crash: Deceased officers are highly trained professionals — Chief of Air Staff
body: AKURE — The Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, has described the Nigerian Air Force personnel killed in Monday’s aircraft crash in Ondo State as highly trained professionals, saying the circumstances surrounding the incident would be thoroughly investigated. Aneke spoke on Thursday when he visited the scene of the crash at Igbokoda in Ilaje Local Government Area of the state. The Air Force chief said it was too early to speculate on the cause of the crash, stressing that experts and investigators would work to establish exactly what happened. He said: “They are highly trained professional officers. I know them personally. All the officers, I know everyone.” “Whatever happened here will be properly investigated. We must sit down to get what happened. This is not the time to speculate what happened. We must get to the root of this.” Aneke described the incident as a major loss to the Nigerian Air Force and the families of the deceased personnel. “It’s a very big loss. I am bereaved and no amount of words can be enough to calm the relatives of the victims,” he said. The Chief of the Air Staff also assured the families of the deceased that the Nigerian Air Force would not abandon them, adding that efforts would be made to recover the wreckage and determine the cause of the accident. He said, “I assure Nigerians that we will make sure to get the wreckages of the aircraft and get to the root of it. We will make sure that nothing of this will happen again. “I assure the families that they will not be left alone. Air Force will be responsible to the families and make sure that children and families are taken care of.” Aneke also commended the dedication and professionalism of the personnel involved in the operation, as well as the support provided by sister security agencies, government authorities and local communities. He specifically appreciated the police and other security agencies for their assistance in the response to the crash. The Air Force chief had earlier commended the personnel involved in the operation for their dedication and professionalism, while expressing appreciation to all those who contributed to the response and recovery efforts. The post Ondo aircraft crash: Deceased officers are highly trained professionals — Chief of Air Staff appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: South Korea to recall its ambassador to Ukraine over North Korean POW dispute
body:
FILE - Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy speaks during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly at United Nations headquarters, on Sept. 23, 2026. Seth Wenig/AP hide caption
SEOUL, South Korea — South Korea said Thursday it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine, stepping up its protest against Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's recent revelation of a supposedly secret transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea.
The South Korean announcement came days after its President Lee Jae Myung threatened to take unspecified punitive steps if Ukraine refuses to apologize over the revelation.
South Korea's Foreign Ministry didn't say when the ambassador, Park Hee-chang, will be brought back home. A ministry statement said that South Korea will continue consultations with Ukraine, adding it hopes the dispute between the two countries would be resolved smoothly.
South Korea and Ukraine became embroiled in a diplomatic row after Zelenskyy spoke about the transfer of the North Korean soldiers during his U.N. speech on Sept. 23. South Korea has accused Ukraine of violating a nondisclosure agreement on their transfer in mid-September, but Kyiv has denied agreeing to such a deal.
The soldiers were among thousands of North Korean troops deployed to support Russia's war against Ukraine. Since their capture in early 2025, the soldiers had expressed their desires to resettle in South Korea, because they could face persecution if repatriated home. South Korea had said it would accept them, because it legally regards the North as part of its territory and has a policy of accepting and financially supporting North Korean defectors.
South Korean officials said the non-disclosure agreement was made because they were concerned about the safety of the North Korean soldiers and their relatives in the North. But many experts say South Korea's liberal government likely also worries the disclosure of their arrival may hurt its efforts to improve ties with North Korea.
North Korea's state media hasn't commented on the soldiers' transfer. But the North previously reacted with fury to major defections of its citizens, accusing South Korea of kidnapping them. North Korea has shunned any talks with South Korea and the U.S. and focused on bolstering its nuclear program since 2019.
It's unclear what other steps South Korea would take. Experts say maintaining good relations with Ukraine is in South Korean national interests because Kyiv could provide Seoul with intelligence about North Korea's expanding cooperation with Russia and its battlefield experiences. They say cooperation with Ukraine is important for South Korea's partnerships with many Western countries supporting Ukraine over the war.
Observers say Zelenskyy disclosed the transfer of the North Korean POWs to expose the danger of North Korea's military support to Russia as a way to win more international assistance.
South Korea has provided $445 million in humanitarian assistance to Ukraine since 2022. In July, Lee pledged $100 million in aid to Ukraine in a meeting with Zelenskyy,
