title: Why Anne Carson won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
body: Canadian poet Anne Carson has won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature, with the Swedish Academy recognising her experimental approach to writing and her ability to bring ancient Greek literature into the modern world. The 76-year-old author , whose best-known works include Autobiography of Red , The Beauty of the Husband and Nox , was announced as this year's laureate on Thursday. The academy awarded Carson the prize “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature”. Anders Olsson, chairman of the Nobel Committee for Literature, said Carson's achievement lay in her ability to combine classical scholarship with poetry, fiction and other literary forms. “Almost all her literary production has centred upon the intersection between the philologist's obsession with words and the poet's desire for new meaning,” he said during the announcement. Carson has spent four decades drawing on ancient mythology, poetry and philosophy to explore love, grief, desire and identity. Her books frequently combine poetry with fiction, essays, translation and visual art, challenging conventional distinctions between literary forms. Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary of the Swedish Academy, said she had reached Carson by telephone shortly before the announcement. The writer was in Iceland, where she had been “listening to the wind”. “She was taken by surprise, but very happy. I can hear that in her voice,” Carlberg said. Carson succeeds Hungarian novelist Laszlo Krasznahorkai , who won the prize in 2025, and South Korean author Han Kang , the 2024 recipient. The award carries a prize of 12 million Swedish kronor (approximately $1.2 million) and will be presented in Stockholm on December 10. Who is Anne Carson? Born in Toronto in 1950, Carson developed an interest in ancient Greek literature while at secondary school, where a Latin teacher began teaching her Greek during lunch breaks. She went on to study classics at the University of Toronto, earning a doctorate in 1981, and subsequently taught at universities across Canada and the United States, including McGill University and the University of Michigan. Carson has also translated major ancient Greek writers, including Sappho, Sophocles and Euripides, while reimagining their stories in her own work. Her previous honours include a MacArthur Fellowship in 2000, the TS Eliot Prize in 2001 and Spain's Princess of Asturias Award for Literature in 2020. She has also won the Griffin Poetry Prize twice, in 2001 and 2014. Which works explain her Nobel Prize win? Among the works highlighted by the Nobel Committee was The Glass Essay (1995), a long poem about a woman recovering from a failed relationship who visits her mother in the moorlands, bringing with her the writings of Emily Bronte. Olsson said the work demonstrated Carson's ability to combine poetry, storytelling and literary criticism, with the narrator's experiences becoming entwined with those of her mother and Bronte. “The poetry needs the story, and the story is in turn given energy by the leaps and scene shifts of poetry,” he said. One of Carson's most acclaimed works is Autobiography of Red (1998), a novel written in verse that reimagines the ancient Greek myth of Geryon, a monster killed by the hero Herakles. Carson transforms Geryon into a young man with red wings, following his journey through adolescence, heartbreak and self-discovery. The book combines a contemporary coming-of-age story with the fantastic imagery of classical mythology. Olsson praised Carson's “extraordinary ability to give the classical literary tradition an intensely contemporary feel”, highlighting her use of modern language and experiences to reinterpret ancient stories. He also recalled that Carson had once described boredom as her greatest enemy, saying she confronted it with “drastic humour and wit”. She followed Autobiography of Red with The Beauty of the Husband (2001), subtitled A Fictional Essay in 29 Tangos . The book follows a woman reflecting on her marriage to an unfaithful husband, with each of its 29 sections opening with lines from the Romantic poet John Keats. Olsson described the work as a confrontation between Keats's ideas about beauty and the painful realities of a deteriorating marriage. The book won Carson the 2001 TS Eliot Prize, making her the first woman to receive the British poetry award. Grief became the subject of Nox (2010), created following the death of Carson's brother Michael. The book is presented as an accordion-folding collection of photographs, letters, drawings and poetry, drawing on an elegy by the ancient Roman writer Catullus, who also mourned the death of his brother. Olsson described Nox as “a creation as sculptural as it is literary”, highlighting how Carson uses the physical form of the book to examine memory and loss. Her engagement with Greek tragedy also produced Antigonick (2012), an illustrated reworking of Sophocles' Antigone , while Red Doc> (2013) returned to the characters of Autobiography of Red as adults. Carson's most recent collection, Wrong Norma (2024), contains 25 pieces of poetic prose accompanied by her own artwork. It was a finalist for the 2024 National Book Award for Poetry and won the National Book Critics Circle Award for Poetry in 2025. Olsson said Carson's influence extended beyond literature through collaborations with visual artists, choreographers and theatre directors. “This demonstrates the freedom with which she relates to literary expectations and rule systems,” he said, describing her work as an important influence on international art and literature since the 1990s.

title: Fact-checkers find systematic discrepancies in Bucha 'casualty list', GFCN says
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. International fact-checkers have found systematic discrepancies in the list of people recorded as killed in Bucha and are continuing their investigation, the Global Fact-Checking Network (GFCN) told TASS.
The association recalled that Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov presented a report at the Dialogue about Fakes 4.0 forum on September 22 of this year, addressing the falsification of the events in Bucha in March 2022 by the Kiev regime. He said Kiev had repeatedly "contradicted itself" over the number of allegedly killed civilians, while international organizations and Western media had used the figures without verification, making them publicly available.
"Analysts from different countries found systematic discrepancies after examining the data in the lists at the Bucha memorial. The findings called into question the official version of events. They established that the memorial complex has eight steles bearing the names of at least 198 disputed individuals who do not fit Ukraine's portrayal of the memorial as honoring 'civilians killed in Bucha.' The individuals include Ukrainian military personnel from armed forces, territorial defense forces, the Security Service of Ukraine, police, and the National Guard, including members of the Azov terrorist nationalist formation (the organization is recognized as terrorist and banned in Russia)," GFCN said.
Irish journalist Chay Bowes noted that the memorial lists people who had participated in combat since 2014. "This wall lists Azov fighters and people who fought since 2014 during the so-called anti-terrorist operation that Kiev launched against the people of Donbass," Bowes said.
His report also mentions people whose names appear both on the memorial dedicated to "civilians" and on official lists of "Bucha defenders," including Anatoly Prikhodko. "They actively fought the Russian army with weapons in their hands as combatants, rather than innocent civilians allegedly killed by Russian forces," Bowes stressed.
Brazilian geopolitical analyst and columnist Raphael Machado, in turn, pointed out that some people whose names appear on the memorial dedicated to "civilians" are openly listed on Ukrainian government websites as military personnel. GFCN says that at least 26 people on the list were unofficial participants in combat who assisted the Ukrainian army and attacked Russian military personnel with weapons and explosive devices.
French journalist Christelle Neant pointed to discrepancies identified in the reported causes and circumstances of death. She cited the case of 68-year-old Galina Semenyuk, who died from cancer but whose name was nevertheless included on the memorial's list of "victims".
At the same time, 42 people listed on the monument died elsewhere in Ukraine and therefore do not fit the memorial's portrayal of those "killed in Bucha."
In addition, 73 people listed on the steles have no digital footprint on the internet or in open databases, which may indicate that the data were fabricated. "There is no information about these people on the internet or anywhere else; it appears that no one knows who they are. This may be why the Ukrainian authorities have been so slow to provide detailed information about the identities of these alleged victims," Bowes said.
Greek journalist Thanassis Avgerinos described the coverage of the events in Bucha as "a psychological operation to mislead the international public," while Brazilian analyst Pepe Escobar called it "a false-flag operation."
GFCN experts said that listing combatants and people who died of natural causes as civilian victims shows that the tragedy is being used to support a political narrative. Editor-in-Chief of PIA Global Tadeo Castiglione said that analysts cross-checked the identities against municipal obituaries, local community channels, and funeral reports. They found that some people listed as civilians killed in the conflict were actually combatants who died in armed clashes. Others were local residents who died of heart failure.
The experts called on the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine to audit its own reports in light of the newly revealed facts, which were published even before the Ukrainian side had completed its own investigative proceedings. "If credible new evidence emerges regarding the identity, status, whereabouts, or cause of death of individuals previously registered as civilian victims, these cases should undergo an independent second review. The main priority should be examining cases involving significant discrepancies in four key elements: identity, status, location, and cause of death," Nepalese expert Tanka Timilsina said.
GFCN said that the identified cases of data fabrication, the lack of a digital footprint for dozens of reported victims, and the deliberate inclusion of combatants on civilian lists call into question the legitimacy and portrayal of the Bucha memorial. "We therefore call on the international community, relevant UN bodies, and independent human rights and journalistic organizations to initiate a comprehensive and objective investigation based on the published materials, the report cited in the article, and the new data," the association concluded.
On March 30, 2022, Russia pulled back from the town of Bucha and from Kiev’s vicinity as a goodwill gesture during negotiations with Ukraine in Istanbul. On March 31, the head of the local administration confirmed this before cameras. A few days later, Western television broadcast footage that showed dead bodies lying in the streets, in contrast to earlier recordings. In Russia, a criminal case was opened for the dissemination of false information about the Russian army.

title: Russia to take part in modernization in Mozambique — ambassador in Moscow
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Russian companies are going to participate in modernization in Mozambique, Ambassador in Moscow Jose Mateus Muaria Katupha told TASS.
"You know, we have just ended our intergovernmental commission in Moscow yesterday, and I'm happy to announce there were many Russian companies wanting to participate in the process of modernization of Mozambique," the Ambassador said.
Mozambique is the country "which needs infrastructure for development," the diplomat said. "We have a huge program for industrialization of the country, and many companies from Russia are bidding for providing not only equipment but technical assistance in the maximization of the exploration of the infrastructures of Mozambique, both railways and maritime transport and other areas of infrastructure, especially in the area of tourism," he stressed.

title: AratheJay brings Nimo Live Experience to Cape Coast on October 11
body: Ghanaian Highlife and Afro-fusion artiste AratheJay will perform live at XCape Beach Resort in Cape Coast on Sunday, 11 October. The singer, born Samuel Ofei Ankrah Badu, says the concert will be a special moment for the Central Region, as it marks his first-ever live performance in the historic city. “This will be a special moment for the people of Cape Coast, because for the first ever time, I’m going to have a show there. It’s going to be a live band performance,” AratheJay said. The Cape Coast show forms part of a nationwide city tour leading up to his major headline concert in Accra this December. According to the artiste, the tour is designed to give fans an intimate experience of his evolving sound. “We are leading the audience to an experience which is going to happen in December in Accra. But before that, we are going to touch a couple of cities, so we just came from Kumasi, we do Cape Coast and hopeful another city before closing the year with Nimo Live Experience in Accra,” he explained. The award-winning crooner promised fans in Cape Coast an unforgettable night with his live band, featuring some of his biggest records. Fans should expect AratheJay to unleash countless hit songs to create an irresistible atmosphere. He described the upcoming concert as a deeper connection to his artistry. “Nimo Live is AraTheJay live on stage. One set at a time, you get to hear AratheJay and listen to his music, but this time you get to feel the individual, get to understand the depth to what he makes music with. It’s not just lyrics and melodies, it’s more than that. That’s why I yearn for the audience to come for Nimo Life, come and experience me more live,” he said. Known for blending traditional Ghanaian Highlife with Afro-soul and contemporary Afrobeats, AratheJay has been spotlighted by Apple Music’s Africa Rising Class of 2025 and Up Next programme, OkayAfrica and Amplify Africa, a testament to his potential to take on the world.

title: Canadian poet Anne Carson wins Nobel Prize in literature
body:
Celebrated Canadian poet Anne Carson has won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
The Swedish Academy said the award was in recognition of Carson’s “bold and inventive oeuvre.”
A poet, essayist, classical scholar and translator, Carson is renowned as a master of esoterica whose body of work constitutes a genre unto itself.
With a bibliography of more than 20 books of poetry, essays, plays, libretti and translations of ancient Greek texts, Carson has defied literary conventions with her signature synthesis of the antiquities and the avant-garde.
She’s amassed a devoted readership and a raft of critical accolades, including two Griffin Poetry Prizes, a Governor General’s Literary Award, the T. S. Eliot Prize for Poetry, a MacArthur “genius grant” and a Guggenheim Fellowship.
But as her poetic profile has grown over more than three decades, the particulars of Carson’s personal life have remained notoriously elusive.
Her public reticence is encapsulated by her scant book-jacket biography: “Canadian poet, essayist and translator of Greek mythology.”
A representative for her did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary to the Swedish Academy, said she reached Carson Thursday in Iceland, where she was “listening to the wind.”
Various accounts suggest that Carson was born in Toronto in 1950 and studied classics at the University of Toronto, and has held teaching positions at institutions including McGill University, Michigan University and Princeton University.
Carson made her publishing debut in 1986 with her academic essays on love, “Eros the Bittersweet.”
She gained recognition with a series of genre-bending books in the 1990s establishing her style of culling from the literary canon to explore eternal themes. She invoked influences ranging from the Brontë sisters to the Greek poet Stesichorus in the early sixth century BC.
Carson cemented her reputation with her 1998 novel in verse, “Autobiography on Red,” which recasts the legend of Hercules as a modern-day love triangle.
Carson became the inaugural Canadian winner of the Griffin Poetry Prize for “Men in the Off Hour” in 2001, and was awarded England’s T. S. Eliot Prize for “The Beauty of the Husband” the same year.
In 2014, Carson took the Griffin again for “Red Doc>,” a quasi-sequel to “Autobiography on Red.”
At the time, she told The Canadian Press she was surprised to win, partly because she doesn’t “really like the book” and partly because she’d already won the honour and “thought it wouldn’t be fair” to get it again.
“I don’t mean it’s a bad book,” she said. “I mean, I don’t know if it’s a good book or a bad book. I just have a vision when I start of what a thing is and sometimes it gets there and sometimes it doesn’t.”
She also prevailed in the poetry category at the 2020 Governor General’s Literary Awards for “Norma Jeane Baker of Troy,” which in trademark style blends the story of Helen of Troy with elements from Marilyn Monroe’s life. She was shortlisted again two years later for “H of H Playbook,” a retelling of Euripides’s Greek tragedy, Herakles.
Her more recent works include 2024’s “Wrong Norma,” her first original work since 2016. The collection of “poetic prose pieces” was published alongside her own illustrations.
Carson is the second Canadian woman to be named a Nobel laureate in the literature category, following short story master Alice Munro’s 2013 win. The prize is worth 12 million Swedish kronor, or roughly $1.7 million.

title: The Download: AI roadblocks for humanoids and portable rubber dams
body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. AI breakthroughs in robotics won’t change your life any time soon The hype around humanoid robots is reaching fever pitch. Much of it comes from the idea that the same AI advances behind ChatGPT and Claude could enable robots to imitate human movement the way chatbots imitate human language. But many researchers are skeptical. They argue that such assumptions minimize the challenges of using an intelligence built on language and images to master the infinite variability of the physical world. They also point out that conflating humanoids with so-called generalist machines is misleading. Across robotics labs, tensions have emerged over whether current forms of AI are all that’s needed to perfect all-purpose humanoids or whether an entirely new path is required. Read the full story on what it will take to build truly general-purpose robots . —Jamie Condliffe This story is a collaboration between MIT Technology Review and Aventine , a non-profit research foundation that creates and supports content about how technology and science are changing the way we live. 10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch: WaveSave and its portable rubber dam WaveSave is one of MIT Technology Review’s 10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch 2026 , available exclusively to subscribers . As sea levels rise and flood risks worsen, WaveSave has emerged with an ingeniously simple tool: a portable rubber dam that’s quick to install when flooding starts. Anyone can unfurl the SlamDam on the ground along a riverbank or shoreline and pump it full of water until it swells into place. And there it stands, up to 1.3 meters high, shielding nearby property or structures from damage as waters rise. WaveSave now plans to take its unusual approach to flood protection much further . —Amy Nordrum Subscribers can now access the full 10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch , spanning everything from smart turbines and sustainable cement to carbon dioxide batteries . Why we’re watching these climate tech companies —Casey Crownhart Our Climate Tech Companies to Watch list is always a little ray of hope for me—there are some fascinating ideas out there about how we power our world or move away from fossil fuels. Our chosen companies also reflect several aspects of the current moment. One is that China is the center of the climate and energy tech world. Another is that everybody wants a piece of the data center pie. And then there’s the fact that the grid needs support, with energy storage a key piece moving forward. Here’s what this year’s list reveals about the state of climate tech . This story is from The Spark, our weekly climate tech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday. The must-reads I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology. 1 Scientists in Austria and China have built the first nuclear clocks They could become the world’s most precise timekeepers. ( NYT $) + They could also help scientists search for dark matter. ( Reuters $) + China’s nuclear clock is six times more stable than Austria’s. ( SCMP ) + A space clock could help measure Earth. ( MIT Technology Review ) 2 Three fired OpenAI researchers want to protect AI reasoning monitoring They warn that AI companies could lose a key safety tool. ( WSJ $) + OpenAI fired them for allegedly sharing sensitive information. ( Gizmodo ) + Don’t be fooled—LLMs don’t reason. ( MIT Technology Review ) 3 Samsung has forecast the highest quarterly profit ever for a tech firm The AI chip boom has sent its projected profits to $80 billion. ( CNBC ) + Can AI labs ever turn a profit? ( Reuters $) + What even is the AI bubble? ( MIT Technology Review ) 4 OpenAI’s math breakthroughs point beyond mathematics AI is progressing into increasingly specialised fields. ( Axios ) + OpenAI is catching up with Anthropic on coding. ( WSJ $) + A new AI tool could speed up math research.( MIT Technology Review ) 5 A 194-year-old tortoise has had its genome sequenced His longevity could reveal ways to extend human lifespan. ( Guardian ) + Jonathan is the world’s oldest known land animal. ( 404 Media ) + His youthful mitochondria may help repair DNA. ( New Scientist $) 6 A fraudster who used AI to outstream Taylor Swift has been jailed He used AI-generated songs and bots to earn $8 million. ( NYT $) + But prosecutors said he stole royalty payments. ( Ars Technica ) 7 TikTok allegedly gave kids fake safety features to study engagement The tests measured time spent and ad revenue. ( Reuters $) 8 Burglars could be identified from DNA floating in the air Thanks to a new device that collects airborne genetic material. ( Economist $) 9 Pioneers of mirror-image molecules have won the chemistry Nobel Their work has become a key tool in developing medicines. ( Guardian ) 10 California has declared a human-vs-robot fight illegal The state’s combat-sports laws were never written for machines. ( NYT $) Quote of the day “ We grew a mind.” —David Robinson, who last week quit his job as OpenAI safety transparency lead, tells The New York Times that his former company has built models that develop capabilities their creators did not explicitly design. One more thing We need a moonshot for computing The US government is organizing itself for the next era of computing. Ultimately, it has one big choice to make: adopt a conservative strategy that aims to preserve its lead for the next five years—or orient itself toward genuine computing moonshots. There is no shortage of candidates, including quantum computing, neuromorphic computing and reversible computing. And there are plenty of novel materials and devices. These possibilities could even be combined to form hybrid computing systems. The National Semiconductor Technology Center can drive these ideas forward. To be successful, it would do well to follow DARPA’s lead by focusing on moonshot programs. Read the full story . —Brady Helwig & PJ Maykish We can still have nice things A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .) + An experimental pair of contact lenses can repair themselves with UV light . + Meet Rich, the rescued squirrel who visits the woman who saved him every day . + Reminisce about the lost joy of music piracy with this wistful reflection on a time before streaming. + What would rainbows look like on Tatooine? Randall Munroe, a former NASA roboticist, has the answer .

title: US, Russia confirm Trump's latest Ukraine peace push is falling apart
body:
Editor's note: This story has been updated to include President Volodymyr Zelensky's remarks.
Ending Russia's war against Ukraine through negotiations is currently unattainable, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Greek media outlet Kathimerini on Oct. 8, casting further doubt on President Donald Trump's latest push to broker peace.
The comments confirm earlier Kyiv Independent reporting that Washington's latest effort to advance negotiations faces growing uncertainty.
At this point, there appears to be no prospect of a negotiated settlement, Rubio said . He added that the goal remains out of reach because Russia insists on gaining full control over Ukraine's Donetsk Oblast without fighting, a demand Kyiv has rejected.
The latest rounds of peace negotiations have also stalled over Moscow's territorial demands.
The Kremlin has repeatedly rejected a ceasefire and demanded that Kyiv surrender the partially occupied Donbas, a strategically important region in eastern Ukraine . Moscow is effectively seeking territory that Russian forces have failed to capture militarily.
Ukraine has instead called for a ceasefire along the current front line.
The diplomatic effort now faces another obstacle: Moscow has given little indication that it intends to take part in further talks. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said on Oct. 7 that there were currently no plans for U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine.
"There are currently no plans to hold talks in this format," Ryabkov told reporters.
The latest effort began in early September, when Trump's envoys traveled to Kyiv and Moscow seeking progress before the U.S. midterm elections. The trips produced one tangible outcome: an agreement in principle to hold a trilateral meeting between Ukraine, Russia, and the U.S.
A month later, however, even the trilateral meeting remains uncertain.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said Oct. 8 that Ukrainian negotiators will meet with Trump's envoys in the U.S. later this week to discuss the prospects for peace talks with Russia.
"You can't, on the one hand, negotiate with Russia about future economic projects, and on the other, talk about a diplomatic impasse," the Ukrainian president responded to Rubio.
"We are not in a diplomatic impasse. Shut down (Russia's) entire economy. Silence Russia. Don't feed them with your sales; impose sanctions on their weapons," he added.

title: Show HN: LLM Fuzz CI
body:
By Louis Abraham and Nicolas Devatine Oct 5, 2026 5 min read
We are releasing LLM Fuzz CI , the first CI tool that lets LLM agents attack the tests you wrote, and only reports inputs that fail them.
LLM Fuzz CI is a GitHub Action that lets a coding agent read your code and write adversarial inputs for the tests you mark. Your normal test run replays them, so every report is a real failure of your own assertions.
Code agents have become really good at programming, including at finding bugs (do not get me started about agents creating bugs). Sadly, agents are also extremely good at logorrhea producing torrents of text, flooding programmers with an endless stream of information of seemingly utmost importance. Security scanners are even worse: they drown CISOs in CVE reports rated “medium”, which programmers quickly dismiss as minor, and they never test the business logic anyway.
We tasked ourselves with solving this problem by creating a tool that follows these principles:
(*) As more and more code will be written by LLM, possibly most of it, the role of programmers will actually stay the same: converting business requirements into specs, and producing systems that abide those specs. Both steps need technical skill: writing unambiguous specs (a few rounds of prompting and some technical claude-linguo), defining a correct way to verify them, and spotting any gap between the original intention and the produced system. Even with the best coding agents, non-technical humans still struggle with both steps: without the technical language, they cannot discuss their own specs well.
The solution was pretty natural: have the programmer mark tests as targets and then run an agent to try to fuzz them.
You mark a test, set a spend limit with budget_usd , and optionally restrict the agent to some input keys with params . We supports Python with pytest and JavaScript with vitest .
The agent will be tasked with replacing llm_fuzz_case.input / input.value with a value that will make the test fail.
You can then configure a CI action that will launch the tool in two phases, on two separate machines. First, a coding agent (by default Codex with an OpenAI or OpenRouter key, but we also support Claude Code) reads the code and the marked tests, tries to break them, and when succeeding, exports the inputs.
Second, a fresh runner checks out your code again, downloads those inputs, and replays them through your normal test run. The agent is free to do whatever it wants on the first machine: run your code, install things, edit files to understand them. None of it reaches the second one. The only thing that crosses is a file of inputs.
Finally, every run writes a summary, an artifact with the inputs and the agent’s trace, and optionally creates a GitHub issue and can fail the build.
You can find more information in the README.md .
Fuzz testing, or fuzzing, originally means throwing a lot of unexpected inputs at code and watching what breaks. Classic fuzzers start from a seed input and mutate bytes at random, sometimes guided by coverage, then look for crashes, timeouts or surprising results. That works well for low-level code. It struggles with higher-level code: the fuzzer does not know what your function is supposed to do, which parameters interact, or how to tell a logic bug from a legitimate corner case. Checks that depend on meaning slip through because the random generator never hits the interesting combinations. An LLM agent can read the code and the test, and aim straight at those combinations.
Mixing LLM and fuzzing is not new. OSS-Fuzz-Gen from Google and PromptFuzz have LLMs write fuzz targets for C and C++ libraries. Garak and promptfoo fuzz LLMs themselves, not your code. XBOW (hosted pentesting with verified exploits), OpenAI’s Aardvark and Google’s Big Sleep hunt for vulnerabilities on their own, without your tests as the judge. But LLM Fuzz CI is the first tool that:
Unlike classic security scanners, LLM Fuzz CI has the ability to find advanced vulnerabilities by actually reading and understanding the code. Unlike “PR-review” tools, no noise is created: this is a tool for programmers to enforce guarantees of their code.
Generating arbitrary inputs enables use cases not covered by standard fuzzing tools, like attacking LLM agents through their prompts. We first used this tool to test an accounting agent on a testing branch, and discovered that when prompted with a valid account id different from the user’s, it would launch a tool that erroneously allowed access to data of the other account. Smart testing agents are thus able to find and demonstrate complex bugs (even using prompt engineering) from end-to-end tests and not just unit tests. This makes LLM Fuzz CI a nice complement to another testing concept we released last year: cached stubs turn end-to-end pipelines into fast, reproducible tests by caching non-deterministic steps and external calls.
Code has become a commodity, and any recent coding agent should be able to replicate our repo.
Rather than a tragedy, this is fine: nobody needs to care about our particular implementation. It is easy to replicate, or even copy (please do), into the frameworks that will spread it. This new age puts even more emphasis on concepts. The core of innovation has always been novel ideas. Technical implementation was both a gate, because it took technical skills to demonstrate those ideas, and a fun way to spend time (at least for me).
More than a tool, this release is about a novel, simple and useful paradigm of how to use code agents well to protect the quality of software and the time of maintainers.

title: Humanitarian Worker, Police Inspector Killed as Bandits Raid Sokoto Communities
body: Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto A humanitarian and field operations professional, Ms Lydia Chinenye Nwankwo, has been killed following an attack by suspected bandits in Sokoto State. Nwankwo was reportedly attacked alongside members of her team while returning from field operations in Kajiji community, Shagari Local Government Area of the state on Tuesday, October 6, 2026. The development was confirmed by her sister, Chisom Nwankwo, who announced the tragic incident in a Facebook post on Thursday October 8. According to the family, the team came under heavy attack from the armed bandits who opened fire on their vehicle, killing the young humanitarian worker on the spot. The incident has thrown the humanitarian community in Sokoto into mourning, with colleagues describing Lydia as a dedicated field worker committed to serving vulnerable communities in hard-to-reach areas. Meanwhile, the Sokoto State Police Command has confirmed the attack on communities in Shagari LGA, disclosing that a police inspector also lost his life during the incident. The Command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Ahmed Rufai, who confirmed the attack to THISDAY, said the Divisional Police Officer in charge of Shagari LGA had briefed the state headquarters on the development. Rufai, however, noted that the Command was still collating details of the attack to ascertain the full extent of casualties and damage. “I just spoke with the DPO in charge of Shagari now, who confirmed the attack on some communities in the local government. We are still on it. I cannot give details now until I gather my information about the incident. I will get back to you on it,” the police spokesman stated. As at press time, the security situation in the affected communities remained tense, with residents calling on the state government and security agencies to intensify patrols and deploy more personnel to Shagari and its environs to forestall further attacks.

title: Soludo sets up commission to end deadly intercommunal clash
body:
Governor Charles Soludo of Anambra State has set up a judicial commission of inquiry to tackle the deadly intercommunal clash between Amaeze Aguleri and Umuoba Anam in Anambra East Local Government Area of the state.
Mr Soludo set up the commission on Tuesday during a stakeholders meeting at the Government House in Awka, according to a statement on Wednesday by the governor’s spokesperson, Christian Aburime.
Mr Aburime said the commission was tasked with “thoroughly” examining all petitions, complaints, and historical grievances between the two warring communities.
“The commission was mandated to submit its comprehensive report within four months,” he said.
PREMIUM TIMES reports that at least five people have been killed, several houses razed and livelihoods destroyed in the violence that engulfed the communities.
The Anambra State Government earlier ordered the immediate closure of the Otuocha Market following the crisis.
At the Tuesday meeting, Mr Soludo decried the tragic loss of lives and the widespread destruction of properties, emphasising that such lawlessness was entirely unacceptable to his administration.
The governor then directed security agencies to maintain a robust, round-the-clock presence in the affected zones to ensure compliance to his earlier ceasefire order in the communities.
He reassured all parties that his administration remains firm, fair, and uncompromising in its pursuit of lasting peace and justice across the state.
In attendance at the meeting were traditional rulers from the Anambra South and Central senatorial districts of the state.
The Chairman of the Anambra State Traditional Rulers Council, Chidubem Iweka, was among the traditional rulers in attendance.
The traditional rulers, in their separate contributions, condemned the hostilities, specifically highlighting the tragic killings of a minor and an unarmed person from Umuoba Anam.
They also lamented “the retaliatory destruction” of the Idigo Palace, the historic royal residence of Michael Idigo, the traditional ruler of the Aguleri Community.
Speaking as an observer on behalf of the Umueri Community, Charles Okaa, appealed for restraint.
Mr Okaa, a retired justice, urged the state government to enforce the 1982 Supreme Court judgement concerning boundary matters between Umueri and Aguleri as a step toward permanent resolution.
After the deliberations, the stakeholders reached “a multi-point” resolution to foster reconciliation and security.
They also stressed the need for immediate ceasefire and prosecution of perpetrators.
Mr Soludo condemned the attack on the traditional stool, describing it as “an assault on the heritage” of the state.
The governor then announced that the state government would “actively assist” in rebuilding the destroyed palace to restore “traditional dignity.”
The Aguleri–Umuoba Anam dispute dates back decades.
It is primarily a land and boundary dispute, with competing claims over ownership of land around the Anambra River and areas adjoining the two communities.
The Anambra State Government had described the matter as a boundary dispute and, in 2025, referred it to the State Boundary Committee for resolution.
PREMIUM TIMES reports that the dispute resurfaces usually after years of state government intervention.
In March 2015 for instance, a clash between the two communities left at least one person dead and several houses destroyed.
After the state government’s intervention, the clash ceased but resurfaced 10 years later in 2025.
Within the time, traditional rulers of the two communities presented different accounts of the origin of the disagreement with all laying claims to the ownership of the disputed land.
The fresh violence in the two communities has also been attributed to the long-standing land dispute.

title: Kazakhstan Names Former Finance Official Deputy Defense Minister Amid Military Shake-Up
body: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev appointed Tatyana Savelyeva deputy defense minister on October 7. The former vice minister of finance and member of parliament joins a ministry undergoing a major investigation following the deaths of 14 service members during exercises in the Caspian Sea. The investigation has led to criminal cases and arrests, while senior military commanders have been dismissed. Savelyeva replaced Asker Beisenov, who was dismissed from his position on the same day. To take up the appointment, she resigned early from the Kurultai, Kazakhstan’s new unicameral parliament. Savelyeva joined it in late August 2026. The 50-year-old Savelyeva has spent most of her career working in public finance. From 2016 to 2023, she served as vice minister of finance, then became a member of the Mazhilis, the lower house of the former parliament, and secretary of the Committee on Finance and Budget. She became the committee’s chair in February 2024. In August 2026, she was elected to the Kurultai representing the Adilet party. The Defense Ministry has not yet announced which areas Savelyeva will oversee. Her predecessor, Beisenov, previously headed the ministry’s Department of Economics and Finance. Political analyst Daniyar Ashimbayev links Savelyeva’s appointment to the investigation into the Defense Ministry following the deaths of the service members in the Caspian Sea. He recalled corruption investigations within the ministry, including irregularities in military procurement and supplies. In Ashimbayev’s assessment, Savelyeva’s experience in the Finance Ministry and parliament could prove useful in bringing order to the military budget. On September 24, during the Khazar Qorgany 2026 naval exercises in the Mangystau region, on Kazakhstan’s Caspian coast, 17 service members were swept out to sea. Three were rescued, and 14 died. The tragedy sparked public outrage and questions about how the exercises were organized, personnel training, and the actions of the military command. On September 27, Tokayev dismissed Defense Minister Dauren Kosanov . Aidos Myrzakhmetov became the new head of the ministry. The chief of the General Staff, the commander-in-chief of the Naval Forces, and other senior military officers subsequently lost their positions. On October 5, the president was presented with the initial findings of the Defense Ministry investigation. A commission headed by Deputy Chair of the Security Council Aida Balayeva identified violations in the organization of exercises, service member safety, discipline, and logistical support. Thirteen criminal cases have been opened over the suspected theft of state property, abuse of office, and other violations. The deaths of the service members are being investigated separately. At the October 5 briefing, officials said five military officials had been arrested in connection with the deaths. On October 6, the Interior Ministry announced the detention of former navy commander Kanat Niyazbekov on suspicion of negligence, with a court authorizing his arrest. Investigators also uncovered cases of hazing and violence against service members. Tokayev instructed officials to prepare a military reform plan, including changes to management, personnel training, discipline, and safety measures. On September 27, he gave the Security Council Office and Defense Ministry ten days to submit the plan. The Security Council is due to consider it in the second half of October. Savelyeva is not the first woman to serve as Kazakhstan’s deputy defense minister. In 2001, Zhannat Yertlesova held the same position and also had experience in the government’s economic policy departments.

title: Oil transit through Strait of Hormuz has reached nearly 80% of February levels — Rubio
body:
ATHENS, October 8. /TASS/. Oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have reached nearly 80% of pre-Iran war levels, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in an interview with the Greek newspaper Kathimerini .
"Oil shipments via the southern route [of the Strait of Hormuz], which we cleared of mines, have already reached nearly 80% of pre-conflict levels. The only country unable to regularly ship oil from the Middle East is Iran, whose supplies have been completely blocked or halted by the blockade," Rubio asserted.
The US and Israel launched military operations against Iran on February 28. In June, Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding providing for an immediate cessation of hostilities on all fronts, including Lebanon. However, on the night of July 8, the US resumed large-scale strikes on Iran, accusing it of violating the terms of the agreement regarding the Strait of Hormuz, through which approximately 25% of global oil trade and about 20% of liquefied natural gas trade pass. Subsequently, the US administration effectively signaled an end to the use of large-scale military force against Iran, shifting toward an attempt to economically strangle the country through sanctions.

title: Lavrov to hold talks with ASEAN secretary-general in Moscow on October 13 — MFA
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Russia’s top diplomat Sergey Lavrov and ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn will hold talks in Moscow on October 13, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said at a briefing, commenting on the secretary-general’s upcoming visit to Russia.
"During the talks between the Russian foreign minister and the ASEAN secretary-general scheduled for October 13, they are expected to discuss the implementation of the tasks set by the leaders of Russia and the organization at the anniversary summit in Kazan held on June 17-18 this year, as well as prospects for advancing our strategic dialogue, focusing on closer coordination at international and regional platforms, ensuring stability, food and energy security, the development of the Northern Sea Route, expanding cooperation in addressing new challenges and threats, broadening trade, economic and technological cooperation, and developing social, cultural and humanitarian ties, including, of course, youth contacts," the diplomat said.
The ASEAN secretary-general’s visit, which will run from October 12 to 15, will include meetings and talks with officials from Russia’s Emergencies Ministry, Ministry of Science and Higher Education, Agriculture Ministry, Digital Development Ministry and Energy Ministry, as well as an address at a thematic session of Russian Energy Week. "These events are expected to give impetus to practical cooperation with ASEAN in various sectors," Zakharova added. "The Association’s secretary-general plans to hold substantive talks with representatives of Russian business under the auspices of the Russia-ASEAN Business Council and with the expert community, including at a conference on Russia and ASEAN in the Asia-Pacific region."
The visit will also include a meeting between the ASEAN secretary-general and the chairman of the Board of the Eurasian Economic Commission on prospects for implementing the cooperation program for 2026-2030 and establishing cross-platform cooperation in the region.

title: UBIDS hosts WAC-SRT closing conference as regional partners push for sustainability beyond funding cycle
body: The University of Business and Integrated Development Studies (UBIDS) has hosted the International Alumni Meeting and Conference (AMCO) of the West African Centre for Sustainable Rural Transformation (WAC-SRT), bringing together scholars, institutional leaders and alumni from across West Africa and Germany to evaluate the initiative’s impact and map out its future sustainability. The multi-day conference marks the closing chapter of the centre’s primary funding cycle under the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) and the German Federal Foreign Office, which concludes between 2026 and 2027. Officially declaring the conference open at the UBIDS campus in Wa, the Vice-Chancellor of UBIDS and Project Lead for WAC-SRT, Prof. Emmanuel Kanchebe Derbile, revealed that the centre played a foundational role in the operational take-off of UBIDS when the university gained autonomy. “We became a university in 2019 by law, and by May 2020 we had started operations with the constitution of the first-ever Governing Council,” Prof. Derbile stated. “The central administration and many other critical functions or units of this university were supported by the West African Centre for Sustainable Rural Transformation. Many of you may not know that the operations of the central administration for this university started from this centre.” Prof. Derbile highlighted that WAC-SRT was launched on the campus on June 26, 2019, when the institution was still operating as a satellite campus under the University for Development Studies (UDS). He noted that the initiative paved the way for internationalisation in Wa, attracting international postgraduate students from across the sub-region and expanding into cross-border collaborations. To preserve the gains made, Prof. Derbile announced that UBIDS is repositioning the centre within the university’s broader research and grants infrastructure. “We are working to reposition the West African Centre for Sustainable Rural Transformation here at UBIDS as one of the strongest parts of the grantsmanship infrastructure. We are in the process of establishing a Grants Office that would support grantsmanship-related activities, and WAC-SRT comes in handy as part of that infrastructure,” Prof. Derbile noted. He also acknowledged the appointment of Dr. Rudolf Nabogu to the Grants Office and the leadership of the Director of Research, Prof. Frederick Dayour, alongside the WAC-SRT UBIDS Director, Dr. George Dery. Delivering his address, Dr. George Dery underscored that the real impact of the centre extends far beyond the completion of certificates. “WAC-SRT represents much more than a project implemented by a group of institutions. It represents a sustained commitment to building human capacity, strengthening institutions, and generating knowledge for sustainable rural transformation,” Dr. Dery said. “The true value of scholarship cannot be measured only by the number of students supported or degrees completed. Where does the knowledge go? Who benefits from it? What institutions are strengthened?” The Project Coordinator of WAC-SRT and Senior Researcher at the Center for Development Research (ZEF), University of Bonn, Dr. Wolfram Laube, recalled the early stages of establishing the partnership between Anglophone and Francophone institutions, which initially faced mutual scepticism before developing into lasting trust and academic diplomacy. “Beyond the knowledge, beyond the development capacities you may create, there is also this social aspect of collaborating. Meeting each other in person, spending time with each other, seeing each other’s flaws, and seeing each other’s successes is something which I found very valuable in this project,” Dr. Laube remarked. He cautioned that North-South collaborations must remain genuine people-to-people exchanges rather than mere transactions of development assistance. Speaking on behalf of the DAAD Country Director, Ms. Lena Leumer, the Senior Programme Officer at the DAAD Regional Office in Accra, Felix Barnes, assured stakeholders that cooperation would continue through other funding mechanisms. “Funding will be completed by close of 2026/2027, but it’s really the hope that there will be sustainability,” Mr. Barnes noted. “DAAD will not stop there, because there are other avenues of funding that could come in, such as in-country and in-region scholarships. The alumni are certainly our greatest legacy.” Highlighting the programme milestones achieved at the partner campus in Niger, the Academic Assistant of WAC-SRT at Abdou Moumouni University of Niamey (UAM), Dr. Karimoun Massalatchi Illyassou, speaking on behalf of the Dean of the Faculty of Sciences and Techniques, Prof. Bakasso Yacoubou, detailed the cross-border footprint of the initiative. According to Dr. Massalatchi, the centre established the Integrated Master Programme in Sustainable Rural Transformation (EIMP-SRT) in 2018, training eight Master’s cohorts and two PhD cohorts between 2018 and 2026 across engineering and policy tracks. The cohorts comprise students from Niger, Ghana, Mali, Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast and Sierra Leone. Adding his voice, the WAC-SRT Coordinator at UDS, Prof. Isaac G.K. Ansah, paid tribute to the four founding architects of the centre: Dr. Wolfram Laube, Prof. Emmanuel Derbile, Prof. Rabani Adamou and Prof. Michael Kpalo, now Deputy CEO of Operations at the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Prof. Ansah challenged the alumni body to maintain active and productive networks. “Let not our alumni network be a WhatsApp group where, on Friday nights, when we are tired, we just send messages. Let’s be an important asset that you can leverage to establish very good relationships that can materialize in the future.” The conference continues with research presentations and gallery walks demonstrating community-level action research interventions across beneficiary West African states.

title: FIFA Ranking: Ghana drop five places to 70th following AFCON qualifying defeats
body: The Black Stars have fallen to 70th in the latest FIFA Men’s World Ranking following a difficult start to their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. Ghana, previously occupying the 65th position, dropped five places and lost 25.73 points after suffering humble defeats in their opening two qualifying matches, losing 2-0 to Côte d’Ivoire before falling 4-2 to The Gambia. The latest rankings, released on October 7, 2026, were based on 338 men’s international matches played since the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup on July 19. These included UEFA and Concacaf Nations League fixtures as well as 2027 AFCON qualifiers. The poor results mark a challenging period for the four-time African champions, who also failed to qualify for the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. Following the recent set of defeats, Ghana mutually parted ways with head coach Carlos Queiroz. A scheduled friendly match against Africa’s top-ranked team, Morocco, was also cancelled. Ghana, currently ranked 14th on the African continent, is preparing to rebuild under new management. The Black Stars will look to get back on track in their next international fixture when they face Somalia in back-to-back qualifiers. Somalia is currently ranked 200th in the world. Sitting directly above Ghana in the global standings are the United Arab Emirates in 65th, Albania in 66th, Honduras in 67th, Cabo Verde in 68th, and Jamaica in 69th position, just one place ahead of the Black Stars. Elsewhere in the continent’s standings, Morocco remains Africa’s highest-ranked team at 7th in the world, followed by Senegal in 18th. Côte d’Ivoire sits in 29th, while Nigeria dropped four places to 30th. At the summit of the global standings, the 2026 FIFA World Cup champions, Spain, remain top of the world ranking, with runner-up Argentina second and France third.

title: No rift between Agric and Finance Ministries — Eric Opoku dispels rumours
body: The Minister of Food and Agriculture, Eric Opoku, has dismissed reports of disagreements between his Ministry and the Ministry of Finance, saying both institutions remain committed to advancing the government’s Reset Agenda. According to him, while misunderstandings and miscommunication may occur between institutions, it should not be interpreted as evidence that one ministry is working against another. Speaking at a press briefing in Accra, Mr Opoku said the two ministries are working towards the same national development objectives. “We are working to actualise the same agenda. The Reset Agenda introduced by His Excellency President Mahama,” he said. The Minister acknowledged that misunderstandings can occur, even within families and smaller groups, but said such situations do not mean the parties are working separately. “You know even in our families, in our small circles, misunderstandings and miscommunications do occur. That never suggests that we are doing separatists. We are working together to actualise the Reset Agenda,” he said. Mr Opoku therefore urged the public not to create the impression that some government ministries are working against others. “Let us not create that erroneous impression that other ministries are working against some ministries,” he added. Government rules out total rice import ban On rice imports, Mr Opoku has also ruled out a total ban, saying domestic production currently accounts for about 56 percent of Ghana’s total rice demand. He said the remaining 44 percent supply gap would have to be met through imports while government works towards achieving rice self-sufficiency by 2028. The Minister explained that Ghana imports food because domestic production is currently insufficient to meet demand. “We import food because we are unable to produce. If tomorrow we are able to produce what we eat sufficiently, what is the essence of going to import food again? It doesn’t make sense. So we import what we cannot produce,” he said. Mr Opoku said the government’s approach is therefore to regulate imports rather than impose a complete ban. “So we must import only the 44 percent. And we need to ensure that importation is regulated. It is not about banning,” he said. He reiterated that the government’s ultimate objective is to achieve self-sufficiency in rice production by 2028.

title: N18m Fraud: Police arrest man in Ogun for allegedly impersonating prophet on Facebook
body:
The Police Command in Ogun State has arrested a suspect, Adewale Arojah, for allegedly impersonating a cleric on Facebook and defrauding victims of over N18 million.
The command’s spokesman Oluseyi Babaseyi, a deputy superintendent of police, disclosed this in a statement issued on Thursday in Abeokuta, the state capital.
Mr Babaseyi said the suspect was arrested by police operatives of the Ilaro division following a complaint lodged on 3 October by one Muyiwa Akogun, popularly known on Facebook as “Prophet Dr. Muyiwa Akogun.”
He said Mr Akogun had reported that members of the public were complaining about fraudulent activities being carried out through a duplicated Facebook account bearing his identity.
According to Mr Babaseyi, the suspect was a spiritual son of Mr Akogun and has allegedly used the cleric’s identity to deceive unsuspecting members of the public.
He said upon receipt of the complaint, the Divisional Police Officer (DPO), Ilaro, immediately deployed intelligence and detective operatives to track the suspect.
He noted that sustained technological monitoring and intelligence-led investigation led to the suspect’s arrest in a village in Ajegunle in the Ilaro/Ibogun axis.
“Upon his arrest, the suspect confessed during interrogation to impersonating Akogun and using his identity to offer fake prophecies and prayer services to unsuspecting victims.
“Preliminary investigation revealed that the suspect targeted people seeking spiritual assistance through the cleric’s Facebook page and allegedly defrauded victims in Nigeria and abroad of over N18 million.
“The suspect has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Eleweran, Abeokuta, for further investigation to determine the extent of the alleged offences and identify possible accomplices,” he said.
Mr Babaseyi quoted the Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, as commending the Ilaro operatives for their vigilance and swift response.
Mr Ojajuni reaffirmed the command’s commitment to tackling cybercrime, identity theft and other forms of criminality in the state.
He also advised members of the public to verify the authenticity of social media accounts belonging to religious leaders and public figures before engaging with them.
He urged citizens to avoid transferring money to unverified persons for spiritual remedies or other services.
Mr encouraged members of the public to report cybercrime, impersonation and suspicious activities through the Gateway Shield toll-free line, 0800 000 9111, or 09164859299 and 09154293464.

title: BRICS: Jinapor cautions Ghana against ‘free lunch’ as NPP demands scrutiny
body: Ranking Member of Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abu Jinapor, has cautioned the government to carefully assess the potential risks and benefits of Ghana’s decision to join BRICS, warning that the move could have implications for the country’s national interests. The Damongo MP said while membership of the emerging economic bloc could provide Ghana with new opportunities, including access to funding and diversified international partnerships, the country must not assume that the benefits would come without consequences. His comments come after Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa announced that Cabinet had approved Ghana’s decision to formally apply to join BRICS, as part of efforts to diversify the country’s international partnerships and deepen South-South cooperation. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show, Mr Jinapor said Ghana’s foreign policy must first and foremost serve the country’s national interest. “All foreign policy must be near to national interests. So there’s absolutely no benefit in a foreign policy move if it does not inure to the national interest of a particular country.” He acknowledged that joining BRICS could offer Ghana important benefits, particularly by expanding its partnerships beyond traditional allies. However, he insisted that the possible implications of the decision must be thoroughly examined. “There’s absolutely no free lunch,” he said. ‘What is the implication?’ Mr Jinapor said the government’s argument that BRICS membership could open up new sources of funding, particularly through the New Development Bank (NDB), required further scrutiny. He questioned whether Ghana would actually gain significant financial independence if access to such funding came with conditions involving existing international institutions. “We are told that we may be in a position to source some new funding from the New Development Bank of BRICS,” he said. “But we are also told that even to access funding from that bank, there’s a condition precedent that the IMF has to give authorisation. So if that is the case, what is the implication?” The former Lands and Natural Resources Minister said Parliament must also examine the possible impact of increased economic and political influence from major BRICS countries such as China and Russia. He said questions surrounding the extent of Chinese influence on Ghana’s economy and national life, as well as the implications of closer relations with Russia, should form part of the assessment. Ethiopia’s experience Mr Jinapor further urged the government to study the experiences of countries that have already joined BRICS before Ghana proceeds with its application. He cited Ethiopia as an example, saying its experience had produced both benefits and challenges. According to him, Ethiopia had benefited from assistance and funding opportunities through the New Development Bank but had also faced concerns over its trade imbalance and increased imports from BRICS countries, particularly China. “We need to take a look at what has been the experience of some of those countries which have joined,” he said. He argued that Ghana could learn valuable lessons by examining how membership has affected the economies and international relationships of the countries that have already joined the bloc. BRICS currently has 11 full members, including Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. South Africa relationship Mr Jinapor also questioned how Ghana’s existing relationship with South Africa could affect its participation in the bloc. South Africa is one of the founding members of BRICS, but the MP said Ghana’s bilateral relationship with the country was currently poor. “Our bilateral relationship with South Africa is almost at the bottom’s end,” he said. He therefore argued that the government must consider what the current state of Ghana-South Africa relations could mean for Ghana’s participation in a grouping in which Pretoria remains an important player. ‘We need a lot more reflection’ Mr Jinapor said Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee had only received a general briefing from the Foreign Affairs Minister on the government’s intention to pursue BRICS membership and had yet to fully interrogate the decision. “We need a lot more reflection on this particular move,” he said. He acknowledged the government’s stated objective of diversifying Ghana’s international partnerships and strengthening cooperation with developing countries. However, he stressed that Ghana’s long-standing policy of non-alignment must also be considered. “It is all good to diversify our partnerships, but without doubt, this will come with some implications as well, some of which may be adverse to our national interest as a country,” Mr Jinapor said. The government says the BRICS bid is intended to give Ghana greater options for development financing, trade, investment and industrialisation while complementing, rather than replacing, its existing relationships with traditional development partners.

title: Bono East Education Directorate invites basic school teachers for SHS/SHTS reposting
body: The Bono East Regional Education Directorate has opened an opportunity for suitably qualified professional teachers currently teaching at the basic school level to express interest in being reposted to selected Senior High Schools and Senior High Technical Schools (SHS/SHTS) across the region. According to a press release issued on Thursday, September 29, the initiative is aimed at addressing existing subject-teaching vacancies in schools where the services of qualified teachers are required. According to the Directorate, interested teachers must possess the relevant subject knowledge, academic background, professional competence, and teaching experience necessary to effectively teach at the SHS/SHTS level. Subjects with vacancies The areas in which teachers are being sought include: Visual Arts Home Economics (Food and Nutrition) Economics Clothing and Textiles Social Studies English Language Literature in English Wood Technology Physics Biology Chemistry Electricals/Electrical Technology Government Geography Graphic Design Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Christian Religious Studies (CRS) General Science Ghanaian Language (Asante Twi) Business Management Application process Teachers interested in the reposting opportunity are required to submit an application letter, together with copies of their relevant academic and professional certificates. Applications should be addressed to: The Regional Director Bono East Regional Education Office Post Office Box 50 Nkronza – B/E The Directorate has urged interested teachers to submit their documents to the appropriate office no later than Wednesday, October 21. The opportunity is specifically targeted at professional teachers currently serving in basic schools who meet the required academic and professional standards for teaching at the SHS/SHTS level. Teachers seeking consideration are therefore encouraged to ensure that their applications and supporting documents are submitted before the stated deadline.

title: Most Compensation for Uzbekistan’s Dok-1 Max Victims Remains Unpaid
body: Families affected by Uzbekistan’s Dok-1 Max poisoning scandal are still owed most of the 78 billion soums awarded in compensation, more than two years after the court verdict, according to the Bureau of Compulsory Enforcement . The case dates back to late 2022, when children across Uzbekistan fell ill after taking contaminated cold medicines, including Dok-1 Max, manufactured by the Indian pharmaceutical company Marion Biotech. Laboratory tests confirmed that samples of Dok-1 Max and another syrup, Ambronol, contained dangerous levels of diethylene glycol and/or ethylene glycol, toxic substances that can cause severe kidney damage and death. By February 2024, the medicines had been linked to the deaths of 68 children. On February 26, 2024, a court in Tashkent sentenced 23 defendants in connection with the scandal, including pharmaceutical executives and officials responsible for drug testing and regulation. Sardor Kariyev, a former head of Uzbekistan’s pharmaceutical development agency and state drug testing center, received an 18-year prison sentence. Singh Raghvendra Pratap, director of Quramax Medical, the company that imported the medicines into Uzbekistan, was sentenced to 20 years. An investigation by the country’s Anti-Corruption Agency identified failures in drug registration, certification, and oversight that had created opportunities for corruption. The issue of unpaid compensation has resurfaced following complaints on social media that payments had stopped. In a statement reported on October 7, the bureau said it was continuing efforts to recover money from Kariyev and other convicted defendants. Enforcement officers seized Kariyev’s properties in Tashkent. A nonresidential building on Furqat Street was sold at an electronic auction for 793 million soums (about $67,000). Residential properties in the Chilanzar district, valued at a combined 7.1 billion soums (about $601,000), remain up for auction. According to the bureau, proceeds from the property sale, together with money paid by Kariyev’s relatives, have enabled the distribution of 16.7 billion soums ($1.41 million) to the claimants. The recovered funds were divided equally among them. That leaves 61.3 billion soums (about $5.19 million) outstanding. The bureau has given no indication of when the families might receive the remaining compensation.

title: Current German authorities need war; Merz's actions prove it — Russian MFA
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. The current German authorities want war and make no secret of this; the authorities in Berlin - led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz, whose actions speak volumes - need it to somehow distract its own population from domestic problems and "prolong the life of an administration that has discredited itself and gone bankrupt," Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told a news briefing.
"I have already commented on Merz's visit to Kiev; his rhetoric, it seems to me, is yet another confirmation: they need war," she noted. "For people like Merz, it is simply the only way to somehow distract their own population from mounting domestic problems and prolong the life of their discredited and bankrupt administration."
According to Zakharova, Berlin's involvement in the Ukrainian conflict is not merely a matter of political assessment but an "accomplished fact."
"Germany is a participant in the conflict on the side of the Kiev regime. Germany itself has been stating this for years. What reason do we have not to hear these statements from Germany and not to see the reality that backs them up? To put it in such terms, it is simply an established fact," Zakharova emphasized. "The German leaders themselves have never actually hidden this.".

title: ICRC Moves To Optimise Zungeru Hydropower Plant’s 700MW Capacity, Holds Talks With Power, Water Ministries, BPE, Others
body: *Reviews contractual, operational limitations to plant’s efficiency The Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC) has stepped up its regulatory oversight of the $1.3 billion, 700-megawatt Zungeru Hydropower Project, with a view to improving the plant’s performance. The plant, which is operated under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) arrangement, is currently generating about 350 megawatts to the National Grid, according to the ICRC. The commission said the move was in line with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s charge to unlock the potential of Nigeria’s power sector. The President had reaffirmed the commitment in his 2026 Democracy Day speech, declaring that, “Electricity is a democratic dividend we owe every Nigerian.” The ICRC, acting under the ICRC Act 2005, convened a stakeholders’ meeting in Abuja involving the Federal Ministry of Power, Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, Bureau of Public Enterprises (BPE) and the concessionaire, Penstock Limited. The BPE acts as grantor under a power of attorney from the Ministry of Power. Speaking at the meeting, ICRC Director-General, Dr. Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh, said PPP assets such as Zungeru could not be allowed to operate below capacity as the administration works to address the country’s power challenges. He said the meeting was convened to identify and address the issues hindering the plant’s optimal performance. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s promise to Nigerians that he will solve the power problem is not words for the sake of it. It is a statement he meant, and he has charged all of us to support him by playing our roles to deliver on this promise,” he said. Ewalefoh explained that the ICRC was established as the regulator of PPPs and was therefore not a party to any PPP agreement, but was responsible for ensuring compliance by both the grantor and concessionaire with the terms and obligations contained in the agreement. Section 20 of the ICRC Act states: “The Commission shall: a. take custody of every concession agreement made under this Act and monitor compliance with the terms and conditions of such agreement; b. ensure efficient execution of any concession agreement or contract entered into by the Government; c. ensure compliance with the provisions of this Act; d. perform such other duties as may be directed by the President, from time to time and as are necessary or expedient to ensure the efficient performance of the function of the Commission under this Act.” Ewalefoh said, “Signing a concession agreement is only the first step; implementation of the terms in the PPP agreement is what delivers results. In PPP, risks are shared and no party is doing the other a favour. Our duty is to ensure sustainability, return on investment is achieved, services are delivered, and value for money is secured in the interest of the Nigerian people.” The ICRC DG disclosed that the ICRC Act 2005 defines the Commission’s reporting line to the President, adding that similar compliance reviews, would be carried out on other PPP- operated power plants, including Kainji, Jebba, Shiroro, Dadinkowa and Kashimbila, and a final report submitted to the President. Ewalefoh pledged the commission’s commitment to working with all stakeholders, particularly the Federal Ministry of Power, to ensure that PPP power projects contribute optimally to meeting Nigerians’ energy needs. He said the ICRC would also review other existing PPP arrangements to ensure optimal performance, stressing that efficiency was a key reason government assets were handed over to the private sector. At the end of the meeting, the ICRC and the stakeholders itemised the legal and operational issues raised and agreed on a date to reconvene.

title: Field services and SATCOM upgrade orders expand Gilat Defense’s presence across U.S. defense programs
body:
Petah Tikva, Israel, October 8, 2026 – Gilat Satellite Networks Ltd. (NASDAQ: GILT, TASE: GILT), a worldwide leader in satellite networking technology, solutions and services, today announced that Gilat DataPath has received orders totaling more than $8 million from the U.S. Department of War for field services and SATCOM system upgrades supporting deployed military communications systems. Deliveries are expected over the next 12 months. The orders further expand Gilat Defense’s presence across U.S. defense programs and reflect continued demand for its operational support capabilities and SATCOM expertise. The orders build on Gilat DataPath’s ongoing support of deployed U.S. military communications systems, combining field services with SATCOM upgrades to address evolving operational needs. This combination enables Gilat Defense to support customers throughout the operational life of their systems, maintaining existing capabilities while helping adapt networks to new mission requirements.. “These awards reflect the U.S. Department of War’s continued confidence in Gilat Defense’s ability to s upport mission-critical communications for defense operations ,” said Nicole Robinson, President of Gilat DataPath. “By combining advanced field services with proven SATCOM system upgrade capabilities, we help ensure deployed communications systems remain ready to support operational requirements whenever and wherever they are needed.” Source: Gilat Click here to read the latest issue of ESD.

title: Zelenskyy: Ukraine not in diplomatic corner, but Russia's mouth and economy must be shut
body:
Ukraine is currently not in a diplomatic corner, but it is necessary to shut Russia's mouth and close off its economy, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy has stated.

"We have heard about very many different moments during this war. Very many dead-end situations, difficult corners, and so on, and people, leaders, politicians drive themselves into a corner. title: South Korea test-flies its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon
body:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung delivers a speech during the Armed Forces Day at a military base in Gyeyong, South Korea, Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026. Jeon Heon-kyun/EPA POOL via AP hide caption
SEOUL, South Korea — South Korea flight-tested on Thursday its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon, designed to fly at least five times the speed of sound and evade missile defense systems, bringing Seoul closer to what it says could be game-changing weapons capabilities.
There was no immediate response from North Korea, which last week tested its own hypersonic missile that landed in the waters near Japan.
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung attended the test, saying it's a major step in strengthening the country's conventional defense capabilities, according to a statement. It did not elaborate where the test took place.
The statement said the weapon separated from its booster rocket at the planned altitude, then descended and maneuvered both vertically and horizontally before hitting a test target. It said once developed, the weapon would be able to strike key targets by surprise in the "Korean Peninsula theater of operations."
Lee stressed that South Korea "must secure our security through our own strength," and also inspected the country's most powerful Hyunmoo-5 ballistic missile on Thursday, his office said. It did not mention any direct comments by Lee on the North.
Tensions between the Koreas have increased in recent weeks after three South Korean soldiers were injured in land mine explosions last month near the heavily armed inter-Korean border.
The South's military and the U.S.-led United Nations Command concluded the blasts were caused by devices planted by North Korea, which has denied responsibility and ridiculed the South's demands for an apology.
North Korea has also stepped up weapons testing activity as its leader Kim Jong Un expands his military nuclear program while taking an increasingly hard line toward Seoul.
Kim has so far rebuffed U.S. President Donald Trump's calls to revive their diplomacy that broke down in 2019, with his government demanding that Washington abandon its "hostile" policy toward Pyongyang and drop demands for its denuclearization as a precondition for talks.
The tensions have been a setback for Lee, who favors engagement with North Korea and has tempered his rhetoric toward the North even as public anger grows over the mine blasts.
Lee has also called for strengthening South Korea's conventional defense capabilities while reducing its reliance on the United States, which unilaterally decided to scale back a major military exercise with the South in August, with Trump citing his "very good relationship" with Kim.
In its latest weapons test on Oct. 3, North Korea launched what it described as a hypersonic intermediate-range missile that it said flew more than 1,000 kilometers (621 miles). Japan said the missile landed in waters outside of its exclusive economic zone.
South Korea said it detected the missile flying more than 700 kilometers (435 miles), while Japan's Defense Ministry said it assessed that the missile flew about 680 kilometers (422 miles).
Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of the North Korean leader, claimed the differing flight estimates by the two U.S. allies showed they are incapable of properly tracking such a missile during its flight and would therefore not be able to intercept it.
