title: Diplomacy or war? US-Iran deadlock reaches fork in the road
body: Communication channels between the US and Iran remain open, with new messages exchanged through mediators, five diplomats and sources have told The National , as efforts to reach a lasting agreement to end the seven-month-old war remain elusive. The push to establish a fresh diplomatic path following the failure to achieve a breakthrough in New York during the UN General Assembly last month is unfolding against a backdrop of growing signs that both sides are preparing for a major confrontation. Last week, a source in Tehran told The National that Iran was preparing for a “major round of fighting”. Days later, US media reports suggested the Trump administration is weighing renewed strikes on Iran before the November 3 midterm elections, and that the Pentagon had ordered preparations for possible major combat operations. Gulf and Pakistani diplomatic sources said Qatar and Pakistan remain engaged in diplomacy with both sides, seeking to bring Washington and Tehran back to the negotiating table. “We remain engaged,” said a Pakistani diplomatic source. “Behind the scenes, negotiations are still happening, messages are being passed, and engagement is continuing.” Qatar and Pakistan have been acting as key intermediaries in the conflict, which erupted following US and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February. The two countries helped facilitate a settlement and brokered a provisional truce agreement in June that quickly fell apart. The war in the Middle East has jolted global energy markets and fuelled inflation. Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route. US President Donald Trump rejected Tehran’s latest offer and has warned that military operations could intensify after the midterm elections. “After Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi returned from New York, all diplomatic channels were effectively closed,” an Iranian source said. “This was one of the reasons behind the unusually strong warnings subsequently issued by Iran’s armed forces and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps [IRGC] regarding any further attack.” But a source close to Iranian negotiators said message exchanges have since resumed. “China has also occasionally played a role in trying to bring the two sides’ positions closer, at Washington’s request,” the source added. “The current exchange does not appear likely to produce meaningful results. The new US strategy is to continue exchanging messages while applying pressure intended to force Iran to submit to American demands. At the same time, Washington is mobilising for a third round of attacks against Iran.” On Thursday, Mr Araghchi said ​d Iran is still reviewing Washington's ​response to ⁠its proposal under which ⁠the ​Strait ⁠of Hormuz ‌could ​be reopened within seven days, and could reply within days. "The ⁠diplomatic process is still continuing," he confirmed. 'Making demands' Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said on Wednesday that Iran’s military could carry out further pre-emptive attacks if it deemed them necessary to deter future strikes. He also said the army had built up a large stockpile of newly developed offensive and defensive weapons, including missiles and drones, and was continuing to produce them. US officials have also refused to rule out further escalation after Washington sent a third aircraft carrier to the region. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said during a visit to Greece on Wednesday that Iran had missed multiple opportunities to reach a deal over its nuclear programme . Earlier, Vice President JD Vance stressed that Iran must make a “meaningful” reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity to meet Washington’s demands and end the war. On Tuesday, Qatar said that its mediation efforts between the US and Iran were ongoing, confirming that the two sides were exchanging messages and that Doha was still acting as a mediator. The comments came as Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni visited Doha this week and met Qatar’s Emir Sheikh. “The visit was publicly presented as being focused on the fate of the missing Iranian pilots, but there has also been a broader diplomatic purpose behind it,” said one of the Iranian sources. Iran says three pilots were detained by Qatari forces after their military aircraft were downed in Qatar’s airspace in March. Doha has denied the claim, saying its search-and-rescue teams recovered the remains of one Iranian pilot and handed them over to Tehran. The latest diplomatic activity also coincided with a visit to Pakistan by UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, who called on the US and Iran to end the conflict and return to diplomacy. But the latest exchanges have yet to overcome fundamental differences over how a potential agreement should be structured. “The US is making demands of Iran, but the Americans are not providing the Iranians with any guarantees,” said a source in Tehran. “The Iranians want firm guarantees that cannot subsequently be reversed. “There is a strong internal struggle between the IRGC, the official diplomatic channels and Parliament. There is significant opposition to negotiations because talks with the Americans have been tried repeatedly in the past and have failed.”

title: Rappler Recap: 4 things we learned from BIR witness about Sara Duterte wealth
body: MANILA, Philippines – Sara Duterte earned from the Davao City government even when she was already vice president, and registered a net income that was much lower than her declared net worth. Rappler’s Dwight de Leon recaps key details revealed by Anne Loraine Garcia-Marquez, a witness from the Bureau of the Internal Revenue, on the 36th day of the Vice President’s trial on Thursday, October 8. – Rappler.com

title: FIDF releases video library of October 7 testimonials, incl. ex-hostages, IDF soldiers
body: The New York-based Friends of the IDF (FIDF) nonprofit organization released an English-language digital video library on Sunday, archiving firsthand testimonies and accounts of the October 7 massacre.FIDF said that the library was intended to be accessible to supporters of Israel in the United States, including both Jews and Christians.“Since October 7, we have been moved by the surge of supporters across Jewish and Christian communities in the United States who want to understand more closely what happened in Israel on that devastating day and the days that followed and hear directly from the people who experienced it," Maj.-Gen. (Res.) Nadav Padan, CEO of FIDF, said.Former hostages, IDF soldiers film testimonials of October 7The archive features over 12 hours of footage consisting of over 50 filmed testimonies from former hostages, IDF soldiers, and the families of massacre victims.Among those who gave their testimonials for the library are Moshe and Shira Shapira, parents of St.-Sgt. Aner Shapira; Rabbi Doron Peretz, father of Capt. Daniel Peretz; Col. Elad Edri; wounded soldier Izzy Ezagui; and former hostages Noa Argamani, Amit Soussana, Maya Regev, Almog Meir Jan, Edan Alexander, and Maxim Harkin."Three years later, it is important not only to preserve these testimonies, but also to make them accessible in English to the communities that support Israel and IDF soldiers," Padan said. "This library allows them to hear firsthand from soldiers, hostage survivors, and families, and to learn the personal stories behind October 7."

Xbox is launching a new division, called “XP,” that’s dedicated to Xbox experiences that aren’t video games, including films and TV adaptations, consumer products, live events, and partnerships with creators and brands. Different teams at Xbox already do this work, but it will all now fall under the centralized XP division.
XP formalizes four “investment areas,” according to a blog post by Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball:
XBOX PICTURES: Bringing our worlds and characters to new audiences through film, television, and other forms of linear storytelling.
XBOX PRODUCTS: Creating products that are authentic to the fandom that allow fans to celebrate and express the franchises they love.
XBOX PLACES: Bringing communities together through live events, immersive experiences, attractions, broadcasts, and destinations.
XBOX PARTNERSHIPS: Working with creators, brands, and communities to develop new experiences, sponsorships, and brand partnerships.
XP will be led by Kayleen Walters, who is moving from her role heading up Minecraft -maker Mojang to be president of the new division. Mojang will next be led by Maria Angelidou-Smith, who is leaving her job as Reddit’s chief product officer to become CEO of Mojang and Minecraft , and she starts on October 19th.
Xbox is already developing several film and TV adaptations, including a sequel to the successful A Minecraft Movie , a third season of Prime Video’s Fallout live-action series , a Call of Duty film , and a Diablo animated series for Netflix .
“Great games remain at the center of these franchises and at the heart of XBOX,” Ball says. “XP will partner with the best creative minds across our studios, along with trusted partners, to build on that foundation and create more ways for people to experience the worlds they love.”
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma also sent an email about the changes to employees. She had previously told staff that the company would build “long-term plans” for Xbox’s franchises “across film, television, consumer products, sponsorship, live experiences” as part of her broader “reset” of the Xbox business. Since taking over in February, Sharma has enacted sweeping layoffs , sold off studios, and made big changes to Xbox’s studio structure, including putting Activision in charge of Halo .
In 2012, Microsoft established Xbox Entertainment Studios to make film and TV adaptations of Xbox games, but shut it down two years later .

title: ‘Thousands Ready This Year’: Ukraine to Get SPYS Interceptors
body:
Thousands of new SPYS interceptor drones designed to destroy Russia’s jet-powered attack UAVs are ready for delivery to Ukraine this year, German defense company Quantum Systems said.
The company plans to provide tens of thousands of the interceptors under a German-financed program, Quantum Systems Vice President Matthias Lehna said during a press briefing in Berlin on Wednesday, Oct. 7, according to Ukrinform .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“Over the weekend, an LOI [letter of intent] was signed to secure a package of tens of thousands of SPYS, which are capable of intercepting jet-powered drones,” Lehna said.
Asked when the first systems could reach Ukraine, he replied: “Thousands of units are ready for delivery this year.”
A letter of intent outlines the planned cooperation but does not constitute a final procurement contract.
SPYS was jointly developed by Quantum Systems and Ukrainian manufacturer WIY Drones through their joint venture, Quantum WIY Industries.
The interceptor was created to counter fast, maneuvering aerial targets, including Russia’s Geran-4 and Geran-5 jet-powered attack drones.
According to WIY Drones , SPYS can reach a maximum speed of 480 kilometers per hour and has a cruising speed of 200 to 250 kph.
It has a tactical radius of 15 kilometers, a maximum flight distance of 30 kilometers and an operating altitude of up to 4,000 meters. Its stated maximum flight duration is 10 minutes.
The system supports automatic takeoff, deployment toward the intercept zone and AI-assisted terminal guidance. It can be equipped with optical (daylight) or thermal cameras and integrated with radars and other sources of targeting data.
Its developers say the interceptor is intended to protect military positions, mobile units and critical infrastructure.
SPYS incorporates lessons from the combat use of STRILA, an earlier interceptor produced by WIY and Quantum Systems.
Quantum Systems plans to use production capacity already established for STRILA to accelerate the manufacture of SPYS.
“And I am talking about several thousand per month,” Lehna said when discussing potential production volumes.
In March, Quantum Systems announced that Ukraine’s Security and Defense Forces had tasked it with providing 15,000 STRILA interceptors to the National Guard. The SPYS package is a separate project focused on the faster jet-powered threat.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced financing for several tens of thousands of Quantum Systems interceptors during his visit to Kyiv on Sunday, Oct. 4.
The drones will be manufactured in Ukraine as part of Germany’s military assistance package for the winter of 2026-2027, the company said .
Merz’s visit produced 15 German-Ukrainian agreements worth more than €8.5 billion , covering air defense, drones, missiles and energy protection.
“Ukraine needs interceptor drones at industrial scale,” Quantum Systems co-CEO Sven Kruck said. “By expanding production in Ukraine, we can respond faster to the immediate threat.”
Lehna said Ukraine’s success rate against Russian jet-powered drones had risen from initially low levels to more than 30 percent, with some recent attacks showing intercept rates above 50 percent.
He cautioned that the improvement did not result from drone interceptors alone.
Ukraine combines multiple systems, including electronic warfare, ground-based defenses, interceptor drones and F-16 fighter aircraft, which have increasingly been used against the faster Russian UAVs.
Kyiv is separately seeking large quantities of 20-millimeter ammunition for its F-16s , allowing pilots to use their onboard cannons against drones instead of expending scarce and expensive air-to-air missiles.
Russia launched almost 3,500 jet-powered drones against Ukraine in September , according to Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson Yuriy Ihnat.
The growing number of fast drones has forced Ukraine and its partners to develop cheaper interception methods that can be produced and deployed on a scale comparable to Russia’s expanding attacks.

title: Wa West MP commissions education and health infrastructure projects across rural communities
body: The Member of Parliament for Wa West, Peter Lanchene Toobu, alongside officials of the Wa West District Assembly, has commissioned and handed over several completed educational and health infrastructure projects across rural communities in the district. The tour covered projects at Varempere, Gombile and Dabo, and concluded with a grand durbar at Pase. The completed infrastructure includes a six-unit primary classroom block at Varempere, a long-stalled Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) compound at Gombile, a Junior High School (JHS) block at Dabo, and a modern CHPS compound with residential staff quarters at Pase. Addressing the durbars, Peter Lanchene Toobu highlighted the principle of continuity in public administration, arguing that changes in government must never justify the abandonment of taxpayer-funded infrastructure. “We don’t really care whether a project was started by President Kufuor or President Nana Akufo-Addo. As long as it was meant for the people and funded by the state, it must not be abandoned,” Toobu stated. “Democracy should not be reduced to voting alone; the true essence of governance lies in the tangible developments brought to communities between elections.” At Varempere Primary School, the commissioning of the six-unit classroom block addressed long-standing infrastructure deficits. The MP also handed over 50 plastic chairs to support early childhood education and promised additional furniture. The District Director of Education, Seidu Kassim, handed the keys to community leaders and urged them to protect the investment. “This building is now in the hands of Varempere. Let us embrace a culture of maintenance so that we do not return here to find broken fixtures and hanging windows,” Mr Kassim said. PTA Chairman Bayor Adams thanked the MP and the Assembly, pledging that parents and teachers would take care of the facility. At Dabo, where a modern JHS block was commissioned, the MP warned contractors against delivering substandard work, noting that an earlier school block constructed in 2006 had deteriorated within four years. Dabo JHS students expressed their excitement about the new facility. Bonle Bernice said: “Previously, moving motorbikes and pedestrians distracted us because our classroom lacked doors and windows. Now, we have a quiet and secure place to learn, and we promise to study hard and score single-digit aggregates.” Another pupil, Ganiu Misbawu, welcomed the new structure but appealed for additional teachers to help students prepare for the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE). Bultou Naa, Naa Touganle M. Philip, who spoke on behalf of the representative of the Dabo Naa, commended the MP and the Assembly while requesting the electrification of the school to support ICT learning. He also appealed for a modern community market and the establishment of a technical Senior High School. The commissioning tour also significantly improved access to healthcare for residents in Gombile and Pase. At Gombile, where a CHPS compound that was started in 2019 was revived and completed with legacy funds from the District Assemblies Common Fund, community elder Dole Naa, Naa Iddrisu Lala, known as “Nansaldau”, said the facility would help prevent maternal emergencies. “When a woman goes into labour in the middle of the night, transporting her over rough roads on a motorbike has always been dangerous. This facility brings dignity and safety to our mothers and wives,” he stated. The MP assured residents that the Gombile CHPS compound would soon be connected to the government’s off-grid solar programme. At the grand durbar in Pase, Kong Naa, Naa Yendau Dong Issac, commended the initiative and called for united community support to maintain the clinic so it could eventually be expanded into a full health centre. The Assembly Member for the Dorimon Electoral Area, Fuseini Saaka, also commended the Assembly and the MP. He explained that Pase initially had a community-initiated health outpost before the Assembly intervened to construct the permanent and fully furnished CHPS facility. He noted that neighbouring communities, including Guo, Kong and Kondoni, would directly benefit from the facility, sparing residents the need to travel long distances to Dorimon to access healthcare. Mr Saaka pledged that the community would recruit a security guard and cleaner. He also made two specific appeals. “We appeal to the authorities to post a midwife here to assist the nurse and ensure safer deliveries for our pregnant women. Furthermore, Dorimon is central to our traditional area, and the current health centre is no longer adequate; we urgently appeal for it to be upgraded into a polyclinic.” The Wa West District Health Director, Cecilia Kakariba, described the Pase facility as “hope and life for rural people”, highlighting that the inclusion of staff quarters would end the reliance on intermittent outreach visits. Ms Kakariba appealed for additional equipment and services to make the clinic fully operational. “To provide comprehensive service, we urgently need a dedicated motorbike for the nurse to collect drugs from Wechiau and carry out outreach, electricity and water connections, and a solar vaccine refrigerator to safely store critical vaccines and medicines,” she said. She also warned residents against neglecting the security of health workers, noting that previous security lapses in the district had forced the withdrawal of some health workers. Representing the District Chief Executive, the Deputy Coordinating Director of the Wa West District Assembly, Martin K. Berisie, noted that the Assembly had earlier commissioned an institutional guest house and provided furniture in Wechiau, alongside other projects at Tanina, Dodoma and Metii. “So, development is a shared responsibility. While the government is providing the resources, the Assembly is providing the technical know-how, the MP is providing or lobbying for more development projects for the district, and the traditional authorities are also releasing the land for us to construct these projects,” Mr Berisie said.

title: EU extends Russia sanctions over hybrid attacks and destabilization abroad for another year
body:
According to Ukrinform, the Council of the EU announced this on its website .
The decision was made in light of Russia's continued and intensified hybrid activities, including Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI) against the EU and its member states and partners.
Restrictive measures in view of Russia's destabilizing activities currently apply to 80 individuals and 20 entities.
Those listed are subject to an asset freeze, and EU citizens and companies are forbidden from making funds, financial assets or economic resources available to them. Natural persons also face a travel ban that prohibits them from entering or transiting through EU territories.
The framework for restrictive measures in response to Russia's destabilizing actions was set up on October 8, 2024 to target those engaged in actions and policies by the government of the Russian Federation, which undermine the fundamental values of the EU and its member states, their security, stability, independence and integrity. The sanctions regime targets also those responsible for Russia's hybrid activities against third countries and international organizations.
The European Union stressed that it would continue to draw on the full range of tools available to protect, prevent, deter from and respond to such malicious behavior.
On October 7, the ambassadors of EU member states (COREPER) agreed on the largest-ever expansion of the sanctions list against Russia.
According to diplomatic sources, the new restrictions cover 1,569 individuals and entities, including 743 individuals and 826 companies, linked to Russia's military-industrial complex, as well as 77 individuals involved in illegitimate elections to the Russian State Duma held in the occupied territories of Ukraine.
The expansion will form part of the implementation of the sanctions agenda announced by EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and is expected to be formally approved at the October 12 meeting of the EU Foreign Affairs Council.

title: 7 Best Resources to Learn About Self-Evolving AI Agents
body:
The next step for AI agents? Self-improvement. Here are 7 resources to get started.
AI agents are quickly moving beyond systems that simply receive an instruction, call a tool, and return an answer. A growing research direction asks a more ambitious question: can an AI agent improve itself through experience? These systems are known as self-evolving (or self-improving / recursively self-improving) AI agents. Rather than keeping the same behavior after deployment, they may learn from previous failures, accumulate memory, build reusable skills, improve prompts, adapt tool-use strategies, or modify parts of their own reasoning pipeline. In this article, we will cover the 7 best resources to learn about self-evolving AI agents.
I would recommend this as the first resource before you study agents that modify themselves. It will help you understand how ordinary agents work. It teaches the basic Think/Act/Observe loop, tool use, reasoning, agent frameworks such as smolagents , LangGraph and LlamaIndex , agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) , function-calling fine-tuning, observability, and evaluation. The course is free and includes hands-on assignments and a final benchmark-based project.
Stanford's CS329A: Self-Improving AI Agents is probably the best structured academic starting point for this topic. It covers self-improvement techniques for large language models (LLMs) — including Constitutional AI, verifiers, test-time compute, and reinforcement learning — as well as tool use, memory, multi-step reasoning and planning, evaluation frameworks, and applications such as coding agents and research assistants. The best part is that the syllabus is organized around research papers rather than just agentic frameworks, so it gives you a deeper understanding of how agents improve themselves . I would highly recommend following the lecture sequence, reading the papers, and trying to reproduce a few of the ideas.
This survey is one of the most useful resources for understanding what researchers actually mean by a self-evolving agent . It frames evolution as a feedback loop connecting the agent, its environment, system inputs, and an optimizer. The survey discusses which parts of an agent can evolve — including the model, memory, prompts, tools, and multi-agent organization — and covers domain-specific systems in programming, finance, and biomedicine.
This is a useful complement to the previous survey. It tells you what the field looks like in 2026. It separates improvement of the foundation model itself from improvement of the agent's scaffolding — such as prompts, memory, tools, skills, and control logic. An agent that rewrites its prompt, one that builds a skill library, and one that fine-tunes its own model are doing very different things. This survey provides a system-level taxonomy for understanding those differences and discusses evaluation and open research problems.
You can use this repo as a bibliography after reading one of the surveys above. The repository organizes papers by what is being improved: model parameters, prompts, memory, tools, skills, and complete agent scaffolds. It also collects benchmarks, courses, talks, workshops, code, and newer 2026 work such as OpenSkill and evolving skill systems. Given how quickly agent research is developing, a continuously updated bibliography like this is often more useful than repeatedly searching arXiv from scratch.
This is a broad research map that covers model-level self-improvement, harness and scaffold evolution, memory, embodied systems, automated AI R&D, benchmarks, and safety. It includes papers, frameworks, tools, and evaluation resources across these different directions. It's extremely useful for seeing how self-evolving agents fit into the larger recursive self-improvement (RSI) landscape.
This list is narrower and more operational. It focuses on the "harness" — the surrounding system of tools, memory, control loops, evaluation, and so on. It includes foundational essays, papers, and practical engineering perspectives, making it useful for understanding how agents can improve not just their outputs, but the harness and processes they use to produce those outputs .
In my opinion, a sensible learning order for this topic would be Hugging Face Agents Course → Stanford CS329A → the two surveys → Awesome Self-Improving Agents → Awesome RSI → Awesome Harness Self-Improvement. The field is progressing rapidly, so don't worry about trying to read everything. Pick a direction that interests you, follow a few key papers, and build something yourself.
Kanwal Mehreen is a machine learning engineer and a technical writer with a profound passion for data science and the intersection of AI with medicine. She co-authored the ebook "Maximizing Productivity with ChatGPT". As a Google Generation Scholar 2022 for APAC, she champions diversity and academic excellence. She's also recognized as a Teradata Diversity in Tech Scholar, Mitacs Globalink Research Scholar, and Harvard WeCode Scholar. Kanwal is an ardent advocate for change, having founded FEMCodes to empower women in STEM fields.

title: VFD Group creates first-ever deputy managing director role, announces appointee
body:
VFD Group Plc has announced the appointment of Ijeoma Emezie-Ezigbo as its Deputy Managing Director, effective 5 October.
The company disclosed this in a statement on Thursday, noting that the appointment marked a significant step in the Group’s institutional development and executive leadership structure.
VFD Group recently created the role, and Ms Emezie-Ezigbo is the company’s first deputy managing director.
The Group Managing Director, Nonso Okpala, said creating the Deputy Managing Director role reflects VFD Group’s commitment to building the Group as an institution with the governance depth, leadership capacity, and succession structures required for long-term sustainability.
“Our ambition is to build an organisation whose strength extends beyond any individual, supported by strong systems, capable leadership and a clear institutional direction,” Mr Okpala said.
He added that Ms Emezie-Ezigbo’s experience in transaction advisory, corporate finance and strategic management will bring valuable depth to its executive leadership as the company continues to build for the future.
Speaking on her appointment, Ms Emezie-Ezigbo expressed her commitment to support the company with sound decision-making and creating sustainable long-term value across the Group.
“I am pleased to join VFD Group at this important stage in its institutional journey. I look forward to contributing my experience in corporate finance, transactions and strategic management to strengthening governance, supporting sound decision-making and creating sustainable long-term value across the Group,” she said.
Ms Emezie-Ezigbo brings more than two decades of experience spanning corporate finance, transaction advisory, mergers and acquisitions, business valuation and strategic financial management across Nigeria, Canada and other African markets.
She most recently served as Partner and Head of Transaction Services, West Africa, at KPMG Nigeria.
Her career also includes senior roles at Stanbic IBTC Group, IBM Canada and Canadian Tire Corporation.
Ms Emezie-Ezigbo’s appointment is expected to deepen VFD Group’s corporate governance framework, strengthen strategic oversight and reinforce leadership continuity as the investment company advances its long-term growth ambitions.
The newly appointed deputy managing director holds a First-Class Honours degree in Business Administration, specialising in Marketing, from the University of Nigeria.
She also holds a Master of Finance degree from Cass Business School, London, and has completed the Advanced Management Programme at Lagos Business School.
Her professional qualifications include Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (FCA), Associate Chartered Certified Accountant (ACCA UK), Chartered Professional Accountant in Ontario, Canada, and Certified Valuation Analyst.
Ms Emezie-Ezigbo joins the Group’s executive leadership alongside Group Managing Director Nonso Okpala and Executive Directors Folajimi Adeleye and Morenike Ominike. The Board is chaired by Olatunde Busari (SAN).
The appointment forms part of VFD Group’s broader commitment to institutionalisation, with a focus on strengthening governance, developing leadership capacity and building a resilient organisation positioned for sustainable growth beyond any single individual.

title: Rivers 2027: Amaechi ally dumps ADC, returns to APC
body: By Daniel Abia P/HARCOURT — A former political ally of ex-Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi, Dr Sokonte Davies, has left the African Democratic Congress (ADC), citing better prospects within the All Progressives Congress (APC). Davies, a former governorship aspirant and founding member of the ADC, announced his decision to return to the APC on Wednesday in a statement sent to Vanguard. He said the decision followed extensive consultations with his family, political associates, constituents and elders, adding that he had assessed where he could best serve the interests of his people and contribute to the political and economic development of Rivers State. Davies, in the statement titled “Return to the Progressive Family: My Decision to Rejoin the All Progressives Congress (APC),” said he was also committed to contributing to the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and the political stability of Rivers State. He said, “After extensive consultation with my family, political associates, constituents, and elders, and following the cessation of my membership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) recently, I hereby announce my decision to return to the All Progressives Congress (APC), a party in which I was privileged to be a foundational member.” Davies said his decision was informed by “deep reflection, patriotic conviction, and a clear-eyed assessment” of where he could best serve his constituents and contribute to national development. He described the APC as the platform he considered most suitable for progressive governance, national unity and grassroots development. “For me, this is a homecoming,” he said. Davies recalled his role as a founding member of the APC, saying he remained committed to the party’s founding ideals, including democracy, social justice, true federalism, inclusive growth and respect for the rule of law. The former ADC chieftain described his time in the opposition party as one marked by service and commitment. He thanked the leadership and members of the ADC, particularly its national leadership, for the opportunity to serve and the relationships built during his membership. “I bear no ill will. Politics is a marketplace of ideas; we can disagree without being disagreeable,” he said. Davies wished the ADC well in its future endeavours, while pledging to work with APC members and stakeholders at the ward, local government, state and national levels. “I return to the APC as a loyal and committed member. I pledge to continue to uphold the party’s work with constitution, respect its leadership, and work with all stakeholders to strengthen the party at the ward, local government, state, and national levels,” he said. He also pledged to deploy his experience, networks and goodwill to support the APC’s vision and the government’s developmental agenda. Davies urged his supporters and associates to remain calm, law-abiding and focused, while calling on those who shared his political ideals to join the APC. “Let us join hands with like-minded progressives to build the party and serve our people. I call on all who share our ideals to join the APC as we work together for a better future,” he said. The former governorship aspirant also expressed appreciation to the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, for what he described as his “very warm and excited friendly reception.” He also thanked APC National Vice Chairman, Chief Victor Giadom, for facilitating his return to the party, as well as party elders and members for their encouragement and acceptance. “Together, we shall work for the Nigeria and Rivers State of our dreams,” Davies pledged. title: ‘There don’t seem to be prospects of a negotiated settlement,’ Rubio says of Russia–Ukraine war
body: There is currently no prospect of a peaceful settlement to the Russia-Ukraine war, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in an interview with the Greek newspaper Kathimerini. Rubio said the war is now in a state of “strategic stalemate”: Russia continues to demand full control over Donbas, a condition Ukraine considers completely unacceptable. Strategic stalemates are only broken in one of two ways: a) through a negotiated settlement, or b) through escalation by one side or both that ends up spreading beyond the confines of the original conflict. Right now, there don’t seem to be prospects of a negotiated settlement. Direct talks between Russia and Ukraine, mediated by the United States, took place in early 2026. The talks were interrupted by the start of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and have not resumed since. Both Ukraine and Russia officially say they are ready for new rounds of talks. title: F-35 Jets Meant for Turkey Spotted in U S Warehouse
body:
Six F-35A Lightning II fighter jets manufactured for Turkey remain stored at a U.S. facility years after Ankara was removed from the F-35 program, according to images of the aircraft and reporting on their status.
Turkey joined the F-35 program in 2002, with its defense companies entering the aircraft’s manufacturing and supply chain in 2003. Ankara contributed about $1.4 billion to the program and planned to acquire 30 F-35As initially, with a long-term requirement of up to 100 aircraft.
The six aircraft were assigned Turkish tail numbers and stationed in the United States for Turkish pilot training. The first Turkish F-35 was delivered in 2018, and Turkish pilots began training flights with the aircraft.
The United States removed Turkey from the program in 2019 after Ankara acquired Russia’s S-400 air-defense system, citing concerns over the Russian system’s compatibility with the F-35 and potential exposure of sensitive aircraft capabilities. The six completed jets were not transferred to the U.S. Air Force and instead remained in storage.
The aircraft are maintained under preservation procedures designed to prevent corrosion and protect sensitive systems, including the use of specialized fluids, sealed components and periodic maintenance.
The S-400 remains the principal obstacle to Turkey's return to the F-35 program and the lifting of U.S. CAATSA sanctions. One proposed solution is transferring the S-400s to a third country, but Russia has reportedly conditioned such a move on the recipient being a friendly state that would not transfer the systems to Ukraine.
Recent contacts between U.S. President Donald Trump and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan have fueled speculation about Turkey's possible return to the F-35 program. A proposed four-stage roadmap reportedly includes returning the six stored aircraft to Turkey, arranging a new order for 30 F-35As, restoring Turkish defense companies to the program's production partnership, and integrating Turkish-made weapons such as the SOM-J cruise missile into the F-35 fleet.
Any return, however, would depend on resolving the S-400 dispute and related U.S. sanctions.

title: One injured in Russian attack on Kyiv dies in hospital – official
body:
The death toll from the Russian attack on the capital on Thursday, October 8, has increased after a wounded victim succumbed to injuries in the hospital, the Kyiv City Military Administration reports.

"Unfortunately, a man who sustained injuries as a result of today's Russian attack on the capital has died in the hospital," the administration said in a statement on its Telegram channel.

Previously, reports indicated three fatalities and 14 injured, two of whom were in serious condition.

title: 2027: Obi doesn’t need governors to win South-South — IHIF
body: By Emmanuel Iheaka OWERRI — The Igbo Heroes and Icons Foundation (IHIF) has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, does not need the backing of state governors to secure support in the South-South geopolitical zone in the 2027 election. Leader of the foundation, Hon. Chinedu Nsofor, stated this while reacting to comments attributed to the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, on Obi’s political strength and reliance on popular support rather than political heavyweights. Nsofor said the key question ahead of the 2027 election should not be whether Obi has access to government machinery, but whether a candidate can build broad national support based on character, competence, record of service and the confidence of ordinary citizens. He said the election should not be reduced to a contest between political establishments or ethnic calculations, but should give Nigerians an opportunity to assess the records, programmes and governing philosophies of the various candidates. The foundation also rejected the assumption that political support could be automatically determined by government structures or financial resources. “Rivers State has an electorate capable of making its own political judgment, and voters will assess competing candidates according to their own interests and experiences,” the group said. IHIF argued that the 2023 presidential election demonstrated that a significant grassroots movement could emerge around a candidate outside the traditional political power structure. The foundation said its advocacy for an Igbo presidency was not intended to exclude any region, religion or ethnic group, but was based on what it described as equity, justice and fairness. It noted that different Nigerian communities had historically sought and received support from other regions in their quests for the presidency. The group called for a national conversation involving the North, South-West, North-Central, South-South and South-East on whether the presidency should continue to rotate among the country’s major geopolitical constituencies. It also urged political leaders to focus their campaigns and programmes on rebuilding the economy, reducing poverty, improving education and healthcare, addressing insecurity and ensuring responsible management of public resources. title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Building new revenue streams
body: Insight. Revenue diversification can strengthen an organisation’s resilience and create new avenues for growth. CEOs should examine whether existing capabilities, customer relationships, intellectual property, distribution networks, or partnerships can support additional sources of revenue. However, new revenue streams should complement the organisation’s strategy rather than create unnecessary complexity. Key Strategies: Identify assets and capabilities that can create additional value. Examine unmet needs among existing customers. Explore complementary products and services. Assess recurring and scalable revenue opportunities. Establish clear financial and strategic criteria for new ventures. CEO Leadership Actions. Review the organisation’s dependence on its existing revenue sources. Identify at least two credible opportunities for revenue diversification. Require all new revenue initiatives to demonstrate a clear path to customer value and financial sustainability. Actionable Tip. Ask: “What else could we offer our existing customers that solves a meaningful problem and creates additional value?” Why This Matters? A diversified revenue base can provide greater flexibility when market conditions change. The CEO’s responsibility is to ensure that new revenue streams are strategically relevant, financially sound, and manageable within the organisation’s capabilities. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader, and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

title: Sweden expands domestic role in Gripen E engine support
body:
Sweden wants to expand its domestic expertise in the engine that powers the Saab Gripen E/F fighter , under a new cooperation agreement between Saab and GKN Aerospace announced on Thursday.
The agreement follows a Swedish government decision to strengthen national capabilities related to the General Electric F414-GE-39E engine, known locally as the RM16. GKN will progressively assume greater technical and support responsibilities within the Gripen E/F program.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
The move does not introduce a new engine supplier or replace General Electric, which developed the F414 in the United States. Instead, it seeks to give Swedish industry a larger role in maintaining and supporting the propulsion system throughout the fighter's service life.
GKN already has experience with the RM16. In 2020, the company began developing domestic support and maintenance capabilities for the engine at its Trollhättan facilities in Sweden. The latest agreement aims to expand those activities through closer cooperation with Saab.
GKN has a much broader role in the engine used by the earlier Gripen C/D. The Volvo RM12, derived from the General Electric F404, was adapted for Swedish requirements and has long been supported by the company's domestic engineering and maintenance operations.
GKN holds the RM12 type certificate and has responsibilities covering technical development, maintenance, repairs and long-term support. Its involvement also includes modernization work intended to extend the engine's operational life.
The Gripen E/F uses the more powerful F414, and Sweden does not have the same level of technical authority over its propulsion system. The new agreement could narrow that difference, although Saab has not specified which additional activities will be transferred to GKN.
The companies have not announced new manufacturing arrangements, investment figures or a timetable for the expansion. There is also no indication that GKN will take over production of complete F414 engines from General Electric.
The agreement comes as Saab expands the international customer base for the Gripen E/F. Brazil remains the largest export customer, with an original order for 36 aircraft and a major industrial partnership with Saab through Embraer. The Brazilian manufacturer operates a Gripen E final assembly line at Gavião Peixoto and participated in the development of the two-seat Gripen F.
In July, Saab and Embraer signed a preliminary agreement covering the potential production of another 20 Gripen fighters in Brazil for international customers.
Colombia has ordered 17 Gripen E/F fighters, comprising 15 single-seat aircraft and two two-seat versions. Thailand has contracted four aircraft, while Ukraine is also entering the program through agreements with Sweden for new Gripen E fighters.

title: Lithuania Deploys Troops to Kaliningrad Border
body:
On Wednesday, Oct. 7, LRT reported that Lithuania’s Defense Minister, Robertas Kaunas, had ordered the deployment of military personnel to assist border guards along the border with Kaliningrad .
The initial deployment of 100 troops came in response to a request from Interior Minister Martynas Katelinas following an incident on the Latvia-Belarus border during the night of Oct. 5-6, when 20 migrants, reportedly escorted by armed men, attempted to cross illegally into Latvia.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Speaking to LRT, Kaunas said the deployment was initially planned for “a couple of weeks” but stressed that the situation would be continuously assessed. If necessary, both the duration of the mission and the number of troops could be increased.
“The process is dynamic. We are monitoring the environment and here, together with the Minister of Internal Affairs, with the approval of the Government, we will respond as necessary,” Kaunas said.
The attempted incursion into Latvia is being viewed as another example of Russian-backed hybrid activity aimed at increasing pressure on Europe’s eastern borders. Per LRT reports, nearly 12,000 people have been prevented from illegally crossing the Latvian border from Belarus this year. In August, several individuals were apprehended after using two tunnels dug between the two countries.
According to Latvia’s Interior Minister, Jānis Dombrava, writing on X , the Oct. 5-6 incident involved a group of masked and armed individuals who attempted to push around 20 illegal migrants into Latvian territory from Belarus. The group openly threatened Latvian military personnel and border guards.
On Tuesday morning, Oct. 6, the armed group reportedly crossed the border again, vandalized an electrical distribution cabinet, and removed border surveillance cameras before retreating back into Belarus ahead of a response by Latvian authorities.
On Facebook , Kaunas said that Lithuania was also increasingly concerned that similar incidents could occur along its own border. In addition, authorities were monitoring the growing risk of a possible Russian mobilization, which could trigger an influx of Russian citizens seeking to avoid conscription.
“Security is being strengthened with preventive purposes, seeing signals of a possible increase in aggressive foreigners due to possible mobilization in the Russian federation,” Kaunas wrote.
One issue of particular concern is the lack of any physical barriers on the border with Kaliningrad, to which he noted:
“On the border with Belarus, we also have physical protection, that is, a wall and a fence have been built, so the measures to protect the border have been strengthened. At the same time, on the Kaliningrad side, we do not have physical barriers, so more people are needed to ensure border protection. This is a question of human resources.”
The Interior Minister echoed these points on Wednesday on Facebook, saying: “We are strengthening the protection of the border with Kaliningrad - we are using the military. After yesterday’s incident on the Latvian border, having assessed the overall security situation in the region and signals that Russia may announce mobilization, we are taking additional preventive actions.”

title: Canada’s Anne Carson wins Nobel literature prize
body: The Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded on Thursday to Canadian poet Anne Carson, an essayist and classicist who brings a modern twist to mysticism and antiquity in her writings about love, desire and despair. The 76-year-old — who announced in 2024 that she has Parkinson’s disease — was honoured “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature,” the Swedish Academy said. The permanent secretary of the Academy, Ingrid Carlberg, said she had briefly spoken to Carson. “We didn’t have so much time to speak. All she had time to tell me was that she is for the moment in Iceland, where she’s listening to the wind.” “She was taken by surprise, but very happy. I could hear that in her voice.” A professor of classics with a background in dead languages, literature, anthropology and history, she was described by The New York Times in 2001 as “one of the great pasticheurs.” Her unique contemporary poetry earned her several key literary prizes in the 1990s, including the 1996 Lannan Award and the 1997 Pushcart Prize. A year later, “Autobiography of Red: A Novel in Verse” — loosely based on the Greek myth of the monster Geryon and Herakles but transformed into a modern tale of a gay love triangle — received widespread praise. The Academy said almost all of Carson’s literary production “has centred upon the intersection between the philologist’s obsession with words and the poet’s desire for new meaning.” It singled out her poem “Nox”, printed on one continuous sheet of paper in homage to her brother who died in 2000, as “an unforgettable work”. “Palpable here is a deep sense of loss that works its way up from below. The result is a creation as sculptural as it is literary, an epitaph in the form of a box containing an accordion-fold-out of pictures, letters and other written texts dedicated to her dead brother,” the Academy said. Carson has been mentioned as a possible Nobel laureate for years. – Women under-represented – Many literary critics had predicted the award would go to a woman this year, given the frequent criticism directed at the Academy over the overrepresentation of Western white men among its picks. There have been just 19 women laureates out of 122 since the Nobel literature prize was first awarded in 1901. A 2018 sex assault scandal left the Academy in tatters and more than half of its 18 members were replaced. Since then, every other literature laureate has been a woman. Last year, the award went to Hungary’s Laszlo Krasznahorkai, whose works explore themes of postmodern dystopia. The literature prize is the fourth of the six Nobels to be announced over the course of a week. The winners of the medicine, physics and chemistry prizes were announced earlier this week in Stockholm, while the peace prize will be announced in Oslo on Friday. Among those seen as possibilities are the Save the Children charity and Mykola Kuleba, a Ukrainian children’s rights activist campaigning for the return of kids illegally taken to Russia from occupied territories. Sudan’s Emergency Response Rooms (ERR), a vast network of volunteers risking their lives to help people facing the double threat of war and hunger, could also be a potential laureate. Yet others mentioned are the UN special rapporteur for the occupied Palestinian territories Francesca Albanese, Pope Leo XIV, press freedoms with an award to the Committee to Protect Journalists, or international justice bodies such as the International Criminal Court (ICC) and the International Court of Justice (ICJ). The Nobel economics prize will round up the 2026 awards season on Monday. Each Nobel prize comes with a diploma, a gold medal and a $1.2 million prize sum, to be shared if there is more than one laureate in each discipline. Carson will receive the award from King Carl XVI Gustaf in Stockholm on December 10, the anniversary of the 1896 death of scientist and prize creator Alfred Nobel. title: Ondo air crash: Imo PDP suspends campaigns for three days
body: By Emmanuel Iheaka OWERRI — The Imo State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has suspended campaigns and all political activities for three days in honour of victims of the Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Ondo State. The party, in a statement signed by its State Publicity Secretary, Lancelot Obiaku, described the incident as a painful loss and commiserated with the families of the deceased. The PDP directed its organs at the ward, local government and senatorial district levels, as well as its candidates, to suspend all political activities with immediate effect as a mark of respect for the victims. The party said the suspension was also intended to demonstrate solidarity with the families of the deceased officers and crew members. “The Imo State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) hereby suspends campaigns and all party activities for three days as a mark of respect for the victims of the recent tragic crash involving a military aircraft in Ondo State, which resulted in the death of gallant soldiers and crew members who lost their lives in the line of duty,” it said. The party extended its condolences to the families, friends, colleagues and loved ones of the deceased, as well as the Nigerian Armed Forces. It said the sacrifice of the fallen personnel, who devoted their lives to the service and protection of the country, would not be forgotten. “The loss of these brave men and women, who devoted their lives to the service and protection of the nation, is deeply painful. Their sacrifice will not be forgotten, and their service to Nigeria will always bear witness to their courage, patriotism and commitment to the country,” the statement said. The PDP urged the bereaved families and others affected by the crash to find solace in God, while praying for strength and fortitude to cope with the loss. Meanwhile, the party commended President Bola Tinubu and security agencies for their efforts in securing the release of corps members who were abducted in Imo State days earlier. The PDP said the release of the corps members had brought relief to their families and the wider community. It stressed that no family should be subjected to the uncertainty and anguish associated with having loved ones held in captivity. The party also called for continued efforts to protect citizens and ensure their safety across the state and the country. title: ‘Save part of the cake for us’ – Ga Mantse asks Roads Ministry to create jobs quota for Ga indigenes
body: The Ga Mantse, Nii Teiko Tsuru II, has appealed to the Roads and Highways Ministry to create a quota for Ga indigenes in employment opportunities within the sector. According to him, reserving opportunities for people from the Ga State would ensure that indigenes benefit directly from development taking place in the capital, which they host. The Ga Mantse made the appeal when Roads and Highways Minister Governs Kwame Agbodza paid a courtesy visit to the Ga Mantse Palace. He said the traditional council was responding to concerns about a reported shortage of workers within the Roads and Highways sector. “We are making a note that you set up a quota for our Ga indigenes to be employed in the various sectors, either engineering or part of your artisan workforce,” he said. Nii Teiko Tsuru II said the arrangement would help ensure that Ga indigenes benefit from opportunities created through development projects in the capital. “It will help us a lot to know that at least part of the cake has been saved for us and the indigenes of this soil who form the host of this capital,” he added. The Ga Mantse also commended the Roads and Highways Minister for what he described as progress on road projects in the Ga State. He said his observations of some of the roads under construction suggest that work is progressing well and expressed confidence that proper supervision and management would help government meet its targets ahead of Ghana’s 70th anniversary next year. “I know that your supervision, attention and good management would let us achieve our targets in due time for next year’s 70th anniversary of our country,” he said. Nii Teiko Tsuru II further called on the Ministry to support the Ga Mantse Foundation, which he said is undertaking several interventions in education, skills development and the welfare of young people. He said the Foundation has supported the construction and refurbishment of schools, provision of sanitation facilities and initiatives aimed at improving the enrolment, retention and academic achievement of girls. The Ga Mantse said the Foundation is also exploring vocational and entrepreneurial skills training to equip young people with skills for employment and self-reliance.

title: A 3-year-old girl came to visit her aunt in Pryluky, Ukraine. By morning, a Russian missile had killed her grandmother and uncle
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); A Russian missile strike on an apartment building in Pryluky, a town in northern Ukraine's Chernihiv Oblast, killed 22 people on 7 October, regional police reported on the morning of 8 October. Five of the dead were children: three one-year-old boys, an eight-year-old boy, and a 13-year-old girl, police said. Russian strikes on Pryluky, Kremenchuk, Oleksandriia, and Kyiv killed 28 people on 7 October, Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi said . For the town, it was the second deadly missile strike since May. Behind the toll are families like this one: three generations hit by a single strike. A family visit that ended under rubble Three-year-old Zlatoslava is now in the Chernihiv Oblast children's hospital, Pryluky district police chief Vladyslav Stoianov told . Her mother, Kateryna, is hospitalized too. The two had come on the evening of 6 October to visit Kateryna's sister, police officer Yuliia Malysh. The girl's father stayed home in Lynovytsia, a village 15 km away. Yuliia was wounded and is in hospital, Stoianov said. Her husband, Oleh Malysh, was killed. Until recently, Oleh had fought at the front in the Chernihiv Oblast police rifle battalion. The sisters' mother, Liudmyla, had also come over that evening, and she died too. All the family details come from Stoianov, who was describing a colleague's family. Suspilne first reported that the filmed rescuer had carried Zlatoslava. It then corrected itself: he had carried a different child, five-year-old Zoriana. Vyhivskyi also gives the girl's age as five, and he named the rescuer as State Emergency Service section commander Pavlo Levchenko. With colleagues, Levchenko freed the girl and her mother after the blast threw them out of the building. title: Al-Aqsa Flood and the beginning of Israel's strategic erosion
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 08 (MNA) – Three years after Al-Aqsa Storm, Israel has inflicted massive damage across the region, but has yet to achieve a single lasting political victory, raising doubts about its strategic direction.
Three years after the Al-Aqsa Storm operation, the importance of this operation cannot be summarized only in its military dimensions. October 7, 2023, was a point that changed a set of security, political, and media equations in West Asia. This operation occurred under conditions in which the Palestine issue, after years of the siege of Gaza, the occupation of Palestinian territories, the expansion of settlements, and the intensification of pressure on Palestinians, was moving away from the priorities of regional and international policy. The process of normalization of relations between some Arab countries and the Zionist regime had also strengthened the impression that the Palestine issue could be marginalized without a root solution. Al-Aqsa Storm stopped this process and brought Palestine back to the center of West Asian developments.
The first blow was struck against Israel's security image. For years, Tel Aviv had built an important part of its power on a combination of intelligence superiority, technology, the separation wall, surveillance systems, and military capability, and presented this set as the guarantor of the security of the settlements and residents of the occupied territories. But October 7 showed that even such an extensive network cannot create absolute security. More importantly, Israel's internal reports and investigations subsequently revealed serious weaknesses in the performance of the security and military structure. Therefore, the issue was not just the infiltration of Palestinian forces into areas under Israeli control; rather, it was a blow to public trust in the regime's ability to provide security.
Tel Aviv's response to this failure was a widespread war against Gaza. Israel announced big objectives such as destroying Hamas, returning the captives, and creating a new security reality. But the main problem from the very beginning was the gap between the announced objectives and the possibility of their realization. The widespread and destructive war was able to inflict heavy damage on Gaza, but it did not eliminate the political issue of Palestine. Hamas was not removed from the Palestine equation, and the future of Gaza, the manner of governance, the issue of disarmament of the Resistance groups, and even the shape of Israel's relationship with this region still face serious questions.
This is precisely where the concept of "military victory" separates from "strategic victory." An army may destroy a large part of the opposing side's infrastructure, but if it cannot shape the post-war political conditions in accordance with its objectives, military victory does not necessarily turn into strategic victory. The Gaza experience has highlighted this contradiction precisely. Israel was able to employ an enormous level of its military power, but it still faces an issue that existed before the war as well: how can the Palestine issue be solved merely through military means?
This pattern is also observable on the Lebanon front. Israel dealt heavy blows to Hezbollah, but could not remove this movement from Lebanon's political and security equations. The return of clashes in 2026 also showed that even inflicting considerable damage on a military actor does not necessarily mean the end of the threat or a permanent change in the balance. Regarding Iran as well, direct attacks by Israel and America could not remove Tehran from regional equations. On the contrary, direct confrontation highlighted the importance of Iran's missile capability, strategic depth, and regional capacity more than before in the security calculations of West Asia.
From this perspective, one can speak of a cycle: after October 7, Israel entered war to restore deterrence; the war expanded; but the wider the scope of the conflict became, the more the military, economic, political, and diplomatic costs increased, and on the other hand, the main objectives still faced serious obstacles. In other words, the attempt to compensate for one security failure itself led to a set of new crises.
One of the most important consequences of this process was the return of the Palestine issue to the center of world public opinion. Images and reports related to the situation in Gaza, widespread protests in various countries, and increasing political pressures on Israel caused an issue that, before October 7, had been affected by the normalization process in many regional equations, to once again become one of the main topics of international politics. The move by a number of countries toward recognizing Palestine and the increase in disagreement between Israel and some of its Western allies showed that the diplomatic cost of the war for Tel Aviv is also increasing.
Inside occupied Palestine as well, the effects of this erosion have become apparent. The security failure of October 7 intensified the dispute over responsibility for it and exposed the performance of Benjamin Netanyahu and the ruling political structure to criticism more than before. The issue of captives, the continuation or cessation of the war, the future of Gaza, the economic costs of the conflict, and social and political divisions revealed fissures that had existed before but gained greater depth after the war. In this way, Israel was trying to rebuild its image of power and cohesion while simultaneously facing a crisis of internal trust and increasing political pressures.
Even at the regional level, the image has changed. Before October 7, the process of normalization of Israel's relations with some Arab countries could create the impression that the Palestine issue was no longer the main obstacle to the formation of a new regional order. But the Gaza war, and then the expansion of conflicts to Lebanon, Syria, and other places, made this process more complicated. The Palestine issue once again became one of the important criteria of Arab public opinion for evaluating Israel's policies and increased the political cost of approaching Tel Aviv.
Therefore, three years after Al-Aqsa Storm, perhaps the most important question is not how much damage Israel has inflicted on various battlefields; the more important question is whether it has been able to achieve its political objectives. The answer to this question is negative.
Al-Aqsa Storm was a turning point because it showed that the Palestine issue cannot be solved by setting it aside from regional equations. Israel entered a widespread war to restore deterrence, but this war not only did not eliminate the Palestine issue, but brought it back to the center of the world's attention, increased Israel's political and diplomatic costs, made its internal fissures more apparent, and dragged the scope of the confrontation to multiple fronts.
Three years later, therefore, one can speak of a "cycle of failure"; a cycle in which a security failure was answered with war, the war led to erosion, and the erosion created new crises. Perhaps the most important legacy of October 7 is this: Israel showed that it has the ability to inflict very extensive military blows, but it has not yet been able to establish a link between this military power and a lasting political victory. And as long as this gap exists, the end of every war can be the beginning of the next crisis.

title: Latvia receives first Hunter infantry fighting vehicle
body: Hunter is a tracked combat vehicle based on the ASCOD platform. It has been upgraded for modern mechanised infantry operations and interoperability with Latvian and NATO equipment. Its configuration includes NATO-standard Level 4 armour, an automatic cannon, anti-tank weapons and a machine gun. Each vehicle can carry six soldiers in full combat gear. “The delivery of infantry fighting vehicles is an important step in strengthening Latvia’s defence capabilities,” said Defence Minister Raivis Melnis. “They will significantly enhance the mobility, protection and firepower of our mechanised units, while also strengthening cooperation between the National Armed Forces and NATO Allies.” “It is particularly important that Latvia’s defence industry is actively involved in the implementation of this programme: we are not only acquiring modern equipment, but also developing the country’s domestic industrial and technological capabilities,” Melnis said. “This demonstrates that Latvia is capable of implementing complex projects within a short period of time and making targeted investments in the security of our country.” Orders and industrial participation The Ministry of Defence ordered 42 vehicles from Spain’s GDELS-Santa Bárbara Sistemas in January 2025. It ordered another 42 in June that year. Latvian industry accounts for at least 30% of the initial contract’s implementation. The vehicle introduction programme runs from 2025 to 2029. A maintenance subcontract signed in September 2025 calls for greater participation by Latvian companies to strengthen security of supply. The maintenance contract runs for 13 years, until 31 December 2037. The Land Forces’ Mechanised Infantry Brigade will be the vehicles’ primary user. Its soldiers chose the name Hunter, or “Mednieks” in Latvian, drawing on a figure in Latvian mythology associated with courage, skill and survival. Source: Ministry of Defence of Latvia (press release) .

title: One killed, four injured, including two children, in Russian strike on civilian infrastructure in Sumy – official
body:
One person was killed and four others sustained injuries, including two children, as a result of a Russian strike on a civilian infrastructure facility in Sumy, Head of the Sumy Regional Military Administration Oleh Hryhorov reports.

"One person was killed and four others were wounded as a result of a Russian strike on Sumy. My sincere condolences to the family and friends of the deceased," Hryhorov wrote on his Telegram channel on Thursday.

According to him, preliminary reports indicate that two children sustained minor injuries. Two adults were also wounded, with one of them in serious condition.

Hryhorov noted that Russian forces targeted a civilian infrastructure facility, preliminarily utilizing long-range rocket artillery and firing four shells at the city.

title: Russians attack passenger bus in Mykolaiv region, injuring 1 – official
body:
Russian occupation forces continue to target civilian transport, First Deputy Head of the Mykolaiv Regional Military Administration Heorhiy Reshetilov reports.

"Today in the village of Lymany, Halytsynove community, Russia attacked a scheduled bus operating on the Mykolaiv – Lupareve route using an FPV drone. A 66-year-old driver was injured. His condition is satisfactory. The windows and roof of the bus were damaged," Reshetilov wrote on his Telegram channel.

He specified that the bus was operating without passengers at the time of the attack.

title: COCOBOD raises GH¢3.4bn in first cocoa notes offer, 15% below indicative GH¢4bn target
body: COCOBOD has raised approximately GH¢3.4 billion through its first commercial paper issuance, falling about GH¢604 million short of the indicative GH¢4 billion presented to investors. COCOBOD’s investor presentation The funds were raised through Cocoa Capital PLC, the wholly owned company established by COCOBOD to borrow from investors under its new domestic financing programme. According to the published results, GH¢3.39 billion was allotted at a yield of 11%. The notes were issued on October 5, 2026, and will mature on June 28, 2027. Source: Ghana Stock Exchange The amount represents approximately 85% of the initial GH¢4 billion financing plan for the first tranche. However, the GH¢4 billion was an indicative figure in the investor presentation. That distinction matters because the amount accepted is not necessarily the total amount investors offered. The published results do not state how much COCOBOD received in bids or whether some were rejected. It is therefore unclear whether investors offered less than expected, demanded rates COCOBOD was unwilling to pay, or whether the company decided to raise a smaller amount. The issuance also took place later than initially planned. Cocoa Capital’s September 25 announcement set out an indicative timetable for bidding to close on September 30, followed by settlement and issuance on October 1. The notes were eventually issued on October 5, four calendar days later. Source: Cocoa Capital’s initial announcement Their duration was also reduced from 270 to 266 days. The final yield of 11% was at the upper end of the initial guidance of 10.5% to 11%. These developments raise questions about how readily COCOBOD was able to secure the funds on its preferred terms. But without the full bidding results, they do not explain why it raised less than initially envisaged. The first issuance forms part of a programme allowing up to GH¢16.3 billion in notes to be outstanding at any time. Approximately GH¢14 billion is intended to finance cocoa purchases through commercial paper, while GH¢2.3 billion in longer-term bonds is intended to refinance existing debt. There is also an unresolved question over how the first GH¢3.4 billion will be used. As JoyNews Research previously reported, the investor presentation assigned commercial paper to cocoa purchases. The issuance announcement, however, also listed repayment of a bridge loan obtained to refinance COCOBOD’s legacy debt. Read here: COCOBOD asks investors to fund cocoa purchases, but proceeds may also repay old debt The latest notice does not disclose how much will be used to purchase cocoa and how much, if any, will repay that loan. The prospectus says details of bridge funding should be disclosed in the relevant pricing supplement, the document setting out the terms of each issuance. As of October 8, that document was not available on Cocoa Capital’s website. Meanwhile, COCOBOD has indicated that it could return to the market shortly. Speaking on Channel One TV’s The Point of View on September 28, Deputy Chief Executive in charge of Finance and Administration, Ato Boateng, indicated that COCOBOD could return to the market about two weeks after the first issuance. “Maybe two weeks later… we’ll come in and then do another tranche, and then we’ll finally look at the GH¢2.3 billion, which is the longer term, ” he said. Deputy Cocobod CEO, Ato Boateng His comments suggest that the next round of fundraising could follow shortly. The first offer gives COCOBOD a basis for deciding how much to seek next and at what price. Whether investors will provide more money on similar terms remains to be seen. For now, the amount raised is known. How much investors offered, why COCOBOD accepted less than its initial financing plan, and how the money will be divided between cocoa purchases and debt repayment remain unclear.

title: UK expands Russia-related special designation list by 26 positions

title: Zimbabwean Writer Simbarashe Kundizeza Wins 2026 Caine Prize
body:
Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Steyn Kundizeza has won the 2026 Caine Prize for African Writing, according to an announcement published on the Caine Prize website .
Mr Kundizeza beat four other writers shortlisted for the prize, including Nigerian writer Akinwande Remilekun Jordan, who was the only Nigerian on this year’s shortlist.
Mr Jordan was the only Nigerian on this year’s shortlist, with his short story, So Long It’s Starting To Look Like Eternity , competing with stories from Kenya, Cameroon, Egypt and Zimbabwe. The story was published by Naira Books in the anthology A House That’s Not A Home.
The judging panel was chaired by Nigerian broadcaster and journalist Bola Mosuro, who led a five-member panel that selected Mr Kundizeza as the winner.
The Zimbabwean author won the £10,000 prize for his short story, The Blue Fighter, which was published by The Shallow Tales Review.
The win makes Mr Kundizeza the third Zimbabwean to win the main Caine Prize, after Brian Chikwava won in 2004 and NoViolet Bulawayo won in 2011. Nigeria has had seven winners since 2001, including Helon Habila, Segun Afolabi, E.C. Osundu, Rotimi Babatunde, Tope Folarin, Lesley Nneka Arimah and Irenosen Okojie.
The story follows a young boy named Tinashe and his family as they struggle with money after his father leaves his job to build fish tanks.
As the family runs out of money, Tinashe’s mother must decide between supporting her husband’s dream and making sure the family can survive.
At first, The Blue Fighter sounds like a story about fish tanks, but it’s really about a family facing hard times.
Tinashe’s father becomes so focused on building fish tanks that the family begins to suffer. His mother has to find ways to keep the home running while dealing with her husband’s dream.
This makes the fish tanks more than just objects in the story. They become a symbol of the father’s dream and the price the family pays for it.
Mr Kundzeiza said the story grew from a poem by Vangile Gantsho that he came across during the LOATAD Black Atlantic Residency in Accra.
He said the poem made him think about “tenderness” and the need to keep going, which later shaped the story. He also said he wrote the first draft in one sitting, then revised it to improve the story.
Mr Kundizeza was one of five writers shortlisted for this year’s prize.
Melara Mvogdobo of Cameroon, Dieu Merci!
Akinwande Jordan of Nigeria, So Long Now It’s Starting To Look Like Eternity
Yasmine Zohdi of Egypt, The Absence of Stains
Ms Mosuro described the story as “gripping, moving and beautifully crafted,” saying Mr Kundizeza captures “the complexities of family, denial and devotion with remarkable emotional power.” She added that the story is told in a “deceptively simple manner” but has “a profound and lasting impact.”
Mr Kundizeza is a Zimbabwean writer based in Harare.
He is an Associate Editor at African Writer Magazine. His work has also appeared in Transition Magazine, The Wrong Patient and Other Stories from Africa and The Shallow Tales Review.
His novel manuscript, Freelance, won the 2024 Island Prize for Debut African Fiction. He was also a finalist in the 2018 Africa Book Club Short Story Competition and took part in the 2025 LOATAD Black Atlantic Residency.
The Caine Prize was first awarded in 2000. It is given each year for a short story written by an African and published in English.
The winner receives £10,000, while each of the other shortlisted writers receives £500.
For Mr Kundizeza, the win also signals that the time he has spent writing alongside his other responsibilities has been worth it.
He said the recognition has given him more confidence to keep making time for writing.
