title: Turkish mayor defects to Erdogan's party in opposition stronghold
body: The mayor of Turkey ’s most prominent opposition stronghold has defected to President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s ruling party, in a move that prompted protests and criticism over the state of the country’s democracy. Mr Erdogan’s Justice and Development Party (AKP) has never won a mayoral election in Izmir, Turkey’s third largest city. It is widely seen as a bastion of secular opposition parties who reject the president’s brand of Islamist nationalism. But mayor Cemil Tugay joined the AKP in a ceremony on Wednesday, and in a short speech described the party as “protector of the defenceless.” Mr Erdogan said he would support Mr Tugay “with all our resources in the effort to serve Izmir.” Taking control of Izmir, a province home to 4.5 million people, is a major win for the Turkish President, whose party has long criticised the opposition’s governance of the key Aegean coast centre. It was “a new era” and “a fresh start for Izmir,” local AKP chief Bilal Saygili said in a post on X. The move is the most prominent of a spate of recent defections to the AKP, in what critics have described as efforts by the ruling party to maintain rule over city governance despite an overwhelming defeat in local elections in 2024. “What does this tell us about the state of Turkish democracy? Well, it tells us that it doesn't exist,” Berk Esen, an Istanbul-based political scientist, told The National. Following Mr Tugay’s move, more than 1,000 protesters took to the streets in Izmir chanting slogans criticising the move, but were met with security barricades and anti-riot police, AFP reported. Local professional groups said Mr Tugay no longer had legitimacy and had disrespected the electorate’s wishes. “At this point, what must be done is to step down from that office,” Izmir Bar Association said in a statement on social media. He has “betrayed the duty entrusted to him,” the medics’ association said. Nine people resigned as advisers to the municipal theatre, saying that Mr Tugay’s defection “disregards the will of Izmir’s people and our audience.” Mr Tugay had previously denied he was considering joining the AKP. His wife had told him she would divorce him and his mother that she would disown him if he did so, he told Turkish media in January. Despite this, his wife Oznur Tugay appeared alongside her husband and Mr Erdogan at Wednesday's ceremony. Mr Tugay had won the mayoralty in 2024 with 48.97 per cent of the vote for the Republican People’s Party (CHP). At the time, the CHP was Turkey’s main opposition party, but in May this year it was hit with a lawsuit that saw its leadership removed and replaced. That prompted the formation of another group, the New Party, which has since taken over as the country’s largest opposition force. Mr Tugay left the CHP following the May lawsuit but did not join the New Party and continued to serve as an independent mayor. Opposition parties retain control of the municipal council. Critics of Mr Erdogan’s AKP characterise the defection as part of a pressure campaign on Turkey’s political opposition, which has faced arrests, lawsuits and defections over the past two years. “Elections are losing their meaning and significance because even if the ruling party loses elections, it can figure out extra-legal, extra-constitutional ways of reversing the outcome of these elections – in other words, reversing opposition victories,” Mr Esen said. Mr Tugay is not the first provincial mayor to defect to the AKP. Last year Ozlem Cercioglu, the mayor of Aydin in western Turkey, resigned from the CHP and switched to the AKP. Tens of district-level mayors, a less senior position than a provincial mayor, have also defected, alongside two MPs. Other opposition officials have been arrested. Seven opposition provincial mayors have been arrested since the 2024 vote, six of whom are still in prison, according to a tally published yesterday by news website Oksijen . The most prominent case is Istanbul’s mayor Ekrem Imamoglu , who remains in prison following his arrest in March 2025. He denies wrongdoing in multiple corruption cases that are currently going through the courts. Twenty-nine district-level mayors have also been arrested, including 13 in Istanbul. Mr Tugay’s predecessor as mayor of Izmir, Tunc Soyer, who is currently also in prison on corruption-related charges, criticised the defection in a message written from the high-security facility where he is being held. “Do not bow your head, beautiful Izmir,” he wrote. The Turkish government denies political motives in any lawsuits and says the judicial system is independent.

title: India interested in cooperating in Russia in marine infrastructure sphere — minister
body:
NEW DELHI, October 8. /TASS/. India assigns a special place to cooperating with Russia in the sphere of shipbuilding, port modernization and development of other marine infrastructure, Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal told TASS.
"We are trying to make our every vertical globally standard," the minister said. This pertains to the shipbuilding ecosystem, modernization and mechanization of ports, transport connectivity, creation of industrial clusters and development of cities around the ports, Sonowal said. Attention is also paid to "high-end skill required for the ship building and ship repair, ship recycling, and also the ecosystem," the minister stressed.
India is interested in cooperating "with Russia, especially, they are our old friend. We are always interested to walk together. We have been walking for decades together. So our like kind of friendship is growing much stronger day by day, Sonowal added.

title: What is Crazy Horse Paris? Famous French cabaret show to open in Dubai
body: One of Paris's most famous cabaret shows is coming to Dubai, bringing its signature blend of dance, music, elaborate lighting and theatrical illusion to the Middle East for the first time. Crazy Horse Paris will open a permanent production at Zabeel Theatre in Jumeirah Zabeel Saray on Palm Jumeirah on November 12, with tickets starting at Dh400. Called The Dubai Edition , the show has been created specifically for the emirate, adapting the Parisian institution's distinctive performances to regional culture and customs. It will also be the only permanent Crazy Horse Paris production outside the French capital, where the cabaret has been entertaining audiences for 75 years. Featuring 18 international dancers, the Dubai show will combine choreography, visual projections, music and optical illusions in an intimate 200-seat venue. What is Crazy Horse Paris? Founded in 1951 by French artist and entrepreneur Alain Bernardin, Crazy Horse Paris opened at 12 Avenue George V, close to the Champs-Elysees. Unlike traditional cabaret productions built around elaborate costumes, comedy and large ensemble performances, Crazy Horse became known for its sensual, highly stylised approach to dance. Its signature performances use carefully positioned lighting, shadows and projections to transform the dancers' bodies into part of the visual spectacle. The shows often feature artistic nudity, although the emphasis is on choreography, illusion and the interplay between light and movement rather than conventional striptease. Over the decades, Crazy Horse has become a fixture of Parisian nightlife, attracting international visitors and developing a reputation for combining glamour with experimental stagecraft. It has also collaborated with prominent figures from fashion, music and entertainment, including Beyonce, Christian Louboutin, Jean Paul Gaultier, Elie Saab, Dita Von Teese and Lisa from K-pop group Blackpink. How will the Dubai show be different? While the original Paris production is known for its provocative performances, organisers say The Dubai Edition has been reimagined to reflect regional culture and customs. The production will retain Crazy Horse's signature visual techniques, including lighting effects, optical illusions and precisely choreographed routines, while introducing new elements created for its Dubai audience. The extent of the changes, including how the original show's more revealing performances will be adapted, has not yet been detailed. Under the artistic direction of Andree Deissenberg, chief creative and brand officer of Crazy Horse Paris, the production will feature 18 dancers selected from hundreds of international applicants. The performers underwent six months of specialised training in Paris before joining the Dubai cast. "With The Dubai Edition, our objective was to create a show that is immediately identifiable as Crazy Horse Paris while developing a production specifically conceived for Dubai," Deissenberg said. "It draws on our artistic heritage, visual language and creative precision, while introducing new elements adapted to the venue and its audience." Where will Crazy Horse Paris be performed in Dubai? The production will take place at Zabeel Theatre inside Jumeirah Zabeel Saray on Palm Jumeirah. The venue has been transformed into an intimate cabaret with seating for 200 guests, designed to bring audiences closer to the performers. The Dubai production is being operated by 111 Management, a hospitality group based in the emirate. What can audiences expect? There will be two experiences available each evening. The Show is a 90-minute performance featuring choreographed dance routines, visual effects, a DJ and a master of ceremonies. For those looking for a longer evening, The Show & Dinner combines the performance with a three-course dining experience over approximately three hours. The entertainment continues after the final performance with a DJ set. There is also a private Crazy Suite for groups of up to 14 guests, designed for celebrations and exclusive bookings. When does Crazy Horse Paris open in Dubai and how much are tickets? Crazy Horse Paris – The Dubai Edition opens on November 12, with performances scheduled daily. The show begins at 7pm, with doors opening at 6pm. The Show & Dinner experience begins at 9.30pm, with doors opening at 9pm. Tickets for The Show start at Dh400 while tickets for The Show & Dinner start at Dh900, with higher-priced categories offering premium seating and additional hospitality benefits for each. Admission is restricted to guests aged 21 and above.

body:

title: Maduro's wife suffered heart attack in July in US prison, lawyers report
body:
NEW YORK, October 8. /TASS/. The wife of captured Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, Cilia Flores, suffered a heart attack a few months ago while in US prison, Associated Press reported citing her lawyers.
Representatives of 69-year-old Flores said she suffered a heart attack in July. They added that her heart problems cannot be treated in prison. Flores lost 11 kilograms during her time in custody. Her lawyers said they would seek her transfer to house arrest.
On January 3, the United States attacked civilian and military sites in Venezuela, captured Maduro and his wife, and took them out of the country. Maduro and Flores appeared before the US District Court for the Southern District of New York on January 5. US authorities charged them with involvement in drug trafficking, but both pleaded not guilty. Delsy Rodriguez, who served as Venezuela’s executive vice president under Maduro, is currently serving as the country’s interim president.

title: Kyrgyzstan Court Jails Kadyr Atambayev and Temirlan Sultanbekov
body: A court in Kyrgyzstan has sentenced Kadyr Atambayev, the son of former President Almazbek Atambayev, to four years in prison and opposition Social Democrats leader Temirlan Sultanbekov to seven years over an alleged plot to seize power following last year’s parliamentary elections. The defendants denied the allegations, and Sultanbekov described the prosecution as politically motivated shortly before the October 8 verdict. The trial at Bishkek’s Pervomaisky District Court was held behind closed doors despite defense lawyers’ requests for public hearings, preventing independent scrutiny of much of the evidence. Kadyr Atambayev entered politics in 2021, when he was elected to Bishkek’s city council as a Social Democrats representative. His father served as Kyrgyzstan’s president from 2011 to 2017 but fell into conflict with his successor, Sooronbay Jeenbekov, and subsequently faced several criminal prosecutions. Sultanbekov leads the Social Democrats, a party closely associated with the former president’s political circle. He is also a vice president of the Socialist International, an international association of socialist and social democratic parties. He was previously convicted in a separate case involving allegations of vote buying during the November 2024 local elections. His new seven-year prison term takes into account the earlier sentence. The latest case began on November 22, 2025, eight days before Kyrgyzstan’s early parliamentary elections. Police detained ten people, including Social Democrats members, former lawmakers, and associates of Almazbek Atambayev. Investigators alleged that the group was preparing to organize unrest after the vote. Atambayev and Sultanbekov were among those charged with preparing a forcible seizure of power. Defense lawyers challenged the prosecution’s evidence. Lawyer Asel Argymbaeva questioned a recording used in the case, alleging that it was made before investigators obtained judicial authorization for surveillance and that expert examinations found no calls for violence. The court acquitted former lawmaker Kubanychbek Kadyrov, while some other defendants received lesser penalties or were released from custody. Those convicted have the right to appeal. The verdicts come less than four months before Kyrgyzstan’s presidential election on January 27, 2027, in which incumbent President Sadyr Japarov intends to seek a second term. Since Japarov came to power in 2020, Kyrgyzstan has adopted a presidential system that concentrates greater authority in the head of state. The presidential election is taking place amid criminal prosecutions of several prominent political figures and restrictions on rallies in central Bishkek.

title: Russian strikes kill at least 10, injure 45 across Ukraine over past day
body:
At least 10 people were killed and 45 others injured in Russian attacks across Ukraine over the past day, local authorities said on Oct. 8.
In Donetsk Oblast , four people were killed and six others injured, Governor Vadym Filashkin said .
Two of those people died in Zelenye. In Sloviansk, one person died and three were injured, while a high-rise building, an administrative building, a shop, a service station, a gas station, a car, and a bus were damaged. In Veselia Hora, Novodonetska community, one person died, and a private house was damaged. One person was injured in Zolote Prudy, and a private house, a car, and a truck were damaged. In Druzhkivka, a person was injured.
Russia attacked across Ukraine with 142 Shahed-type drones, 82 of which were jet-powered overnight on Oct. 8, Ukraine's Air Force said . The Air Force said it shot down or suppressed 126 drones.
In Ukraine's capital city Kyiv , four people were killed and 21 others injured, including four children, the Kyiv city military administration (KMDA) said .
In Solomianskyi district, a UAV fell on the roof of a five-story residential building, causing a fire, while elsewhere in the district falling debris injured one person. In Desnianskyi district, falling drone debris also caused a fire in a 12-story residential building.
In the wider Kyiv Oblast , three people were injured overnight, regional governor Tymur Tkachenko said . Two people were injured in Bucha district and one person in Brovary district. Three warehouses, an infrastructure object, a private house, and four vehicles were also damaged across the oblast.
In Sumy Oblast , two children, fourteen-year-old boys, died from the detonation of an explosive object, while four people were injured from Russian drone strikes, according to the Sumy military state administration. In the city of Sumy, a 46-year-old woman and men aged 69 and 49 were injured by Russian drones, while a 62-year-old man was injured in Velykypysarivska.
In Kharkiv Oblast , three people were injured overnight, said regional governor Oleh Syniehubov. In the city of Kharkiv, a 67-year-old woman was injured, while a 62-year-old man was injured in the city of Dergachi, and a 70-year-old woman was injured in the village of Dobrenka.
In Kherson Oblast , Russian attacks injured five people, regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin said . Russian forces also struck critical and social infrastructure, residential areas, in particular, a high-rise building and four private houses, as well as private cars.
In Zaporizhzhia Oblast , three people were injured by Russian attacks over the last day, regional governor Ivan Fedorov said . He said he knew of 84 reports of damage to housing, cars, and infrastructure in the oblast.
In Odesa Oblast , the Russian attack damaged the territory of a parking lot, damaging several cars, and an animal shelter, killing one of the animals inside, regional governor Oleh Kiper said . Damage to civilian enterprise, settlements, and a bus were also reported in Dnipropetrovsk and Rivne oblasts.

title: Dzata Cement proves Ghanaians can build large-scale businesses – Ibrahim Mahama
body: Business mogul Ibrahim Mahama has called for greater belief in Ghanaians and urged the state to provide deliberate support to help more local entrepreneurs grow. He stressed that entrepreneurship was not only about creating a successful company, but also ensuring that the enterprise survives its founder. Mr Mahama, who is the Founder, Sole Shareholder and Group Chief Executive Officer of DZATA Holdings, said one of his motivations for establishing Dzata Cement was to demonstrate that Ghanaians could build major businesses rather than remain dependent on foreign-owned enterprises. “There are other ventures in which I want to prove to Ghanaians that we can’t always be beggars and only be employees of foreign companies. We can build it ourselves,” he said last Tuesday at the fifth anniversary celebration of Dzata Cement, a Portland cement production factory in Tema. Mr Mahama said his experiences and achievements in establishing Dzata Cement were a validation of a conviction that Ghanaian entrepreneurs could conceive, finance, build and operate large-scale industrial businesses and create enterprises capable of competing in sectors critical to national development. The only wholly Ghanaian-owned cement manufacturing company, Dzata Cement, marked five years of resilience last Tuesday, showcasing the proof that indigenous companies can thrive in all areas. Mr Mahama weathered significant financial, operational and market challenges to establish the company as a growing and recognised brand in the country’s construction industry. Dzata Cement’s journey, therefore, represents more than the establishment of a manufacturing plant; it is a demonstration of the entrepreneurial vision of the founder of DZATA Holdings, who set out to challenge the long-held perception that large-scale industrial ventures, particularly in the cement industry, had to be built and owned by foreign companies. Five years on, the cement manufacturing operation, located on a 10-acre plot near Tema Port, represents an investment of more than $100 million. The plant uses technology from German equipment developer Haver & Boecker to produce Portland Cement, with bagging lines capable of averaging 120 bags per minute. The company says its current operations have a capacity of about 80,000 bags a day, equivalent to approximately two million tonnes annually. The company is expected to produce its 30 millionth bag of cement within days, providing a significant production milestone in its five years of operations. Mr Mahama also urged those in leadership to challenge younger people with responsibility to help nurture a new generation of “doers who can take over from the current generation. He said he had deliberately stepped away from the day-to-day management of Dzata Cement to give younger leaders the opportunity to take risks, acquire experience and develop their managerial capabilities. “In life, some of us should learn these lessons. We won’t live forever. So sometimes we should give the children the opportunity to be able to take that risk of managing,” he said. Mr Mahama explained his broader succession philosophy: “What we do is that we start running together and then as our children grow, we employ them into the business, we teach them, and then we go into retirement.” That philosophy is already reflected at Dzata, where his daughter, Nafisa Mahama, serves as Managing Director. Mr Mahama traced the origins of Dzata Cement to his days as a cement transporter and mining contractor. His involvement in transporting cement gave him the opportunity to observe the industry closely, including the manufacturing and distribution processes. Mr Mahama recalled following his trucks to the Ghacem facility in Takoradi and taking a closer look at the plant and how cement was produced. Rather than seeing the enterprise as beyond the reach of a Ghanaian entrepreneur, the experience convinced him that he could build a similar facility. “I looked at the structure and said, look, I could build one,” he recalled, saying that resolve became an investment decision. Mr Mahama travelled to Germany, engaged equipment manufacturers and began putting together the financing required to establish the plant. The project, however, was confronted by significant financial and operational difficulties during construction and installation. At a critical stage, the business magnate said his younger brother and other individuals provided support that helped complete the installation of the equipment. Mr Mahama said the difficulties of bringing the project on stream did not derail the vision, but became part of the story of an entrepreneur determined to establish a Ghanaian-owned industrial operation in a highly competitive sector. He paid tribute to distributors who stood by the company during its difficult early period. The challenges included raising funds to clear imported clinker, creating a difficult situation while the business was still trying to establish itself in the market. The distributors, however, rallied around the company and helped it overcome the challenge. “They all joined hands together, the cement came, we allocated it to them, and then Dzata Cement started,” Mr Mahama said. He also acknowledged the support of former Trade and Industry Minister, Alan Kwadwo Kyerematen, during the administration of former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo. “Alan, wherever you are, I’m giving you a thumbs up. Thank you very much for standing behind us,” Mr Mahama said. His entrepreneurial journey was also shaped by scepticism from some industry players. Mr Mahama recalled an encounter with an expatriate executive who expressed doubts that a Ghanaian could build a cement plant. He said the comment strengthened his determination to prove the doubters wrong. The Managing Director of Dzata Cement, Nafisa Mahama, said the fifth anniversary was an opportunity to express gratitude to the customers whose confidence had helped the company to reach the milestone. She said Dzata Cement was celebrating the anniversary with a deep sense of appreciation for customers who had believed in the brand and chosen its products for their construction projects. She also thanked distributors, describing them as an essential part of the company’s journey. Ms Mahama acknowledged that some distributors had remained with Dzata Cement even during periods when the company faced significant challenges, helping it build the market presence it enjoys today. She also described the employees as the heart of the company and paid tribute to their dedication, sacrifices and commitment to the business. Ms Mahama pledged that employee welfare would remain a priority as the company entered the next phase of its development. She expressed appreciation to local and international suppliers, GCB Bank, the government, state institutions and the Chamber of Cement Producers for their contributions and support. She pledged management’s commitment to strengthening operations, maintaining the quality of Dzata Cement and improving services to customers and distributors. Ms Mahama said the company would increase investment in its people to ensure that Dzata Cement developed the human capacity required to serve Ghana for generations. Beyond the anniversary, the company has outlined plans to strengthen its manufacturing capacity and market position. Plant Director, Abderrahim Ouahab, said the company’s immediate priorities included expanding its cement portfolio, introducing additional grades and exploring a possible 25kg bag alongside the current 50kg packaging. He said the company would also strengthen its laboratory, increase Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) training, pursue ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 standards; improve spare-parts and inventory management and deploy artificial intelligence (AI) and digital tools in selected operations. A major capital project is the installation of a 300-tonne-per-hour Multi Big Bag Receiver, designed to improve jumbo-bag handling, cement transfer, screening, dust collection and recycling. The company also plans to expand storage capacity to 40,000 tonnes and develop an automated packing facility capable of about 6,000 tonnes a day. The managers said the long-term target was to produce at least three million tonnes of cement annually. The Finance Director, Godfred Barnes, said Dzata Cement’s progress had been built on hard work, sacrifice and resilience, stating that the company had navigated supply-chain disruptions, freight costs, inflation, exchange-rate volatility and operational pressures. He said finance was not merely about counting money but protecting the company’s vision, with every department responsible for efficiency and financial sustainability. Mr Barnes reaffirmed Dzata Cement’s ambition to become Ghana’s number-one cement manufacturing company by 2030, saying the first five years had laid the foundation while the next five would build the legacy through disciplined investment, stronger distribution, dependable production, customer service and tighter cost management. The company also intends ultimately to expand into ready-mixed concrete and other cement-related products and services.

title: Strait of Hormuz to stay closed until Iran resolves its issues — supreme leader’s adviser
body:
RABAT, October 8. /TASS/. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz will return to normal only after all of Iran’s problems have been resolved, Adviser to the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic Mohammad Mokhber said.
"The Strait of Hormuz will not be opened until the country’s problems are resolved," Mokhber said, as quoted by the IRNA news agency.
He added that Tehran was "changing its strategy in proportion to changes in the adversary’s strategy." According to Mokhber, Iran’s actions may take various forms, but the leadership of the Islamic Republic "is doing everything that serves the state’s best interests.".

title: The fallen noble profession: The sad tale of the Ghanaian teacher
body: For years, it was a noble profession. To be a teacher was to be respected. Today, it has become an object of ridicule. The Ghanaian teacher, who holds the future of this country in a chalk-stained hand, is now the punchline of jokes in tro-tros, markets, and family gatherings. It is a painful irony that the one who teaches others to become rich is unable to escape poverty himself. It is now described as a profession good for ladies, because the income alone cannot sustain a family. The assumption is that a woman will be supported by her husband, so she can afford to teach. For a man who must be the breadwinner, the salary is an insult. Consequently, many now see teaching not as a career, but as a stepping stone. It is something you do while waiting for a better opportunity. The ultimate disrespect comes from the very children we taught. After nurturing them and watching them graduate and become successful, they meet you on the road and ask with surprise, “Sir, are you still teaching?” As if to remain a teacher is a sign of failure. Walk into any staff common room at the end of the month, and the conversation is the same. It is about OD. Overdraft has become an unofficial part of the teacher’s salary. We are the first to get to the bank on payday, not because we are eager to save, but because our debts are waiting. Among all civil servants, the teacher is known as the poorest. While others are discussing plots of land and investments, the teacher is calculating how to make his salary reach the next month. We have become synonymous with being miserly, not because we love money too much, but because we have too little of it. This economic hardship has created a social stigma that follows us everywhere. Society now defines a teacher by his deprivation. The wearing of second-hand clothes, popularly known as “foos or abroni waa wo”, and used shoes is seen as our hobby. We are mocked for marrying food vendors, as if seeking a partner who can ensure you will at least eat is a crime. These jokes, though laughed at, carry a painful truth about how low the profession has sunk in the eyes of the public. If the situation in public schools is bad, the plight of our colleagues in the private sector is worse. Those teaching in schools run by a single individual or family suffer the most. Their salaries are nothing to write home about, and to make matters worse, the salary for January will be paid in the middle of February. They work the hardest, are supervised the most, yet are paid the least, with no job security and no pension to look forward to. The shame is most felt at home. During family gatherings where contributions are made for funerals or weddings, the teacher is the one who contributes the least. He bows his head in shame while his younger brother, who stopped school in Junior High School and learned a trade, contributes ten times more. It is in these moments that the most painful words are whispered to him: “There were so many lucrative jobs out there, but you chose to become a teacher.” The pride that once came with the profession has been replaced with quiet regret. The reality of our daily lives makes these words even harder to bear. We struggle to pay our rent in Accra and Kumasi, where landlords demand two years’ advance. We find it incredibly difficult to cater for the higher education of our own children, even though we spend our lives educating other people’s children. We go on vacation, but we cannot go on holiday. A trip to Ada or even across the border to Togo is a luxury we cannot afford. Our vacation is spent under a mango tree, marking piles of exercise books with a red pen that is almost dry. And so, we are told our reward is in heaven. This is the final consolation given to us. The white missionaries indeed brought both the Bible and the Western school system. It seems, however, that they left the promise of a heavenly reward for the teacher while others enjoy their earthly rewards. The teacher is told to be content with the knowledge that he is doing God’s work. But even the Bible declares that a worker deserves his wages. This is not a plea for pity. It is a call for national reflection. A nation that mocks its teachers mocks its own future. A hungry teacher cannot effectively teach a hungry child. A teacher who is constantly worried about where his next meal will come from cannot inspire children to dream big. If Ghana wants a quality education system that can compete with the rest of the world, we must first restore dignity to the teaching profession. This goes beyond the annual Best Teacher awards. It requires a living wage that reflects the importance of our work, better conditions of service, and genuine respect from society. Until we do this, we will continue to lose our brightest teachers to other professions, and our classrooms will be left with those who have no other choice. The joke, in the end, will not be on the teacher. It will be on the nation that chose to laugh at the very hands that built it. For without the teacher, there is no doctor, no lawyer, no engineer, and no president.

title: Cybersecurity compliance mandatory for critical infrastructure owners – Sam George
body: The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has stressed that cybersecurity obligations are mandatory for owners of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII). Speaking at a workshop on “CII Resilience Beyond IT: Securing Ghana’s Operational Technology Ecosystem”, organised by the Cyber Security Authority (CSA) in partnership with Cybershield as part of National Cybersecurity Awareness Month (NCSAM) 2026, the Minister said compliance with the Directive for the Protection of Critical Information Infrastructure is essential to responsible digital operations and national resilience. He urged CII owners to strengthen cybersecurity governance, appoint accredited cybersecurity leadership and ensure timely reporting of cybersecurity incidents. He also called for regular audits and vulnerability assessments to identify and address weaknesses in critical systems. The Minister further stressed the need for CII owners to engage only Tier 1 licensed cybersecurity service providers, noting that effective protection of Ghana’s critical infrastructure requires sustained compliance and strong cybersecurity practices.

title: Kebbi teachers get consequential salary adjustment, NUT clarifies
body: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi BIRNIN KEBBI — The Kebbi State chapter of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT) has clarified that the state government did not newly approve a N75,000 minimum wage specifically for teachers, saying the amount was earlier approved for workers across the state. The state NUT Chairman, Comrade Abubakar Zaki Sarki, made the clarification at a press conference in Birnin Kebbi on Wednesday, explaining that teachers were now benefiting from the consequential salary adjustment arising from the approved minimum wage. According to him, the adjustment followed the verification and review of the state’s teaching workforce and was aimed at aligning teachers’ salaries with the new wage structure. Sarki said the state government had commenced implementation of the consequential adjustment for 17,620 verified teachers following Governor Nasir Idris’ approval and endorsement of the White Paper on the report of the committee set up to audit the teaching workforce and review the applicable salary structure. “The N75,000 minimum wage was not newly approved for teachers. It had earlier been approved for workers in the state. What is being implemented for teachers now is the consequential adjustment required to align their salaries with the approved minimum wage structure,” he said. The NUT chairman said the salary review had helped to close the gap between teachers and other workers in the state who were already covered by the N75,000 minimum wage. He also disclosed that the state government had approved the payment of responsibility allowances to headteachers and assistant headteachers serving in public primary schools. Sarki said the affected teachers would begin to receive the adjusted salaries and approved allowances with effect from September 2026. He commended the Kebbi State Government for what he described as its sustained commitment to improving teachers’ welfare and strengthening the education sector. The NUT chairman specifically cited the government’s rehabilitation of 2,650 schools and construction of 200 new schools, describing the projects as significant interventions aimed at improving the learning environment and strengthening public education in the state. He urged teachers across the state to reciprocate the government’s efforts by rededicating themselves to their duties and maintaining high standards of professionalism, discipline and commitment to educating children. Sarki also advised members of the public to disregard what he described as misleading claims being circulated by “agents of mischief” suggesting that the state government had abandoned teachers. He said the latest salary adjustment and other interventions demonstrated the government’s commitment to the welfare of teachers and the development of the education sector. The post Kebbi teachers get consequential salary adjustment, NUT clarifies appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Police have no reason to be corrupt – Kogi CP
body: ‎By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja Kogi State Police Commissioner, Nazir Bello Kankarofi, has called on members of the public not to keep quiet but to report any rank-and-file officers or officers of his command who engage in any corrupt practices. The CP, while speaking on Wednesday during the command’s 2026 Customer Service Week celebration, themed “The Extra Mile”, called on civil society organisations, journalists and the general public to hold them accountable anywhere they are found wanting. ‎The CP reiterated that paying money to the police for bail of suspects was wrong and illegal and urged anyone found doing that or collecting any form of bribes to report such officers to the SERVICOM unit of the police at the state headquarters. ‎The police boss also rolled out some mobile line numbers to the public, namely: 08107899269 for police illegal action or brutality and 07038329084, 08152195982 for emergency cases. ‎Kankarofi acknowledged that police brutality, extrajudicial activities, corruption and other misconduct by some officers had continued to undermine public confidence in the force. ‎But the CP stressed that under his watch, he would not tolerate any act of indiscipline or corrupt practices, saying the police would continue to protect lives and property in the state without any form of compromise. ‎He said the issue of underfunding that characterised the force in the past has to a greater extent, now better under the present government, said they (police) no longer have reasons to engage in extortion or other negative dealings. ‎Kankarofi therefore urged officers to uphold accountability, professionalism and respect for citizens’ rights. ‎In his words: “The members of the public are our bosses. It is from their taxes that we are being paid our salaries. We are not their masters, but rather we are their servants.” ‎Earlier, the Acting Officer in Charge of the SERVICOM unit, ASP Chikak Emmanuel, said the Kogi State Police Command had reintroduced its SERVICOM complaint mechanism, with complaints from members of the public to be acknowledged within 48 hours and resolved within five to 15 working days. ‎Emmanuel said the mechanism would provide a structured channel for residents to raise concerns and receive responses and urged residents to submit their complaints and recommendations to the command. The post Police have no reason to be corrupt – Kogi CP appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Iru Ekun to deepen collaboration with Police, Army, DSS – Igboho
body: By Adeola Badru Yoruba Nation activist and founder of Iru Ekun Security Network, Chief Sunday Adeyemo, popularly known as Sunday Igboho, has reaffirmed the organisation’s commitment to deepening collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, Nigerian Army, Department of State Services (DSS) and other security stakeholders in tackling insecurity across the South-West. Igboho made this known on Thursday while announcing plans to strengthen the operations and official engagements of Iru Ekun, particularly with the establishment of the organisation’s Federal Capital Territory (FCT) office in Abuja. He said the security network would continue to work with conventional security agencies to promote safety, peace and tranquillity in communities across the South-West, stressing that collaboration among security stakeholders remained critical to combating kidnapping, banditry and other criminal activities. Igboho also expressed appreciation for the support received by Iru Ekun from the Federal Government under President Bola Tinubu and the South-West governors in addressing insecurity and other forms of criminality in Yorubaland. “Iru Ekun Security Network would not take for granted the immense support from President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s-led Federal Government and South-West governors in tackling insecurity and other criminalities in Yorubaland,” he said. The development came as KSI Construction Company Limited donated a plot of land valued at N50 million to Iru Ekun for the construction of its FCT office, a move Igboho said would further strengthen the organisation’s official engagements in Abuja. He commended the management of the company for the gesture, describing the support from corporate organisations and individuals as an important boost to community security initiatives. “Apart from the backing and valuable support at the governmental level, I want to commend the management of KSI Construction Company Limited, Abuja, for gifting Iru Ekun a plot of land in FCT,” Igboho said. He disclosed that the company had also concluded plans to donate 10 brand-new motorcycles to Iru Ekun to support its operations during the proposed unveiling of the organisation in Abuja. “They have also concluded plans to donate 10 brand-new motorcycles for our operations during the proposed unveiling of Iru Ekun in Abuja,” he said. Igboho added that increased involvement by corporate bodies and individuals in local security initiatives would provide additional impetus to efforts to tackle insecurity beyond the South-West. “The logistic support and active involvement of corporate bodies and individuals in local security initiatives would serve as impetus to further combat insecurity, not only in the South-West, but also in Nigeria,” he said. Meanwhile, the Group Managing Director of KSI Construction Company Limited, Dr Koleola Emmanuel Oladeni, said the company’s decision to support Iru Ekun was informed by what he described as the security network’s exploits since the commencement of its operations in the South-West. Oladeni said the activities of Iru Ekun personnel, in collaboration with the Police, DSS, Nigerian Army and other agencies, had contributed to a reduction in kidnapping, banditry and other crimes in parts of Yorubaland. “We noticed a drastic reduction in worrisome cases of kidnapping, banditry and other crimes in Yorubaland. And this was as a result of Iru Ekun Security personnel’s operations backed by the police, DSS, Nigerian Army and others,” he said. According to him, the activities of criminal elements had been significantly curtailed, with reported reductions in abductions, killings on South-West highways and attacks on agrarian settlements. “The nefarious activities of hoodlums have been significantly checkmated. Abduction, killings on South-West highways, and attacks on agrarian settlements have been reduced recently,” Oladeni said. He said the company’s donation of the land was intended to enable Iru Ekun establish a permanent presence in Abuja, while the motorcycles would further support its field operations. “This informed our donation of a piece of land for Iru Ekun to build their office in Abuja. We are also giving them 10 brand-new motorcycles during the unveiling of their office in Abuja, which will be constructed on the donated plot,” he said. Oladeni further urged corporate organisations and individuals to support those contributing to national security, saying such assistance would encourage volunteers involved in protecting communities. “If they decide to volunteer themselves for the security of our nation, it behoves us at the corporate and individual levels to support and encourage them in any form.“ “That was why we assisted Iru Ekun in this regard. It is our token to boost the security and safety of our people,“ he added. The post Iru Ekun to deepen collaboration with Police, Army, DSS – Igboho appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Teachers’ strike: Final-year SHS students worry over lost learning time and WASSCE preparation
body: With little or no academic instruction, final-year senior high students are particularly worried about lost learning time as the nationwide teachers’ strike continues. For many students in Kumasi, the school day has become a routine of reporting to class, sitting for hours and eventually returning without a single lesson. The nationwide strike by the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG) began on September 25, 2026, over outstanding concerns including the placement of promoted teachers on new salary levels and negotiations on conditions of service. Recent engagements between the government and the unions have so far failed to produce a resolution. For students, however, the disagreement between government and teachers has translated into something much more immediate: a growing gap in their education. “We come to school, and there is nothing to do,” said a Form Three student at Prempeh College who described the experience as frustrating, particularly for students preparing to leave secondary school. “We don’t have any work to do. No teachers have been coming to class, and we have little time to cover the syllabus before WASSCE starts,” he added. The student said the normal school routine has continued, but without teachers, much of the day is spent simply waiting. Another Form Three student said the situation was especially worrying for final-year students who have limited time left to prepare academically. According to the student, some learners have resorted to extra classes as the only available avenue for structured teaching, but that option is not accessible to everyone. Students whose families cannot afford additional lessons risk falling further behind, raising concerns about the unequal impact of the strike on learners from different economic backgrounds. For final-year students, the uncertainty is particularly concerning as they prepare for examinations and the transition beyond secondary school. Earlier observations in Accra showed classrooms largely vacant, with some students left on school compounds without teachers to supervise or teach them. In some schools, students were seen playing while others remained in classrooms. The situation has continued to put pressure on school authorities, who must keep students occupied and safe while normal academic activities remain suspended. Amid the disruption, some schools are finding ways to ensure students are not completely idle. One such response has been the organisation of activities under Freshers Week, giving newly admitted students opportunities to participate in programmes designed to keep them engaged during a period when regular teaching has been severely affected. Although such activities cannot replace classroom instruction, they provide students with structured engagement and an opportunity to develop interests outside the traditional academic setting. The activities also offer a degree of relief from what has otherwise become a monotonous routine of coming to school, sitting in classrooms and waiting without lessons. For freshers, the programmes can help with social interaction, orientation and integration into school life, while giving the broader student population something constructive to participate in during the disruption. But students say activities cannot replace teaching. Despite the positives, students acknowledge that such initiatives are not a substitute for their teachers. For students in Form Three, in particular, entertainment and extracurricular activities cannot address the academic pressure created by weeks without regular lessons and can only serve as a temporary relief in this period. Their concern is not simply about being bored. It is about the cumulative effect of lost instructional time. With every additional day without teaching, students worry about topics that remain uncovered, revision schedules that are disrupted and the possibility of having to catch up under intense pressure once teachers eventually return. The government has repeatedly appealed to the unions to suspend the strike, and discussions are still ongoing to get teachers back in the classrooms as soon as possible. For students, the hope is simple: that the negotiations end soon and teachers return to their classrooms. Until then, school authorities are left trying to keep students occupied, while learners — especially those in their final year — continue to count the cost of days without teaching. While Freshers Week and other school activities may provide a welcome distraction, students say what they ultimately need is to get back to learning.

title: 100 days to election: Don’t sell, surrender your PVC — Obi’s office
body: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Peter Obi Media Office has urged Nigerians not to sell or surrender their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs, or accept money and other inducements in exchange for their votes. The media office of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, also urged voters to remain vigilant against schemes capable of compromising the electoral process. In a statement issued on Thursday and signed by its spokesman, Idris Zekeri, the office said Nigerians should protect their PVCs and ensure that their votes count during the elections. The statement came as the office said there were exactly 100 days to the election, urging Nigerians to resist attempts to influence their voting decisions through financial inducements. It alleged that the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, was exploiting poverty in the country by offering money to Nigerians in exchange for their PVCs. The claim could not be independently verified. The Obi media office also alleged that some state governors were collecting PVCs from citizens, including civil servants, in exchange for payment of their salaries and allowances. “Exactly 100 days left to election day, we urge Nigerians to remain vigilant against anyone offering money or inducements in exchange for your vote, your PVC, or participation in any scheme aimed at compromising the electoral process,” the statement said. It added: “Reports from some states indicate that some state governors, who have nothing positive to show to persuade their citizens, including civil servants, are collecting their PVCs in exchange for the payment of their legitimate salaries and allowances.” The office urged Nigerians to collect their PVCs, keep them secure and refuse to hand them over to anyone. “Your PVC is not for sale. Your vote is not for sale. Your future is not for sale. Collect your PVC. Keep it secure. Do not hand it over to anyone,” it said. The office further urged voters to reject bribes, report suspected electoral manipulation to the relevant authorities and vote according to their conscience on election day. “On election day, turn out, vote according to your conscience, protect your ballot, and insist that your vote counts,” it said. The office also called on Nigerians to defend their votes through lawful means and contribute to strengthening the country’s democracy. “Hold your PVC firmly. Use it responsibly. Defend your vote legally. Defend your democracy and create a new Nigeria that will be possible and OK,” the statement added. The post 100 days to election: Don’t sell, surrender your PVC — Obi’s office appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: EU firmly on path of confrontation with Russia, worsening its problems — diplomat
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova predicts that European countries’ problems will worsen as a result of their confrontation with Russia.
"The European Union embarked on a path of confrontation with our country, initially under pressure from the United States and then simply out of inertia. And this path will not allow it to resolve its pressing issues, indeed, it will never allow it to do so," the diplomat said at a briefing. She explained: "Because this path will only exacerbate the problems Europe already faces."
Zakharova stressed that the EU leadership "quite deliberately and consciously chooses to ignore this simple truth."
The Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman also pointed to those who truly benefit from Europe’s current course: "The forces behind the fomenting of Nazism and fascism in the heart of Western Europe included forces from outside Europe. The hybrid threat to Europe comes not from Russia at all, but either from its own political elites, from the reckless and irresponsible policies they pursue, or from those outside the European continent who sponsor the escalation of conflicts within Europe."
Zakharova attributed the unsubstantiated accusations of hybrid attacks against Russia made by EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas to a desire "to shift the European public’s attention away from the mounting problems in their own countries and toward an imaginary 'Russian threat.'"
"The more serious the problems EU countries face as a result of their own mistakes and miscalculations, stemming from their decision to embark on a path of hybrid warfare against our country, the more incredible and far-reaching the plans they attribute to Russia in this sphere become," the diplomat stated.
According to Zakharova, "this confrontational rhetoric is being used to justify large-scale military preparations, increased support for the Kiev regime, provocations, and confrontational actions against Russian citizens and legal entities."
"Citizens and businesses in European countries are already feeling the full consequences of this approach. These include soaring levels of government debt in these countries, problems with energy poverty and security, and declining output in key industrial sectors," the Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman said.

title: Navy uncovers 40,000 litres of suspected crude oil in Delta
body: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has uncovered approximately 40,000 litres of substance suspected to be crude oil stored in a large dugout reservoir in the Oteghele general area of Delta State. The discovery was made on October 7, 2026, by the Nigerian Navy Ship Delta (NNS DELTA) during an anti-crude oil theft operation following credible intelligence on suspected crude oil theft and related illicit activities in its area of operations. Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday. He said the recovered substance and the dugout reservoir were subsequently handled in accordance with established procedures. According to him, the latest operation followed an earlier discovery by NNS DELTA in the Oteghele area, where about 30,000 litres of suspected crude oil were uncovered on September 21, 2026. Folorunsho said the recurring discoveries demonstrated the Navy’s continued efforts to disrupt illicit crude oil storage activities and deny criminal operators access to the nation’s petroleum resources. He said, “The Nigerian Navy will continue to sustain intelligence-led operations across its Area of Operations to disrupt crude oil theft and protect the nation’s critical petroleum resources.” The post Navy uncovers 40,000 litres of suspected crude oil in Delta appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Isaias intensifies to hurricane. And, judge orders Pike execution evidence preserved
body:
Good morning. You're reading the Up First newsletter. Subscribe here to get it delivered to your inbox, and listen to the Up First podcast for all the news you need to start your day.
Tropical Storm Isaias intensified into a hurricane overnight and is forecast to make landfall as early as tomorrow night near the Alabama Gulf Coast and the Florida Panhandle. Coastal communities in its path are preparing for high winds and flooding by stocking up on supplies to board up windows and gather sandbags. Residents who live farther inland are also preparing for inches of rain and wind.
The Plains oil refinery is seen on March 10, 2022 in Mobile, Alabama. Brandon Bell/Getty Images hide caption
Republicans currently have a slim majority in the House , holding 218 seats to the Democrats' 214. With less than a month until Election Day, an NPR analysis of both parties' campaigns highlights key races that will shape control of the House in 2027. The Cook Political Report lists 43 competitive districts, including 22 toss-ups. But both parties are pouring hundreds of millions of dollars into shaping a much larger electoral landscape.
The Davidson County Chancery Court in Nashville has ordered Tennessee prison officials to preserve all evidence related to the botched lethal injection of Christa Pike last week. This includes log books, medical waste and all communications from officials involved in the execution attempt. The court granted Pike's attorneys "liberal access" to her, requiring prison officials to respond to requests for in-person visits within two hours. Pike's attorneys said that she is now awake, speaking and receiving critical medical care after several days of unconsciousness.
CNN, MS NOW and Politico are in federal court today to argue that Trump is infringing on their constitutional rights by blocking their access to the White House. The news outlets say that they have the right to determine how, what and where they can cover the president at any given time. A judge last month issued a temporary restraining order preventing the Trump administration from barring the outlets from the White House while the court considered the lawsuit.
by Cooper Katz McKim , The Indicator from Planet Money associate producer
Diesel fuel has been pricier than regular gasoline, with a few exceptions, since 2004 David Zalubowski/AP Photo/David Zalubowski/AP hide caption
The cost of diesel fuel is breaking records left and right. The previous record was $5.85/gallon. A few weeks ago, it hit $6.53/ gallon . If I drove a diesel car, I might stay home.
At the Indicator, we've been watching whether President Trump would try to lower prices by banning exports of diesel fuel. He did not do that, though he did make diesel cheaper by expanding the use of tax-exempt diesel for highway vehicles through the end of the year. Still, I wondered why diesel prices are so consistently higher than regular gas.
We have a weekly newsletter at The Indicator where we track what's driving the economy and how it affects your life. It was the right platform to ask: Is diesel fuel inherently more expensive than regular gas?
The answer: NO! Before 2004, diesel was actually cheaper. But step by step, the price got higher.
The first domino to fall: taxes . In 1993, the federal excise tax on diesel increased to 24.4 cents, 6 cents more than the regular gas tax.
Soon after, demand for diesel began to skyrocket. China and India were ramping up industrialization, agriculture and new infrastructure to new levels. The world saw diesel vehicles take off.
In the U.S., the last major domino to fall was air quality standards . In 2006, diesel fuel needed to have less sulfur, which required new — and more expensive — refining and distribution methods.
One lesson that stuck with me is how diesel is essential for the modern economy. It's needed in shipping, long-haul trucking, mining and backup generators. Whether the cost is high or low, the demand is there. Regular gasoline? Demand is a little squishier.
You can check out the full segment here . And if you liked this story, subscribe to The Indicator newsletter here !

title: Lithuania Deploys Army to Kaliningrad Border After Belarus-Latvia Breach
body:
Lithuania is deploying troops to reinforce its border with Russian exclave Kaliningrad, officials announced late Wednesday, citing concerns over potential military mobilization in Russia and renewed hybrid threats.
The decision follows a high-profile security breach on the border between Latvia and Belarus this week, said Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas.
Defense Minister Robertas Kauna confirmed the deployment of border security, saying it was a “preventive” step in response to “signals of a possible increase in aggressive foreigners due to possible mobilization in Russia.”
Kaunas said around 100 soldiers would help guard the Lithuanian-Russian border over the next two weeks, according to the Elta news agency.
“The order is being executed immediately,” Kaunas wrote on Facebook
Katelynas and Lithuania’s border security service stressed that the situation along the Kaliningrad border remains calm, with zero illegal border crossings from neighboring Belarus over five consecutive days.
On Tuesday, Latvian authorities reported that masked and armed individuals escorted a group of 20 irregular migrants to push through the Belarus border into Latvian territory. The masked operatives damaged electrical equipment and stole border surveillance cameras before retreating back into Belarusian territory.
Also this week, the Kremlin warned that Lithuania’s preliminary parliamentary vote to lift a constitutional ban on hosting foreign nuclear weapons marked a dangerous escalation of regional tensions.

title: Canadian author Anne Carson awarded 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
body:
STOCKHOLM, October 8. /TASS/. The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature has been awarded to Canadian author Anne Carson, the Nobel Committee for Literature at the Swedish Academy said.
Carson is awarded the prize "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature".
"Anne Carson has, throughout her entire career, combined poetry writing with translation work and teaching at various universities. Almost all her literary production has centered upon the intersection between the philologist’s obsession with words and the poet’s desire for new meaning. She has herself identified the etymology of words as the starting point for all her work," the committee pointed out.
Carson, a native of Toronto, is an English-language writer, poet, essayist, and translator. Born in 1950, she studied at the University of Toronto and has taught at universities across the United States and Canada.

title: The Bamba revolution and a maiden broadcast
body: Last weekend, a long-awaited Kukurudu Delegates Congress ended with a new executive whose names and faces ‘passeth’ all understanding. As expected, this has led to champagne celebrations in places, and fear and panic elsewhere. It’s clearly the type of congress that should have come with an advisory: ‘caution: painkillers advisable ahead of results declaration.’ As it turned out, a few contestants went home blowing their noses in funeral lamentation; and one or two contestants pleading alibi for the swearing-in ceremony due to congress ‘fatigue.’ The rival party, on its part, was asleep with one eye open, and clearly heart-broken; but I respect their firm decision to endure collateral waist pains in dignified silence. At the Congress, the list of candidates offering to serve the elephant party was a virtual who is who, and could have been flag bearer contenders: John Boadu the supremo; JFK, Hawa Koomson, Boakye Agyarko, Mustapha Hamid, Nana Akomea, Nana B, Titus Glover; Miracles Aboagye, Abankwa, Thompson, Dr China, etc.; a solid team of experienced game changers vying to die for their party. But a few other candidates drew giggles and could have been confronted by congress organisers: ‘Krakye, before God and Man, which part of your body qualifies you to be Vice Chairman?’ Such contestants must have lost their way, and strayed to the wrong ‘funeral.’ This was a party of lawyers, indeed an Abrɔfosɛm People’s Party. ‘What do you want here? ’ Of the 11 vacant slots, the position of 1st Vice Chairman was the most sought after: attracting 13 powdered faces. It was the closest to the Supreme Chair position, which attracted only four names, one of whom later took to his heels from stage fright. The 1st Vice is the spot often eyed by high-profile persons who pretend it was all they sought, but in truth use this as a stepping stone to higher heavens. In the absence of the chairman at meetings, the 1st Vice may quietly thank the good lord for his boss’s unfortunate toothache, and unwillingly replace him upstairs, until the missing tooth is providentially restored. Happily, our society permits references to the 1st Vice Chair as simply ‘Chairman Koo Hia,’ since ‘Vice Chairman Koo Hia’ is rather a mouthful. At the congress, the category of 1st Vice Chairman presented several known dignitaries, plus one anonymous soul who in public functions would normally attract the label, ‘et cetera et cetera,’ in the words of the MC. Did ‘Mr Et cetera’ lose his way, jay-walking to a NPP Congress? No. He was Kojo Bamba, a former bodyguard of charismatic Nana B, who was also in the race. Was it then a contest between Master and Servant? Would Bamba not rather bow out in deference? No. The servant’s campaign message indeed was a celebration of Asante diplomacy at its best: ‘Fellow party members, with due respect, please go ahead and vote for the two learned gentlemen (akrakyefo): Nana B and Nana Akomea. But simply add my name as the third in your order of preference. I am a mere security hand, and will be in attendance to protect the ballot if added; my duty will be to simply stop the rival party from bullying and intimidating us.’ This was not a campaign of boss abuse, insult, vilification among competing kinsmen. It was a fragment of Asante diplomacy dating back to the 19th century. At the weekend Congress, Bamba looked different among contestants. He was in military gear, depicting the look of the Burkinabe capo, Captain Ibrahim Traore, followed by teeming throngs of youth. Dressed in military gear, Bamba’s appearance alone spoke louder than words. What was unknown was Bamba’s widespread popularity among delegates at the Congress: accomplices with sealed lips. The long and weary day and night ended with a results declaration at dawn, which kept trickling in until the bombshell. While most results conformed to wide expectations, the breaking news swiveled around Kojo Bamba, the faceless wretch who had shattered expectations and won the enviable slot of 1st Vice Chairman. He had humbled his superiors, whacking them to Second and Third Positions. This was a historic revolt by the grassroots, and a major landmark in our political history. The optics were shattering, and led to a courteous alibi at the swearing-in ceremony, where the two Big Men were unavoidably absent due to ‘fatigue.’ The casualty ward quickly filled to capacity, but has since thinned out. Like true democrats, many have conveyed congratulations to Chairman Boadu and others, including Kojo Bamba, the new hero. Quietly disturbed is the rival Umbrella party, currently nail biting, and contemplating a 24-hour retreat. Conference Theme? The Bamba Factor in Ghana’s democracy. Below, I humbly reproduce excerpts of ‘Chairman Bamba’s maiden broadcast to his teeming fans last weekend: Chairman Bamba speaks: “I come here today armed with profuse thanks. I cannot rise to leadership leaving my own people behind. Colleagues, please lace your boots for the task ahead…When i was doing my rounds during the campaign, I pleaded with you to vote for me to win. My promise was to hand over power back to you. During voting at the Congress, you neither gave me the third nor the second position as Vice Chairman; you honored me with the position of 1st Vice Chairman. It is now my duty to give back the power to you, but also add several more parliamentary seats to our party. That’s my job description. “I will make sure the new national leadership of NPP comes down to your level. Our new leadership has individuals with varying backgrounds. It is often said that the NPP cannot be led by people who are not lawyers, who are without master’s degree or professorial titles. I will prove them wrong… Politics is not won with certificates but with humility, self-sacrifice…commitment and courage. I will be guided by these virtues to prove others wrong. You can be a leader if you are human with blood circulating in you; if you have a tongue to speak and ears to listen. You can even aim to be president: it is neither by riches nor poverty. Those of you who were misled to follow another political party because they embraced all, including grassroots; today, your own brother is here. Please file behind me, and lend me your support. “Tro tro drivers, auto mechanics, carpenters, your own is now here. When you want to visit me, there is no need to write an application; no need to book an appointment…my office is yours.… Come help me bring back the NPP. Are you not proud your own man comes next after Mahmoud Bawumia and John Boadu? Are you not proud? Together we can even exceed the achievements of our forebears. “I who am undeserving… I who was taken for nothing in a party full of lawyers and doctors, full of professors; a party reserved for people with multiple degrees. A party not cut for senior high school graduates… You would normally not find me here. But today, the party has rewarded the servant working under his master; it has rewarded a mere tenant, a mere security guard…If the party has rewarded me, Kojo Bamba, a poor underdog… if it has uplifted a virtual homeless, let no one belittle themselves… Based on your hard work for the party, you will be rewarded. Help me to succeed so it may not be said, ‘we told you, those holding no degrees or masters; non-PhDs, non-lawyers, non-medical doctors cannot lead the NPP.’ I will do all I can with your help to prove sceptics wrong. “Your NPP party does not discriminate against the rich or poor, literate or non-literate, or those with or without academic certificates. Note that I am not beyond advice. Feel free to come and advise me when I return from break; so I will be well equipped to contribute my quota working for DMB. I am a Ghetto Boy; your own is now here… Gone are the days when we worked tirelessly for others to enjoy. My father once told me, ‘He who has pounded the food to make a pleasant meal cannot be stopped from dipping his hands…’ “Today, I virtually panic waking up to see where I am: a mere underdog.”

title: Russian embassy awaits clarification following Dutch defense chief’s 'enemy' remark
body:
THE HAGUE, October 8. /TASS/. The Russian Embassy in the Netherlands is awaiting clarification following Dutch Defense Minister Dilan Yesilgoz-Zegerius’ remark describing Russia as "an enemy," an embassy spokesperson told TASS.
"We are waiting for the Netherlands’ authorities to provide official and unequivocal clarifications regarding the bellicose rhetoric of their minister," the spokesperson said.
According to the diplomat, the defense chief "effectively conceded that they want an armed conflict with Russia." The embassy stressed that although Russia has no wish to go to war with Europe, including the Netherlands, it would not "allow anyone to use the language of threats and ultimatums."
The Dutch newspaper De Telegraaf reported earlier that Yesilgoz-Zegerius said during discussions of the country's defense budget that Russia "is no longer an aggressor," but "an enemy" for the Netherlands.

title: WHO confirms no new plague cases reported in Siberian region, Russia’s watchdog says
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. The World Health Organization (WHO) has not confirmed reports of new plague cases in the Irkutsk Region in Russia’s Siberia, the country’s sanitary watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, said in a press release on Thursday.
"The World Health Organization also did not confirm information about new [plague] cases. In response to requests from the WHO and in compliance with international medical and sanitary norms, Rospotrebnadzor submitted full and exhaustive information about the measures taken, confirming the absence of any risks to the population’s health," the press release reads.
The global health body also confirmed that there are no risks of a sanitary-epidemiological emergency in the Irkutsk Region, the Russian agency added.

title: India pens deal for BrahMos fire control systems and launchers
body:
India’s Ministry of Defense has signed a contract with BrahMos Aerospace Private Limited (BAPL) to procure BrahMos fire control systems and launchers for Indian Navy ships.
The contract, valued at Rs 661.50 crore (around $68 million), was signed in New Delhi on October 6 under the Buy (Indian-IDDM) procurement category.
The procurement includes BrahMos fire control systems and launchers intended for Indian Navy ships. The ministry said the project has a minimum indigenous content of 68% and will involve various Indian industries, including micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
The project is expected to generate employment over a three-year period and contribute to the Indian Navy’s maritime strike capabilities and the wider indigenization of defense technology.
The BrahMos system is deployed aboard various Indian Navy frontline warships and serves as the service’s primary surface-to-surface missile system for maritime strike operations. According to the ministry, the system can engage land and sea targets at extended ranges with high accuracy at supersonic speed.

title: Three killed, 14 injured in Russian attack on Kyiv
body:
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
"Fourteen people have now been injured in the capital since the beginning of the day on October 8. Three people were killed," Klitschko wrote.
He noted that eight of those injured are being treated in city hospitals, with two in serious condition.
As reported, a Russian drone struck a four-story store building in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district, killing two people and injuring two others.
In Kyiv's Holosiivskyi district, debris from a Russian drone was reported to have fallen in an open area.
Earlier reports said that one person had been killed and 11 injured in Kyiv.

title: PANDEF mourns victims of Ondo Air Force crash, seeks probe
body: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, has mourned the victims of the Nigerian Air Force (NAF) aircraft crash in the Igbokoda area of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State. PANDEF also called for a thorough and comprehensive investigation to determine the circumstances that may have contributed to the crash and similar aviation tragedies. In a statement issued on Thursday and signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, the forum said the people of the South-South received the news of the crash with “deep shock and pain.” The aircraft crashed on Monday, October 5, 2026, in the vicinity of Igbokoda, Ondo State. PANDEF said several South-South indigenes were among those listed as victims, while describing the loss of the military personnel and other passengers as a painful blow to their families and the nation. The statement read in part: “The Board of Trustees and the National Leadership of the Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), on behalf of the people of the South-South geopolitical zone, have received with deep shock and pain the tragic news of the crash of a Nigerian Air Force aircraft.” The forum expressed condolences to the affected families, the Nigerian Air Force, the Federal Government and Nigerians, noting that many of those who died were young Nigerians serving the country. “More painful is the fact that most of the deceased were young Nigerians who have now laid down their lives for the peace and security of our nation during the line of duty. “There is no greater sacrifice than this, and Nigeria will always honour them individually and collectively,” it said. PANDEF urged Nigerians to continue praying for the affected families as well as military personnel serving in various operational theatres across the country. The forum also said the tragedy underscored the need for the Federal Government to sustain investment in military equipment, maintenance and operational readiness. “This tragic occurrence also underscores the imperative need for the Federal Government to prioritize continuous investments in the combat readiness and equipment maintenance of our military personnel,” PANDEF said. It further called for a “thorough and full investigation” to establish all the circumstances surrounding the crash and determine factors that may have contributed to it and similar incidents. PANDEF also appealed to Nigerians to unite in efforts to promote peace and security across the country amid ongoing security challenges. “Finally, PANDEF calls on all Nigerians at all levels to unite around our government to instill peace and security across our country during this period when our nation is confronted with diverse security threats and challenges to the wellbeing of ordinary citizens,” the statement added.
