title: Goethe-Institut Director on Kazakhstan’s Cultural Ties with Germany
body: What does genuine intercultural dialogue look like in an interconnected yet polarized world? The Times of Central Asia spoke with Friederike van Stephaudt, director and head of cultural programs at the Goethe-Institut in Kazakhstan, about cultural relations between Germany and Kazakhstan. She discussed literary translation and how young people’s interest in studying or working in Germany can develop into lasting cultural connections. TCA: When you came to lead the Goethe-Institut in Kazakhstan, what aspects of the country’s culture and society particularly interested you? Friederike van Stephaudt: What fascinated me from the very beginning was Kazakhstan’s unique position at the intersection of tradition and modernity. The country combines a rich nomadic heritage with rapid urban development and a strong orientation toward the future. I was also struck by the diversity of cultural influences that have shaped Kazakhstan throughout its complex and multidimensional history. Different communities, languages, memories, and traditions coexist and interact here, creating a cultural landscape that is both dynamic and deeply layered. For me, Kazakhstan is a place where questions about identity, belonging, and cultural transformation are constantly being negotiated, which makes it an incredibly interesting environment to live and work in. TCA: How would you assess the current state of cultural relations between Germany and Kazakhstan? What changes have you observed in these relations in recent years? Friederike van Stephaudt: I would describe the cultural relations between Germany and Kazakhstan as lively, productive, and based on genuine mutual interest. What I particularly appreciate is that cultural exchange today is no longer understood as a one-way transfer of knowledge or artistic practices. There is a strong desire on both sides to learn from one another. While Germany and Kazakhstan often approach cultural, social, or artistic questions from different perspectives, we also discover many similarities and shared concerns. Topics such as social transformation, memory, sustainability, inclusion, and digitalization are relevant in both countries. Over recent years, I have observed a growing openness toward collaborative formats that allow artists, cultural professionals, and institutions to work together as equal partners. TCA: The Goethe-Institut’s mission is not limited to promoting the German language; it also aims to foster dialogue between cultures. In Kazakhstan, which of these two areas are you currently prioritizing? Friederike van Stephaudt: For us, these two areas cannot really be separated. We do not prioritize one over the other because language and cultural dialogue are closely interconnected and mutually reinforcing. Learning a language always means engaging with another culture. It offers access to different perspectives, ways of thinking, and forms of expression. At the same time, meaningful cultural exchange becomes much richer when people can communicate directly with one another. This is why we see language promotion and intercultural dialogue as two sides of the same coin, and our work aims to strengthen both equally. TCA: How strong is the interest in learning German in Kazakhstan? Have the motivations and aspirations of young people who want to learn German changed in recent years? Friederike van Stephaudt: Interest in learning German remains strong in Kazakhstan. Of course, motivations evolve over time, and we observe certain trends and shifts from year to year. Many young people are interested in educational opportunities, academic exchange, and professional prospects connected to Germany. At the same time, we see increasing interest among people who simply want to broaden their horizons, engage with another culture, or participate in international networks. As the Goethe-Institut, we work closely with schools and universities to demonstrate the wide range of opportunities that learning German can offer. Language skills are not only valuable for studying or working abroad; they also foster intercultural competence and open doors to international cooperation. TCA: Young people in Kazakhstan are often interested in Germany because of opportunities for education, employment, and professional development. How can the Goethe-Institut transform this interest into deeper cultural connections? Friederike van Stephaudt: Practical opportunities such as studying, working, or conducting research in Germany are often the first point of contact, and we support this interest through information programs, scholarships, and various exchange opportunities. At the same time, we believe it is important to present Germany not only as a destination for education or work, but also as a cultural space. This begins in our language courses, where cultural studies and contemporary social topics are an integral part of learning. We teach German as a living language connected to real people, diverse experiences, literature, arts, and everyday life. Through this approach, professional interest can gradually evolve into a deeper understanding of cultural complexity and mutual exchange. TCA: How familiar do you think readers in Kazakhstan are with German-language literature? Beyond classics such as Goethe, Schiller, and Kafka, what opportunities do you see for introducing contemporary German-language literature to readers in Kazakhstan? Friederike van Stephaudt: It is difficult to assess how familiar Kazakh readers are with contemporary German literature as a whole, but we certainly see a growing interest. The challenge, as in many countries, is making contemporary voices accessible through translation and exchange. This is why the Goethe-Institut regularly supports translations of German literature into Kazakh. We also invite German authors to Kazakhstan and create opportunities for direct encounters between writers and readers. A particularly memorable example was our collaboration with the German author Mareice Kaiser, who traveled with us through Kazakhstan in 2025. The events attracted a broad audience, and the discussions following the readings were remarkably lively and engaged. Such encounters demonstrate that contemporary literature can create meaningful conversations across cultural and linguistic boundaries. TCA: How would you assess the current state of translating Kazakh literature into German? Which Kazakh writers or poets do you think might be particularly interesting to German readers? Friederike van Stephaudt: Although interest in Central Asia has grown in Germany in recent years, Kazakh literature is still not sufficiently represented on the German-language book market. Translation therefore plays a crucial role in creating visibility and enabling literary exchange. What makes Kazakh literature particularly interesting for German readers is its ability to combine local experiences, historical perspectives, and universal questions. Rather than highlighting individual names, I would emphasize the importance of creating more opportunities for translators, publishers, and literary institutions to work together. Sustainable translation structures are essential if we want readers in Germany to discover the richness and diversity of contemporary Kazakh literature. TCA: What kinds of projects could be developed to introduce the history of Kazakhstan’s German community to the younger generation? Friederike van Stephaudt: This is actually a topic we are already actively working on. One promising approach is to use artistic and narrative formats that resonate with younger audiences. For example, we are planning to invite a German-Kazakh graphic novel artist to Kazakhstan. Graphic novels and comics are particularly interesting because they combine visual storytelling with historical reflection. They offer innovative ways of approaching complex histories and can make personal experiences more accessible to younger generations. More broadly, I believe that artistic formats are especially powerful because they create emotional connections and open up new perspectives. They encourage people not only to learn about history, but also to reflect on how historical experiences continue to shape societies today.

title: Tokayev Calls for Stronger Regional Cooperation at Central Asia-Azerbaijan Summit
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has called for stronger economic integration, transport connectivity, water cooperation and artificial intelligence partnerships among Central Asian states and Azerbaijan at the eighth Consultative Meeting of Heads of State of Central Asia and Azerbaijan in Avaza on Oct. 8. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev delivers a speech at the eighth Consultative Meeting of Heads of State of Central Asia and Azerbaijan in Avaza, Turkmenistan. Photo credit: Akorda. Held in the year marking 35 years of independence of the Central Asian states and Azerbaijan, the meeting focused on expanding regional cooperation and strengthening stability amid growing geopolitical tensions, Akorda reported. Trade and connectivity Tokayev proposed increasing intraregional trade from approximately $13 billion to at least $20 billion and called on governments to develop a joint action plan to achieve this target. He also highlighted the potential of border trade and logistics hubs, as well as industrial cooperation centers, to create regional value chains. Tokayev stressed Kazakhstan’s efforts to strengthen transport connectivity, noting the nearing completion of the Moyynty-Kyzylzhar and Darbaza-Maktaaral railway lines and the planned opening of the Bakhty-Ayagoz route next year. He underscored the growing importance of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, or the Middle Corridor, and said World Bank estimates indicate that cargo traffic across the Caspian Sea could increase almost fourfold by 2040 if planned infrastructure projects are implemented. Tokayev also proposed discussing the possible integration of the Middle Corridor with the TRIPP transport initiative at the expert level. Water and AI cooperation Water security was identified as another key priority. Tokayev called for new approaches to managing transboundary water resources and proposed advancing a Framework Convention of Central Asia on Water Use. He also reiterated Kazakhstan’s initiative to establish an International Water Organization under the auspices of the United Nations. In the technology sector, Tokayev proposed creating a Central Asian Partnership Program on Artificial Intelligence to facilitate cooperation among universities, research centers and technology companies. He also suggested developing a Declaration on the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence by Central Asian States and Azerbaijan. Security and humanitarian ties Tokayev stressed the importance of coordinated efforts against terrorism, drug trafficking, human trafficking, organized crime and other transnational threats, including the misuse of digital technologies by criminals and terrorists. He also called for stronger cultural and humanitarian ties through youth exchanges, academic cooperation and a common information space. Among the proposals were a regional television channel based on Kazakhstan’s Silk Way TV, a 2027 Youth Forum on Volunteering, and a common calendar of major cultural, scientific, sporting and tourism events. Focus on implementation Tokayev urged greater attention to implementing regional initiatives, noting that more than 200 initiatives have been put forward since 2018, while only a small proportion have been implemented. He proposed that foreign ministries inventory existing initiatives and assess their relevance and prospects. A Joint Statement was adopted following the eighth Consultative Meeting of Heads of State of Central Asia and Azerbaijan. The post Tokayev Calls for Stronger Regional Cooperation at Central Asia-Azerbaijan Summit appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Zaluzhny enjoys highest trust rating among Ukrainians at 64%, Zelenskyy, Budanov tied at 53% – poll
body:
Former Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine and current Ambassador to the United Kingdom Valeriy Zaluzhny holds the highest level of public trust among Ukrainian politicians and officials at 64%, while President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Head of the Main Directorate of Intelligence Kyrylo Budanov each hold 53%, according to a survey conducted by the Rating Group sociological group on October 3-5, 2026.
According to the trust ratings, 64% of respondents trust Valeriy Zaluzhny, while Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Kyrylo Budanov are trusted by 53% each. Mykhailo Fedorov is trusted by 38% of respondents, Yevhen Khmara by 29%, and Petro Poroshenko and Andriy Sybiha by 24% each.
At the same time, 70% of respondents expressed distrust in Petro Poroshenko, 40% in Volodymyr Zelenskyy, 31% in Kyrylo Budanov, 25% in Valeriy Zaluzhny, 25% in Mykhailo Fedorov, 18% in Andriy Sybiha, and 16% in Yevhen Khmara. Furthermore, 29% of respondents had not heard of Fedorov, 43% of Khmara, and 48% of Sybiha.
In the event of hypothetical presidential elections in the first round, Volodymyr Zelenskyy would receive 22.9% of the vote, and Valeriy Zaluzhny 20.2%.
"The top two leaders in electoral sympathies are Volodymyr Zelenskyy (22.9%) and Valeriy Zaluzhny (20.2%). They are followed by Petro Poroshenko (7.6%), Mykhailo Fedorov (7.6%), and Kyrylo Budanov (6.7%)," the survey states.
The poll was conducted by the Rating Group sociological group from October 3 to 5, 2026, using the CATI (Computer-Assisted Telephone Interviewing) method among 1,000 respondents aged 18 and older across all regions of Ukraine, excluding temporarily occupied territories and areas lacking Ukrainian mobile communication at the time of the survey. The sample was formed through random mobile number generation and weighted according to current State Statistics Service data. It is representative by age, gender, and settlement type, with a margin of statistical error not exceeding 3.1 percentage points at a 0.95 confidence level.

title: Cupertino might be made for your mom, but it’s a good take on tech
body:
Cupertino brings the tech backlash to the CBS procedural — an initially awkward combination, but with rewarding results. The show starts off just slightly unsure, but quickly figures out what to do with these strange times, creating fictionalized dupes of the Zizians, Polymarket, Jeff Bezos’ looksmaxxing obsession, OpenAI stealing Scarlett Johansson’s voice, and the fight for AI guardrails, among other familiar tales, and using them to speak to the feeling of helplessness in the face of rapid change that extends well beyond the greater San Francisco area. It turns out the seemingly outdated tools of broadcast TV are a fantastic way to tackle our uncertain future. 
Please don’t think Cupertino is some kind of Blue Bloods Bay Area or CSI: The Computer. (Sorry, I mean CSI: Cyber, a real show that lasted two seasons and starred Ted Danson, obviously.) Yes, the show is network TV, in the old-fashioned, 20-episodes-in-a-season sense, and it’s airing on CBS in the highly suspicious age of Ellison. But it has certain pedigree coming from creators Robert and Michelle King, the married couple behind the wonderful Elsbeth, Evil, The Good Wife, and The Good Fight. The Kings are often credited as uniquely sophisticated for network TV. But that still leaves some big questions about what this show is and who it’s for.
Also, yes, it is (mostly) a case-of-the-week show about an upstart Silicon Valley law firm taking on Big Tech one suit at a time. Price Siffre (pronounced “cipher”) is made up of lawyers Michael Price (Mike Colter, aka Luke Cage) and Olivia Siffre (Rachel Keller, Legion), along with their assistant Christy Palladino (Ella Stiller), all of whom left the same evil AI company under not-great circumstances in the pilot. (My recommendation is to skip that first episode — just know they sue tech companies — or at least don’t hold it against the show.) Cipher maybe isn’t the wrong word for this main group: Michael is handsome and guarded, Christy is a King-classic spunky investigator type, and Olivia is religious and loves musicals, so she’s introduced listening to Godspell — it took me probably four whole episodes to forgive the show for that too-cute detail. The ensemble really starts to come together, though, when it’s revealed to be a secret Girls5eva reunion, with the additions of Renée Elise Goldsberry as Michael’s ex/rival and Busy Philipps as MacKenzie Scott (formerly Bezos) if she was very fun and a little drunk.
Maybe that’s not quite selling you — two out of five members of a fake girl group from a criminally underwatched sitcom and a bunch of ripped-from-the-headlines tech trials, made by people in their 60s for people in their 60s. But the Kings have their bona fides when it comes to the subject matter — The Good Wife was called “the most tech-savvy show on TV” by Wired in 2013, the same year that BuzzFeed said “everyone in tech needs to be watching” it. That show tackled Bitcoin, viral videos, NSA spying, and the goofy-ass names of 2010s tech startups without being hacky or hammy. Granted, being “good at tech” on an Obama-era show about lawyers in Chicago is different from being “good at tech” on a 2026 show called Cupertino.
[Image: Olivia Siffre (Rachel Keller) and Michael Price (Mike Colter) are as surprised as anyone that they’re founding law firm to take on Big Tech. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/3172660_Cupertino_S1_0897bc2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
One of the creators’ greatest strengths is worldbuilding, and as their vision of Silicon Valley expands it starts to cohere. This is a landscape packed with data brokers, rationalists, underpaid AI trainers, software developers who put ASCII dicks in their code as a gag, gerontocratic judges, petty billionaires, and the frustrated contractors who build their offices and bunkers. That’s where a perceived weakness becomes a strength: The longer network season allows for tangents, explorations, multi-episode arcs, successful fake-outs, and surprise recurrences. These figures can, do, and likely will return, and the show has the time and space to let them unfold and disappear until their resurfacing is a delight. It’s a trick rarely so surprising or fun in clockwork six-to-13-episode streaming seasons, when a detail in episode 3 pretty much has to pay off in episode 7.
This isn’t just good TV, it creates a sense of truth and claustrophobia that the show benefits from; these well-drawn people (mostly) all feel caught together in a highly specific and completely deranging reality. So it follows that the prevailing mood is sort of a peppy paranoia — the dark twist of actual reality, though, is that we’re post-paranoid. Suspicion about the reaches and aims of Big Tech has been shown to be grounded and, frankly, reasonable. The firm’s work suing “the big seven” fictionalized companies comes at a time when every device could be listening and deepfakes mean nothing’s guaranteed to be what it seems. Who wouldn’t be looking over their shoulder, under their desk, and into the source code?
Somehow still, though, the show approaches its central preoccupation — AI — with a healthy fear but surprising lack of judgment. This can be frustrating if you’re sensitive about bots being anthropomorphized (oh, that’s happening, all right), and there were moments early on when I feared the “wrong” lessons were being imparted. But the lack of clean or easy answers makes this a subtler take on what we should be scared of today. 
Cupertino arrives at a time when tech backlash is coming to screens in a big, big way — in cinemas with The Social Reckoning, You Can See Everything, Artificial, and Musk, and on TV too with The Altruists, a Netflix show about FTX coming in November, and AMC’s The Audacity hitting Netflix this past summer. But while The Audacity felt like it was preaching to (and occasionally screaming at) the choir, Cupertino’s key is that it’s about to be fed to an audience that might not be following the finer points of the Hugging Face hack, and riffing on these themes, stories, and real-life archetypes with intelligence, nuance, and some small remainder of joy.
Cupertino premieres on CBS on October 8th.

title: Dear LLM, or how I stopped getting generic advice
body:
An axiom in the LLM community is that the more relevant context you provide to the model â the more useful the reply. When it comes to your work projects, the solution is simple â docs, docs, docs. But what about a standard chat interface? Itâs what made LLMs popular in the first place: we opened ChatGPT for the first time and started playing around, asking it eternal questions and whatnot. Nowadays, we mostly use it as a replacement for Google Search. Any everyday question goes there, and itâs still perfect for that.
There is also a category of diary-worthy questions some of us come to an LLM with, some examples being: âHow do I get rid of bad-habit-x?â, âI lost my job, how do I find a new one?â, âHow do I achieve Y?â. If you ever asked an LLM a similar question, the reply is usually along the lines of âmany people go through X, and here is *some general advice that isnât very likely to help*â
The thing is â itâs missing the context about your life, decisions, common mental traps you fall into. Modern chats have some memory system, which youâd think would solve this, but the âmemoryâ is filled with random insignificant stuff you âgoogledâ there, which is the much more common use-case for an LLM chat.
On top of that, being on the privacy-conscious side of the spectrum, I personally donât like to dump all my life context into a single ChatGPT chat, whether itâs safe on their servers or not. Talking to others about these more sensitive LLM conversations, Iâve noticed a pattern, where people purposefully give less context about themselves, or use incognito mode or some alternative chat interface that promises anonymity.
Iâve been thinking about these pains for some time, before starting to build a solution in the beginning of 2026. I was still working full time in parallel, so I only managed to build a sketchy working prototype for myself. Since then, Iâve had about a hundred conversations there, polished it a lot, onboarded a few users, and finally open-sourced it recently.
The core idea is simple, yet powerful, and itâs the one thing I have barely changed since the very first prototype. You have two layers: diaries (e.g. personal) and topics (e.g. blogging, which country to live in, job-search). You select a diary and a topic, then start a conversation. Nightly, context from your conversation is extracted into a topic summary, then the most significant context from the topic summary is extracted into the diary.
Every new conversation gets summaries of both corresponding diary and topic. This allows you to choose a context you want behind a conversation, and whatever new thoughts surface in that conversation will be similarly pushed with a decreasing level of detail through the topic into the diary the following night.
And regarding sending your whole life context to ChatGPT â my app is open-source and self-hosted, so you are the one holding the keys to your database, though you still route LLM calls to external providers (CF Workers AI, OpenRouter), which is a trade-off I accepted, until we have local LLMs in every house.
I am currently working on a v2 frontend, where mental models that I developed through using the app will become part of the UI itself. E.g. categories will be called diaries, and selecting one will be one-click instead of three. Topic-selection will be automated.
There is currently an entry-barrier as well: having to go through a multistep process just to deploy it, and then it takes a lot of time to fill your context through conversations to feel the core value. I plan to balance these out with a demo, a streamlined deployment, and a tutorial that seeds the app with initial context and makes a user familiar with the interface.
The talking diary has become my daily companion, and the model underneath doesnât matter as much as the fact that it has my context and can surface something Iâve already discovered myself before. For example, I noticed a repeating pattern, where I overinvest in one skill way past the point of diminishing returns, yet completely ignore complementary skills that would move me forward faster. Now the app tries to match that pattern to my new entries, and catches me slipping into it.
Itâs a tool that summarizes MY thoughts and corrects me when I betray MY OWN decisions. To continue the idea from my last post â âMaking LLMs not eat my foodâ¦â , where I talked about making a coding agent teach me TypeScript instead of spitting it out for me â the talking diary is not eating my food for me â I bring the ingredients, and itâs cooking for me!
Thereâs room for LLMs to be used more meaningfully â as tools before everything else. They donât have to be slop-producing factories, where you just let it reproduce the stolen training data in an infinite loop, without adding any useful input to make it unique. Use the tool wisely, and get the most out of it.

body:

title: Russia ready to help seek compromises to open Strait of Hormuz — Foreign Ministry
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. The situation in the Middle East requires urgent efforts toward normalization, and Russia is ready to help seek compromises to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz for regular vessel traffic, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said at a briefing.
"It's crucial that we exert maximum possible efforts to normalize the situation in the Middle East and restore full-fledged shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The Russian Federation remains ready to facilitate the search for compromise solutions based on international law and with due regard for the legitimate rights and interests of all parties involved. Our assets include trusting relations with all states in the region without exception," she said.
The diplomat stressed that from the very beginning of the unprovoked armed aggression by the United States and Israel against Iran, Russia had warned of the serious consequences these actions would have for food security in the world’s most vulnerable countries. "We supported our position with facts and figures. Russia is interested in free, uninterrupted and safe navigation along international maritime routes," she said. "At the same time, we do not believe it is right to discuss the current situation, or the security crisis in the region as a whole, in isolation from the escalation provoked by US actions, which have effectively imposed a naval blockade on Iran. A return to normality is unlikely to be possible without addressing the root causes of the current crisis."
The Strait of Hormuz is a vital transportation route for fertilizer supplies to the global market, Zakharova highlighted. "According to expert estimates, about 30% of all fertilizers and a significant share of the raw materials used to produce them pass through this route every year. Due to disruptions in logistics, available production and export capacity has fallen by almost 40%. The global market has been deprived of about 2.7 million metric tons of products and commodities that are critical to agriculture," Zakharova pointed out.
She added that the scale of the fertilizer shortage on global markets and the rise in fertilizer prices had prompted WTO members to revise their forecast for global trade growth this year, from the previously expected 4.6% to 1.9%. "The main reason is, of course, the destabilization of commodity markets, including agricultural chemicals. According to the organization’s assessment, the crisis in the Middle East is threatening global food security, as fertilizer shortages could lead to lower crop yields. The International Chamber of Commerce has warned that a transport collapse and a blockade of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz could trigger a global food security crisis. If the strait is not fully reopened in the near future, grain prices, which in September approached their 2022-2023 peak, will continue to rise," she said.

title: Casualties from Russian attacks on Kyiv rise to 14 injured, 3 killed – mayor
body:

title: Genre-defying Canadian poet Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
body: STOCKHOLM, Sweden – Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature,” the Swedish Academy said on Thursday, October 8. “She was very taken by surprise,” said Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary of the academy, which awards the prize worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million). “We didn’t have so much time to speak, and all she had time to tell me was that she is for the moment in Iceland, where she’s listening to the wind.” Carson’s work often blends verse, prose, dialogue, and translation in a genre-defying mix. Born in Toronto, the 76-year-old has also held Icelandic citizenship since 2022 and has spent considerable time on the Arctic island in recent years. She is widely known for her translations of classical Greek literature, which heavily influence her work that ranges from opera libretti to literary criticism and verse novels such as Autobiography of Red from 1998. “Almost all her literary production has centered upon the intersection between the philologist’s obsession with words and the poet’s desire for new meaning,” the Academy said. “She has herself identified the etymology of words as the starting point for all her work. Her translations from Classical Greek may be regarded as independent works in their own right.” Her style is exemplified in Norma Jeane Baker of Troy from 2019, a performance piece, which mixes the stories of Helen of Troy in Euripides’ play Helen and Marilyn Monroe. The Academy also praised her ability to explore “the possibilities of writing, a process by which the literary sketch has become of particular value to her.” “Bearing witness to this is Float (2016), a work consisting of 22 chapbooks on different subjects, capable of being read in any order,” it said. Life without Proust Often heralded as her greatest work, Autobiography of Red demonstrates Carson’s ability to “actualize the classical literary tradition,” the Academy said. In the book, she re-examines age-old questions such as “What happens when you love someone who will ultimately destroy you?” Tapping into more modern inspirations, Carson reflected on the character of Albertine, one of the narrator Marcel’s love interests in Marcel Proust’s In Search of Lost Time , in her own book The Albertine Workout . Carson had spent seven years reading Proust’s masterpiece and said in an interview with Canada’s CBC Radio One in 2016 that she suffered withdrawal symptoms after finishing the book, leading her to write The Albertine Workout as a way to prolong the experience. “You think life goes on after Proust, but it seems so gray,” she said. Carson started taking boxing lessons when she was already in her 70s because of a Parkinson’s disease diagnosis. The sport is recommended as a therapy because it helps pay attention to hand-eye coordination and the sequencing of actions. She reflected on the disease’s impact on her handwriting in an interview at the Louisiana Literary Festival in Denmark in 2024: “I scrub out whole paragraphs in shame…the shame of bad handwriting.” Carson, who has taught classics at universities in Canada and the United States, has said that she considers herself a visual artist as much as a literary one. “I think of making a poem as making an object. I have always thought of them more as drawings than as texts, but drawings that are also physically enterable through the fact of language,” she said in the CBC interview. Carson had been among favorites this year Carson had been among the favorites to win this year’s prize, according to bookmakers Ladbrokes, and takes a place beside luminaries such as Alexander Solzhenitsyn, Alice Munro and Ernest Hemingway as a recipient of the award, which often divides opinion among book lovers. The Academy has been lambasted for ignoring some of the literary titans of the last 120 years such as Leo Tolstoy, Virginia Woolf and Jorge Luis Borges, criticized for snubbing US authors — though it gave the prize to singer-songwriter Bob Dylan in 2016 — and accused of being too obscure in its choices. Defenders say the Academy has made popular picks, such as Colombia’s Gabriel Garcia Marquez in 1982 and Doris Lessing in 2007, and argue that part of its task is to highlight lesser-known literary traditions. Last year’s prize was won by Hungarian writer Laszlo Krasznahorkai. Established in the will of Swedish dynamite inventor and businessman Alfred Nobel, the prizes for achievements in literature , science and peace have been awarded since 1901. Literature was the fourth of this year’s Nobels to be announced this week, following medicine, physics and chemistry. The peace prize winner will be announced in Oslo on Friday, October 9. – Rappler.com $1 = 10.0190 Swedish crowns LITE

title: Gunmen Kill Expatriate, Two Others In Kebbi Attack
body: At least three people have been killed and two others injured following an attack by gunmen on the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway construction project in Maiyama Local Government Area of Kebbi State. The victims include two security operatives and an expatriate working on the road project, while two civilians sustained gunshot injuries. According to the Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the Kebbi State Police Command, Superintendent Bashir Usman, the incident occurred at a construction site in Gubba Village, through Andarai District of Maiyama Local Government Area. Usman said armed men suspected to be Lakurawa terrorists, allegedly encroaching from the Kebbe axis of neighbouring Sokoto, attacked the construction site, killing two security agents and a foreign national. He said two civilians were also injured in the attack and subsequently evacuated for medical attention. The police spokesperson added that, on the same day, another attack by the suspected terrorists along the Birnin Malam axis was successfully repelled by police teams. He said joint security forces responded to the attacks, with tactical teams deployed to strengthen security and prevent further attacks. The PPRO further disclosed that scores of the attackers were neutralised by military personnel, while several motorcycles were recovered. Following the incident, construction activities at the affected site have been suspended as security agencies intensify surveillance and deploy additional operatives to the area. The PPRO assured workers on the project of the government’s commitment to their safety, urging them to remain calm and resolute as security agencies continue efforts to safeguard their lives and property. Recently, Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris, visited Jandutsi and other neighbouring communities bordering Gubba Village to sympathise with residents over recent bandit attacks in the area. The governor also reaffirmed the commitment of his administration to strengthening security and protecting communities affected by the attacks. The post Gunmen Kill Expatriate, Two Others In Kebbi Attack appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Gunmen kill Plateau community leader, injure two others – Group
body:
Gunmen have killed a youth leader and former chairman of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association (BYM) in Gashish District of Plateau State, Paul Danladi.
Mr Danladi was reportedly killed around 6 p.m. on Wednesday near Rantis Village along the Gashish-Barkin Ladi road while riding his motorcycle to Barkin Ladi, according to the BYM.
The association confirmed the killing in a statement issued by its National Publicity Secretary, Rwang Tengwong, on Thursday in Jos.
The BYM said Mr Danladi was a respected community leader and condemned his killing, while calling on security agencies to investigate the incident and arrest those responsible.
The association also reported two other attacks in parts of Plateau State on Wednesday in which two people were injured.
According to the group, one person sustained serious injuries in an attack around Gwom-Ajang in Foron and was taken to the Jos University Teaching Hospital for treatment.
Another victim, identified as Mafeng Lamba, was reportedly injured along Sho Road and taken to a hospital for treatment.
The BYM further alleged that Bitrus Dadon was attacked along the same road and had his motorcycle stolen.
The incidents occurred amid continued concerns over attacks on communities and travellers in parts of Plateau, particularly in Barkin Ladi, Riyom and Jos South Local Government Areas.
The association urged the Plateau State Government, police, Nigerian Army, Department of State Services and other security agencies to strengthen surveillance and intelligence gathering around vulnerable communities and roads.
It also called for a proactive security response to prevent further attacks and protect residents.
Efforts to obtain confirmation from security agencies were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.
The circumstances surrounding Mr Danladi’s killing and the identities and motives of the attackers could not be independently established.

title: Haredi protester dragged by vehicle at Jerusalem's entrance as anti-draft demonstration begins
body: Haredi (ultra-Orthodox) demonstrators protesting the arrest of draft dodgers are still gathered at the Jerusalem light rail near Bar Ilan Street, the Israel Police spokesperson announced in a statement on Thursday evening.While the protest started as an organized demonstration in support of draft evaders, it devolved into a riot targeting the expansion of Jerusalem's light rail, Ynet reported.According to the police statement, rioters damaged buildings and infrastructure, set fire to trash cans, and threw stones at police officers and security forces, injuring them. One protester has been arrested as a result, Ynet added. Additionally, female police officer had to be rescued after rioters attacked and damaged her vehicle."Police officers continue to operate resolutely at the scene to maintain public order," the statement said.Haredi (ultra-Orthodox) protesters block traffic on Highway 4 during anti-draft demonstration, October 8, 2026. (CREDIT: ISRAEL POLICE)Hundreds gathered near Chords Bridge to protestA haredi protester was dragged by a vehicle at the entrance to Jerusalem as hundreds of demonstrators gathered near the Chords Bridge on Thursday afternoon to protest the arrest of draft dodgers.המוקד: נהג דורס מפגינים בירושלים (הרשקוביץ) https://t.co/2pBjcp9Vi6— חדשות המוקד (@hamoked_il) October 8, 2026The protest, organized by the anti-IDF draft extremist haredi Jerusalem Faction (Peleg Yerushalmi), took place throughout central Israel and Jerusalem following the arrest of two haredi draft evaders earlier this week in Beersheba and Eilat.In Jerusalem, the city's light rail operations were halted due to the protests. Police added that dozens of protesters had gathered on Bar-Ilan Street, disrupting traffic in the area. Footage shared on social media shows police officers attempting to forcibly drag protesters off the road near the entrance to the city.Additionally, protesters in Jerusalem stopped a vehicle carrying a haredi soldier. The soldier was rescued by police officers on the scene using tear gas to repel the protesters. One person was arrested. In central Israel, Israel Police closed Highway 4 to traffic. Earlier in the day, officers were deployed near the Bnei Brak Interchange and Geha Junction, at the entrance to Petah Tikva. Three additional protesters were arrested for assaulting officers on Highway 4, police said in an evening statement."Protest is a right; disturbing public order is not," Police Commissioner Daniel Levy said in an afternoon statement. Protesters also surrounded the building where an election campaign conference by the haredi Sephardi Shas party was being held in Modi'in Illit. Party chairman Arye Deri was present at the event, a Shas spokesperson confirmed to The Jerusalem Post.Shas to protesters: 'Do not allow the attorney-general and Kaplan money to sow division among us'In response to the protesters attempting to breach the Shas event, the party's leadership told haredi protesters to channel their anger at Israel's attorney-general."The deliberate and painful arrests of yeshiva students at this time, and the chaos we are now witnessing on Israel's roads, are the work of the attorney-general, aimed at breaking up the right-wing bloc, turning public opinion against the ultra-Orthodox community, and causing some of its members to refrain from voting. This is blatant and unprecedented interference by the judicial system and elements within the Military Police in the election campaign," the party said in a statement. "According to information in our possession, Kaplan protest activists are behind the funding of the demonstrations. They have been joined by extremist elements who are leading violent and life-threatening protests. These actions do not represent the ultra-Orthodox community, constitute a terrible desecration of God's name, and cause serious damage to efforts to regulate the status of those studying Torah.""And to the ultra-Orthodox public, we say: Do not allow the attorney-general and Kaplan money to sow division among us. Do not let them win!"In response to Shas's statement, the Committee to Save the Torah World said that its protesters remembered the way the party's leaders treated them when a haredi draft law was being drafted in the Knesset. "Even then, when that Torah position was proclaimed loud and clear, the crocodile tears and fake displays of emotion emerged, accompanied by the same foolish and false accusation: that the Left and the Kaplan protest movement were behind the struggle," the committee said in a statement."Neither the Left nor Kaplan. It is the God-fearing community alone that is leading the struggle to save the Torah world, supported by effective organizations that genuinely care for the welfare and protection of Sephardi and Ashkenazi yeshiva students and kollel scholars — independently funded and free of political calculations."All for the sake of Heaven, and solely to save the Torah world from the harsh conscription decree."The demonstrations lasted between two and three hours and caused severe traffic disruptions during rush hour. Police recommended that the public stay updated on road blockages and congestion and, where possible, travel via alternate routes."Right now, we are once again witnessing the approach favored and rewarded by the current Netanyahu government: 'We would rather die than enlist,'" Yashar Party head Gadi Eisenkot wrote in a Thursday X/Twitter post."Under this government, the lives of Israeli citizens who serve and work have turned into a succession of disasters, failures, and accidents. Their quality of life is treated as nothing more than a nuisance, sacrificed for the sake of political survival, while draft dodgers have become the ones calling the shots.""This distinction between the value of different lives not only erodes Israeli society but also undermines our security," wrote Eisenkot. בשעות האלה אנחנו שוב עדים לשיטה המתוגמלת והעדיפה על ממשלת נתניהו הנוכחית: ״נמות ולא נתגייס״. תחת הממשלה הזו, חייהם של אזרחי ישראל המשרתים והעובדים הפכו לשרשרת של אסונות, מחדלים ותאונות. איכות חייהם היא לא יותר ממטרד, המוקרב לטובת הישרדות פוליטית, והמשתמטים הפכו לבעלי הבית. ההבחנה בין דם לדם לא רק מדרדרת את החברה הישראלית, היא גם פוגעת בביטחון שלנו. אתמול ציינו את המחדל והאסון החמורים בתולדות ישראל, תחת הקואליציה הזאת, ואת גבורת הבנים והבנות שהצילו נפשות בעם הזה מתוך אחריות, אהבה ומחויבות עליונה להגנה על הבית. במקום לחזק את צה״ל, להישמע להפצרות הרמטכ״ל לסייע ולחזק את מי שאמון על בטחוננו בעוד לוחמים - ממשלת ההשתמטות מטפחת את הכאוס ואי-הסדר ברחובות. מה שקורה עכשיו הוא קדימון לישראל תחת קדנציה נוספת של קואליציה כזאת. מדינת ישראל לא יכולה להרשות לעצמה עוד 4 שנים כאלה. לא נאפשר להם לדרדר את ישראל לעוד ארבע שנים כאלה. אני פונה לכל ישראלי שהתמונות והסרטונים מרתיחים אותו - קחו את הכעס לקלפי. הפעם, נחזיר את ישראל לדרך הישר!— Gadi Eisenkot - גדי איזנקוט (@gadi_eisenkot) October 8, 2026"Yesterday, we marked the gravest failure and disaster in Israel's history, occurring under this coalition, as well as the heroism of the sons and daughters who saved lives out of a sense of responsibility, love, and an unwavering commitment to defending our home." "Instead of strengthening the IDF and heeding the Chief of Staff's urgent pleas to support those entrusted with our security and our combat troops, this 'government of draft evasion' fosters chaos and disorder in the streets," he accused. "What is happening now is a preview of what Israel would look like under another term of such a coalition."Ramat Gan concert expected to draw 17,000 peopleA second major event is expected to worsen traffic congestion: a concert at Ramat Gan Stadium on Thursday evening.The show, featuring Israeli artists Omer Adam, Odaya, Osher Cohen, Idan Raichel, Ben Zur, and Rita, is expected to draw approximately 17,000 spectators, adding significant vehicle and pedestrian traffic to roads leading to the stadium and surrounding area.Police will have to manage both events simultaneously, assigning officers to maintain public order at the protest sites while also securing the concert and directing traffic around the stadium.The main concern is that road blockages during the protests, should they occur, could also affect traffic heading toward Ramat Gan Stadium and cause widespread disruptions throughout the area.Keshet Neev, Avi Solomon, Alon Hachmon, Hodaya Ran, and Jerusalem Post Staff contributed to this report.

title: Qorvo Announces X-Band RF Front-End for AESA Radar Systems
body:
Qorvo has announced an X-band RF front-end solution for active electronically scanned array (AESA) radar systems, combining high transmit output with low-noise, high-linearity receive performance while reducing RF content within the array lattice.
The solution centers on the QPX0252, a four-channel beamformer IC covering 7.9 to 12 GHz. Qorvo says its transmit output can directly drive compatible front-end modules (FEMs), including the QPF5012, eliminating external driver amplifiers. Companion devices provide GaN power-amplifier bias control and RF switching.
The architecture addresses the limited space available in flat-panel AESA arrays, where beamformers, FEMs, power-control and switching circuitry must fit within constrained lattice spacing.
“ Beamformers are typically designed as stand-alone components, leaving customers to integrate the FEMs, bias control and RF switching around them,” said Diwakar Vishakhadatta, vice president of Defense & Aerospace Products at Qorvo. “ We developed the QPX0252 as part of the X-band front-end architecture, defining its transmit, receive and control functions around the requirements of the radar system.”
For high-power radar applications, Qorvo says the FEM establishes a low system noise figure while the QPX0252 operates in a high-linearity mode. The company’s system analysis indicates up to 20 dB higher cascaded input P1dB compared with other market offerings.
Qorvo said QPX0252 samples and evaluation kits are available now and are compatible with its production X-band FEMs across multiple power levels and configurations. Supporting gate-bias, drain-bias and RF switch-control devices are also sampling, with the company citing sub-100-nanosecond Tx/Rx switching.
The solution was announced at European Microwave Week 2026 in London.

title: Ethiopia and Eritrea edge closer to direct conflict as troops enter Tigray
body: Eritrean troops have crossed into Ethiopia 's Tigray region and come under fire from Ethiopian drones as they pushed south, a conflict monitor said. It is the clearest sign yet that Ethiopia's renewed internal troubles could spark a war between the two neighbours. Eritrean troops have crossed the border at the town of Zalambessa and headed for the road between Adigrat and Idaga Hamus, said Dr Jalale Getachew Birru, East Africa analyst at the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data project (Acled). “Ethiopian National Defence Forces drones targeted Eritrean troops at Guada as they travelled by vehicle towards Idaga Hamus,” he said. Residents of Adigrat, about 25km south of the border, told Reuters they saw two military vehicles carrying dozens of Eritrean soldiers pass through the town on Wednesday morning. Ethiopia demanded that the troops leave. “All foreign military forces operating within our sovereign territory must withdraw immediately,” said Enatalem Melese, Government Communication Minister. Eritrea did not deny its troops had crossed the border. In a post on X, Information Minister Yemane Meskel on Wednesday accused Ethiopia of building “a fallacious narrative of 'self defence' to rationalise and camouflage its war of aggression”. The crossing into Ethiopia comes days after federal forces retook Mekelle, the Tigrayan capital, from the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF). According to Acled data, Tigray Defence Forces, the TPLF's armed wing, have a heavy presence in Idaga Hamus and Adigrat. Many TPLF leaders are in the rural Ahferom district of central Tigray, Dr Jalale said. He said Eritrea is suspected of backing the Alliance for Survival, a coalition of seven armed groups, including the TPLF, that was formed last month to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. Eritrea has two possible motives, he said. It was unhappy with the 2022 Pretoria agreement, which ended the war in Tigray, because it wanted the TPLF destroyed. Asmara's grievances against the TPLF date back to the 1998-2000 border war, when the party led Ethiopia. Dr Jalale said it wants to turn Tigray into a buffer zone that is hostile to Addis Ababa. “Hence, Eritrean forces entered the war in Tigray to halt the Ethiopian government and allied forces from reaching the border and potentially fighting within Eritrea's territory,” he said. The commander of the pro-government Tigray Peace Force, Gebreigziabher Beyene, made a similar point. Eritrea is “deliberately deploying its forces so that the fighting takes place inside Tigray rather than spilling into Eritrea”, he told AFP. Ethiopia closed its embassy in Asmara last Thursday and expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats, accusing them of threatening national security. Eritrea responded by cutting ties. The US has warned that “the Horn of Africa cannot sustain another military conflict and humanitarian crisis”. In a statement on Saturday, it urged both countries to exercise “maximum restraint”. Eritrea's move also puts the spotlight on Egypt, which has its own dispute with Ethiopia over its share of the Nile, in addition to the latter's Red Sea ambitions. Cairo has spent the past few years building ties with Asmara. In October 2024, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El Sisi and his Eritrean counterpart Isaias Afwerki agreed with Somalia's President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud on a framework for strategic co-operation that includes Red Sea security. Ahmed Moussa, a prominent pro-government Egyptian television host, said on Saturday that Egypt and Eritrea have a joint defence agreement, though no text has ever been made public. With Cairo and Addis Ababa trading blame over the Nile dam and also expelling each other's diplomats last week, the question now is how far Egypt would go if its ally faces a serious Ethiopian attack.

title: Strike on Ukrainian public bus leaves 30 dead as blackouts worsen in Kyiv
body:
Locals and rescuers clear the rubble of a residential building destroyed in a Russian missile strike on Pryluky, Ukraine, Wednesday. Evgeniy Maloletka/AP hide caption
KYIV, Ukraine — A Russian-guided bomb exploded next to public buses filled with passengers in eastern Ukraine, authorities said Thursday, killing 30 people as part of a wave of attacks that also worsened power outages in the capital.
The morning attack occurred next to a bus stop in the war-torn city of Kramatorsk in Ukraine's Donetsk region, prompting public transport to be suspended in the area.
"There is no doubt that Russia is cynically targeting civilians," Oleksandr Honcharenko, head of the city's military administration, said, adding that the rescue effort had been hampered by subsequent Russian attacks using small drones.
Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4 1/2 years since Moscow's full-scale invasion. Russia has escalated its aerial attack in recent weeks, putting pressure on Ukraine as it prepares for winter and hitting the infrastructure keeping its war-battered economy afloat. Recent targets have included energy systems, key industries, railways, post offices, shopping centers, telecom networks, gas stations and grain exports.
A rescue worker sits on the ground next to a residential building destroyed in a Russian missile strike on Pryluky, Ukraine, Wednesday. Evgeniy Maloletka/AP hide caption
Thursday's attack followed a Russian missile strike a day earlier that killed 22, including five children, in the northern Ukrainian town of Pryluky. Rescuers were searching the rubble of a residential building. At least 54 people were wounded. Several survivors slept in heavily damaged apartments because they couldn't find anywhere else to stay.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy traveled to Pryluky on Thursday with visiting British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who announced new sanctions on Russia.
Zelenskyy warned that Russia will likely escalate daily missile and drone attacks as winter approaches. He appealed for additional defense support from NATO countries.
"It is important that support in words takes concrete form in new packages for Ukraine's defense," he wrote in an online post. "Supplies of anti-ballistic capabilities, ammunition for our combat aircraft and investments in interceptors — all of this is directly helping save lives every day."
In audio clips responding to journalist's questions Thursday evening, Zelenskyy said a Ukrainian delegation would meet in the U.S. with President Donald Trump's representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff for two days beginning Friday to discuss strengthening Ukraine's air defenses, among other issues.
Ukraine's energy company DTEK said national grid operator Ukrenergo had ordered emergency power outages in Kyiv. Regular, rolling outages that occur on a schedule across the country will be halted during these shutdowns.
Officials are urging families to prepare emergency kits, store drinking water and maintain backup power sources, as Moscow keeps up the intensity of its attacks.
Kyiv police said bomb disposal specialists defused two unexploded ballistic missile warheads, each weighing about half a ton, after they landed near residential buildings. Late Wednesday, Russian drones struck Kyiv's Obolonskyi and Desnianskyi districts, killing four people and injuring 12, including four children, police said.
Russian technology giant Yandex said one of its data centers in the western Ryazan region was damaged in a Ukrainian drone attack, taking the site offline.
Also Thursday, Ukraine said its forces struck a large oil refinery complex in the city of Salavat, some 1,200 kilometers (about 750 miles) east of Moscow. Ukraine's General Staff described the complex as one of Russia's largest oil refining and petrochemical facilities. The claim could not be independently verified.
Ukrainian drones also reached Russia's Omsk region in western Siberia, more than 2,000 kilometers (1,242 miles) from the border with Ukraine. Omsk regional Gov. Vitaly Khotsenko said most of the drones were shot down by air defenses, but one "reached a northern industrial hub." He didn't elaborate. Russian independent news outlet Astra reported that the Omsk oil refinery was on fire after the attack. There was no official confirmation of the report.
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said his government presented proposals to both Russia and Ukraine aimed at protecting civilian shipping in the Black Sea, while warning that commercial trade and grain exports could be disrupted by escalating military offensives.
Separately, Lithuania deployed about 100 additional soldiers to help secure the NATO member's border with the Russian enclave of Kaliningrad, the Baltic country's defense minister, Robertas Kaunas, said. Sandwiched between Lithuania and Poland, Kaliningrad is separated from mainland Russia and remains a major security concern for NATO's eastern flank.
