title: Emeka Rollas apologises to Regina, mother, Ned Nwoko, others over marital crisis remarks
body:
Emeka Rollas, the former president of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN), has apologised to actress Regina Daniels and her mother, Rita Daniels, following comments he made amid the actress’s marital dispute with her estranged husband, Ned Nwoko, the senator representing Delta North.
PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that Mr Rollas spoke on the dispute, saying he witnessed Mr Nwoko raise concerns about Regina’s smoking habit. He said he decided to speak because he was mentioned in the controversy.
According to him, some of the incidents cited by the senator happened in his presence. He maintained that his decision to speak was motivated by concern for Regina’s wellbeing and was not intended to ridicule or disgrace her.
The former AGN president also expressed disappointment with Okey Bakassi, Charles Inojie, Chinyere Wilfred, Jide Kosoko and Sanni Danji, whom he said were aware of the situation but failed to speak out.
He stated that their silence left him to face attacks alone after he became involved in the controversy. Mr Rollas also directed criticism at Rita, urging her to pay greater attention to her daughter’s health instead of the AGN elections.
He, however, faulted Mr Nwoko for making the family dispute public and using social media to call out Regina. Mr Rollas also rejected claims that Mr Nwoko had financed the guild, paid for and furnished its office or donated $200 million to the organisation.
Meanwhile, Mr Rollas issued an apology to the people he mentioned during the crisis, conceding that his approach could have been different. He posted the statement on Instagram on Thursday.
Looking back at the events, the former AGN president said he had learnt that being correct about a matter was not enough if the situation was not handled properly.
He said: “On 20 November, during a period of intense pressure surrounding the Actors Guild of Nigeria and its leadership, I made a public statement concerning Senator Prince Ned Nwoko, Regina Daniels, Mrs Rita Daniels, members of the AGN Board of Trustees and some of my colleagues. At the time, I believed strongly in the issues I raised and had my reasons for speaking.
“But today, looking back, I must honestly admit: I regret the timing, the platform and the manner in which | handled it. These were people I had related with, worked with and, in some cases, considered friends. More importantly, I made those statements at a time when a family was going through a deeply personal and difficult period. I should not have taken that path.”
Furthermore, Mr Rollas said he could not determine whether those involved would forgive him, stressing that accepting his apology was their choice.
He said he chose to apologise after revisiting the incident and recognising that his conduct at the time was not something he was proud of.
He added that his recent encounter with Rita, which happened while some people were trying to broker peace between them, also encouraged him to rethink his words and apologise for what he had said.
“So today, without excuses or conditions, I sincerely apologise: to Mrs Rita Daniels and the Daniels family. To Senator Prince Ned Nwoko and his family. To Regina Daniels.
“To the AGN Board of Trustees. And to Okey Bakassi, Charles Inojie, Chinyere Wilfred, Jide Kosoko, Sanni Danji, Agility, Nazareth Jesse, my former aides and every colleague whose name I mentioned. I am sorry”, Mr Rollas noted.
He stressed that a good leader must have the courage to speak out while also possessing the humility to admit when they could have approached an issue differently.
“I waited longer, or chose a better path. I may still hold my convictions about some of the issues I raised then, but I take responsibility for my actions and my timing. As I move forward, I choose peace, reconciliation, dignity and respect. I am human. I made a mistake. I have reflected. And today, I say sincerely: I am sorry.”

title: ‘I Don’t Know What To Believe,’ How Russians Are Grappling With Plague Scare
body: When a woman died of suspected plague in Siberia last week, Oksana was in the maternity ward for observation. “Everything was fine, and then they told us that a woman had died. And they wouldn’t let anyone in or out,” the 35-year-old told AFP. For four days, she was kept in a hospital in Shelekhov, the same town where a 28-year-old lab worker, Darya Shipilova, had been hospitalised before she was reported to have died of plague. Russian authorities have downplayed the incident, saying that she died from “pneumonia of an unknown aetiology” and that post-mortem analysis showed no trace of an infection connected with her “professional work” at the Irkutsk anti-plague institute. In this undated handout picture released by the Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute, specialists work in a laboratory as part of anti-epidemic measures during the 2019 Winter Universiade in Krasnoyarsk. (Photo by Handout / Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute / AFP) | Handout / Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute / AFP Local media reports suggested she could have contracted the disease after breaking a test tube at the laboratory. The incident has triggered global concern about a possible outbreak and calls for Russia to provide more information. It has also drawn criticism and comparisons with Moscow’s long history of downplaying or covering up the scale of health disasters — ranging from the Soviet response to the 1986 Chernobyl disaster to the coronavirus pandemic. A woman wearing a face mask walks past the anti-plague institute in the city of Irkutsk on October 7, 2026. (Photo by TATYANA MAKEYEVA / AFP) | TATYANA MAKEYEVA / AFP In Shelekhov, rumours have filled the information abyss. “I’ve read about it being some kind of unclear pneumonia or Covid, something like that. To be honest, I don’t believe in anything anymore,” Oksana, who declined to give her surname, told AFP. “There’s so much information that I no longer know what to believe or who to listen to.” “The day it happened, my mum rang me, shouting that 10 people had already died, even though there were no official reports,” Alexandra Iskalova, a 22-year-old who works in a medical centre, told AFP. “I’d read somewhere that it was something like Hong Kong syphilis, and that it was actually caused by bears,” she said, referring to a fictional disease from a popular Russian TV show. “People were absolutely panicking because there were no official statements,” she added. ‘We don’t know’ On the streets, the town appears outwardly calm — no panic and few masks. People walk past street vendors in the town of Shelekhov, where an employee of the Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute had died in a local infectious diseases hospital, in the Irkutsk region on October 7, 2026. (Photo by STRINGER / AFP) | STRINGER / AFP Yet many told AFP they are concerned. “It’s frightening,” said Alina, 22. “My brother’s at primary school. They’ve already made masks compulsory, so they have to wear them everywhere. They’re even allowed to stay off school if they’re really worried.” She said her aunt works at the anti-plague institute and was also quarantined. Tatyana, 66, is also frustrated by the lack of official guidance from the authorities. “Of course we’re worried … How on earth are we supposed to protect ourselves?” “We don’t know how the infection spreads. Or how it’s detected,” she added. “There are a lot of rumours going around, all kinds of information, and it’s unclear what’s true. In reality, nobody is telling us what actually happened.” On Wednesday, World Health Organization (WHO) chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged Moscow to clarify “media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause” from the Irkutsk institute. World Health Organization (WHO) Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus looks on during a press conference on global health issues, in Geneva, on October 7, 2026. Photo by FABRICE COFFRINI / AFP When asked about a possible second case, the Kremlin appeared to reject it. “The vast majority of what the media is reporting regarding this situation is false information,” spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters. Rospotrebnadzor said Wednesday that the situation in the Irkutsk region remained “stable”, and that nearly 5,000 tests had been conducted, none of which revealed dangerous pathogens. US President Donald Trump has offered to “help” Russia and said he would call his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to discuss the reports. That offer was widely laughed off on the streets of Shelekhov. “It’s just funny,” said Olga, a 68-year-old former accountant. “In his heart he was probably happy that Russia had some problems, some kind of ‘plague’,” she added. “He’d probably be glad if we really had an epidemic in our country.” AFP The post ‘I Don’t Know What To Believe,’ How Russians Are Grappling With Plague Scare appeared first on Channels Television .

title: UK ramps up sanctions against Russian shadow fleet, crypto industry, big oil
body:
Editor's note: this article was updated with further details provided in a U.K. government press statement released after this article was first published.
The U.K. published 38 new sanctions listings on Oct. 8, targeting ships helping Russia evade existing sanctions and a range of companies in Moscow's military-industrial complex, energy, and cryptocurrency sectors.
"The message is simple: if you help Russia fund or equip this war, you will face the consequences," reads a U.K. government press release.
Among the businesses in the new sanctions listings are three cryptocurrency exchanges and two payment platforms.
Xeltox Enterprises, one of those listed entities has "been involved in obtaining a benefit from or supporting the government of Russia by carrying on business in a sector of strategic significance (...) the financial services sector," reads the U.K. government's sanctions listing .
Russia has increasingly sought to use cryptocurrency , which is hard to track, to circumvent global sanctions, and the new U.K. sanctions target the "A7" network, which is at the heart of Moscow's attempts to evade financial sanctions.
That has prompted the U.K., the U.S ., the EU , and Ukraine to target crypto schemes in recent sanctions packages.
Also featuring on the listings are two further oil companies: Zarubezhneft and INK Capital.
"The U.K. was the first country in the G7 to sanction the top four Russian oil companies," reads the press statement.
The U.K. has also added 12 ships to its list of sanctioned vessels accused of being part of Russia's shadow fleet — dilapidated vessels suspected of helping Moscow evade price caps and bans on its trade in oil and gas.
That takes the number of ships sanctioned by the U.K. to 645 and the total number of Russia sanctions to 3,537.

title: General Staff: Defense Forces strike Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refining complex in Bashkortostan
body:
Units of the Ukrainian Defense Forces struck the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refining and petrochemical complex located in the city of Salavat in the Republic of Bashkortostan, Russia, on Thursday, resulting in a fire at the facility, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported on Telegram.

According to the military agency, Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat is one of Russia's largest oil refining and petrochemical complexes, with a processing capacity of up to 10 million tonnes of hydrocarbon raw materials per year. The enterprise produces automotive gasoline, diesel fuel, fuel oil, bitumen, polyethylene, and other refined and petrochemical products.

The General Staff noted that the facility is actively utilized to supply the needs of the armed forces of Russia.

title: Speculations about Russian interference in foreign elections groundless — MFA
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. There can be no talk of any interference by Russia in elections abroad; unlike the West, Moscow does not engage in such practices Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova has said.
She commented on remarks by Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani, who suggested that Russia might attempt to influence elections in Italy.
"There can be no suspicion of Russian interference in electoral processes abroad. That is not our style - unlike Western political elites, who brazenly and crudely intrude into election campaigns before the eyes of the entire world, and sometimes even kidnap national presidents, exert direct pressure on the political communities of states that interest them, or - I repeat - act with absolute impunity. Nothing constrains them as they shape political processes in sovereign nations," she said.

title: Hendel calls on Ofer Winter to break with Netanyahu's bloc, form 'Zionist bloc' with Reservists
body: Leader of the Reservists-Economic party Yoaz Hendel on Thursday called on People of Israel party chairman Ofer Winter to sign a surplus vote-sharing agreement ahead of the upcoming elections and jointly declare that the two parties would only join a Zionist government without haredi (ultra-Orthodox) or Arab parties.Hendel's right-wing party has called for a broad Zionist government without extremists to be formed after the elections. It has stated that it does not belong to either Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc or the opposition bloc seeking to replace the premier.Winter has endorsed Netanyahu as prime minister, despite calling for a change in leadership after the October 7 Hamas attacks in 2023. His right-wing party consists of candidates who have not been in the Knesset before, nor were they part of the security failures surrounding October 7.“Winter, reverse your statement that you are only with Netanyahu and the haredi parties. You cannot win on the battlefield with haredi parties. You cannot meet the missions on the front,” Hendel said in a statement outside the Tel Hashomer IDF recruitment office. Let's sign a surplus vote agreement and jointly declare that we are two parties that will only enter a Zionist government.“Together, we will be a blocking bloc against non-Zionist governments and coalitions with haredi or Arab parties,” he added.Hendel made the call for Winter to sign with him ahead of the approaching deadline for submitting surplus vote-sharing agreements before the October 27 election.Hendel seeks vote-sharing partner as opposition, coalition finalize dealsIn Netanayhu's bloc, his ruling Likud party on Tuesday signed a vote-sharing agreement with the Religious Zionist Party (RZP) led by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich.Meanwhile, all the major parties in the opposition bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu signed surplus vote-sharing agreements in September, with the stated aim of increasing the number of seats won by the bloc.In a surplus vote-sharing agreement, the two parties pool their surplus votes after the initial allocation of Knesset seats following the elections.If the combined surplus is enough to secure an additional seat, one party can receive it, potentially strengthening the bloc to which the parties belong.The deal is only relevant if both parties pass the electoral threshold. Both the Reservists-Economic party and the People of Israel have recently polled either just above or below the electoral threshold.As parties sign vote-sharing deals, Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit left outNational Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's far-right Otzma Yehudit party, part of Netanyahu's coalition bloc, has not signed a surplus vote-sharing agreement. The party stated that Likud had refused to sign a surplus-vote sharing agreement with Otzma Yehudit.It accused Likud of seeking to form a unity government with Gadi Eisenkot, chairman of the Yashar party and the leading candidate for prime minister in the opposition bloc in recent polling.

title: UAE and Thailand conclude Cepa talks to boost trade and investment
body: The UAE and Thailand have concluded negotiations for their Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement , which is expected to remove trade barriers and boost bilateral relations. The countries began talks on the deal in 2023 and launched a joint business council the same year. As part of the negotiations, they discussed avenues to enhance trade, investment and opportunities to expand co-operation, the ministry of Foreign Trade said in a statement on Thursday. In the coming phase, the UAE and Thailand will finalise the legal and technical procedures required for the agreement to be signed and implemented, it said. The Cepa is expected to accelerate trade flows, unlock new investment opportunities and strengthen private sector co-operation in priority sectors, including advanced manufacturing, logistics, food security, digital trade, renewable energy and precious metals. “The conclusion of negotiations … embodies our shared commitment to building stronger economic bridges between South-East Asia and the Middle East,” said Minister of Foreign Trade Dr Thani Al Zeyoudi “Thailand is one of the most dynamic and diversified economies in the region, and this agreement will open new avenues for companies, investors and entrepreneurs in both countries to expand and access high-growth markets.” The Cepa builds on strong ties between the UAE and Thailand. Bilateral non-oil trade in the first half of 2026 jumped by more than 75 per cent year-on-year to $10.2 billion. Trade last year also grew more than 65 per cent to $12.3 billion. The UAE's key non-oil exports to Thailand include gold, aluminium and other industrial goods. “These figures reflect the growing integration of the two economies and the scale of opportunity the agreement can unlock,” the ministry said. “By reducing trade barriers, enhancing market access and stimulating investment flows, the Cepa will support our long-term economic objectives and generate new opportunities across a wide range of strategic sectors,” Dr Al Zeyoudi added. The UAE has signed 38 Cepas with trading partners as it seeks to boost investment ties, expand its non-oil economic base and broaden exports. The Cepa programme is a key pillar of the UAE's foreign trade agenda, which aims to increase non-oil foreign trade to Dh4 trillion ($1.1 trillion) by 2031.

title: Two of Britain’s new E-7 aircraft airborne
body: Both of the Royal Air Force’s delivered Boeing E-7 Wedgetail aircraft were flying at the same time on Thursday afternoon, the first occasion on which the two have been airborne together. WT001 came south from RAF Lossiemouth for the orbit areas in the South West using the callsign Boeing 31, while WT002 was out of MOD Boscombe Down as Boeing 38. Between them they represent two thirds of the entire future British airborne early warning fleet. The second aircraft was still being outfitted by STS Aviation at Birmingham Airport as recently as January, so its appearance out of Boscombe Down marks its arrival in the flight test programme alongside the first aircraft. The Wedgetail is built on the Boeing 737 Next Generation airframe, the same basic aeroplane as the RAF’s Poseidon maritime patrol fleet, and carries the Northrop Grumman Multi-role Electronically Scanned Array radar in the distinctive dorsal fin above the fuselage. The array has no moving parts, which is the main departure from the rotating radomes of earlier airborne early warning aircraft, and it allows the operator to concentrate the radar’s attention on a particular sector while continuing to scan elsewhere. #RAF Royal Air Force Boeing E-7A Wedgetail AEW.1 2x #43C97A WT001 – BOEING 31 #43C97B WT002 – BOEING 38 Both RAF Wedgetail AEW.1’s are currently airborne this afternoon. WT001 made its way down from Lossiemouth for the orbit areas in the South West, while WT002 has departed… pic.twitter.com/jaTrS1apv1 — Armchair Admiral (@ArmchairAdml) October 8, 2026 The most recent milestone before this one came on 21 May, when WT001 landed at RAF Lossiemouth for the first time, flown by a mixed Boeing UK and Royal Air Force crew. The station has spent a long time preparing for it. Group Captain Sarah Brewin, the station commander at Lossiemouth, said at the time: “We have been working hard to get ready to operate these aircraft.” Stu Voboril, Boeing’s vice president and programme manager for the E-7, said: “We look forward to continuing test and evaluation as the aircraft moves closer to entry into service.” That test and evaluation phase is split between Boscombe Down and Lossiemouth, which explains Thursday’s pattern of one aircraft working out of each. Boeing UK hands the aircraft over to the Royal Air Force once the phase is complete, at which point 8 Squadron takes them on. The post Two of Britain’s new E-7 aircraft airborne first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: German lawmakers approve funds for eight-ship fleet of sub-hunting frigates
body: VIENNA — German lawmakers on Thursday approved the acquisition of four additional MEKO A-200 DEU frigates from shipbuilder TKMS, bringing Berlin’s planned fleet to eight ships after the government abandoned its troubled F126 program. The Bundestag budget committee had approved the first four vessels July 8, alongside an option for four more. The Defense Ministry said the decision to exercise that option will give the German Navy a single, eight-ship class intended chiefly for anti-submarine warfare. Delivery of the first vessel is set for 2029, the agency said in a statement. The ships will support NATO missions in the Baltic and North seas, the Atlantic and the High North, according to the announcement. Berlin selected the MEKO design after withdrawing from its contract with Damen Naval for six F126 frigates, which had initially been intended to supply the Navy’s future anti-submarine warfare capability. The ministry attributed its withdrawal to “considerable performance problems” by Damen, saying it had completed a broader assessment before terminating the arrangement. The program change has already triggered a costly dispute. Damen is seeking €4.7 billion ($5.3 billion) in damages from the German government, arguing that Berlin’s termination was politically motivated and legally unfounded, Der Spiegel reported last week. The F126 effort had already cost Germany more than €2 billion without delivering a ship, according to public broadcaster ARD . The initial four-ship MEKO purchase carried a reported €6.3 billion price tag, while the four-ship option was valued at €5.3 billion. Reuters reported that the second tranche, including project support and reserves, would cost roughly €5.6 billion; the projected operating costs for those four vessels through 2045 amount to another €1.55 billion. The Defense Ministry argued that selecting one ship type should simplify training, maintenance and logistics. It also said variants of the MEKO A-200 are already in service with allied navies. TKMS described the envisioned eight-ship production run as the company’s largest-ever surface vessel contract. “With the four frigates already on order, the program has entered the implementation phase,” the shipbuilder said in a statement. As part of its post-2022 buildup, the German military has put a heavy emphasis on anti-submarine warfare abilities in the Baltic, North Sea and, especially since the crisis over Greenland, in the Arctic. The F-126 was meant to be an integral part of this strategy. Other, more successful, procurements aimed at combating submarines include the Boeing P-8A Poseidon maritime-surveillance aircraft, the first of which landed in Germany almost exactly a year ago.

title: UPS missed warning email before F-35 stealth parts ended up in China
body: A missed warning about US arms export restrictions allowed components from an Australian F-35 stealth fighter to pass through Hong Kong and end up in Chinese hands, raising fresh questions about oversight of the aircraft’s international supply chain. The incident involved a cockpit canopy and a weapons-bay door, both coated with radar-absorbing material, that were being returned to the United States for possible repair or disposal in late May 2026. According to a Bloomberg investigation published on October 7, 2026, a UPS employee failed to act on an email from freight forwarder DSV warning that the shipment was subject to US International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). The message may have reached a different IT system from the one used by the employee responsible for the consignment. The components were supposed to travel from Australia to San Francisco through South Korea and Taiwan. When the shipment fell behind schedule, UPS changed the route to include Hong Kong, where Chinese authorities subsequently took possession of the parts. Pentagon investigates F-35 shipping failure The diversion, first made public by Politico in September 2026, has prompted investigations by the Pentagon and US State Department, as well as calls from lawmakers to examine the global logistics network supporting US military equipment. Pentagon officials briefed staff of the House Foreign Affairs and Armed Services committees on September 29, 2026, according to Bloomberg. The Pentagon has characterized the components as unserviceable, while the F-35 Joint Program Office said it was working with US authorities and industry partners to recover them and prevent a recurrence. Lockheed Martin, the aircraft’s manufacturer and the principal contractor responsible for its global spare parts network, said it was cooperating with logistics partners to improve oversight. “While we cannot discuss the details of which logistics partner was involved, we are working closely with them to help develop and implement preventive measures to strengthen our collective oversight and prevent recurrence,” the company said. After Bloomberg presented its findings about the missed email, Lockheed said it had “nothing to add or correct regarding the series of events you mentioned.” US auditors had already flagged supply-chain oversight gaps The shipping failure comes against a background of longstanding concerns over accountability for spare parts within the F-35 program. In a June 2026 report , the GAO found that the US Department of Defense still could not fully account for components moving through the fighter’s supply chain. The watchdog reported gaps in inventory records, including incomplete information about the number and location of spare parts. It also cited findings that contractor procedures allowed government-owned property to be distributed before authorization, and sometimes without it. The problems predate the Hong Kong incident. In May 2023 , the GAO found that one F-35 prime contractor had recorded losses involving more than one million spare parts, valued at over $85 million, since May 2018. The F-35 Joint Program Office had reviewed fewer than 2% of those losses. The same investigation found more than 19,000 spare parts awaiting disposal instructions, some for as long as five years. The GAO recommended stronger procedures for tracking losses and handling components classified as excess, obsolete or unserviceable. As of September 2026, the recommendations remained open, with the Pentagon still working to address the identified deficiencies. Australia maintains diverted F-35 parts were not sensitive A Royal Australian Air Force F-35A Lightning II from No. 75 Squadron taxis at RAAF Base Tindal. (Credit: U.S. Air Force photo) The incident has also raised concerns about possible exposure of the F-35’s low-observable technology. Although the components were no longer serviceable, their radar-absorbing coatings could potentially provide information about the aircraft’s stealth characteristics. Australia, which operates 72 F-35A fighters, has been assisting US authorities with the investigation since the diversion became public. Speaking at RAAF Base Edinburgh on September 22, 2026, Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles said Canberra was examining its handling of the shipment but emphasized that responsibility for the wider investigation rested with the United States and Lockheed Martin. Marles said there was “a sense of comfort” because “we’re not talking about sensitive equipment here, or sensitive parts.” He reiterated that assessment when questioned further, although he deferred to the United States and Lockheed Martin for a definitive characterization of the components. A day later, Australian Minister for Defence Industry Pat Conroy was asked whether espionage could have played a role in the diversion. “I’m not going to comment on the specifics of this as there are ongoing investigations through the F-35 supply chain, principally through America,” Conroy said. The post UPS missed warning email before F-35 stealth parts ended up in China appeared first on AeroTime .

title: German Spy Scandal Puts Central Asian and Caucasus Espionage Cases in Focus
body: The arrest of former German intelligence chief August Hanning has drawn attention to Azerbaijan. German journalists reported that he allegedly had contacts with Azerbaijan’s intelligence service. Baku rejected the allegations, while German prosecutors have not confirmed any Azerbaijani involvement. In recent years, citizens of Central Asia and the South Caucasus have repeatedly been implicated in espionage and treason cases. The accused and suspects include former intelligence chiefs, military personnel, officials, scientists, and foreign nationals. Some have received lengthy prison sentences, while others remain under investigation. In many cases, information about alleged foreign intelligence connections is limited to media reports. German Scandal and Ties to Baku On October 6, 2026, the German authorities detained 80-year-old August Hanning, who headed the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from 1998 to 2005. Former BND employee Manfred D. was also taken into custody. Hanning is suspected of attempted treason, obtaining state secrets, and acting on behalf of a foreign intelligence service. Manfred D. is suspected of assisting in the alleged offenses. Both were placed in pretrial detention on October 7. According to federal prosecutors, in the spring of 2010, Hanning reached an agreement with his former subordinate to obtain intelligence documents in exchange for money. By June 2022, Manfred D. had allegedly provided him with approximately 2,000 documents, including classified materials. By then, Hanning was working as a private consultant and, investigators believe, used the information for commercial purposes. According to German media reports , the documents included materials on Iran’s nuclear program, Russia’s armed forces, and information received from partner intelligence agencies. Investigators also allege that Hanning prepared an analytical memorandum for an officer of a foreign intelligence service. It remains unknown whether the intended recipient received it. Der Spiegel reported alleged contacts between Hanning and a representative of Azerbaijani intelligence. The investigative outlet CORRECTIV examined his longstanding ties to Baku, including his participation in the German-Azerbaijani Forum. German prosecutors have not identified the foreign intelligence service involved in the investigation. Azerbaijan rejected reports of its involvement and warned of damage to relations with Berlin. An Azerbaijani official also claimed that German intelligence representatives had assured Baku that the investigation was unrelated to Azerbaijan, although this has not been publicly confirmed by the German authorities. The classified documents were discovered during a separate investigation. In September 2025, police searched Hanning’s premises in connection with the alleged abduction of the children of German businesswoman Christina Block from Denmark. The discovery led to a separate criminal investigation opened in May 2026. Hanning’s lawyer acknowledged that his client possessed confidential documents, but rejected allegations he had passed on information to Germany’s detriment or received payment for doing so. Kazakhstan’s Espionage and State Secrets Cases In Kazakhstan, one of the best-known treason cases of recent times involved the prosecution of China expert Konstantin Syroyezhkin, who worked for many years at the Kazakhstan Institute for Strategic Studies under the president. Syroyezhkin was detained in February 2019 and sentenced to ten years in prison in October. The trial was held behind closed doors. Media reports alleged he had passed information to China, but the National Security Committee (KNB) did not publicly identify a foreign state or intelligence service. Syroyezhkin was released on parole in April 2024 and received a presidential pardon that September, lifting the restrictions associated with his parole. In 2022, the KNB announced verdicts in three other cases. Marat Shaikhutdinov, a former first deputy secretary of the Security Council, received seven years for unlawfully collecting and disclosing state secrets; Leonid Skakovsky was sentenced to eleven years and three months for treason, while Oleg Zhdan received eleven years for espionage. The details remain classified. In the summer of 2026, Uzbek citizen Ikboljon Koraboyev, a professor of international relations at Maqsut Narikbayev University, was detained in Astana, suspected of espionage under Article 176 of Kazakhstan’s Criminal Code. The article concerns the collection or transfer of classified information to a foreign state or intelligence service. Koraboyev’s relatives told the BBC ‘s Uzbek service that investigators had accused him of passing information to an employee of Uzbekistan’s consulate. The KNB has not publicly confirmed the allegation or disclosed details of the investigation, although it said Uzbekistan had been officially notified of his detention. Kazakh citizens have also figured in investigations abroad. In April 2026, Kazakh citizen Sergei K. was detained in Berlin. German prosecutors suspect him of cooperating with Russian intelligence. According to investigators, beginning in May 2025, he collected information about military assistance to Ukraine, German defense industry companies, and developers of drones and robotics. He is also accused of photographing military convoys, identifying potential sabotage targets, and attempting to recruit new participants. Kazakhstan’s Foreign Ministry confirmed his detention. Uzbekistan: Trials of Former Military Officers and Experts In 2019–2020, Uzbekistan held a series of closed trials on treason charges. The defendants included former employees of defense agencies and state research institutions. Media outlets linked some cases to alleged work for Russia. In May 2020, Rafik Saifulin, former director of the Institute for Strategic and Interregional Studies under the president of Uzbekistan, was sentenced to twelve years in prison. According to RFE/RL sources , prosecutors alleged that he had passed state secrets to Russia. Saifulin partially admitted his guilt, but maintained that the materials involved were analytical reports rather than classified documents. In July of the same year, Akbar Yarbabayev, former head of a department of the Armed Forces’ Joint Staff, received eleven years and six months for treason. His wife, Elena, was also convicted and given a six-year suspended sentence, with a three-year probationary period. Media reports alleged that the couple had cooperated with Russian intelligence, but the authorities did not identify a foreign intelligence client. Iranian Intelligence: From Israel to the Caspian In June 2026, Israeli intelligence agencies detained Behruz Sobirgon , a Tajikistan-born Russian passport holder whom Israeli reports also described as a Tajik citizen. He was suspected of working for Iran. According to the Israeli police, he had been in contact with an Iranian handler since January, photographed the port of Haifa, collected information about locations where Iranian missiles had struck, and attempted to recruit others to carry out assignments. In early July, prosecutors announced plans to indict him and sought to keep him in detention pending legal proceedings. In Azerbaijan, alleged Iranian intelligence activities have been the subject of several criminal proceedings. In 2024, Zahir Askerov, a former captain in the Caspian Sea Oil Fleet, was sentenced to 16 years for treason. According to Azerbaijan’s State Security Service, he was recruited while studying religion in the Iranian city of Qom. Investigators alleged that Askerov passed on information about naval exercises, foreign companies, and cargo destined for oil platforms. In January 2025, an appeals court upheld the verdict. In November 2022, Azerbaijani intelligence agencies announced the detention of five citizens suspected of collecting information for Iran about the military, purchases of Turkish and Israeli drones, and energy infrastructure. Interest in such facilities can be explained by Azerbaijan’s military cooperation with Israel and Turkey, as well as the importance of Caspian oil and gas infrastructure. Azerbaijan borders Iran, and relations between the two countries have repeatedly deteriorated over security issues. The Ryan Case and Relations with France In December 2023, Azerbaijan arrested French businessman Martin Ryan on suspicion of spying for France’s foreign intelligence service, the DGSE. He was sentenced to ten years in prison in March 2026, despite denying that he had knowingly engaged in espionage. France rejected the charges and condemned Ryan’s detention as arbitrary. Paris linked Azerbaijan’s treatment of French nationals to deteriorating relations between the countries following Baku’s military takeover of Nagorno-Karabakh in September 2023 and France’s support for Armenia. Ryan was pardoned and released in September 2026, a day after the EU removed Uzbek-born Russian billionaire Alisher Usmanov from its sanctions list following pressure from France. Three European diplomats told Reuters that Paris believed Azerbaijan had used the detention to press for the sanctions to be lifted, an allegation Baku denied. In espionage cases, publicity itself can become an instrument of state policy. Some investigations receive extensive coverage, accompanied by statements from intelligence agencies and diplomatic protests. Others take place behind closed doors, without journalists having access to evidence or even the identity of the country allegedly receiving classified information. As a result, the public often learns much more about the sentence than about the crime itself.

title: Dragon Capital slashes outlook, sees Ukraine GDP dropping 0.5% in 2026, 1.0% in 2027
body:
The intensification of Russian attacks since July 2026 has inflicted significant damage on Ukraine's economy, prompting leading Ukrainian investment company Dragon Capital to substantially downgrade its macroeconomic forecast: it now expects real gross domestic product (GDP) to decline by 0.5% this year and by 1.0% next year, whereas before the escalation it had forecast possible growth of 1.5% this year and 0.5% next year.
"These estimates are based on the assumption that Ukrainian air defenses will eventually be able to counter jet-powered drones more effectively, but the shortage of interceptors for ballistic missiles will remain a significant problem," the company said in a press release published Thursday.
Dragon Capital recalled that, taking into account the initial consequences of the escalation, it cut its forecast for real GDP growth in 2026 by 0.5 percentage points (p.p.) in early August, to 1.0%, but the latest developments, in particular the expansion of the range of targets attacked by the enemy, indicate that the negative impact on the economy will be more substantial.
A significant part of Ukraine's territory where major industrial assets, including metallurgical enterprises, are concentrated is within the range of ballistic missiles, it said. Although damaged production assets can likely be repaired, the threat of repeated strikes will prevent steelmakers from resuming full-scale operations.
"We believe that grain exports by sea may resume next year as a result of a diplomatic agreement similar to the 'grain corridor' that operated in 2022-2023. However, reaching an agreement covering a broader range of facilities, including the widely discussed 'energy truce,' appears unlikely," the press release said.
According to Dragon Capital, a blockade of Black Sea ports could reduce real GDP by 2.2%, provided that agricultural exports are partially redirected to alternative routes, particularly to Danube ports. If grain exports by sea are unblocked before the start of the spring sowing campaign, these losses could be reduced by 1.5 p.p., to 0.7%.
However, another 1.5% of GDP will be lost due to the shutdown of steel production and, consequently, a reduction in iron ore mining, since it is impossible to redirect these shipments to export under conditions in which the seaports are blocked, the release said.
As reported, the World Bank recently downgraded its forecast for Ukraine's economic growth in 2027 from 4% to 1.5%, while maintaining its estimate for growth this year at 1.2%.
At the end of September, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) downgraded its forecast for Ukraine's GDP growth in 2026 to 1.5% and in 2027 to 2.5%.
Economy and Environment Minister Oleksandr Kravchenko said at the end of September that he was allowing for a downward revision of the 2027 GDP growth forecast by 0.3-0.5 p.p. from the already incorporated pessimistic scenario (from 1.3% to 0.8-1%) and for 2026 to 0.5%, compared with the current forecast of 1.6%.
The National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) lowered its estimate for real GDP growth this year to 1.1-1.2%, compared with its estimate of 1.8% at the end of July this year.

title: Open an office in Ukraine, officer tells defence firms
body: Companies that want their equipment used by Ukrainian units should put staff and an office inside the country and begin by asking soldiers what the problem is, the chief unmanned systems officer of the 2nd Corps of Ukraine’s National Guard told the Apex Europe conference in London on Wednesday. Oleksii Krymeniuk, whose corps is known as Khartiia and numbers up to 35,000 personnel across formations ranging from infantry to uncrewed systems units, was asked how feedback from operators reaches developers and what makes the cycle work. His answer put the burden squarely on the supplier instead of on the units doing the fighting. “The main actor in this kind of feedback loop and in this kind of conversation between the unit and the industry is the industry, because this unit is constantly fighting, and unfortunately we don’t have enough time and enough resources to communicate and to ping pong and to talk to this industry,” he said. Turning up a couple of times a year for a demonstration does not count, in his view. “They should hire the guys in Ukraine, have a Ukrainian office, and they should constantly communicate about the challenges that that unit can encounter, because some challenges that you think are challenges in Ukraine, they are not challenges, and some challenges you even didn’t hear,” he said. He was candid about the companies that arrive with a solution already decided. “I’ve seen some companies that came to us, they propose some solutions to some problems, but for us it’s not a problem. They just want to sell us something, and they want to get this kind of approved by Ukrainian unit sign, and then it would be much easier for them to sell their products in the international market,” he said. The example he reached for was the first-person-view drone, the product most often carried into Ukraine by visiting firms. “I’ve seen a number of companies that came to us trying to sell us FPV drones, but we have an enormous number of companies inside of Ukraine that already sell us these drones, and they’re much cheaper than the drones that we can get from international markets,” he said. Companies willing to work that way should expect frank conversations and not take them personally. “Some of these words, they couldn’t be very polite, because sometimes it could be very rough and straightforward as any military. But it’s not that we don’t want to help you,” he said, explaining that there is simply not time for a longer version of the conversation. His own corps has met industry halfway by standing up a small team whose only job is talking to companies and sorting what is relevant from what is not, since the number of firms now approaching units has become very large. “So it’s a two-way situation,” he said. Asked what advice he would give a national armaments director, he returned to where equipment gets proved. “First of all, you should buy some stuff that is tested in Ukraine and fully combat tested. Not the guys who came to a very safe zone, made a couple of flights there, and say okay, it’s completely tested in Ukraine. I think it should be truly tested on the front line,” he said. His second point was about what a buyer should be planning for. “I think there is still a belief in the decisive battle as a concept, that we can buy very expensive stuff and it will be one battle and you will win,” he said. “But from the experience of Ukraine, and from history, each war is a war of attrition, and if you can achieve mass production, mass usage of it on the ground, you’ll be successful.” Several of the companies on the panel described doing precisely what he asked for. Helsing has around fifty people in an office in Ukraine, Ark Robotics has seventy per cent of its workforce in the country with teams embedded in frontline units, and Havoc also keeps people there. The post Open an office in Ukraine, officer tells defence firms first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Zelenskyy announces important negotiations with partners in near future
body:
Important negotiations with partners are scheduled for Thursday and Friday, which could yield concrete results to strengthen Ukraine's defense, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy has reported.
"Today and tomorrow there will be important negotiations with partners. We count on them to yield a concrete result to strengthen our defense," Zelenskyy wrote on his Telegram channel on Thursday.
In addition, he noted that the search and rescue operation following the Russian missile strike on a residential building in Pryluky, Chernihiv region, has concluded. As a result, 22 people were killed, including five children, and another 54 people were injured, including seven children.
The Russians also struck a bus stop in Kramatorsk, with 12 fatalities reported. Another two people were killed in Kyiv.
"Four more people were wounded, two of them children. In Odesa region, an animal shelter was damaged by a Russian drone attack. Energy infrastructure was under attack once again. In total, Russian shelling caused damage in 10 regions," Zelenskyy added.
He thanked partners who did not remain silent about Russian crimes, while emphasizing the importance of support taking concrete forms in new defense packages.
"Deliveries of anti-ballistic systems, ammunition for our combat aviation, investments in interceptors—all of this actually works to save lives every day," the president stressed.

title: Death toll from Russian strike on two buses in Kramatorsk rises to 33, 18 injured
body:
The Donetsk Regional Prosecutor's Office reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
"As of now [12:36 Kyiv time], the number of people killed in the morning attack on passenger buses has risen to 30. Eighteen people were injured," the prosecutor's office said in an updated statement.
Ukraine's State Emergency Service later reported that 33 people had been killed and another 18 injured in the Russian strike.
The strike sparked fires in two passenger buses and in an open area.
Rescuers provided assistance to the injured and extinguished the fires.
Three people were killed in the village of Bilenke, part of the Kramatorsk urban community, as a result of the strike. Rescuers recovered one of the victims from the rubble of a private house.
At around 10:00 on October 8, Russian forces struck Kramatorsk with a UMPB D-30 SN guided bomb. The munition hit a street where two passenger buses were traveling at the time. At that point, 12 people had been reported killed and 14 injured.

title: Hisbah arrests 6 women in alleged anti-prostitution operation in Yobe
body: By Maryam Abdul-Aziz Usman, Damaturu The Yobe State Hisbah Commission has arrested six women suspected of engaging in sex work during an operation in Gadaka, Fika Local Government Area of the state. The women were arrested in the Abuja area of Gadaka town during a weekend operation conducted by operatives of the commission’s Fika Local Government Area command. The operation also targeted locations suspected of selling and processing alcoholic drinks, according to the commission. Head of Administration of the commission in Fika LGA, Malam Musa Abari Talba, who confirmed the arrests, said the operation was part of efforts to check activities considered contrary to the religious and moral values of the community. Talba said the operatives also embarked on awareness campaigns during the exercise, warning residents against activities they described as harmful to the peace and moral conduct of the society. He said: “The operation was carried out by our men at the weekend in the Abuja area of Gadaka. Six women suspected of engaging in sex work were arrested.” According to him, the operatives also visited locations suspected of selling and processing alcoholic drinks, where residents were cautioned against activities prohibited by law. He added that the commission used the opportunity to preach to residents and encourage them to comply with the law and shun practices considered detrimental to the community. Talba said the exercise was not limited to arrests, stressing that the commission’s broader objective was to promote peace, discipline and good moral conduct among residents. He further disclosed that similar operations would continue across the local government as part of efforts to ensure compliance with the law and promote peaceful and orderly communities. The post Hisbah arrests 6 women in alleged anti-prostitution operation in Yobe appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Flydubai co-pilot planned attack on Israel months before attempted hijacking, investigation reveals
body: Hamam al-Hammami, the Omani national flydubai co-pilot who recently attempted to hijack a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, had initially planned to carry out his attack in July, The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing people briefed on the investigation into the incident.According to the WSJ, Hammami told investigators that he had sought to crash a plane into an Israeli target, such as Ben-Gurion Airport, due to the situation in Gaza during the Israel-Hamas War.He had been prepared to hijack a plane in July, sources said, with some adding that he had held back because he cared about one of the flight's crew members.Hammami hired by flydubai in post-COVID recruitment pushAccording to a previous WSJ report on Tuesday, Hammami was hired by the airline during a push by the United Arab Emirates-based carrier to expand its pilot staff.The report came after it was alleged that Hammami had previously been banned from flying by Omani authorities over concerns regarding his radical ideological views and that flydubai may have hired him in February without conducting thorough background checks.According to the WSJ, the airline's recruitment spree began after the COVID-19 pandemic, as the carrier worked to expand its model of providing low-cost, high-volume flights amid an industry-wide shortage of pilots.Goldie Katz contributed to this report.

title: Google wounded the internet, AI companies are treating the injury with mercury
body:
Finding something in an information mess is not a new problem, archivists have been working on it for hundreds of years. While their work focus mostly on phisical archives the underlying problem and challenge is fundamentally the same on the digital world. Google's original mission was to "organize the world’s information and make it universally accessible and useful". Almost 30 years later, that problem is still there.
To tackle this challenge, Google built a service consisting of indexing everything it can put its hands on and provide internet's users a single entry point for it. The idea was good as it somewhow solves the issue: I have questions, there is a shit amount of information out there that I cannot possible process so I enter my query in a text box and get results of things that can satisfy it. The problem with narrowing the Internet to a single entry point is all the side-effects of it:
The list go on but the situation is this: the solution that Google envisioned led to a natural enshittification .
Going into the year 2027 the problem got out of hands. Search engines (and the web itself) got so enshittified that trying to find something useful is no longer possible. Let's recap what a modern experience of browsing the web looks like:
With the quality of Search Engines nowadays it is more than clear that users are going to pivot to whatever promises a better experience. We poison the internet so much that people are begging for a new experience to deal with it. And yes, here it comes AI companies with their radioactive quackery (did you know that radioactive thootpaste was a thing?) trying to sell us yet another magic text box. This one comes with a new flavor: to digest all the shit in the internet for you so you don't need to manually browse it. I sometimes find myself asking to the AI because I cannot longer tollerate yet another web search. The main problem however is that AI depends on searching! Underneath, what AI does is search the internet, read every page and summarize all the findings. If what they find while searching the internet is the garbage content we have released for engagement with search engines, the AI is going go that extra mile of effort to serve you a beautiful plate of shit.
So what's the solution you would say? No idea yet. But here are some good starting points to keep in mind:
The good thing is that the problem didn't change in nature (just in scale) it is still a problem of organizing a lot of information and, now more than ever, determine what has long-term value that it is worth keeping. I guess archivists are going to be more needed than ever.

title: Russian plague scare: Everything we know as health chief calls for information
body: The World Health Organisation has demanded more information following the death of a laboratory worker at a Russian plague research laboratory. Danya Shipilova, 28, a laboratory worker at the Irkutsk Research Anti-Plague Institute in Shelekhov, Siberia, died on October 2 after developing pneumonia of undetermined cause. Russia has placed more than 200 people in quarantine after the incident. The circumstances surrounding her illness, and the nature of the research conducted at the institute, have raised international concern about the potential threat of a plague outbreak. However, Russian authorities have denied reports of a confirmed case of pneumonic plague in the region. The World Health Organisation has asked Moscow to provide more details about the incident, including laboratory test results for Ms Shipilova and those placed in quarantine. At a media briefing on Wednesday, WHO director general Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said Russian authorities had held a meeting on October 2 after a resident of Irkutsk Oblast in Eastern Siberia was suspected of having contracted a dangerous infection. “WHO has asked the Russian Federation for more information in accordance with the International Health Regulations,” Dr Tedros said. “The Russian Federation responded, saying that no case of plague had recently been reported in the Irkutsk Oblast and that they had placed about 200 contacts in quarantine.” The WHO has requested additional information about laboratory testing, the reasons for the public health measures and the health status of those who were quarantined. It has also asked Russia to clarify media reports about a second employee who allegedly developed pneumonia of undetermined cause. Dr Tedros said the WHO had offered technical support on plague and laboratory biosafety and biosecurity but had not been able to conduct a full risk assessment or establish a complete picture of what had happened. “Timely, complete and transparent information sharing under the International Health Regulations is essential to clarify conflicting reports and enable an accurate assessment of potential public health risks,” he said. The US and the EU have also urged Russia to be transparent about the incident. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov had rejected media reports about the suspected plague case. Risk to public The US Centres for Disease Control and Prevention said it was monitoring developments. “We are working across the US government to assess developments as additional information becomes available,” the CDC said. “While the circumstances of this reported case remain unconfirmed, plague is a serious bacterial disease that is treatable with antibiotics, particularly when recognised and treated early. “At this time, there is no indication of a broader threat to the US,” the CDC said. The CDC added that pneumonic plague can spread through respiratory droplets during close contact. Rapid identification and treatment of infected people, together with monitoring of potentially exposed individuals, are important public-health measures. What is pneumonic plague? Pneumonic plague is a severe lung infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. It is the most serious form of plague. How does it spread? Close contact: Pneumonic plague can spread when an infected person coughs or sneezes and someone else inhales the respiratory droplets. Infected animals: Rarely, people can be exposed to respiratory droplets from animals with pneumonic plague, including domestic cats. Secondary infection: Bubonic or septicaemic plague can progress to pneumonic plague if the bacteria reach the lungs. What are the symptoms? Symptoms usually appear quickly, within three days of exposure, but sometimes as long as a week after contact. They include sudden fever, chills, headaches, weakness and shortness of breath, similar to some seasonal illnesses such as influenza. These symptoms can be followed by rapidly worsening pneumonia and chest pain with coughing that frequently produces bloody or watery mucus. Is there a treatment? Yes. Plague can be treated with antibiotics, particularly when treatment begins promptly. Because pneumonic plague can progress quickly and can be fatal without treatment, suspected cases require urgent medical assessment, isolation and appropriate antibiotic dosage. Antibiotics used to treat plague can include gentamicin, doxycycline, ciprofloxacin and moxifloxacin, depending on the clinical circumstances and medical guidance. Recent plague cases Arizona, US, July 2025: A man died from pneumonic plague a week after exposure to sick cats. Despite receiving antibiotics and oxygen, the man died within eight hours of his admission to hospital. Global endemic areas: The bacterium Yersinia pestis is active in wild rodent populations in about 26 countries. Seasonal cases are reported most frequently in Madagascar, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Peru. There are about seven cases a year in the US, mainly in the western part of the country.

title: Herzog to award heroism medal to six Israelis who helped foil flydubai hijacking
body: President Isaac Herzog awarded six Israeli civilians who helped prevent the recent attempted flydubai hijacking the Presidential Award for Civilian Heroism.The President's Office presented the award to Tali Manes, Zvika Manes, Yaniv Hayoun, Dr. Shota Musayev, Asaf Rajuan, and Or Pardilov during a ceremony at the President's Residence in Jerusalem for their role in preventing the would-be hijacker from crashing the plane.Herzog initially announced earlier this month that he would recommend four Israelis for the award: Yaniv Hayoun, Dr. Shota Musayev, Zvika Manes, and Asaf Rajuan. Later, he also said he would add Tali Manes, Zvika's wife, to the list.“Tali, Yaniv, Tzvika, Or, Assaf, Dr. Shota, the Medal for Civilian Bravery being awarded to you here today symbolizes more than the fact that you saved lives,” Herzog said in his remarks.“The civilian bravery and resourcefulness demonstrated by the heroes present here cannot overshadow the obligation to obtain full answers. Everyone, all of us, deserves clear and satisfactory answers,” he added.“The Medal for Civilian Bravery is being awarded to you also because, in the moment of truth, you revealed something much deeper: You revealed the face of the Israeli spirit. A spirit of courage. A spirit of extraordinary resourcefulness. A spirit that says: When there is danger, we act.”He went on to praise the heroes of flight 1073 for their “simple, human, and profoundly Israeli act: At the moment when a choice had to be made – you chose life. For all of this, I award you today the President's Medal for Civilian Bravery.”The medal was specially created by Sari Srulovitch, a Jerusalem silversmith and designer.In parallel, Herzog awarded the Presidential Medal of Honor to Israel Bonds for its role in contributing to Israel's global economic standing.Herzog awards Israel Bonds Presidential Medal of Honor“For 75 years, Israel Bonds has served as a vital bridge between the State of Israel and supporters, financial institutions, and investors around the world,” the president said.“From the earliest days of our statehood, investors across the globe have placed their trust and their resources in Israel's economy and development. Since October 7, 2023, their extraordinary support has been a powerful expression of solidarity and of confidence in the strength and resilience of our people and our economy. The State of Israel owes you profound gratitude.”Presidential Medal for Civilian Heroism established after October 7Herzog established the civilian heroism award following the October 7 massacre, after numerous accounts emerged of civilians risking their lives to rescue others during the Hamas-led attack and the war that followed. It honors civilians who displayed extraordinary courage while placing their lives in genuine danger to save others.The award, described as Israel's highest civilian valor honor, is conferred after the president's advisory committee examines candidates and makes a recommendation.
