Its tuition-free model, she stated, was intended to remove the cost of professional training as a barrier for early-career professionals, while providing them with practical skills, professional judgement and confidence. “The academy is also building a growing community of participants and alumni that could serve as an emerging talent pipeline for the communications industry across Africa and beyond,” the founder stated, adding that it would continue to expand the programme, improve its curriculum and make quality professional development more accessible to young communications professionals.

title: MK Ofer Cassif indicted for assaulting police officer during South Hebron Hills protest
body: The Jerusalem Magistrate's Court convicted MK Ofer Cassif of assaulting a police officer during a protest in the South Hebron Hills more than four years ago.The conviction, handed down on Thursday by Judge Bialin Elazar, was for assaulting a police officer under aggravated circumstances, an offense punishable by between three months and five years in prison. The offense applies when an assault is connected to an officer's lawful duties and is intended to obstruct, prevent or interfere with their work.Sentencing arguments are scheduled for January 13 next year.Responding to the conviction in a post on X/Twitter, Cassif wrote: “I will continue my struggle, together with my friends, against all the crimes of the occupation: genocide, ethnic cleansing, and fascism within Israel. I promise you that we will emerge stronger from the election and send the Kahanists and all the criminals where they belong.”The incident took place on May 13, 2022, in Masafer Yatta, a cluster of Palestinian communities in the South Hebron Hills at the center of a decades-long dispute over evictions from an area designated as an IDF firing zone. The communities' struggle against demolition and displacement was documented in No Other Land, the Israeli-Palestinian film that won the 2025 Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature.According to the indictment, protests were held in the South Hebron Hills on that day in 2022, following a Supreme Court ruling concerning villages in Masafer Yatta. Orders were issued declaring the area around the Route 317 junction and dirt roads leading to the villages a closed military zone.Cassif arrived by car to join the protesters, after about 80 had arrived at around 11 a.m. and eventually set up camp on one of the dirt roads leading to Masafer Yatta. Because Cassif had parliamentary immunity, security officers allowed him to move freely between the designated and approved protest area and the area outside it.However, security personnel stopped his vehicle on a dirt road and prevented him from driving into the protest area, citing safety concerns and the prohibition on Israelis entering Area A. He was permitted to continue on foot.According to the indictment, Cassif later returned to the car to drive it, leading to a heated argument with Border Police Ch.-Insp. Dor Amitai and police officer Yitzhak Azulay.Cassif called Border Police officers 'scum of the human race,' court saysAccording to a court summary, Cassif called the officers “dirty liar,” “fraud,” “criminal,” and “scum of the human race.”Cassif then got into his car. With Azulay standing in front of the vehicle to block it, Cassif reversed several meters and then drove slowly forward until the front of the car struck Azulay's left leg. The court found that Cassif acted knowingly and intended to obstruct Azulay in the performance of his duties.Azulay struck the hood of the vehicle with his hand. When Cassif got out, the argument continued. At one point, Azulay raised his finger and lightly touched Cassif's face. In response, Cassif raised his right hand and forcefully struck the left side of Azulay's head, causing him pain in his head and leg.Cassif denied the charge and argued that his parliamentary immunity entitled him to drive through the area. He claimed that striking the officer with his vehicle had been accidental and that hitting him with his hand was an instinctive act of self-defense. He also raised a preliminary claim of selective enforcement.The court rejected the defense arguments, ruling that the security forces acted lawfully and within their authority to prevent danger to life and unauthorized entry into Area A.It found that Cassif's parliamentary immunity allowed him to move freely on foot within the protest area but did not give him the right to endanger people or obstruct police officers by driving.The court also found beyond a reasonable doubt that Cassif knowingly struck Azulay with his vehicle and intended to obstruct him. It ruled that striking the officer's head went well beyond self-defense and was grossly disproportionate to what the court described as accidental contact caused by Cassif's own movement. The court also rejected the selective-enforcement claim, finding a clear evidentiary distinction and no defect in the prosecution's conduct.

title: Dubai school plans scholarship in memory of teacher after 33 years of service
body: Gems Education plans to honour the life and legacy of Dubai teacher Anjana Sanalkumar with a scholarship in her memory, recognising her 33 years of service with the school group . Ms Sanalkumar, a teacher and examination officer at the Westminster School in Dubai, died on Wednesday. The cause of her death has not been disclosed. The school announced her death on social media and in a letter to the Gems community from group chief executive Dino Varkey. He paid tribute to Ms Sanalkumar's decades of teaching and the relationships she built with colleagues. “Her passing is a profound loss, particularly for her family, friends and the entire community at the Westminster School,” Mr Varkey wrote. Gems Education intends to establish the Anjana Sanalkumar Memorial Scholarship at the school. "We are currently finalising the details of the Anjana Sanalkumar Memorial Scholarship at The Westminster School, including its scope, eligibility criteria and selection process, and will share further information with our community in due course," Carl Roberts, executive principal, CEO and brand ambassador for Westminster Schools, told The National . The Westminster School invited former and current pupils, teachers and colleagues to pay tribute to Ms Sanalkumar. “As we come together to remember and celebrate the life of Ms Anjana, we invite everyone who knew and loved her to share a heartfelt message, memory, or a few words in her honour in the comments,” the school said in an Instagram post. A memorial service was live-streamed at 3pm on Thursday so those unable to attend in person can take part remotely. “Your words, memories, and presence – near or far – mean more than we can express. Thank you for helping us honour and celebrate a life that touched so many,” the school said. Hundreds of students, teachers and alumni have posted messages of remembrance on the school’s social media. Juliet Carolyn, a former biology teacher and department co-ordinator at school, stated that she had the privilege of knowing and working with Ms Sanalkumar for 11 years. “She was such a beautiful soul, kind, compassionate, and deeply empathetic. Hearing of her passing is truly heartbreaking. May the Almighty God comfort and console her family and loved ones during this difficult time of grief,” she wrote. Former student Ahmed Azab described Ms Sanalkumar as one of the teachers he was always happy to see. “Whenever we met her regarding school issues, she always met us with grace and compassion, helping us find a solution. Never did she make me feel judged or add to the stress I was in,” he wrote. Another former student, Faisal Mushtaq, said Ms Sanalkumar taught him computer science in the early 2000s. “Very helpful, caring and smiling. I was fortunate enough to meet her two years ago at the school alumni event,” he wrote, sending his condolences to her family and the school community.

title: Russian strike on buses kills 33, say officials, as deadly attacks on Ukraine surge
body: Thirty-three people have been killed in a Russian glide bomb attack on two civilian buses in the frontline city of Kramatorsk, rescue officials say. Another 18 people were wounded, said Donetsk regional head Vadym Filashkin, accusing Russia of targeting a bus carrying passengers to kill as many civilians as possible. Images posted by local prosecutors showed the burning metal shell of the bus along with debris and some of the victims on the road. Kramatorsk and neighbouring Slovyansk are part of a so-called fortress belt that Russia is trying to seize as part of Vladimir Putin’s claim to the entire Ukrainian industrial region of Donbas. However, Thursday’s attack follows a dramatic surge in Russian attacks across the country and a heavy increase in civilian casualties. Russia is now launching constant air raids against Ukraine, with sirens ringing throughout the day in the capital Kyiv. According to the UN, Ukraine saw more civilians killed by August this year than were killed in all of 2025. In one single attack that destroyed a five-storey block of flats in Pryluky east of Kyiv early on Wednesday, 22 people were killed, including five children. Three of the children were only one year old. Moscow is yet to comment on the latest attack, however rescue officials said the attack caused a fire on two buses that were both carrying passengers. Filashkin appealed to anyone who was still in the Donetsk region to move to safer regions of Ukraine. Given the sharp deterioration of security in the two neighbouring cities, he said all public transport had been ordered to stop. The safety of civilians was paramount, and “we have no right to risk the lives of passengers and drivers”, he said. Moscow has often cited the “liberation” and “protection” of the predominantly Russian-speaking Donbas as justification for the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. It is made up of two regions – Luhansk and Donetsk – and with most of Luhansk under Russian control, the Kremlin is also aiming to capture remaining 20% of Donetsk territory still held by Ukraine. Zelensky offered his condolences to families and loved ones affected by the latest attack and said Ukraine’s partners needed to provide “concrete action through new defence packages for the protection of Ukraine”. Ahead of the Pryluky attack, the Ukrainian leader had warned this week of warned of intelligence suggesting plans for a major Russian onslaught, and in Kyiv families responded by heading to metro stations for shelter. Such warnings are for now one of the best defences Ukrainians have. Interceptor missiles are in short supply around the world, so Ukraine has little chance to stop incoming Russian ballistics. Both Russia and Ukraine have intensified long-range strikes on each other in recent months, with Russian attacks targeting Ukrainian data centres and logistics warehouses. For much of the war Kramatorsk acted as a logistics and supply hub for the Ukrainian military, however it has now come under almost daily Russian attack as its military moves closer to the east of the city. Glide bombs in particular have been launched at Slovyansk and Kramatorsk. The bombs are fitted with winglets so they glide towards their target rather than simply fall. In late August as many as nine glide bombs were fired at Kramatorsk in one day. Kramatorsk City Council described the strike as a “horrific crime committed by the Russian army against the civilian population”. “Once again, the Russians have struck a location where there are absolutely no military targets.”

title: NAF helicopter makes precautionary landing in Makurdi after Benue operation
body:
A Nigerian Air Force helicopter made a precautionary landing in Makurdi, the Benue State capital, after completing a close air support operation against suspected kidnappers in Ogbadigbo Local Government Area.
The incident occurred on Wednesday, when the helicopter landed on farmland around Utur, Tse-Igboji area of Makurdi.
The Nigerian Air Force said the pilot made the precautionary landing while returning to base from the operation, about 10 nautical miles from the airfield.
According to the NAF, the decision was made as a professional precaution and in line with established operational and safety procedures following combat missions.
The Air Force said the operation disrupted the activities of suspected kidnappers and supported the advance of surface forces.
It said the helicopter has since returned safely to base.
The incident occurred two days after a Nigerian military aircraft crashed in Ondo State, amidst concerns over military aviation operations.
PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that 32 people were on board the military aircraft that crashed in Ondo State on Monday. The Aviation Minister, Festus Keyamo, said the aircraft had 25 passengers and seven crew members on board.
The Nigerian Air Force had said the aircraft was travelling from Benin to Lagos on a routine mission before it crashed close to the Naval Base in Igbokoda, Ondo State.
Mr Keyamo said search and rescue operations were ongoing following the crash.
Unlike the Ondo incident, the NAF said Wednesday’s helicopter landing in Makurdi was precautionary and that the aircraft subsequently returned to base.
The Air Force said it remained committed to supporting surface forces through coordinated air and ground operations against criminal elements.

title: ITF Marks 55 Years of Driving Skills, Industrial Growth
body: Yemi Kosoko in Jos The Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of the Industrial Training Fund (ITF), Dr. Afiz Oluwatoyin Ogun, has highlighted the institution’s achievements over the past three years, reaffirming its commitment to skills development and human capital advancement as the Fund marked its 55th anniversary in Jos. Speaking at the anniversary celebration, Ogun said the ITF had sustained its relevance since its establishment in 1971 by adapting to the changing needs of the Nigerian economy and workforce. He noted that under his administration, the Fund had expanded skills acquisition programmes, strengthened local and international partnerships, digitised key operations, improved staff welfare and upgraded training infrastructure across the country. The ITF boss identified the Skill-Up Artisans (SUPA) programme as one of the institution’s flagship interventions, designed to train, certify and professionalise artisans nationwide. He added that the Fund had also advanced Nigeria’s global skills competitiveness through strategic collaborations and the establishment of structures that align vocational training with international standards. In a goodwill message, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Oil and Gas Free Zones Authority (OGFZA), Alhaji Bamanga Usman Jada, described the ITF as one of Nigeria’s most strategic agencies, given its central role in developing the nation’s human capital. Jada commended the quality of facilities at the ITF Centre of Excellence in Jos, which he described as being of international standard, and praised the leadership of Dr. Afiz Oluwatoyin Ogun for the progress recorded by the organisation. He stressed that Nigeria’s future prosperity would depend more on the development of its human resources than on its natural endowments, adding that the ITF remained critical to converting the country’s growing population into a skilled and productive workforce. He further lauded the Federal Government’s efforts to create an enabling environment for investment and industrial growth, while urging continued support for skills development as a catalyst for economic transformation. The event brought together government officials, industry leaders, development partners, members of the organised private sector and ITF staff to celebrate the institution’s contributions to manpower development and industrial growth over the last 55 years. Stakeholders at the ceremony expressed confidence that the Fund would continue to play a pivotal role in enhancing workforce competitiveness and supporting Nigeria’s long-term economic development objectives.

title: Russia’s Yastreb-S EW system to be upgraded to counter Starlink — developer
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Russia’s newest electronic warfare (EW) system, the Yastreb-S, is being modernized to jam Starlink satellite communications used by Ukrainian drones, Igor Potapov, an official representative of its developer, NPP Design Bureau, told TASS.
"The Yastreb system itself is currently undergoing testing. The Yastreb-S version requires modernization to shift frequencies to the operating bands of Starlink systems for maximum suppression of all possible threats. The frequency shifter has already been made, and all that remains is to integrate it and begin testing," he said, calling the system the "Starlink killer."
He added that this will deprive enemy attack unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) of satellite communications.
Potapov said earlier that the Yastreb 1.0 system is undergoing final testing, and Russian troops will begin using it in November. According to the expert, the Yastreb 1.0 has no analogues in its class. The system covers a wide frequency band from 100 to 6,000 MHz. The system’s electronic intelligence capabilities include video interception with image transmission to the operator’s network.

title: South Korea recalls ambassador to Ukraine
body:
Amid growing tensions between Seoul and Kyiv, South Korea made the decision to recall its envoy to Ukraine. This is another result of the ongoing dispute regarding the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war between the countries.
Seoul announced the move in a press release on Thursday, after Foreign Minister Cho Hyun warned Kyiv of an upcoming firm reaction. „ The government has decided to recall its ambassador to Ukraine ,” reads the release. „The government hopes that all outstanding issues between the two countries will be resolved amicably and will continue consultations with the Ukrainian side towards this end.”
The recalled ambassador is Park Ki-chan, who has served as South Korea’s highest-ranking diplomat in Ukraine since February 2025. He is a specialist on Russia and has previously held diplomatic postings in Moscow, Warsaw and Belgrade.
The diplomatic dispute between the parties began on 23 September , when Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed during the general debate at the UN General Assembly session that two North Korean prisoners of war had been transferred to South Korea. The soldiers were captured by the Ukrainian military during fighting in Russia’s Kursk Oblast in 2025.
The matter was intended to be confidential, and President Lee Jae-myung accused Zelenskyy of breaching this secrecy. Ukrainian authorities denied the existence of a confidentiality clause. In response to Kyiv’s position, Seoul accused Ukraine of portraying President Lee as a „liar” and violating the dignity of the state. A public apology was demanded, which was delivered; however, as South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun stated, it failed to meet expectations. It was emphasised that the government in Seoul would take „firm action.”
South Korean news agency Yonhap assesses that the recall of the ambassador „represents the culmination of actions” related to this case. It adds that such a move „is recognised in international relations as one of the strongest forms of protest .”

title: Army takes over Old Oyo Park for military training in aftermath of school abduction
body:
The Nigerian Army has taken over the stretch of the Old Oyo National Park in Oyo State for military training, months after more than 46 pupils and teachers were abducted from schools in Oriire Local Government Area.
The move is aimed at denying kidnappers and other criminal groups access to the vast forest, which the military identified as one of the areas targeted during efforts to rescue the victims.
Punch reported that the army’s General Officer Commanding, 2 Division, discussed this on Wednesday when he received members of the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists, Oyo State Council, at the division’s headquarters in Ibadan, the Oyo State capital
Mr Mahmuda said the Chief of Army Staff, Waidi Shuaibu, directed the division to use the park as a training site after the victims of the Oriire abduction were rescued.
He said the military’s presence in the park would make it difficult for criminal groups to continue using the forest as a hideout.
“On the order of the Chief of Army Staff, Lt. General Waidi Shuaibu, the 2 Division has taken over the entire stretch of the Old Oyo National Park as a training site in order to prevent the repeat of the Oriire kidnap saga,” Mr Mahmuda said.
The development marks a shift from the Army’s earlier deployment around the park to a more sustained military presence in the area.
In September, Mr Mahmuda visited troop locations around the Old Oyo National Park and charged soldiers to remain vigilant and maintain an aggressive posture against security threats. The visit included the Igbeti–Igboho–Sepeteri road, the headquarters of the 169 Motorcycle Battalion at Ikoyi-Ile and the Abaja Response Area in Oriire.
The army’s latest decision follows the abduction of pupils and teachers from three schools in Ahoro-Esinele and Yawota communities in Oriire Local Government Area on 15 May.
Affected schools are Community High School and Community Grammar School, Ahoro-Esinle, and Yawota Baptist Nursery and Primary School. The abducted victims spent 56 days in captivity before they were rescued by security forces on 10 July.
The Army had said the rescue followed an intelligence-led operation targeting the kidnappers’ network and hideouts, including areas around the Old Oyo National Park.
Mr Mahmuda said converting the park into a military training ground would serve both operational and security purposes by keeping troops active in an area previously vulnerable to criminal activity.
He also appealed for closer cooperation between the military and the media, particularly in the verification of information relating to security operations.
“I will appeal to you to avoid publishing information without first confirming its exact and true nature with the military,” he said. “Sometimes, when unverified information is released, it can cause more harm than the information it intended to address.”
PREMIUM TIMES reported that the Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, in late September had received the report of the Judicial Commission of Inquiry into abduction drawn from the account of 72 witnesses including victims and experts.
Mr Makinde stated that the state will review the report and its recommendations to identify institutional or operational failures and implement measures to prevent a recurrence.

title: Russia has no plans for armed conflict with Western Europe — MFA
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Moscow has no plans for an armed conflict with Western Europe, and Russia poses no threat to anyone, Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said at a news briefing.
"If Germany’s top intelligence official publicly voices his own fantasies, it means that Europe is indeed in great danger. I will repeat this for the sake of clarity: Russia threatens no one. The Russian president and foreign minister have repeatedly stated that Moscow has no plans for an armed conflict with Western Europe," Zakharova said, commenting on remarks by the head of Germany’s foreign intelligence service.
"One could ask those who voice such things - or at least those who can explain what they mean - to clarify their position. How do they justify these fantasies of theirs? What do they cite as the goals, objectives, or reasons for the actions they fabricate and attribute to us?" she noted. "After all, there is a wealth of facts - often cited by the very people making these claims - indicating that it is they who are rapidly pursuing something akin to militarization - or, more accurately, a kind of militant frenzy. This involves not only expanding the military-industrial complex but also ideologically brainwashing their own populations to embrace Russophobia and the idea of 'inevitable conflict.' This is precisely what the Russian president has addressed in his repeated statements."
Zakharova pointed out that should such aggression originate from Western Europe or the EU, a response would follow. "As for the nature of that response, you need only re-read the president's relevant statement," she concluded.

title: Another Tragedy Averted as NAF Helicopter Makes Precautionary Landing in Benue
body: * Helicopter, crew members safely return to base, says NAF Linus Aleke in Abuja Barely 48 hours after the fatal crash involving a Nigerian Air Force (NAF) ATR-42 aircraft in Igbokoda, Ondo State, another NAF helicopter has made a precautionary landing in Benue State during an air interdiction operation in Ogbadigbo, a border town between Benue and Enugu States. The incident occurred barely 24 hours after the Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo (SAN), called for joint aviation safety measures to prevent frequent air mishaps involving military aircraft. The call became imperative following the military’s record of at least 10 air mishaps in the past decade, some of which resulted in tragic fatalities, including the death of the former Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lt Gen Ibrahim Attahiru, and other senior military officers aboard a Nigerian Air Force Beechcraft King Air 350i (NAF203) aircraft en route to Kaduna on May 21, 2021. The latest incident occurred at Utur Tse-Igboji, Bar Council Ward, along the Welfare Quarters–Mopol 13 Ring Road in Ogbadigbo Local Government Area of Benue State. According to eyewitnesses, the pilot made a precautionary landing, prompting residents to rush to the scene to assist the officers on board. All those on board reportedly survived and exited the helicopter safely. In a statement in response to reports of the incident, the Nigerian Air Force, through its Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, said the helicopter had successfully provided close air support to ground forces during an operation targeting suspected kidnappers in the Ogbadigbo area of Benue State, near the Enugu–Benue boundary. According to Ejodame, the operation disrupted the activities of the suspected criminal elements and supported the advance of ground forces. Responding to reports of the precautionary landing, he said: “Following the successful completion of the mission, the pilot, on return to base, exercised his professional discretion to execute a precautionary landing approximately 10 nautical miles from the airfield. “This is in accordance with established operational and safety procedures following combat missions. The helicopter has returned to base.” Although the Service did not disclose the specific reason for the precautionary landing, the statement stressed that the NAF remained committed to sustaining pressure on criminal elements, providing close air support to ground forces and protecting communities through coordinated air and ground operations. Ejodame said the successful outcome of the operation underscored the NAF’s continued resolve to deny criminal elements freedom of action and support efforts to restore safety and security to affected communities.

title: Plevris: First Agreement on African Return Hub Expected After Christmas
body: Greece expects to sign its first agreement with an African country to establish a migrant Return Hub after Christmas, Migration and Asylum Minister Thanos Plevris said on Thursday. Speaking to SKAI, Plevris said Greece is working with Denmark, Austria, Germany and the Netherlands on the initiative, which is designed to facilitate the transfer of migrants whose asylum applications have been rejected to designated centres outside the European Union. “We expect to be in a position to sign the first agreement with an African country after Christmas,” Plevris said, adding that the agreement would allow migrants with rejected asylum claims to be transferred there. The five countries have already established a Core Group to develop the Return Hub model, with Greece playing a central role in the initiative. A framework for cooperation with a third country was agreed in September, with the participating governments aiming to move towards implementation in 2027. Return Hubs targeted for 2027 Plevris said the Return Hubs are expected to become an additional tool in European and Greek migration policy, particularly for people whose asylum applications have been rejected but whose return to their countries of origin cannot immediately be carried out. Greece has been pushing the initiative alongside its European partners, with discussions involving potential host countries in Africa. The first pilot is expected to move forward in 2027. The minister also reiterated Greece’s proposal for an emergency European mechanism to deal with sudden and exceptionally large migration pressures. Under the Greek proposal, special measures could be activated during a major migration crisis, including the temporary suspension of asylum procedures under specific circumstances. Plevris has said the proposal has received support in principle from European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Greece sees major shift in migration routes Plevris said migration flows across Greece’s maritime border with Türkiye have fallen to historically low levels, with around 6,000 arrivals recorded during the first nine months of the year. The main pressure has instead shifted towards the route from Libya to Crete, where arrivals have reached approximately 16,000 over the same period. The shift has placed Crete at the centre of Greece’s current migration challenge, as authorities continue efforts to manage arrivals from North Africa while strengthening returns of people whose asylum applications have been rejected. Plevris said Greece is continuing to increase returns while working to implement the European Pact on Migration and Asylum, arguing that effective returns and the creation of Return Hubs are key components of the government’s migration policy. Greece has previously said the new Return Hub framework will operate under European and international law. Source: AMNA The post Plevris: First Agreement on African Return Hub Expected After Christmas appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: TikTok stars Peller, Jarvis expecting first child
body: Popular Nigerian content creators Peller and Jarvis have announced that they are expecting their first child together. The couple made the announcement in an Instagram post on Thursday, sharing pictures of the baby bump. The photographs showed the couple dressed in matching white outfits, posing together against an ocean backdrop on a beach. They also revealed that their journey has been filled with laughter, tears, prayers and growth, adding that God has continued to write their story through it all. Jarvis wrote: “From two people who once had no idea where this journey would take us… to husband and wife, and now soon to be parents. “A little piece of our love is coming into this world. Our greatest blessing. Our answered prayer”. The TikTok stars, who got married in a civil ceremony in Lagos on July 29, faced public scrutiny shortly after as fans claimed Jarvis was already pregnant, pointing out changes in her appearance. The young couple, however, dismissed the rumours, claiming her weight gain was linked to late-night meals. The post TikTok stars Peller, Jarvis expecting first child appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: 6.3-Magnitude Earthquake Hits Vanuatu, Says US Agency
body: A shallow 6.3-magnitude earthquake struck the Pacific island nation of Vanuatu on Thursday, the United States Geological Survey (USGS) said. The tremor’s epicentre was about 110 kilometres (68 miles) east of Luganville, the Pacific island nation’s second-largest city, the monitor said. The risk of landslides and the number of people exposed were low, it said in an assessment. Earthquakes are common in Vanuatu, a low-lying archipelago that straddles the tectonic Ring of Fire, an arc of seismic activity stretching through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin. The latest is not the first recorded on the island this year. In August, a magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck off the coast of the South Pacific nation, according to the US Geological Survey. The tremor’s epicentre was about 56 kilometres (35 miles) northeast of the small coastal village of Port Olry, at a depth of 188 kilometres, according to the USGS. There were no early reports of damage and Vanuatu’s natural hazards department did not immediately issue a tsunami warning. At least 6,438 people were killed when a twin earthquake struck Venezuela in June. Venezuelan authorities said that at least 60,000 homes were affected in some way, with 24,000 being left uninhabitable, while thousands of Venezuelan residents remain in temporary camps, where conditions are precarious. A collapsed building is seen from the base camp of the French Civil Security Training and Intervention Regiment (UIISC 7) at the Karting La Guaira complex in Caraballeda, La Guaira state, Venezuela, on June 27, 2026, as they assist with rescue operations following earthquakes. Photo by MIGUEL MEDINA / POOL / AFP In July, a magnitude 5.1 earthquake in the Andes region of Peru killed five people. The night tremor injured another 21 people as it shook the town of Chongos Bajo about 300 kilometers (180 miles) east of Lima, the Geophysics Institute of Peru said. The epicenter’s depth was 24 km (15 miles). The director of the National Civil Defense Institute, General Luis Vasquez, T, said that because the epicenter was at a shallow depth and many houses in that area were made of adobe or a wood, cane and mud blend called “quincha,” some towns suffered significant damage. AFP The post 6.3-Magnitude Earthquake Hits Vanuatu, Says US Agency appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Glenfiddich unveils Aston Martin F1-inspired 16-year-old whisky in Lagos
body:
Glenfiddich has unveiled a new 16-year-old limited-edition whisky developed in collaboration with the Aston Martin Formula One Team.
The whisky was unveiled at “A Night Beyond Expectations”, held at The Precision Hall on Victoria Island, Lagos, on Saturday.
The event, which brought together business and cultural leaders, creatives, celebrities and leading tastemakers, also marked the Nigerian launch of BEYOND, Glenfiddich’s international campaign built around its partnership with the Formula One team.
According to the company, the whisky was matured using five types of casks: first-fill bourbon barrels, Port casks, Fino Sherry casks, Oloroso Sherry casks and wine casks.
It is the second 16-year-old expression released under the partnership between Glenfiddich and the Aston Martin Formula One Team.
Glenfiddich said the collaboration draws on similarities between whisky production and Formula One engineering, particularly the attention to detail and long development processes both fields require.
The release was inspired by the work of Glenfiddich Malt Master Brian Kinsman and Aston Martin Formula One Team Managing Technical Partner Adrian Newey.
The first 16-year-old expression from the partnership was released in 2025 and matured using American oak wine casks, new American oak casks and second-fill bourbon barrels.
Glenfiddich and the Aston Martin Formula One Team announced their multi-year partnership in November 2024.
The company did not disclose the Nigerian price of the latest whisky, the number of bottles allocated to the country or when it would become available at retail outlets.
The Lagos event featured a product exhibition, whisky-tasting sessions and displays examining whisky production and Formula One engineering.
Guests also experienced a runway-style entrance and fashion and design elements built around the event’s “Sport Avant-Garde” dress code.
The company said the inclusion of Nigerian fashion, design and contemporary culture was intended to adapt the international campaign for a local audience.
The Lagos activation brought Glenfiddich’s global BEYOND concept into conversation with Nigeria’s creative scene, using fashion, music, design and contemporary culture to explore the relationship between heritage and modern expression.
Through the campaign, the brand sought to connect the precision associated with whisky-making and Formula One engineering with the creativity and individuality of Nigerian culture.
Nigerian creatives Nancy Isime, Swanky Jerry and Ifeanyi Nwene contributed to the campaign’s local expression, bringing perspectives from film, fashion, lifestyle, craft and design to the Lagos experience.
The Lagos activation was the first of two events planned in Nigeria. A second event is scheduled for Abuja on 10 October, with a greater focus on whisky collecting and production.

title: Rubio says he currently sees no prospects for ending Russia-Ukraine war through talks
body:
According to Ukrinform, Rubio said this in an interview with the Greek newspaper Kathimerini .
"Well, unfortunately, it seems to be going into its fifth year, which was never the original plan. I don’t think that was Putin’s plan for this war, so it hasn’t gone the way he planned it. And I think what it is now, unfortunately, is a strategic stalemate, which is a dangerous thing. Strategic stalemates are only broken in one of two ways: a) through a negotiated settlement, or b) through escalation by one side or both that ends up spreading beyond the confines of the original conflict. Right now, there don’t seem to be prospects of a negotiated settlement," Rubio said.
According to him, Washington is ready to play a constructive role if an opportunity for a diplomatic solution emerges.
"We are prepared to play whatever role we can in making that happen. And we have tried in the past, but so far it’s been elusive. The Russians have defined victory as the totality of Donetsk; they’ve repeatedly stated that as their goal and they continue to state that as their goal. And that’s a condition that, for Ukraine, is simply unacceptable," he said.
The United States is also closely monitoring the risks of escalation with great concern.
"Just yesterday, some ships were attacked in the Black Sea through a coordinated drone attack. We’re worried about a sabotage operation in a neighboring country that can spiral out of control," Rubio said.
He added that there are clear indications that Russia will use the upcoming winter as something they want to use to destroy what remains of the electric grid in Ukraine and force them into capitulation. Meanwhile, Ukraine has grown more effective in its ability to conduct long-range strikes deep into Russia.
"So, we share the same concern. The whole world is going about this thing like something that could escalate and perhaps become a broader conflict. So, we stand prepared to facilitate and continue to explore any opportunity for a negotiated settlement. We think it would be good for Russia and Ukraine, but so far, it’s proving elusive," Rubio said.

title: Big Tent Decries Tinubu’s Latest Wasteful Jamboree on Incomplete Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway
body: Another expensive ceremony for a fraction of a road while Nigerians starve, die young and live in insecurity The Utomi-led Big Tent Coalition has strongly condemned the Federal Government’s plan to stage yet another lavish inauguration ceremony for Section One of the controversial Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. Minister of Works, Dave Umahi, has announced that the 47.47-kilometre Section One is “ready for commissioning”. This is barely more than 6% of a project widely described as spanning about 750 kilometres across nine coastal states. Not long ago—on May 31, 2025—the same Tinubu-led All Progressives Congress (APC) government organised a grand ceremony to “commission” just 30 kilometres, less than 5% of the total length.​ A statement issued by Director of Media and Communications, Big Tent, Charles Odibo, asked that: “Since when did the commissioning of unfinished, partial stretches of road become the new normal of governance in Nigeria? How low has the bar for ‘achievement’ sunk that a government now celebrates fractions of projects with fanfare, motorcades and millions of naira in public funds while the vast majority of the highway remains incomplete?” According to the coalition, “These wasteful jamborees are an insult to a nation that continues to lag badly on the real measures of performance—human development.” Big Tent noted that Nigeria ranks 164th out of 193 countries on the latest Human Development Index with a score of just 0.560. Life expectancy stands at approximately 54.5–54.9 years—among the lowest in the world.​ On poverty, World Bank estimates place the rate at around 63% in 2025/2026, meaning roughly 139–140 million Nigerians live below the poverty line. Education remains in crisis, with learning poverty estimated at about 70% for children under 10 (many unable to read a simple sentence) and millions still out of school. Security continues to deteriorate: Nigeria ranks near the bottom of the Global Peace Index (around 142nd–148th out of 163 countries in recent editions) and features among the countries most affected by terrorism. Underemployment, youth joblessness and the absence of decent work remain widespread realities for millions of families.​ Odibo further stated that while ordinary Nigerians struggle with hunger, insecurity, collapsing public services and a future that looks increasingly bleak, “this government finds the resources and the appetite for repeated expensive ceremonies over incomplete roads. It is a clear demonstration that the Tinubu administration lacks the competence, capacity, compassion and character required to govern a serious nation.” Big Tent reminded well-meaning citizens that “this election season presents Nigerians with a clear choice”. The Big Tent Coalition therefore called on citizens to “see through the optics, the photo-ops and the unfinished projects dressed up as legacy achievements. We urge Nigerians to reject this pattern of governance and vote for leaders who are truly committed to a New Nigeria that works for all—leaders such as Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso—who prioritise results over rituals, people over pageantry, and genuine development over wasteful jamborees. “Enough of the ceremonies. Deliver the full road. Fix the indices that actually matter. Nigeria deserves better”.

title: Ex-Rep Member Threatens Atiku’s Lobbyist With Legal Action, Rejects Tinubu Link
body: A former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Ehiozuwa Johnson Agbonayinma, has threatened legal action against Karl Von Batten, also known as Ikemefuna Okeke, over an X post he described as misleading, insisting that his petition to the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) was not politically motivated. Agbonayinma, a member of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), a Nigerian and a citizen of the United States of America, faulted the use of his photograph in a publication linking his 14-day ultimatum to the EFCC with President Bola Tinubu, rejected suggestions that he was acting on behalf of the president, the All Progressives Congress (APC) or any political interest. In a statement made available to journalists on Thursday, the former lawmaker said the publication created a false impression about his identity, motives and involvement in the matter, warning that he would consider legal remedies over what he described as a misrepresentation of his position. He maintained that his demand for the reopening of corruption allegations and reports involving former Vice President Atiku Abubakar was a personal initiative undertaken in the interest of accountability and the rule of law. “For the avoidance of doubt, I did issue a 14-day ultimatum to the EFCC, calling on the commission to reopen the corruption allegations and reports involving Alhaji Atiku Abubakar. I stand by my call for accountability and the rule of law,” he said. The former lawmaker, however, denied any connection with Tinubu or the APC in relation to the petition, stressing that he neither acted on the president’s behalf nor pursued the interests of any political party. “My action was entirely personal, undertaken in my capacity as a Nigerian citizen who believes that allegations of financial impropriety involving public office holders deserve proper investigation,” he stated. “Both the US senate, homeland security have conducted and concluded investigations. It is only left for the EFCC to do the right thing by prosecuting him,” Agbonayinma said. He argued that the issues raised in his petition should not be reduced to partisan politics, insisting that allegations against public figures should be subjected to credible investigation irrespective of their political affiliations. “My call for the reopening of Atiku Abubakar’s corruption reports is not about Tinubu, APC, PDP, ADC, NDC or any political party. It is about accountability, transparency and the principle that no individual should be above the law,” he added. He urged the EFCC to determine the merits of the allegations through a transparent process, noting that the appropriate authorities should establish whether there were grounds for further investigation. He also challenged Atiku’s legal team to address the substance of his petition rather than attribute political motives to his intervention. Agbonayinma warned that the use of his photograph to advance what he considered a misleading narrative would not be treated lightly, adding that he was prepared to pursue legal action against those responsible for the publication. Reaffirming his position, he said his intervention was driven by the need to promote accountability without fear or favour, irrespective of political considerations. “I acted as a Nigerian, not as Tinubu’s representative. Let the record be clear,” he declared.

title: Ben Affleck on Machine Learning and Computer Vision
body:
I've always been kind of into computers since I was young. And then when film started to move from analog film to digital, I became more interested in that aspect of it. And the visual effects workflow for many years has included machine learning.
So I can write like pretty shitty Python scripts and stuff like that because with convolutional neural networks, which were the sort of precursors to what the transformer can do, which is just much more computation simultaneously, you would do things like look at what's called a tensor, which is just the numerical translation of a visual image in numbers — like the batch number, the frame number, the red, green, and blue values of each pixel in each frame.
And a tensor, you use a convolutional neural network to identify patterns in that that would reveal what's called edge detection or feature extraction, which is just identifying patterns enough to know like this is where the window ledge is, so we can more easily take the green screen image out and replace it with something.
This is a quotation collected by Simon Willison, posted on 7th October 2026 .

title: Russia’s Prosecutor General’s Office seeks Netherlands extradition of 9 ICC officials
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Russia’s Prosecutor General’s Office has sent the Netherlands a request for the extradition of nine representatives of the International Criminal Court (ICC) who were convicted in absentia in Russia, including ICC President Piotr Hofmanski and Prosecutor Karim Khan, the Russian supervisory authority’s press service said.
"The Russian Prosecutor General’s Office has sent requests to the Ministry of Justice and Security of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, as well as to a number of other countries, for the detention and extradition of International Criminal Court President P. Y. Hofmanski, ICC First Vice-President C. L. K. Carranza, ICC Prosecutor K. K. A. Khan, and ICC judges T. Akane, R. S. Aitala, S. H. U. Godines, B. Schmitt, R. A. S. Alapini-Gansou and H. B. Mahfoud," the statement said. All nine have been placed on an international wanted list.
In December 2025, the Moscow City Court found all nine ICC representatives guilty in absentia of offenses under Part 2 of Article 299 of the Russian Criminal Code (bringing a person known to be innocent to criminal responsibility or unlawfully initiating a criminal case), Part 2 of Article 301 (unlawful detention, arrest or custody), and Part 2 of Article 360 (attacking persons or institutions enjoying international protection, or threatening to do so). They were sentenced to prison terms ranging from three and a half to 15 years.
The Prosecutor General’s Office recalled that, citing the political bias of the International Criminal Court, the Russian president issued an order in November 2016 declaring Russia’s intention not to become a party to the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court. Notification of this intention was sent to the UN secretary-general. Russia has never been and is not a party to the ICC Rome Statute and does not recognize its jurisdiction.
"Despite this, ICC Prosecutor Khan unlawfully brought criminal charges against Russian citizens in The Hague. The ICC Presidency, in the absence of legal grounds, instructed the chamber’s judges to issue manifestly unlawful arrest warrants against them. These decisions were made in violation of fundamental principles and norms of international law and without any evidence that the individuals in question had committed the alleged crimes," the Prosecutor General’s Office said.

title: Group of 20 graduates rescued after being abducted in Nigeria
body: A group of 20 young people who were abducted in south-east Nigeria last week have been rescued, police say. The graduates were kidnapped on 1 October while they were travelling for a national community service programme in the Abia and Akwa Ibom states in the south of the country. They were rescued by the police with the assistance of other security agencies. Police spokesman Ani Iniedu said in a statement on Wednesday the group were rescued at Amakohia Ubi in Imo State after a sustained search-and-rescue operation. The group are being looked after and have been taken for medical evaluation. The police, military and other security agencies conducted intelligence-led searches of forests and suspected hideouts, he said, but he did not say whether any ransom was paid or if any arrests had been made. But the police spokesman did say they were making efforts to apprehend the perpetrators and bring them to justice. The police had previously said they had identified the location where the group was being held but could not rescue them because it was mined with explosives. The group of young people were participating in the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), which is a compulsory one-year community service programme for most Nigerian university graduates, where people are posted to different parts of the country. The group were travelling in two buses travelling on a major highway from Ibadan in south-western Oyo state to NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states when gunmen attacked the vehicles. The incident has reignited concerns over insecurity and kidnapping along roads in the south-east. Before they were released, the father of one of the people who were abducted, Omotosho Adewale, told the BBC that the kidnappers had demanded a ransom of 50m naira ($37,680; £28,440), which he could not afford. “There’s no peace of mind. I’ve not eaten in three days,” he said in between tears. Kidnapping for ransom is a major security problem in Nigeria, involving criminal gangs and armed groups. The authorities have not released any information about the identity of the attackers. The government has outlawed paying ransoms to kidnappers in an attempt to remove the incentive for the gangs but this has had little effect.

title: IN BRIEF: Kremlin comments on pending Putin-Trump call, prospects of Ukraine settlement
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin did not receive any messages from US leader Donald Trump on his birthday, a TASS correspondent quoted Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov as saying.
TASS has compiled key statements from the Russian presidential spokesman.
President Putin did not receive any messages from the US leader on his 74th birthday yesterday, Peskov said: "There were no congratulatory messages from Trump."
The exact timing of a potential Putin-Trump phone call has yet to be coordinated, the Kremlin spokesman told reporters: "As soon as the exact timing of a conversation is agreed and it [the phone call] takes place, we will let you know. We will not conceal anything."
Meanwhile, there has been no delay in arranging such a call, Peskov noted: "There has been no delay at all. As soon as [a Putin-Trump call] is agreed, and contacts take place, [we will let you know]."
Moscow is grateful to New Delhi for its interest in having the Ukraine conflict resolved, according to Peskov: "We are very grateful to the Indians for the interest they have shown in a settlement. We welcome any attempts, any efforts from countries that can somehow contribute to resolving the situation around Ukraine or somehow help urge the Kiev regime and, most importantly, the Europeans to bring it onto a peaceful track."
No peaceful settlement of the Ukraine conflict is in sight for the time being, he lamented: "No such thing is in sight at this point."
Russia is convinced that a settlement in Ukraine must be comprehensive, while piecemeal measures will not suffice, Peskov maintained: "We have repeatedly stated that piecemeal solutions and agreements will not enable us to reach a comprehensive settlement. It is a very complex matter, and the settlement must be comprehensive."
Russia believes that agreements regarding Ukraine must be guaranteed for generations to come and safeguarded against collapse, he continued: "We need a solution for future generations -- one that is guaranteed and safeguarded against collapse. The president has repeatedly spoken about this, including at the [recent] Valdai forum."
Freezing the Ukrainian conflict will not help resolve it, Peskov argued: "Let’s put it this way: a temporary halt or a freeze won’t help either."
The possibility of Tehran pulling out of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) may be raised at talks between President Putin and his Iranian counterpart, Masoud Pezeshkian, on the sidelines of the upcoming CIS summit, the Kremlin spokesman said: "If Iran finds it necessary to brief us of it and if these plans are really being implemented, then [the issue] will certainly [be brought up at the meeting]. However, it’s crucial to understand if this is really [on the agenda], because we have heard statements from lawmakers. Those aren’t always, say, in line with the country’s actual foreign policy plans."
The Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) has proved to be beneficial for its member countries in decades of its history, Peskov maintained: "The CIS format itself has proved to be beneficial to its member countries and quite relevant for more than a decade of its history."
It has been a platform for more advanced integration processes, he said: "The CIS format has paved the way for more advanced forms of integration, which is also very important."
Putin will meet with all participants in the upcoming CIS summit in Turkmenistan on the sidelines of the event, Peskov announced: "The president will have [an opportunity] to communicate with all other participants on the sidelines of these cultural events tonight. It means that he will talk with almost everyone on the sidelines [of the summit]."

title: Helsinki will not ban face coverings in schools, but tightens guidelines
body:
The city council voted against an outright ban on face coverings at a meeting on Wednesday, but a new safety guideline for schools will be issued.
The City of Helsinki will not ban the wearing of items such as headscarves, balaclavas and other face-covering garments in schools and colleges.
However, the city will instead add a requirement to schools' safety guidelines stating that a student must be identifiable during instruction and assessment.
The decision follows a meeting of Helsinki City Council on Wednesday, which dealt with a motion submitted by the Finns Party calling for a ban on the wearing of headscarves in schools and colleges.
National Coalition Party (NCP) councillor Seida Sohrabi also filed a separate, but almost identical, motion.
Sohrabi said face coverings such as niqabs, burqas, and balaclavas should be banned because they make it impossible to identify a child. The Finns Party wanted to extend the headscarf ban to include school staff, particularly teachers.
City councillors did not however vote in favour of an outright ban. The Finns Party also lost a vote calling for the motion to be reconsidered.
The City of Helsinki has been preparing a new safety guideline for schools, and the majority of the city's councillors said this reworking is a sufficient means of dealing with the matter.
The guideline regarind face coverings will stipulate that a student's face must be visible during lessons in order to ensure interaction, participation, legal protection and safety.
The guideline will however not be rolled out as a universal rule — rather as a case-by-case policy — but the main principle is that there must be a justifiable reason for requiring a student to show their face in a given situation.
The requirement for the face to be visible must not be related to the student's appearance, clothing or other personal characteristics, the guideline also emphasised.
Satu Järvenkallas , executive director of the city's education division, told Yle via email that the clarified safety guideline will be put into use in schools as soon as possible.
The issue has been widely debated in Finland since Minister of Social Security, Sanni Grahn-Laasonen (NCP), wrote last year in a post on X that "burkas and niqabs — scarves and veils covering the face — are not suitable for school".
Earlier this year, the cities of Tampere and Vantaa both announced plans to ban face coverings in their schools.

title: Shadow Tanker Hit by Ukrainian Drones Threatens Spill Off Russia's Black Sea Coast
body:
Authorities in the Russian Black Sea resort region of Sochi said that a massive oil tanker set afire and left adrift by Ukrainian drones is no threat to local bathers and waters, and that beaches closed to protect bathers and wetlands are now open to the public, local media reported on Thursday.
Sochi Mayor Andrey Proshunin said in a Wednesday statement that his office was closely monitoring offshore sea quality, telling voters the situation was under control and that citizen safety was his highest priority.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“At present the open fire on the tanker has been liquidated and rescue vessels are observing. Pollution of water with the oil cargo [carried in the tanker] has not been recorded. The tanker is drifting with the current along the shoreline,” Proshunin said.
“Local environmental watch agencies are checking pollutant levels in water, air and the ground across the greater Sochi region, and as a safe measure all beaches will be closed to swimming until those checks are complete,” he continued.
“I ask all to remain calm, to observe current rules and restrictions, and to trust only reliable sources of information. The situation is under constant monitoring by the city operational staff,” he added.
Russia’s national environmental watch agency Rospotrebnadzor, in a Wednesday announcement published by the Kremlin-sponsored news agency TASS, took the same position but didn’t mention the drones.
“There is no pollution to the Black Sea as a result of the fire aboard the tanker near Sochi. Agencies are monitoring the shore belt and waters of the Black Sea,” the agency said.
Dmitry Plishkin, head of the Sirius region containing Sochi and adjacent towns and villages, said in a Thursday statement that all local waters and beaches had received a clean bill of health for environmental safety and are now open.
Plishkin’s statement made no reference to the damaged 107,000-ton tanker which, according to Sochi-based news platforms, was in international waters drifting slowly northeast in light seas.
The Liberia-flagged Aframax Rio, a 246-meter (807-feet) long and 107,113-ton deadweight vessel built in 2004, is sanctioned by Ukraine as a shadow tanker Russia uses to evade Western oil export sanctions. The Aframax was southbound when it was hit and set fiercely afire in an early Tuesday evening drone attack.
The blaze under clear skies some 15 nautical miles (30 km) off the shore of Sochi – the heart of the “Russia Riviera” Black Sea resort region – was observed by thousands of local residents and tourists.
Video of the burning ship showed flames engulfing the entire top deck, with the fiercest fires concentrated around the middle of the tanker. The US Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), run by NASA, showed fires burning near the tanker for more than 24 hours before being extinguished.
The Liberia-flagged Afromax Rio burns following a Ukrainian drone strike offshore from the Russian resort port of Sochi on Oct. 6, 2026. The vessel, sanctioned by Ukraine as a shadow tanker, was reportedly fully loaded and left drifting. (Photo via sochiradar / Telegram) Advertisement
The Liberia-flagged Afromax Rio burns following a Ukrainian drone strike offshore from the Russian resort port of Sochi on Oct. 6, 2026. The vessel, sanctioned by Ukraine as a shadow tanker, was reportedly fully loaded and left drifting. (Photo via sochiradar / Telegram)
Imagery of the fire and its expansion recorded live from shore on Wednesday showed the blaze most concentrated in the central portion of the ship’s upper deck, an area often targeted by Ukrainian airborne drones attacking tankers in the past. Ukrainian sea drone attacks in past strikes on tankers have focused on engine rooms and propellers near the stern.
The Russian local news platform Sochi Radar reported that the Aframax Rio was fully loaded and that so much oil had spilled into the water and caught fire that firefighters were prevented from moving to extinguish the blaze quickly.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, in his Wednesday evening broadcast, said the Ukrainian military had attacked and badly damaged a tanker in the Black Sea, but he did not name the vessel, nor did he specify the type of drones used in the attack.
Local Russian news platforms identified the Ukrainian military as having operated the drones that attacked the tanker.
The US-based shipping information platform Marine Executive , in a Thursday article, said that the fire started in the center of the ship in the cargo tank area and then spread aft down the starboard side. Later that evening, the report said burning oil that had escaped from the tanker’s holds was visible on the water, beneath a towering column of smoke.
According to the world civilian vessel tracking group MarineTraffic, the last time the Aframax Rio turned on its transponder was Oct. 5 off the coast of Georgia, and since then its location has not been visible to satellite tracking. Its registered owner is Rio Enterprises SA, a Marshall Islands company.
The Greek news platform Protothema , in its Wednesday article, reported the tanker “is linked to Andreas Hadjiyiannis’ Hellenic Tankers.” As of Thursday, no major ship tracking platform showed the ship’s location.
Marine tracking platforms showed past port destinations for the vessel included Sapsun, Turkey and Sika, India.
According to Kyiv, both countries help Russia evade sanctions by receiving shadow tankers loaded with Russian crude, which is then refined into legitimate product not subject to sanctions.
The Black Sea shipping tracker Blackseanews.net showed the vessel’s operator as Hellenic Tankers Co LTD, an Athens-headquartered business, and its last officially recorded voyage as from Russia’s Novorossiysk port to Saudi Arabia’s Rabigh port in May 2026.
On Sept. 22, Robert “Magyar” Brovdi, commander of Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces (USF), claimed his strike forces had attacked and disabled 300 Russian “shadow-fleet” tankers since July 6, with 134 strikes in the Sea of Azov and 166 in the Black Sea.
The most environmentally damaging Russian shadow fleet tanker sunk in those waters was the Vologaneft-212, which went down in a December 2024 storm near the resort port of Anapa with more than 4,000 tons of heavy fuel oil aboard.
Leaking product souked hundreds of kilometers of resort beaches and sensitive wetlands on the Russian Black Sea coast and in Russia-occupied Crimea. The most intense period of the Black Sea storm season is from late October through March.
A press release from the ship’s declared operator, a Singapore-based company called Executive Ships Management, said all 23 crew members were safe ashore after the drone strike. The company said it was investigating the ship’s current status, including any potential threat it might pose to navigation, waters or the shoreline in the area.
Stefan Korshak is the Kyiv Post Senior Defense Correspondent. He is from Houston Texas, is a Yalie and since the mid-1990s has worked as correspondent/photographer for newswire, newspapers, television and radio. He has reported from five wars but most enjoys doing articles on wildlife and nature. You can read his weekly blog on the Russo-Ukraine War on Facebook, Substack and Medium. His new book on the 2022 Siege of Mariupol is available on Amazon UK and Amazon US .

title: Russia, Belarus warned as NATO’s Ukraine-related steps risk nuclear conflict
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Moscow and Minsk are concerned about NATO’s actions concerning the Ukraine conflict, which could lead to a nuclear conflict, the parties to the Treaty on the Establishment of the Union State of Russia and Belarus said in a joint statement published on the Russian Foreign Ministry’s website.
"We express special concern over the activities of NATO and its member states, aimed at creating challenges and threats to the security and interests of Russia and Belarus," the statement reads.
In particular, Moscow and Minsk regard as the most destabilizing NATO countries’ actions triggering serious risks, "primarily ongoing hostile steps regarding the Ukraine crisis, which risk leading to a direct armed conflict between nuclear powers, as well as plans and practical steps to deploy US and other Western medium-and shorter-range ground-launched missiles in Europe."
In addition, Russia and Belarus pointed to "efforts to build missile defense capabilities that define and fuel the European segment of the United States’ global missile defense system, deploy military infrastructure and major combat forces, as well as step up military activities by the alliance’s member states along the borders of the Union State of Russia and Belarus, develop schemes and capacities of the so-called joint NATO nuclear missions based on the US nuclear weapons deployed in Europe."
