title: Why we’re watching these climate tech companies
body: This week, we released our 2026 version of our Climate Tech Companies to Watch list. It’s an annual project that the MIT Technology Review team puts together. Our goal is to highlight some of the promising, interesting advances and firms we think are worth paying attention to in the world of climate and energy technology. The list is always a little ray of hope for me—there are some fascinating ideas out there for changing how we power our world or moving away from fossil fuels to reduce the greenhouse-gas emissions that cause climate change. Our chosen companies tend to reflect several aspects of the current moment. Here are some of the companies we picked and the key themes worth highlighting. China is the center of the climate and energy tech world Forgive me—I know I’ve made this point before. Feel free to call me Captain Obvious. But I think China’s dominance in energy technology is a global trend that bears repeated mentioning. China is home to the world’s largest grid, and renewables are coming online more quickly than I can wrap my head around. Contributing to that boom is Envision Energy , a renewables giant appearing on our list for the second time. The company has installed over 100 gigawatts of wind power worldwide, as well as over 50 gigawatt-hours of battery storage. Like many other Chinese companies right now, Envision is looking beyond the crowded Chinese market and setting its sights abroad, with projects in Germany, Brazil, and Australia and upcoming work in Vietnam. China is also leading innovation in key technologies. I’ve been fascinated by the potential for next-generation batteries coming out of its companies: All the big ones, along with a host of smaller ones, are racing to develop solid-state batteries. They could be both safer than existing EV batteries and longer in range. WeLion New Energy is particularly interesting. The battery company announced a big lab result last year, achieving 824 watt-hours per kilogram—more than three times the energy density of a standard lithium-ion battery today. Lab results in battery research are notoriously difficult to scale, but WeLion is also working to deploy semi-solid-state batteries, which could come to fruition faster than purely solid-state cells while still improving on lithium-ion’s performance. Everybody wants a piece of the data center pie We included just three companies from the US on the list, and two of them have received a major boost from Big Tech as companies look to power data centers. (The third, Brimstone , is leaning into another political hot topic, critical minerals.) Technologies that can provide consistent power are in high demand. Fervo Energy is bringing next-generation geothermal power to the grid by using horizontal drilling and hydraulic fracturing to make it practical in more places. The company went public in May, raising $2.2 billion in its IPO, and plans to have a gigawatt’s worth of plants operational by the end of 2030. X-energy is building helium-cooled small modular nuclear reactors. The reactors’ small size lends flexibility, and the company is currently working on a 320-megawatt cluster of them in collaboration with Amazon in Richland, Washington. (For what it’s worth, I’m interested in what this technology could do for industrial facilities—the company has a deal with Dow that could see it deployed at one of the company’s chemical plants in the early 2030s.) The grid needs support, and energy storage will be a key piece moving forward I know, I know—I haven’t stopped talking about batteries since I started writing this newsletter four years ago. But the energy storage market has surpassed even my expectations over that time. And as solar and wind quickly come online, they need storage to help them meet more of the grid’s demand. Form Energy is on the list for a third time for its iron-air batteries, which could enable cheaper long-duration energy storage. The company has a massive project in the works, to the tune of 30 gigawatt-hours, which will be used to help power a Google data center. It could be the world’s largest battery project in terms of capacity by the time it comes online, which is expected to happen in phases between 2028 and 2031. Taking another tack, Energy Dome is using compressed carbon dioxide to store energy on the grid. This technology is already cheaper than lithium-ion batteries for longer durations (think 10 hours or more), and the company is working to scale quickly. I covered the company in 2022 , before it had its first commercial plant running. Now it has plans for over 30 gigawatt-hours’ worth of plants around the world, including one with Google in Ireland that’s slated to come online in 2028. And Moment Energy is working to use the million EV batteries that are expected to reach the end of their life by 2030. The company has a facility in Vancouver, British Columbia, that repurposes used batteries for backup power. This year hasn’t been all sunshine and rainbows for climate tech. But I’m hopeful that some of the companies on this list, and the technologies they build, will keep nudging us in the right direction. This article is from The Spark, MIT Technology Review ’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday, sign up here .

title: [Rappler Investigates] Washing dirty money
body: Let us count the ways. From what we’ve learned from flood control corruption, there’s the use of casino gambling chips . Remember how Department of Public Works and Highways engineers gambled the hours away, lost a little here, then walked away with stupendous winnings, effectively washing illicit funds collected from irregular activities? From past investigations, we’ve also learned that real estate is another common method of obscuring the origin of funds, sometimes involving multiple companies and layers of ownership or ownership transfers of estates and luxurious properties. In recent events, allegations of “money laundering” initially flitted in relation to former speaker Martin Romualdez, but Ombudsman investigators are said to still be firming up their case. Moody’s defines money laundering as the “illegal process of taking money generated through criminal activities and making it appear as though it comes from legitimate sources. Criminal proceeds are usually moved through the financial system using various methods to disguise the illegal origin of these funds, with the intention of using these disguised funds without detection.” More than a decade ago, Rizal Commercial Banking Corporation got entangled with money-laundering allegations too. Recall the Bangladesh Bank heist and how it seemed like a Netflix whodunnit? Hackers stole over a million dollars from the Bangladesh central bank, with at least $81 million wired to the Philippines. Some key figures got away. Fast forward to 2026 and we’re hearing of similar methods. Money-laundering experts warn against businesses that involve a lot of cash movements. Think service-oriented businesses or retail, drug trafficking, forced labor, or pig-butchering scams . Others just simply buy lots and lots of expensive paintings, or perhaps even insurance. Interestingly during the impeachment trial on Tuesday, October 6, one of the insurance resource persons said that, typically, ordinary folks would get up to maybe three, four, or even five insurance policies. The Duterte couple, Sara and Manases, clearly were extraordinary, going by the number of policies they took out for themselves. There were at least 19 held by the couple since 2010. Subtext of the revelations appeared to be that money laundering was also in the works. But what types of transactions fall within the purview of the Anti-Money Laundering Act? Business reporter Lance Yu explains that the Anti-Money Laundering Council looks at “covered transactions” by virtue of size (over P500,000 in one banking day) and “ suspicious transactions ” due to surrounding circumstances. Read more here . The prosecution has tried to establish too that the Vice President has been less than honest in declarations made in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs), when these submissions are supposed to be made under oath. Could this be the most damaging yet against Sara, given precedence set by the Renato Corona impeachment years back? Read related stories: LIST: Duterte-Carpio bank accounts, balances detailed in impeachment trial Is Sara Duterte unaware of BPI accounts with father Rodrigo? Sara, Rodrigo Duterte hid P96M through unutilized manager’s checks — prosecution Why BPI asked AMLC to delete P2-B worth of transactions from Duterte-Carpio records If the prosecution winds up with its presentation of evidence this week, the defense should be having its turn next week. There are early indications of the path they will take: distance Sara from both her husband’s transactions and from those of the former president’s. Is this, however, believable or credible, and doesn’t it violate the essence of the SALN’s intent of accountability, truthfulness, and accountability? Question is, will the public, which has probably been desensitized to billions of pesos lost from the flood control scandal, still be enraged? Let me know what you think. Till Thursday after next! title: Three Russian brands expand operations overseas
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Three Russian brands entered international markets in the third quarter of 2026, according to analysts at NF Group.
"The geography of expansion remains focused primarily on nearby markets. In the third quarter of 2026, three domestic brands began operating abroad," the report states.
It is noted that Fix Price opened stores in Belgrade and Novi Sad; the company plans to build a network of 10 outlets in Serbia. Askona launched two showrooms in Bishkek and a local online store in Kyrgyzstan. MIUZ Diamonds opened its first franchise store in Uzbekistan at the Hotel Uzbekistan in Tashkent.
Russian retailers are testing new formats and entering new markets, said Evgenia Khakberdieva, Regional Director of the Retail Real Estate Department at NF Group. According to her, some projects are being launched online.
Earlier, Natalia Kermedchieva, an expert with the Association of Commercial Real Estate and Retail Experts, told TASS that many brands that had left the country view Russia as an attractive market and are looking to return.

title: MHI splashes Japan's seventh Taigei-class submarine
body:
Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) held a naming and launching ceremony for the new Taigei-class submarine being built for Japan’s Ministry of Defense.
As disclosed, the ceremony took place at Kobe Shipyard on October 8, 2026. The new submarine was named Shogei and is the seventh vessel of the Taigei-class, which succeeds the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force’s (JMSDF) Sōryū-class submarines.
Following the launch, MHI will carry out outfitting work, including the installation of the submarine’s hull systems, machinery, electrical equipment and weapons. The submarine is scheduled to be delivered to Japan’s Ministry of Defense during fiscal year 2027.
In March this year, JMSDF commissioned the fifth vessel in this class, Chogei, built by MHI. Chogei has a length of 84 metres, a hull diameter of 9.1 metres, and can accommodate a crew of 70 members. Unlike its sister vessels, the submarine also features separate accommodation spaces for female crewmembers.
The ship is a conventionally powered submarine that employs a diesel-electric propulsion system and runs submerged using electricity from lithium-ion batteries. Compared to the Soryu-class submarines, it features sonar with improved detection capabilities and a quieter hull structure, with a standard displacement of approximately 3,000 tons.
Taigei-class submarines are also being built by Kawasaki Heavy Industries (KHI), so the sixth vessel in this class, Sougei, was launched and named in October last year.

title: Russian drone strikes store in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district, two killed, two injured
body:

A search and rescue operation is ongoing.

title: Deliveroo Cut AI Churn Alerts by 90%. Did It Save Partners?
body:
Deliveroo rebuilt a churn model that overwhelmed retention teams. Fewer offline alerts haven't proved better retention.
By Growth Signal Desk October 6, 2026 8 min read
Alerts down over 90% offline, precision up eightfold
Send only as many alerts as the team can act on, and keep a comparable group untouched to learn whether outreach keeps customers.
Deliveroo’s churn model cried wolf. Now a randomised holdout will show whether the sharper list works.
Deliveroo had a retention problem inside its retention system. Its model was built to catch restaurants that might leave the marketplace, and it raised so many warnings that the people expected to act on them could never work through the list.
Growth teams know this failure well. A score can look useful on a dashboard while making the work queue worse. When almost every account looks urgent, a retention manager still has no answer to who gets the next call.
In a first party engineering account published on 22 September 2026 , Deliveroo data scientist and economist Firat Yaman described how the company rebuilt that system around a scarce resource. The scarce resource was the time of its restaurant account managers and retention team. Churn means a customer, in this case a restaurant partner, leaves. A churn model scores who looks likely to go.
Deliveroo connects consumers, riders and restaurant, grocery and retail partners . Restaurant churn creates costs because the marketplace has spent time and money finding and onboarding each partner. A preventable departure also shrinks the selection customers can choose from.
The previous system watched restaurant performance statistics and flagged accounts that resembled partners who later churned. Deliveroo says it was built on purpose for high recall. Recall is the share of all real leavers the model catches. Precision is the share of flagged accounts that really were about to leave. Chasing recall alone is easy, because flagging everyone catches everyone.
Churn is rare, though. Catching almost every potential case meant creating a flood of false positive churn alerts, which are flagged restaurants that were fine. The queue outgrew the retention team. Every call to a healthy restaurant carried an opportunity cost, because an account manager could have phoned a genuinely vulnerable partner instead.
The growth constraint was usable intervention capacity.
The replacement churn prediction model estimates a probability for every restaurant, ranks the accounts and applies an adjustable threshold, which is the cut off score above which a restaurant gets flagged. Deliveroo can move that threshold to keep the number of alerts in line with what its teams can realistically investigate.
The adjustment changes the system’s objective. Instead of asking how many eventual leavers the model can catch, the team asks whether the top of the list holds enough real risk to justify each contact.
Deliveroo also weighs a restaurant’s wider importance to the business when prioritising the queue. Yaman kept the features, weighting formula and intervention capacity private, so another marketplace could not rebuild the scoring system from the article. The copyable lever is simpler. Set the alert threshold from the team’s weekly capacity, then measure the opportunity cost of every false positive.
Like what you read? Get our weekly round-up of the deep research.
Forecasting future churn invites data leakage, where information from a later period slips into training or parameter selection and makes the model look smarter than it is.
Deliveroo used rolling window cross validation. Each configuration trained on historical observations and was checked on a later period, then the window rolled forward and the check repeated. The team also chose precision over recall, since restaurant churn is infrequent and outreach capacity is limited.
For interpretability, the pipeline calculates Shapley values, a method that shows how much each input pushed a prediction up or down, and surfaces the feature that contributed most to each estimated churn probability. The model runs weekly in an Argo pipeline, a workflow tool that schedules automated jobs, and sends the risk score with supporting information to its internal users.
The distinction changes how teams use the model. A probability can decide who enters the queue, while an explanation can help an account manager prepare the conversation. The article leaves open whether showing that explanation improves the quality of outreach.
Deliveroo reports that offline testing cut the number of flagged restaurants by more than 90% and improved precision eightfold. Recall fell, as expected. The company argues the trade made sense because its team had no way to action the much larger pool the old system produced.
Those are company reported classification results, and they stop short of showing that the system saved restaurants. Deliveroo withheld the model’s absolute precision, recall, sample size, evaluation period and confidence intervals. An eightfold lift could start from a low base, and fewer alerts can look efficient even when the remaining interventions leave behaviour untouched.
This is where the retention outreach experiment becomes the more important part of the work.
A holdout is a group you deliberately leave untouched so you can see what happens without your action. Deliveroo is randomly assigning restaurants flagged by the new model to treatment and control. The retention team and account managers see alerts for the treatment group. Alerts for the control group stay hidden. The stated hypothesis says treated restaurants will churn at a lower rate.
The comparison tests the combined pipeline. Prediction, prioritisation, human follow up and the action offered to a partner all sit inside it. It cannot isolate which part creates any observed effect, yet it answers the business question a retention owner needs first. Does the system reduce churn compared with leaving the same type of at risk account alone?
The control group also gives Deliveroo a cleaner check on calibration, which asks whether a restaurant given a 30% churn chance really leaves about 30% of the time. Because those restaurants receive no alert driven intervention, the team can compare their predicted churn probabilities with observed churn while the treatment leaves the outcome untouched.
As of the publication date, that experiment was still running. Deliveroo had yet to report its duration, audience size, market coverage, outreach script or result. Any claim that the model reduced churn would therefore be premature.
A growth team can use the operating lesson without reproducing Deliveroo’s machine learning stack. Start with the decision queue. Count how many alerts the team can action, how many prove useful, how many displace higher value work and whether the action moves the metric the business owns.
Say a model produces 1,000 alerts but the team can investigate 100. Optimising recall across all 1,000 solves the wrong problem. Ranking, an adjustable capacity threshold and a randomised holdout make the system auditable in business terms.
Deliveroo’s account also marks the boundary between prediction and growth. Restaurant churn prediction can show where risk sits. Only a controlled intervention can connect an accurate score to retention, because the score alone cannot prove the risk is preventable or that the company chose the right response. Matas ran a similar holdout on dormant loyalty subscribers , while Wantedly found that a candidate ranking boost barely moved churn .
Alert volume also affects sales teams. Sterling’s AI insurance sales agent had to choose when to step in during a quote journey, and its test kept a control group to prove the interruptions helped.
The same problem of deciding when a signal deserves action appears in seven operators’ limits on AI autonomy , including rules that keep predictable failures away from the model.
It was built for high recall, so it caught most at risk restaurants but flagged far too many accounts. Churn is rare, so the queue outgrew the retention team and every call to a healthy restaurant displaced a call to a vulnerable one.
It estimates a churn probability for each restaurant, ranks the accounts and applies an adjustable threshold matched to team capacity. It runs weekly and shows the top contributing feature per score using Shapley values.
No. The 90% reduction and eightfold precision gain are offline, company reported classification results. Whether outreach saves restaurants is the question of the randomised holdout, which was still running at publication.
Count how many alerts the team can action, set the threshold from that weekly capacity, treat every false positive as an opportunity cost, and keep a randomised holdout to measure whether outreach changes the outcome.

title: Teen's AI-guided mountain hike ends with a helicopter rescue and a lesson in common sense
body:
A 16-year-old had to be airlifted off a dangerous rock face on Crown Mountain near Vancouver after planning his route with an AI chatbot. Bryce Vincent Gowryluk used Anthropic's Claude to find a new way to the summit but ended up on the "Widowmaker Arete," a steep cliff that requires climbing gear, according to the New York Times .
He got stuck on a five-foot-wide ledge and called the police, who alerted the volunteer North Shore Rescue team. Rescuers tracked his cellphone, sent a helicopter, and dropped two team members above his position. One rappelled down to Bryce and guided him to a spot where the helicopter could winch him up.
Bryce said he doesn't blame Claude and takes responsibility, noting he also used Google Maps and AllTrails during planning. Rescue manager Paul Markey said Claude has no actual knowledge of locations or terrain and that AI is no substitute for experience and common sense on the trail. Anthropic didn't respond to a request for comment. Bryce says he'll keep climbing but never use AI for route planning again. Ad Ad

title: Ethiopia Cabinet Reshuffle: PM Abiy Fills Four Key Posts
body: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed (PhD) has announced four key government appointments, following several cabinet reshuffles made earlier today. Under the new appointments, Alemtsehay Paulos steps in as the Minister of Mines, succeeding Habtamu Tegegn (Eng). Ambassador Betre Mengistu has been named Head of the Prime Minister’s Office and Minister of Cabinet Affairs. Additionally, Fikadu Tesema takes over as Government Whip, replacing Tesfaye Beljige following his appointment as President of the South Ethiopia Regional State. Meanwhile, Adem Farah retains his position as Head of the Democratic System Building Center with the rank of Deputy Prime Minister, and Enatalem Meles continues in her role as Minister of Government Communication Service.

title: Road crashes in Ghana fall 9.48% in September 2026, fatalities drop 7.82% – MTTD
body: Road crashes in the country decreased by 9.48% in September 2026, while fatalities fell by 7.82%, according to the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD). The department’s Director of Education, Research and Training, ACP Alexander Kwaku Obeng, attributed the improvements to increased enforcement against speeding and public education by the Ghana Police Service. He said police data also showed a 12.19% decline in the number of vehicles involved in crashes. Motorcycle crashes decreased by 7.14%, while injuries fell by 15%. ACP Obeng explained that the Police intensified the issuance of electronic violation notices and caution notices from September 10, ahead of the planned nationwide introduction of the automated enforcement system on November 1, 2026. He said speeding remained the initial priority, with sensors being used to detect offences. Drivers and vehicle owners receive electronic notices supported by video evidence showing the violations. According to him, involving vehicle owners in the process had encouraged them to promote responsible driving, while motorists were becoming more cautious. “We issue the ticket to you, and you are confronted with the video; watch it and see what the driver is doing. The owners become advocates and drivers become cautious, and that’s what we have seen,” he said. ACP Obeng said the combination of monitoring, warnings and sensitisation was influencing motorists to reduce their speed. He spoke on Citi FM. “People are beginning to reduce their speeds because we are there, we are sensitising, and we are warning, and we are determined that 1st November will go live,” he added. The Police intend to maintain their focus on speeding as preparations continue for the nationwide rollout.

title: US sets new demands for Iran deal
body:
By R Anil Kumar

Washington/Tehran/Bengaluru, Oct 7, 2026. United States Vice President JD Vance has called for Iran to make a “meaningful” reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity as part of an agreement to end the war, a demand experts say may signal a softening of Washington’s earlier insistence that Tehran abandon enrichment altogether.



His comments come amid hardline rhetoric from other senior US officials. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has reiterated that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon, while President Donald Trump has warned the war will end through either “the nice way or the not-so-nice way”.

Officials in Tehran, meanwhile, have questioned whether Washington genuinely wants negotiations as the US-Israel war on Iran enters its eighth month.

Tehran’s negotiators are more concerned with sanctions, frozen Iranian assets, the US naval blockade and fighting across the region – issues remain the main obstacles to a deal.

What the US said

Vance said that Iran needed to demonstrate its commitment to not developing nuclear weapons by changing its enrichment programme. “If you don’t want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60 percent enriched fuel?” he said.

“If you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don’t build highly enriched fuel. That’s a very basic threshold issue.”

Enriching uranium makes it usable as fuel for nuclear reactors or, at much higher levels, for nuclear weapons. The International Atomic Energy Agency reported that Iran had enriched uranium to 60 percent, below the roughly 90 percent considered weapons-grade. In its May 2025 assessment, it found no credible indications of a structured nuclear programme.

Vance added that the US was speaking with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, although “it’s not totally clear how their country makes decisions”.

Meanwhile, Rubio, speaking to reporters in Athens, accused Iran of missing several opportunities to reach an agreement.

“Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon, simple, period, end of story,” he said.

He also claimed Iran had “lost complete control” of the Strait of Hormuz and that its economy was “in total and complete freefall”. Under “crippling” sanctions, it was “about to reach a place few countries in the world have been”, he argued.

Analysts say the comments suggest pressure on Tehran remains central to Washington’s approach, even as Vance’s wording leaves open questions about what nuclear restrictions it would accept.

Iran’s Reaction

Iran President Pezeshkian said on Monday that negotiations with Washington were “futile”, accusing the US of using talks while pursuing Iran’s government.

“Our problem with the United States is that every time we come to the negotiating table, war is immediately imposed upon us,” he said during a meeting with Armenia’s foreign minister.

“They have attacked us three times following talks so far; this demonstrates that they do not seek dialogue. On the contrary, their goal is to bring down the Islamic Republic of Iran,” he said, according to Iran’s official IRNA news agency.

“With an enemy that resorts daily to assassination, sanctions, pressure and threats – and breaks its promises – negotiations become futile, and our nation will not accept such an approach.”

However, Araghchi, addressing foreign ambassadors in Tehran on October 4, said, “Only negotiations based on justice and fairness” could end the conflict, suggesting there is still room for negotiations to continue and a deal to follow.

The statements follow an Iranian proposal presented during the United Nations General Assembly in New York in late September to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume negotiations. Trump subsequently rejected it.

Comparison with previous proposals

Iran’s latest proposal sought to build on the June 17 memorandum of understanding signed by the two countries, which briefly eased the conflict before breaking down. The new proposal, offered a few weeks ago, essentially compressed the timetable and changed the sequence of steps towards a settlement.

The proposal outlined that fighting would stop on all fronts, including Israel’s offensive in Lebanon. Washington would lift its naval blockade and oil sanctions, and release frozen Iranian assets. The Strait of Hormuz would reopen after seven days, followed by negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme.

Experts say the proposal could have offered Trump a route to restoring shipping ahead of November’s US midterm elections. But differences over the sequence of events remain unresolved.

However, Washington’s focus on enrichment risked overlooking Tehran’s priorities. “The US is trying to soften its stance on the nuclear question with the Iranians, but for the Iranians, this isn’t the real sticking point. It’s the blockade, the lifting of sanctions, the unfreezing of assets and an end to conflicts across the region.”

A deal allowing limited enrichment would also invite comparisons with the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, or JCPOA, negotiated under US President Barack Obama. The agreement restricted Iran’s nuclear programme in exchange for sanctions relief. Trump withdrew the US from it in 2018.

A nuclear agreement had been possible before the current war. “Arguably, a nuclear deal was within reach at several points. We had the JCPOA, of course, but then the Iranians were at the point of agreeing something similar back in February and January. The talks mediated then all suggested a nuclear agreement could be reached, and yet, the decision was taken to go to war.”

The other obstacles to a deal

Tehran would need commitments extending beyond the nuclear question. The Iranians would require the lifting of sanctions, the lifting of the blockade and the unfreezing of assets, or at least a road map to that, alongside an end to the conflict in Lebanon and a permanent ceasefire in the Gulf.”

Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains another source of uncertainty, despite Rubio’s claim that Iran has lost control of the waterway.

Although Gulf oil exports have recovered significantly, attacks on vessels continue. On Tuesday, 12 crew members on board a Panama-flagged tanker were injured by an unknown projectile while crossing the strait, India’s Ministry of External Affairs said.

Gulf oil flows, excluding Iran, reached more than 81 percent of pre-war levels in September, according to maritime intelligence firm Kpler. Wider Middle East crude exports exceeded pre-war levels on 14 days that month.

The recovery could ease pressure on the US to reach an agreement, although continuing attacks leave questions over how secure the passage is.

Washington’s apparent softening on enrichment suggested it remained uncertain about how fully shipping through Hormuz had recovered.

“If the Americans were confident the strait was open properly, then they’d be pushing for a harder deal.”

title: South Korea to recall Ukraine envoy amid North Korean POWs dispute
body:
Editor's note: This article has been updated to include a comment from Ukraine's Foreign Ministry. South Korea decided to recall its ambassador from Ukraine, the South Korean Foreign Ministry announced on Oct. 8, amid ongoing deterioration in Kyiv-Seoul relations.
The decision to summon Ambassador Park Hee-chang home comes after Seoul demanded an apology from Kyiv over the disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to South Korea.
Seoul claims that President Volodymyr Zelensky broke a confidentiality agreement when he announced the transfer during his U.N. speech on Sept. 23.
The dispute escalated further when Zelensky's office claimed that no such agreement existed, prompting South Korean President Lee Jae Myung to threaten retaliatory measures.
"The government looks forward to the smooth resolution of all pending issues between the two countries and will continue consultations with the Ukrainian side to this end," the South Korean Ministry said in a press release .
Ukraine invited South Korea’s ambassador to the Foreign Ministry to “seek constructive solutions” to the ongoing diplomatic issue, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi told journalists on Oct. 8. “We are convinced that diplomacy should prevail over emotions. Despite Seoul’s decision to recall the ambassador (in Ukraine), Ukraine remains open to resuming constructive dialogue — even if it takes time.”
His South Korean counterpart, Cho Hyun , claimed on Oct. 6 that he had received an apology from Sybiha but said it was not on "the level we expect, so we intend to take firm measures."
Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi later clarified that Sybiha merely expressed regret over the escalation in the diplomatic dispute.
Kyiv announced in January 2025 that it had captured two North Korean soldiers during battles in Russia's western Kursk Oblast.
The two were among the many thousands dispatched by North Korean dictator Kim Jong Un in 2024 to bolster Russian forces in the border region, making North Korea the only country to send its serving forces to fight on Moscow’s side to date.

title: Hindustan Shipyard Launches First Fleet Support Ship ‘Surya’ for Indian Navy
body: India’s Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL) launched the Indian Navy’s first Fleet Support Ship (FSS-1), Surya , on October 6, 2026, at a ceremony attended by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh as the chief guest. HSL also laid the keel of the fifth Fleet Support Ship (FSS-5) on October 6, 2026. The company also inaugurated several upgraded facilities, including an upgraded slipway and a 300-tonne Goliath crane, as part of efforts by India’s Ministry of Defence (MoD) to enhance the performance of the state-owned shipyard in Visakhapatnam, the country’s naval hub. The upgraded slipway will enable HSL to build and launch ships of up to 45,000 DWT. Meanwhile, the Kone Goliath crane, designed and manufactured by L&T Geostructure, will be used for the precise handling of heavier blocks during modern block construction. L&T’s shipbuilding arm is also a major subcontractor for the FSS program, building components for two ships under a contract with HSL. FSS-1 is expected to be inducted in mid-2027. The contract for five ships was inked in August 2023 and the keel of FSS-1 was laid in November 2024. Representative image of a Fleet Support Ship for the Indian Navy by design consultant firm SEDS. The Fleet Support Ships are intended to provide at-sea replenishment and sustained logistical support to naval operations. Designed and built indigenously by HSL, the ships will feature enhanced cargo and fluid capacity, onboard first-line maintenance workshops, a helicopter deck capable of supporting Multi-Role Helicopter operations, and self-defence systems. Once commissioned, the FSS will become the largest class of vessels in the Indian Navy by displacement, exceeding even the service’s aircraft carriers. The ships will be equipped with systems supplied by Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), including a Combat Management System, communications systems, and electronic warfare systems. BEL signed a contract for these systems in 2023. HSL designed the FSS with SEDS serving as the prime consultant. Although Türkiye’s TAIS was initially intended to serve as the design partner in the late 2010s, deteriorating relations between India and Türkiye put the planned foreign design partnership on hold. The specifications of the Surya class FSS, as reported earlier by Naval News , are as follows: Length: 222.8 m Width: 31.5 m Draught: 9.5 m Complement: 214 Range: 12,000 nm at 16 knots, 9,000 nm at 20 knots The post Hindustan Shipyard Launches First Fleet Support Ship ‘Surya’ for Indian Navy appeared first on Naval News .

title: Russian drone barrage on Kyiv kills 6, injures 17, disrupts electricity, water supplies
body:
Russian drone strikes on Oct. 8 have killed four people and injured at least 19 in Kyiv, the city's authorities said.
A Russian drone struck a four-story commercial building in Solomyanskyi district, killing two and injuring two, and leading to a fire, while the wreckage of another fell on the Holosiivskyi district, Klitschko said .
Prior to that strike, Klitschko said that Russian attacks on the capital this morning had killed one person and injured 11 others.
A fourth person died of their injuries in hospital, the Kyiv city military administration (KMDA) said in the afternoon.
Klitschko raised the number of injured to 19, 13 of which were hospitalized, in an update on 07:21 p.m. local time.
At 10:00 a.m. local time, Ukraine’s biggest private energy firm DTEK announced emergency energy shutdowns in Brovary, Buchanskyi, Vyshgorod, and Boryspil districts of the oblast.
Shortly after, KMDA announced that the right bank of Kyiv may experience interruptions in water supply, as the power decrease in the electricity grid also meant a decrease in pressure of the water supply network. This applied especially to the Holosiivskyi, Sviatoshynskyi, Solomyanskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts.
The drop in voltage from external power supply centers also temporarily halted Kyiv Metro train services and escalator operations, the KMDA said .
DSNS also said that a fire broke out at a logistics facility in the Buchanskyi district in Kyiv Oblast following a Russian drone strike.
In Sviatopetrivske in Buchanskyi district, a school-kindergarten and a nearby playground in a residential complex were damaged in the attack, Kyiv Oblast Governor Tymur Tkachenko said . In another settlement in the district, a woman was injured and hospitalized, he added.
Overnight, Russian drone strikes on Kyiv had already killed four people and injured 21 across four districts, KMDA said .
In Solomyanskyi district, a UAV fell on the roof of a 5-storey residential building, causing a fire, while elsewhere in the district falling debris injured one person.
In Desnyanskyi district, falling drone debris also caused a fire in a 12-storey residential building.
At the time of writing, Klitschko said there had been a further strike on Shevchenko district, emergency services were dispatched.
Russia attacked across Ukraine with 142 Shahed-type drones, 82 of them jet-powered, on the night of Oct. 8, Ukraine's air force said . The Air Force said that air defense shot down or suppressed 126 of these drones.

title: Rubio’s Acropolis Speech Draws Global Attention as US Secretary of State Lays Out Vision for the West
body: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s address in Athens, delivered in the shadow of the Acropolis, has drawn major international attention, with the Wall Street Journal calling it a potential “speech of the year” as Rubio laid out his vision for the future of the West. Speaking in Greece for the first time, Rubio used the setting of the Acropolis and the legacy of ancient Athens to connect the foundations of American democracy with classical Greece. Rubio’s Acropolis Speech Draws Global Attention as US Secretary of State Lays Out Vision for the West His speech ranged from Pericles, Thucydides and Homer to the Persian Wars and Plutarch , while also offering a forceful defence of national sovereignty, military strength and Western power. Rubio pointed directly to the influence of ancient Greece on the United States, telling his audience that American history is “covered with the fingerprints of antiquity” and that Greece is “literally etched into the architecture of our government.” He also highlighted Philadelphia, where the US Constitution was written, noting that the city’s name itself is Greek. ‘Speech of the year’ Rubio’s appearance against the backdrop of the Acropolis quickly became a focus of international media coverage. The Wall Street Journal described his Athens address as a compelling response to what it sees as a crisis of confidence across the Western world, calling it the “speech of the year.” The newspaper highlighted Rubio’s argument that the West can regain confidence by reconnecting with its historical traditions, ambitions and principles. The New York Times focused on Rubio’s call for Europe to “awaken” and argued that the Secretary of State used his Athens platform to promote a renewed emphasis on Western power and ambition. CNN , meanwhile, interpreted the speech through the lens of American politics, describing Rubio’s appearance against the Acropolis as a potential indication of how he could position himself beyond the current Trump era. The speech is likely to fuel further speculation about Rubio’s political future and possible ambitions ahead of the 2028 US presidential election . The Guardian similarly portrayed the address as an attempt to connect Donald Trump’s “America First” approach with the history and political traditions of ancient Greece. From Plutarch to America’s founders Rubio placed particular emphasis on the influence of ancient Greek and Roman thought on the founders of the United States. He cited Plutarch , noting that the Greek biographer was the author most frequently referenced in the Federalist Papers. According to Rubio, America’s founders were deeply aware of their place within history and drew heavily on the political and philosophical lessons of classical antiquity. For Rubio, that connection remains relevant to the challenges facing the West today. A warning to the West The Secretary of State also delivered a broad criticism of globalisation and international institutions, arguing that Western nations had gradually surrendered elements of their sovereignty while weakening their military capabilities and industrial bases. He rejected the idea that nationalism should be treated as a negative force and called for a renewed emphasis on national interests. Rubio argued that international institutions had not eliminated national competition, war or the pursuit of power. Instead, he said nations continue to compete over territory, technology, resources, markets, energy and influence . He warned that the world has entered a new era of great power competition, marked by war, terrorism, aggression and emerging threats. Greece as the backdrop The location of the speech was central to Rubio’s message. With the Acropolis and Parthenon providing the backdrop, the US Secretary of State repeatedly returned to the influence of ancient Greece on Western political thought and the development of American institutions. He argued that ancient Athens represented many of the characteristics he believes remain essential to Western civilisation, including individuality, ambition, exploration, innovation, risk and the pursuit of achievement. Rubio ultimately presented Athens not simply as the setting for his speech, but as a historical reference point for his argument about where the West came from and where it should go next. His message from Greece was clear: the West is at a turning point, and its future, in Rubio’s view, will depend on whether Western nations rediscover confidence in their own history, sovereignty and power. The post Rubio’s Acropolis Speech Draws Global Attention as US Secretary of State Lays Out Vision for the West appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Airbus completes autonomous taxi trials with A350 at Paris Charles de Gaulle
body:
Airbus has completed a three-year research program into autonomous aircraft taxiing after conducting 30 hours of tests with an A350 at Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport in July 2026.
The results were disclosed by French newspaper La Dépêche on October 8. The tests demonstrated the ability of the aircraft to navigate airport taxiways automatically, detect obstacles and stop when necessary, although Airbus has not announced plans to introduce the technology on production aircraft.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
Known as Optimate , the system uses cameras, radar, lidar and positioning technologies to monitor the aircraft's surroundings. Pilots select a destination through a cockpit interface, and the system calculates the route and controls the aircraft's movements on the ground. The crew can resume manual control at any time.
The Optimate research program began in late 2023 and was publicly presented by Airbus in May 2024. Engineers initially tested the technology using an electric truck equipped with an experimental A350 cockpit. The vehicle reproduced airport ground operations without requiring a commercial aircraft.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
The research campaign included approximately 1,500 hours of simulation and 500 hours of testing with the modified vehicle before the trials with the A350 in Paris.
The technology is intended to assist pilots at complex airports, where crews must follow taxi instructions, monitor other aircraft and ground vehicles, and identify potential runway incursions.
Airbus had already demonstrated automatic taxiing, takeoff and landing with an A350 through its ATTOL project in 2020. In January 2023, the manufacturer also disclosed results from its DragonFly demonstrator, which tested autonomous taxi assistance, emergency diversion and automatic landing capabilities on an A350-1000. Optimate concentrates on ground navigation and obstacle detection in the airport environment.
The manufacturer has not disclosed a certification schedule or indicated whether the system will be offered on the A350 or other commercial aircraft.

title: Oil tanker fire in Black Sea caused no environmental issues — Kremlin spokesman
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. The burning of oil aboard a tanker in the Black Sea did not result in significant environmental damage, Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said in response to a question from TASS, adding that "we got off lightly."
The Kremlin spokesman noted that the situation did not require any presidential directives, as the Ministry of Transport responded promptly and effectively.
"Regarding the ‘thank God’ aspect, it is worth noting that the cargo was crude oil rather than refined petroleum products. In terms of potential environmental damage, crude oil is, so to speak, less harmful. A single tanker was damaged, and the oil it carried burned off completely, effectively causing no harm to the environment," Peskov explained.
He stressed that all necessary measures had been taken promptly and effectively. "As the saying goes, we got off lightly," he added.

title: N18m fraud: Man allegedly impersonating Ogun prophet on Facebook arrested
body: The Police Command in Ogun has arrested a suspect, Adewale Arojah, for allegedly impersonating a cleric on Facebook and defrauding victims of over N18 million. The command’s Spokesman DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, disclosed this in a statement issued on Thursday in Abeokuta. Babaseyi said the suspect was arrested by operatives of the Ilaro Division following a complaint lodged on Oct. 3 by one Muyiwa Akogun, popularly known on Facebook as “Prophet Dr. Muyiwa Akogun.” He said Akogun had reported that members of the public were complaining about fraudulent activities being carried out through a duplicated Facebook account bearing his identity. According to Babaseyi, the suspect was a spiritual son of Akogun and has allegedly used the cleric’s identity to deceive unsuspecting members of the public. He said upon receipt of the complaint, the Divisional Police Officer (DPO), Ilaro, immediately deployed intelligence and detective operatives to track the suspect. He noted that sustained technological monitoring and intelligence-led investigation led to the suspect’s arrest in a village in Ajegunle, along the Ilaro/Ibogun axis. “Upon his arrest, the suspect confessed during interrogation to impersonating Akogun and using his identity to offer fake prophecies and prayer services to unsuspecting victims. “Preliminary investigation revealed that the suspect targeted people seeking spiritual assistance through the cleric’s Facebook page and allegedly defrauded victims in Nigeria and abroad of over N18 million. “The suspect has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Eleweran, Abeokuta, for further investigation to determine the extent of the alleged offences and identify possible accomplices,” he said. Babaseyi quoted the Commissioner of Police, CP Bode Ojajuni, as commending the Ilaro operatives for their vigilance and swift response. Ojajuni reaffirmed the command’s commitment to tackling cybercrime, identity theft and other forms of criminality in the state. He also advised members of the public to verify the authenticity of social media accounts belonging to religious leaders and public figures before engaging with them. He urged citizens to avoid transferring money to unverified persons for spiritual remedies or other services. The CP encouraged members of the public to report cybercrime, impersonation and suspicious activities through the Gateway Shield toll-free line, 0800 000 9111, or 09164859299 and 09154293464. title: Justice Democrats announce new executive director
body: The progressive political action committee Justice Democrats has appointed Rev. Hodari Williams as its new executive director. The change sets the organization up to hone a civil rights message ahead of the 2028 election cycle, Williams told POLITICO. His appointment, shared first with POLITICO, comes at a time when self-proclaimed progressives (and socialists) are flooding the scene. The PAC has had its most successful election cycle ever, helping seven candidates — including Donavan McKinney in Michigan, Melat Kiros in Colorado and Darializa Avila Chevalier in New York — defeat incumbents in the primaries. While those candidates are heavily favored to win on Election Day, the fates of three other Justice Democrats candidates, including Tennessee’s state Rep. Justin Pearson, remain less certain going into November. At one point, the group tried to get Williams to run for office. Though he declined, Williams said now is the right time to force change. “America and its present-day politicians, from my experience, have a high blood pressure of promises and anemia of political courage,” Williams said in an interview, using a common Kenyan political expression. “Right now, JD is producing candidates who have the political courage to deal with the crises that are existing in marginalized and disenfranchised communities, and I want to be a part of that.” Williams, 46, was born and raised in Lakewood, New Jersey. His parents were activists and community organizers who raised him on the legacy of the Civil Rights Movement. After graduating from Francis Marion University in Florence, South Carolina, with his bachelor’s degree, he joined the NAACP as a field organizer for voter rights and empowerment while pursuing his Master’s of Divinity at the Interdenominational Theological Center. In his time with the NAACP, Williams traveled across the Black Belt, where he said he witnessed poverty and inequity up close. “Civil rights traditionally has been something that people have tried to separate from progressivism … but these movements are inseparable,” said Williams. “What I witnessed in the South as a worker in voter rights and voter empowerment and education, and as a regional representative for the NAACP, was that the conditions that created inequity still existed and needed to be confronted and challenged.” His work took him to Kenya, where he served as a program coordinator with the Presbyterian Church USA. In Nairobi, he supported the Green Belt Movement’s work against deforestation and its mission to highlight environmental justice as a tool for economic empowerment and self-determination. Now, as some Black and brown voters express concerns of being tokenized by traditional Democratic candidates, Williams plans to bring his experience working in racial justice circles to his new role. “I have worked in communities that have borne the brunt of failed promises from the current Democratic leadership,” Williams said. “I have opened the doors of my congregations to politicians and have experienced the absence of those politicians after the elections.” He continued: “Black communities have become destinations for environmental hazards and data centers. Unemployment has risen. Black federal employees have been targeted. The list goes on. I’ve pastored these people. I've prayed with them. I've listened to them as they've shed tears. Now I've decided I want to move from triage work to really transformational work.” Some of that work will require challenging other Black leaders. “Unfortunately, many of our Black politicians have become victims of corporate capture, and their voices have been taken by entities like AIPAC,” said Williams, referring to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee. “They have not really been able to stand for the issues that are affecting the communities that that many of us are fighting for, and JD candidates are free from that, and they're free to take bold and significant action to move forward legislation.” But with the 2026 election cycle nearly over, the PAC is already brainstorming how to establish a strong progressive coalition for the 2028 presidential election. That will mean convincing the mainstream Democratic party that Justice Democrats have built a lasting coalition of the party’s base, said Williams. “We hope that the Democratic Party would see that we're developing a blueprint to show them how the base is being energized around the issues that are kitchen table issues that people want us to deal with,” said Williams. “It's not enough for us just to have a call to defeat a fascist president. We don't want a fascist president. We want him out, but we also want a vision of what America could look like when affordability, healthcare, civil rights, housing, and livable wages — all of those things are at the top of the political agenda,” he added. Williams succeeds current executive director and co-founder Alexandra Rojas, who will become president of Justice Democrats’ board and will support Williams as a senior adviser.

title: Fewer targets, more waves: jet-powered Gerans partly free Russia to concentrate missiles, ISW says
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russia is concentrating missiles on a smaller, more specific set of targets, and its jet-powered attack drones are part of the reason, the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) assessed . Its combined attack overnight on 7 October killed 22 people in Pryluky, the State Emergency Service (SES) said as of the morning of 8 October. Russian milbloggers noted the shift the same day. Russia often uses concentrated drone and missile strikes to overwhelm localized Ukrainian air defenses and destroy urban centers, ISW noted. Pryluky, where the strike killed children, was one of the areas a Russian channel says drew a significant share of the Kh-101s that night. With winter close, ISW expects the same pattern against Ukraine's energy grid, with jet drones partly letting Russia keep its missiles for priority targets without firing many more. Missile waves on a few areas, Russian channels claim Russia launched 48 Kh-101, Iskander-K, and Kalibr cruise missiles overnight on 7 October, Ukraine's Air Force reported . It also fired ballistic missiles, Zircon and Oniks anti-ship missiles, and 130 strike and decoy drones, 46 of them jet-powered Shahed-type models. Explore further 22 killed in Russian missile strike on Pryluky, including five children Russian milbloggers claimed the same day that Moscow had grouped a large part of its missile salvo into repeated waves on a few areas, while other weapons kept stretching Ukraine's air defenses elsewhere. The pro-war Russian Telegram channel Dva Mayora described the change as a switch from striking with splayed fingers to a series of hits with missile "fists." Defenders must then absorb a sharply rising load around one chosen site as one wave follows another, the channel claimed. Citing Ukrainian monitoring channels, it claimed that roughly 30 or more Kh-101 cruise missiles flew toward Pryluky, Kremenchuk, Svitlovodsk, and Oleksandriia in Chernihiv, Poltava, and Kirovohrad oblasts. It put the Kremenchuk group at up to 15 missiles, Kh-101s and Kalibrs among them, aimed at the area of Kremenchuk and its hydroelectric plant. Jet drones take some of the load off Russia's missiles ISW said the jet-powered versions penetrate Ukrainian air defenses deeper and more reliably than propeller models. In ISW's assessment, that partly lets Russia concentrate cruise and ballistic missiles on priority targets without significantly raising missile use. Russia builds about 3,000 Geran-4 and Geran-5 jet drones a month, Ukraine's military intelligence agency (HUR) told Militarnyi in August. Russia likely intends to make city life untenable and force Ukraine to capitulate to its demands, ISW assessed. Such tactics have not worked before and are unlikely to work now, analysts added. They called cheap countermeasures to jet drones and small cruise missiles vital, alongside Western air defense aid such as US-made Patriots, which can stop ballistic missiles. Ukraine has already paired a Soviet-era Kub launcher with American RIM-7 interceptors to catch jet drones.
