title: Medical debt is crushing hospital patients in LA. Health officials may have a fix
body:
Naman Shah examines a patient at Monrovia Health Center, a Los Angeles County public health clinic in Monrovia, California. Shah says reducing medical debt in the community will depend on effective prevention strategies, just as stopping the spread of infectious disease does. Lauren Justice/KFF Health News and Tradeoffs hide caption
LOS ANGELES — Every Tuesday, Naman Shah sees tuberculosis patients at a small public clinic in Los Angeles' San Fernando Valley. Shah, a physician and epidemiologist at the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health, pores over images of battered lungs, listens to labored breathing and checks medications.
For stories on the science of healthy living, subscribe to NPR's Health newsletter.
It's part of an initiative dating to the early 20th century to control infections so tuberculosis doesn't spread. "We like doing things upstream," Shah said, "meaning before they happen, not after the damage is done."
Today, Shah and his colleagues are applying the same principle to medical debt. A key part of that effort is a new system to allow every hospital in LA County to easily screen patients for financial aid. The goal: to stop low-income families from getting a bill that buries them in debt.
Shah estimates this system could prevent several hundred million dollars of medical debt every year.
Shah at Monrovia Health Center. Lauren Justice/KFF Health News and Tradeoffs hide caption
In the U.S., an estimated 100 million adults have some form of healthcare debt. In LA County, the nation's most populous, public health officials calculate that about 800,000 residents have medical bills they can't pay.
"The impacts of medical debt were staggering," said Shah, who used to staff a rural health clinic in India and, since 2023, has led a county initiative in LA to tackle the debt problem.
"People end up with credit card debt and then a vicious cycle of high interest rates and poverty," he said. "People forgo their prescriptions. People forgo appointments. And then you get into worse health."
Hospitals typically offer financial aid to patients with low incomes. But information about assistance is often hard for patients to get . Applying can be cumbersome. And many eligible patients never seek aid, research shows.
"Most people walk into the hospital and walk out without any knowledge of financial assistance," said Jared Walker, founder of Dollar For, a nonprofit that helps patients nationwide apply for aid, often called charity care.
"The impacts of medical debt were staggering," says Shah, who since 2023 has led a Los Angeles County initiative to tackle the debt problem. Lauren Justice/KFF Health News and Tradeoffs hide caption
That's fueling debt. It's also driving costly collection efforts that even hospital officials acknowledge pointlessly target low-income patients who are unlikely to be able to pay.
"They're turning their wheels trying to collect on debt that isn't collectable," said Adena Tessler, regional vice president for the Hospital Association of Southern California.
One potential solution is a system that automatically screens and qualifies low-income patients for financial aid without requiring an application. This is called presumptive eligibility .
Some hospitals already use such systems, which rely on software that checks patient eligibility based on publicly available information such as credit history.
The strategy can be very effective. Shah said hospitals that have deployed presumptive eligibility systems have reported as much as a 50% increase in the amount of financial aid they give patients.
Under a state law passed last year, all California hospitals will have to start doing presumptive eligibility screening by next July.
But the systems can be expensive and difficult for smaller hospitals to implement. Only about 1 in 5 hospitals in LA County currently use them, Shah said.
Public health officials wondered whether they could help more hospitals set up the systems.
The county, which, like many local governments, faces major fiscal challenges, couldn't pay for this, Shah said. But the public health department could bring together healthcare and hospital officials in the county to figure out another solution.
"The beauty of government is not when it always has to do the work," Shah said. "We have the ability to make sure that people cooperate."
The Hospital Association of Southern California, initially wary of the county initiative, came to see improving hospital financial aid programs as beneficial to hospitals, many of which were wasting money on collections. "The billing process is cumbersome and costly," said Paul Young, a senior vice president with the association.
The association agreed to procure a digital presumptive eligibility system and make it available to its members. This bulk-purchasing approach, which Young compared to "a Costco model," would lower the cost for individual hospitals, he said.
At the same time, L.A. Care, a nonprofit health plan that administers Medicaid coverage for more than 2.5 million low-income county residents, committed $2 million to set up the system.
The investment reflected the safety net insurer's mission to make medical care accessible to more people, said Melanie Fontes Rainer, who leads strategic planning for L.A. Care. "It's going to make Los Angeles County better," she said.
Getting the new system up and running by January, as the partners hope, faces challenges.
Hospital officials are figuring out how the system will be funded in the long term. And it's unclear how many of the county's 88 acute care hospitals will ultimately use it, even if it's cheaper and easier to access.
The partners are also working to improve the data that the system relies on to screen patients. One goal is to link the system to tax records maintained by the state of California. This would provide hospitals with more accurate information on patients' income than current systems, which often rely on estimated income.
Walker, the patient advocate at Dollar For, said he's heartened by the county's effort. "I'm optimistic that we can make a better charity care system," he said. "And the fact that hospitals in LA County are willing to be innovative and creative about ways we can do that is super encouraging."
For his part, Shah said county public health officials recognize that a better screening system at hospitals won't by itself eliminate medical debt. But he said the public health department couldn't ignore a problem that affects more county residents than asthma or tobacco use.
"Prevention is our bread and butter," he said.
This article is part of Hidden Help , an investigative series from Tradeoffs and KFF Health News about how hospitals can protect their patients from the life-altering harms of medical debt.

title: US, Russia discuss possibility of selling gas to Europe via Nord Stream
body: Senior Russian and American officials discussed bringing in an American investor for the Nord Stream pipeline projects, sources told Reuters. Kirill Dmitriev, the Russian president’s special representative for investment and economic cooperation and head of the Russian Direct Investment Fund, and Jared Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, took part in the talks. Both are also involved in talks aimed at ending the war between Russia and Ukraine. Dmitriev and Kushner have met in Moscow and New York in recent weeks. It’s unclear how extensively they discussed Nord Stream at those meetings. The topic remains on the agenda, according to sources. Another source told Reuters that the two sides are unlikely to reach a deal in the medium term. The White House, for its part, said U.S. authorities would need to approve any such deal and that no discussions about Nord Stream had taken place recently. Kushner views business cooperation as a key factor in reaching a peace agreement, according to Reuters. A deal allowing American participation in the Nord Stream pipelines would let the U.S. profit from energy supplies to Europe after the war ends. Dmitriev favors resuming sales of Russian gas to Germany. In September, he met with representatives of the U.S. Department of Energy and the Treasury Department and discussed potential U.S.-Russian energy initiatives. Germany is Europe’s largest energy consumer. It is unclear how interested Washington is in reviving the flow of Russian gas to the country. Before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, most of Germany’s gas came from Russia via the Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 pipelines. After the war began, the flows stopped and the pipelines came under EU and U.S. sanctions. Germany and other European countries, which are preparing to defend against Russian hybrid attacks and a possible invasion, are expected to oppose any resumption of Nord Stream’s operations. title: Cape Town launches specialised SWAT, drone units
body:
Cape Town Mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis has launched the City’s new specialised Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) and aerial surveillance units, together with Alderman JP Smith, Mayoral Committee Member for Safety and Security.
The SWAT unit will provide highly-skilled support for serious crime and high-risk incidents beyond conventional policing, while the Metro Police Aviation Unit focuses on aerial surveillance for faster, safer and smarter ways to combat crime, the City of Cape Town said during the launch on 7 October.
“I was pleased to see the City’s new specialised units in action today. The City will continue doing whatever it takes to make Cape Town safer, and will stop at nothing to build our resources and powers, because that is what the public deserves and needs,” said Hill-Lewis.
“These highly-skilled SWAT and aerial surveillance units form part of our broader safety investments, including over 1 300 new City police officers added in this term of office, a new Highway Patrol unit, major safety technology rollout, and a new state-of-the-art digital nerve centre to coordinate all City policing operations.
“The City’s growing policing capacity clearly shows that our officers are ready for expanded powers, especially to investigate gang, gun and drug crime. We must make full use of all policing resources in Cape Town to bring a positive change for communities living in daily fear of violent crime
“We are also heartened by the 35% increase in SAPS requests to view our footage for police investigations over the last year. This increases the chances of successful convictions as we work to expand our digital coordination and safety technology network,” Hill-Lewis added.
Combatting gang-related activity and extortion
Hostage and barricaded suspects support to SAPS
Smith said the Unit is equipped with an armoured vehicle, modern firearms, and other advanced tech – including night vision and heat detection. The vehicle is a MAX SWAT 4×4 from SVI Engineering. It was taken into service earlier this year.
“Expert SWAT team members have extensive SAPS Special Task Force experience, and are further supporting the City’s Training College to develop a detailed curriculum for future growth and continuity in this critical metro policing capacity,” said Smith.
The Metro Police Aviation Unit includes officers with pilot certification, four types of aircraft for different operational needs, and specialised vehicles with connectivity, off-grid power, and external monitors, the City of Cape Town said.
The Metro Police Aviation Unit’s key support areas include:
Detection is enhanced by thermal and zoom cameras, with AI-assisted tracking and laser rangefinder to pinpoint exact locations of suspects and activity, for example in bush or across rooftops.
A live overhead picture is streamed to control centres, helping to direct and protect officers on the ground. High-resolution imagery and scene-mapping document evidence to support case dockets for investigations.
The Unit can also provide a visible aerial presence to deter crime, including loudspeaker messaging and night-spotlight.
“Air support is a force multiplier, widening what officers can see and shortening the time to a confident, safe decision. We have seen that drone flights and surveillance support early crime-fighting successes and arrests,” added Smith.
Intelligence-led arrests in Delft, Somerset West and Strand
Tracking and arrest of a wanted suspect on the run in Elsies River
Support at beaches for liquor confiscations and enforcement
New digital nerve centre for City policing
A live demonstration by the new specialised units was conducted at the Joint Policing Services Operational Centre (JPSOC), the City’s new digital nerve centre which will integrate all City policing resources and safety technologies deployed throughout the metro.
The JPSOC – now in the final stages of operationalisation – will integrate a range of existing and emerging policing technologies, including:
Drones, operated through the City’s Aviation Unit as well as third-party service providers
Body-Worn Cameras (BWC), In-Vehicle Cameras (IVC) and Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) technology
Citizen and Trusted Partner Apps to strengthen communication and information sharing
Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation
The City’s bodycam deployment will soon reach 3 000 cameras in the field, while 530 enforcement vehicles have In-Vehicle Cameras (IVCs) with Automated Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) functionality and printers for warrants and summons.
“The various safety tech solutions we’ve introduced help create a real-time operational picture to improve situational awareness and inform decision-making. We are now at a point where officers can stream live feeds to our operations centre from their mobile cameras, augmented by drone, ANPR and CCTV footage. I am excited to see how we can keep building on this to advance public safety into the future,” said Smith.

title: IN BRIEF: Two residents of Trans-Baikal detained for preparing election provocations
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) detained two residents of the Trans-Baikal Region, who, acting on instructions from Ukrainian intelligence agencies, were preparing provocations during the recent parliamentary elections, the FSB said.
TASS has compiled the key details available so far.
- The Federal Security Service in the Trans-Baikal Region thwarted the illegal activities of two Russian citizens who, acting on instructions from Ukrainian intelligence agencies, were involved in preparing a series of provocations aimed at destabilizing the social and political situation in the region during the State Duma elections.
- FSB officers detained the suspects on the eve of the Single Voting Day during operational and investigative measures.
- One of the suspects is a woman who was a member of a precinct election commission.
- It has been established that a member of the Freedom of Russia Legion terrorist organization, controlled by the Ukrainian Security Service and outlawed in Russia, instructed a local woman to join one of the region’s precinct election commissions, the FSB said.
- The woman’s handler tasked her with "obtaining some ballots and promotional materials, collecting and providing information on preparations for the vote by political parties and candidates, as well as rigging the election results."
- The second detainee is a resident of the city of Krasnokamensk.
- According to the FSB, he was recruited by the Ukrainian Security Service to gather information on the election campaign and photograph regional government buildings and the recruitment office.
- In addition, he was ordered to set fire to the city office of one of the political parties ahead of the active phase of the vote, using an improvised incendiary device, the FSB added.
- The woman confessed to cooperating with the Ukrainian intelligence service, as seen in a video released by the FSB.
- According to her, while browsing various websites in search of an opportunity to earn some money, she was contacted by a man who suggested that she assist him.
- The woman said that he first asked what festive events were taking place in the city and whether locals were gathering and sending humanitarian aid to the special military operation zone.
- The suspect said she had provided him with the requested information.
- According to her, the man also asked her to join a local election commission, which she did.
- The suspect added that her handler had asked her to send photos of a polling station and ballots and to monitor the voting process and possible attempts to rig the election.
- She never received any money from him.
- The second suspect has also confessed.
- He said he had been looking for a job when a person asked him to take photos of recruitment offices and administration buildings.
- According to the man, the handler later promised him "good money" for setting fire to the local office of a political party.
- Investigative and operational activities are underway to establish all circumstances of the illegal activities of the perpetrators, as well as their possible contacts.

title: Vladimir formation of Russia’s Strategic Missile Force undergoes scheduled inspection
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. The Vladimir missile formation of Russia’s Strategic Missile Force (RVSN) is undergoing a scheduled comprehensive check with the deployment of the Yars road mobile launchers along combat patrol routes, the Russian Defense Ministry reported.
"In accordance with the Strategic Missile Force training plan for 2026, a commission from the RVSN command is conducting a comprehensive inspection of the Vladimir missile formation, which includes a command-staff exercise with a fixed-base missile unit under the leadership of RVSN Commander Colonel General Sergey Karakayev. In addition to the fixed-site missile formation, autonomous launchers from the Strategic Missile Force’s mobile-based missile formations have been deployed along combat patrol routes as part of the exercise. During the exercise, crews of the Yars mobile ground-based missile systems are practicing marching and maneuvering operations," the ministry said in a statement.
The Yars road mobile launchers are also practicing the dispersal of missile battalions, including tactical displacement and traversing sections of simulated contaminated terrain and engineer obstacles, as well as organizing camouflage and security measures.
Support forces (deployed to their designated areas) as well as attached units from the Moscow Military District are involved in the maneuvers. Following the exercises, a commission from the Strategic Missile Forces command will assess the readiness of command and control bodies and the training of crews.
Army aircraft and Strategic Missile Force’s unmanned systems units, with extensive use of UAVs, are being deployed for aerial reconnaissance of vehicle routes and for the search for and detection of simulated saboteurs. The main objective of the exercises is to improve the coordination of military command and control bodies. During the inspection, the formation’s personnel are demonstrating a high level of training and readiness to perform their assigned missions, the ministry specified.

title: Stefanos Tsitsipas Advances at Shanghai Masters With Straight-Sets Win
body: Stefanos Tsitsipas has made a winning start at the Shanghai Masters, defeating Belgian qualifier Kimmer Coppejans in straight sets to advance to the second round. The Greek star, ranked No. 43 in the world, overcame the world No. 232 6-3, 7-5 in a composed opening-round performance. Tsitsipas quickly found his rhythm against Coppejans, breaking clear in the opening set to take it 6-3. The second set was more closely contested, but the Greek produced when it mattered most, closing it out 7-5 to secure his place in the round of 64 . Tsitsipas now faces a significantly tougher test against No. 18 seed Luciano Darderi in the next round. The Shanghai victory gives the Greek another opportunity to build momentum as he looks to climb back up the ATP rankings. title: Sea drone vs. air drone: Ukraine’s Sargan-3000 turns anti-aircraft gunner
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); A Ukrainian Sargan-3000 sea drone shot down a Russian Shahed flying on a mesh radio network, Ukraine's Navy reported on 7 October. Ukrainian sea drones have downed Russian aircraft before, but with missiles . This one used a machine gun. Russia has been hitting Odesa with air attacks that come in waves with short gaps between them. Guarding the sky over water is harder than over land. Since fall 2025, Russia has also used mesh radio networks to reroute Shaheds mid-flight and dodge Ukrainian air defenses. That leaves Ukraine needing more ways to meet these drones out at sea, before they reach its ports and coast. A Shahed steered by radio A mesh-network drone passes its control signals along a chain of radio relays , drone to drone and on to ground antennas. That lets a Russian operator steer it in flight. In May, Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov, then a Defense Ministry adviser, said only about 5% of Shaheds had got through in a recent Russian strike, and predicted that Russia would answer with jet-powered versions and strikes near the border. By July, Ukraine was testing jamming against mesh-controlled jet Shaheds, he said. Protector RWS turret on the Ukrainian Sargan-3000 naval drone, October 2026. Screenshot from a video by the Ukrainian Navy The Sargan-3000 fired its Protector remote weapon station, Militarnyi reported. The station is a remotely operated 12.7-mm (50-caliber) machine gun with electro-optical sights. The outlet added that the Sargan-3000 is designed for combat missions far from Ukraine's coast. Built for the open sea Ukraine's Navy took the Sargan-3000 into service in April 2026, according to Militarnyi. The drone boat has a combat radius of up to 1,600 km. It moves at 40–55 knots and carries up to 450 kg of payload. In September, a Sargan-3000 sank a Russian uncrewed boat with machine-gun fire. Militarnyi called it the first battle between uncrewed sea platforms in history. Analyst H.I. Sutton wrote that the boat carried a Protector made by Norway's Kongsberg. That is the same weapon station named in the October shootdown. Sutton added that Russian attack sea drones work closely with Shaheds, which can relay the boats' mesh radio signals. title: Ndume meets new Theatre Commander over schoolchildren, others in captivity
body: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Senator Mohammed Ali Ndume, representing Borno South Senatorial District, has taken the safe return of the abducted Lassa and Musa schoolchildren and Biu-bound travellers to the attention of the military leadership in Borno. Ndume made the call Wednesday when he paid a courtesy visit to the newly deployed Theatre Commander, Operation HADIN KAI, Major General Ibikunle Ajose, at the Maimalari Military Cantonment, Maiduguri. The meeting, held behind closed doors, focused on security matters affecting Borno and the wider North-East, with the safe recovery of the abductees among the Senator’s immediate concerns. Recalled that over 40 pupils/students were abducted in Mussa, and after some few weeks, another abduction of over 30 students were abducted in Lassa, in addition to a road ambush by terrorists along Biu-Buratai-Buni Yadi where some passengers including a toddler were kidnapped since February 2026, with no any information in their whereabout. Speaking after the meeting, Ndume commended the Nigerian military for its sustained efforts in confronting insecurity and urged the troops to intensify ongoing efforts towards the safe and successful recovery of the Lassa and Musa schoolchildren and the Biu-bound passengers. “The Army must be commended. Alhamdulillah, the security situation is improving. Most of what we discussed will not be disclosed because they are security matters, but certainly, the safe release of the Lassa and Musa schoolchildren and the Biu travellers is my priority for now.” The Senator also raised the strategic importance of major roads linking Borno South, including the Gombe–Biu and Damboa–Maiduguri roads, noting that he has consistently advocated their construction and improvement because of their importance to security, commerce and the movement of people. Ndume, a former Chairman of the Senate Committee on Army, also welcomed the recent salary increase for military personnel approved by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, describing it as an important step towards improving the welfare and motivation of members of the Armed Forces. He said the improved welfare of personnel would complement the sacrifices being made by troops in securing communities across the country. Earlier, Major General Ajose described Ndume as a friend of the military and said the Senator’s visit provided an opportunity to discuss security issues affecting the North-East. He appreciated Ndume for consistently prioritising the security and welfare of his constituents and assured that the military would continue to build on its successes in the ongoing fight against insecurity. title: Architect Launches Liquid Inference, a Real-Time Auction for LLM Inference
body: Architect Financial Technologies has launched Liquid Inference , an LLM router that runs a live auction for every request. Liquid Inference is an LLM inference marketplace from Architect where providers bid to serve each prompt. The buyer pays the lowest offer that meets its rules. For developers, it is quite simple message: swap a base URL, keep your code, and let providers compete on price. What is Liquid Inference? Liquid Inference is an exchange-style router for LLM inference. According to Architect , providers post offers to serve specific models. Each request is auctioned across every provider quoting the named model. The lowest-priced offer that meets the buyer’s rules wins. The product comes from a trading firm, not an AI lab. Architect runs the AX perpetual futures exchange . In May 2026 it acquired a US Designated Contract Market to list GPU compute futures, pending regulatory review. The team used its experience building financial exchanges to create two-sided price discovery for inference. How does the inference auction work? The flow has 4 steps: Request: A client sends a standard OpenAI or Anthropic API call. Rules: The buyer’s constraints filter eligible offers. Auction: Providers quoting that model compete. The lowest qualifying offer wins. Receipt: The max price is locked before generation. Billing covers metered usage only. Buyers can set per-job cost caps, time to first token limits and minimum throughput . They can also require approved regions, zero data retention and provider or model allow lists. An Auto mode can pick the model for a given unit of work. Harrison’s LinkedIn post adds routing rule presets and full multi-modal support. Account holders can view live order books, per-provider and per-model quotes, and cleared transactions. That level of market data is unusual for an LLM API. What do buyers get? Drop-in compatibility with agentic coding tools. The post lists Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Pi and Cline. Free email signup. The first 500 users get $20 of free inference, per Harrison. A referral program: 20% of referred fees as free inference, plus 10% on second-level referrals. What do inference providers get? Providers onboard through the Liquid Inference app. Harrison says new providers are verified “in minutes, not weeks.” All prompts use the OpenAI API standard. A REST and WebSocket API registers models and quotes. Providers can update quotes based on their own costs. That lets them sell spare GPU capacity only when they want. Payouts run through Stripe, with itemized records of every job. How does Liquid Inference compare with OpenRouter and Hugging Face? Feature Liquid Inference OpenRouter Hugging Face Inference Providers Routing model Per-request auction across quoting providers Price-weighted load balancing, inverse square of price Fastest provider by default; :cheapest suffix optional Model / provider count “Hundreds” of models; providers not disclosed 500+ models, 80+ providers 18 listed partners API compatibility OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible OpenAI-compatible OpenAI-compatible, chat only Price cap Max price locked before first token max_price parameter Not disclosed Data controls ZDR, regions, allow lists zdr , data_collection , only / ignore Provider preference order Platform fee Not disclosed 5.5% card credit fee, $0.80 minimum No markup Free credits $20 for first 500 users Not disclosed $0.10/month free, $2.00 PRO Public market data Live order books and cleared trades Not disclosed Not disclosed window.addEventListener("message",function(e){if(e.data&&e.data.mtpLiH){var f=document.getElementById("mtp-li-frame");if(f)f.style.height=e.data.mtpLiH+"px";}}); Key Takeaways Liquid Inference auctions every LLM request across competing providers. Max price is locked before the first token, with a per-job receipt. Works with OpenAI and Anthropic clients, including Claude Code and Cursor. First 500 users get $20 free; referrals earn 20% of fees. Fees, provider list and latency data are not yet public. Check out the Technical details . All credit goes to the researcher of this project. title: 2027: Presidential aide claims Tinubu will win by wider margin
body:
Daniel Bwala, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, has claimed that the president will secure a significantly wider margin of victory over his opponents in the 2027 presidential election.
Mr Bwala made this statement while appearing on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday.
“Let me tell you and let me say it categorically, and I will be happy to come back. The margin of gap that President Bola Tinubu will give each and every one of these candidates will be so much that you won’t believe it,” he said.
The conversation comes ahead of the 16 January 2027 presidential election, in which Mr Tinubu is seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC).
He is among 18 presidential candidates listed for the election, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Omoyele Sowore of the African Action Congress (AAC) and Sandy Onor of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).
Mr Bwala attributed his confidence partly to the growing support for Mr Tinubu among governors elected on opposition party platforms.
The presidential aide said the number of governors supporting Mr Tinubu in 2027 would exceed the support the president received from governors during the 2023 election.
Mr Bwala also defended the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, including the removal of petrol subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market.
He acknowledged that the reforms had increased poverty in the short term but argued that the government had made progress since their introduction.
“There is no part of the world where you start a reform like that there will not be discomfort. More people went down to poverty, acknowledged, but since when the reform started to today, we have made marked progress,” he said.
Mr Bwala also acknowledged that a significant number of Nigerians remain poor but maintained that the government had made progress since the reforms began.
“So, you cannot discount that even though there are quite a number of our population that are poor which we admit, but we have made progress so far,” he said.

title: Ghana retains strong investment potential despite financing challenges – Emerging Market Advisory
body: Ghana continues to offer significant investment opportunities in areas including energy, ports, digital payments, agribusiness and regional trade, despite relatively high financing costs and currency pressures. The latest Africa Investment Pulse report by Emerging Market Advisory identifies Ghana as one of the key markets in West Africa where investors continue to see demand and growth opportunities, but with greater attention to how projects are financed. The report projects West Africa’s economy to grow by 4.7 percent in 2026, saying the outlook continues to support the region’s investment case. It identifies Ghana and Nigeria as markets where investors are being more cautious because of higher interest rates and currency movements. For Ghana, the report estimates a policy rate of 14 percent during the review period, while the cedi weakened by about 3.8 percent against the African Development Bank’s Unit of Account between May and August. Despite these pressures, the report says the region’s large consumer markets, growing urbanisation, mobile money adoption, Atlantic trade gateways and rising energy demand continue to create opportunities for investors. It identifies payments, telecommunications infrastructure, distributed energy, ports, logistics, consumer platforms, agri-processing and healthcare distribution among the sectors with strong investment potential. The report, however, cautions that Ghana and other West African markets must overcome several constraints to fully realise these opportunities. These include foreign-exchange liquidity, high local financing costs, fragmented regulation, power reliability, customs challenges and uneven policy implementation. “West Africa offered the strongest growth and market-scale opportunities, but higher inflation, expensive credit and uneven currency liquidity required local-currency finance, export revenues or blended structures,” the report states. The report says investors are increasingly favouring projects that have predictable revenue streams and can withstand currency and financing pressures. For Ghana, this means projects linked to hard-currency earnings, reliable customers or strong public-sector support are more likely to attract financing. The report also highlights the importance of infrastructure and regional trade to Ghana’s investment prospects. It says the country’s position within West Africa’s trade network, combined with demand for energy, logistics and digital services, provides opportunities for investors willing to navigate the financing environment. But the report stresses that economic growth alone will not be enough to attract capital. “Across Africa, investor decisions were therefore driven not by GDP in isolation but by whether growth could generate cash flows capable of absorbing inflation, debt costs and currency movement while preserving debt service, repatriation and risk-adjusted returns,” it says. Emerging Market Advisory therefore sees Ghana’s investment environment as one that requires selective positioning rather than a broad-based approach. Projects with strong cash flows, credible sponsors and appropriate financing structures are expected to remain more attractive as investors balance Ghana’s growth opportunities against currency and financing risks.

title: Bwala admits Tinubu’s Reforms Pushed More Nigerians Into Poverty
body: Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has admitted that the administration’s economic reforms pushed more Nigerians into poverty. He, however, insisted that the country has made “marked progress” since the reforms were introduced. Bwala spoke during an interview on Channels Television, amid renewed debate over the impact of the administration’s removal of petrol subsidy and foreign exchange reforms. “Please let it be clear even to the opposition, the reason why you have this number of poor people and some of these doomsday analytics that people are giving is because we undertook a reform,” he said. “There is no part of the world where you start a reform like that there will not be discomfort. “More people went down to poverty, acknowledged, but since when the reform started to today, we have made marked progress which is what we have spent the last three years talking to Nigerians about”, he stated. Bwala said the increase in poverty could not be considered separately from the economic restructuring undertaken by the administration. “So, you cannot discount that even though there are quite a number of our population that are poor which we admit, but we have made progress so far,” he added. The admission comes against the backdrop of continuing disagreement among economists, opposition politicians and the Federal Government over the consequences of the reforms. The World Bank has acknowledged improvements in Nigeria’s macroeconomic position following the reforms, including stronger external balances, improved fiscal conditions and continued economic growth. It has, however, also warned that the gains have not yet translated sufficiently into improved living standards for millions of Nigerians. The bank estimated in 2025 that Nigeria’s poverty rate had risen substantially over the preceding years, although it noted that much of the increase occurred before the Tinubu administration came into office. The International Monetary Fund has similarly recognised improvements in macroeconomic stability while warning that poverty and food insecurity remain significant challenges. For many households, the removal of petrol subsidy and the depreciation of the naira translated into higher transportation, food, energy and other living costs. Economists have consequently drawn a distinction between improved macroeconomic indicators and the immediate welfare of households. Chief Executive Officer of the Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise, Muda Yusuf, has argued that the reforms helped restore macroeconomic stability and address longstanding distortions. He, however, said the ultimate test would be whether the gains translate into higher incomes, jobs, lower poverty and improved living standards. Other analysts have similarly argued that the reforms may have corrected some structural problems while imposing substantial adjustment costs on households and businesses. The Federal Government has maintained that the measures were unavoidable because of the fiscal and structural weaknesses it inherited in 2023. President Tinubu has repeatedly argued that continuing the petrol subsidy would have left the government with fewer resources for infrastructure, social services and development. The administration has also pointed to increased Federation Account revenues following the removal of the subsidy. Finance Minister and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said the Federal Government and the subnational governments received increased revenues from subsidy savings between June 2023 and December 2025. Oyedele, however, acknowledged that reducing poverty remained one of the administration’s major unfinished tasks. The government has consequently highlighted its social intervention programmes, student loans, consumer credit initiatives, agricultural support and CNG transportation scheme as measures designed to cushion the impact of the reforms.

title: Gunmen kill youth leader, injure two in Plateau
body: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed a youth leader and former chairman of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association (BYM), Gashish District, Rwas Paul Danladi, and injured two others in separate attacks in Barkin Ladi and other parts of Plateau State. Danladi was attacked at about 6pm on Wednesday around Rantis Village along the Gashish-Barkin Ladi road while returning to Barkin Ladi on his motorcycle. The Berom Youth Moulders-Association, BYM, confirmed the killing in a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Rwang Tengwong, and made available to newsmen in Jos on Thursday. According to the association, “Rwas Paul Danladi was attacked on Wednesday evening around Rantis Village while returning to Barkin Ladi on his motorcycle.” The BYM condemned the killing, describing Danladi as a respected community leader, and extended its condolences to his family, friends and the entire Gashish community. The association said other attacks were also recorded across parts of the Berom communities on Wednesday, leaving two persons injured. According to BYM, one person sustained serious injuries following an attack around Gwom-Ajang in Foron and was taken to the Jos University Teaching Hospital for treatment. The association added that Mafeng Samuel Lamba was injured along Sho Road and taken to hospital. It further alleged that Bitrus Pam Dadon was attacked along Sho Road and had his motorcycle stolen. The group called on the Plateau State Government, Nigeria Police Force, Nigerian Army, DSS and other relevant security agencies to urgently investigate the killing, apprehend those responsible and strengthen surveillance along vulnerable roads and communities in Barkin Ladi, Jos South, Riyom and other affected areas. BYM also urged the security agencies to intensify intelligence gathering and take proactive measures to prevent further attacks and protect residents. Efforts to reach security agencies for confirmation of the killing and the reported attacks were unsuccessful as of press time. title: Production Starts on Netherlands New Airbus H225M Caracal Helicopters
body:
Production of the Netherlands’ new H225M Caracal helicopters has officially started at Airbus Helicopters in France, marking a new phase in the country’s development of a dedicated rotary-wing capability for Special Operations Forces.
The Dutch-configured Caracal is designed to operate in diverse flight conditions and alongside NATO and other international partners. It will be capable of exchanging information with platforms and units including the Embraer C-390M, F-35, 11th Air Mobile Brigade, Marine Corps and Army.
The helicopters are being acquired under the SOF Air Rotary Wing (RW) program and will be operated by 300 Squadron. The Netherlands has ordered 12 H225Ms, with testing scheduled to begin in 2028 and the first aircraft due for delivery in early 2030. Deliveries are expected to continue through 2032. Personnel training and operational development are being conducted alongside the aircraft program.
The H225M is an 11-tonne, twin-engine tactical transport helicopter powered by two Safran Makila 2A1 turboshaft engines. It can carry up to 28 fully equipped troops or be configured for medical evacuation with 11–12 stretchers.
The helicopter has a maximum takeoff weight of 11.2 tonnes, a cruise speed of approximately 262 km/h and a maximum speed of up to 324 km/h. Its standard range is around 920 km, extending to approximately 1,253 km with auxiliary fuel tanks; aerial refuelling can further increase its range.
Its intended missions include special operations support, tactical troop transport, combat search and rescue (CSAR) and medical evacuation (MEDEVAC). Depending on configuration, the H225M can also carry mission-specific weapons, including 7.62 mm or 12.7 mm door-mounted machine guns, 68 mm rocket pods and anti-ship missiles, while defensive equipment includes radar-warning and chaff/flare systems.
