title: CDP Empowers Over Two Million People in Katsina
body: Francis Sardauna in Katsina The Katsina State-owned Community Development Programme (CDP) has empowered more than two million people across the state through various empowerment initiatives and rural development projects. The state Coordinator of the CDP, Professor Kamaludden Kabir, disclosed this last Tuesday during the inauguration of the executive committee members (EXCOs) of ‘Dikko Mayar Da Alkhairi Da Alkhairi’. Kabir said the beneficiaries were drawn from all the 361 wards across Katsina State, and stressed that the state government rural revitalisation initiative has improved the livelihoods of citizens and created opportunities for economic empowerment. He said the initiative had continued to impact communities across the state through various interventions aimed at supporting vulnerable people and enhancing their economic wellbeing. The coordinator explained that the state government, through the CDP, distributed 400,000 bags of fertiliser to farmers and 60,000 bags of assorted grains to vulnerable citizens across the 361 wards of the state last year. He added that the same quantities of fertiliser and grains were distributed by the community development programme this year to boost food productivity and assuage the plight of vulnerable households in the state. “In the past three years, the Katsina State Government, through the Community Development Programme (CDP), has successfully reached out to more than two million people through various empowerment programmes and rural development projects,” he said. Responding, the state Governor, Dikko Umaru Radda, said the World Bank has expressed interest in taking the state’s community development programme framework as a model for consideration and possible adoption in other states across the country. He said the development followed a recent engagement with a World Bank delegation, which expressed satisfaction with the effectiveness and grassroots impact of the programme. Radda said the recognition demonstrated the value of the CDP’s community-based approach to delivering government interventions and ensuring that development programmes reach people at the grassroots. He commended the CDP for taking government interventions and development initiatives to communities across the state, saying its work had helped bridge the gap between government programmes and the people. Earlier, the state All Progressives Congress (APC) Chairman, Dr Bashir Gambo Saulawa, urged members of the group to communicate the achievements of the Radda-led administration to the people at the grassroots. He enumerated the recruitment of 10,000 teachers, construction and renovation of schools, educational opportunities for less-privileged students to study abroad, road projects, the modernisation of healthcare facilities and the renovation of Danja Dam for irrigation development as some of the achievements of the state government. He stated that the ‘Dikko Mayar Da Alkhairi Da Alkhairi’ movement would become a formidable grassroots platform within the APC to mobilise support for the administration across the state.

title: South Korea Recalls Ambassador From Ukraine Amid Diplomatic Rift Over North Korean POWs
body:
South Korea will recall its ambassador to Ukraine amid a diplomatic dispute over Kyiv’s disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul, South Korean news agency Yonhap reported on Thursday, Oct. 8.
The recall comes after weeks of escalating tensions between the two countries, with Seoul accusing Kyiv of violating a confidentiality agreement and saying Ukraine’s subsequent apology did not go far enough.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The dispute began on Sept. 23, when Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced during his address to the UN General Assembly that Ukraine had transferred two captured North Korean soldiers to South Korea.
The two soldiers were captured by Ukrainian forces in Russia’s Kursk region in January 2025 while fighting alongside Russian troops. One was carrying Russian military identification documents, while the other had no identification.
Zelensky said the soldiers had not been easy to capture alive, adding that one had attempted suicide to avoid being taken prisoner. Reports later indicated that the two initially rejected an offer to move to South Korea but changed their minds later in 2025.
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung criticized Zelensky after the announcement , saying the public disclosure could create unspecified problems.
Seoul said the two governments had agreed to keep the transfer confidential because of security concerns surrounding the soldiers and their relatives in North Korea.
Ukraine disputed Seoul’s characterization of the agreement.
Zelensky’s office said South Korea had been informed in advance that the Ukrainian president intended to mention the transfer in his UN speech. Kyiv also argued that Zelensky had not disclosed identifying information about the soldiers or sensitive operational details.
South Korea nevertheless demanded an official explanation and apology , accusing Kyiv of violating the confidentiality arrangement.
The issue became increasingly contentious after Kyiv initially rejected Seoul’s characterization of the agreement.
On Oct. 2, Lee warned that South Korea would take “further measures” if Ukraine continued to refuse to acknowledge the agreement and publicly apologize. Seoul had already summoned Ukraine’s ambassador over the dispute.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha described the dispute as a “diplomatic misunderstanding” and said Kyiv wanted to resolve it quickly, stressing that South Korea remained an important partner.
By Oct. 6, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Sybiha had apologized in messages exchanged between the two sides.
But Cho said the apology fell short of Seoul’s expectations.
South Korea was then considering several possible responses, including recalling its ambassador to Ukraine , Park Hee-chang.
Cho said confidentiality had been agreed upon from the outset and was intended to protect the soldiers and their relatives, who remain in North Korea.
He also offered his personal interpretation that Zelensky may have wanted to demonstrate at the UN that Ukraine had acted appropriately as a liberal democracy.
The diplomatic dispute comes as Seoul faces separate questions over South Korean fuel shipments to Russia.
A Guardian investigation found that more than 176,000 metric tons of fuel, mostly diesel, were loaded at South Korean ports in July and August and transported to Russia’s Far East.
Seven tankers made 14 voyages , with three of the vessels reportedly under UK or EU sanctions. One sanctioned tanker received fuel through a ship-to-ship transfer in South Korean waters, potentially making the origin of the cargo harder to trace.
The shipments came as Russia faced growing fuel shortages following Ukrainian strikes on its oil-refining infrastructure.
According to the International Energy Agency, Russian refinery throughput fell in June to its lowest level in more than two decades, while diesel production was nearly 30% below the level recorded a year earlier.
Data analyzed by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air showed Russia’s seaborne imports of oil products surged in August.
The reported increase in shipments from South Korea began in July, around the same time Lee pledged $100 million for Ukraine’s reconstruction at a NATO summit in Turkey.
South Korea has rejected suggestions that the reported shipments violated its export controls.
The South Korean Foreign Ministry said on Oct. 8 that refined petroleum products, including commercial diesel and aviation fuel cited in The Guardian report, were not subject to South Korea’s export controls on Russia.
It also said it had not established whether the fuel was actually of South Korean origin and was conducting further checks into the vessels’ routes.
The ministry said South Korea’s overall exports to Russia had fallen by more than half since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
An adviser to Zelensky criticized the reported shipments as being in “sharp contrast” with Seoul’s sanctions policy. South Korea called those remarks “factually incorrect” and “inappropriate.”
The two disputes come against the backdrop of deepening military cooperation between Russia and North Korea.
Pyongyang has deployed troops to support Russia’s war against Ukraine and has supplied Moscow with ammunition and other military assistance in exchange for economic and military benefits.
The two North Korean soldiers captured in Kursk were among the first known North Korean troops taken alive by Ukrainian forces.
South Korea, meanwhile, has provided Ukraine with financial and humanitarian assistance but has maintained a policy against directly supplying lethal weapons to countries involved in active conflicts.
Seoul has also emerged as a major global arms exporter, including through multibillion-dollar weapons deals with European countries since Russia’s full-scale invasion.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: URCS provides assistance at Russian missile strike site in Kremenchuk
body:
The Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) is operating at the site of the liquidation of the consequences of the Russian missile strike in Kremenchuk, Poltava region.
"Teams from the Poltava Regional and Kremenchuk City organizations of the Ukrainian Red Cross Society are working at the site of the aftermath of the strike on a residential area of Kremenchuk together with special services," the URCS reported on Facebook on Wednesday.
The URCS has set up an aid station where victims receive first aid and psychological support as needed. Residents of damaged apartments are provided with necessary materials for temporary home repairs, drinking water, hot drinks, and facilities to charge their mobile phones.
Due to the persistent threat of repeated attacks, operations at the site are periodically suspended, with everyone moving to shelters. As soon as the security situation allows, volunteers and rescue workers resume providing assistance to the victims.
As reported, the enemy attack on Kremenchuk killed two people. As of Wednesday evening, 47 injuries were reported, including two children. According to the Regional Military Administration, the attack damaged five multi-story residential buildings containing 431 apartments, as well as 35 private houses, while six private houses were destroyed.

title: Coleman Demands Stiffer Penalties for Cable Counterfeiters
body: Kayode Tokede Coleman Technical Industries Limited yesterday called for stiffer penalties for manufacturers and distributors of counterfeit and substandard cables, saying weak enforcement is encouraging the growth of the illicit trade. The company’s Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, George Onafowokan, made the call while responding to questions from journalists after a media tour of Coleman’s factories in Sagamu, Ogun State. Onafowakan said the Standard Organisation of Nigeria (SON) needs to strengthen its enforcement efforts to protect genuine manufacturers and consumers from substandard products. He argued that confiscating and destroying counterfeit cables without prosecuting those responsible would not serve as an effective deterrent. The Coleman boss questioned the number of counterfeiters prosecuted by SON, alleging that the regulator had not done enough to ensure that offenders faced criminal sanctions. He also alleged that SON sometimes focuses on charging manufacturers for testing cables rather than working with relevant agencies to prosecute those involved in counterfeiting. Onafowokan said regulators should emulate the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), which, according to him, had intensified enforcement against counterfeit pharmaceutical products. “If there is no consequence, all you’ve done is just to remove a little off my shelf. I’ll buy another one because you did not tell me I’ve become a criminal for doing it,” he said. He stressed further that substandard cables could cause fires and endanger lives, making stronger enforcement and prosecution necessary. Onafowokan disclosed that Coleman had been working with the Nigeria Police Force, including the office of the Inspector-General of Police (IG), Tunji Disu, and various zonal and state Police Commands, to tackle cable counterfeiting. He said the company had incurred significant costs supporting investigations and legal processes, including laboratory testing of suspected adulterated cables. According to him, Coleman was awaiting the conclusion of a case which could become the first in Nigeria in which a person would be convicted and jailed specifically for adulterating cables. Onafowokan said counterfeit cables were highly profitable because they were produced with reduced quantities and inferior materials but sold at prices close to those of genuine products. He said substandard cables could be 30 to 40 per cent less material in length, allowing counterfeiters to make excessive profits while putting consumers at risk. The Coleman CEO also called for greater government support for local manufacturers under the Nigeria First policy, noting that the company had benefited from increasing local-content opportunities in the oil and gas and telecommunications sectors. Also speaking, Coleman Executive Director, Michael Onafowokan, said SON had a critical responsibility to create an enabling environment for quality products while tackling counterfeiters. He urged the regulator to strengthen its enforcement efforts, noting that counterfeiting was increasingly taking place within Nigeria in addition to the importation of substandard products. The Chief Operating Officer, Mr. Ilori Sanusi, called on the federal government and the National Assembly to review existing laws and ensure that penalties for counterfeiting were commensurate with the seriousness of the offences. He argued that inadequate punishment could encourage offenders, stressing that penalties should be strong enough to serve as a deterrent

title: Ukraine strikes Russian air base hosting An-124, Il-76 transports
body: The Defense Forces of Ukraine struck the Seshcha military airfield in Russia’s Bryansk region, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine said in a statement published on Telegram on October 7, 2026. The General Staff said it was still assessing the extent of the damage. The statement did not say which weapons were used or what was hit at the base. The airfield was one of several Russian military targets Ukrainian forces struck on October 6 and overnight into October 7, inside Russia and in occupied areas of Ukraine, according to the statement. The same night, Russia launched a large missile and drone attack on Ukraine, during which Swedish Gripen fighters supported Polish air defense operations . Home to Russia’s An-124 transport regiment Seshcha is home to the Russian Aerospace Forces’ 566th Military Transport Aviation Regiment, which operates the An-124-100 Ruslan heavy transport aircraft. Аеродром Сєща. Кладовище "Русланів". https://t.co/TLhE3lP15s pic.twitter.com/vCgKAkXqWR — Зåступ барабøлі (@Hlopak_) May 20, 2020 Il-76 transports have also been based at the airfield. Satellite imagery published by Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty in April 2022 showed An-124 and Il-76 transports at Seshcha alongside fighter aircraft and helicopters. The imagery was published as Russian aviation was being relocated from Belarus following the withdrawal of Russian forces from northern Ukraine. Seshcha has also previously been used to launch Shahed-type strike drones. In 2023, Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat identified the airfield as one of Russia’s main Shahed launch sites, a role also reported by British military intelligence. Radar, electronic warfare and drone sites also hit Elsewhere in the Bryansk region, the Ukrainian General Staff said its forces struck a Russian electronic warfare station near Hrynovo and a radar station near Elionka. Near Russian-occupied Donetsk, Ukrainian forces hit a site used to store, prepare and launch strike drones, according to the statement. Drone command posts near Bilotserkivka and Kamianka in the Zaporizhzhia region were also targeted. The General Staff also reported strikes on Russian command and observation posts near Hirnyk, Ukrainske and Kurakhivka in the Donetsk region. In the occupied part of the Luhansk region, Ukrainian forces struck a command and observation post and logistics depot near Krynychne, as well as a fuel and lubricants depot near Kondriuche. The post Ukraine strikes Russian air base hosting An-124, Il-76 transports appeared first on AeroTime .

title: BREAKING: Three Children Rescued as Istanbul Building Collapses
body: Eight people, including three children, have been rescued from the rubble of a seven-storey apartment building in Maltepe, Istanbul, while rescue teams continue searching for six others, according to the latest statement from the Istanbul Governor’s Office. The building’s three lower floors collapsed at around 5:40am today on Dogu Street in the Cevizli district for reasons that remain unknown. Rescue teams evacuated residents who had become trapped on the upper floors. Risk of further collapse Rescue operations are proceeding with particular caution because of the building’s instability. Authorities have also evacuated neighbouring buildings, Istanbul Governor Davut Gul said. “The building is at risk. There is a possibility of collapse. The rescue efforts are being carried out in a controlled manner,” Gul said. Regarding those taken to hospital, he added: “No one’s life is in danger.” The Disaster and Emergency Management Authority (AFAD), firefighters, medical teams and police are operating at the scene. Environment and Urbanisation Minister Murat Kurum said rescue teams continue their efforts to locate those still trapped without interruption. Prosecutors launch investigation Authorities will investigate the cause of the collapse and the building’s permits as part of a judicial and administrative inquiry. According to the Istanbul governor, the apartment building was constructed in 1987 and contains 12 flats. Official records list 33 residents. The relevant prosecutor’s office has assigned a deputy chief prosecutor and two prosecutors to investigate the incident. The post BREAKING: Three Children Rescued as Istanbul Building Collapses appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: How 'Musk' director Alex Gibney became a critic
body:
Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk gestures on stage at the Capital One Arena after President-elect Donald Trump is sworn in as the 47th President of the United States in Washington, DC on Monday, January 20, 2025. Ken Cedeno/UPI/Alamy Live News hide caption
Some time ago, Alex Gibney got curious about how Elon Musk accumulated impossibly vast amounts of wealth and power.
So the Oscar-winning documentarian did what he does best, spending four years of deep research into Musk's world to create a film that's nearly as many hours long, each minute kept riveting by a trove of dreadful facts, videos, legal documents and interviews with people close to the tech entrepreneur.
"I started out as — if not an admirer — at least somebody who is sort of interested in what he was doing and liked it," Gibney told Morning Edition host Steve Inskeep.
Gibney, who narrates the film, says he was a "proud" owner of a Tesla Powerwall energy storage system at his home and Tesla solar panels on his roof.
But Gibney's perspective shifted as he prepared his film, Musk , which opens in theaters Friday. It's due to stream on HBO in a few months.
"I became increasingly resentful and angry. When [Defense Secretary] Pete Hegseth basically said that they were now going to use xAI to be fully integrated into the Department of War, it was like an out-of-body experience," he said, referring to the artificial intelligence company founded by Musk that's behind the Grok AI assistant.
Alex Gibney spent four years making his nearly four-hour film Musk . Jigsaw Productions hide caption
The leadup to the film's release has seen some controversy after Musk used several insults to describe Gibney — " an idiot " was among the mildest ones — and threatened a defamation lawsuit.
In a letter sent to Gibney's Jigsaw Productions company that emerged in September, Musk attorney Alex Spiro focused on an exchange between Gibney and Ashley St. Clair, a one-time MAGA influencer who had a child with the billionaire.
St. Clair describes in the film text messages Musk sent her before the November 2024 presidential election in which he said he was "feeling more optimistic" about Donald Trump winning because "tomorrow we unleash the anomaly in the matrix."
Musk further told St. Clair that he planned on tapping "'lasers' from space," adding that "I have over 10 thousand lasers in space right now."
In the film, Gibney asks St. Clair if she believes Musk's texts referred to satellites owned by his rocket company, SpaceX. She responds, "I don't know where else he has lasers."
NPR has obtained and authenticated the texts between Musk and St. Clair, which were sent on Oct. 6, 2024.
Spiro's letter, which NPR has also reviewed, says that Gibney made a "false" insinuation that SpaceX's Starlink satellites somehow uploaded votes for Trump in swing states, a debunked conspiracy theory.
"We don't claim that he changed votes in the 2024 election. All we do is to show that he was bragging to his lover that he had special access to understanding the outcome of the election in a way that other people didn't," Gibney told NPR. "Was he lying to her or was he just bragging or was he telling us something that we shouldn't know? I don't know. That's for the viewer to decide."
Gibney, who's previously investigated the likes of Enron and blood-testing startup executive Elizabeth Holmes in his films, said that when he trained his lens on Musk, he prepared for the possibility that the maverick CEO would try to sue him.
"We had a battery of lawyers reviewing everything that we did. I actually hired an independent fact checker to check our own fact checkers inside. So against the richest man, the truth is not always a defense, but I'm counting on his commitment to the principles of being a free speech absolutist."
Gibney also noted that a lawsuit would trigger a discovery process by which he could subpoena Musk's internal documents.
As he took a closer look at SpaceX and Tesla, Gibney noticed that while the two companies "had achieved great things technologically... their stock price was way out of proportion to their actual economic value." The filmmaker says Musk achieved this by overselling his products.
SpaceX performed a vital service, ferrying equipment into space and developing rockets that could be reused cheaply.
But the film says Musk cast the company as an even grander venture, forever about to colonize Mars.
Tesla made popular electric cars, but the film says Musk oversold them as self-driving.
According to the film, they weren't made with enough sensors for that, which is why some have crashed . " That's a level of overpromising that leans into fraud," Gibney said.
NPR has reached out to Spiro, Musk's attorney, about the specific claims made in the film but has not heard back.
The broadcast version of this story was produced by Kaity Kline .
NPR does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews. Anyone who makes such an offer or request is not an NPR employee and does not represent NPR.

title: Ijeoma Ude’s ShakaraSquare Sets Stage for Ankara Kids Fashion Show on October 10
body: Lagos is set to experience a vibrant fusion of colour, culture and runway style as ShakaraSquare.ng , under the leadership of its founder and convener, Ijeoma Ude, prepares to host the highly anticipated Ankara Kids Fashion Show on Saturday, October 10. The event promises to transform the runway into a lively celebration of African heritage, bringing together young runway talent, top fashion brands, and community support in the heart of the city. The showcase will star children aged five to 12, who will take to the runway in custom African print creations crafted by seven featured designers. Beyond the glitz of the catwalk, the event is designed to give young children a platform to build self-confidence, express their creativity, and connect with their cultural roots through contemporary African fashion. Speaking on the vision behind the initiative, founder and convener Ijeoma Ude emphasized that the fashion show extends far beyond aesthetics, serving as an empowering space for the next generation to proudly embody their identity. The dedication of participating mothers has been a central pillar of the event’s preparation, with many parents personally curating and providing the audition outfits that helped launch their children onto the runway. A creative lineup of fashion houses will present their collections during the show, including U-JAY Fashion, Prime Start Apparel Concept, Rose & Michell, RA-Jaz Clothiers, DE LOOK, BY CANDY Luxury Costumes, and Kingstrybe. Complete with professional makeup artists, custom accessories, and tailored styling, the production will offer a polished stage for each designer’s vision. The event has drawn strong backing from corporate institutions, local government, and lifestyle brands. Official sponsors include Kellogg’s Company, Zenith Bank Plc, Mikano International Limited, Amuwo Odofin Local Government, Lagos State Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture, Wendy’s Cold, Paddysco Sports Limited, and Stylenest Hair & Beauty. With final preparations underway, the ShakaraSquare Ankara Kids Fashion Show promises an engaging cultural experience for parents, fashion enthusiasts, and supporters of young Nigerian talent alike.

title: American, Russian officials meet on bringing US investor into Nord Stream gas pipeline to Germany
body: Top Russian and US officials, including US Special Envoy Jared Kushner, have held talks about bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream pipelines that delivered gas to Germany before Russia invaded Ukraine, five people with knowledge of the situation said.The discussions included Kirill Dmitriev, a close adviser to Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Kushner, the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump, the people said.Kushner, who has been trying to broker a truce between Russia and Ukraine, views doing business as central to restoring peace. Such a deal would enable US investors to profit from energy flows to Europe once the war ends.Dmitriev and Kushner have met in Moscow and New York in recent weeks. While it was unclear to what degree they discussed Nord Stream on those occasions, the topic remains on the agenda, two of the people told Reuters."Any deals will have to be negotiated by Russia with DFC (US International Development Finance Corporation) and Treasury and must benefit United States taxpayers and companies," a White House official said when asked about the pipeline discussions.There had been "no Nord Stream discussions recently," the official told Reuters.Dmitriev, who has campaigned for a resumption of Russian gas sales to Germany, met last month with US Energy and Treasury Department representatives to discuss potential US-Russia energy initiatives. A representative for Dmitriev declined to comment.It remains unclear how interested Washington is in pursuing the restarting of Russian gas flows to Germany, which is Europe's biggest energy consumer.A US official said that given the obstacles, a deal is unlikely in the medium term. The US and the EU have sanctioned the Nord Stream gas pipelines, making any restart illegal.Trump could waive or soften US sanctions, but if Democrats win control of Congress in next month's midterm elections, this would become harder.Germany and other European countries, which are spending billions of euros to rebuild their militaries to defend themselves from Russia, would strongly resist reopening Nord Stream.A spokeswoman for Germany's economy and energy ministry said Europe had sanctioned Nord Stream and Russian gas and that Germany had found alternatives. She said any reopening of the pipelines would require government approval, and that was not desired.Before Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Germany bought more than half of its gas from Russia through the two Nord Stream pipelines. They were mothballed after Moscow throttled supply to Europe and were blown up in a series of underwater explosions in September 2022.Europe distrusts Russia as Washington-Moscow talks continueTalks between Moscow and Washington are taking place against a backdrop of deep European mistrust of Russia's motives.Earlier this year, the heads of five European spy agencies told Reuters that Russia did not want to end the war quickly and was using US talks to push for business deals instead.Relations between Russia and Germany, which is among the biggest providers of military support to Ukraine, have hit a low ebb, as officials in Berlin have accused Russia of mounting a systematic campaign of hybrid attacks.Some German lawmakers say that business deals would bolster Moscow as it pursues war with Ukraine."This threatens to be a dirty deal that will cost Europe dearly," said Michael Kellner, a lawmaker who led German energy policy in the aftermath of the Ukraine invasion."Americans and Russians will share the profits," he said.While Germany's coalition government opposes restarting the pipeline, Alternative for Germany (AfD), the country's most popular political party, wants to do so.Dmitriev will meet the AfD leadership early next year to discuss selling Russian gas again.But selling ownership of the company that controls the Nord Stream gas pipelines to a US investor or restarting Russian gas faces hurdles.The company is 51% owned by Russian state energy giant Gazprom, with a further 31% split between two German entities and the rest in the hands of a French and a Dutch firm.The two German shareholders are seeking to keep their shares to maintain German influence if Gazprom sells its stake, another person said.Days after the Moscow meetings, Kushner said in Kyiv he had spoken to European counterparts about how the war pushed up energy prices, advocating "prosperity agreements" to encourage peace and give "leaders... something to look forward to."Germany, Europe split over potential Russia gas dealWhile a gas deal would please the Kremlin, it would split German public opinion, which is divided over buying Russian energy, and Europe, where Poland and the Baltic states are particularly vulnerable to Russia and reject energy ties.Poland's political leadership is watching the discussions to reopen the pipeline but remains firmly opposed, one person with knowledge of the government's thinking said.Kushner and Dmitriev have also been discussing the sale of a collection of businesses, from oil refineries to petrol stations in Europe and elsewhere, owned by Russian energy company Lukoil, two other people familiar with the matter said.Under that plan, a consortium of the DFC federal investment agency and investors from Qatar and the United Arab Emirates would buy the assets, while US authorities would lift sanctions, those people said."On Lukoil, Steve (Witkoff) and Jared (Kushner) worked with DFC to negotiate a substantial upfront payment and profits interest for the United States," said a White House official.Lukoil and Gazprom did not respond to requests for comment.

title: The Macallan Joins One Gidi Night Premiere to Celebrate Storytelling, Craft
body: Lagos came alive on Thursday night as One Gidi Night officially premiered at Silverbird Galleria, Victoria Island, bringing together members of the film industry, celebrities, media personalities, influencers and distinguished guests for an evening celebrating Nigerian storytelling, culture and entertainment. With The Macallan joining the celebration, the premiere brought together film, culture and a premium guest experience in one memorable evening. Written, produced and directed by filmmaker James Abinibi, One Gidi Night is a Lagos-set crime thriller that takes audiences through one dangerous night, exploring survival, desperation and ambition. The film features Gabriel Afolayan, Wunmi Toriola, Uzor Arukwe, Itele D Icon, Idia Aisien and other members of the cast. Inspired by Lagos and the unpredictability of everyday life in the city, the film explores what happens when ordinary circumstances take an unexpected turn. At its heart is a story about pressure, choices and consequences, with each character navigating their own version of survival. For Abinibi, the intention was not simply to tell a thriller, but to create an experience that keeps audiences engaged while giving them something to think about afterwards. The filmmaker describes wanting audiences to laugh, hold their breath, debate the film and ultimately reflect on the choices people make and where those choices can lead. The premiere brought that spirit to life, with guests stepping onto the red carpet before settling in for the highly anticipated screening. Beyond the film itself, the evening created space for conversations, connections and shared moments among members of the creative and entertainment community. The Macallan further complemented the evening with its premium hospitality experience, giving guests an opportunity to enjoy the whisky as they celebrated the film and the creative team behind it. More than a premiere, the night was a celebration of great storytelling, creative craftsmanship and the excellence that goes into bringing a compelling story from an idea to the screen. For a film built around the idea that the smallest decisions can lead to unexpected places, One Gidi Night leaves audiences with more than just a night of entertainment. It invites them to think about the pressures people face, the choices they make and how those choices can shape their journey.

title: WATCH: Downed Russian Jet Drone Crashes Near Kyiv Cars
body:
Dramatic video from Kyiv appears to show a burning Russian jet-powered drone falling from the sky and crashing within meters of cars during an attack on the Ukrainian capital.
The footage, published on Thursday, Oct. 8, by the local Telegram channel Ukraine Online , shows a flaming object descending rapidly toward an area occupied by several vehicles.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The channel identified it as a Russian jet-powered drone intercepted over the city. Kyiv Post could not independently verify the precise location, type of drone, or circumstances in which it was brought down.
No casualties or significant damage directly connected to the incident shown in the video had been officially reported at the time of publication.
The video emerged as Russian forces continued sending jet-powered drones toward Kyiv. Monitoring channels reported several such aircraft approaching and flying over different parts of the capital during the latest air raid.
Jet-powered models are faster and more difficult to intercept than conventional Shahed-type drones powered by propeller engines. Even after being hit by Ukrainian air defenses, their wreckage and undetonated warheads can pose a serious danger to people, buildings and traffic below.
Kyiv authorities regularly urge residents to remain in shelters until an official all-clear, warning that falling debris from intercepted missiles and drones can be deadly.
The clip was published following another Russian attack on Kyiv in which a drone struck a 12-story residential building in the Desnianskyi district. Four people, including two children, were injured, while rescuers evacuated 22 residents, including eight children.
Authorities have not said whether the falling drone captured in the video was connected to that strike.
Previous attack kills woman and hits apartment block
The footage emerged after Russian drones struck Kyiv on Wednesday, Oct. 7, causing casualties and damage in several districts of the capital.
In the Desnianskyi district, a Russian drone struck a 12-story residential building at the level of the 10th floor. The resulting fire spread to the upper floors and partially damaged the building’s structure. Four people, including two children, were injured, while rescuers saved 22 residents, among them eight children.
In the Obolonskyi district, authorities found the body of a woman near a burning car at a site where drone debris had fallen.
Officials have not said whether the falling drone shown in Thursday’s video was connected to either of those locations.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Property Testing with Agent Swarms
body:
Have agents build the machinery to find bugs in your repo, then let that machinery generate and check cases without spending tokens on each one. You can do this with ordinary coding agents, without access to a closed cybersecurity program. Writing reference implementations, generators, and assertions for every custom data structure and algorithm is now work you can hand to a swarm.
Pick a complex repo at work. Ask the people who know it well which parts worry them. Give a strong planning agent the property-testing skill from my agent-skills repo and those leads. It gives the agent methods for choosing targets, building reference models and generators, and turning failures into reviewable fixes. Target custom data structures, query planners, graph algorithms: complicated behavior with a simple way to check correctness.
I wanted to give this a proper test drive, so I ran it on Codex, jj, uv, Prometheus, Babel, and rv, mostly in the background alongside regular work. Including the original Router run, that’s more than 100 correctness findings . As of October 13, twelve of my fix PRs have merged : four in uv, three in Prometheus, and five in rv . Another Prometheus report was fixed by an upstream contributor , and OpenAI has confirmed a Codex fix for an upcoming release.
Codex alone produced fourteen distinct correctness reports . OpenAI builds it with its own frontier models, including unreleased versions. One example: start with abcd , enter Vim Replace mode, and type X . Before the pending key flushes, error recovery prints Xabcd ; the actual edit produces Xbcd . The recovery copy reconstructed the text but lost the editor’s mode. OpenAI confirmed a fix for 0.163.0 or 0.164.0 . The other reports have reproductions and proposed repairs in my fork , linked from upstream issues. Same public playbook.
The merged fixes include uv overrides losing optional-dependency guards , which could include a dependency even when neither extra activating it was requested; Prometheus returning a panic instead of its documented NaN on empty quantile input ; and histograms losing counter-reset metadata when reducing schemas .
Frank Noirot also read this post, pointed the skill at KittyCAD’s cloud-sync IndexedDB code, and found two bugs. Both fixes are merged: wait for transaction commit before acknowledging writes , and close connections after aborted cursor transactions . Both PRs credit the post and skill. The recipe transfers to other people, repos, and languages.
I also offered to run this on people’s repos in exchange for a donation to a trans charity. Joe Fabisevich took me up on it with $500 , so I ran it on Boutique , his Swift persistence library. That produced five PRs : one fix and four reproduction-only reports, all still open as of October 13.
I first did this at Apollo GraphQL on Router , our Rust GraphQL router, used in production by Intuit and Wayfair and already backed by thousands of unit and integration tests plus extensive snapshot testing. About three days of agents running in the background alongside my regular work turned up more than 30 correctness bugs in edge cases of internal data structures and algorithms. I supplied initial guidance and occasional nudges.
Have an agent write a simple reference implementation and assertions comparing it with the real one over generated operation sequences. Rust’s property-testing library proptest generates cases, checks assertions, and shrinks failures into smaller reproductions. A Vec and some O(n²) loops may be enough to check a heavily optimized implementation. Once built, this test suite can check as many histories as you’re willing to run.
Keep the sprawling discovery suite on its own branch. For each confirmed bug, have the agents produce a standalone PR with a regression test and a minimal fix.
I used Astra for planning, Sol to orchestrate, and Sols and Lunas to write proptests in parallel worktrees. Have the planner audit beyond your initial leads.
Compare cached metadata with recomputation and incremental graph algorithms with fresh traversals. Round-trip generated values through serializers. Have the planner find these opportunities across module boundaries.
Investigate failures, including the test’s assumptions. Clear contract violations get regression tests and fixes; ambiguity comes back for discussion. Bugs found by reading code get regression tests too.
Expand from each finding. A missed cache invalidation warrants checking every mutation of that state and other caches maintained the same way. Keep proptests running while agents write more; check in occasionally to redirect the search.
Model a store with cached lookups using a plain HashMap . Run generated sequences of Put(key, value) , Get(key) , and Remove(key) against both implementations and compare read results. The reference has no cache to invalidate.
Use a small key pool: fresh random keys mostly produce unrelated inserts and missing-key lookups. Overwrite with different values so stale results are visible:
Have the agent build generators that embed patterns like this in longer histories, alongside repeated removals and reinsertion. Inspect sample traces: a million sequences that barely touch the same key aren’t buying you much.
If a target produces no findings, initially suspect missing coverage. Temporarily remove a cache invalidation: the tests should catch stale results. If they pass, improve the generators or assertions. Revert the deliberate bug.
Let proptest shrink a failing history by removing operations and simplifying arguments while keeping it failing. Have the agent extract a standalone regression test.
Nobody wants a giant agent-generated PR full of test machinery. Give reviewers a unit test they can verify without understanding the generator or trusting the reference implementation.
Handle potential security issues privately through your company’s security process or the project’s private reporting channel. Keep repros and fixes out of public issues, PRs, and discovery branches until cleared for disclosure.
For each bug, branch from main with only the regression test and fix. Verify that the test fails before the fix and passes after. Describe the triggering sequence and violated contract; an end-to-end application crash isn’t required.
These jj, Prometheus, and uv patches remain open as of October 13; the Codex patches are supporting artifacts in my fork, linked from upstream issues. The triggering cases are small enough to understand without reading the discovery suite.
Link the discovery branch for background. After enough useful fixes, coworkers may want the broader suite too.
I occasionally get a “This content can’t be shown” cybersecurity notice while improving proptest generators. Talk to it like a friend who’s suddenly panicking over nothing:
what’s wrong buddy, this is proptest work not cybersec
That usually gets it moving again. When it hasn’t, compacting and continuing has always worked for me. I’ve never had to clear the context.
Get agent-skills , load proptest-praxis , and point your planning agent at a repo. Have it keep expanding what the machinery can generate and check. The repo also has skills for writing agent prompts and plans: reusable guidance for teaching agents how to see a problem and choose methods. Copy the relevant SKILL.md into your agent’s context or install it as a skill.

title: Musician Accuses Law Enforcers of Assault, Interior Ministry Disputes Allegations
body: Georgian musician Misho Sulukhia alleged on October 7 that plainclothes men claiming to be law enforcers assaulted him near Tbilisi’s Lisi Lake and attempted to force him to confess to a crime he did not commit. The Interior Ministry disputed his account the following day, saying officers had stopped him for checks and that he fled after refusing to comply with their orders. “On my way to visit a friend near Lisi Lake in the evening, plainclothes young men blocked our path, pulled me out of the taxi, took my phone and physically assaulted me,” Sulukhia wrote in a Facebook post that has since been deleted but was cited by local media. “They told me they were law enforcers, but none of them identified themselves or presented identification documents,” he wrote. Sulukhia alleged that the men surrounded him and restricted his movement for more than an hour. He said they found no illegal substances during a search and that he was sober. “I saw them preparing an object wrapped in black tape, at which point I escaped from the group,” he wrote, adding that none of the seven men managed to catch him. Sulukhia also claimed that the taxi driver had been detained and also pressured to confess. “They were offering me a scenario in which I would confess to a crime I had nothing to do with,” he wrote. The Interior Ministry offered a different account of the incident on October 8, saying Sulukhia, who it described as previously convicted of a drug-related offense and currently serving a suspended sentence, had been walking suspiciously through a wooded area near Lisi Lake when officers stopped him for police check. According to the ministry, Sulukhia refused to comply with lawful police orders, dropped his mobile phone and fled the scene. The ministry said officers secured and sealed the phone, along with a bank card found in its case, in accordance with established procedures. Authorities said administrative proceedings had been initiated under Article 173 of Georgia’s Code of Administrative Offenses, which concerns failure to comply with a lawful order from a law enforcement officer. The ministry’s statement did not address Sulukhia’s allegations of physical assault or his claims concerning the taxi driver. In a follow-up Facebook post on October 8, Sulukhia expressed concern that authorities could fabricate evidence to justify their actions, citing what he described as the concerns of lawyers and well-wishers. “They will prepare search warrants backdated to the previous day. Eight police officers will say whatever is needed to justify everything I went through,” he wrote. The musician’s allegations came shortly after another reported case of police abuse. On October 7, Sergey Kancheli, 23-year-old anti-government protester, said in a Facebook post that he had left Georgia after six police officers allegedly detained and assaulted him on September 27. Kancheli said the officers took him to a cemetery, scratched his face with a knife, threatened him with a gun and were pressuring him to engage in sexual act. He said he was now in a safe country. title: Kanye West received $20 million for canceled St. Petersburg concerts and is unlikely to return it, Kommersant reports
body: Rapper Kanye West, also known as Ye, received about $20 million for two canceled concerts in St. Petersburg, the Russian business daily Kommersant reported, citing sources familiar with the situation. “That’s not his net fee: that money also covers things like paying for his staff,” one of the publication’s sources said. Another source suggested that West would not return the money to the organizers, since his contract does not require it. Anna Subcheva, head of Say Agency, which organized the shows, told Kommersant that her company had not broken “a single law.” She said that after the concerts were announced, her company, she herself, and West faced a wave of negativity from competitors that also received support in the media. Asked by journalists whether the concerts might be held on different dates, Subcheva replied, “We’ll see.” Kanye West was scheduled to perform at Gazprom Arena in St. Petersburg on October 10 and 11. After the concerts were announced, lawmakers and pro-war activists began actively voicing discontent over the rapper’s visit to Russia. Whether to hold or cancel the concerts was even discussed in the Kremlin. A week ago, Say Agency announced it was canceling the shows, and the Russian concerts disappeared from West’s tour schedule. The same day, Kommersant reported that St. Petersburg police had opened a review of Say Agency for fraud. The collected materials would go to the Interior Ministry’s central office in Moscow, which would decide whether there were grounds to open a criminal case. The review was prompted by a complaint from a St. Petersburg Legislative Assembly member to whom ticket buyers had complained. The organizers claimed that more than 100,000 tickets, priced between 9,000 and 160,000 rubles, were sold in the first two days of sales. After the concerts were canceled, they promised to refund the money. At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. title: Hanwha Philly Shipyard to build MDA's new MRIV
body:
Hanwha Philly Shipyard (HPSI) has received a contract to build the Missile Defense Agency’s (MDA) new missile range instrumentation vessel (MRIV).
TOTE Service will serve as the construction manager (VCM) for the Missile Range Instrumentation Vessel (MRIV) program. The contract award is for up to three vessels, with one firm vessel being awarded at this time.
The MRIV design builds on the national security multi-mission vessel (NSMV) platform currently in production at Hanwha Philly Shipyard under TOTE Services’ management. The MRIV will share the NSMV hull design and substantial commonality with the existing platform, helping reduce design and construction risk.
HPSI will build the MRIV using the active production line, existing supply chain, and skilled workforce already in place from the NSMV program.
At approximately 160 meters in length, the new MRIVs will replace Pacific Tracker and Pacific Collector, which currently support missile range instrumentation missions and were constructed in 1965 and 1970, respectively.
“Hanwha Philly Shipyard is proud to bring our proven shipbuilding capabilities to a program that directly supports our nation’s security,” said David Kim , CEO of Hanwha Philly Shipyard.
“The MRIV program demonstrates the value of maintaining an active, capable U.S. shipbuilding industrial base, one that can take proven platforms, experienced people and established production infrastructure and put them to work for new and increasingly important missions. We are honored to continue our partnership with TOTE Services and to build these vessels here in Philadelphia.”
“Signing the Missile Range Instrumentation Vessel contract and executing the shipyard subcontract brings us closer to delivering the next generation of U.S. defense capability,” said Jeff Dixon , President of TOTE Services.
“Our proven Vessel Construction Management model means we’re hitting the milestones sooner and making meaningful progress faster.”
The vessel will be delivered to the Maritime Administration (MARAD), which will operate the vessel for the MDA.
The program comes as the United States places renewed emphasis on strengthening the nation’s maritime industrial base and expanding domestic shipbuilding capacity to support both economic and national security priorities.

title: Release climate, gender and environmental funds on time – CSOs urge government
body: Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) have called on the government to accelerate the release of funds allocated to climate action, gender-responsive programmes and environmental protection to ensure that budget commitments translate into tangible benefits for vulnerable communities. Kasa Initiative Ghana and ABANTU for Development, convening partners of the Kasa Initiative’s Gender and Climate Platform, said increased allocations in the 2026 Budget were commendable but would have limited impact if funds were not released on time and properly accounted for. The organisations made the call in a joint statement following their review of the 2026 Mid-Year Fiscal Policy Review presented to Parliament in July. They said the review showed significant gaps between allocations and actual releases for several programmes, raising concerns about the pace at which resources were reaching beneficiaries and frontline institutions. The organisations noted that the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) programme had received GHS485 million of its GHS1.1 billion allocation for 2026 by June, representing about 44 per cent. They said although LEAP had completed its 100th payment cycle and reached approximately 1.5 million individuals, with 226,930 households moved above the extreme poverty threshold following reassessment, the level of funding released remained below half of the annual allocation. Similarly, the Ghana School Feeding Programme, which currently supports more than 4.5 million pupils and over 34,000 caterers and cooks, had received GHS877 million of its GH¢1.98 billion allocation by June, also representing about 44 per cent. The organisations expressed particular concern about funding for the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS), saying only GH¢16 million, representing about 11 per cent of its GH¢150 million 2026 allocation, had been released by June. They said NAIMOS had intensified enforcement operations, recording 200 intelligence-led operations, 207 arrests and the seizure or destruction of 168 excavators and 2,800 Chanfang platforms. “Given the state of Ghana’s forests and water bodies, the pace of funding to frontline environmental enforcement agencies is inadequate,” the organisations said. They also raised concerns over the Government’s response to the June 2026 floods in Greater Accra. According to them, although Parliament approved GHS350 million from the Contingency Fund for emergency flood response, the money could not be accessed because the Fund was subject to a court garnishee order. This resulted in the Government reallocating GHS226 million from the existing budget of the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources, while a permanent solution to flooding had been deferred to the 2027 Budget. The organisations further called for greater transparency in budget reporting, citing the reporting of GHS915 million released for goods and services under the Ministry of Education as a combined figure for sanitary pads and the Capitation Grant. They said the absence of a disaggregated figure for the Free Sanitary Pads Programme made it difficult for citizens and civil society organisations to track how much had actually been spent on the initiative. However, they welcomed the implementation of the first phase of the Women and Youth in Aquaculture Programme, which is operating in 80 districts and benefiting 4,000 people organised into 80 cooperative groups. The organisations said Ghana’s economic performance provided some fiscal space for Government to improve the release of funds for climate and gender-related programmes. They cited real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of 6.4 per cent in the first quarter of 2026 and a primary balance surplus on both a cash and commitment basis as indicators of the economy’s improved fiscal position. They, therefore, urged the Government to prioritise investment in women farmers, fisherfolk, youth and climate-vulnerable communities, particularly in northern Ghana, coastal areas, forest-fringe communities, and flood-prone urban settlements. They also called for the institutionalisation of Climate and Gender Budget Tagging across all Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), as well as the publication of simplified annual reports showing allocations, releases, expenditure, and results. The organisations recommended the establishment of a national monitoring framework to track climate and gender outcomes rather than expenditure alone. They further urged Government to strengthen participatory budget monitoring through civil society engagement, Public Expenditure Tracking Surveys, and district-level accountability mechanisms. They called for the restoration and strengthening of ecosystem restoration programmes, including Tree for Life, with clear targets and reporting requirements. The statement also urged Government to accelerate the release of funds to NAIMOS and other frontline environmental enforcement agencies during the second half of 2026. On emergency funding, the organisations called for the Contingency Fund and other disaster-response resources to be protected from legal encumbrances to enable Government to respond promptly to emergencies. Kasa Initiative Ghana and ABANTU for Development said timely and transparent disbursement of budgeted resources was critical to ensuring that public spending delivered measurable outcomes for women, youth, and vulnerable communities. They reaffirmed their commitment, together with members of the Gender and Climate Platform, to monitoring public expenditure, generating evidence, and engaging policymakers throughout the 2027 Budget cycle.

title: NVIDIA PivotOPD Teaches Multi-Turn AI Agents to Recover From Pivotal Mistakes
body:
NVIDIA researchers, with Princeton University and the University of Maryland, have introduced PivotOPD , an on-policy distillation method for multi-turn LLM agents. PivotOPD on-policy distillation trains an agent to avoid its most damaging early mistake, and to recover when it happens anyway. Against 13 baselines, it posts the best average on ALFWorld, WebShop and Search-based QA for Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-8B students. The takeaway: recovery is learnable, and standard OPD rarely teaches it. TL;DR Size: A training method, not a model. Tested on Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-8B students, plus a Nemotron-3.5-SFT student on SWE-Bench Verified. Runs on: Trained on NVIDIA H100 nodes. Adds 0 inference cost, so the trained agent runs wherever its base model runs. Performance: First on all 8 per-benchmark averages against 13 baselines, across 3 seeds. Best: Recovers from 72.7% of replayed pivotal mistakes, vs 20.3% for standard OPD. Worst: 55.9% on ALFWorld “Look” tasks with the 1.7B student, vs 83.9% for SOD. Bottom line: Best: teaches recovery that outcome-only RL cannot reach. Worst: depends on replayable environments and a teacher whose pivots match the oracle in 77.8% of failed rollouts. What is a pivotal mistake in a multi-turn agent? A pivotal mistake is an action that lengthens the shortest remaining path to finishing a task, or makes it unsolvable. ALFWorld’s symbolic oracle measures this at every turn. Across Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3-235B-A22B, 59% of failed rollouts (155 of 262) contained one. The first pivotal turn arrived early, at a median of turn 8 to 12 out of 30. The agents then wasted 18 to 21 more turns without recovering. In replays of Qwen3-8B failures, correcting the pivotal turn raised success from 8% to 59%. Leaving the mistake in place and forcing the right action for the next 2 turns still reached 58%. Why does standard on-policy distillation miss it? Standard OPD lowered the held-out failure rate from 79% to 56%. Failures after a pivotal turn only fell from 51% to 49%. The correct action stayed below 1% probability at every pivotal turn, so 8 rollouts rarely sample it. Outcome-based RL shares the blind spot: if every rollout fails, the group-relative advantage is 0. How does PivotOPD work? PivotOPD adds 3 components to group-based RL, combined in a single PPO update. Pivot detection : A larger teacher model reads each rollout and its outcome in hindsight. It picks candidate turns and names a gold action at each. A turn counts as pivotal when the student’s action differs from the gold action. On ALFWorld, detected pivots land within 1 turn of the oracle’s pivot in 77.8% of failed rollouts on average. Preventive distillation (reverse KL) : A frozen copy of the student, hinted with the gold action, re-scores the student’s own response. This pushes the student away from the committed mistake. Recovery distillation (forward KL) : After each pivot, the teacher names a recovery action for up to K turns. The hinted self-teacher writes recovery responses, and the unhinted student trains on them. Forward KL is mass-covering, so it lifts actions the student almost never samples. The teacher only names actions. Token-level targets come from the student’s own hinted distribution. How does PivotOPD perform on agent benchmarks? With the 1.7B student, PivotOPD averages 73.7% on ALFWorld, 5.5 points above SDAR. It averages 44.5% on Search-based QA, 5.9 points above RLSD. On WebShop it beats RLSD by 1.2 in score but by 14.1 in success rate (76.6%). With the 8B student, it reaches 93.0% on ALFWorld, 47.4% on Search-based QA and 81.9% WebShop success. Margins are smaller, at least 1.8 points. With Qwen3-8B as its own teacher, PivotOPD still wins all 3 benchmarks by at least 1.5 points, 3.9 on average. On SWE-Bench Verified , a Nemotron-3.5-SFT student taught by Nemotron-3-Super went from 62.8% to 66.0%. Standard OPD reached 63.0%, and the teacher scores 73.0%. Recovery is the standout. Across 72 replayed pivotal mistakes, PivotOPD recovered 72.7% of the time, vs 8.3% for the base model, 20.3% for standard OPD and 45.8% for preventive-only. It averaged 9.7 turns to recover, against an optimal 6.2. #mtp-pivotopd-wrap iframe{width:100%!important;border:0!important;display:block;background:#111!important;border-radius:14px;}#mtp-pivotopd-wrap hr,#mtp-pivotopd-wrap p:empty,#mtp-pivotopd-wrap del,#mtp-pivotopd-wrap s{display:none!important;} Prev

The selected budget is K = 2 on ALFWorld and K = 1 on WebShop and Search-based QA. Key Takeaways Over half of failed agent rollouts hinge on 1 early, recoverable mistake. Standard OPD barely touches these failures: 51% to 49%. PivotOPD recovers from 72.7% of replayed mistakes, vs 20.3% for OPD. Best average against 13 baselines on ALFWorld, WebShop and Search QA. 0 inference overhead, but code is not yet released. Check out the paper and the project page . title: Ethiopia Unveils New Cabinet Reshuffle
body: women represent 41 percent Ethiopia’s House of Peoples’ Representatives on Thursday unanimously approved 22 ministerial nominees presented by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, formally establishing the Cabinet of the new Government. The nominations were submitted during the second regular session of the 7th parliamentary term. In one of the most closely watched changes, former Planning and Development Minister Fitsum Assefa (PhD) has been appointed Minister of Finance. She replaces Ahmed Shide, who was elected Speaker of the House of Peoples’ Representatives at the opening of the new parliamentary term. Fitsum had led the Ministry of Planning and Development for the past eight years. Former Ethio Telecom Chief Executive Officer Frehiwot Tamiru joins the Cabinet as Minister of Innovation and Technology. The government has also restructured several ministries: the Ministry of Planning and Development has been renamed the Ministry of National Strategy and will be headed by its former State Minister, Bereket Fissehatsion. The former Ministry of Transport and Logistics has been reconstituted as the Ministry of Logistics, with former Oromia Deputy President Sadat Nesha appointed to lead it. Several senior figures retain their previous portfolios, ensuring continuity in key sectors. Temesgen Tiruneh continues as Deputy Prime Minister. Gedion Timothewos remains Minister of Foreign Affairs, Professor Birhanu Nega stays on as Minister of Education, and Addisu Arega retains the Agriculture portfolio. Hana Arayaselassie continues as Minister of Justice, while Habtamu Itefa (PhD), Mekdes Daba (Dr.) and Aynalem Niguse remain at the helm of Water and Energy, Health, and Revenues, respectively. Other notable moves include the appointment of Mohammed Idris, previously Minister of Peace, as Minister of Defense, and Fisseha Yitagesu (PhD), former head of the Industrial Parks Development Corporation, as Minister of Industry. Former Tourism Minister Selamawit Kassa now leads the newly structured Ministry of Culture and Tourism, while Alemtsahay Paulos, previously a cabinet minister in the Prime Minister’s Office, has been appointed Minister of Mining. Shewit Shanka, who formerly served as Minister of Culture and Sport, becomes Minister of Women and Social Affairs. The new Cabinet brings in figures from parties that competed in the June 2026 general election. Musa Adem, chairman of the Afar People’s Party (APP), has been appointed Minister of Peace, while Education Minister Birhanu Nega is associated with the Ethiopian Citizens for Social Justice (EZEMA). Women account for nine of the 22 ministers (approximately 41 percent). The appointments also mark the first time a minister from the Harari Region has been named to a federal cabinet post. Additional appointments include Awelu Abdi as Minister of Labor and Skills, Yasmin Wohabrebbi as Minister of Trade and Regional Integration, Mohammed Abdurahman (Eng.) as Minister of Urban and Infrastructure, Sultan Weli (PhD) as Minister of Irrigation and Lowlands, and Aklilu Tadesse (PhD) as Minister of Youth and Sports. The Cabinet changes come with the formation of the new federal government following the opening of the seventh parliamentary term on October 5, when newly elected members were sworn in and Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed was re-elected and sworn into office for another five-year term. Full list of the newly approved ministers Gedion Timothewos (PhD) — Minister of Foreign Affairs Addisu Arega — Minister of Agriculture Fitsum Assefa (PhD) — Minister of Finance Mohammed Idris — Minister of Defense Birhanu Nega (Prof.) — Minister of Education Hana Arayaselassie — Minister of Justice Yasmin Wohabrebbi — Minister of Trade and Regional Integration Fisseha Yitagesu (PhD) — Minister of Industry Habtamu Itefa (PhD) — Minister of Water and Energy Mekdes Daba (Dr.) — Minister of Health Awelu Abdi — Minister of Labor and Skills Aynalem Niguse — Minister of Revenues Bereket Fissehatsion — Minister of National Strategy Selamawit Kassa — Minister of Culture and Tourism Alemtsahay Paulos — Minister of Mining Sadat Nesha — Minister of Logistics Shewit Shanka — Minister of Women and Social Affairs Musa Adem — Minister of Peace Frehiwot Tamiru — Minister of Innovation and Technology Mohammed Abdurahman (Eng.) — Minister of Urban and Infrastructure Sultan Weli (PhD) — Minister of Irrigation and Lowlands Aklilu Tadesse (PhD) — Minister of Youth and Sports With parliamentary approval secured, the new ministerial Cabinet now forms the core executive leadership of Ethiopia’s federal government for the coming five-year term.

title: AI coding agents and a rerun of the operating-system wars
body:
Photo source: Rod Long (@rodlong) | Unsplash
Attending the Agentic AI for Science workshop at MPCDF in Garching got me thinking about the platforms we are starting to build our scientific workflows around. The workshop programme brings together hands-on work with agents, examples from scientific software development and materials simulations, and perspectives from industry. For someone interested in free and open-source software, this raises some familiar questions: who controls those platforms, what can we change ourselves, and how much of our work can we take elsewhere?
The software development work discussed at the workshop is an example of agentic engineering , a term used by Simon Willison in his guide , Martin Fowler , and Andrej Karpathy . IBM also uses the term , as does the Linux Foundation's AGNTCon + MCPCon programme .
Coding agents use language models to generate code and tools to execute it, while engineers define the problems, guide the work, and verify the results. What interests me here is the software around the model. An agent harness supplies context, exposes tools to the model, and manages their execution. The flagship GPT, Claude, and Gemini models are proprietary, but the software using them does not have to be (and often isn't, as we will discuss below). We can use the same model through different harnesses, with different licenses, tools, and restrictions. Choosing the model, deciding where it runs, and choosing the harness are separate decisions, even when a product offering bundles them together.
A few harnesses and development environments for programming, scientific workflows, and other tasks illustrate these differences. This is only part of the picture: agents embedded in enterprise applications bring their own integrations and dependencies.
This led me to a somewhat loose comparison: Claude Code reminds me of Windows, Codex CLI of BSD, OpenCode and the like of Linux, and Antigravity of the Macintosh. Each comparison emphasizes something different: compatibility, permissive reuse, independence from suppliers, or the appeal of an integrated experience.
If you have used Claude Code in a terminal, the first part probably sounds wrong already. How does a program that reads files, invokes shell tools, and fits into a Unix workflow resemble Windows? Bear with me. The resemblance is in how people build tools and workflows around the software, rather than how its interface looks.
Windows was proprietary, but Microsoft very much wanted other developers to write software for it. The more applications were available, the more useful Windows became, and the more reasons users had to keep using it. Developers, in turn, had a reason to support Windows because that was where their users were. Having everyone build around your platform is a powerful position to be in.
I see a similar possibility with Claude Code. Anthropic controls the product, which is distributed under its commercial terms , while other developers can extend it through plugins containing skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers . Those servers expose tools and data to agents through the shared Model Context Protocol (MCP) . A proprietary product can attract a great deal of third-party software. Windows certainly did.
The more interesting part is what happens outside Claude Code itself. Suppose you maintain a competing harness and a user points it at a repository containing a CLAUDE.md file. You could ask the user to copy the instructions into your preferred format, but reading the existing file is more convenient. Sure enough, OpenCode supports CLAUDE.md as a fallback when no AGENTS.md exists , along with other Claude Code conventions.
Once enough people write instructions and extensions for one product, supporting those conventions becomes useful even to its competitors. The compatibility requirement can outlive the decision to use the original product. That is the Windows part of the comparison. The terminal interface is beside the point.
The advantage of existing tool support also influenced me when choosing between Markdown and reStructuredText for teaching materials . I preferred reStructuredText, but Markdown was supported by the tools my students and colleagues already used. The technically preferable option, from my perspective, lost to the one that was easier for everyone to work with.
Codex requires a little more care, since the name covers several different things. Here I mean Codex CLI , whose code is available under the Apache 2.0 license . OpenAI's overview distinguishes the open-source components from the proprietary ones.
Furthermore, Codex CLI can use custom providers and local models through Ollama or LM Studio . The endpoint and model need to be compatible with what the harness expects, but the CLI can be used independently of OpenAI's model service.
Why BSD, then? BSD grew out of work on Unix at the University of California, Berkeley , initially tied to AT&T's code and licensing, and eventually became freely redistributable in both source and binary form. Its descendants are useful operating systems in their own right, and their permissive licenses also allow their code to become part of proprietary products (as happened with FreeBSD code in Sony's PlayStation 4 ).
The BSD part is that someone can take the code and build their own product from it, including a proprietary one. OpenAI develops Codex CLI for its own offering, but others can modify and reuse it without having to release their changes as open source.
Codex has no equivalent of BSD's history of removing encumbered Unix code. Its permissive license does, however, allow a fork to make independence from proprietary services its central goal, rather than an alternative configuration. That would be a change in the project's direction, rather than a legal separation. A vendor can develop the software without having exclusive control over what others build from it.
OpenCode puts the choice of model provider near the center of its offering. Its documentation covers different model services, local models, and custom endpoints. You can keep the harness and change what it connects to.
The Linux comparison makes sense to me because users can choose between vendors without giving one supplier control over the whole workflow. Commercial interests are very much present (hello, Linux distributions), but users need not depend on any one supplier.
OpenCode does not have to occupy this position alone. Cline , Crush , and Maki fit into the same comparison, with different users preferring different interfaces and ways of working. The variety itself resembles the Linux world: there need not be one product that everyone agrees to use. These harnesses are separate implementations rather than distributions of a shared kernel, but the familiar disagreements about which one suits whom would fit right in.
The BSD and Linux comparisons overlap: OpenCode can also be permissively reused, and Codex CLI supports alternative providers. They emphasize different things, though. The BSD parallel concerns what others can build from the implementation; the Linux parallel concerns users choosing between suppliers. Codex is closely associated with OpenAI, while OpenCode presents provider independence as a reason to choose it.
Supporting multiple model providers does not, by itself, tell us how a project is governed or how users can influence its direction. Provider choice does, however, let you keep the harness while changing the model. For someone who wants to keep using a familiar workflow while changing suppliers, that is a useful property.
The Macintosh comparison adds another reason to choose a platform: how well it fits with everything else you already use. Continuity connects a Mac and an iPhone through features such as Handoff and Universal Clipboard, while AirPlay extends the picture to Apple TV. Each connection gives someone who already owns one Apple device another reason to choose the next one from Apple too. The integration is itself a reason to choose the product.
Antigravity brings the editor, terminal, browser, and Agent Manager into one development environment. Its competitors offer similar capabilities, so their presence alone does not distinguish Google's approach. The Macintosh comparison concerns how well Google brings them together with the services a team already uses.
The connections extend to Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, and Chat through Google's Workspace MCP servers. These currently require Developer Preview access, configuration, and OAuth authorization; using a Gemini model alone does not provide that access. For a team already using Workspace, a request to change a web page could begin in an email, refer to a specification in Docs, and finish with code changes and an email draft reporting the result. Google's documentation describes the tools for reading that data and taking actions, although a particular workflow still depends on permissions and agent behavior.
This approach can include open-source components. Apple has Darwin, WebKit, and Swift ; Google publishes the code for Antigravity's Python SDK under Apache 2.0 , although running it also requires a separately distributed compiled runtime. Neither example makes the complete system open source.
There is a useful limit to the comparison: competing harnesses, including Claude Code, can use those same MCP servers. A team can keep its Google services while changing its harness. The Macintosh-like bet is that the complete experience is convenient enough to make people choose it , even when the individual parts have alternatives. First-party integrations can make staying attractive, while shared protocols can make leaving easier.
Taken together, these examples show why a simple division into open and closed harnesses is insufficient. There are several freedoms involved, and having one does not automatically give us the others:
For example, a proprietary harness can support independently distributed extensions. An open-source harness can depend heavily on one company's services. A permissively licensed harness can become the basis for a proprietary product. These combinations should hardly surprise anyone familiar with the history of free and open-source software.
When I wrote about Microsoft's relationship with open source , I argued that opening individual components was only part of the issue. File formats, compatibility, and control over the surrounding platform mattered too. I think the same applies here. Having the source code is valuable, but we should also ask how much of our work we can take with us if we decide to leave.
Saying “I use Claude” leaves out part of the setup. Claude through Claude Code and Claude through OpenCode can have different tools, instructions, permissions, and ways of presenting results. Those instructions include built-in instructions supplied by the harness, as well as instructions supplied by the user or repository. Even with the same model, they can change how an agent approaches a task, uses tools, and decides when to ask for help. The model is only one part of the system doing the work. The harness determines which tools the model can request, how those requests are authorized and executed, and which results return to the model as context for its next step.
This makes models somewhat like processors and agent harnesses somewhat like operating systems. Changing the model can change behavior far more than replacing a processor with a compatible one, so I would not push that analogy too far. Still, it helps explain why choosing a model does not settle the choice of development environment.
Suppose a team has spent months building reusable skills, writing repository instructions, connecting internal tools, and agreeing on how to review agent-generated changes. Changing a model setting might take a minute. Moving all of that to a different harness and checking that it still works as expected could take considerably longer.
The model could become easier to replace while the workflow becomes harder to move. Some of that is ordinary migration work, which also exists between independent open-source tools.
