title: Greece Sets New Rules on Equal Pay and Salary Transparency
body: New rules on pay transparency, equal pay for women and men, and worker protection will take effect in Greece on November 1, 2026, under a new circular from the Ministry of Labour and Social Security. The circular provides guidance on the implementation of Law 5316/2026, which incorporates EU Directive 2023/970 into Greek law. It outlines employers’ obligations and workers’ rights while providing businesses with practical tools and examples of good practices. The rules apply to private-sector employers, employees and job applicants who fall within the ministry’s jurisdiction. Salary structures based on objective criteria From November 1, all employers, regardless of the number of people they employ, must establish and apply salary structures that ensure equal pay for equal work or work of equal value. Employers must document the structures in writing, allow comparisons between different positions, establish a review procedure and clearly define the components of pay for each employee category. Employers must base job evaluations on objective and gender-neutral criteria. Where employee representatives exist, the parties must agree on the criteria. The criteria must take into account skills, effort, responsibility and working conditions. Employers may also consider other factors relevant to a particular job or position, such as seniority and relevant non-technical skills. Employers covered by a collective labour agreement may use the job categories and salary scales established by that agreement. Pay transparency before hiring The circular prohibits references to gender or marital status, as well as criteria or information that could result in direct or indirect gender discrimination, in job advertisements, announcements, recruitment notices and regulations concerning the selection of candidates. Job applicants have the right to receive information from prospective employers before their first interview about the starting salary or salary range for the position, based on objective and gender-neutral criteria. They must also receive information about any collective labour agreement provisions applicable to the position. Workers gain access to pay information Employees can submit a written request for information about their individual pay level and the average pay levels, broken down by gender, for employees performing equal work or work of equal value. Employers must provide the information within a reasonable period and, in all cases, within two months of the request. Employers must also inform their staff annually about this right and explain how employees can exercise it, while complying with personal-data protection and confidentiality rules. Support for businesses The circular includes a model salary structure and practical tools to help businesses comply with the new requirements. These include the FAIR PAY pay-gap calculator and the European Institute for Gender Equality’s toolkit for gender-neutral job evaluation, which provides employers with a step-by-step guide for creating or reviewing systems for evaluating and classifying jobs. Pay-gap reporting for companies with 100 or more employees Companies with at least 100 employees face additional reporting obligations concerning the gender pay gap. Employers must provide the Ombudsman with information including: the overall gender pay gap; the gender pay gap for supplementary or variable pay; the overall median gender pay gap; the median gender pay gap for supplementary or variable pay; the percentage of female and male employees receiving supplementary or variable pay; the percentage of female and male employees in each pay quartile; and the gender pay gap within each employee category, broken down by ordinary basic pay and supplementary or variable pay. Employers with 250 or more employees must submit the information by June 7, 2027, and annually thereafter. Employers with 150 to 249 employees must submit the information by June 7, 2027, and every three years thereafter. Employers with 100 to 149 employees must submit the information by June 7, 2031, and every three years thereafter. Employers must also provide the relevant pay-gap information to employees and their representatives. At the request of the Labour Inspectorate or the Ombudsman, employers must provide the information within two months. Where available, they must also provide information covering the previous four years. Joint pay assessment A joint pay assessment becomes mandatory when three conditions occur simultaneously: women and men have a difference of at least 5% in average pay within any employee category, objective and gender-neutral criteria do not justify the difference, and the employer has not corrected the difference within six months of submitting the relevant information. The assessment aims to identify, correct and prevent unjustified pay differences. It includes an analysis of the proportion of women and men in each employee category, average pay levels and supplementary or variable pay, and the reasons for any differences based on objective and gender-neutral criteria agreed by the employer and employee representatives. It also examines improvements in pay following maternity, paternity, parental or carers’ leave and identifies measures to address unjustified pay differences. The assessment must also evaluate the effectiveness of measures introduced following previous joint pay assessments. Protection for workers The circular also clarifies the judicial and administrative protections available to workers, including the right to full compensation for employees affected by unequal pay. It sets out procedures for resolving related labour disputes through the Labour Inspectorate, with the participation of the Ombudsman. Workers will also receive protection against retaliation and adverse treatment because they have taken action to secure their right to equal pay. The post Greece Sets New Rules on Equal Pay and Salary Transparency appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Terrorist killed as police repel attack in SE Iran
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 08 (MNA) – One terrorist attacker was killed and several others wounded after police forces responded forcefully to an attack on a patrol in Golshan county, Sistan and Baluchestan province.
The Sistan and Baluchestan police information centre announced that, following an explosion along the exit route of two police units from the county police command headquarters in Golshan, shootings by armed individuals subsequently took place, which were met with a fierce and forceful response from police forces.
Following the readiness and rapid reaction of the police forces, one of the terrorist attackers was killed, and a number of other armed elements were wounded.
The area is under the monitoring and surveillance of security and police forces, and measures to identify and deal with other elements involved in this terrorist act are continuing.

title: MAA, KSrelief sign joint implementation programme for 20 solar-powered boreholes in Ghana
body:
Markaz Aleawn Alyaqin Humanitarian Services (MAA) and the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief) have signed a Joint Implementation Programme (JIP) for the construction of 20 solar-powered boreholes across five regions of Ghana.
The JIP was signed at the KSrelief headquarters in Riyadh and will be implemented over a period of eight months, benefiting an estimated 76,555 people in schools and communities.
The beneficiary locations include Asawase M/A Cluster of Schools, Sepe Cluster of Schools, Akrom Cluster of Schools, Garden City Special School, Sakafia Islamic Senior High School, Parkoso Senior High School, Kumasi Academy, New Konkrompe Senior High School and the University of Energy and Natural Resources (UENR).
Other beneficiary communities include Techimantia, Vea, Bongo Gurigo, Kudorogo, Kofiase, Bepoase, Sawua, Kokoado, Homabenase, Badaase and Aboabo No. 1–4, among others.
Under the programme, each facility will comprise a solar-powered borehole, a 10-cubic-metre water storage tank and six water taps, providing sustainable access to safe water for drinking, sanitation, hygiene and other essential needs.
The project forms part of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s continuing humanitarian and relief efforts through KSrelief, which extend to communities in need around the world and seek to provide sustainable solutions that contribute to improving living conditions.
Markaz Aleawn Alyaqin Humanitarian Services has expressed its sincere gratitude to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince and Prime Minister, for their continued support for humanitarian and relief efforts worldwide.
MAA also extended its appreciation to Dr Abdullah A. Al-Rabeeah, Advisor at the Royal Court and Supervisor General of KSrelief, and Eng. Ahmed bin Ali Al-Baiz, Assistant Supervisor General for Operations and Programs, for their continued commitment to humanitarian service and cooperation.

title: Greek Scientists Join Global Hunt for Cosmic Neutrinos
body: The search for astrophysical neutrinos has become a global effort stretching from the ice of Antarctica to the depths of the Mediterranean, with Greek scientists contributing to the KM3NeT neutrino telescope. This year’s Nobel Prize in Physics recognises Francis Halzen for his decisive contribution to IceCube, the cosmic-neutrino telescope embedded in the Antarctic ice. However, IceCube is not the only observatory studying the Universe through neutrinos. Scientists are developing a corresponding telescope deep beneath the Mediterranean Sea through the KM3NeT experiment, which includes Greece’s National Centre for Scientific Research “Demokritos”. In February 2025, KM3NeT made the cover of Nature after detecting KM3-230213A, the highest-energy cosmic neutrino ever observed. Its energy was 30 times higher than that of any previously detected neutrino. The discovery also provided the first evidence that the Universe produces neutrinos at such extreme energies, offering information about violent events beyond the Milky Way. “Astronomy through neutrinos is only just beginning,” Aikaterini Tzamarioudaki, research director at the Institute of Nuclear and Particle Physics at NCSR “Demokritos” and a member of the KM3NeT experiment, told the Athens-Macedonian News Agency (AMNA). Until recently, scientists mainly studied the Universe through two types of messengers: photons and charged particles, or cosmic rays. Neutrinos offer a new way to investigate the origins and nature of cosmic rays because they do not bend under interstellar magnetic fields and are not absorbed along their journey. Combining information from different messengers also provides a powerful new tool for understanding the processes taking place in astrophysical phenomena across the Universe, Tzamarioudaki said. Neutrinos: The Invisible Messengers Neutrinos are tiny subatomic particles with extremely small masses and no electric charge. They can travel virtually unhindered from the most distant regions of the Universe. Although neutrinos rank as the second-most abundant particles in the Universe after photons, they interact only minimally with matter. As a result, billions pass through the human body every second without leaving a trace. Neutrinos emerge across a vast range of energies and through many different processes. The Sun produces enormous numbers of low-energy neutrinos through nuclear fusion, while much smaller numbers of high-energy neutrinos originate from particle collisions during catastrophic cosmic events, including stellar explosions and black-hole activity. Because their journeys remain largely undisturbed, neutrinos act as cosmic messengers, carrying information directly from their astrophysical sources to detectors on Earth. From Antarctica to the Mediterranean Detecting cosmic neutrinos requires enormous observatories positioned deep beneath water or embedded in ice. These instruments search for faint flashes of light that reveal the particles’ presence and can help scientists identify and interpret violent astrophysical events. Nobel laureate Francis Halzen proposed using ice to detect high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and his contribution proved decisive in developing IceCube in Antarctica. In 2013, IceCube detected 28 high-energy neutrinos originating beyond the Solar System, providing the first confirmed evidence of neutrinos of astrophysical origin. Since then, IceCube has reported strong evidence of neutrino emissions from two galaxies as well as from the Milky Way. Europe’s corresponding cosmic-neutrino detection infrastructure lies beneath the Mediterranean Sea: the KM3NeT neutrino telescope. Construction remains underway and is expected to finish in 2030. KM3NeT consists of two detectors: ARCA, positioned in the deep waters off Sicily, and ORCA, located near the coast of Toulon in France. ARCA targets high-energy neutrinos from galactic and extragalactic sources and detected the highest-energy cosmic neutrino ever observed. Once completed, the detector will occupy a volume of one cubic kilometre. The scale of its achievement is particularly significant because KM3NeT detected the record-breaking neutrino with only one-tenth of ARCA’s final configuration. Tzamarioudaki said KM3NeT/ARCA’s exceptional ability to determine the direction of neutrinos will contribute not only to detecting high-energy neutrinos but also to identifying their astrophysical sources and improving scientists’ understanding of violent phenomena in the Universe. The experiment follows three completed pilot projects aimed at detecting neutrinos. One was the Nestor experiment, conducted at Pylos in Greece, while the other two took place in southern France and Sicily. The international KM3NeT scientific collaboration brings together more than 360 scientists from 68 institutions across 22 countries, including NCSR “Demokritos”. Italy’s National Institute for Nuclear Physics (INFN), a KM3NeT partner responsible for collecting data from ARCA, said this year’s Nobel Prize in Physics represented significant recognition for the entire neutrino-physics and astroparticle-physics community. The NCSR “Demokritos” Institute of Nuclear and Particle Physics team involved in the research includes Institute Director Christos Markou, Tzamarioudaki, researcher Evangelia Drakopoulou, technical staff and students. The Greek team plays a key role in constructing and operating KM3NeT, analysing its data and managing the experiment. The post Greek Scientists Join Global Hunt for Cosmic Neutrinos appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Major Superiors gather in Wa to chart future of consecrated life
body: Leaders of Catholic religious institutes and consecrated men and women from across Ghana have gathered in Wa for a week-long plenary assembly to reflect on the future of consecrated life and strengthen the Church’s mission in a changing society. The Biannual Plenary Assembly of the Conference of Major Superiors of Religious, Ghana (CMSR-Gh), is taking place from 4 to 10 October 2026 at the In-Service Training Centre in the Diocese of Wa. Held under the theme, “Synodal paths to mission sustainability: Walking together in hope”, the assembly brings together religious leaders, consecrated persons and other collaborators for prayer, reflection, dialogue and discernment on their service to the Church and society. Opening the assembly on Tuesday, 6 October, CMSR-Gh President Sr Dr Lucy Hometowu, SMMC, called for stronger collaboration among congregations, saying their different charisms, traditions and apostolates should serve as a source of strength rather than division. “The time has come for us to move beyond simply working alongside one another to genuinely walking together,” she said. Call for greater collaboration Sr Dr Hometowu urged consecrated persons to pool their gifts, experience, personnel and resources to respond more effectively to contemporary challenges. “No single Congregation can respond adequately to all the needs of our time. But when we bring our gifts, experiences, personnel and resources together, we can accomplish much more,” she said. She identified formation, vocation promotion, youth empowerment, safeguarding, ecological justice, healthcare, education, pastoral ministry, social transformation and communication as areas for greater collaboration. Other priorities included caring for elderly and infirm clergy and consecrated persons, as well as managing resources sustainably. She said the CMSR-Gh offered a platform for members to learn from and support one another, while discerning how best to serve the Church and society. Wa Diocese welcomes participants The Bishop of Wa, Most Rev Francis Bomansaan, M.Afr., welcomed participants to the diocese, describing them as co-workers in the vineyard of the Lord. In an address read on his behalf by the Vicar General of the Wa Diocese, Very Rev Fr John Kunpiel, the bishop expressed appreciation for the various charisms and contributions of congregations serving in Ghana. He described the assembly as an opportunity for renewal, reflection on the prophetic and apostolic role of consecrated persons, and stronger collaboration in evangelisation. “This Biannual Conference, my dear brothers and sisters, is more than a meeting. It is a moment of renewal,” he said. Bishop Bomansaan said the theme was timely as the universal Church continued implementing the synodal process. He encouraged participants to practise “working together, listening together, discerning together, and acting together”. He urged them to listen deeply to God and one another during their time in Wa, and to return to their communities with renewed zeal, fresh vision and stronger bonds of fraternity. Mission should outlive its leaders Delivering the keynote address, Franciscan priest and academic Friar Dr Joseph Kwame Blay challenged the Major Superiors to look beyond maintaining existing projects and structures and consider how the Church’s mission could endure beyond the current generation of leaders. He said schools, hospitals, social care institutions and church buildings established by religious institutes were means through which the Church participated in Christ’s mission, rather than the mission itself. “The mission belongs to Christ. We are stewards, collaborators and servants of a mission that precedes us and will outlive us,” he said. Fr Blay explained that a sustainable mission required the transmission of faith, charism, competence and responsibility from one generation to the next. “A mission can have money and still be unsustainable. It can have buildings and still be unsustainable. It can have vocations and still be unsustainable,” he said. He outlined the spiritual, vocational, leadership, institutional, charismatic, financial and material dimensions of sustainability, urging religious institutes to prepare successors deliberately. He warned that a leadership system dependent on one strong individual was fragile and called for a culture that developed people, shared responsibility and prepared the next generation. “The real test of a missionary is not only what happens while he or she is present, but what remains when he or she is gone,” he said. From individual projects to shared mission Fr Blay also called for a shift from an ego-centred approach to mission towards one rooted in Christ and collaboration. He urged religious institutes to strengthen local responsibility, invest in indigenous vocations, develop succession plans, build networks among congregations and explore sustainable economic models without allowing financial considerations to overshadow their mission. He also advocated stronger cooperation between religious institutes and dioceses, saying they had complementary roles in sustaining the Church’s mission. “The question, therefore, should not be: Who owns the mission? But: How can the bishop, diocesan clergy, religious and lay faithful together sustain Christ’s mission entrusted to this local Church?” he said. According to him, the future depended on moving from “mission done for people” to “mission done with people”. The assembly continues until 10 October, with participants reflecting on the challenges and opportunities facing consecrated life and its contribution to the Church in Ghana.

title: President Sheikh Mohamed and Syria's Al Shara discuss regional security in call
body: President Sheikh Mohamed and Syrian President Ahmad Al Shara stressed the need to bolster security and stability in the region during a phone call on Thursday. The two leaders discussed the implications of the latest developments in the Middle East and underlined the importance of serving the interests of all people in the region, state news agency Wam reported. The discussions come amid heightened tension in the Gulf after drone and missile attacks on King Khalid International Airport and Abha International Airport in southern Saudi Arabia killed three people and injured 36 others, the kingdom's General Authority of Civil Aviation said. Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for the strikes, which have also raised concerns about the impact of the conflict on air travel. Sheikh Mohamed and Mr Al Shara also discussed bilateral relations and explored ways to further expand co-operation , with a focus on economic and development sectors. Advancing UAE-Syria ties The two sides have taken significant steps to strengthen ties between their nations. In September, Sheikh Mohamed and Mr Al Shara held high-level talks in Abu Dhabi as part of the Syrian leader's working visit to the Emirates, where he took part in the in the 24th Arab Media Summit in Dubai . Central to their discussions was a recent visit by a UAE economic delegation to Syria, which both sides highlighted as a significant step towards establishing frameworks for economic recovery. The leaders said the visit had helped lay the groundwork for strategic partnerships and projects aligned with both countries' development goals. Abu Dhabi-based Eagle Hills is working on two major projects in Syria including a residential and tourism development as part of a framework agreement the company has signed with the Syrian government. Total investment in the two projects in Damascus and Latakia has not been disclosed but Syria 's Arab News Agency reported they will create more 40,000 jobs. The Central Bank of the UAE last week agreed to deepen bilateral co-operation with regulators in Syria and Morocco, focusing on key areas to boost financial stability and technology. The preliminary agreement with the Central Bank of Syria includes a framework for building technical expertise for payment systems, monetary policy, cash management and financial technology, the CBUAE said in a statement on Friday. On Friday, Latakia Racecourse in Syria will host the UAE President's Cup for Purebread Arabian Horses, in a further demonstration of the robust links between the countries. The showpiece race will be held as part of the two-day UAE-Syrian Festival, which gets under way on Friday and features 15 races for purebred Arabian horses.

title: Thursday, 8 October 2026
body: Armenia Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has classified the Shaki incident as a ‘regular criminal incident’. Pashinyan argued that it could have ended differently if Ani Avetisyan, the woman injured by the Azerbaijani soldier, had waited for police to arrive. He also said the detained soldier will serve at least part of his sentence in Armenia. At the same time, Defence Minister Suren Papikyan acknowledged that there were shortcomings related to the incident that will have consequences. He also added that the soldier did not resist when he was arrested, which showed that he had not crossed the border on purpose as part of a planned mission. The founder of the Adequate party, Artur Danielyan, has been arrested for a Facebook post. The Investigative Committee claimed he defamed the National Security Service by suggesting that the Azerbaijani soldier was not acting alone. Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan has concluded his official visit to Iran. Mirzoyan noted that Iran was satisfied with the Trump Route and was willing to discuss all issues and economic opportunities that it would provide. A manager of a popular restaurant in Yerevan, Gustav, has been caught secretly filming customers in the restaurant’s unisex bathroom. The restaurant says he has been fired, while the Interior Ministry says criminal proceedings are underway. A teacher who was filmed beating a student in Gegharkunik has been detained . The paintings confiscated from detained former Finance Minister Gagik Khachatryan will now be available to the public. Khachatryan’s defence team has argued that the exhibit violates Khachatryan’s right to privacy. Azerbaijan A court has sentenced the former advisor to the US-based German Marshall Fund to seven years and six months in prison. Mehriban Rahimli was charged in the NGO case, but the sentence was suspended for a probation period of four years. The government has approved new ‘secular’ dress code requirements for public school. Teachers’ clothing and accessories must ‘comply with the principle of secularism in general education’, while school administrations will be responsible for monitoring compliance with the requirements. Georgia Civil activist Sergei Kancheli has said he left Georgia after police officers allegedly assaulted him at a cemetery. According to Kancheli, on 27 September, the officers scratched his face with a knife and threatened him with a gun, pointing it at his head, chest, and other parts of his body. He also said they ‘forced’ him to have ‘sexual intercourse’. Kancheli added that the abuse lasted for around 50 minutes, after which the officers left the scene. He said he has filed a lawsuit and plans to continue seeking justice against those responsible. The Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association (GYLA) says that the Special Penitentiary Service has obstructed Giorgi Davitaze’s lawyer from taking notes while meeting his client. Davitadze has accused staff at Rustavi Prison No 6 of raping him, claims the prison service denies. Detained opposition politician Aleko Elisashvili said yesterday that inmates at Rustavi Prison No 6 had staged a protest in solidarity with Davitadze. Elisashvili said several inmates had also self-harmed in protest. According to Elisashvili, the situation at the prison remains tense. Singer Misho Sulukhia has claimed that unidentified men in civilian clothes stopped and assaulted him near Tbilisi’s Lisi Lake and demanded that he confess to a crime. The Interior Ministry told OC Media that Sulukhia was moving suspiciously in a wooded area, failed to obey a police order, dropped his phone, and fled. The ministry said his phone and bank card were sealed as evidence and an administrative case was opened for disobeying a police order. Economy Minister Mariam Kvrivishvili has been promoted to Deputy Prime Minister. Yesterday, Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze thanked Kvrivishvili and the ‘economic team’ for their work in several areas, including strengthening economic cooperation with China, reducing external debt, and ‘maintaining and ensuring sound fiscal indicators’. Abkhazia President Badra Gunba congratulated Russian President Vladimir Putin on his birthday yesterday. ‘In our country, you enjoy unquestioned authority and deep respect. The people of Abkhazia remember well and highly appreciate the support you have provided to our republic over many years’, Gunba said. South Ossetia Oleg Gagiev has been appointed head of the Interior Ministry’s Economic Crimes Department. Gagiev previously worked in economic crime units in North Ossetia. Yesterday, four people suffered from carbon monoxide poisoning in two separate incidents. In both cases, the victims were hospitalised , but are in a stable condition. The North Caucasus Chechen Head Ramzan Kadyrov has received the Honorary Architect of Russia award. Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin presented Kadyrov with the award during the opening of the Akhmat-Khadzhi Kadyrov Boulevard in Grozny’s Putin district, stating it was for ‘significant contributions to the development of architecture and urban development’ in Russia and Chechnya. Kadyrov has at least 78 other awards and titles, Caucasian Knot has recorded. Russia’s Interior Ministry has placed a former employee of Kabarda–Balkaria’s Russian National Guard (Rosgvardiya) Directorate on a wanted list. According to Mediazona , Shamil Uchev, 38, has been linked to the Arbitrum financial pyramid scheme, in which at least 50 people have been recognised as victims and the damages estimated at ₽70 million ($820,000). Uchev is now reportedly based in Bali. The brother of the former Daghestani Head Ramazan Abdulatipov has been released from prison early . Rajab Abdulatipov was originally detained in September 2018, and in March 2021, he was sentenced to 12 years in a maximum-security prison after being found guilty of bribery and fraud. The head of the republic’s Public Monitoring Commission, Shamil Khadulaev, did not specify the grounds for Apdulatipov’s early release, though speculation has arisen that he was either released on parole, or that his prison sentence was commuted to forced labour. For ease of reading, we choose not to use qualifiers such as ‘de facto’, ‘unrecognised’, or ‘partially recognised’ when discussing institutions or political positions within Abkhazia, Nagorno-Karabakh, and South Ossetia. title: Rafael and Raytheon deliver first Iron Dome interceptor made entirely in America to Israel
body: The companies established the plant through their Raytheon-Rafael Area Protection Systems (R2S) joint venture to build manufacturing capacity in the United States. The factory expands a partnership that has supported Tamir production for more than a decade under U.S. workshare requirements for Iron Dome. IMDO Director Moshe Patel said the production line forms part of efforts to accelerate manufacturing across Israel’s missile defense systems. Rafael said the facility creates American jobs and strengthens the U.S. defense industrial base. “As part of IMDO’s efforts to accelerate production across all missile defense systems, this new production line represents a significant step in strengthening the shared production capabilities of Israel and the United States,” Patel said. “U.S. BMD funding for U.S.-Israeli cooperative missile defense programs, including emergency supplemental funding, is reinvested in the U.S. industrial base, strengthening production capacity, deepening our partnership with MDA and the U.S. Government, and enhancing both nations’ ability to protect their citizens.” Tamir was developed under IMDO’s leadership, with Rafael as prime contractor, and serves as Iron Dome’s interceptor. According to Rafael, Iron Dome has recorded more than 10,000 operational interceptions in 15 years of service. “Today, for the first time, Tamir is being built outside Israel, here in Camden,” said Shlomo Toaff, Rafael’s executive vice president and head of its Air and Missile Defense Division. “We are proud to have turned this facility into a working production line.” “For the customers who depend on Tamir, that means another reliable source,” Toaff said. “For the U.S. Marine Corps, it supports SkyHunter.” IMDO is responsible for the Israeli Air Force’s air and missile defense architecture and works with the U.S. Missile Defense Agency on cooperative programs. Together with the agency and defense companies in both countries, it leads the development and co-production of David’s Sling and Arrow, and the co-production of Iron Dome. Arkansas Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders attended the ceremony alongside U.S. Missile Defense Agency Deputy Director and Acting Director for Test Maj. Gen. Jason D. Cothern. Israeli military and diplomatic officials, Patel, Toaff and R2S CEO Jonathan Casey also attended.

title: Middle East flights: Singapore Airlines, Scoot and Wizz Air extend suspensions
body: International airlines continue to adjust schedules for Middle East flights as airspace restrictions linked to the Iran war persist. Against the backdrop of continuing geopolitical uncertainty across the region, here's how airlines are adapting their operations. Wizz Air Wizz Air has postponed the planned restart of its Abu Dhabi and Dubai routes, cancelling all flights to and from both destinations for the winter season. “Regional airspace restrictions extended on September 30 require significantly longer routings to these destinations, increasing flight times and costs and making both A321neo and A321XLR operations commercially unviable under current conditions,” the airline told The National . Wizz Air also said flights to and from Amman are affected by the EU Aviation Safety Agency's latest conflict zone information bulletin, which recommends that airlines do not operate within Jordanian airspace at any altitude. Singapore Airlines Singapore Airlines flights to Dubai were scheduled to resume on August 2, but the suspension has been extended until December 1. “As the situation remains fluid, other flights may be affected,” the airline said on its website. “Customers affected by cancellations will be reaccommodated on alternative flights or can seek a full refund of the unused portion of their ticket.” Scoot The low-cost subsidiary of Singapore Airlines has suspended its flights from Singapore to Jeddah until December 2. Customers affected by cancellations may request a full refund if they choose not to continue with their travel or rebook on alternative Scoot flights, the airline said. Air Canada Air Canada has extended the suspension of its flights to Tel Aviv and Dubai until the end of March 2027. Passengers affected by the cancellations are advised to check directly with the airline for rebooking and refund options as schedules continue to be adjusted. “If you are in either of these regions, please do not head to the airport unless you have a confirmed flight with another airline, and your flight is operating as scheduled. Your safety is our top priority,” the airline said on its website. Air France Air France has resumed its regular flights to Tel Aviv and Beirut. Flights to Riyadh and Dubai are however suspended until October 24. “Affected customers are being contacted individually. Air France reiterates that the safety and security of its customers and crew are its absolute priority,” the airline said. Cathay Pacific The Hong Kong carrier has extended its suspension of flights to Dubai and Riyadh until January 31, 2027. “Affected travellers will be offered the flexibility to rebook, reroute or refund their tickets. Cathay will continue to closely monitor the evolving situation in the Middle East,” the airline said. Air Astana Kazakhstan's national carrier had earlier suspended flights from Almaty and Astana to Dubai until September 30. But flights between the cities are now available to book for travel on October 1 onwards. British Airways British Airways has revised its schedule for several Middle East destinations, with flights to Dubai set to resume on November 3. The airline will initially operate one daily flight between London and Dubai during the winter season, before increasing to twice-daily services for the summer. Flights to Abu Dhabi will remain suspended for considerably longer, with services scheduled to resume during the winter 2027-2028 season. Elsewhere in the region, BA's Doha service resumed on September 1 at a reduced frequency of one flight a day, down from twice daily. Flights to Tel Aviv are scheduled to resume on October 25 with one daily service, while Riyadh flights will restart on November 3, also at one a day. Amman services are due to resume on November 4 with four flights a week. Flights to Bahrain will remain suspended until the end of March 2027. Lufthansa Lufthansa Group airlines will gradually resume flights to Dubai from late October, restoring connections from several European cities. Lufthansa will restart services between Munich and Dubai on October 25, followed by flights between Frankfurt and Dubai on October 26. The German airline will operate up to five weekly services on the routes. Swiss will resume daily flights between Zurich and Dubai from October 27, while Austrian Airlines will restart its Vienna-Dubai service on December 12, operating up to five flights a week. Eurowings will also restore three routes between Germany and Dubai. Daily flights from Berlin will resume on November 1, alongside four weekly services from Stuttgart. Three weekly flights from Cologne Bonn Airport will follow from November 3. The Lufthansa Group is also restarting services to other destinations in the region, including Tel Aviv, Beirut and Amman. The group said it “continuously monitors and evaluates the situation in the Middle East” and remains in close contact with relevant authorities. “The safety of passengers and crew is always the top priority for the Lufthansa Group,” it said, adding that the continuing volatility in the region means short-notice changes to individual routes may still be necessary. American Airlines American Airlines has extended its travel alert for passengers flying to, through or from Tel Aviv, with flexible booking options now covering travel into March 2027. Affected customers who bought tickets by March 28, 2026, can make a one-time change without a fee for journeys scheduled up to March 26, 2027. Rebooked travel can take place through April 2, 2027. For Doha, the existing alert covers travel scheduled between February 28, 2026, and January 6, 2027, with rebooked journeys permitted through January 13, 2027. Passengers must keep the same origin and destination, and rebook in the same cabin or pay any difference in fare. Eligible travellers can also cancel their trip and request a refund. Delta Air Lines Delta has extended the suspension of flights between Atlanta and Tel Aviv until December 18. The launch of flights between Boston and Tel Aviv has been delayed until further notice, although services between New York-JFK and Tel Aviv resumed on September 6. Customers affected by the Atlanta suspension can rebook their journeys or request a refund for the portion of their trip that has not been flown. Virgin Atlantic Virgin Atlantic flights to Dubai remain suspended until October 2027, with tickets for the resumed service to go on sale later this year, the airline said in a notice on its website. “If you're looking to travel sooner, you can still book a Dubai holiday with Virgin Atlantic Holidays, flying with Emirates,” it added. Finnair Finnair has extended the suspension of its flights to both Dubai and Doha until March 27, 2027. “Finnair continuously monitors the security situation in different regions and, when necessary, makes changes to flight routes or operations. The security situation in the Middle East has remained unstable, with no clear signs of improvement,” the airline said. KLM KLM has adjusted its flight schedule across the Middle East and continues to avoid the airspace of Iran, Iraq and Israel, as well as parts of the Arabian Gulf. The airline has resumed services to Tel Aviv, with flights stopping in Larnaca, Cyprus, where the crew will rest overnight. “We always check the situation and adjust our flights to keep you safe and give you the best options,” the airline said. Flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Dubai remain suspended until October 24. Passengers affected by cancellations can rebook their journeys for a later date or request a refund, depending on their ticket conditions. Turkish Airlines Turkish Airlines has resumed flights to Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Damascus, Beirut and Amman as the carrier continues to restore services across parts of the Middle East. But flights to Tehran remain suspended. The airline also warned of further disruption due to the latest escalation. “Some of our flights to and from Iran and the surrounding region have been cancelled. The current situation in the region's airspace is being monitored in real-time, and additional flight cancellations may occur,” the airline posted on its website. ITA Airways The national carrier of Italy has resumed flights between Rome and Riyadh, but flights to Dubai are suspended until October 24. “Passengers can request rebooking on an alternative flight or a refund of their ticket,” the airline said. AirBaltic Flights operated by the Latvian flag carrier between Riga and Dubai remain suspended until October 24. Korean Air Korean Air's regular service between Incheon and Dubai remains suspended, with no date set for flights to resume. “As limited airspace capacity related to the conflict involving the US, Israel and Iran continues, the suspension of the Incheon-Dubai route will be extended until further notice,” the airline said. “A decision on when to resume flights will be made at a later date, following a comprehensive review of Dubai Airport's normalisation and market demand recovery.”

title: Polish deputy minister talks about tests of new drones. Will they reach Moscow?
body:
Deputy Minister of National Defence Cezary Tomczyk, in an interview with Defence24, spoke about tests conducted a few weeks ago over Poland covering a distance of approximately one thousand kilometres, as well as the practical vetting of companies seeking to supply the military with unmanned aerial vehicles and countermeasures. We also asked the minister whether the tested drones would be able to reach Moscow.
“A few weeks ago, we conducted tests over Poland covering a distance of a thousand kilometres. We are talking about drones that flew through a corridor created over Poland, flying over training grounds – very interesting conclusions. At the same time, we tested various equipment designed to detect or counter these drones. Above all, we must use this in practice and on many levels. This practicality is most important here,” said Tomczyk.

Asked whether the drones would be capable of reaching Moscow, the deputy minister replied that the conclusions are “very optimistic”. He emphasised that the ministry does not base its assessments on presentations, but on trials in conditions close to combat.
“To everyone who comes – and plenty of companies do – we say: show us what you can do. Is it a design or a product? If it is a product, we invite you to the training ground. We will create a certain situation, an exercise – after all, they do not know what tasks they will face. And you either meet our requirements or you don’t,” he said.
As an example, he cited the trials over a distance of approximately one thousand kilometres. The military jammed the drones and intentionally made it difficult for them to complete the task to verify the real combat value of the designs.
“Just as was the case with the drones over a distance of a thousand kilometres: we jammed these drones, we did everything to make the task difficult for them. Some companies proved themselves, some less so. I think it is a very interesting experience with many conclusions,” Tomczyk added.
The tests the deputy minister spoke about concern the Deep Precision Strike programme, under which the Polish Armed Forces are testing Polish, relatively inexpensive unmanned strike systems capable of precision strikes on targets approximately 1,000 km away. Earlier, in September, the military designated a special air corridor over the country – from the area of the training grounds on the coast towards the training ground in Nowa Dęba – specifically for the flights of such machines. The General Staff emphasised at the time that the tested drones were unarmed, and the aim of the trials was to assess whether domestic designs could provide a cheaper alternative to missiles and air operations for deep strikes.

title: Aegean Airlines Ranked Europe’s Safest Airline in New 10-Year Safety Index
body: Greek flag carrier Aegean Airlines has been ranked the safest major airline in Europe in a new 10-year safety index, finishing ahead of Ryanair and Austrian Airlines. Aegean scored 89 out of 100 in the 2026 European Airline Safety Index, which assessed 20 of Europe’s largest eligible low-cost and mainline airlines based on flight volumes recorded by EUROCONTROL in 2025. The index, produced by AirAdvisor, examined airline performance across six categories, with the greatest weighting given to safety records. The categories were: Safety record: 40% Certification and audits: 20% Operational safety systems: 15% Fleet age and technical profile: 10% Pilot training: 10% Financial stability: 5% Aegean received a perfect 40/40 for its safety record , with no qualifying accidents recorded during the 2016 to 2025 assessment period. The Greek carrier also scored strongly for operational safety, fleet profile and financial stability, recording 13/15, 9/10 and 5/5 respectively. AirAdvisor stressed that the ranking is designed to compare airlines across multiple safety related factors and should not be interpreted as declaring an individual airline either safe or unsafe. Aegean’s top position also highlights the importance of looking beyond accident records alone. British Airways, SAS and Eurowings also achieved a perfect 40/40 safety record but finished outside the top five after scores in the other categories were taken into account. Low-cost airlines also perform strongly Ryanair finished second overall with 86/100 , followed by Austrian Airlines on 85.5/100 . Norwegian ranked fourth with 85/100, while SunExpress completed the top five with 84.5/100. Three of the five highest-ranked airlines were low-cost carriers, challenging the perception that cheaper airfares necessarily come with lower safety standards. Across the 20 airlines assessed, low-cost carriers recorded an average score of 79.2 , compared with 82.8 for mainline airlines. Low-cost airlines actually performed better in the fleet category, averaging 7.8/10 compared with 7.1/10 for mainline carriers. Wizz Air and Pegasus received perfect scores for fleet age and technical profile, although the report cautioned that aircraft age alone should never be treated as a measure of safety. A newer aircraft can offer technological and efficiency advantages, but older aircraft can continue to operate safely for decades when properly maintained. 2026 European Airline Safety Index rankings Aegean Airlines – 89/100 Ryanair – 86/100 Austrian Airlines – 85.5/100 Norwegian – 85/100 SunExpress – 84.5/100 Air France – 83.5/100 British Airways – 83.5/100 Iberia – 83.5/100 Turkish Airlines – 83/100 Lufthansa – 83/100 KLM – 82.5/100 easyJet – 82/100 Eurowings – 81.5/100 SAS – 81.5/100 Wizz Air – 79.5/100 Transavia – 79/100 Vueling – 77/100 Jet2 – 73/100 SWISS – 72.5/100 Pegasus Airlines – 64.5/100 The result puts Greece’s Aegean Airlines at the top of the European ranking , ahead of some of the continent’s biggest aviation names. title: Greece Could Become Gas-Sufficient After Ionian Drilling
body: Results from an exploratory drilling operation in Block 2 of the Ionian Sea are expected in May or June 2027, after the Energean-ExxonMobil-Helleniq Energy consortium plans to drill the Asopos 1 target in April. The drilling will determine whether the target identified through seismic surveys contains natural gas or oil. However, further drilling will be needed to establish whether any discovery is commercially exploitable and determine its size. If estimates of a 270 billion cubic metre gas deposit are confirmed, Energean CEO Mathios Rigas said Greece could become self-sufficient in natural gas and an exporter. Rigas made the remarks at the Eastern Mediterranean Gas Forum on Wednesday. Confirmation drilling, which will also require environmental approval, will take about a year and could begin in 2028. If the results prove positive, a further three years would be required to install the infrastructure needed to extract and transport the hydrocarbons. On Tuesday, the Regional Council of the Ionian Islands approved the Environmental Impact Assessment for the Asopos drilling operation. If hydrocarbons are discovered, ExxonMobil will take over as head of the consortium from Energean. Other projects discussed The Ionian drilling project was among several Greece-related initiatives discussed at Wednesday’s Eastern Mediterranean Gas Forum. Greece-Cyprus electricity interconnection : Authorities in Greece and Cyprus expect the issuance of a NAVTEX for the continuation of seabed surveys within days, according to sources from both countries. The sources said the project would not require Turkish permission. The European Investment Bank is also expected to complete its financial and technical assessment, while Cyprus is expected to pay €25 million to the Independent Power Transmission Operator (IPTO) for expenses already incurred. Vertical Gas Corridor: Countries participating in the project are collecting data to determine the network investments needed to meet demand from 2027, when the EU plans to end Russian natural gas imports. Gas transmission system operators from participating countries will meet again in Sofia in January. DESFA CEO Maria Sferoutsou said efforts are also under way to improve the efficiency of existing infrastructure before new projects are built. Greece-Egypt electricity interconnection: Greece and Egypt continue to support the GREGY electricity interconnection project. Carbon storage at Prinos: A floating platform that will inject carbon dioxide into the depleted Prinos field is currently at Perama and is expected to arrive in the Kavala offshore area in November, according to Energean sources. The project aims to complete its onshore facilities for receiving liquefied carbon dioxide, regasification, wells and injection infrastructure by 2030. In the meantime, industrial companies emitting the carbon dioxide are expected to make investment decisions on capturing and transporting their emissions to Prinos. Egypt, which has substantially greater available carbon-storage capacity, also asked Greece on Wednesday for technical assistance in organising the market and establishing the necessary regulatory framework, according to reports. title: Battlegroup North tank crews destroy more than 10 Ukrainian warehouses near Kharkov
body:
BELGOROD, October 8. /TASS/. Crews of T-80BVM tanks from the motorized rifle regiment of Russia’s Battlegroup North’s 6th Guards Combined Arms Army have destroyed more than 10 Ukrainian drone storage and control sites in the Kharkov Region, a tank platoon commander with the call sign Matros told TASS.
"A reconnaissance UAV crew detected Ukrainian personnel transporting drones in the Kharkov Region. Further reconnaissance of the area helped to locate more than 10 UAV control and storage sites, as well as a fortified strongpoint through which Ukrainian drones were being delivered. On command, the tank crews opened fire on and destroyed the targets with high-explosive shells," the commander said.
According to Matros, Battlegroup North troops are engaging Ukrainian targets from concealed firing positions. "We prepare our positions in advance, try to create several access routes to them, and camouflage them as much as possible from enemy reconnaissance. This helps preserve our combat vehicles," he added.
Units of the Battlegroup North, while carrying out combat missions in the special military operation, continue to tighten the encirclement around and destroy Ukrainian formations in the Kharkov Region.

title: South Sudan raises Ebola alert after Kenya confirms first case
body: South Sudan has raised its alert level for Ebola following confirmation of the first case in neighbouring Kenya, health authorities said on Wednesday, although no cases have been confirmed in South Sudan. Caretaker Health Minister Dak Duop Bichiok said the government was closely monitoring the regional situation and had placed the national health system on a high state of alert because of South Sudan’s borders and the movement of people and goods across the region. “We want to reassure the citizens of South Sudan and all the residents within our borders that no confirmed cases in South Sudan have been reported,” Bichiok said at a press conference in Juba. He said the confirmation of Ebola in Kenya had increased the risk of cross-border transmission, particularly because of South Sudan’s proximity to affected areas of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and regional travel routes through Uganda and Kenya. The government has urged communities, travellers, transport operators, religious leaders and civil society organisations to cooperate with health officials carrying out screening at border crossings and other points of entry. Dr. Ader Machar Aciek, acting executive director of the National Public Health Institute, said preparedness measures had already been activated following Ebola outbreaks in the DRC and Uganda. “We have people doing screening at the points of entry across the border, along the border in the 15 high-risk counties, as well as our international airport, Juba International Airport,” Aciek said. He said South Sudan currently had eight infectious disease units equipped to isolate and manage suspected or confirmed cases. According to the World Health Organization, South Sudan’s preparedness level has improved since the regional outbreak was first reported, rising from 29% in May to 45% in June and 65% currently. Dr. Moses Ongom, WHO’s officer in charge in South Sudan, attributed the improvement to efforts by the Ministry of Health, the National Public Health Institute and partners to strengthen surveillance, response and case-management capacity. He cautioned, however, that improved preparedness should not lead to complacency. Africa CDC Country Director Dr. Tolbert Nyenswah said South Sudan had surveillance systems, disease-detection mechanisms, rapid response teams and laboratory testing capacity that could help it respond quickly if a case were detected. “The priority is not only to prevent the virus from entering South Sudan but also to ensure that the country can rapidly contain any outbreak,” Nyenswah said. He cited Uganda’s response to its recent outbreak, saying authorities had contained it within 92 days after 20 cases and two deaths were recorded. The health ministry urged the public to remain calm but vigilant and to report suspected cases, particularly people showing symptoms such as fever, vomiting, diarrhea or unusual bleeding. It advised people to avoid direct physical contact with suspected patients, practice regular hand hygiene, avoid contact with potentially infected animals and refrain from handling the bodies of people who may have died with Ebola-like symptoms. The government said suspected cases could be reported through the toll-free health hotline 6666. title: Off the menu: Angel’s Pizza, Figaro Coffee owner set to exit PSE
body: MANILA, Philippines – The company behind popular Filipino brands Angel’s Pizza and Figaro Coffee is planning an exit from the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE). Figaro Culinary Group, which also operates Tien Ma’s Taiwanese Cuisine and Koobideh Kebab, announced on Wednesday, October 7, that its board had approved plans to voluntarily delist from the PSE, less than five years after making its stock market debut in January 2022. Delisting means the company’s shares would no longer be traded on the exchange. It does not mean the company is shutting down its restaurants, though the investing public will no longer be able to have an ownership stake in the Figaro group. So what happens to people who invested in Figaro? Under the tender offer plan, Figaro Coffee Systems, the group’s wholly owned subsidiary that operates its restaurant businesses, will offer to buy shares held by minority investors for P0.82 apiece. (READ: Pizza overtakes coffee in Figaro group’s store footprint as Angel’s Pizza rises ) For comparison, Figaro originally sold shares to the public at P0.75 apiece when it listed in January 2022, raising around P767 million to help fund its expansion. Monde Nissin, the food manufacturer behind Lucky Me! noodles and SkyFlakes crackers, is among the major shareholders excluded from the proposed buyout. The company acquired a 15% stake in Figaro in 2023 for P820.3 million, equivalent to P1 per share, and is not participating in the P0.82-per-share tender offer alongside two other major shareholders, Carmetheus Holdings and Camerton. Figaro’s stock market exit is not yet a done deal. Based on the disclosure, the delisting still requires shareholder approval, completion of the tender offer, and Figaro Coffee Systems and the major shareholders collectively reaching at least 95% ownership. A special stockholders’ meeting is scheduled for November 13 to vote on the proposal. Trading in Figaro shares was suspended on Thursday, October 8, to give investors time to digest the announcement and assess the offer. – Rappler.com Must Read [Vantage Point] What Robinsons Retail’s delisting signals about the Philippine market ALSO ON RAPPLER [ANALYSIS] Voluntary delisting of 8990 from PSE: Why it’s a cause for concern [ANALYSIS] Injap Sia’s MerryMart’s disconcerting voluntary delisting plan [Vantage Point] PNCC’s great puzzle: Why delisting isn’t so simple Robinsons Retail trading stopped as Gokongwei group completes share transfer for delisting

title: Tokyo considers allowing nuclear weapons to be brought into Japan — newspaper
body:
TOKYO, October 8. /TASS/. Japan’s government currently has no intention of revising the country’s non-nuclear principles but is considering a proposal to permit nuclear weapons to be brought into the country under an exception, the Sankei newspaper reported, citing government sources.
The initiative is viewed as a measure to strengthen the deterrence of potential adversaries based on the idea of the United States’ "nuclear umbrella," the paper noted.
A provision allowing nuclear weapons to be brought into the country as an exception may be included in new fundamental documents on security, which the Japanese government plans to adopt at the end of the year. This would allow ships carrying nuclear weapons to enter Japanese ports, the newspaper said.
According to Sankei, such a move would require addressing numerous issues, including defining the circumstances in which nuclear weapons could be brought to Japan and developing a mechanism to coordinate visits by such vessels with local authorities.
The paper noted that some members of the country’s ruling Liberal Democratic Party were calling for a cautious approach to such decisions, so discussions on the issue were expected to continue. Another proposal circulating in the government is to include a provision in the fundamental security documents on discussing the possibility of providing the country’s Navy with nuclear-powered submarines.
Japan maintains three non-nuclear principles: not possessing, not producing and not permitting the introduction of nuclear weapons into its territory. The principles, which have no force of law, were formalized through a government decision and a regular parliamentary resolution. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has repeatedly said that her cabinet adheres to the three non-nuclear principles. However, she has been consistently moving away from the obligation to pursue the same policy in the future.

title: Brent crude tops $104 per barrel on ICE for first time since September 29
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. The price of Brent crude oil futures for December 2026 delivery on the London-based ICE exchange rose above $104 per barrel for the first time since September 29 of this year, trading data showed.
As of 10:06 a.m. Moscow time, Brent crude was up 3.83%, trading at $104.04 per barrel.
By 10:11 a.m. Moscow time, Brent accelerated its gains to $104.07 per barrel (+3.86%). Meanwhile, WTI crude futures for November delivery rose by 3.55% to $91.41 per barrel.

title: Ukraine’s Frodo robot carries wounded soldier in first reported evacuation
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); A company of unmanned ground systems from Ukraine's 92nd Assault Brigade used the robotic system Frodo to evacuate a wounded soldier, Frontline Robotics told Militarnyi on 7 October. Ground robots are being used to evacuate wounded soldiers from the drone-dominated " kill zone ," a band tens of kilometers deep on both sides of the front line. About 112,000 logistics and evacuation missions by ground robotic systems were recorded from January through August 2026, according to Ukraine's Defense Ministry. Operator credits speed and suspension The operator, callsign Tango, named speed and the ability to perform complex maneuvers as the robot's main advantages, according to Militarnyi. The unit also praised Frodo's adaptive suspension, which it said smoothed out rough terrain and kept the wounded soldier's transport relatively comfortable. The Frodo ground robot's evacuation mission with Ukraine's 92nd Assault Brigade, autumn 2026. Screenshot from video: Frontline Robotics What Frodo can carry, and how far The robot has a 6×6 wheel layout with independent suspension, adjustable ground clearance of 170–330 mm, and a top speed of 40 km/h. Its recommended payload is 200 kg, and its maximum is 400 kg, according to Frontline Robotics. The company lists its range as 150 km on asphalt and up to 90 km over rough terrain with the recommended load. Frodo supports several communication channels, and one person can swap its batteries in about two minutes. Frodo had passed the Defense Ministry's codification and could carry remote-controlled modules such as the Burya turret, Militarnyi reported on 30 September. The 92nd Brigade had used ground robots to evacuate wounded soldiers before. In September 2025, the brigade evacuated three wounded soldiers using a ground robot, according to Militarnyi.
