title: Top US diplomat says prospects of negotiated settlement in Ukraine 'elusive'
body:
ATHENS, October 8. /TASS/. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the path toward a negotiated way out of the Ukraine conflict has been slippery.
"We stand prepared to facilitate and continue to explore any opportunity for a negotiated settlement. We think it would be good for Russia and Ukraine, but so far, it’s proving elusive," the top US diplomat told the Greek daily Kathimerini in an interview.
Rubio called the conflict a "strategic stalemate" now. "Strategic stalemates are only broken in one of two ways: a) through a negotiated settlement, or b) through escalation by one side or both that ends up spreading beyond the confines of the original conflict. Right now, there don’t seem to be prospects of a negotiated settlement," he noted. Washington is still prepared to play a constructive role though, the diplomat added.

title: Meta policies fail as scam ads, deepfakes impersonating Nigerian public figures litter Facebook
body:
In mid-April, a sponsored video appeared on the Nigeria Daily Report Facebook page. The video shows a figure of Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, the senator representing Kogi Central at the National Assembly, introducing viewers to a “lucrative” investment scheme.
“I am going to reveal a secret to you…today is your lucky day,” she appeared to have said in the video , a deepfake now seen and liked by over a thousand users on Facebook.
Mrs Akpoti-Uduaghan’s figure in the video told viewers they could invest a one-off N430,000 to earn N14 million monthly –a mouth-watering 3,000 per cent monthly return on investment.
“It is important to understand one thing, opportunities like this can’t be opened up to everyone at once,” her figure said in the video.
But the senator didn’t make the video, and she had long disclaimed any endorsement of investment platforms before this video surfaced.
“Although the video looks like me and even sounds like me, it is not real,” she had said about a similar video a month earlier. “It is fabricated and misleading content created to scam unsuspecting members of the public.”
The creators used deepfake technology to create a physical persona of the senator, then uploaded it. The creators also promoted the video to reach more Facebook users.
Through Meta, Facebook’s parent company’s advertising platform , anyone can pay Facebook to promote posts to targeted audiences. The scammers who created this video paid for the ads, and the social media platform inadvertently helped them reach more potential victims to defraud.
As traditional advertising in the mass media dwindles due to increased use of social media platforms, tech companies have cashed in on digital advertising, raking in billions of dollars. But these sparsely regulated advertisements have also served as a launchpad for fraudsters farming for new, unsuspecting victims.
The tech giant said it is constantly taking steps to address the scam ads. But critics argue that it has been slow to address the problem because the fraudulent ads continue to generate revenue for the company.
Meta’s own internal documents confirm the social media company earns money from scam ads like this.
Reuters reported last year that Meta internally projected in 2024 that it would earn $16 billion, or about 10 per cent of its overall annual revenue, from running advertising for scams and banned goods.
Internal documents reviewed by Reuters also revealed that Meta charges higher ad rates than rejecting ads when it suspects an advertiser is likely a scammer.
Although Meta’s ad policies state that it doesn’t allow fraudulent or misleading ads, such ads have flooded the social media platform, some of them specifically targeting Nigerians.
“…we don’t allow advertisers to run ads that promote products, services, schemes or offers that use identified deceptive or misleading practices, including scams to take money from people or access personal information,” reads part of Meta’s advertising policy.
However, more deepfake videos impersonating prominent Nigerians have appeared on the social media platform and have remained on the platform months after they were fact-checked.
In May, a deepfake video appeared on the Facebook page Nigeria Daily Bulletin , showing the presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, asking social media users to invest N350,000 to earn N4.5 million.
“This is not just about making money for some people; it means achieving financial independence earlier than expected,” Mr Obi appeared to have said in the video. “For others, it creates a chance to rebuild savings, support their families and plan for the future with confidence.”
The caption for the video asked social media users to hurry and register as “Registration Is Closing — Only Limited Access Still Available.”
But the link in the video leads to a phoney website –‘welceastming.website.’ The website clones Channels Television’s website, using its emblems, but with false stories about investment platforms.
The website also contains a false interview purportedly conducted by the TV station’s Seun Okinbaloye and Mr Obi. In the interview, the page attributed several comments on the ‘AfriQuantumX’ investment scheme to Mr Obi. The hyperlink on the page leads to a form requesting users’ names, emails and phone numbers.
Meanwhile, the video with the deepfake of Mrs Akpoti-Uduaghan is also linked to another fishy website –‘springbunnhopes.online.’
A review of the webpage on a website analysis page, WHOIS , showed that key details about the webpage had been redacted through a privacy service provided by a company named ‘Withheld for Privacy ehf.
‘Withheld for Privacy ehf’ is an Icelandic domain privacy service used by website administrators to protect their personal contact details from public directories.
Meta confirmed to PREMIUM TIMES that the ads and deepfake videos violated its policy. But these posts remained on the platform for months. They were only removed in July after this newspaper contacted the social media company, asking if they violated its policies.
“We have reviewed the material shared with us and are taking action on content that violates our policies,” a Meta spokesperson told our reporter in an email.
“It’s against our policies to run ads that deceptively use public figures to try to scam people, and we remove these ads when we detect them.”
The tech giant also told PREMIUM TIMES that it is investing heavily in “trained review teams” to identify and remove such ads.
“This problem isn’t new,” it added. “Scammers use every platform available to them and constantly adapt to evade enforcement. That is why Meta has specialised systems to detect celebrity bait, invests heavily in trained review teams, shares tips on avoiding scams and offers tools to report potential violations.”
Deepfake videos of influential Nigerians have flooded Facebook, often used to promote fraudulent investment scams, and in some cases to drive traffic to gambling websites.
Facebook first announced plans to remove deepfake videos in 2020, but such videos have only flooded the platform six years later.
In another deepfake video on Facebook, the Director-General of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, appeared in her signature Ankara, delivering a speech. The video, which cloned her voice, introduced social media users to an investment scheme where users can invest N380,000 to earn N2,660,000 daily.
“It is real, verifiable and backed by a system designed for your success…I personally assure the safety of your funds and complete confidentiality,” it said.
But Mrs Okonjo-Iweala took to her X handle to warn Nigerians against the video and other investment platforms using AI and deepfakes to impersonate her.
“As I repeatedly said, I never post anything on Instagram, Facebook or WhatsApp,” she wrote. “Anything emanating from these sources with my image is not from me. I only post on Twitter/X. I just don’t want people to be duped.”
The page that posted the video – Moonbeam Meadows – remains active on Facebook, but appears dormant. It only featured a few posts and pictures of gardens. It has fewer than 10 posts in all.
It’s similar to the page that shared the deepfake of Mrs Akpoti-Uduaghan. The page, Nigeria Daily Report , remains on Facebook, but with no visible activity. Although it ran the video as an ad in April, a search of the page’s ad history on Meta Ads Library turns up empty search results. The Ads Library was supposed to show details of the ads, including the target, for how long they ran and who paid for the ads.
Meta said it removed over 159 million scam ads on Facebook last year alone and took down 10.9 million accounts on Facebook and Instagram associated with criminal scam centres.
But the pages, featuring the deepfake of Mrs Akpoti-Uduaghan and Mrs Okonjo-Iweala, have remained on the platform for months. Although hidden from the page’s profile, one could still visit it with the link, indicating it has not been taken down by the platform. The post was only taken down in the first week of July, after PREMIUM TIMES contacted Meta, asking if the post violated its policies.
“What they (scammers) do is to hide the post from the public profile of the page, but you can see it as a sponsored ad if you fall into the target audience,” said Nurudeen Akewushola, a fact-checker at FactCheckHub.
Mr Akewushola explained that users who click on scam ads are likely to see more of them because of Meta’s ad-personalisation system, which tries to deliver ads based on a user’s interests.
The platform also said in March that it has deployed Artificial Intelligence to analyse and take down celebrity-bait and brand impersonation.
“Scammers use subtle tricks and deceptive framing that are hard to catch with traditional detection systems,” it said. “Our experts and specialists in combating scams built advanced AI systems that can analyse multiple signals — such as text, images, and the surrounding context to spot a broader range of more sophisticated scam patterns faster and at scale.”
Despite this, the videos have continued to thrive on Facebook, and many prominent Nigerians have continued to be victims of these deepfakes. The Chairman of the United Bank for Africa (UBA), Tony Elumelu, the Group Chairman of Zenith Bank, Jim Ovia , and Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote , have all featured in deepfakes used to promote fraudulent investment schemes and posted on Facebook.
Popular journalists like Channel TV’s Seun Okinbaloye and RadioNow’s Kadaria Ahmed have also been victims of these deepfakes.
On several occasions, each of these individuals has distanced themselves from any investment platforms. Yet, new videos promoting new platforms have shown up, with little done by the social media company to curb them.
“It looked and sounded remarkably real, but it was completely fake,” Mr Elumelu said in a statement distancing himself from a deepfake featuring him and used to promote an investment scheme. “This incident highlights a growing and serious threat to digital trust.”
Nigerian fact-checkers have already fact-checked lots of these videos. “(But) it has become very difficult to even fact-check all of these videos,” said Mr Akewushola.
Mr Akewushola, who has fact-checked several similar videos, explained that the sheer scale of such ads overwhelms the fact-checkers who get to work on them frequently.
He said the practice has also become sophisticated as the scammers learn new ways to hide their identities.
Meta told PREMIUM TIMES that the scammers have constantly adapted to evade its scrutiny, but noted that it will continue to intensify efforts to identify and remove them and offer tools for users to report potential violations.

title: Klitschko: Russia attacks on Kyiv Thursday kill 1, injure 11
body:
Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko reported on Thursday morning that as a result of Russian attack, one person was killed and nine of the wounded were hospitalized.

"One person died. 5 injured as a result of Russia’s attack on the capital on the morning of October 8. Four of the wounded were hospitalized," the mayor wrote on his Telegram channel.

"Since the beginning of the day on October 8 in Kyiv, as a result of Russian attacks, one person has died. 11 city residents were injured. Medics hospitalized 9 of the wounded," Klitschko added later.

Earlier, he reported that UAV debris fell in an open area in the Holosiyivsky district, and medics were dispatched.

Media outlets reported a loud explosion near the "New England" residential complex.

title: Russia’s Battlegroup West destroys 104 Ukrainian heavy combat multicopters in past day
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Over the past 24 hours, Russia’s Battlegroup West has destroyed a total of 104 Ukrainian heavy combat multicopters, 55 unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) control centers, and four Starlink satellite communication stations, the battlegroup’s spokesman Ivan Bigma reported.
"Air defense crews and mobile armed units downed 60 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles, five loitering munitions, and 104 enemy heavy combat multicopters," Bigma said.
According to him, 55 Ukrainian UAV control centers, four Starlink satellite communication stations, two motorcycles, 40 ground robotic systems, and two enemy field ammunition depots were identified and destroyed.

title: RENK wins transmission order for Patria tracked vehicles
body: The German drivetrain manufacturer RENK has taken a follow-on order worth €30 million from Patria for transmissions to go into the TRACKX family of light tracked vehicles, the company stated . Patria placed an initial pre-production batch at the beginning of the year, and this order is substantially larger, with deliveries scheduled to begin in 2027. The transmission involved is the HSWL 076, developed for light tracked vehicles in the 10 to 20-tonne class, weighing around 700 kilograms and combining steering, braking and propulsion in a digitally controlled drivetrain. Michael Masur, chief executive of vehicle mobility solutions at RENK, said: “The announced vehicle procurements by Finland and Sweden are a key step towards series production for TRACKX. We have been involved with this vehicle family through the development, testing and pre-production stages, and will now be continuing this cooperation with Patria. “At the same time we are working with Patria to further develop the technological potential of the platform, with a particular view to manned and unmanned vehicle concepts.” Finland and Sweden placed their first TRACKX orders at the end of September, with deliveries also due to start in 2027. RENK, based in Augsburg, turned over around €1.4 billion in 2025 and has been listed in Frankfurt since February 2024, joining the MDAX index the following year. Neither company has said how many transmissions the order covers. The post RENK wins transmission order for Patria tracked vehicles first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: [Pastilan] ‘Walang alam’
body: The financial records presented and validated by the Anti-Money Laundering Council and bank executives at Vice President Sara Duterte ’s impeachment trial this week point to a pattern of money being moved, obscured, and kept out of plain sight. The Dutertes, multi-millionaires after all, held tens of millions of pesos across a maze of accounts. At least P96 million was floated in financial limbo, shifted into manager’s checks and kept inside the bank while disappearing from customers’ accounts when their wealth had to be declared. The apparent purpose, as presented by prosecutors, was to keep the money out of sight during the filing of their mandatory statements of assets, liabilities and net worth . Billions of pesos in transactions involving the Vice President and her husband were flagged as suspicious . There are millions more received from China by a company linked to them, given a semblance of legitimacy by purported supplies of banana chips, a rather crunchy explanation for a rather large sum. Must Read Sara, Rodrigo Duterte hid P96M through unutilized manager’s checks — prosecution If it is not unexplained wealth, as the Sara Duterte defense asserts and would have us believe, then what is the explanation? Hocus-pocus There’s something sinister about money that disappears without actually going anywhere. There’s no robbery the way bank robbers stage it, no getaway car, no maleta stuffed with cash in this particular case. The money stays safely in the bank, but vanishes from the paperwork. On Wednesday, October 7, prosecutors presented records showing about P96 million in manager’s checks linked to Duterte and her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte. The transactions point to a pattern in which substantial sums were kept from appearing in year-end balances. Consider this: In January 2010, the father and daughter opened a joint time deposit at a BPI branch with more than P40 million. After 12 renewals, it had grown to P41.7 million. When the deposit matured in March 2011, the money was converted that same day into a manager’s check. Except the money did not actually leave the bank. It moved into a settlement account separate from the customer’s account, where the bank held the funds backing an unused manager’s check. If the check remained unused for six months, the amount could be returned to the purchaser’s account. Now, if that isn’t hocus-pocus, I don’t know what is. The money could leave the customer’s account without leaving the bank, then return months later. Nothing really had to disappear in this modus. It only had to stop showing up on the radar, especially at year-end, when the money had to be declared. Another P55 million was held through a similar manager’s check during the same period, bringing the total to about P96 million. The defense says Sara Duterte did not know about the transactions because she did not sign them. Let me get this straight: her father could open a joint account, deposit and move P96 million around, and his daughter was simply out of the loop? Really? P96 million and Sara, the daughter, had no idea? The ‘walang alam’ defense “Walang alam” (Has no knowledge) is now doing an extraordinary amount of work for the defense. Sara’s brother, Davao Mayor Baste Duterte , used it on the witness stand days ago. And Sara’s disbursing officer used it too. If everyone involved is “ walang alam,” then we have reached a remarkable situation. There are hundreds of millions of pesos, if not billions, mountains of paperwork and transactions recorded by banks and the AMLC, yet apparently none of them knows anything . So who does? The documents know. The numbers know. The banks know. Apparently, everyone knows except the Dutertes. 30 bank accounts. Seriously? The bank balances presented a day earlier, on Tuesday, October 6, offer another little arithmetic to think about. Sara and her husband had at least 30 active accounts across several banks between 2022 and 2025. At year-end, those accounts held more than P59 million in 2022 and over P71 million in 2023. Then came 2024, when the total fell to about P22 million. In 2025, it climbed again, exceeding P35 million. Must Read LIST: Duterte-Carpio bank accounts, balances detailed in impeachment trial The sharp contraction came in 2024, the same year Sara resigned as education secretary . She quit in June that year, and her bank balances then took a conspicuous plunge. Coincidence? Perhaps. But when the dates line up so neatly, calling it coincidence begins to sound less like an explanation and more like an alibi. Who, exactly, needs 30 bank accounts? And how does someone end up with that many accounts, including joint accounts, without apparently knowing they exist? Damage control Tuesday, October 6, 2026, was a damage-control day for Sara. As the Senate impeachment court tackled the financial evidence — something the Vice President’s lawyers and husband had desperately sought to prevent — Sara faced the cameras in Davao to attack allegations by former policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. , who claims he delivered cash to members of the Duterte family on instructions from a former House speaker. Between Gracioso’s word and the financial records, the former is far easier to attack from a public relations perspective. A witness can be denied or discredited but financial records, backed by bank executives, are considerably harder to explain away. The Davao press conference therefore offered a ready-made distraction, shifting public attention from bank documents and figures in the impeachment court to a familiar battle of accusations in the Southern Mindanao city. China connection With Cale88 Foods, the impeachment case moved beyond unexplained wealth and into questions of national security. Records show Cale88, linked to Sara’s husband, received P319.3 million from China. Some transactions were flagged as suspicious, and a senator said some firms that dealt with Cale88 turned out to be Chinese state-owned. China is hardly a politically neutral source of money. It rejects a ruling which upheld the Philippine territorial right while stubbornly asserting its claims, and it has been bullying our people. Against the West Philippine Sea backdrop, Chinese-linked money flowing into a company associated with the husband of the sitting Vice President raises very, very serious questions. Why was such money flowing into the company in the first place? Banana chips? And were the entities behind it advancing Chinese state interests? Who was paying whom, and why? That deserves answers, not evasions. Convince us, Madame Vice President, that you and your ilk are not Tsinadors — by your words, and more importantly, by your deeds. Pastilan . – Rappler.com

title: Ukrainian drones strike oil refinery in Russia’s Bashkortostan
body: Ukrainian drones struck Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat, one of Russia’s largest oil refining complexes, in Salavat, Bashkortostan, overnight on October 8, the Ukrainian monitoring Telegram channels Exilenova+ and Supernova+ reported. Astra, an independent Telegram channel, reviewed photos and videos from eyewitnesses and concluded that the fire likely broke out on the grounds of Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat. Ukrainian drones have targeted the refinery more than once during the full-scale war between Russia and Ukraine. Bashkortostan authorities declared an air raid alert overnight because of the threat of a Ukrainian drone attack. They have not reported on the aftermath of the attack. In addition, “drone debris” fell on the grounds of a facility in Krasnodar, according to a local emergency response headquarters. Fragments of the drone damaged a building and sparked a fire. No one was injured, and the facility’s nature was not specified. Russia’s Defense Ministry said its air defenses shot down 399 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions, occupied Crimea, and the Black Sea since the evening of October 7. Drone strikes have forced Russian oil refineries to suspend or halt operations, contributing to a fuel crisis in Russia over the summer. In early October, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky promised that Ukraine would step up its attacks on Russian oil refineries. Russia’s Defense Ministry threatened to respond by expanding its strikes on targets in Ukraine. At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication. title: Kazakhstan, UK Reaffirm Commitment to Expanding Strategic Partnership
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev received UK Minister of State for Trade Lord Anas Sarwar on Oct. 7 to discuss strengthening bilateral trade and investment ties and expanding cooperation in energy, transport, digitalization and artificial intelligence. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev meets with UK Minister of State for Trade Lord Anas Sarwar. Photo credit: Akorda Strong trade and investment ties Tokayev highlighted the importance Kazakhstan attaches to developing relations with the United Kingdom, noting constructive political dialogue and growing contacts between the two countries, Akorda reported. “Kazakhstan and the United Kingdom are connected by constructive political dialogue and active contacts at various levels. I am confident that we have significant potential to expand cooperation,” Tokayev said. The UK remains one of Kazakhstan’s key trade and investment partners. Bilateral trade increased by 83% in 2025 to more than $1.6 billion, while more than 500 British companies currently operate in Kazakhstan. President Tokayev also underscored the importance of developing human capital alongside trade and investment, calling on Kazakhstan’s younger generation to broaden their international outlook and strengthen foreign-language skills, notably English. Tokayev conveyed his warm wishes to UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and invited him to visit Kazakhstan. Lord Sarwar welcomed the continued development of the strategic partnership and thanked President Tokayev for supporting British business projects and efforts to maintain a favorable investment climate. “We closely follow Kazakhstan’s dynamic development and highly value the closeness of our approaches to key topics on the international agenda. We are united by our commitment to open and trusted partnership, innovation, mutual confidence and free trade,” Lord Sarwar said. Cooperation in emerging and priority sectors Tokayev and Sarwar also discussed prospects for expanding cooperation in energy, transport and logistics, digitalization and artificial intelligence, while also highlighting the importance of strengthening humanitarian ties, academic exchanges and joint education initiatives. The discussions continued during a separate meeting between Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy Serik Zhumangarin and Lord Sarwar, the Prime Minister’s press service reported. Zhumangarin described the UK as an important and reliable strategic partner, noting that the British delegation’s visit provides fresh momentum for bilateral relations and creates opportunities to translate existing agreements into concrete projects. Lord Sarwar reaffirmed the UK’s readiness to deepen cooperation with Kazakhstan, and both officials expressed commitment to open, constructive dialogue and to advancing priority areas of partnership. The post Kazakhstan, UK Reaffirm Commitment to Expanding Strategic Partnership appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: How Orbih refused Amaechi’s offer to abandon my gov bid – Wike
body: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has disclosed that the late Chief Daniel Orbih turned down every inducement from the then Governor of Rivers State, Mr Rotimi Amaechi, to withdraw his support for Wike’s governorship ambition. Wike spoke in Abuja on Wednesday at a night of tributes in honour of Orbih, the former National Vice-Chairman (South South) of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP, who died on August 31 at the age of 64. “There was nothing in this world that was not done to induce him. My governor then sent people to Dan, offered him everything in this world, but Dan stood firm and said, ‘No, I will not accept, I will not agree,'” the minister said. Wike traced their bond to the turbulent period between 2013 and 2014, when he said political adversaries made desperate attempts to derail his ambition. “Today I am a Minister of the FCT; yesterday I was a governor. Who did God use for me to become governor? It was Dan,” he said. He said Orbih, as South South National Vice-Chairman of the PDP, backed his campaign by donating two bulletproof Mercedes-Benz buses for his security and mobilising massive structural support across the region. The minister also spoke of Orbih’s selflessness, saying the late politician never sought personal gain, patronage or government contracts throughout Wike’s eight years as governor. “Dan is not a typical Nigerian politician. Throughout my eight years as governor, he never came for one day, either by phone or coming to my house to say, ‘I need this contract.’ Never,” he said. According to Wike, loyalty ran in Orbih’s family. “The only way I can identify a politician that is reliable is when that politician has stood in times of crisis. Loyalty, commitment to friendship, and being a brother’s keeper run in Dan’s family,” he said. Wike stressed that without Orbih’s strength as National Vice-Chairman protecting the region’s interests, many current national and state lawmakers would not have attained their positions. He noted that Orbih laid the foundation for cross-party collaboration in Edo State and supported many politicians there without benefiting from it. He insisted that Orbih deserves a state burial for his contribution to political developments in Edo and urged stakeholders from the state to act on it. “I will continue to keep my relationship with Dan’s family. I think I will also discuss with the family on how to keep the legacies of Dan,” Wike said. Senator Magnus Abe, Chairman of the Board of the Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, said he is a politician today because Orbih introduced him to politics. “I was the Director General of his first campaign in the United Nigeria Congress Party, when he ran for governor and I went everywhere in Edo with him. “Dan was indeed a bridge builder par excellence. We are gathered here today not because Dan is dead. We are gathered because of the life that he lived and that life impacted all of us in so many different ways,” Abe said. Senator Adams Oshiomhole, who represents Edo North in the Senate and is a former Governor of Edo State, said Orbih made him a better governor. “So my happiness today is that Dan and I, whatever our political differences we might have had, the truth is, Dan made me a better governor. “So, when I’m making a decision, the first thing I’ll ask is, ‘If this goes out today, what is Dan Orbih going to say?’ Each time I abstain from doing something because of what the opposition led by Dan will interpret to the people, before I do it will be better prepared. “That is why I say Dan helped me to be a better governor,” he said. He thanked Wike for reuniting him with Orbih after a prolonged political difference. “It was right at Wike’s residence in Port Harcourt that Dan and I started hugging,” Oshiomhole said. Addressing the family, he said: “Please take consolation from the fact that your father built bridges of unity, of progress, and he never did that at the expense of family and he was committed to the growth and development of Ogbona kingdom.” The PDP presidential candidate, Senator Sandy Onor, described Orbih as “a profound public intellectual, a quintessential lover of Edo people, a defender of Edo heritage, a Nigerian patriot and a social colossus.” “Dan was a great man by every measure, a true family man, a great husband, and a worthy father,” he said. The post How Orbih refused Amaechi’s offer to abandon my gov bid – Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Study flags ChatGPT for Teens as ‘unacceptable risk’ for children
body: MANILA, Philippines – ChatGPT for Teens, launched by OpenAI in mid-August , promised stronger protections for teen users of the artificial intelligence chatbot. However, Common Sense Media (CSM), a nonprofit which tests and gives ratings to entertainment and technology media, assessed ChatGPT for Teens and called it an “Unacceptable Risk for all children under 18.” The CSM study , released on Wednesday, October 7, said that while some of the advertised protections held up in their tests, including refusing explicit sexual roleplay, other protections apparently failed or were worse off with the Teen mode setting engaged. Said CSM, “We are concerned that ChatGPT for Teens could give parents false confidence in guardrails that frequently don’t work.” Among the CSM’s criticisms were that ChatGPT for Teens still encouraged engagement even if it posed a risk to the safety of the teen using it. These engagement cues were “pervasive even in crisis situations,” such as in mentions of self-harm, psychosis or eating disorders. Further, parental alerts for teen accounts don’t work as expected, as no alerts were sent when their tests explicitly discussed suicidal thoughts, self-harm, or an eating disorder on over a dozen new parent-linked accounts. Their tests also showed alerts were only sent for accounts “with weeks of sensitive-topic history, which suggests that alerts depend on accumulated account history, not the severity of what a teen says.” In a TechCrunch report on the CSM findings, OpenAI responded by disputing the assessment and said the group’s testing did not “accurately reflect how ChatGPT’s teen safeguards work in practice.” OpenAI also raised concerns about the methodology of CSM’s study. “Our review of Common Sense Media’s methodology shows that the bulk of their testing may have begun and concluded before activation of parental controls was complete, making their findings inaccurate,” an OpenAI spokesperson said. OpenAI also released data on Wednesday regarding ChatGPT for Teens , saying use was apparently limited. According to OpenAI, teens spent less than 15 minutes a day on the service on average, with fewer than 2% spending more than three consecutive hours on it. Additionally, teens would take breaks or end conversations with the chatbot within five minutes in nearly half of the instances. The Common Sense Media study comes amid recent scrutiny of tech company products meant to keep users engaged or using a product or service. Meta Platforms, for one, agreed to pay $18 billion to settle US lawsuits over social media addiction. The Common Sense Media study, which can be downloaded for free, is available on this page . – Rappler.com

title: FACT CHECK: Contrary to claim, Marcos has no plans to resign
body: Claim: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is planning to resign. Rating: FALSE Why we fact-checked this: The Facebook reel bearing the said claim has already received 1 million views, 17,100 reactions, 9,800 comments, and 1,400 shares as of writing. While the video was posted on September 18, it continues to gain traction up to this date with a new comment written on Thursday, October 7. It shows a news graphic with Marcos’ photo. The person talking in the Facebook reel says, “ Good news ‘to mga idol sa lahat ng mga DDS: Bongbong Marcos may plano na mag-resign. Automatic na si VP Sara diyan na maging presidente kapag nag-resign si Bongbong Marcos .” (Good news to all the DDS out there: Bongbong Marcos plans to resign. VP Sara would automatically become president if Bongbong Marcos steps down.) “ Anong masasabi ninyo mga idol kapag nag-resign na si Bongbong Marcos kasi ito talaga ang plano niya ngayon ,” he added. (What do you think, folks, if Bongbong Marcos resigns? Because that is actually his plan right now.) The facts: Marcos did not say that he is planning to resign. The false claim is actually the opposite of the news that the person was showing in the video. On September 18, GMA News posted a news graphic with Marcos’ photo and a headline that reads, “Marcos has no plans to resign, Palace says.” In an interview with GMA News’ Unang Balita, Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said, “ Unang-una, walang magre-resign (First of all, no one will resign),” responding to the previous statements from Vice President Sara Duterte’s camp that she is willing to take over as president. Earlier in September, during her speech in a rally with her supporters before the Quezon City Regional Trial Court, Duterte called on Marcos to resign, citing the problems currently faced by the country under his administration. No resignation: Marcos and Malacañang have always been firm in rejecting resignation calls. In May 2025, the President said that quitting his post will not do anything good. Instead, Marcos said that he is reviewing his performance as a president through ratings. “I’ll share with you one thing. That as we were doing the performance review, and when we see shortfalls in performance, I don’t leave it at that. I look and ask why is that the case? And that is why we ask all the heads of agencies to also submit their courtesy resignations because we have to look at deeper, not just look at the secretary,” he said. Malacañang, in November 2025, also reiterated that resignation is not an option for Marcos. “ Option ba ito? The President is still working and keeps on working for the country, so hindi option sa administration, sa Pangulo, ang pagbibitiw ,” said Castro. (Is this an option? The President is still working and keeps on working for the country so it is not an option for the administration and the President to resign.) Previous fact checks: Rappler has previously fact-checked similar false claims about Marcos’ resignation: FACT CHECK: Marcos remains president, did not resign FACT CHECK: Marcos not resigning following flood control corruption rallies FACT CHECK: Marcos not resigning, video twists podcast remarks FACT CHECK: Lacson did not demand Marcos’ resignation FACT CHECK: Video of rally calling for Marcos’ resignation is AI-generated FACT CHECK: Marcos not forced out of Malacañang – Angelee Kaye Abelinde/Rappler.com Angelee Kaye Abelinde is a student journalist based in Naga City, and an alumna of Rappler’s Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship 2024. Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

title: Russian oil refinery in Salavat hit by Ukraine, General Staff confirms
body:
An overnight Ukrainian strike on the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refinery in Russia's Bashkortostan region caused a large blaze at the plant, Ukraine's General Staff confirmed on Oct. 8.
Several images and videos show the moment the plant was struck, as well as thick smoke and fire coming from the grounds of the refinery.
"(The facility) is one of Russia's largest oil refining and petrochemical complexes," the General Staff said in a post on social media. "The facility has a processing capacity of up to 10 million tons of hydrocarbon feedstock per year and produces automotive gasoline, diesel fuel, fuel oil, bitumen, polyethylene, and other oil refining and petrochemical products."
The Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat facility is located some 1,300 kilometers (800 miles) from the front line in Ukraine.
The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) drones previously hit the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat plant in September, a source in the agency told the Kyiv Independent on Sept. 24.
A fire broke out at the plant following several drone strikes, the source said. Local authorities have also confirmed the attack.

title: Why the AI Determinism Argument Annoys Me
body:
First up, who the heck am *I* to have an opinion on this?
Well, I am a computer scientist specializing in deterministic sequences used in randomized algorithms.
Read my peer reviewed published papers on blue noise, read my blog posts on irrational numbers and the benefit of using them as pseudorandom number sources, read what I’ve written about using light weight cryptography to shuffle and group objects in constant time, with random access and inverse lookups using the Chinese remainder theorem. Watch my YouTube videos of the same. I find these things fascinating, so if you are interested, here are some of my favorites:
Beyond White Noise For Real Time Rendering (YouTube): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tethAU66xaA Constant Time Stateless Shuffling And Grouping (EA Blog Post): https://www.ea.com/seed/news/constant-time-stateless-shuffling Irrational Numbers (Blog Post): https://blog.demofox.org/2020/07/26/irrational-numbers/
Ok so i know about determinism, but do I know about AI and ML? I stick to the bare metal of ML and don’t like to go into the highly abstracted levels that most modern ML people do, but yes. I know backprop, dual numbers (forward mode AD), ADAM, and other random things. During the AI winter, I kept myself warm implementing neural networks in excel (when I wasn’t working on game dev).
Machine Learning For Game Developers (YouTube): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sTAqWRsEiy0
I also have an ML patent (pending) I won’t describe here, that is pretty interesting. Unfortunately, I fear it would help something like terminator’s skynet to exist. I tried to park the patent at a game company, thinking that would be safe, but now the American Fascist Party’s very own Jared Kushner and the Saudi prince who ordered the murder and dismemberment of Jamal Khashoggi own EA, and my patent, so RIP to humanity i guess.
Funny thing – a core feature of that patent is deterministic ML.
Ok so it annoys me that people complain that LLMs aren’t deterministic. I am annoyed because it isn’t that they want it to be deterministic, it’s that they want it to be RIGHT, and they don’t even realize it.
Considering each square, “When asked the same question multiple times”… :
The argument that determinism is the problem with LLMs says that you want option #2 or #4 and are fine with either. You are saying “I don’t care if it’s right, I just want it to do the same thing every time”. If you are thinking this, good job: you are now breathing manually. (Note this feeling: This is what it feels like to be wrong. Do you feel it often?)
What people really want is #3 and #4. They don’t care if it’s random or not, they just want it to be CORRECT.
Any “random variation” within being correct doesn’t make it any less correct. If it did, you wouldn’t consider it correct, and it wouldn’t be part of box #3.
Yes i even am talking about LLMs generating code or executing some set of steps that a python script is probably better suited to. If you are in box #4, you are 100% happy. If you are in box #3, you are still fully happy because what it is doing is CORRECT. If you say “yeah but i need zero variation in the code generation or the utility execution”, ok so that’s part of your definition of CORRECT and you get that. If you don’t get what you consider correct, it is in a different box.
You can run an LLM deterministically – both during training, and during inference. Set the seed of all pseudorandom number generators used, make sure nothing runs on CPU or GPU threads in a way that is non deterministic. This is fully possible and not even a big stretch. If you only know vibe coding you might think this is magic, but unfortunately it’s mundane as heck.
Would that make you happy? Of course not. It puts you into box 2 or 4 for every question you ask, but you don’t get to choose which box you end up in. The only variation in the network output comes from your input.
(Oh no, did i forget rounding modes? Go learn how an RTS works before you have an opinion about the feasibility of program determinism across different machines and compilers.)
“But bro – you are mixing up terms. The network represents a distribution in high dimensional space and the output is a single sample. You taking one sample using a a single pseudorandom value as input doesn’t make it deterministic.”
Think about square number 3 in my lovely MS Paint ™ diagram. It gives random but correct answers when asked the same question repeatedly. How is that possible? BECAUSE IT’S A PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTION WITH WIDER SUPPORT.
Square #4 has a ~dirac delta as a distribution. That is the only difference.
Yes, I know it’s a distribution, so what.
There’s a debate about whether the universe is deterministic or not.
As best as we can tell, it is absolutely deterministic, except perhaps at the quantum level, which somehow seems to get laundered into determinism at large scales. Maybe through the central limit theorem, for all we know.
If that’s true, it is deterministic already so you can relax. Everything is exactly as you say you want it to be. Still not happy? THAT’S BECAUSE YOU DON’T CARE ABOUT DETERMINISM, YOU WANT IT TO BE RIGHT.
Also, maybe take a couple steps back from the kool-aid bowl. That stuff is bad for your health.

title: Scores Injured as Motorcyclists, Ticket Sellers Clash over Levies in Ondo
body: Fidelis David in Akure Scores of people have been injured following a violent clash between commercial motorcycle operators, popularly known as Okada riders, and ticket sellers in Akure, the Ondo State capital, over alleged multiple levies imposed on the riders. The clash, which occurred in some parts of the Akure metropolis, was triggered by disagreements over the collection of levies from commercial motorcycle operators, with the riders accusing ticket sellers of demanding additional payments after they had already paid similar charges. The dispute centred on an alleged daily levy being collected under the guise of an ‘emblem’, with some of the riders accusing the Chairman of Akure South Local Government Area, Hon. Gbenga Fasua, of imposing multiple charges on them. The development reportedly disrupted commercial motorcycle operations in some parts of the city as the riders protested over what they described as multiple and unauthorised collections. One of the riders, Jimoh Akindele, accused the Akure South council chairman of directing ticket sellers to collect additional levies from operators despite payments already made for similar purposes. “We see this as double taxation because we cannot imagine Hon. Fasua selling an emblem for riders in Akure South. He claimed it was meant for Akure South Local Government Area, and they are collecting N7,000 from us as a total package. “This is totally wrong. He sent boys to move around different locations to collect levies from us. We learnt that the levy is not for the state government but Akure South Local Government Area, and the state government is not aware of it. That is why we are saying enough is enough! We cannot take it anymore,” he said. Another rider, who identified himself simply as Adekunle, said the multiple collections had become a major burden on operators already struggling to make a living. He said: “We are not against paying government levies, but there should be transparency. You cannot collect money from us several times for the same purpose. “We pay in the morning and another person comes later to demand another ticket. When we ask questions, nobody gives us a satisfactory explanation. They will say it is for Akure South Local Government Area. “Fasua is even using the local security outfit that he set up known as Tiger Base, to terrorise Okada riders in Akure, and this is very wrong.” Adekunle appealed to the state government led by Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa to urgently intervene in the dispute to prevent the situation from escalating, saying the alleged multiple collections had heightened tension between commercial motorcycle operators and ticket sellers. However, reacting to the allegations, Fasua denied knowledge of the controversial collections, saying the alleged emblem was not authorised by him and that no proceeds from its sale had accrued to Akure South Local Government. Fasua said he became aware of the controversy after encountering some of the protesters in front of the Government Office, where they were raising concerns over the alleged collection of additional stickers. According to him, the protesters told him that they had already collected stickers earlier in the year, including one issued during the Ogun Festival period, but were being asked to obtain another one, which would make it the third sticker for the year. He said he intervened by asking those involved to suspend the collection pending clarification from the state government, adding that he intended to discuss the matter with Governor Aiyedatiwa. “I told them to hold on with these sales. Let’s get clarity from the governor. I subsequently went to about two other spots and told them to hold on with these sales until we get clarity from the governor. “I am the representative of the people of Akure. I was voted for, and of course, I am their voice. That was why I said, let me speak with the governor about it,” Fasua said. On the allegation that the controversial emblem emanated from his office and the Akure South Local Government, the chairman said the use of the council’s name on the emblem did not mean that it was authorised by him. “Where the issue lies is that they wrote the name of my local government on it, but it does not come from me. When they showed me the ones they had taken-the first one for the year and the second one-they were using the name of my local government to generate funds. I know nothing about it, and not even a dime has come to the local government area,” he said. Fasua added that he personally photographed one of the emblems shown to him, saying the amount displayed on it was over N7,000. “I remember I snapped one copy of the emblem they showed me. It is N7,000-something. So, if this thing is being sold at N3,000 or N7,000-something and not even one naira comes to the local government, that is why I said let me speak with the Governor first,” he said. The council chairman appealed to the protesters and other parties involved in the dispute to desist from actions capable of disrupting peace in Akure. “My message is that they should stop such. We are not aware of those things, and specifically, Akure is known for peace. My message is, please, let’s avoid any form of protest or action that will disrupt the peace we enjoy in Akure,” Fasua said.

title: Saab and GKN Aerospace sign long-term deal to expand Gripen E/F engine support
body: The agreement covers propulsion support, capability development and contributions to Saab’s international Gripen campaigns. It sets out how the companies will work together on engines and propulsion, with the aim of strengthening the aircraft’s offering for Sweden and overseas customers. “Gripen is one of the world’s most advanced fighter aircraft systems,” said Sara Eklöf, senior vice-president for Governmental Solutions – defence and space at GKN Aerospace. “This agreement strengthens our collaboration with Saab and expands GKN Aerospace’s role in supporting the long-term development of the Gripen E/F propulsion system.” GKN Aerospace already maintains Gripen engines and provides technical support in Sweden. The deal extends that cooperation to long-term capability development and broader support for current and future Gripen operators. “Gripen is built on strong industrial partnerships,” said Johan Segertoft, head of Saab’s Gripen Business Unit. “By deepening our collaboration with GKN Aerospace, we strengthen the conditions for continued development, high availability for our customers and a competitive offering in the global market.” The companies will continue exploring ways to strengthen Sweden’s long-term capability related to the Gripen E/F engine. GKN Aerospace also holds the type certificate for the RM12 engine, which powers the Gripen C/D fleet.

title: Bwala admits Tinubu economic reforms increased poverty
body:
The Special Adviser to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has acknowledged that the administration’s economic reforms increased poverty but insisted that the government has made significant progress since introducing the measures.
Mr Bwala spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday while defending the reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration since it assumed office in May 2023.
The reforms include removing the petrol subsidy and unifying the foreign exchange market.
The measures triggered a sharp rise in the cost of living, with households and businesses facing higher transportation, logistics and production costs.
Mr Bwala acknowledged that the immediate impact of the reforms was painful and that more Nigerians fell into poverty during the process. He, however, argued that the hardship was an unavoidable consequence of economic restructuring.
“Please let it be clear, even to the opposition, the reason why you have this number of poor people and some of these doomsday analytics that people are giving is that we undertook a reform.
“There is no part of the world where, if you start a reform like that, there will not be discomfort. More people went down to poverty, acknowledged, but since the reform started to today, we have made marked progress, which is what we have spent the last three years talking to Nigerians about.
“So, you cannot discount that even though there are quite a number of our population that are poor, which we admit, but we have made progress so far,” he said.
Mr Bwala’s comments come days after Mr Tinubu, in his Independence Day address, said the reforms had helped improve economic stability, citing lower inflation, rebuilt foreign reserves and a more stable foreign exchange market. The president said the government had moved from the reform phase to a focus on prosperity and reducing the cost of living.
Mr Bwala also said he was confident Mr Tinubu would perform better in the 2027 presidential election than he did in 2023.
Mr Tinubu won the 2023 election with 8,794,726 votes, defeating Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party by 1.81 million votes and Peter Obi of the Labour Party by 2.69 million votes.
Mr Bwala predicted that the president would widen his margin over his opponents in the next election.
“Let me tell you and let me say it categorically, and I will be happy to come back. The margin of gap that President Bola Tinubu will give every one of these candidates will be so much that you won’t believe it,” he said.
He attributed his confidence partly to the growing support for Mr Tinubu among governors elected on opposition party platforms.
Several governors have defected from opposition parties to the ruling All Progressives Congress since the 2023 election. Mr Bwala said he expected more governors to support Mr Tinubu in 2027 than did so during the last presidential election.

title: AI agent designs a complete RISC-V CPU from a 219-word spec sheet in 12 hours
body:
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .
AI chip design startup Verkor.io claims, in a research paper published in March, that its agentic AI system, Design Conductor, autonomously produced a complete RISC-V CPU core — taking a 219-word requirements document and generating a verified, layout-ready design in 12 hours, which is orders of magnitude faster than the standard 18- to 36-month timelines seen in commercial chip design.
This is the first time an autonomous agent has built a working CPU from spec to GDSII layout file, according to Verkor. The resulting processor — VerCore — is a five-stage pipelined, in-order, single-issue core that met timing at 1.48 GHz on the ASAP7 7nm process design kit, scoring 3,261 on the CoreMark benchmark. Verkor’s paper goes into detail on the pipeline architecture, which includes instruction fetch, decode, execute, memory, and writeback stages with early branch resolution and operand forwarding.
During optimization, the system independently implemented a fast Booth-Wallace multiplier that clocked at 2.57 GHz and a one-cycle branch penalty design that the agent selected after implementing and testing both one-cycle and two-cycle variants. Verkor compares VerCore's CoreMark performance to Intel's Celeron SU2300, a 2011 mobile chip based on the Penryn architecture . A five-stage in-order core with no caches and no out-of-order execution is a fairly straightforward design by industry standards. Verkor's own paper notes that leading-edge chips cost north of $400 million and take 18 to 36 months with engineering teams in the hundreds, but VerCore is far simpler than those designs. That said, the 12-hour timeline is still notable for a fully autonomous run from spec to layout, even if it did require "many tens of billions of tokens" at this comparatively pale level of complexity.
VerCore hasn’t been physically fabricated and was instead verified in simulation using Spike, a reference RISC-V ISA simulator, and ASAP7 is an academic process design kit, not a production 7nm node. Verkor says it can run a uCLinux variant in simulation. Verkor's paper is candid about the limitations of the underlying language models, admitting that the agent sometimes “underestimates the complexity of work that is required to address certain issues.” For example, in one case, when failing to meet timing, Design Conductor tried to make major changes to "deepen the pipeline, instead of looking for simpler explanations." In another case, the researchers observed the model reasoning about Verilog, an event-driven language, as if it were sequential code. "While we found that this did not impact DC's ability to achieve functional correctness, it made it more challenging for DC to debug timing issues," the researchers explained. The researchers estimate that five to 10 human experts will still be required to guide the system toward a production-ready chip. In addition, compute requirements grow non-linearly as design complexity increases, which makes the whole process less practical on a commercial scale. Verkor said it plans to release VerCore's RTL source and build scripts by the end of April, and the company also intends to showcase an FPGA implementation at DAC (the annual Electronic Design Automation Conference). Previous AI chip design efforts, such as the Chinese researchers who produced a RISC-V CPU in under five hours in 2023 and the more recent QiMeng project , used different methodologies and architectures. Verkor’s Design Conductor handles the full design process from spec to GDSII autonomously, though it shares the same limitation that all other AI-designed chips have: no physical silicon.

title: State Veterans Support Service to be established in Ukraine – Veterans Affairs Ministry
body:
The State Veterans Support Service is to be established in Ukraine on the basis of the State Veteran Space digital platform, the Ministry of Veterans Affairs reports.
"A State Veterans Support Service will be created in Ukraine. Its goal is to change the approach to supporting veterans: instead of independently searching for necessary services and institutions, a person will have an assigned specialist who will coordinate their entire route and monitor the outcome," the ministry's statement reads.
It is noted that the Service will operate at both central and regional levels, incorporating a nationwide network of specialists dedicated to supporting war veterans and demobilized individuals.
"Upon receiving information about demobilization or a military medical commission conclusion, a person's data will automatically flow into the 'Oskar' CRM system. Following this, the veteran will be assigned a support specialist, who must contact the individual within 24–48 hours," the department explained.
Specifically, during the initial contact, the specialist will assess the primary needs of the veteran: health status, prosthetics requirements, psychological condition, housing issues, and opportunities for economic self-realization.
Subsequently, an individual action plan will be formulated based on this assessment, which the veteran will be able to approve via the Diia application.
The support pathway will comprise five core stages: preparation for discharge from military service; transition to civilian life; health recovery and psychological support; economic independence and professional self-realization; and socialization and community participation.
Moving forward, the specialist will coordinate navigation through the entire pathway and ensure that essential services are not only assigned but actually delivered.
"The criterion for performance and support must not be the number of consultations or issued referrals, but the actual outcome for the veteran and their family," the Ministry of Veterans Affairs emphasized.
Among other measures, plans include reforming the workload assessment model for support specialists. Instead of the current model, where a single specialist may handle up to 100 cases, a point-based system will be introduced to account for the complexity of each individual case.

title: Kusum pharma assesses destroyed Ukrainian Sumy plant, shifts supply to India
body:
Pharmaceutical company Kusum is calculating the losses from the destruction of its plant in Sumy by the aggressor and is preparing to supply medicines from its manufacturing facilities in India.

"As for the medicines destroyed at the plant, we have not yet finalized our calculation of the losses. There are still stocks of some medicines in warehouses, but we cannot yet forecast how long they will last," the company told Interfax-Ukraine.

Kusum said that production is currently being distributed among its manufacturing facilities in India.

"If no regulatory obstacles are artificially created, they are ready to gradually begin producing the medicines that were specifically manufactured in Sumy," Kusum said.

At the same time, the company emphasized that its production in India complies with European GMP standards and that its plants have regulatory accreditation in 22 countries worldwide.

title: US begins direct talks with Myanmar in reversal of isolation attempts following military coup
body: The Trump administration has begun direct talks with Myanmar's military-installed government, according to US officials and others familiar with the outreach, in a sharp reversal of Washington's efforts to isolate the country's generals after the 2021 coup.The US Assistant Secretary of State for Intelligence and Research, Michael Vance, played a leading role in the outreach, which has focused on shutting down scam centers that target Americans but could lead to broader engagement, including on Myanmar's rare-earth mineral deposits, according to seven current and former officials and others familiar with the policy shift.Vance joined talks with coup leader-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing in the capital Naypyitaw on September 15-16. The meeting was aimed at securing the release of American businessman Adam Castillo but also provided an opening for further engagement, four of the people said.Last month's meeting - the highest‑level contact since the coup - underscores a broader Trump‑administration foreign policy tilt away from democracy promotion toward transactional engagement.The presence of Vance, who was confirmed as the State Department's top intelligence official in August, and his ongoing role in US policy toward Myanmar have not been previously reported.Min Aung Hlaing, the former military chief, remains under US sanctions for human rights abuses, including the 2016-2017 mass killings and expulsions of hundreds of thousands of Rohingya Muslims that Washington declared a genocide. Less than two weeks after Vance's visit, Myanmar's military conducted an airstrike on a crowded marketplace in Rakhine state, killing over 50 people and injuring scores more, according to United Nations human rights officials.The State Department said it engages with all groups in Myanmar on issues affecting US interests and raises the need to cease violence and release political prisoners.“You don't solve problems by ignoring them. You solve problems by addressing them,” spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a statement.A spokesperson for the military-backed government did not respond to a request for comment. Min Aung Hlaing, who has cited electoral fraud to justify the coup and labeled his opponents as terrorists, is seeking international legitimacy for his nominally civilian government.Current and former officials say Vance has met players from all sides of Myanmar's complex conflict and helped shape the Trump administration's policy toward the country.Intelligence chiefs - such as Vance - do not typically steer policy because of concerns about compromising analytic independence.“If you let policy dictate to intelligence, you can't be sure you're getting a real honest assessment of the facts,” said Richard Betts, an adjunct senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations who has consulted for US intelligence agencies.Pigott declined to address Vance's role but said the administration “operates as a team with the president as the lead.”Former US official detained in Myanmar, US holds negotiations for releaseCastillo, a former head of the American Chamber of Commerce in Myanmar, was detained at Yangon airport on June 11 by Myanmar authorities on what his supporters have described as trumped-up charges. The US government has not commented on whether Castillo was wrongfully detained.People familiar with the matter said White House, National Security Council, and State Department officials held back-channel negotiations with Myanmar officials to secure his release. One person said Myanmar asked only "to have an official engagement at the right level with the US government" in return.Castillo declined to comment beyond crediting US President Donald Trump for his release.The meeting builds on a June meeting between US and Myanmar officials in Tokyo also involving Vance, four people said. One of the people said officials from the Treasury Department, which oversees sanctions, the Department of Homeland Security, and the Pentagon took part.It was unclear who represented Myanmar at the talks.Vance, who became involved in Myanmar policy while advising Vice President JD Vance on Asian affairs, has also met in person and virtually with the democratic opposition and ethnic armed groups fighting the military, five of the people said.US looking to shut down Myanmar fraud operationsA major focus of the US push is getting Myanmar's help in shuttering scam hubs operating on its territory that run romance and other frauds, which have scammed Americans out of billions of dollars. Two people familiar with the matter said the FBI has had direct contact with Myanmar's authorities on cyber scams.Researchers say many scams are run from areas under militia control, with some proceeds flowing to the military, raising doubts about whether Myanmar's leaders are serious about enforcement.US officials also discussed access to Myanmar's massive deposits of heavy rare earths that are used in electric vehicles and wind turbines. US officials acknowledge obstacles: the deposits mainly lie in territory held by ethnic armies fighting Myanmar's military government, and China, currently the main importer, could see any US role as a challenge.Still, with Washington seeking to diversify supply chains away from China, Myanmar's deposits remain a recurring topic in conversations, the people said.After the 2021 coup, US president Joe Biden's administration froze Myanmar's assets at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and imposed sanctions on senior officers and military‑linked businesses.In 2022, Congress authorized non-lethal support for the opposition, funding early-warning systems for airstrikes and incentives for officers to defect.Most of those programs were cut during Trump's foreign-aid overhaul last year, according to four current and former officials and State Department correspondence with Congress reviewed by Reuters.The State Department said its engagement with the military government does not diminish its relationships with other groups. The US continues to provide assistance to areas outside military control, it said, without detailing that aid.Top Foreign Affairs Committee Democrat decries shift in Myanmar relationsRep. Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said the shift was “contrary to both our values and our interests.”“By engaging Min Aung Hlaing while failing to implement congressionally mandated sanctions and deploy appropriated democracy funding, Secretary (Marco) Rubio is ceding US leadership and providing this murderous regime greater international legitimacy,” Meeks said in a statement to Reuters.Myanmar's government, installed after elections that rights groups criticized as a sham, has hired lobbyists to press its case in Washington.In April, Roger Stone, a longtime Trump adviser, began consulting for DCI Group on behalf of Myanmar's Ministry of Information, according to Foreign Agents Registration Act filings. Stone was convicted in 2019 of obstructing a congressional investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 election. Trump later pardoned him.A newsletter distributed by DCI warned in June that Washington risked losing access to critical minerals if it did not engage with Myanmar.

title: Ukraine is buying 135 mobile shelters for border crossings as Russian drones reach from the Danube to Poland
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine plans 135 basic mobile shelters for civilians at 28 of its border crossings, the State Agency for Restoration and Infrastructure Development said on 7 October. Since the start of September, Russian drones have repeatedly struck crossings on Ukraine's borders with Moldova and Romania. Since mid-September, strikes have also reached the Polish border near the Yahodyn crossing in Volyn Oblast. On 13 September, a Russian drone strike set a gas station near the crossing on fire. On 28 September, the blast wave from another strike damaged the checkpoint building. On 25 September, First Deputy Minister for Restoration, Infrastructure and Transport Serhii Derkach said Ukraine is exploring with its neighbors whether some checkpoints could move onto their territory. No agreement has been reported. On 2 October, Moldovan Interior Minister Daniella Misail-Nichitin said Moldova had set up shelters next to its crossings with Ukraine and started relocating staff from joint checkpoints. 135 shelters for travelers and border staff The shelters will stand at the crossings and on the roads leading to them. Regional recovery services in Vinnytsia, Odesa, Chernivtsi, Zakarpattia, and Volyn oblasts are running the purchases. The agency said the shelters will make the border safer for people crossing it and for checkpoint staff. Border regions where Ukraine plans to install shelters. Map: Euromaidan Press In Chernivtsi Oblast, one of the 10 tenders the agency lists on Prozorro, Ukraine's public procurement system, covers eight shelters for 50 people each and three for 20 each, Ukrinform reported . They will stand on the approach road to the Porubne–Siret international crossing on the Romanian border. The work is expected to cost UAH 38.5 million (about $855,000), excluding VAT. Russian strikes on crossings On 5 October, at about 09:38, a projectile fell near the Palanca–Maiaky–Udobne crossing on the Moldovan border. It ricocheted off the ground into a shuttle bus parked by the barrier and also damaged a control booth. One Moldovan border officer suffered light injuries, and the crossing was suspended, Moldova's Border Police said , linking the incident to Russia's attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure. Moldovan authorities did not specify the projectile's type or origin. Overnight on 9 September, Russian drones struck the Starokozache crossing with Moldova, killing two people and injuring three. On 1 September, Russian Shahed drones hit the Orlivka ferry crossing on the Danube, opposite Romania's Isaccea, and temporarily shut it down. Another Russian strike on 6 September halted the crossing again.
