title: Trump to give Elon Musk top US science medal
body: President Donald Trump will present close ally Elon Musk and other tech bosses with the top US scientific award at a ceremony on Thursday, the White House said. Google co-founder Sergei Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD chief Lisa Su will also receive the National Medal of Science at the “Science: A New Golden Age” summit. Computer mogul Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella will get the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, the top award in its field. “The Trump Administration is grateful for the contributions of these incredible leaders in science and technology. These recipients are helping ensure America keeps leading the world in innovation,” White House spokeswoman Liz Huston said in a statement to AFP on Wednesday. Space X and Tesla tycoon Musk has returned to Trump’s good graces after they fell out last year over his role heading the cost-cutting Department of Government Efficiency. He was also the biggest donor to Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign. Musk and Huang were both at Trump’s state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping last month. Along with other tech bosses they were also at the White House last week for talks in which tech chiefs promised to self-regulate against possible threats from artificial intelligence. Trump has dismissed warnings that AI could wipe out humanity, insisting it is crucial for what he calls the “Golden Age” of the US economy in his second term. But Trump’s Republican Party could lose control of Congress in midterm elections next month amid voter concerns over the Iran war and the cost of living. AFP The post Trump to give Elon Musk top US science medal appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: ECG warns customers against fake meter sales, MoMo fraud
body: The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has warned customers across the country against fraudsters posing as its staff or agents to sell fake meters and demand payments through personal mobile money accounts. The company says customers should not send money to private MoMo numbers for electricity services. ECG General Manager for External Communications, Dr Charles Nii Ayiku Ayiku, said the company operates a fully cashless payment system, with customers required to make payments through official channels. “ECG runs a fully cashless system,” Dr Ayiku said. “All payments must go through the ECG Power App or the shortcode *226#. Money sent to a personal MoMo number does not reach the company and will not reflect on your account.” Dr Ayiku identified the sale of meters by individuals as one of the schemes being used to defraud customers. He said some individuals pose as ECG staff or agents and offer to supply and install new meters for a fee. Others advertise meters on WhatsApp and social media platforms, including TikTok, before asking customers to make payments. In some cases, customers receive unregistered meters which ECG may treat as an illegal connection. “ECG does not sell meters through individuals,” he said. He urged customers seeking new meters or electricity services to use official ECG channels, including district offices and the ECG Power App, and to pay only approved fees through the company’s official payment platforms. The second scheme involves phone calls from individuals claiming to be ECG staff. According to Dr Ayiku, the caller may tell a customer that their meter is ready and then provide a personal MoMo number for payment. “Our staff does not ask customers to pay into personal mobile money wallets,” he said. “Treat any such call as a fraud attempt.” He said the fraudsters often rely on urgency to pressure customers into making payments before verifying the information. Dr Ayiku urged customers to take time to confirm any request purportedly coming from ECG before making a payment. He advised customers to: Never send money to a personal MoMo number provided by someone claiming to be an ECG employee. Avoid buying meters from individuals, online adverts or WhatsApp contacts. Make electricity payments only through the ECG Power App or *226#. Keep PINs, passwords and verification codes confidential. Ask anyone visiting their home or business on behalf of ECG to produce a valid staff identification card. End suspicious calls and report the number to ECG and the police. “Pay only through the ECG Power App or *226#,” Dr Ayiku said. “Treat all other payment requests as fraud and report them.”

title: I don’t want my children’s English identity questioned – Badenoch
body: Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has defended the British identity of her mixed-race children, saying she does not want to live in a country where their English identity is questioned. Badenoch, MP for North West Essex, made the remarks during her speech at the Conservative Party Conference 2026 on Wednesday, while criticising Reform UK MPs over what she described as attempts to question people’s identities. “I don’t want to live in a country run by people who threaten journalists, who call veterans traitors, and debate whether my mixed-race children are English,” she said. “I don’t want to explain to my son when we’re watching our brilliant England team play football that some people don’t think our black players are English,” she said. She recalled former England internationals Ian Wright and John Barnes, saying their English identity was not questioned in the same way. “I remember back in the day when Ian Wright and John Barnes were playing, nobody was questioning whether they were English,” Badenoch said. “We certainly didn’t have sitting MPs questioning whether they were English,” she added. Badenoch warned against what she described as attempts to take Britain backwards, saying the country should not accept such divisions. “We must not let these people take us backwards. That is not the country we are,” she said. She also accused Reform UK MPs of openly questioning people’s identities, drawing a distinction between the party and the Conservatives. “Reform MPs are openly questioning people’s identity. They are not like us. We are not like them,” Badenoch said. “We are different. We are the Conservative Party,” she added. The post I don’t want my children’s English identity questioned – Badenoch appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Wizz Air cancels winter season flights to Abu Dhabi and Dubai
body: Wizz Air has postponed the planned restart of its Abu Dhabi and Dubai routes, cancelling all flights to and from both destinations for the winter season. The airline had planned to operate UAE flights from October 25 to March 27. The low-cost airline said last month that it was resuming flights to Abu Dhabi and Dubai, alongside routes to Jeddah in Saudi Arabia and Amman in Jordan. The airline had said this week it would delay the launch of some routes to Abu Dhabi until January, following security updates from Europe's aviation regulator. "Regional airspace restrictions extended on September 30 require significantly longer routings to these destinations, increasing flight times and costs and making both A321neo and A321XLR operations commercially unviable under current conditions," the airline said in a statement to The National . It also confirmed that flights to and from Amman are affected by the EU Aviation Safety Agency's latest conflict zone information bulletin, which recommends that airlines do not operate within Jordanian airspace. "We regret the disruption to travel plans and will continue to monitor developments, reassessing operations as safety guidance and operating conditions evolve," Wizz Air said. International airlines have been forced to adjust schedules for Middle East flights in the aftermath of the US-Iran war as airspace restrictions persist. Wizz Air suspended its European-operated services to the Middle East in late February due to the regional conflict. The UAE services were part of a wider restoration of 12 routes and 49 weekly flights to the Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Jordan over the winter, providing 470,000 seats across services to nine European cities. The airline was set to resume operations after its low-cost subsidiary, Wizz Air Abu Dhabi, ceased operations in September 2025.

title: VFD Group Appoints Ijeoma Emezie-Ezigbo as Deputy Managing Director
body: VFD Group Plc, a leading investment company with interests across financial services, technology, capital markets and other strategic sectors, has announced the appointment of Ijeoma Emezie-Ezigbo as deputy managing director and executive director, effective October 5, 2026. The appointment marks a significant step in the group’s institutional development, reinforcing its governance structure, executive leadership depth and long-term succession planning. The appointment, disclosed in a notice filed with Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) on October 2, 2026, reflects VFD Group’s continued commitment to building an institution designed for sustainable growth beyond the contributions of any single individual. Emezie-Ezigbo brings more than two decades of experience spanning corporate finance, transaction advisory, mergers and acquisitions, business valuation and strategic financial management across Nigeria, Canada and other African markets. Most recently, she served as Partner and Head of Transaction Services, West Africa, at KPMG Nigeria, where she led transaction advisory engagements across the region. Her career also includes roles at Stanbic IBTC Group, IBM Canada and Canadian Tire Corporation. Her academic and professional credentials include a First-Class Honours degree in Business Administration, specializing in Marketing, from the University of Nigeria; a Master of Finance degree from Cass Business School, London; and completion of the Advanced Management Programme at Lagos Business School. She is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria, an Associate Chartered Certified Accountant in the United Kingdom, a Chartered Professional Accountant in Ontario, Canada, and a Certified Valuation Analyst. Speaking on her appointment, Group Managing Director, VFD Group Plc, Nonso Okpala, said: “Our institutionalization journey requires us to build governance structures, leadership capacity and succession frameworks that are sustainable beyond any individual. The creation of the deputy managing director role reflects our commitment to strengthening executive oversight, deepening institutional resilience and positioning VFD Group for its next phase of growth. Ijeoma’s depth of experience in transaction advisory, corporate finance and strategic leadership will contribute meaningfully to this ambition.” Commenting, Emezie-Ezigbo, said:“I am pleased to join VFD Group at this important stage of its institutional development. I look forward to working with the Board and executive leadership to strengthen governance, support strategic execution and contribute to building a resilient institution that creates sustainable long-term value for its stakeholders.” The appointment forms part of VFD Group’s broader institutionalisation strategy, focused on strengthening governance, enhancing leadership continuity and building the organisational capacity required to manage a growing portfolio of businesses across multiple markets. By deepening its executive leadership structure, the Group continues to reinforce its commitment to sustainable value creation, institutional resilience and long-term growth.

title: Google halts work on data centres as Finnish police probe suspected illegal logging
body:
Authorities ordered Google to suspend building work at two planned data centre sites following a complaint about the clearance of hundreds of hectares of forest.
The Finnish Supervisory Agency (known by its Finnish acronym LVV) has ordered Google to halt preparatory building work on two planned data centres, announced last month as part of the tech giant's 13 billion euro investment in Finland.
LVV's order was issued to Google's subsidiary Tuike Finland over concerns that the preparatory work for the data centres could "significantly alter the environment". This work included the removal of trees and topsoil, construction of site roads and storage areas, and changes to ditches, according to LVV.
In a statement, the agency added that the suspension order will remain in effect until environmental impact assessment procedures have been completed for the two sites at Muhos and Kajaani.
Yle understands that LVV began investigating Google's activities at the two sites after suspicions were raised publicly that illegal logging had taken place in the areas.
Tabloid Iltalehti reported on Wednesday that police have launched a preliminary investigation into the preparatory work carried out at the Muhos site.
Investigators are seeking to determine whether there is sufficient evidence of a crime having been committed to warrant the opening of a pre-trial probe.
IL added that the preliminary investigation began after a request was filed with police on 2 October by a private individual.
In its own statement, Google said it had "fallen short of our own high standards in this instance", adding it intends to fully comply with the LVV order.
Tuike Finland has until 14 October to provide an explanation to LVV.
Yle News reporter Ronan Browne explains why Google's investment announcement was not universally well-received.

title: 2027: Gov Yusuf reconciles Deputy Senate President Barau, Bichi
body: Gov. Abba Yusuf of Kano State has reconciled Deputy Senate President, Barau Jibrin, and a member of the House of Representatives, Abubakar Bichi, ahead of the 2027 general elections. This is contained in a statement by the governor’s media aide, Sanusi Bature, on Wednesday in Kano. Bature said that the governor facilitated the reconciliation meeting which lasted for two hours on Tuesday in Abuja. He said that the meeting provided an opportunity for the two prominent APC leaders to address their differences and discuss the need to work together for the collective interest of the party. Barau represented Kano-North Senatorial District, while Bichi represented Bichi Federal Constituency, and Chairman House Committee on Appropriations. The statement quoted the governor as urging the two political leaders and their supporters to bury their differences and grievances. According to Yusuf, the success of the APC requires unity, mutual understanding and collective commitment among its leaders and members. He underscored the importance of working together for the success of President Bola Tinubu and all the APC candidates in the elections. The governor urged party members to put the overall interest of the party above individual differences. “Political disagreements are part of democratic engagement, but such differences should not be allowed to undermine the unity, stability and progress of the party,” Yusuf was quoted as saying in the statement. Yusuf stressed that the APC remained one family, adding all stakeholders have a responsibility to resolve internal crises through dialogue, consultation and mutual respect. He enjoined supporters of the two leaders to embrace reconciliation, avoid inflammatory statements, character assassination and acts capable of promoting disuniting in the party. Yusuf expressed confidence that the reconciliation would contribute to greater unity among APC members, and strengthen its collective efforts ahead of the 2027 general elections. “Henceforth, I do not expect any of your supporters to come out and abuse one another. We must put a stop to these unnecessary distractions. “The APC is set to win all elective positions in Kano come 2027 by God’s Grace,” Yusuf said. The statement also quoted Barau and Bichi, as warning their supporters against fueling internal conflicts within the party in the state. They assured their continued support, loyalty and commitment toward the success of the party at the poll in the state. (NAN) The post 2027: Gov Yusuf reconciles Deputy Senate President Barau, Bichi appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Organized group smuggled over 4.7 tonnes of Ukrainian amber abroad disguised as Lithuanian – Prosecutor General's Office
body:
Under the procedural guidance of prosecutors from the Specialized Environmental Prosecutor's Office of the Office of the Prosecutor General of Ukraine, a notice of suspicion has been served to the organizer and three members of an organized group who allegedly set up the illegal export of Ukrainian amber disguised as stone of Lithuanian origin.
"To legalize the origin of the amber, they used companies in Ukraine and Lithuania. In April 2026, 5.9 tonnes of predominantly small amber, dust, and sand were imported from Lithuania to Ukraine, although the documents indicated significantly larger fractions," the Office of the Prosecutor General reported on its Telegram channel on Thursday.
The investigation established signs of fictitiousness in this import. "In particular, the drivers and the director of the Lithuanian company, who according to the documents were supposed to be involved in the transportation, were not actually in Lithuania, and the Ukrainian company did not make payments under the contract," the prosecutor's office clarified.
According to the agency, the illegally mined amber was subsequently sorted, weighed, and packaged for export at warehouses in several Ukrainian regions. "In the export documents, it was designated as goods of Lithuanian origin," the statement notes.
The prosecutor's office emphasizes that between April and June 2026, more than 4.7 tonnes of amber with an estimated value of UAH 10.7 million were moved abroad under this scheme.
More than 20 searches were conducted while documenting the group's activities.
Four individuals have been served notices of suspicion of smuggling goods committed using official position by an organized group (Part 3 of Article 201-3 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine).

title: Gombe NBA accuses AIG of extortion, police chief denies allegation
body: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Gombe Branch, has called for an investigation into allegations of extortion, intimidation and unprofessional conduct levelled against the Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG), Force Criminal Investigation Department (FCID) Annex, Gombe, Emmanuel Agene. The NBA also urged the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Tunji Disu, to investigate the allegations and take appropriate action if they are established. Chairman of the Gombe NBA, Barrister Alhassan Mu’azu, made the call on Wednesday evening after the branch’s monthly congress attended by lawyers, elders and past leaders of the association in Gombe. Mu’azu said the allegations followed a complaint by a member of the branch, Barrister E.S. Tizhe, who represented Ahmed Shuaibu Gara in a matter being investigated at the FCID Annex over an allegation of cyberbullying. According to him, Tizhe had gone to the police facility to represent his client in accordance with the constitutional right of a person under investigation to legal representation. Mu’azu cited Section 36 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which guarantees the right to counsel in criminal proceedings. He alleged that money was demanded as a condition for Gara’s release on bail, describing such a demand, if established, as unlawful and unconstitutional. The NBA chairman said the branch subsequently constituted a committee comprising senior members and elders to examine complaints concerning activities at the FCID Annex. “We have been gathering information. It is not only that of Tizhe. The branch had to constitute a committee of bar leaders and elders of the branch to investigate the activities and alleged extortion that is ongoing,” he said. Mu’azu said the committee had received information from other persons who allegedly had similar experiences and was preparing its report for submission to the appropriate authorities. He further alleged that some lawyers had been subjected to embarrassing treatment while representing their clients at the police facility, insisting that the NBA would not remain silent if the allegations were substantiated. “We are condemning this in the strongest terms. We are calling on the Inspector-General of Police to ensure that these activities are properly investigated and that the AIG, if found wanting, must be prosecuted,” he said. The NBA chairman said the branch was prepared to present whatever evidence it had to the police authorities or any competent investigative body. He also disclosed that Tizhe had petitioned the IGP over the matter and that the petition was subsequently referred to the AIG for his response. Mu’azu alleged that following the petition, Agene contacted him and asked him to appear before him. “The AIG kept calling me as the chairman of the branch that I should come, as if he wanted to arrest me. That is wrong,” he alleged. He said the NBA was awaiting the outcome of the IGP’s consideration of the petition, adding that the association could seek judicial redress if it was dissatisfied with the handling of the matter. “If the Inspector-General of Police is not taking action, we are going to join hands with our President of the Nigerian Bar Association. “We are going to ensure that we sue not only the AIG FCID Annex, but, if no action is taken, the entire Nigerian Police Force, including the Police Service Commission,” he said. Lawyer alleges N700,000 payments In his petition to the IGP dated September 7, 2026, Tizhe of Habu Abdu & Co. alleged that his client was arrested on August 14, 2026, following a complaint involving alleged criminal mischief and criminal defamation of character. The lawyer alleged that after his client’s statement was obtained, they were taken to the AIG’s office, where, he claimed, money was demanded for the suspect’s release. According to the petition, the AIG allegedly told him that his client would be granted bail and asked the suspect to “drop some money.” Tizhe alleged that his client initially paid ₦100,000. He further alleged that he was asked to submit his Call to Bar certificate and NBA identification card as part of the bail process. The lawyer said that after a surety was produced, he returned to collect the documents but alleged that they were not immediately released to him. Tizhe also alleged that his client was asked to pay another ₦100,000 on August 17, while he personally paid ₦500,000 on August 20 following what he described as threats. The petition further alleged that complainants seeking investigation of criminal complaints at the FCID Annex were sometimes required to pay between ₦50,000 and ₦100,000 before investigations could commence. Tizhe consequently asked the IGP to intervene and investigate what he described as alleged extortion at the FCID Annex, Gombe. AIG denies allegations Responding to the petition, however, AIG Agene denied demanding or receiving money from Gara, his surety or the lawyer. In a letter dated October 2, 2026, addressed to the IGP, Agene said the case involved an allegation of cyberbullying against Gara, adding that the suspect had made a statement during the investigation. The AIG said the lawyer subsequently requested administrative bail for his client and that the conditions for bail were communicated to the parties. He explained that the lawyer initially offered to stand as surety for the suspect but was informed that, as the suspect’s solicitor, he could not act as surety. According to him, the lawyer later produced a police auditor, Usman Adamu, as surety. Agene said he directed the lawyer to indicate that he knew the proposed surety and provide his Call to Bar certificate and identification card to facilitate the suspect’s production when required. He maintained that the documents were voluntarily submitted and denied that their submission was connected to any demand for money. “The AIG Force CID Annex Gombe neither had discussion of any money and/or received same from both the suspect, the surety and the solicitor,” Agene stated. He challenged the lawyer to produce evidence to substantiate the allegation that money was demanded or collected. The AIG also alleged that investigators subsequently had difficulty reaching the surety after the suspect’s release. Agene further accused the lawyer and the suspect of attempting to use social media to intimidate persons in pursuit of financial compensation, alleging that similar accusations had previously been made against the FCID Annex in 2025. He described the extortion allegation as an attempt to tarnish his reputation and questioned why he would demand ₦50,000, as alleged, after years of service in the police force. Agene insisted that he neither demanded nor received money from the suspect, the surety or the lawyer. He also asked the lawyer to appear with the suspect and surety for the continuation of the investigation. The AIG further warned that the lawyer could face legal action over alleged obstruction of an offender and defamation of character if the matter was not resolved. The allegations made by the NBA and the lawyer have not been judicially established, while the AIG has expressly denied wrongdoing. The matter remains subject to any investigation or other lawful proceedings that may follow. title: FACT CHECK: Jonvic Remulla remains DILG chief
body: Claim: Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla has been removed from office. Rating: FALSE Why we fact-checked this: A Facebook reel bearing the said claim has already received 239,000 views, 8,800 reactions, 1,000 shares, and 491 comments as of this posting. It was posted on September 20 and continues to gain traction up to this date. It shows photos of Remulla, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla, Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte, and vlogger Claire Contreras. The text on the video says, “ LIGWAK SI JONVIC REMULLA! SIBAK SA PUWESTO?! BOYING ISUSUNOD NA? (Jonvic Remulla out! Dismissed from his post?! Is Boying next?)” At 1:30 timestamp of the reel, it cites the statement of vlogger Contreras to support its claim: “ So, unahin na natin na binoldyak (sinita) ni bangag si Jonvic dahil nga ang daldal dahil nga nabuking o binuking niya yung plano talaga nilang pagdukot kay Harry Roque, kay Spox Harry at saka siyempre kay Zaldy Co. ” (So, let’s start with the fact that “Bangag” called out Jonvic for talking too much, specifically because he exposed their actual plan to abduct Harry Roque, Spox Harry, and, of course, Zaldy Co.) The facts: Remulla was not removed from his post. He remains as the DILG secretary , according to the department’s official website. There are also no official announcements from Malacañang or credible news reports that can support the claim. The false post stemmed from Remulla’s earlier claim that Roque’s application for asylum had been denied. It was eventually denied by Roque saying that, “My application for asylum has been submitted for resolution, and I continue to await the official decision of the competent Austrian asylum authorities.” Roque also claimed that Remulla’s statement was part of a “sinister plan,” adding that this may be conditioning the public for a possible attempt to abduct him. Remulla then admitted errors on his previous claims about Roque’s asylum bid. He said, “In his case, it’s neither denied nor accepted. So under the eyes of the law, he still does not have asylum.” Malacañang’s response: The Palace said Remulla might be called out over his incorrect asylum claim, but they still need to identify whether the Interior secretary made the statement in good or bad faith. “ Kung inamin naman po niyang siya ay nagkamali at hindi naman ipinapalagay na ito’y sinadya para ilihis ang kaisipan ng ating mga kababayan, maaaring ma-call out ang mga sinabing ito ng Secretary Jonvic. Pero tingnan po din natin kung ito ba ay sinadya o may bad faith ,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said. (If he has admitted to making a mistake and assuming it wasn’t intended to mislead the public, then Secretary Jonvic’s statements could certainly be called out. However, we should also examine whether it was intentional or done in bad faith.) Remulla also faced previous criticisms about his class suspension announcements but Marcos defended the Interior secretary and clarified that he will not be removed from office. Previous fact checks: Rappler has previously fact-checked similar false claims about public officials’ dismissal: FACT CHECK: Hontiveros, Romualdez not removed from office FACT CHECK: Ombudsman Remulla still in office, not dismissed by Supreme Court FACT CHECK: Bato dela Rosa not removed from Senate FACT CHECK: Padilla not ‘kicked out’ of Senate FACT CHECK: Congress did not remove Sara Duterte as VP FACT CHECK: Marcos remains president; no transfer of power to Sara Duterte – Angelee Kaye Abelinde/Rappler.com Angelee Kaye Abelinde is a student journalist based in Naga City, and an alumna of Rappler’s Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship 2024. Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

title: Why we withheld information on abducted NYSC members – Uzodimma
body:
Governor Hope Uzodimma of Imo State has praised security agencies for their “swift intervention” that led to the “safe release” of the 20 prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) abducted along the Onitsha-Owerri Road in the state.
In a statement on Wednesday, Mr Uzodimma said he was “particularly grateful to the security agencies for the discreet and collaborative manner in which they tackled the challenge”.
The governor thanked the parents and families of the prospective NYSC members for their patience and understanding throughout the difficult period.
PREMIUM TIMES previously reported that the abducted prospective NYSC members were released on Wednesday following a joint operation conducted by the State Security Service, military personnel and police operatives in Imo State, Nigeria’s South-east.
The prospective NYSC members were abducted at about 6:30 a.m. on 1 October along the Owerri-Onitsha Road by Umunoha in Imo State.
They were travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom States when the attack occurred.
In the Wednesday statement, Mr Uzodimma said the state government “deliberately adopted a discreet and coordinated approach to avoid releasing too much information” to Nigerians.
The governor explained that “because the issue involved the security of lives, the government was cautious about releasing too much information to the public, hence the discreet manner in which it was handled.”
He stressed that releasing excessive information about the abducted NYSC members could have jeopardised the investigation, arguing that the approach was necessary to ensure the safe return of the victims.
Mr Uzodimma assured that his administration would continue to support measures to protect citizens’ lives and property and ensure the country’s security.
The governor urged Nigerians to remain hopeful and continue to have faith in the federal government’s efforts to address security challenges in the country.

title: Trump says Iran conflict will be over 'shortly,' sending oil prices tumbling down
body:
NEW YORK, October 8. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump said the conflict with Iran would end soon after which global oil prices should plummet.
"What’s going to happen will be - as soon as that’s over which will be shortly - oil prices are going to come tumbling down," Trump said in an interview with CBS.
There is no more a nuclear weapon threat in Iran, the US leader emphasized.

title: Yemen downs Turkish-made Saudi drone over Taiz
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 08 (MNA) – Yemen's armed forces announced they downed a Turkish-made, Saudi-owned armed reconnaissance drone of the Bayraktar Akinci type in the skies over Taiz province.
Yahya Saree, spokesman for Yemen's armed forces, announced that YAF downed an armed reconnaissance drone of the Turkish-made Bayraktar Akinci type belonging to Saudi Arabia over Taiz province.
He added that the drone was targeted and downed using an appropriate weapon.
The spokesman for Yemen's armed forces also announced that the drone was targeted while carrying out a mission in the skies over Taiz province.

title: It was built to shield Russian crops from hail. Now it’s being pitched as a drone interceptor
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russia has shown a drone interceptor built on the Alazan, a civilian anti-hail rocket, Militarnyi reported . The sample went on display at a weapons exhibition that Russian dictator Vladimir Putin toured at the Chebarkul training range in the Urals on 2 October. Ukraine now sends drones at Russia by the hundreds, by Moscow's own count. Russia's Defense Ministry claimed its air defenses intercepted nearly 900 overnight into 6 October. Russia's missile-based air defense was built to repel aircraft raids and a few cruise missiles, not swarms of low-flying drones. In May, Ukrainian intelligence said Russia was adding four regiments, 24 battalions, and 162 batteries to counter Ukrainian strike drones. The converted Alazan, which Militarnyi calls an anti-drone system, is one more piece of that search. Meanwhile, the commander of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, Robert Brovdi, said his forces struck 300 Russian air-defense assets between January and 19 September. From hail reagent to shrapnel Based on the size of the sample on display, the interceptor builds on the Alazan-2M or Alazan-6 series, Militarnyi assessed. The outlet put the stated cost at up to $12,000 per unit but did not say who named the figure. In civilian service, the rocket flies about 10 km, climbs up to 8 km, and carries about 0.5 kg of reagent. For air defense, the developers plan to replace that reagent with a fragmentation warhead. Militarnyi's analysis of the published photos describes the front end as a steering assembly: four cruciform deflector fins, probably paired with a seeker or a fuze. At the rear sit folding stabilizers and the open nozzle of a solid-fuel motor, held in a metal cradle. Anti-drone missile based on the Alazan, 2 October 2026. Photo: kremlin.ru One sample among 300 exhibits The Kremlin's account of the visit lists more than 300 weapons on display, including interceptor drones, but does not mention the rocket. Propaganda channel Russia 1 aired the interceptor in its report from the visit, and the Kremlin pool of state news agency RIA posted photos. Read also Ukraine squeezes more defense out of Soviet-era stock, pairing Kub launcher and American RIM-7 interceptors to catch Russia’s jet-powered drones Ukrainian units hit record number of Russian air defense systems and radars in September, one of them 552 kilometers away Ukraine’s answer to Russia’s jet-powered Shaheds: a small new missile named Nika, heading into testing

title: France's Le Pen opposes Ukraine EU membership over farming fears
body:
French far-right politician Marine Le Pen spoke against EU membership for Ukraine on Oct. 7 by whipping up fears that Kyiv's agricultural sector would destroy France's.
Le Pen is leading the polls for France's April 2027 presidential election, and her stance on Ukraine and Russia has already become a key campaign issue for her and her competitors .
"If Ukraine were to enter the European Union, we would be the first to suffer," Le Pen claimed in a video posted to social media.
"We would be the losers, not only in terms of competition with a large agricultural country like Ukraine, but also in the sharing out of Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) (subsidies), because the CAP is a shrinking cake," Le Pen said.
The CAP is an EU program established in 1962 that subsidizes the EU's farming sector, allowing small and uncompetitive farms to continue to exist.
It is also at risk of being reduced already, as Brussels haggles over the bloc's 2028-2034 budget. The fear is that adding a large agricultural country such as Ukraine would exacerbate that situation further.
Le Pen's comments came one day after the European Commission published a communication on the future of enlargement , which noted that the bloc needs to seriously address how to integrate Ukraine's farming sector into the EU smoothly.
Ukraine "will and can become a member of the CAP. Under which conditions, this will be discussed," said the EU's Enlargement Commissioner, Marta Kos , at a press conference on Oct. 6.
"We also have to protect the farmers in the EU, and we are already discussing this subject with Ukraine," Kos added.
Agriculture Minister Taras Vysotskyi said, "We understand the sensitivity of certain segments for European farmers," in written comments shared with the Kyiv Independent.
However, he thinks there are also many opportunities for the EU that come with bringing in Ukraine's farming sector, even for European farmers.
"We do not share the approach under which Ukraine's integration is viewed exclusively as a threat to European farmers," Vysotskyi said.
And Kyiv's lobby for agriculture in Brussels, the Ukrainian Agribusiness Club (UCAB), said that while it understands the concerns of European farmers, it is "increasingly concerned by an excessively protectionist approach towards the integration of Ukrainian agriculture," in an Oct. 7 press statement .
For UCAB, part of the answer lies in communication.
"UCAB has consistently advocated an open and structured dialogue with European farmers, EU institutions, and member states to jointly develop a model for the future enlarged European agricultural market."

title: 2027: CSOs, Others Urge Ebonyi Electorate to Vote for Candidates with Competence, Track Records
body: Benjamin Nworie in Abakaliki Civil Society Organizations and other stakeholders in Ebonyi State have called on the electorate in the state to look beyond political manifestos, slogans and personalities, and critically interrogate the competence, capacity, policy proposals, and track records of various candidates of political parties for the 2027 general election. The stakeholders made the call last Monday in Abakaliki, the state capital during a democratic dialogue organised by the Centre for Media and Dialogue Initiative(CMDI) in collaboration with the Correspondents’ Chapel, Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Ebonyi State chapter, with the theme: ‘Beyond the Manifesto: Ebonyi 2027 Election and the People’s Interrogation of Next Leadership’. The Programme Director of the Centre, Eze Chikodiri Igwe, said the essence of the dialogue was to provide a credible, respectful and non-partisan platform where candidates could explain their programmes while citizens, the media and other stakeholders interrogate their policy choices and capacity to deliver. Igwe said democracy required more than campaign promises, stressing that voters must demand clear explanations on how proposed policies would be implemented, the resources required and the mechanisms for measuring performance and holding elected officials accountable. “A manifesto tells us what a candidate promises. Democracy, however, requires us to go further and ask: What is the problem? What is the proposed solution? How will it be delivered? What resources will it require? “What priorities will guide the choices? How will citizens measure performance? And what mechanisms will make leadership accountable to the people?” he said. He explained that the objective of the initiative was not to endorse any candidate or political party, but to move electoral discourse “from political promises to public policy; from slogans to substance; from personalities to capacity; and from campaign rhetoric to measurable commitments.” Igwe added that the electorate had the right to ask questions, candidates had the responsibility to provide answers, while the media has a duty to interrogate claims and provide citizens with credible information to enable them make informed choices. “Ultimately, the objective of this programme is to help create a better-informed electorate and a more substantive electoral conversation ahead of the 2027 elections. “We are not here to tell Ebonyi people what choice to make. We are here to strengthen the quality of the questions that must precede that choice,” Igwe said. He maintained that an election was not merely about choosing who would occupy an office, but about deciding who would be entrusted with the hopes, resources, security and future of the people. In his remarks, the Chairman, Correspondents’ Chapel, Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Ebonyi State chapter, Uchenna Inya, said journalists have a responsibility to set the agenda for public discourse and ensure that the electorate is adequately informed about candidates and their programmes. Inya said the media must interrogate candidates on what they intended to offer the people, how they planned to implement their policies, and what mechanisms would be deployed to address critical sectors such as agriculture, healthcare, security, and the economy. He stressed that journalists are not partisan actors in the electoral process, but professional stakeholders whose responsibility is to report issues accurately and allow citizens to make informed choices. “Our duty is to keep the public informed, educated and focused on a people-centred agenda,” Inya said, adding that the media would continue to report electoral issues based on facts while advocating a peaceful, free and credible process. He urged political actors and their supporters to eschew violence and allow the electorate to freely exercise their democratic rights. Representing the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) at the event, Mrs. Esther Idam described citizens as critical stakeholders in the electoral process, and urged registered voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) ahead of the elections. Idam also cautioned voters and political actors against misinformation and fake news, urging citizens to verify information before sharing it on social media platforms. She warned youths against allowing themselves to be used to perpetrate electoral violence, stressing that a peaceful environment was essential for credible participation. According to her, voters should familiarise themselves with their designated polling units and comply with electoral guidelines rather than resort to confrontation when difficulties arise. She further emphasised the need for political parties, candidates, agents and voters to understand the rules governing accreditation, voting and the collation process. The INEC representative also reiterated the commission’s commitment to an inclusive electoral process, noting that women, youths and persons living with disabilities are important participants in the democratic process. She stated that the commission would provide a level playing ground for all candidates for the general election. The dialogue attracted candidates and representatives of various political parties, including the Labour Party, ADC, PDP, NDC, ARM and other political parties that participated in discussions on the quality of leadership required in Ebonyi State and the expectations of voters ahead of the 2027 elections. However, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and its candidates didn’t participate in the dialogue. The state Chairman of the People’s Democratic Party (PDP), Chief Chukwuma Igwe, represented by the state Publicity Secretary of the party, Darlington Onwe, urged the APC to explain to the state while it has been avoiding debate and other activities geared toward peaceful and free and fair conduct of the 2027 general election. “The APC leaders deliberately avoided this dialogue in which they were duly notified. The governor was personally invited, and if he was too busy, he was supposed to send a representative like our principal, Chief Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii, the governorship candidate of PDP, did by sending someone to represent him. “Chief Ifeanyi Odii was not in the country but he still sent someone to represent him. The state PDP Chairman, Chukwuma Igwe, was unavoidably absent due to flight issues but he had to send the Publicity Secretary of the party to represent him. “The APC was not around here; its members ran away from the dialogue because they don’t have anything to show. PDP has been challenging them to a debate but they have continued to run away because there is nothing tangible to show,” Onwe said.

title: Russian troops launch 31 strikes across Donetsk region, killing 4 – official
body:
Russian occupation forces subjected settlements across Donetsk region to 31 attacks over the past 24 hours, Head of the Donetsk Regional State Administration Vadym Filashkin reported.
"Over October 7, the Russians killed 4 residents of Donetsk region: 2 in Zelenе, and 1 each in Slovyansk and Vesela Hora. Another 6 people in the region sustained injuries over the past day," Filashkin wrote on his Telegram channel.
Specifically, in Slovyansk, 1 person was killed and 3 were wounded, with damage inflicted on an apartment building, an administrative building, a shop, a service station, a gas station, a car, and a bus. In Kramatorsk, a person was wounded and three cars were damaged.
Two administrative buildings were damaged in Oleksandrivka; in Zoloti Prudy, a person was injured and a private house, a car, and a truck sustained damage; private homes were damaged in Petrivka Persha and Novostepanivka. In Vesela Hora within the Novodonetske community, a person was killed and a private house damaged; an administrative building was damaged in Stepanivka. In Serhiivka of the Andriivka community, 7 houses were damaged. In Druzhkivka, one person was injured.
In Zelene within the Kryvyi Rih community, 2 people were killed.
A total of 256 people, including 32 children, were evacuated from the frontline zone over the past 24 hours.

title: SERAP challenges ₦100m DSS defamation award at appeal court
body: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has urged the Court of Appeal sitting in Abuja to set aside the judgment of the Federal Capital Territory High Court awarding ₦100 million in damages against SERAP in a defamation suit brought by two officers of Nigeria’s State Security Service (SSS). The appeal is scheduled for hearing on Friday. The appeal, filed by SERAP following the judgment delivered by Justice Yusuf Halilu on 5 May 2026, challenges the findings of liability, the award of damages and the consequential orders, including the order requiring SERAP to publish an apology. The Appellant’s Brief of Argument, dated 3 September 2026 and filed at the Court of Appeal by SERAP’s counsel, Tayo Oyetibo, SAN, is based on 24 grounds and raises important questions concerning the essential elements of defamation, the evidential burden of establishing identification, the competence of the evidence relied upon by the trial Court, and the protection of freedom of expression and public-interest advocacy. SERAP said: “The central issue in this appeal is whether the respondents established by credible evidence that the publications complained of referred to them. The publications did not name the respondents, and the descriptions relied upon were general physical descriptions which did not, without more, identify the particular individuals who brought the action.” The lawsuit arose after SERAP published an account on 9 September 2024 alleging that DSS officers had unlawfully entered its Abuja office, following the organisation’s call on President Bola Tinubu to investigate allegations of corruption at the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and reverse fuel price increases. The publications referred to officers from the SSS/DSS and described them, among other things, as “a tall, large, dark-skinned woman” and “a slim, dark-skinned man”. The officers were not named in the publications. SERAP’s Brief of Argument reads in part: “The alleged suspension of the 1st and 2nd Respondents was likewise not supported by independent documentary evidence. The award against SERAP was therefore not only excessive but also arbitrary and ought to be set aside.” “The learned trial Judge relied, inter alia, on assertions that the publication had affected the 1st and 2nd Respondents ‘mentally and psychologically’ and had ‘gone viral’, without sufficient evidence establishing the extent of the publication or any specific professional, financial or reputational injury suffered by the Respondents.” “The award of liability cannot stand where the essential findings on falsity and justification were not supported by the evidence We respectfully submit that the finding of liability and consequential award of damages cannot stand once the findings upon which they were founded are shown to be erroneous.” “Where a claimant is not expressly named in a publication, the burden remains on the claimant to establish by evidence the circumstances from which a reasonable reader would understand the publication to refer specifically to that claimant. That essential link was not established in this case.” “Neither publication identified the respondents by name, rank, designation, office or photograph. The descriptions relied upon were physical descriptions which, on the evidence before the trial Court, were not unique to the respondents.” “The respondents pleaded that members of the public and persons within the SSS understood the publications to refer to them, but no member of the public was called to testify that they had read the publications and understood them to refer to the respondents.” “No independent witness was called to establish the alleged identification, while the social-media reactions relied upon by the respondents were not tendered in evidence.” “The law is settled that the words complained of in an action for defamation must be considered from the standpoint of the ordinary reasonable reader. The question is whether a reasonable person reading the publication would associate the words complained of with the claimant.” “The significance of this principle in the present appeal is considerable. The two SSS/DSS officers were not named in either publication. Their case therefore depended upon establishing by evidence the factual circumstances connecting the descriptions contained in the publications to their particular identities.” “The trial Court consequently supplied the missing identifying link by relying, among other things, on its own observation of the physical appearance of the respondents in Court.” “The trial Court could not properly supply by its own observation the essential identifying link which the respondents were required to establish by evidence. The issue was whether the publications identified the respondents when they were published, not whether the respondents happened to fit the descriptions when they appeared before the Court.” “The respondents instituted this action at the trial Court by initially filing a Writ of Summons against the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project, a non-juristic person. The respondents subsequently amended their Writ of Summons to substitute the said non-juristic entity with the Incorporated Trustees of the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project.” “An action commenced against a non-juristic person is fundamentally defective and does not constitute a misnomer which is capable of amendment. An amendment cannot cure a void originating process nor effect the substitution of a distinct juristic entity for a party that does not exist in law.” “The evidence before the trial Court established that the first respondent signed her witness statement at her lawyers’ chambers rather than before a Commissioner for Oaths. The statutory requirements governing the administration and execution of an oath are not matters of mere formality.” “A witness statement on oath which was not properly sworn cannot be retrospectively validated simply because the witness subsequently adopted the statement in open Court. Adoption cannot cure a fundamental defect in the manner in which the statement was sworn.” “There is no such ambiguity here. The present case is materially different and the authority relied upon does not justify the learned trial Judge’s failure to properly consider the first respondent’s admission concerning the execution of her witness statement on oath.” “The publications ought to have been read as a whole and in their proper factual and contextual setting. Particular words and expressions, including ‘invasion’, ‘harassment’, ‘intimidation’ and ‘unlawful’, should not have been isolated from the facts and circumstances giving rise to the publications.” “The publications concerned the conduct of State security officials who visited SERAP’s Abuja office without prior notice, sought access to staff and management, and whose presence generated concerns and interactions with SERAP staff.” “SERAP’s assessment and characterisation of those events constituted comment on a matter of legitimate public interest. The fact that the respondents disagreed with that characterisation does not, without more, establish defamation.” “SERAP had established the factual foundation for the publications, and the evidence before the trial Court did not establish that the substance of the publications was false. The respondents could not succeed merely by demonstrating that they disagreed with SERAP’s account or characterisation of the events.” “Qualified privilege may be defeated by proof of express or actual malice. No such evidence was established. Mere disagreement with the Appellant’s account does not, without more, establish malice.” “Section 39(1) protects the freedom to hold opinions and to impart information and ideas. That protection is particularly important for civil society organisations whose work necessarily involves scrutinising public institutions and commenting on matters affecting human rights, accountability and the rule of law.” “Officers of a public security agency do not, by virtue of their office, become immune from legitimate criticism concerning the manner in which public functions are performed.” “The right to comment freely on matters of public interest is one of the fundamental rights of free speech guaranteed to the individual in our Constitution.” “The protection of reputation and the protection of freedom of expression must be carefully balanced. That balance is particularly important where the speech concerns the conduct of security agencies and other public authorities.” “The trial Court failed to consider the defences relied upon by the Appellant which were factually and legally available to the Appellant. The imposition of liability and award of outrageous damages were not supported by the evidence led in Court.” “The suit of the 1st and 2nd Respondents was frivolous, vexatious and lacked merit given that the publications in question, as shown in Exhibit D2, were made against the SSS as an institution, yet the two unidentified 1st and 2nd Respondents filed this suit in their personal capacities.” “The central issue in this appeal is whether the essential elements of defamation were established by evidence and whether legitimate public-interest criticism can properly be transformed into personal liability without satisfying those requirements.” “The finding of liability and consequential award of damages cannot stand once the findings upon which they were founded are shown to be erroneous. The learned trial Judge misdirected himself on identification, the meaning of the publications, falsity and the Appellant’s defences.” “SERAP remains committed to lawful and evidence-based advocacy on matters affecting human rights, accountability and the rule of law. Civil society organisations must be able to scrutinise and comment on the conduct of public institutions without the threat of disproportionate legal consequences.” “We urge the Court of Appeal to uphold the requirements of due process and the constitutional protection of freedom of expression and to set aside the judgment and consequential orders challenged in this appeal.” The post SERAP challenges ₦100m DSS defamation award at appeal court appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Over 100,000 Eye Renewed Hope Cities Initiative
body: Kingsley Aliamaka The Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Cities initiative has drawn more than 100,000 expressions of interest from Nigerians across the public, private, and informal sectors, with traders and small business owners in Abuja, Kano, and Lagos among those buying into the scheme. Conceived as a public-private partnership under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the programme brings together the Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development and a consortium of developers, such as Continental Civil and General Construction, Ceezali Limited, and Citec International Limited. President Tinubu personally broke ground at the onset of the flagship project in Karsana, Abuja, where 2,400 housing units are nearing completion. Mortgage Access Widens A central pillar of the programme is the President’s directive to the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN) to extend mortgages to contributors of the National Housing Fund. More than 2,000 Nigerians have already benefited from the scheme, with over 10,000 additional applications currently being processed. The Minister of Housing and Urban Development, Engr. Dr. Muttaqha Rabe Darma, has pushed a reform agenda prioritising Nigerian workers and the informal sector in home sales and mortgage allocation. He has set a target of at least 5,000 mortgages annually and established a committee to overhaul the housing sector more broadly. Infrastructure support has followed suit: at the President’s directive, the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Hon. Nyesom Wike, ensured government-funded access roads to project sites, with the first phase of the Karsana access road already completed. Expansion Across the Country Reassuringly, the Renewed Hope Cities project has moved beyond Abuja. In Janguza, Kano, over 350 units are complete, with another 650 under construction ahead of a March 2027 delivery date. In Lagos, the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway has opened up the Lekki-Epe corridor, prompting developers to begin work on 2,004 units along Monastery Road, with the first 550 expected by April 2027. New sites are also underway in Jibi, by Kubwa on the outskirts of Abuja (2,000 units planned) and also in Kagini, Abuja (1,200 units, as phase two), with construction plans in the pipeline for Asaba, Ibadan, Katsina, Enugu, the Sagamu-Papalanto Road corridor, and Port Harcourt. The government has pledged to eventually extend the scheme to every state, with an ambition of housing 100 million Nigerians. To date, the project has attracted over 100,000 expressions of interest, more than 10,000 firm subscriptions, and thousands of allocation letters and mortgages already issued. Funding and Institutional Backing Financing for the Renewed Hope Cities project has come from a mix of private equity from developers, construction and mortgage finance from the FMBN, financing support from the Family Homes Funds and the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority, and banking support from Keystone Bank Plc, the scheme’s sole commercial bank partner. Momentum has also been built up through cooperative societies across diverse sectors. Staff associations from NMDPRA, NUPRC, NDIC, SEC, SEPLAT, MTN, NLNG, and PENGASSAN Benin, along with the Banex Traders Association, cooperatives within the Federal Ministries of Finance and Foreign Affairs, and trader groups in Kano, have all joined the scheme. Some organisations, including NMDPRA, NUPRC, SEC and NRS, have gone further, covering staff equity contributions outright to remove financial barriers to entry. NMDPRA alone recorded more than 1000 subscribers, with hundreds more from NUPRC and NRS. Over 430 Units Handed Over Recently On September 23, 2026, the Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development, in collaboration with Renewed Hope Cities developers, handed over 430 housing units to the staff and cooperative members of NMDPRA in a ceremony attended by NMDPRA Chief Executive Rabiu Abdullahi Umar, the Minister of Housing, the CEOs of the FMBN and Family Homes Funds, NMDPRA executive directors, and Renewed Hope Cities officials. Housing Minister Darma praised President Tinubu for his consistent backing of housing reforms, noting that every proposal brought to the President for reform has received full support. He commended NMDPRA for being the first organisation to fund a 30 percent equity contribution on behalf of its 430 beneficiaries, and urged the Authority to extend the same benefit to its remaining staff. In his remarks, NMDPRA Chief Executive Umar congratulated the President on the initiative, describing it as an example of policy meeting diligent execution with great success. He noted that NMDPRA’s role in regulating Nigeria’s midstream and downstream petroleum sector makes it central to national development. This, he said, makes the equity support a critical investment in employee welfare, providing staff an opportunity to build long-term household assets through structured homeownership, so that they are motivated to greater commitment. Under the NMDPRA Management arrangement, participating staff have been supported towards meeting their equity obligations, while the balance of the property cost can be financed through applicable mortgage arrangements and other installment payment plans for eligible beneficiaries. The NMDPRA cooperative’s president, speaking on behalf of the 430 beneficiaries, thanked the President, the Minister, and the developers, and praised NMDPRA’s leadership for funding the equity contributions. He appealed for additional funding so that the more than 1,000 staff who have expressed interest in the scheme can receive the same support extended to the first batch of 430 beneficiaries who have secured allocations across the Renewed Hope developments in Abuja, Kano, and Lagos. By and large, the NMDPRA experience presents a potentially replicable model for other Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), government-owned institutions, corporations, and organised cooperatives seeking practical ways to support their employees in achieving homeownership. More Institutions Embrace Equity Support for Staff Following the good example of NMDPRA Management, the Executive Managements of Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) and National Revenue Service (NRS) are also doubly committed to providing financial support for their staff and cooperatives members to ensure they participate fully in securing their homes in the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Cities projects in different parts of the country. As more public institutions lift their staff to own a piece of the Renewed Hope Cities projects, the noble initiative demonstrates how MDAs can complement the Federal Government’s housing agenda by supporting their employees to meet the initial equity requirements associated with home acquisition. Rather than leaving employees to independently bear the full burden of the initial equity requirements, institutions can explore structured employee-support arrangements that enable qualified staff to access housing while spreading the financial obligations over an agreed period. This type of institutional participation can significantly strengthen the ability of organised workers to access housing finance and participate in large-scale government housing initiatives. DEVELOPERS OF RENEWED HOPE CITIES PROJECTS

title: Russian forces launch more than 50 attacks on Sumy region over past 24 hours, causing fatalities and injuries
body:
According to Ukrinform, the Sumy Regional Military Administration reported this on Facebook .
In the Krolevets community, two 14-year-old boys were killed when an explosive device detonated.
In the Sumy community, a 46-year-old woman and two men, aged 69 and 49, were injured when a Russian drone struck. Two women, aged 26 and 50, who were injured on October 6 when a drone struck a high-rise building, sought medical attention.
In the Velyka Pysarivka community, a 62-year-old man was wounded as a result of a Russian drone strike.
The highest number of strikes was recorded in the Sumy and Shostka districts.
The enemy used artillery, mortars, multiple launch rocket systems (MLRS), unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)—including FPV drones—and guided aerial bombs.
In the Sumy community, a supermarket, civilian infrastructure facilities, a private residential building, and vehicles were damaged.
In the Seredyno-Buda community, private residential buildings were damaged.
In the Berezivka community, vehicles were damaged.
In the Konotop community, a civilian infrastructure facility sustained damage.
In the Seredyno-Buda, Esman, Shalyhyne, and Znob-Novhorod communities, private residential homes were destroyed and damaged as a result of earlier Russian strikes. In the Berezivka and Seredyno-Buda communities, civilian infrastructure facilities were damaged.
As reported by Ukrinform, from the morning of October 6 to the morning of October 7, Russian troops carried out nearly 50 strikes on 24 settlements in 12 territorial communities of the Sumy region . There were reports of fatalities and injuries.

title: [AINews] Claude Haiku 5.5 — better than GPT-6 Luna at the same pricing
body: It’s been about a year since Anthropic shipped Haiku 4.5 , and with successive launches of Sonnet and Opus and Fable up to 5.5 it was seeming a little forgotten, especially as OpenAI launched Luna 6 alongside Astra and Sol 6. Well, it’s here, and it’s a welcome update. More in the summary below. AI News for 10/06/2026-10/7/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews’ website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space . You can opt in/out of email frequencies! AI Twitter Recap Top Story: Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 5.5 What happened Anthropic shipped Claude Haiku 5.5, its first Haiku-tier update in about a year. It is priced to match OpenAI’s GPT-6 Luna, and Anthropic cut prices on Sonnet 5.5 and its subscription plans the same day. Pre-launch signals. @scaling01 posted “happy Haiku 5.5 day” before the announcement. @kimmonismus said the model had already appeared in a Claude Code update and predicted “Luna-pricing.” He then posted the pricing ahead of the official post ( @kimmonismus ) and confirmed when it went live ( @kimmonismus ). Official launch. @claudeai and @AnthropicAI called it “the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model we’ve ever released,” costing about 75% less to run than Haiku 4.5 on average. Availability and intended use. It is live on the Claude Platform and in Claude Code ( @ClaudeDevs ). Anthropic positions it as a subagent paired with Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5, for high-volume, cost-sensitive work such as summaries, compactions and database queries. @mikeyk described the split as “Opus does the heavy thinking, Haiku does the high-volume work.” Tiered pricing ( @ClaudeDevs ): Prompt lengthInput / output per 1M tokensCache reads per 1MUnder 100K tokens$0.10 / $0.50$0.01Over 100K tokens$0.50 / $2.50$0.05 Sonnet 5.5 price cut. Cache reads were halved from $0.20 to $0.10 per 1M tokens. Anthropic says this makes Sonnet 5.5 about 20% cheaper on most long-running or agentic work ( @claudeai ). API credits for subscribers. Monthly Claude Platform API credits now come with Max 5x ($100), Max 20x ($200) and Team (up to $500, pooled). They work on any model, including Haiku 5.5, and in third-party harnesses ( @ClaudeDevs ). Same-day SDK update. Computer-use and browser-use toolsets are now built into the Python and TypeScript Claude SDKs. The SDK runs the action loop and sends clicks and keystrokes to drivers from browser_use, Browserbase, E2B or Daytona, so developers no longer write that loop themselves ( @ClaudeDevs , quickstart ). Partner rollouts on day one: Cursor: @cursor_ai claims “10x less than Haiku 4.5” on shorter requests and published CursorBench comparisons ( @cursor_ai ). GitHub Copilot in VS Code: @code reports it “matched Claude Sonnet 5 on many coding tasks while using fewer tokens and steps.” Devin: @cognition reports 58.4% on FrontierCode 1.1, ahead of Sonnet 5 at roughly one-eighth the cost per task, and recommends it as a “sidekick” under an Opus 5.5 lead in Fusion. Arena: added to Agent Arena, Code Arena WebDev, Text, Document and Vision, with scores pending ( @arena ). OpenDocRouter: added the same day (details below). Independent evaluation: Artificial Analysis @ArtificialAnlys published the most detailed third-party numbers ( per-eval breakdown , comparison page ). Intelligence Index: 43 at max effort, up 26 points from the previous Haiku. Slightly ahead of GLM-5.3 Flash (42), Gemini 3.8 Flash (41) and GPT-6 Luna (38). Comparable to Kimi K3 (44), a 2.8T-parameter open-weights model. Trails Claude Sonnet 5.5 at max effort (56) by 13 points. New controls. This is the first Haiku with Anthropic’s effort settings and adaptive thinking. Token usage is the main caveat. At max effort it uses about 162k output tokens per Index task, roughly 3x GPT-6 Luna at max (~50k). Going from xhigh to max adds 2 points for about 1.8x the tokens. At equal score it is still more verbose: Haiku 5.5 at high effort scores 38 using ~55k tokens, versus Luna at max scoring 38 with ~50k. The gap widens at lower effort settings. Cost figures are provisional. Artificial Analysis does not yet model the 5x price step above 100K tokens. Cost-per-task numbers will follow. AA-Briefcase (private agentic knowledge-work eval): 1578 Elo. That is ahead of Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3, and comparable to Muse Spark 1.3 at max. Terminal-Bench 4.0: 33% , up from 0% for Haiku 4.5. Level with GLM-5.3 Flash. Ahead of Gemini 3.8 Flash (20%) and GPT-6 Luna (13%). Knowledge versus hallucination (AA-Omniscience): ModelAccuracyHallucination rateHaiku 5.536%40%Gemini 3.8 Flash55%55%GPT-6 Luna44%77% Part of Haiku’s lower accuracy comes from being more willing to say it doesn’t know. AutomationBench-AA: 35% , versus 53–60% for Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash and GLM-5.3 Flash. A pre-release safety bug caused the model to over-refuse. Anthropic is working on a fix, and Artificial Analysis will re-run the eval and expects the score to rise. Specs: 1M-token context, up from 200k for Haiku 4.5. Text and image input, text output. 5-minute cache writes cost $0.125 per 1M tokens ($0.625 above 100K). Other benchmark claims (mostly vendor or secondhand) @ShayneRedford summarized Anthropic’s reported jumps: OSWorld (computer use): 15% → 72%. TerminalBench: 0% → 39%. This differs from Artificial Analysis’s independent 33% on Terminal-Bench 4.0. 10–50% gains in knowledge work and reasoning. Beats Luna on most of these. 1M context with roughly 12k max output tokens. @alexalbert__ (Anthropic) stressed that Haiku 4.5 shipped Oct 15, 2025, so the comparison spans less than a year. @TheRundownAI reported that it beats GPT-6 Luna “across a variety of benchmarks.” Document parsing (independent, on ParseBench): @LoganMarkewich : overall close to Luna, slightly better on tables, worse on chart understanding. @jerryjliu0 : about $1.2 per 1,000 pages. Good at tables and reading order for the price; weaker on charts, semantic formatting and bounding boxes. Anecdotal: @simonw wrote pricing notes and ran his pelican-on-a-bicycle test. He says it is “SO MUCH better” than Haiku 4.5, which costs 10x more ( comparison ). @AI_Screening says Haiku 5.5 “cooked” Luna on a Three.js zebra simulation (single prompt, not systematic). Opinions and reactions Bullish @kimmonismus : “Way better than GPT-6-Luna, close[r] to Sonnet 5.5… Cheap and smart.” @theo likes the tiered pricing: charging a fifth of the price under 100K tokens “makes it really clear what the model is for.” He also found it striking to see an Anthropic model “so far to the left on the cost/intelligence charts” ( @theo ) and covered the launch on stream ( @theo ). @draecomino : “Haiku at max effort performs like a frontier model.” @kipperrii argues small, cheap models matter more now that they can do “a ton of useful things.” @scaling01 (”cheap af”) and later ( @scaling01 ): “5.5 models are looking good.” @NotTomBrown (”small but mighty”) and @edwinarbus , both from the Anthropic side, posted celebratory notes. Competitive framing The launch is widely read as aimed at OpenAI’s GPT-6 Luna: “rip gpt 6 luna” ( @dejavucoder ), “time to cook Luna” ( @scaling01 ). @kimmonismus framed the Sonnet cache-read cut as Anthropic pressuring OpenAI. On the API credits he added, “OpenAI: your turn” ( @kimmonismus ). @teortaxesTex says Anthropic now has “the deepest product lineup of all labs” (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus/Fable plus Mythos) versus OpenAI’s Luna/Sol/Astra. He still thinks Anthropic “cares less about products,” which he reads as a sign of how much slack it has had through 2026. ThursdAI’s @altryne questioned the middle tier: “Sonnet made sense when Opus was expensive.” The show plans to cover Haiku 5.5 ( @thursdai_pod ). Caveats (mostly from the data, not loud critics) The headline price may overstate real savings. Heavy token use (about 3x Luna at max effort) offsets part of the per-token discount. Prompts over 100K tokens pay 5x more, which matters for long-context agent loops. These two effects likely explain why Cursor’s “10x cheaper on short requests” differs from Anthropic’s “75% cheaper on average.” Factual recall is weaker than Gemini 3.8 Flash and Luna. The over-refusal bug currently depresses the automation score. Not yet benchmarked: Arena scores are pending, and independent cost-per-task figures await tiered-pricing support. Context Haiku 4.5 has been Anthropic’s small model since October 2025. Since then, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash, GLM-5.3 Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash have competed at the low-cost end. Haiku 5.5 matches Luna’s sticker price exactly. It adds effort control and a 1M context. It is explicitly positioned as the cheap worker inside multi-model agent harnesses: Claude Code subagents, Devin Fusion, Copilot subagents, and compaction or summarization steps. Anthropic paired it with Sonnet cache-read cuts and subscription API credits, a coordinated push on agent economics. That push lands amid wider debate over token bills (see @theo below).
