title: Israel, UK agree to keep east Jerusalem consulate open as limited diplomatic mission
body: The United Kingdom's consulate in east Jerusalem has ceased operations, and 20 diplomats will leave Israel under a new understanding reached between Jerusalem and London, Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar announced on Thursday.However, the office will remain open after Sa'ar "authorized the British government to operate a task force of only seven diplomats in the building, which has ceased to be used as a consulate today, with a very limited scope of activity."According to Sa'ar, the British government will not take any action against Israel as a result of the implementation of the September order that led to the consulate's closure."We established a clear principle: It is not possible to act against Israel without Israel taking appropriate measures in response. In this spirit, the measures I announced on 8 September have been implemented: 1. The removal of the British representatives from the International Gaza Support Center in Kiryat Gat. 2. The termination of British activity to train Palestinian Authority forces in Judea and Samaria. 3. The denial of entry to Israel to 12 British elected officials and other British citizens involved in antisemitic and anti-Israel activity, as well as those who deny our very right to exist. 4. The British Consulate in Jerusalem is ending its operations today. Accordingly, the sign of the British Consulate in Jerusalem has been removed," Sa'ar said."We did not want to reach this point, but the actions of the UK Labour Government brought us here. Their latest decision in this series was to initiate a range of far-reaching sanctions against the communities in Judea and Samaria, as well as additional sanctions on defense exports to Israel. All this was accompanied by hostile rhetoric, including false accusations against Israel, such as accusations of 'ethnic cleansing.'" Sa'ar said."This decision adds to a growing and escalating series of unilateral measures against Israel adopted by the Labour Government since taking office in July 2024," Sa'ar continued."These measures included, among others, unilateral recognition of a virtual 'Palestinian state' in September 2025; the renewal of funding to UNRWA; the suspension of licences for defence exports to Israel; the imposition of sanctions on Israeli ministers; the imposition of sanctions on Israeli individuals and entities; the suspension of negotiations on a free trade agreement; restrictions on Israel's official participation in an international defence and security equipment exhibition in Britain; the freezing of military dialogue and security cooperation; the prevention of IDF officers from participating in training at the Royal College of Defence Studies; and repeated, biased and unilateral attacks against Israel in the international arena," Sa'ar added."Over the past week, we held a dialogue with the British Government with the aim of preventing further deterioration in relations between the countries as a result of the closure of the Consulate," he said.Last night, we reached understandings based on the following principles: These principles are: 1. As I announced, the British Consulate in Jerusalem ended its role today. The consul-general and 19 diplomats are ending their assignments and will leave Israel. 2. The building that served as the Consulate is the property of the British Government. We have allowed the British Government to operate a task force of only seven diplomats from the building, which ceased to function as a consulate today. Their scope of activity will be very limited. 3. We agreed on the continuation of dialogue between the governments, within which both sides will be able to raise issues important to them," Sa'ar clarified."We believe in dialogue and will continue to believe in dialogue. Unfortunately, in recent years, no genuine dialogue has taken place with the Labour Government," he said.Israel provided UK with 'vital information in RAF Fairford affair,' Sa'ar says"This is despite good relations with Britain, reflected, among other things, in security and intelligence cooperation. Relations between Israel and Britain are important and have repeatedly proven their value also in protecting the lives and interests of British citizens. Only recently, Israel provided Britain with vital information in the RAF Fairford affair," Sa'ar said."All four measures in my statement of 8 September have been implemented. Alongside this, we reached understandings that serve Israel's interests. In accordance with the understandings we reached, no measures will be taken against Israel as a result of the implementation of the decisions. I thank everyone who was involved in the dialogue and discussions and contributed to reaching the understandings on both sides," he continued."I cannot promise that there will not be further crises in the future. If there are, we will face them on the basis of our core principles. It is important to emphasize again that we did not initiate the current situation. We are interested in good relations with all the countries of the world. But any country that acts against Israel must know that there will be a price for doing so. It will not gain from this, but quite the opposite. Israel will no longer turn its cheek to diplomatic attacks against it," Sa'ar emphasized.UK's Miliband insists Israeli government has no right to close British consulate"We have been clear that we do not accept that the Government of Israel has the legal right to close the British Consulate General in Jerusalem, which has been there for nearly 200 years," British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said on Thursday."The UK government reiterates its long-standing view that east Jerusalem is occupied territory," he added."Following discussions with the Government of Israel, our Consulate General building will not be closing, and will be known as the UK Mission, Jerusalem from today. The UK Mission, Jerusalem is independent, operational, and will continue to deliver vital services for the Palestinian people," said Miliband."This will ensure that we maintain our longstanding British presence and the UK's role in support of two-state solution," he stated."Without an understanding [with Israel], we would not have the necessary assurances for the security and protections of our staff and premises. Accordingly, the UK has temporarily withdrawn a number of staff and families to ensure their safety and security," Miliband said."We will work in the coming months to build back up our presence, and we will not take reciprocal action while such discussions are underway and credible. The UK stands steadfast by the measures we took on 8 September, in concert with the international community, in support of a two-state solution to deliver peace and security for the people of Israel and Palestine," he concluded.Consulate signs, plaques removed from buildingAccording to a Reuters report, consulate workers removed signs and plaques at the British consulate overnight.Reuters journalists saw workers in the consulate remove a plaque reading "British Consulate General" and another sign for its consular section. The British flag was still flying over the building.Israel last month ordered Britain to close the consulate within 30 days and remove its diplomats from the city, after Britain announced sanctions targeting Israeli settlements in the West Bank, including a trade ban on goods made there.UK embassy in Tel Aviv to remain openThe closure order does not affect Britain's embassy in Tel Aviv, which handles diplomatic relations with Israel's government.The British sanctions announcement and Israel's order to close the consulate mark a low in a relationship that has deteriorated over the past three years.Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government has accused Britain's governing Labour Party of being hostile towards Israel.Reuters contributed to this report.

title: General Staff: Russia has lost 1,547,780 troops in Ukraine since Feb. 24, 2022
body:
Russia has lost around 1,547,780 troops in Ukraine since the beginning of its full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported on Oct. 8.
The number includes 1,880 casualties that Russian forces suffered over the past day.
According to the report , Russia has also lost 12,399 tanks, 25,4502 armored combat vehicles, 159,795 vehicles and fuel tanks, 50,883 artillery systems, 2,194 multiple launch rocket systems, 1,692 air defense systems, 443 aircraft, 356 helicopters, 2,890 unmanned ground vehicles, 35 ships and boats, and two submarines.
Ukraine's General Staff has not revealed its own losses during the full-scale invasion, citing operational secrecy. Independent Western think-tank reports agree that the Russian casualties significantly surpass Ukraine's losses, with the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimating the ratio to be "roughly 2.5:1 or 2:1." A January 2026 CSIS report said Ukraine has likely suffered between 500,000 and 600,000 casualties from February 2022 to December 2025, of which between 100,000 and 140,000 are thought to be killed in action. While Ukrainian officials rarely disclose the figure, President Volodymyr Zelensky told France TV on Feb. 4 that at least 55,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed in action since the beginning of the full-scale war, in addition to significant numbers who are missing in action. The intensity of Russian drone attacks and the fighting has made it extremely difficult for Ukraine to retrieve the bodies of fallen soldiers, which are needed for DNA confirmation.

title: Court strikes out criminal case against Taraba media executive
body:
The Upper Area Court No. 7 in Jalingo, Taraba State, on Wednesday struck out a criminal case against media executive and publisher Gabriel Olayinka over an alleged ₦300 million breach of trust.
Mr Olayinka is the Chief Executive Officer of SUM TV and publisher of Taraba News, a media organisation operating in Taraba State.
He is also the pioneer chairman of the Taraba News/SUM TV Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ).
The case was instituted by Danladi Jibrin, who accused Mr Olayinka of criminal breach of trust and cheating in connection with a financial transaction involving about ₦300 million.
His counsel, L.L. Tadok of P.D. Pius & Co. Chambers, filed a preliminary objection challenging the Upper Area Court’s jurisdiction to entertain the matter.
The defence argued that the dispute was civil in nature and also raised questions about the court’s jurisdiction, including the fact that the matter had originally been filed before a chief magistrate’s court.
Counsel to the complainant, D.G. Tukura, consented to the preliminary objection on the jurisdictional issue during Wednesday’s proceedings.
In his ruling, the presiding judge, Lawan Jika, upheld the objection and struck out the case for want of jurisdiction.
The judge consequently discharged Mr Olayinka from the proceedings before the Upper Area Court.
The case had previously attracted attention after Mr Olayinka spent several months in custody.
Earlier proceedings included orders directing banks to produce financial records connected to Taraba Business School, a business associated with him.
Mr Olayinka’s media career extends beyond publishing. During the inauguration of the Taraba News/SUM TV Chapel in 2025, the NUJ Taraba State Council described him as a professional accountant who later ventured into journalism and media management.
The court’s decision does not amount to an acquittal on the substance of the allegations; rather, the criminal proceedings before the Upper Area Court ended after the court found that it lacked jurisdiction to entertain the matter.

title: God used Dan Orbih to make me Rivers governor — Wike
body: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, has recounted how late Chief Daniel Orbih served as the divine instrument that paved the way for his emergence as Rivera governor in 2015. Wike made the disclosure in Abuja on Wednesday, during a night of tributes in honour of Orbih, the National Vice-Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), South South. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Orbih, from Etsako in Edo State died on Aug. 31 at 64. Wike revealed the high-stakes political intrigues, extreme pressure, and financial inducements that Orbih, widely known as simply Dan, resisted to remain steadfast in supporting his gubernatorial ambition. He traced the roots of their close bond to the critical political period between 2013 and 2014, describing it as a turbulent era where political adversaries made desperate attempts to derail his ambition. “Today I am a Minister of the FCT; yesterday I was a governor. Who did God use for me to become governor? It was Dan,” Wike said. Recalling the intense pressure mounted by opponents, including the sitting governor of Rivers at the time, Wike disclosed that massive inducements were offered to Orbih to withdraw his support, but he firmly refused. “There was nothing in this world that was not done to induce him. My governor then sent people to Dan, offered him everything in this world, but Dan stood firm and said, ‘No, I will not accept, I will not agree.’ The minister said that as the South South National Vice-Chairman of the PDP, Orbih backed his campaign by donating two bulletproof Mercedes-Benz buses to strengthen his security and mobilised massive structural support across the region. Wike expressed profound admiration for Orbih’s rare selflessness, pointing out that throughout his eight-year tenure as Governor of Rivers, Orbih never sought personal gain, patronage, or government contracts. “Dan is not a typical Nigerian politician. Throughout my eight years as governor, he never came for one day—either by phone or coming to my house to say, ‘I need this contract.’ Never,” he said. He added that the loyalty and commitment demonstrated by Orbih were traits deeply rooted in his family heritage. “The only way I can identify a politician that is reliable is when that politician has stood in times of crisis. Loyalty, commitment to friendship, and being a brother’s keeper run in Dan’s family,” he said. Wike stressed that without Orbih’s strength as National Vice-Chairman in the South South protecting the region’s interests, many current national and state lawmakers would not have attained their positions today. Highlighting Orbih’s strategic foresight, Wike noted that the late political titan laid the foundation for cross-party collaboration in Edo and supported many politicians in the state but had not benefited from it. The FCT minister insisted that Orbih deserves a state burial, considering his contribution to the political developments in Edo and urged stakeholders in the state to do something about it. He promised to maintain a strong relationship with the deceased family and discuss how to keep Orbih’s legacies. Also, Sen. Magnus Abe, Chairman of the Board of the Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, also disclosed that he is a politician today because of Orbih explaining that it was the deceased that introduced him to politics. “I was the Director General of his first campaign in the United Nigeria Congress Party, when he ran for governor and I went everywhere in Edo with him. “Dan was indeed a bridge builder par excellence. We are gathered here today not because Dan is dead. We are gathered because of the life that he lived and that life impacted all of us in so many different ways,” he said. On his part, Sen. Adams Oshiohomle, representing Edo North in the Senate and former Governor of Edo, said that Orbih made him a better governor. “So my happiness today is that Dan and I, whatever our political differences we might have had, the truth is, Dan made me a better governor. “So, when I’m making a decision, the first thing I’ll ask is, ‘If this goes out today, what is Dan Orbih going to say?’ Each time I abstain from doing something because of what the opposition led by Dan will interpret to the people, before I do it will be better prepared. “That is why I say Dan helped me to be a better governor,” he said. To the family, Oshiohomle said, “please take consolation from the fact that your father built bridges of unity, of progress, and he never did that at the expense of family and he was committed to the growth and development of hisnxommunity. He thanked Wike for reuniting him and Orbih after a prolonged political difference saying, “it was right at Wike’s residence in Port Harcourt that Dan and I started hugging”. In his tribute, PDP presidential candidate, Sen. Sandy Onor, described Orbih as “a profound public intellectual, a quintessential lover of Edo people, a defender of Edo heritage, a Nigerian patriot and a social colossus. “Dan was a great man by every measure, a true family man, a great husband, and a worthy father,” he said. (NAN) The post God used Dan Orbih to make me Rivers governor — Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Kazakh FM Takes Part in CIS and Regional Meetings in Turkmenbashi
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – Kazakhstan’s Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi took part in a regular meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and a meeting of the Foreign Ministers of the Central Asian states and Azerbaijan in Turkmenbashi on Oct. 7. Photo credit: gov.kz CIS ministers prepare for upcoming summit The CIS foreign ministers discussed pressing topics on the international agenda and prospects for multilateral cooperation within the commonwealth. Tileuberdi outlined Kazakhstan’s approaches to cooperation within the organization and put forward several proposals aimed at strengthening the CIS’s potential, the ministry’s press service reported. A key focus of the meeting was preparations for the upcoming CIS Summit, which will bring together the leaders of the Commonwealth’s member states in Turkmenistan on Oct. 9. The ministers approved statements by the heads of state marking the 35th anniversary of the CIS and addressing the preservation of historical memory. They also endorsed draft documents to strengthen cooperation in security, economic, cultural and humanitarian affairs, as well as transport, science, space and information and communication technologies. The meeting concluded with the participants reaffirming their commitment to implementing the agreements reached and enhancing the effectiveness of multilateral cooperation mechanisms. Central Asia and Azerbaijan discuss regional cooperation Tileuberdi also participated in the meeting of the Foreign Ministers of the Central Asian States and Azerbaijan, where the participants discussed regional cooperation within the framework of the consultative meetings and current regional and international topics. Tileuberdi highlighted the progress achieved since the first consultative meeting of the Central Asian Heads of State in 2018, noting that political dialogue had contributed to stronger mutual trust and closer ties between the Central Asian countries and Azerbaijan. “Thanks to the political will of our Heads of State, relations between our brotherly nations have reached a qualitatively new level. The consultative meetings have provided significant momentum for deepening cooperation across trade, industrial cooperation, energy, transport, logistics and digital technologies,” Tileuberdi said. Following the meeting, the ministers agreed on the draft agenda and outcome documents to be signed at the eighth consultative meeting, scheduled for Oct. 8 in Turkmenbashi. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev is also in Turkmenistan for a working visit on Oct. 8-9 at the invitation of President Serdar Berdimuhamedov. The post Kazakh FM Takes Part in CIS and Regional Meetings in Turkmenbashi appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: As APC Women’s Mobilisation Machinery Gathers Momentum…
body: Jonathan Eze writes that political mobilisation becomes substantially more consequential when it is entrusted to people who already possess social relationships within their communities. A former Minister of Humanitarian Affairs, Dr Betta Edu, appears to have approached her assignment as Director of Women Mobilisation of the Presidential Campaign Council with uncommon urgency, organisational intensity and strategic purpose. Barely weeks after her appointment to the position, the ex-Minister has moved the women’s mobilisation agenda beyond the familiar rhetoric of campaign-season enthusiasm into a more elaborate architecture of community engagement. Her mandate, under the leadership of First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, is rapidly assuming the character of a nationwide mobilisation enterprise, with women being organised at ward and community levels ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Edu was listed as Director of Women Mobilisation in the APC Presidential Campaign Council unveiled in August 2026. The scale being projected is considerable: the Directorate says its activation strategy is reaching communities and grassroots structures across the country, with reports putting the target at 176,846 communities/polling-unit locations, while pursuing the broader objective of mobilising 40 million women votes for President Bola Tinubu. Whatever the final electoral arithmetic may be, the significance of the exercise lies in the organisational philosophy behind it. It is an attempt to build a women-centred political network that does not wait until the final weeks of an election before discovering the grassroots. And that is where Edu’s political assignment becomes particularly noteworthy. A Mobilisation Strategy Built From Ground Up The most striking feature of the emerging structure is its geographical spread. From Kaduna and Kano to Katsina and Jigawa; from Kwara and Abia to Rivers, Imo, Cross River, Benue, Plateau, Oyo, Ondo and Osun, reports indicate that women’s meetings, ward engagements and community-level activities are already taking place. In Kwara South, for instance, thousands of women were reportedly mobilised in Offa as part of the broader activation exercise. The women pledged to extend the mobilisation to communities, wards and polling units, with door-to-door engagement envisaged as the campaign structure becomes fully operational. In Rivers, representatives of the Women Mobilisation Directorate have similarly emphasised the importance of taking political engagement to the polling-unit level. The message from these disparate locations is therefore remarkably consistent: the mobilisation is being designed to travel downwards, from the national campaign structure to states, local governments, wards, communities and ultimately households. That is a fundamentally different proposition from merely assembling women at rallies. A rally demonstrates numerical strength for a day. A grassroots network, if successfully maintained, creates continuing political contact. Power of a Nationwide Women’s Network Nigeria’s women constitute an indispensable constituency in any serious national political mobilisation. They are traders, farmers, entrepreneurs, professionals, civil servants, artisans, community organisers, mothers, caregivers, market leaders, religious-community participants and influential actors within families and neighbourhoods. Edu’s strategy appears to recognise that political mobilisation becomes substantially more consequential when it is entrusted to people who already possess social relationships within their communities. A woman who mobilises another woman in her market, street, village, ward or professional association is not simply distributing campaign information. She is using an existing network of trust. This is the political capital upon which the Women Mobilisation Directorate is seeking to build. The reported activation of structures across such a wide geographical expanse therefore represents more than a succession of meetings. It points to an attempt to create a distributed political network, in which the national campaign message is translated into local conversations and community-specific realities. Edu’s Energy As Defining Feature If there is one characteristic that has become increasingly associated with Edu’s current assignment, it is energy. The former minister has entered the mobilisation space with a sense of urgency that suggests an understanding that presidential elections are not won by beginning grassroots work when campaign posters become ubiquitous. The early activation of women across multiple states gives the campaign an opportunity to establish relationships long before election day. In Kwara, for example, the mobilisation has already produced a substantial gathering of women. In the South-East, Edu has spoken of returning to communities and taking the message directly to women, “door-to-door, household-to-household, market-to-market, shop-to-shop, village-to-village and community-to-community.” That language captures the philosophy behind the emerging structure. It is not simply rally mobilisation. It is contact mobilisation. It is the painstaking work of getting political messages into homes, markets, villages and neighbourhoods. Beyond Rallies: Information as a Mobilisation Tool Another notable dimension of the strategy is its emphasis on information. According to the Directorate, the women’s structures are expected not only to mobilise for campaign rallies and election-day activities, but also to communicate information about government programmes, explain opportunities, identify eligibility requirements and help citizens understand how they can engage relevant institutions. Women are expected to discuss issues affecting household incomes, businesses, agriculture, transportation, energy, enterprise development and community development, alongside programmes associated with the Renewed Hope Initiative. The Directorate has also highlighted the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme and other government interventions as areas requiring grassroots communication. In political communication terms, this is important. A presidential campaign cannot depend exclusively on slogans. It must ultimately translate national policies into language that ordinary citizens can understand in relation to their daily experiences. For the APC women’s mobilisation structure, the woman in the market must be able to understand what a government policy means for her business. The farmer must understand its relevance to production. The mother must understand its implications for education, transportation or household welfare. This is where political communication meets grassroots mobilisation. First Lady’s Women-Centred Agenda as a Mobilisation Catalyst The mobilisation is also taking place against the backdrop of the women-focused interventions of the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu. During a recent programme in Imo State, for example, the Renewed Hope Initiative/SDG women empowerment programme reportedly supported 2,500 women, alongside additional cash support announced for beneficiaries. Edu subsequently described the initiative as part of a broader women-focused intervention extending across the geopolitical zones. For Edu, the political communication opportunity is evident: government programmes can become subjects of direct conversation between beneficiaries, community women and the wider electorate. This gives the mobilisation structure something more substantial to discuss than electoral slogans. It allows the campaign to ask a practical question at grassroots level: What has government done, what opportunities exist, who qualifies, and how can citizens participate? Whether voters ultimately accept those arguments remain a matter for voters themselves. But from an organisational standpoint, the strategy provides campaign workers with concrete issues around which community conversations can be organised. From North to South: A Deliberately National Structure Perhaps the most impressive aspect of the reported exercise is its geographical breadth. The mobilisation is not being presented as a sectional project confined to one region or political constituency. Reports indicate activity across northern states such as Kano, Jigawa, Katsina, Kaduna and Zamfara, as well as states in the North-Central, South-West, South-East and South-South. The South-East component is particularly significant because Edu has publicly spoken about taking the campaign message to women throughout the region, including Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi and Enugu, following the Imo engagement. This gives the women’s directorate a truly national character. It is a structure attempting to speak across ethnic, regional, religious and socioeconomic boundaries, while relying on women who understand the peculiarities of their respective communities. That combination of national direction and local agency may ultimately prove to be one of the defining characteristics of the mobilisation. A Network That Could Become a Formidable Political Asset Political organisations are ultimately sustained by people. A campaign headquarters can produce sophisticated communication materials, but it cannot substitute for people who know the streets, villages, markets, wards and communities. That is why the network being assembled under Edu’s direction is politically significant. If the reported structures are consolidated, properly coordinated and sustained over time, they could constitute one of the most extensive women-led mobilisation frameworks associated with the 2027 presidential campaign. This is also where Edu’s personal political network becomes relevant. Her previous national engagements, her experience in public office and her relationships across different constituencies provide an existing reservoir upon which a wider mobilisation structure can be constructed. Her current assignment appears to be converting those relationships into an organised political network with defined grassroots objectives. The distinction is important. A network of contacts is not the same as a network of mobilisation. The achievement lies in attempting to transform the former into the latter. A Pace That Puts Other Political Structures Under Pressure The APC Women Mobilisation Directorate’s reported pace of activation creates a formidable benchmark for other political organisations preparing for 2027. It would be premature, however, to make an absolute factual claim that no other party can match the structure, since competing parties may possess substantial networks of their own and their mobilisation efforts will continue to evolve. What can be said from the activities already reported is that Edu has set an exceptionally ambitious organisational tempo. While political parties across the country are strengthening their structures ahead of 2027, the APC women’s machinery is already reporting engagements across numerous states and communities. In grassroots politics, time is an organisational resource. The earlier structures are activated, the more opportunity exists to identify coordinators, train mobilisers, establish communication channels, understand community concerns and maintain contact with voters. Edu appears to understand this dynamic instinctively. The Real Test: Sustaining the Momentum Yet the greatest measure of this mobilisation will not ultimately be the number of meetings held or photographs generated from political gatherings. It will be sustainability. Can the structures remain active beyond the excitement of their inauguration? Can community coordinators maintain contact with women? Can information about government programmes consistently reach households? Can the network move from meetings to genuine community engagement? Can the enormous national structure be effectively coordinated without losing momentum? Those are the questions that will determine the enduring strength of the project. But the early indicators show that the machinery is not standing still. It is moving. Edu’s Assignment and Politics of Scale The scale of Edu’s assignment is enormous, but so too is the political opportunity. The ambition to engage women across 176,846 communities or polling-unit locations and pursue a 40-million-women mobilisation objective represents an attempt to redefine the scale at which presidential campaign organisation operates. It is a move away from politics as an occasional spectacle and towards politics as continuous grassroots engagement. And in this emerging architecture, Edu has clearly positioned herself as an energetic field commander, someone prepared to take the campaign message beyond conference halls and major cities into the intimate spaces where political opinions are formed every day.

title: Amnesty faults Plateau govt over withdrawal of four-year-old’s defilement case
body:
Amnesty International Nigeria has criticised the Plateau State Government for discontinuing the prosecution of a man accused of defiling a four-year-old girl.
Isa Sanusi, Amnesty International Nigeria’s country director, raised the concerns at a press conference in Jos on Wednesday.
Mr Sanusi said the state government dropped the case despite a court-issued warrant for the accused’s arrest after he repeatedly failed to appear for trial.
The organisation said the decision raised serious concerns about access to justice for the child and the government’s commitment to protecting children from sexual violence.
The case was being prosecuted before the Plateau State High Court in Jos until May 2026, when the state Ministry of Justice discontinued the proceedings pursuant to the constitutional powers of the Attorney-General.
Mr Sanusi questioned the decision, particularly because the accused had allegedly failed to appear in court and a bench warrant had reportedly been issued for his arrest.
“How is dropping a mid-trial sexual abuse case involving a four-year-old in the public interest? How does protecting a fugitive defendant serve the interest of justice?” he asked.
The Amnesty director said the decision should be reviewed because sexual abuse of a child was a serious offence that required the justice system to protect the survivor and ensure accountability.
He also raised concerns about the decision’s implications for implementing the Plateau State Child Rights Law, 2005, and the Violence Against Persons Prohibition Law, 2022.
Mr Sanusi urged Governor Caleb Mutfwang, a lawyer, to intervene and ensure that the case was restored.
He also called on the state attorney-general to publicly explain why the prosecution was discontinued.
“We are calling on the Plateau State Government to retrace its steps. This is not a political matter. It has nothing to do with sentiment. This is a human rights issue,” he said.
Barbara Magaji, Amnesty International Nigeria’s programme manager, said the organisation had previously engaged the Plateau State Government over the matter before deciding to make its concerns public.
She said Amnesty wrote to the state attorney-general seeking clarification on the decision to discontinue the case and also petitioned Governor Mutfwang. Still, she had not yet received a response from the governor.
Ms Magaji acknowledged the attorney-general’s constitutional power to discontinue criminal proceedings. Still, she said the exercise of that power should align with the broader interests of justice and the protection of the survivor.
“Our concern is the survivor. The girl child is at risk if this continues,” she said.
She said the child was in a serious condition when Amnesty became involved in the matter, adding that the organisation’s lawyers were subsequently authorised to prosecute the case after meeting the survivor and her family.
According to her, the matter first came before the court on 12 February, but the accused failed to appear.
She said the court subsequently issued a bench warrant for his arrest, but the warrant had not been executed when the prosecution was discontinued.
Stella Samuel, counsel involved in the prosecution, said the accused had been served with court processes but repeatedly failed to attend proceedings.
She said the prosecution had witnesses and evidence prepared for the trial before the case was discontinued.
“This case is still prosecutable. The law allows the Attorney-General to reinstate it,” Ms Samuel said.
She urged the state government to restore the case so that the allegations could be determined through a full judicial process.
Jacob Pwakim, secretary of the Let The Case Proceed Campaign, said the decision to discontinue the prosecution had disappointed residents who had followed the case.
He said concerned citizens formed the campaign to demand that the case proceed.
Mr Pwakim said the matter went beyond the individual survivor because it concerned protecting children and public confidence in the justice system.
“If a four-year-old cannot get justice, which child can?” he asked.
Amnesty and the campaign urged the Plateau State Government to reconsider the decision and allow the court to determine the allegations against the accused.
Efforts to obtain the response of Philemon Daffi, Plateau State Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, were unsuccessful.
His telephone was switched off when contacted for comment on Wednesday.

title: Greece Advances Ionian Gas Drilling and Major Energy Projects
body: Greece is moving closer to a major new phase in its energy strategy, with exploratory drilling in the Ionian Sea, the Greece-Cyprus electricity interconnection and the Vertical Natural Gas Corridor among the key projects advancing across the region. The developments were highlighted at the latest meeting of the Eastern Mediterranean Gas Forum, as Greece seeks to strengthen its position as an energy hub and reduce its dependence on imported natural gas. Ionian Sea drilling could transform Greece’s energy outlook Exploratory drilling in Block 2 of the Ionian Sea is scheduled for April 2027 by the Energean, ExxonMobil and Helleniq Energy consortium. The first results are expected in May and June 2027 and will determine whether natural gas or oil is present at the Asopos 1 target identified through seismic surveys. However, even a positive result would not immediately establish commercial production. Further appraisal drilling would be required to determine the size and commercial viability of any potential deposit. Energean CEO Mathios Rigas said the area could contain an estimated 270 billion cubic metres of natural gas . If that estimate is confirmed and the resource proves commercially exploitable, the implications for Greece would be significant, potentially allowing the country to become self-sufficient in natural gas and eventually an exporter . The Regional Council of the Ionian Islands has already approved the Environmental Impact Study for the Asopos drilling. A confirmatory drilling programme would require approximately one year, meaning further drilling could take place in 2028. If the results remain positive, around three additional years would then be required to install the infrastructure needed to extract and transport the hydrocarbons. Under the consortium agreement, ExxonMobil would take over as operator if hydrocarbons are discovered. Greece and Cyprus prepare to resume seabed surveys The Greece-Cyprus electricity interconnection is also moving forward. According to sources in both countries, the issuance of a new NAVTEX for the continuation of seabed surveys is expected within days. The same sources stressed that the surveys will proceed without seeking permission from Turkey . The European Investment Bank is also expected to complete its feasibility assessment for the project, while Cyprus is preparing to pay a €25 million instalment to IPTO towards expenses already incurred. The project remains strategically important for connecting Cyprus to the European electricity grid through Greece. Vertical Gas Corridor prepares for 2027 Work is also continuing on the Vertical Natural Gas Corridor , which is designed to strengthen the movement of gas between southeastern Europe and the wider European market. Countries participating in the project are currently collecting data that will determine where additional investment is required to strengthen existing networks. The objective is to ensure sufficient capacity to meet demand from 2027, particularly as the European Union moves towards ending imports of Russian natural gas. A new meeting of the natural gas transmission system operators involved in the project is scheduled to take place in Sofia in January . DESFA CEO Maria Sferoutsa said efforts are also focused on maximising the efficiency of existing infrastructure before new networks are built. Greece-Egypt electricity link gains momentum The GREGY electricity interconnection between Greece and Egypt was also among the projects supported by both countries. The proposed connection would strengthen electricity links between Greece and Egypt while potentially allowing renewable energy generated in Egypt to reach European markets through Greece. Prinos prepares for carbon storage Another major project discussed was the development of carbon dioxide storage at the depleted Prinos field . Energean is leading the investment, with the floating platform that will be used for injecting carbon dioxide currently located in Perama. According to company sources, the platform is expected to arrive in the Kavala maritime area in November . The wider infrastructure is scheduled for completion by 2030 and will include facilities for receiving and processing liquefied carbon dioxide, as well as drilling and injection infrastructure. In the meantime, industries producing significant carbon emissions are expected to make investment decisions on the collection and transportation of CO₂ to Prinos. Egypt, which has substantially greater potential carbon storage capacity, has reportedly also requested technical assistance from Greece on establishing a carbon storage market and developing the necessary regulatory framework. For Greece, the projects underline the country’s expanding role in the Eastern Mediterranean energy network , spanning natural gas exploration, electricity interconnections, regional gas infrastructure and carbon capture and storage. title: UN Human Rights Council adopts resolution on Georgia’s occupied territories
body: UNHRC resolution on Georgia’s occupied territories On 7 October, the UN Human Rights Council adopted a resolution in Geneva concerning Georgia ‘s occupied regions. According to Georgia’s Foreign Ministry, the resolution, entitled “Cooperation with Georgia”, addresses the human rights situation in Abkhazia and the Tskhinvali region ( South Ossetia ). The UN Human Rights Council calls for unhindered access to the occupied territories for the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, as well as international and regional human rights mechanisms. Council of Europe Committee of Ministers urges Russia to withdraw troops from Georgia's occupied territories Among the demands are an end to “borderisation” and freedom of movement for the local population. The resolution also condemns Russia’s actions aimed at annexing Abkhazia and the Tskhinvali region, and reaffirms support for Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders. It expresses concern over discrimination and human rights violations against ethnic Georgians in the Russian -occupied regions. The document also highlights the importance of the Geneva International Discussions, established under the ceasefire agreement of 12 August 2008. The resolution, submitted by Georgia, was adopted by consensus, as it was last year. 'Russia’s annexation of Georgia’s regions would not go unanswered' – embassies on 18th anniversary of August war “The ongoing militarisation of Georgia’s occupied territories threatens the security not only of Georgia, but also regional and European stability”

title: Textron Systems nets US Navy deal for two more SSC craft
body:
Textron Systems Corporation has been awarded a contract modification valued at $230 million by the US Navy to produce two ship-to-shore connector (SSC) craft.
The SSCs are designed to deliver mission-ready capability, moving over tides, terrains and obstacles, enabling access to 80% of the world’s coastline.
Under the contract, Textron Systems will produce and deliver SSC craft at its New Orleans, Louisiana shipyard, which includes engineering, manufacturing and quality and test operations.
The core mission of the SSC is to move personnel and material off amphibious ships. Compared to legacy platforms, the SSCs feature core design enhancements that increase payload size and speed, while streamlining the number of operators and logistics, such as extending the time between overhauls.
“The SSCs are a critical enabler for our nation’s amphibious operations, providing unmatched connector capability wherever mission demands arise,” said Larry D. Randle Jr. , Senior Vice President, Marine Systems.
“Textron Systems is proud to continue delivering mission-ready craft, supporting the Navy and Marine Corps with reliable, next-generation craft that strengthen readiness and operational reach.”
To date, Textron Systems has delivered 18 craft to the Navy, with 13 additional craft currently in various stages of testing and production.

title: Yandex reports fire at data center following drone attack
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. A drone attack caused a fire at a data center operated by Russia’s tech giant Yandex in Sasovo, Ryazan Region, the company said in a statement.
"There were no casualties; relevant services are working at the site to address the aftermath. The data center’s operations have been fully suspended and some Yandex services may be unavailable to users," the statement reads.

title: Olympic Qualifier: Eguavoen confident Falcons can overcome Comoros
body:
Super Falcons interim head coach, Augustine Eguavoen, says the withdrawals of several key players will not affect Nigeria’s chances of progressing in the 2028 Olympic Games women’s football qualifiers.
Nigeria face Comoros in the first round of the African qualifying series, with both legs scheduled at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne-Remo on 9 and 13 October.
Comoros will play both matches in Nigeria because the island nation lacks a standard football stadium suitable for hosting the qualifiers.
Despite the absence of some established players, including Asisat Oshoala, Ashley Plumptre and Oluwatosin Demehin, Eguavoen, while speaking to the NFF media, said he believes the players in camp have enough quality to deliver the desired result.
“It is true that we have several withdrawals, notably Asisat Oshoala, Ashley Plumptre and Oluwatosin Demehin. However, I have confidence in their replacements, as they also have the quality and experience to contribute meaningfully to the team’s success against Comoros.
“Everyone has settled in well in camp as we have a full house now, and our focus is to present a strong and competitive squad for the two matches.”
Only Belarus-based forward Blessing Okpe, who received a late invitation, is still expected to join the team’s camp in Ijebu-Ode.
The Falcons will be led by captain Rasheedat Ajibade as they begin their bid for a second successive Olympic appearance.
Nigeria featured at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games and must now navigate a five-round African qualifying series to secure another place at the global tournament in Los Angeles.
The Falcons, 10-time African champions, must first eliminate Comoros before advancing to the third round, scheduled for March 2027.
With both legs played in familiar surroundings, Nigeria is expected to take advantage of home conditions and establish a strong position in the tie from the first leg.
The team’s current camp includes goalkeepers Chiamaka Nnadozie, Comfort Erhabor and Christiana Uzoma.
The defenders are Farida Abdulwahab, Sandra John, Tumininu Adeshina, Valentina Uroko, Glory Edet, Shukurat Oladipo and Glory Ogbonna.
The midfielders are Christy Ucheibe, Toni Payne, Favour Omenazu, Joy Igbokwe, Jennifer Echegini, Fatimoh Solaty and Suliat Abideen.
The forwards are Rasheedat Ajibade, Shakirat Moshood, Blessing Nkor, Sandra John, Folashade Ijamilusi, Janet Akekoromowei, Uchenna Kanu, Gift Monday and Joy Omewa.
Tunde Eludini is a graduate of the Obafemi Awolowo University Ile-Ife, Nigeria where he studied International Relations. He is a Senior Correspondent coordinating the sports section for PREMIUM TIMES. Twitter : @tundeyeludini

body: MANILA, Philippines – Singaporean singer-songwriter, producer, and musician Charlie Lim returns to Rappler Live Jam on Thursday, October 8! title: Saudi says three dead in airport attacks claimed by Houthis
body: Saudi authorities said Wednesday three people were killed in attacks on two of the kingdom’s international airports, including in the capital Riyadh, after Yemen’s Houthis claimed to have fired on both transport hubs. The Iran-backed Houthis have claimed a wave of attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure in recent weeks, which came as Riyadh-backed forces pressed a counter-offensive against the group’s territorial gains. Since Yemen’s civil war reignited in July, more than 200,000 people have been displaced within the country, the United Nations said Wednesday. The Houthis claimed an attack on Riyadh’s main airport, while the Saudi-led coalition — which backs Yemen’s internationally recognised government in its fight against the group — vowed retaliation. The Houthis later claimed another attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on Thursday and repeated a warning — “for the last time” — to airlines to avoid Saudi airspace. “On Tuesday and Wednesday… Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport were subjected to attacks targeting their facilities,” Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation authority said in a statement. An Egyptian and an Algerian national were killed at Abha airport, while a Sudanese national was killed at Riyadh airport, the agency said. The attacks wounded 36 people, it added. In a subsequent statement, the coalition directly blamed Houthi fighters for the strikes and vowed a response. “The brutal attacks by the Terrorist Houthi Militia on civilian and civilian objects in the Kingdom, most recently targeting (the two airports) will not go unpunished,” it wrote on X. The coalition said it had retaliated by striking 82 “legitimate military targets”, including missile facilities, command centres, communications systems and Houthi gathering sites. Yemen’s government declared a major counter-offensive against the Houthis this week, claiming to have pushed the fighters out of strategic areas on the Red Sea and the port city of Mocha. But the Houthis insist they are holding their territory, and military sources from both sides contacted by AFP have not reported any major changes on the ground. Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify with the situation moving fast and access for journalists difficult. – Flight diverted – Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said Wednesday that the group had targeted Riyadh’s airport in an “accurate” strike that “led to a disruption of air traffic.” The Saudi-led military coalition said on X it “destroyed the ballistic missile launch platform” used in the attack. The Houthis also said they targeted a military supply convoy near the airport in Aden, the interim capital for Yemen’s government. The government’s Saba news agency reported missiles and drones targeting that airport. The agency cited transport authorities as saying one of the missiles landed near the runway minutes before the scheduled arrival of a flight from Cairo, which was forced to divert to Jeddah in Saudi Arabia. Houthi drones and missiles also targeted Saudi Arabia’s Abha airport and King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait, Houthi spokesman Saree said, claiming they had “hit their targets accurately”. It is the second time this week Houthis claimed to have attacked Riyadh’s main airport. – ‘Terrified’ – Saudi Arabia has led an international coalition fighting the Houthis since 2015, and is now trying to roll back the group’s latest advance. The coalition said Monday it was providing air support for the Yemeni government’s counter-offensive. After four years of ceasefire, the Houthis claimed last month they had seized Yemen’s entire western coastline along the Red Sea in the country’s deadliest fighting in years. New clashes on Wednesday in Yemen’s west left at least 62 combatants dead, including 37 Houthis, military sources from both camps told AFP. Saba also reported that a Houthi missile wounded five civilians in Taiz, a city held by government forces. “We went out into the street to check on the wounded and saw young civilians who had been hit,” resident Al-Fateh al-Eisaei told AFP. “The Houthi shell landed in the middle of the street, right in an area crowded with civilians.” Yemen’s government has announced a goal of retaking all Houthi territory — home to most of the country’s population, and much of it held for more than a decade. The humanitarian crisis caused by the war has left most of the nation’s population dependent on aid. Mohammed, a 33-year-old charity worker who fled from Mocha to Aden, told AFP on Tuesday that “people there are terrified” of the Houthis. title: Yusuf: A Technocrat as Oyo Gov in 2027
body: Kamar Adeolu writes that Oyo State deserves a technocrat, policy-strategist bridge-builder, and a governor with leadership competence come February, 2027. Akim Adebola Yusuf towers above all other candidates in the forthcoming race to Agodi Government House in 2027. His performance speaks to it. Available records affirm it. At just 57, this son of Oluyole soil effortlessly displays the noble principles of accomplished leadership, efficient management with Omoluabi, the ennobling qualities of sublime traits. Here is a man of integrity, honour, learning, character, and sound achievements. Schooled and Rooted for Service Yusuf’s upbringing and educational preparation reflect serendipity: a commitment to excellence, service and a predestined pathway. He attended and completed his secondary education at the highly reputable Government College, Ibadan (GCI), the crucible of the old Western Region’s meritocratic tradition in 1984. He then proceeded to the University of Ilorin and obtained a Bachelor of Science in Political Science in 1988. In 1997, he got a Master of Industrial and Labour Relations (MILR) from University of Ibadan. From the same university, he got Master of Business Administration (MBA) in 2002. By dint of hard work, he earned his professional qualification as an Associate of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN) in 2000. In 2014, he got deeply embedded in national and international governance structures by the prestigious National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies, (NIPSS) Kuru following his completion of Senior Executive Course 36 and subsequently acquired the globally rated and highly recognized mni designation — the quiet badge of Nigeria’s strategic elite. Success Across Borders Long before politics beckoned, Yusuf had conquered Banking and Finance, two of the most demanding but very rewarding developmental sectors of every nation’s economy. As Managing Director/CEO of Skye Bank (Gambia) Limited (2009–2013), he successfully ran full banking operations on foreign soil — a test of leadership, adaptability, and financial stewardship that few Nigerian executives ever face. Based on outstanding performance, the system reinvited him as Transition Managing Consultant for Skye Bank (Sierra Leone) Limited in 2019. From 2016 till date, he has been serving as Asset Management Partner of the Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria (AMCON) — the nation’s resolution vehicle where distressed assets are recovered and financial stability is quietly defended. A Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (FCIB, 2014), he is no dabbler in finance, rather, he is an institution-builder with cross-border experience that Oyo State desperately needs to attract investment, create jobs and corporate development. An Impressive Governance Résumé What truly distinguishes Yusuf from the typical aspirant is that he had actually governed at various levels, different places and numerous times. He served as a Special Adviser on Due Process, Policy and Budget Implementation to former Oyo State Governor, Senator Rashidi Adewolu Ladoja’s administration in 2005–2007. In this position, he sat at the nexus of Oyo State’s administration — enforcing fiscal discipline and ensuring that budgets delivered real value to the people. In 2017, he served as Special Adviser (Digital Transformation) to the then Minister of Communication, bringing federal-level policy depth and a digital economy vision to his portfolio. In 2003, he established The Fortune Group, a pro-active respected good-governance advocacy think-tank. This shows an envisioned leader who had been preparing for governance long before seeking votes. This candidate is not a novice in governance. He knows the ropes. He will not get to power to experiment or govern by trial and error. He has actively combined the attributes of a technocrat with deep corporate governance expertise. It is rare, if not impossible, to find a governorship candidate so steeped in competence. Honours, from different sources, have followed his work: Justice of the Peace, Oyo State (2007); Member of the National Institute (mni) (2014); Fellow, Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (2014); and Honorary Doctorate of Science in Public Administration, IBLT University, Lomé, Togo (2023). Through hands-on experience, he has mastered governance effectively and efficiently. Oyo State should not miss this rare opportunity to elect Yusuf, an accomplished man. Tested, Groomed and Grown Unlike first-time contenders, Yusuf has felt the furnace of electoral politics and has emerged stronger. In 2023, he flew the flag of the Action Democratic Party (ADP) in the Oyo governorship race, finishing 5th of 16 candidates — a highly commendable showing for an outsider platform, and clear proof of grassroots appeal and electoral viability. Now, as the Governorship Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for 2027, he returns to the arena not as a novice but as a battle-tested, better-organised and more widely accepted contender. Yusuf, Oyo State’s Best Choice Oyo State stands at a crossroads. It needs more than slogans; it needs substance. More than popularity; it needs competence. More than promises; it needs proven performance. This candidate’s achievements speak to focus, performance and impact which resonates at the grassroots, domestic, national and international levels. He is suave yet substantive, educated yet humble and accessible, accomplished in the boardroom yet conversant with the burdens of the ward at the grassroots — Yusuf offers a rare synthesis: For the Economy: A technocrat who has managed banks, budgets, financial resources across West Africa can really grow Oyo State’s economy. For Governance: A due process expert who will entrench transparency, discipline and value-for-money. For the Future: A digital transformation strategist who will position Oyo youths for the jobs of tomorrow. For Unity: A bridge-builder whose career spans banking and budgeting, state and federal service, grassroots and global exposure. In a state hungry for resounding, character-driven and cosmopolitan leadership, the case for this Oluyole-born technocrat-politician writes itself. Oyo does not just need a governor. It needs an Omoluabi. In Akim Adebola Yusuf, it has found him. -Adeolu writes from Ibadan.

title: ‘No right to enter classroom’: Teacher beats pupil at Armenian school
body: Teacher beats pupil at school in Armenia A video showing a teacher beating a second-grade pupil at a school in the Armenian village of Vardadzor has shocked people across Armenia . A relative of the girl told journalists that she was so frightened by the incident that she had refused to return to school. The girl’s parents appealed to the Gegharkunik regional administration, demanding that the teacher be dismissed. However, they were told that this would only be possible if complaints were filed by at least seven parents. Social media users responding to the video called on the Interior Ministry to investigate the incident and launch criminal proceedings. The Education Ministry said it had contacted the Interior Ministry, the Education Inspectorate and the National Centre for Educational and Psychological Support to ensure a thorough investigation. “Relevant legal procedures will begin shortly to strip this teacher of the right to teach,” the ministry said . Armenia’s Human Rights Defender, Anahit Manasyan, described the violence against the schoolgirl as “unacceptable and deeply concerning”. The Investigative Committee opened a criminal case over allegations of “inflicting severe physical pain or serious mental suffering on a minor”. By the time of publication, reports had emerged that the teacher had been detained. Shortage of sign language interpreters leaves deaf Armenians without access to education Work-life balance for women in Armenia: how to create family-friendly working conditions ‘Parent hour’ and flexible schedules: Armenia changes labour code What happened A relative of the second-grade pupil told Shamshyan.com that the class teacher had first beaten the girl in the classroom. The violence continued in the corridor after the pupil left the classroom. The girl returned home with swollen eyes and marks from the blows on her neck and arms. “ There had been slaps before, but never beatings like this – with hands and a pointer ,” the relative said. The girl has not attended school since the incident. According to family members, she later encountered the teacher by chance in the street and ran home in terror. The girl’s mother said she did not want the teacher to face criminal prosecution but insisted that she be dismissed. Armenian media reported that the incident was discussed at the school the following day. “ The teacher admits her guilt. She submitted a written statement acknowledging what she had done and asked not to be punished. As a result, I issued her a written reprimand ,” school headteacher Gevorg Nersesyan said . He also said such incidents were unacceptable and expressed surprise that a teacher with 30 years of experience could have treated a second-grade pupil in this way. 'Polite children are seen as weak': violence among teenagers on rise in Armenia What is happening in schools: the story of a mother and her 15-year-old son. An expert explains the situation and suggests ways to address it. ‘Schools must be a safe environment for children’ Armenia’s Human Rights Defender, Anahit Manasyan, stressed that schools must provide a safe environment for children. “ Any form of violence against a child or any other form of inappropriate treatment is fundamentally incompatible with respect for the child’s dignity, safety and rights ,” she said. According to Manasyan, children must be protected not only through responses to individual incidents, but also through effective measures to prevent and address potential cases of violence. Manasyan also questioned the effectiveness of mechanisms designed to protect pupils in schools, particularly the work of pupil protection groups. “ The effectiveness of these mechanisms should be assessed primarily on the basis of how they work in practice ,” she said. Pupil protection groups were established in all schools on 1 September 2026 by order of the Minister of Education, Science, Culture and Sport. They were specifically set up to prevent violence, bullying and other high-risk situations. Following the incident at the school in Vardadzor, the pupil protection group held a meeting. However, according to the girl’s relatives, no steps were taken to help her return to school. The Office of the Human Rights Defender said it had launched an investigation into the incident. What makes Armenian migrants return home: personal stories Recently many have been returning to Armenia, but few talk about the reasons Not the first case of violence since start of school year Two weeks ago, a maths teacher at a school in the village of Berdavan in Armenia’s Tavush region slapped a 13-year-old boy across the face. He also pushed the pupil, forcibly made him sit at his desk and hit him on the head with a notebook, striking the child’s eye with its edge. According to the boy’s mother, the teacher’s wife, who is the school’s deputy headteacher, also treated him harshly. She slapped him across the face, pushed him into her office and made him stand in the corner. Although the boy continues to attend school, his mother told journalists that he had been left psychologically distressed by the incident. The teacher has also been charged with “inflicting severe physical pain or serious mental suffering on a minor”. He has been released on an undertaking not to leave the country and suspended from his duties. 'Major cause for concern': expert view on Armenian school students’ low level of knowledge According to an OECD study, 15-year-old Armenian school students rank last in the region in terms of their level of knowledge, particularly in mathematics, science and their ability to analyse what they read. Comment Social media reactions “ A written reprimand is not enough. A teacher like this should be barred from working in education .” “ If people like this were prosecuted, teachers would think twice before raising a hand against someone else’s child .” “ Someone who displays such aggressive and unacceptable behaviour simply has no right to call themselves a teacher. What can such a person teach children – respect, kindness or compassion for others? “ “ If a similar incident had happened in Germany, for example, the teacher could have faced up to five years in prison. Moreover, if the headteacher had seen the footage – had seen a child being beaten – but failed to take appropriate action, questions would also arise about his professional responsibility. “ “ If the teacher behaves so brazenly in front of a camera, it is frightening to imagine what she might have done in a classroom without cameras. She should be dismissed, made to apologise to the child and permanently banned from teaching .” “ The situation is much the same in almost every school. In some, there is physical violence; in others, psychological pressure; and in some, children are simply ignored. At parents’ request, cameras should be installed not only in school corridors but also in classrooms .” “ When such incidents become public, headteachers condemn the teacher’s actions and express utter surprise that someone with more than 30 years of teaching experience could behave this way. But before things reach that point, when we ask for cameras to be installed, those same headteachers come up with a thousand excuses to prevent it .” “ They just don’t want teachers to be embarrassed or parents to see how often a teacher talks on the phone during lessons. “ Young teachers head to remote villages under Armenia’s 'Teach for Future' programme It has been running for over 10 years, aiming to improve education quality. The programme’s structure and achievements over this period.

title: France promised a war economy. CAESAR ammunition still depends on one fragile forge
body:
France has spent the years since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine speaking about a return to the „war economy”. Yet one of the most important links in its 155 mm artillery ammunition chain still rests on a single forge in Tarbes, whose machines are failing, deliveries have been disrupted and ownership remains uncertain. The case is not only about one troubled factory. It is about whether France can still turn political declarations into industrial depth.
France does not lack an ammunition industry. KNDS, Eurenco and other companies remain important parts of the French and European defence-industrial base. The problem lies in one specific and sensitive stage of the chain: the forged bodies used for large-calibre 155 mm artillery shells, including ammunition fired by CAESAR systems. Forges de Tarbes is not „ the only French ammunition factory ”, and it should not be described as such. It is, however, the only French forge able to produce these large 155 mm shell bodies at scale. That distinction matters, because it makes Tarbes a critical domestic point of failure.
This is not an interpretation imposed from outside. In 2026, the French DGA itself acknowledged that KNDS had, in practice, no real domestic alternative for this type of component. That means France can have modern artillery, operational experience, export success and political ambition, but still remain exposed if one industrial stage cannot follow demand.
The orders exist. At the end of 2025, KNDS signed an unprecedented three-year agreement with Forges de Tarbes covering between 60,000 and 150,000 155 mm shell bodies in total for 2026–2028, with the possibility of extending the agreement for another three years. That point has to be stated precisely. It is not an annual volume of 60,000 to 150,000. It is the total publicly announced range for the initial three-year period. The contract confirms that Tarbes remains central to French artillery production, but it does not prove that France has already rebuilt the industrial depth required for a long war.
The gap between ambition and capacity is the real issue . Europlasma had previously presented plans to raise output at Tarbes to 150,000–160,000 shell bodies per year by the end of 2025. Yet in 2026, DGA figures pointed instead to a capacity of around 65,000 shell bodies, with an ambition to reach roughly 100,000 in 2027. In other words, the problem is not only that one factory suffered a difficult month. The problem is that the industrial reality remains far below the level that had been presented as the horizon of the „war economy”.
The latest reports make the situation even more serious. Production was reportedly stopped from around mid-August to mid-September after repeated machine failures. Employees also described severe disruption in raw-material deliveries since March, late salaries and a climate of fear inside the plant. The workforce figure also tells its own story. Recent reporting puts the site at around 60 employees, whereas earlier in 2026 the DGA referred to roughly 100. There may be methodological explanations for that difference, but the image is still troubling, and a site described as essential to artillery production does not look like a secure industrial pillar.
Europlasma’s financial position strengthens that concern. The group reported a heavy loss for 2025, including a net loss attributable to the group of €35.6 million, negative EBITDA and negative equity. It has relied increasingly on highly dilutive convertible-bond financing, a type of instrument about which the French financial regulator has repeatedly warned because it is often used by companies whose financial situation makes conventional credit difficult to obtain. In a normal industrial sector, such a structure would already raise questions. In a critical defence supply chain, it becomes much harder to accept.
The pressure has also reached the physical assets of the factory. In March 2026, the real estate of the Tarbes site was sold in a sale-and-leaseback transaction. In practice, the company exchanged ownership of the site for immediate liquidity while taking on a recurring rental cost. For an ordinary company, this might be presented as a financial adjustment.
There is also no clear public ending to the ownership story. In April 2026, Europlasma announced exclusive negotiations with an unnamed French investor over the sale of its defence activities for around €150 million. The exclusivity period was later extended, and in June the group said talks were continuing. By early October, however, there had been no public confirmation that the transaction had closed and no public identification of the buyer. For a site described as essential to national defence production, such uncertainty is difficult to reconcile with the language of urgency.
The French state has not been absent. Paris provided more than €7 million in public advances or loans in 2022 and 2023 to support modernisation, and the DGA says it remains in regular contact with Europlasma while monitoring the proposed sale in order to protect French industrial sovereignty. This matters, because the case should not be reduced to the claim that the state simply disappeared. The problem is different because the state has been watching, supporting and monitoring, but has not yet presented a clear public solution that matches the strategic importance of the site.
The comparison with Germany is uncomfortable for France. Rheinmetall opened its new 155 mm plant in Unterlüß in 2025 , with planned capacity rising from 25,000 rounds that year to 140,000 in 2026 and up to 350,000 in 2027. The German model is not perfect, and no country has solved every problem in the ammunition chain, but Berlin is bringing a large integrated production site online at the same time as Paris is still dealing with uncertainty around one critical forge.
Poland is also moving in the direction France says it wants to take , although Warsaw has not yet completed the full chain at target scale. MESKO plans new shell-body capacity in Kraśnik, while Nitro-Chem is expanding elaboration capacity and Poland is working with Eurenco on modular charges. The point is not that Poland already has everything. It does not. The point is that Poland is building additional nodes in the chain, while France still depends on one domestic source for a critical forged component. In a long-war environment, that difference matters.
The deeper problem is therefore not that France lacks knowledge, companies or artillery tradition. France remains one of Europe’s most serious military powers, and CAESAR has become one of the most visible symbols of its defence industry. But artillery credibility is not the same as industrial depth. A gun is only as useful as the ammunition chain behind it, and an ammunition chain is only as strong as its most fragile stage. If the shell body depends on one financially vulnerable site, the whole political language of ramp-up becomes weaker.
The issue is therefore not a temporary difficulty at one provincial factory. It is a test of whether France really treats artillery production as part of national power, or only as a sector that can be described in speeches when the political moment requires it. Four years after Paris started speaking about a „ war economy ”, one of the key links in the 155 mm ammunition chain still depends on a single domestic forge, weakened by financial uncertainty, an unresolved ownership situation, ageing equipment and disrupted deliveries. In peacetime, this might be presented as another industrial restructuring. In the current security environment, it is much more serious.

title: Air defense downs 126 of 142 Russian UAVs – Air Force
body:
Overnight into October 8, Russian occupation forces attacked Ukraine with 142 strike UAVs, including Shahed drones, Gerbera drones, and Parodiya-type decoy drones, the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reports.

"According to preliminary data, as of 09:30, air defense shot down/suppressed 126 enemy Shahed, Gerbera, and other types of UAVs," the General Staff's Telegram channel statement reads.

In addition, Russian air attack impacts were recorded at 7 locations, while fallen debris was registered at 4 locations.

The air attack was repelled by aviation, anti-aircraft missile troops, electronic warfare (EW) units, uncrewed aerial systems units, and mobile fire groups of the Ukrainian Defense Forces.

The attack is ongoing, with several Russian UAVs remaining in the airspace.

title: France Delivers First Upgraded Leclerc Tank Turbomachines Sets 25-Unit Annual Target
body:
France has d elivered the first two refurbished turbomachines for its Leclerc main battle tank fleet, marking the start of a new industrial maintenance program designed to secure the availability of the tanks while bringing more of the work under government control.
The French Directorate General of Armaments (DGA) and the Aeronautical Industrial Service (SIAé) said on October 5 that the first two turbomachines had been overhauled at the Aeronautical Industrial Workshop (AIA) in Bordeaux. The units underwent NTI3, or Technical Intervention Level 3, maintenance and were delivered ahead of schedule after testing confirmed that they had regained their original performance.
The turbomachines are a critical component of the Leclerc's hyperbar diesel propulsion system. By supplying compressed air to the engine's cylinders, they increase the amount of air available for combustion and enable the engine to produce greater power.
The overhaul capability was moved into the French Ministry of the Armed Forces and Veterans Affairs as part of a broader effort to control maintenance costs and protect the operational availability of the Leclerc fleet.
In July 2023, the DGA awarded the maintenance contract to SIAé, with AIA Bordeaux responsible for the industrial work and Safran Helicopter Engines acting as a subcontractor. Safran is the original designer of the Leclerc's turbomachine, while KNDS, the tank's industrial prime contractor, was involved in the earlier reindustrialization study.
The decision followed a DGA-led study into restoring an industrial capability for NTI3-level maintenance of the turbomachines. The DGA said using AIA Bordeaux reduced costs compared with quotations received from industry.
The first deliveries now move the program from reindustrialization into production. The target is to refurbish 25 Leclerc turbomachines annually from 2027.
Responsibility for monitoring the contract will now transition from the DGA to France's Integrated Structure for the Operational Maintenance of Land Equipment, within the Ministry of the Armed Forces and Veterans Affairs.
