title: NAF explains confusion over 25, 32 crash victims
body: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has explained the discrepancy in the reported number of victims of the ATR 42 aircraft crash at Igbokoda, Ondo State, saying a misunderstanding of civil and military aviation terminology led to the initial figure of 32 persons being reported. Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, who provided the clarification, said the confusion arose from the different ways civil aviation air traffic controllers and the military use the term “souls on board.” Ejodame explained that while civil aviation terminology could describe the number as “25 souls on board, inclusive of seven crew,” military usage counts the seven crew members within the total figure of 25, rather than adding them to it. He said: “For air traffic controllers, when they normally communicate ‘25 souls on board inclusive of seven crew’, it is minus the seven. “However, for the military, the seven is in the 25. It doesn’t mean you add additional souls. “In this case, there were 25 souls on board: five were active crew, then two were passengers, but they are crew. So, there are seven crew on board reported, but only five were flying at that time. “The other two were on board as passengers.” The clarification followed an earlier announcement by the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, that 32 people comprising 25 passengers and seven crew members had died in the crash. The NAF subsequently clarified that 25 people were actually on board the aircraft, comprising five crew members and 20 passengers. The aircraft, NAF 931, crashed in the Igbokoda area of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State while on a routine mission from Benin, Edo State, to Lagos. Keyamo had said the aircraft disappeared from radar at about 9 a.m. local time, corresponding to 7 a.m. GMT, before it was subsequently located after crashing about halfway through its journey. The wreckage was found in a swamp near a naval base, where it remained submerged as recovery operations continued. The NAF later released the names of the 25 people on board, comprising five crew members and 20 passengers. The five crew members were Squadron Leader MI Aburime, Flight Captain; Squadron Leader AP Man-Ugwueje, Co-pilot; Flight Lieutenant IS Bako, Co-pilot; Warrant Officer Abubakar A, Aircraft Technician; and Corporal Uguru HC, Aircraft Technician. The passengers were Flight Lieutenant TL Lazarus; Flight Lieutenant M Akinloye; Flying Officer IM Adeshina; Master Warrant Officer Onwuka F; Master Warrant Officer Matini BA; Warrant Officer Nuhu FS; Flight Sergeant James RB; Flight Sergeant Mohammed AI; Sergeant Ani AE; Sergeant Izibenikien SI; Sergeant Alafuka C; Sergeant Mbadugha AN; Lance Corporal Ugwuba FC; Lance Corporal Eledan GE; Mrs Ezeh Nneka; Godstmine Tarabina; Joy Micheal; Sunday Micheal; Ukeme David; and Gideon Omotola. The Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, had expressed condolences to the families of those who died in the accident, describing the incident as a deeply painful moment for the Nigerian Air Force and the country. The NAF said search-and-rescue procedures were activated immediately after the accident, with response efforts conducted in coordination with relevant authorities. It added that no survivor had been found. Investigation ongoing On the investigation into the crash, Ejodame said the NAF was relying on established aircraft accident investigation procedures rather than an ad hoc process. He said the Chief of the Air Staff had directed a comprehensive investigation into the circumstances surrounding the crash, with a board of inquiry or committee constituted for the purpose. According to him, the findings would be communicated by the appropriate board or committee after the preliminary report was concluded. The NAF had earlier urged members of the public to refrain from speculation and the circulation of unverified information while the investigation continued. It also appealed to the public to respect the privacy and dignity of the affected families. A condolence register was opened at the Headquarters of the Nigerian Air Force in Abuja for senior government officials, members of the diplomatic corps, heads of security agencies and other well-wishers wishing to pay their respects to the deceased and sympathise with their families. The post NAF explains confusion over 25, 32 crash victims appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Army allegedly detains Plateau human rights defender
body:
A Plateau State-based human rights defender and conflict reporter, Lawrence Zongo, has reportedly been arrested after he visited a military medical facility in Jos to see relatives injured in an attack in Bassa Local Government Area of the state.
Mr Zongo was allegedly taken into custody on Monday at the Maxwell Khobe Cantonment, Rukuba Barracks, which houses the headquarters of the Nigerian Army’s 3 Division in Jos, according to sources familiar with the incident.
The sources said Mr Zongo had gone to the facility after relatives were attacked in Miango, Bassa LGA, on Sunday night.
One of his first cousins was reportedly among those injured and later died from injuries sustained in the attack, the sources said.
The sources alleged that soldiers arrested Mr Zongo while he was at the facility and that he had remained in custody without being formally charged.
They also alleged that he had been denied access to his lawyers and family members.
The claims could not be independently verified as of Wednesday afternoon.
PREMIUM TIMES contacted the spokesperson for the Nigerian Army’s 3 Division, Victor Olukoya Victor, to verify the reported detention.
Mr Olukoya said he was unaware of the development and asked our reporter to call back, saying he was not in a convenient place to speak at the time.
Our reporter subsequently sent him text messages, but he did not respond as of the time of filing this report.
Mr Zongo has for years documented insecurity and alleged human rights abuses in Plateau State.
He has worked as a conflict reporter and human rights documenter, including with TruthNigeria, and as a volunteer with Amnesty International.
His reporting has focused extensively on violence and its impact on communities in Plateau, including attacks in Bassa and other parts of the state.
A separate report published on Wednesday also alleged that Mr Zongo had been detained, identifying him as a human rights defender and conflict documenter.
That report also alleged that Zongo was wearing Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses when he visited the military facility and suggested that this may have contributed to his detention.
However, that claim could not be independently verified, and no official statement links the alleged detention to the glasses.
The circumstances surrounding the reported detention remain unclear.
The Nigerian Army has not publicly confirmed the reported detention or explained any security action against Mr Zongo.

title: Most British manufacturers now eyeing defence work
body: Nearly three-quarters of British manufacturers are already working in defence or exploring how to get into it, and four in five have adopted or are trialling artificial intelligence, according to the accountancy firm Crowe . The findings come from the firm’s Manufacturing Outlook Report, produced with the Confederation of British Metalforming, which found 72 per cent of those surveyed engaged in or examining defence manufacturing opportunities and 80 per cent adopting or actively trialling AI. The same survey found the pressures on the sector have not eased at all. Rising operating costs were named as the biggest barrier to growth by 57 per cent, and 62 per cent put skills shortages at the top of their recruitment difficulties. Crowe said defence manufacturing was emerging as a significant opportunity amid increased focus on national security, supply chain resilience and domestic manufacturing capability. Stuart Weekes, partner and head of manufacturing at Crowe, said manufacturing remained central to British ambitions for innovation, productivity, economic growth and national resilience while Stephen Morley, president of the Confederation of British Metalforming, said manufacturers were dealing with cost and skills pressures while investing in AI, exploring new markets and considering opportunities to bring production back to the United Kingdom. Seventy-two per cent is a remarkable proportion for a sector where defence has historically been a specialist niche served by a few hundred firms, and it reflects a change in how British industry reads the next decade rather than a change in how much work is actually available. Whether the department can absorb that interest is a different question, since the barriers to becoming a defence supplier have less to do with willingness than with security clearances, quality accreditation and the time it takes to get onto a prime contractor’s approved list. The post Most British manufacturers now eyeing defence work first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: The US and Israeli elections are making the Middle East wars worse
body: While proponents assert that the spread of democracy is essential to securing peace, two allied democracies – the US and Israel – are engaged in wars that are actually being exacerbated by the fact that both countries are in the midst of elections. From the beginning, in the American mind, democracy has been seen as more than just a form of governance. Both liberals and conservatives have idealised and elevated the idea of democracy into the equivalent of religious doctrine, making exaggerated claims about the benefits that accrue to societies that are democratic. We have been told that democratically elected governments can claim to be more tolerant, more respectful of minority rights, more accountable for their actions, and less likely to start wars. Given this mindset, several past US administrations have made the spread of democracy a foreign policy priority, arguing audaciously that it was essential for world peace. While the US and some of its allies flaunt these attributes, boasting that their democracies place them above societies with other forms of governance, in reality, their claims of purity and adherence to ideals do not hold up to scrutiny. The glaring contradiction between the values that the US and other democracies espouse, and their actual behaviours, have been clear since America’s founding. After all, the American experiment with democracy was built on the backs of slave labour and the genocide of native Americans. And more recently, when the George W Bush administration launched its campaign to promote democracies worldwide, it did so while blundering through a devastating “war of choice” in Iraq and torturing prisoners in “black sites” they had suborned other countries to make available to US interrogators. Much the same can be said of Israel , which Americans tout as “our closest ally” and the “only democracy in the Middle East”. Like the US, Israel claims that its democracy elevates it above its neighbours, making its actions more just and its behaviour more moral. And like true believers in any ideology, when it is pointed out that reality doesn’t agree with their claims, they deny it and criticise whoever has pointed out the disconnect. The fact that democracies hold elections provides them with yet another reason to boast. However, as the rest of the world sees playing out in both Israel and the US, instead of providing a cleansing moment, elections are often used by contesting parties to justify bad behaviours and exacerbate social tensions. In both instances, instead of implementing the values claimed to be the attributes of democracy, these elections do the opposite US President Donald Trump, for example, needs a way out of his no-win war with Iran, especially because of its negative impact on the economy and consumers, and the insecurity and instability it’s fomenting in the Gulf. But he is loath to look weak by ending the war without some claim of victory, because of the negative impact that might have on his legacy and his hold over his base voters – whom he needs to turn out in November to deliver a victory for the governing Republican Party. And so, he continues his bellicose language and threats towards Iran. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu may have assumed that he could manage a governing coalition of parties even more extreme than his own. But his partners have used their positions to aggravate tensions with Palestinians in both Israel and the occupied lands. And when Mr Netanyahu felt compelled to sign on to ceasefires that were supposed to stop the bombing in Gaza and Lebanon, his agreement proved hollow . In the face of criticism from his opponents and even his coalition partners that he was compromising Israel’s security by not “finishing the job”, his government has continued to violate both ceasefires with impunity, while doing nothing to rein in the widespread violence in the West Bank being fomented by his political allies. He feels he must do this because he cannot afford to lose any of his governing partners, or he’ll be out of office. The bottom line is that in both instances, instead of implementing the values claimed to be the attributes of democracy, in practice these elections do the opposite. Political discourse becomes coarser and more divisive, social tensions are aggravated and warlike behaviours are promoted. Especially troubling is that while reporters and commentators know that the words and actions of both Mr Netanyahu and Mr Trump are directed more at appeasing their constituents than they are at the realities in Palestine, Lebanon or Iran, too often they sin by omission and treat the political posturing as if it were real. For example, instead of being honest and treating Mr Netanyahu’s claims that villages in southern Lebanon need to be demolished to fend off his opponents’ accusations of weakness, they report it as if levelling whole Lebanese villages is needed for Israel’s security. This is what has become of two of the world’s allied democracies, as they cultivate and then prey on the worst instincts of voters, instead of providing solutions and challenging voters to make better choices.

title: Iran FM spokesman meets with new Pakistan envoy
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 08 (MNA) – Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei hosted Pakistan's new ambassador to Iran, Ahmed Siddiqui, on Wednesday afternoon, describing the meeting as productive.
Posting on social media, Baghaei said relations between Iran and Pakistan are based on deep historical commonalities and lasting bonds of friendship.
He noted that Iran was the first country to recognise Pakistan immediately after its independence in 1947, and said Tehran is determined to enhance bilateral relations for the good of both nations.
The meeting took place at the Foreign Ministry on Wednesday afternoon.

title: Four injured in shelling across Kharkiv region in past 24 hours – official
body:
Over the past 24 hours, the Armed Forces of Russia launched strikes against Kharkiv and 11 settlements in the region, leaving four people injured, Head of the Regional Military Administration Oleh Synehubov reported.

"In the city of Kharkiv, a 67-year-old woman was wounded, and a 30-year-old man experienced an acute stress reaction; in the town of Derhachi, a 62-year-old man was wounded; in the village of Dobrenka, Natalynka community, a 70-year-old woman sustained injuries," Synehubov wrote on his Telegram channel.

title: Defense Forces and Russian troops engage in 224 clashes on front line over past 24 hours
body:
According to Ukrinform, this information is contained in a Facebook post by the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine regarding the situation as of 8:00 a.m. on Thursday, October 8.
The enemy launched one missile strike and 74 airstrikes, using 223 guided bombs.
In addition, Russian invaders deployed 8,997 kamikaze drones and carried out 2,499 shelling attacks, 39 of which were from multiple launch rocket systems.
Neskuchne, Pysarivka, Pavlivka, Korchakivka, Velyka Rybytsia, Potapivka, Korenok, and Sopych in Sumy region came under Russian attack.
The Defense Forces’ aviation, missile forces, and artillery struck two UAV command posts, one area where enemy personnel were concentrated, and three Russian artillery systems.
One enemy assault was recorded in the Northern Slobozhanshchyna and Kursk sectors. The Russian Federation’s army launched two strikes with seven guided bombs and carried out 161 shelling attacks.
In the Southern Slobozhanschyna direction, Ukrainian units repelled 12 enemy attacks. The invaders attempted to advance near Hrafske, Synelnykove, and Volokhivka, as well as toward Ternova, Mykolaivka, and Radkivka.
In the Kupiansk direction, the enemy launched two assaults in the areas of Kivsharivka and Novoosynove.
In the Lyman direction, Russian forces launched four attacks in the areas of Novoselivka, Stavky, and Dibrova.
In the Sloviansk direction, Russian troops carried out one attack toward Piskunivka.
In the Kostiantynivka sector, 24 enemy attacks were recorded. The invaders conducted offensive operations in the areas of Kostiantynivka, Illinivka, Vilne, and toward Kurtivka, Pavlivka, and Mykolaipillia. Two more clashes are ongoing.
The enemy carried out 16 attacks in the Pokrovsk direction, attempting to advance in the areas of Bilytske, Svitly, Krasnopodillia, Myrne, Molodetske, and toward Novyi Donbas, Dobropillia, and Serhiivka.
In the Oleksandrivka direction, the Defense Forces repelled one Russian attack toward Ternove.
In the Huliaypole sector, the enemy attacked 14 times, attempting to advance in the areas of Zlagoda, Ternuvate, Dolynka, and Hirke.
In the Orikhiv sector, Russian troops made one attempt to attack in the direction of Mahdalynivka.
In the Kramatorsk and Dnipro River sectors, the Russians did not conduct any assault operations.
In the Volyn and Polissia sectors, no signs of the Russian Federation forming offensive groups were detected.
As reported by Ukrinform, the total combat losses of Russian troops since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine—from February 24, 2022, to October 8, 2026—amount to approximately 1,547,780 personnel.

title: UK keeps Jerusalem mission open despite Israeli closure order
body: Britain will keep its diplomatic mission in East Jerusalem open despite an Israeli order to close the consulate, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said on Thursday, averting an immediate escalation between the two allies as talks continue over the dispute. Mr Miliband said the building would remain independent and operational under a new name, UK Mission, Jerusalem , and continue serving Palestinians in the city and the wider occupied Palestinian territories. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said Israel had implemented measures announced last month, but that the two sides had agreed to continue dialogue. He said the British consulate had ended its role in the city and that 19 diplomats would leave Israel , while a task force of seven British diplomats would be allowed to continue operating from the building with a limited remit. “Following discussions with the Israeli government, our consulate general building will not be closing,” Mr Miliband said. “It will be known as UK Mission, Jerusalem, and will be independent and operational.” The dispute follows Britain's sanctions against Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank . We retain our long-standing presence in Jerusalem. My statement: pic.twitter.com/ABnaopUBwU — Ed Miliband (@Ed_Miliband) October 8, 2026 “We have been clear that we do not accept that the government of Israel has the legal right to close the British consulate general in Jerusalem, which has been there for nearly 200 years,” Mr Miliband said. “The UK government reiterates its long-standing view that East Jerusalem is occupied territory.” His announcement came hours after workers removed signs and plaques identifying the building as the British consulate general. Signage identifying the mission was still missing on Thursday, although the British flag remained flying above the building. Officials that remain are believed to retain the diplomatic protections that governs their work and residence in the city. It is not thought they are accredited through the embassy in Tel Aviv, a long-run aim of the Israeli government. Documentation and status remains as before the recent impasse erupted. The changes implemented on Thursday should not expose the other diplomatic missions in East Jerusalem to further repercussions. The UK government appears determined to preserve its diplomatic presence for Palestinians while avoiding escalation with Israel. “The mission is a fudge, not a downgrade. The UK has a mission to the UN in New York and to the UN in Geneva,” a diplomatic source told The National. Though the implications for the UK's recognition of Palestine were unclear, “a working arrangement is better than none,” they said. UK Middle East Minister Stephen Doughty rejected suggestions that the arrangement represented a political fudge allowing Britain to say the mission remained open while Israel could claim it had closed. “The building remains open. We continue to have staff able to do important work, engaging with the Palestinian Authority, supporting British nationals, and we are engaged in ongoing conversations with Israel on this matter,” he said. Regardless of the name change, Mr Doughty said, Britain’s presence needed to remain. Mr Miliband said: “We will work to build back up our presence in the coming months.” Britain has withdrawn several diplomats, staff and family members in recent weeks. The Foreign Secretary said the withdrawal had been necessary because Britain had not received sufficient security assurances. “Without an understanding, we would not have the necessary assurances for the security and protection of our staff and premises. Accordingly, the UK has temporarily withdrawn a number of staff and families to ensure their safety and security,” he said. The consulate handles Britain's relations with Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza and provides consular services to Palestinians. Britain's diplomatic presence in Jerusalem dates back almost 200 years, well before the establishment of Israel in 1948. Israel ordered the consulate to close within 30 days after Britain announced measures including a ban on imports of goods produced in Israeli settlements and sanctions against individuals and companies supporting settlement activity. The UN and most countries consider the settlements illegal under international law, while Israel disputes that position. Any country that acts against Israel must know that there will be a price for doing so Gideon Saar, Israeli Foreign Minister Mr Doughty said the UK remained engaged in dialogue with the Israelis and would push on with the sanctions on illegal settlements. He said the move, along with Britain's accusation that the Israeli government was turning a blind eye to “ethnic cleansing”, had enraged the Israeli government and led to its decision to close the consulate. Mr Saar said all four measures he announced on September 8 had been implemented, including removing British representatives from the International Gaza Support Centre in Kiryat Gat, ending British activity to train Palestinian Authority forces in the West Bank, and barring 12 British officials and other citizens from entering Israel. He said Israel had agreed to continue dialogue with Britain, but warned: “Any country that acts against Israel must know that there will be a price for doing so.” Mr Miliband also sought to dampen speculation that Britain would retaliate by expelling Israeli diplomats. “We will not take reciprocal action while such discussions are under way and credible,” he said. Britain had been considering expelling Israeli diplomats if Israel forced the consulate to close, sources told Reuters earlier this week. Such a move would have represented a highly unusual escalation between two countries that remain close security and intelligence partners. The confrontation marks another sharp deterioration in UK-Israel relations after Britain repeatedly criticised Israel's conduct in Gaza and Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu 's government has accused Britain's Labour government of hostility towards Israel. “This will ensure that we maintain our long-standing British presence and the UK's role in support of [a] two-state solution,” Mr Miliband said. With the UK reserving its position to hold further negotiations, political ties with the Palestinians will be maintained following the reduction of almost three quarters of the staff posted to the mission. title: Indian in Al Ain wins $1 million draw after trying for 11 years
body: Shaheen Mohammed has been buying Dubai Duty Free tickets since 2015, in the hope of finally hitting the jackpot. Just before turning 39 on October 16, he secured an early birthday gift after being named a $1 million winner on Wednesday. The Indian engineer, an Al Ain resident for six years, bought winning ticket 3097 on September 11. A father of one, he works as a senior estimation engineer for a construction company in Mussaffah. “This really gives people an opportunity to make their dreams come true and helps them achieve their goals,” he said. “This is an early birthday gift to me too.” Mr Mohammed wishes to buy a house back home in Kerala and save the rest for his daughter's education. He is the 285th Indian national to have won $1 million in the Millennium Millionaire promotion since its inception in 1999. The Dubai Duty Free draw is held every other Wednesday, so there are normally two draws a month. The number of Millennium Millionaire winners in each draw depends on ticket sales. There can be one, two or more. Arya Mustafa, who lives in Iraq, won a BMW car with ticket number 1762 in the Finest Surprise Series 1963, which he purchased online on August 20. Seeyali Shamsudheen, 65, an Indian living in Dubai, won an Aprilia Tuono motorbike with ticket number 0270 in the Finest Surprise Series 680. The father of three works in a phone accessories shop in Karama.

title: Greece Agrees to $4 Billion US Defence Package Including Missiles, F-16 Upgrades and Helicopter Support
body: Greece has agreed to acquire approximately $4 billion worth of US-made weapons, aircraft upgrades and military support , strengthening its air force and helicopter fleets as Athens deepens its defence cooperation with Washington. The package was agreed during US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s visit to Athens and includes missiles and precision-guided bombs, upgrades for Greece’s F-16 fleet and long-term support for its military helicopters. Around $1.2 billion will be spent on missiles and precision bombs for the Hellenic Air Force. The weapons will support Greece’s existing fleet of US-made F-16s and its future F-35 fighter jets , with the first Greek F-35 deliveries expected from late 2029. A further $1 billion has been allocated to upgrade 37 F-16 Block 50 aircraft to the advanced Viper configuration. Greece already operates 83 F-16 Vipers , while the latest upgrade programme is expected to be completed by the end of 2027. Another $800 million will be directed towards support for Greece’s older F-16 aircraft, ensuring continued operational capability across the wider fleet. The package also includes $750 million in follow-on support for the Hellenic Navy’s MH-60R Seahawk helicopters and the Black Hawk helicopters being acquired by Greece. Greece is expected to begin receiving its new Black Hawk helicopters next year , adding another major capability to its military aviation fleet. The latest agreements come as Athens continues a broad modernisation of its armed forces, combining new fighter aircraft, upgraded F-16s, advanced weapons and expanded helicopter capabilities. The US defence package further reinforces the growing military relationship between Greece and the United States, with Washington and Athens continuing to expand cooperation across defence, security and strategic infrastructure. title: 2027: Plateau voters, not outsiders, will choose next governor, says Plang
body:
Senator Diket Plang (APC-Plateau Central) has warned politicians against attempting to influence or determine who becomes governor of Plateau State in the 2027 election from outside the state.
Mr Plang said the people of Plateau must be allowed to freely choose their governor, arguing that allowing external political interests to dictate the outcome would undermine the state’s political independence and its leadership role in the Middle Belt.
The senator, who chairs the Senate Committee on Employment, Labour and Productivity, made the remarks in Jos while responding to questions on political developments ahead of the 2027 elections.
“It will be unfair for anybody to think that somebody somewhere can decide who will be governor for us. Then we will lose our honour; we will lose our leadership in the region,” Mr Plang said.
He urged political stakeholders, traditional leaders and residents to ensure that the 2027 election reflects the choice of Plateau voters and that elected officials remain accountable to the people.
“Somebody should not be standing here and feel that someone will make him a leader outside Plateau,” he said.
Mr Plang also warned politicians against what he described as over-ambitious political claims, saying voters would punish those who approach the electorate with arrogance or disrespect.
When asked whether his comments were directed at the Nyesom Wike-led Rainbow Coalition, which has been involved in opposition political realignments ahead of the 2027 elections, Mr Plang said he was not familiar with the group.
“I don’t even know about Rainbow Coalition. I don’t even know what’s happening about Rainbow Coalition,” he said.
He maintained, however, that any politician who believes the leadership of Plateau can be determined by interests outside the state would be making a serious political miscalculation.
Mr Plang also expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would win a second term in 2027, describing the administration’s policies as “futuristic.”
He said the difficulties associated with the early phase of the administration should not necessarily be interpreted as failure, likening them to the challenges governors often face at the beginning of their tenure.
The senator dismissed the emerging opposition alliances against Mr Tinubu as a collection of competing regional and ethnic interests, arguing that the groups would struggle to maintain a united front as the election approaches.
On the wider conduct of the 2027 elections, Mr Plang identified security, electoral preparedness and political conduct as key conditions for a credible process.
He said insecurity must be addressed to enable citizens to participate freely. At the same time, the Independent National Electoral Commission must ensure adequate electoral materials and logistics to strengthen confidence in the process.
He also urged politicians to campaign peacefully and avoid language that could deepen divisions among communities.
“There are three critical requirements for a successful election,” Mr Plang said, identifying security, a transparent electoral process and responsible political conduct.
He said Nigerian voters had become increasingly politically conscious and would not hesitate to reject politicians they consider arrogant or disrespectful at the polls.

title: Oman’s first international AAM sandbox to shape regulations
body:
Muscat: The Advanced Air Mobility Sandbox planned by the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology (MTCIT) and the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) will be a major initiative not just in the Sultanate of Oman but also in the wider region. International and local operators, manufacturers, technology providers, research institutions, and industry partners will get the opportunity for live field performances and trials in the regulatory-friendly environment between December 6 and 10. According to an official connected consortium mandated by the National Advanced Air Mobility Strategy, "This is the first international sandbox, which covers sectors - healthcare, security, agriculture, and air taxis and we invite all operators and service providers to participate in these trials and help us take some reference when we succeed in this mission." The GUAMobility Consortium has been conducting strategic workshops, focused on Investment, Financing & Public-Private Partnerships to support the development of a strong and sustainable AAM ecosystem in Oman. This workshop marks an important step towards transforming Oman’s AAM vision into concrete opportunities for investment, innovation and long-term grow, according to an executive of the consortium. "The idea behind sandbox is to make sure, the idea is to get inputs to enhance regulations and how to create a certification process. Following the conclusion of the Sandbox there will be workshops with about consisting of different operators and authorities. The AAM ports will be developed in all governorates of the Sultanate of Oman, including Muscat, Suhar and Salalah among others." Muscat Airport will be identified mainly for operating taxi services, linking the Sultan Haitham City and other paces. Regarding the actual implementation of the AAM project, the start of the drone-deliveries will be the first implemented, because taxi services will also depend on the corridor to be marked for the service and development of the vertical ports Muscat Airport has been identified for the existing facilities such road and parking infrastructure, security, safety facilities (including fire and rescue), power charging facilities, a gateway linking traditional, advanced air mobility and ground transportation.

title: [Rear View] Nakakaihi ba ang revelations, counsel?
body: It’s a fair question to ask: How many times has Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team asked for a bathroom break since the prosecution began discussing the bank accounts? On Wednesday, October 7, it was defense counsel Michael Poa’s turn to ask permission to answer the call of nature. Impeachment Court Presiding Officer Chiz Escudero let him go with a parting comment: “You may, you may. You’re excused, Attorney Mike. Why is your side always…” He never finished the sentence. The gallery finished it with laughter. The Vice President’s lawyers would be the first to object to the inference but the pattern is hard to miss. The calls of nature seem to grow most urgent whenever the prosecution reaches for the bank records and asks a witness to verify its existence. Nakakaihi nga yata ang revelations. (The revelations are apparently making them pee.) And we can’t blame them. In her Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) from 2019 to 2024, the Vice President listed zero cash on hand and zero cash in bank. That’s six years without a single peso in the bank yet over the same period, her declared net worth climbed from P55.6 million to P88.5 million. Must Read LIST: Duterte-Carpio bank accounts, balances detailed in impeachment trial The prosecution, citing records from private banks, revealed that the Vice President and her husband, Manases Carpio, maintain some 30 active accounts in at least eight banks with a combined P190 million from the time she was elected vice president. Her defenders say the money was there all along, tucked under “other assets” but the explanation does not survive elementary math. Even a math flunker like this writer figured that out. The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) told the impeachment court that the banks reported suspicious transactions involving the Duterte couple, categorized as possible graft involving flood control and infrastructure projects, malversation linked to confidential and intelligence funds, and drug trafficking. These are red flags that prompt a bank compliance officer to report to the agency. Agree, these are not hard evidence of criminal activity, but these are transactions that needed to be investigated by AMLC, especially when the account holder had declared zero cash in her SALN. Then there’s the problematic involvement of Sammy Uy , the Davao businessman and close associate of the Duterte family tagged by self-confessed Davao Death Squad member Arturo Lascañas as a drug lord. The characterization has been dismissed by Uy’s friends, but the AMLC record has not been disputed: two checks from Uy and his associates in favor of the Vice President totaling P14.8 million between October 2011 and April 2012. Must Read Look back: Remember Arturo Lascañas? The AMLC also reported inward r emittances from China to Calle 88 Foods Corp. , a company linked to Carpio . On the surface, there’s nothing wrong with a food company receiving money from other countries. But with our strained relations with Beijing and intelligence reports of Chinese interference, millions coming from state-owned enterprises to a Duterte-linked food company and charitable foundation demand an explanation. Also crying for an explanation is the movement of P193 million from a joint account held by father and daughter into other accounts in the same bank. The defense, so far, has not issued one, opting instead to badger the AMLC official on his credentials and request bathroom breaks. I would propose a drinking game, one shot of your favorite poison per “excuse me, mister presiding officer.” At the rate the defense lawyers are going, the whole gallery would be hammered before the lunch recess. – Rappler.com Joey Salgado is a former journalist, and a government and political communications practitioner. He served as spokesperson for former vice president Jejomar Binay . Must Read [Rear View] DDS senators have the numbers to acquit. Why aren’t they cheering? title: September hotter than usual across parts of Oman
body:
MUSCAT: September was hotter than usual across several parts of Oman, with average temperatures exceeding long-term levels by up to 1.4°C, according to the Civil Aviation Authority. Al Buraimi recorded the highest monthly average among the six stations listed, at 35.9°C, while Dhalkut in Dhofar topped the rainfall figures with 73.4 mm. Average temperatures at six weather stations in Oman were above their long-term September averages in 2026, with Al Rustaq and Al Buraimi recording the largest departures at 1.4°C, according to statistics released by the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA). Al Buraimi recorded a monthly average temperature of 35.9°C, while Al Rustaq registered 34.5°C. Both were 1.4°C above their respective long-term averages for September. Sohar recorded an average of 32°C, exceeding its September average by 1.2°C. Muscat registered 32.1°C and Sur 32.8°C, both 1°C above their long-term averages. Masirah recorded 27.5°C, a departure of 0.6°C. The figures represent monthly average temperatures rather than the highest temperatures recorded during the month. The CAA explained that a temperature anomaly is the difference between the observed monthly average and the corresponding average calculated from records collected over a long period. In its rainfall statistics, the authority listed Dhalkut in Dhofar Governorate as recording the highest accumulated rainfall during September, at 73.4 mm. Qairoon Hairiti followed with 58.6 mm, while Al Hamra recorded 27.8 mm, Saiq 20.2 mm and Salalah 17.6 mm. The authority also highlighted a historical tropical weather event that affected Oman in September 1979. According to international archives cited by the CAA, the system reached tropical storm intensity before weakening and crossing the coast through Al Wusta Governorate as a tropical depression on September 24 that year.

title: 2027: ADC will not accept rigged elections, David Mark says
body:
The National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), David Mark, says the opposition party will abide by electoral rules in the 2027 general elections but will not accept attempts to manipulate the polls against it.
Mr Mark spoke on Wednesday when members of the Governing Council of the Savannah Centre for Diplomacy, Democracy and Development visited the ADC national headquarters in Abuja.
A former Chief Justice of Nigeria, Olukayode Ariwoola, led the delegation, which chairs the centre’s Council of the Wise.
According to a statement by the Office of the ADC National Publicity Secretary, the visit was part of the centre’s engagement with political parties and other stakeholders ahead of the elections.
Mr Ariwoola urged the ADC leadership to ensure that its candidates and members comply with the rules of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and avoid political violence.
Mr Mark said the ADC was committed to conducting its political activities in a way that promotes public confidence in democracy.
“We are committed to playing politics in a manner that promotes public confidence in democracy,” he said.
He said the party would abide by INEC’s rules and its internal code of conduct contained in the “Orange Book”.
“We hold ourselves to the highest standards of good conduct as a political party. We will play by the rules. But we will not accept rigging or allow ourselves to be rigged out,” Mr Mark said.
INEC’s revised timetable schedules the presidential and National Assembly elections for 16 January 2027, while the governorship and state House of Assembly elections will hold on 6 February.
Campaigns for the presidential and National Assembly elections began on 19 August, while campaigns for the governorship and state assembly elections began on 9 September.
The Savannah Centre reconstituted its Council of the Wise earlier this year, with Mr Ariwoola as chair, to engage political leaders, electoral authorities and other stakeholders on peaceful and credible elections.
The ADC unveiled its Orange Book in August, describing it as a set of governance principles and ethical standards for its members and public officials elected or appointed on its platform.
Other members of the Savannah Centre delegation at Wednesday’s meeting included Abdullahi Shehu, Azeez Musa Dankano, the centre’s Executive Director, Sani Bala, Tunji Lardner and Godknows Igali.

title: American Airlines cleared to join rival United as Azul shareholder
body:
American Airlines has received approval to acquire a minority stake in Brazil's Azul , where its US rival United Airlines has been a shareholder for more than a decade. The country's antitrust authority cleared the US$100 million investment on Wednesday, October 7.
The transaction will give American an 8.66% stake in Azul. United, which established its equity relationship with the Brazilian airline in 2015, received regulatory approval in February to increase its existing holding from 2.02% to approximately 8% .
The arrangement will place two competing US airlines within Azul's ownership structure, with both also entitled to representation in its corporate governance bodies.
American's investment was announced in February under Azul's financial restructuring arrangements following its Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the United States.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
The Brazilian Administrative Council for Economic Defense (CADE) had initially cleared the transaction without restrictions in July. However, Abra Group, the parent company of GOL and Avianca, appealed the decision over concerns about competition on routes between Brazil and the United States.
Brazil's antitrust tribunal unanimously approved the investment, subject to a formal agreement establishing safeguards against the exchange of commercially sensitive information.
American will be entitled to appoint representatives to Azul's board of directors and Strategic Committee, which discusses business plans, network development, investments and commercial partnerships.
Under the agreement, its representatives must be excluded from discussions involving sensitive matters in markets where American and Azul compete. The restrictions cover subjects such as pricing, capacity and commercial strategy.
The agreement also requires advance notification of certain future airline investments by American and changes that could expand its influence over Azul.
Abra had argued that the presence of American and United in the same governance structure could create opportunities for coordination between competitors. The regulator concluded that the identified risks could be addressed through enforceable safeguards rather than blocking the investment.
United's relationship with Azul predates the Brazilian carrier's financial crisis. The US airline originally acquired a minority stake in 2015, alongside a commercial partnership, and maintained that investment through Azul's restructuring.
American and Azul also have an existing codeshare agreement. The new investment will add an equity relationship to their commercial cooperation, although neither US airline will acquire control of the Brazilian carrier.
Azul entered Chapter 11 protection in May 2025 and completed its restructuring in February 2026. The American investment was arranged through warrants issued under the reorganization plan.

title: Russian stock market declines at start of main trading session on Moscow Exchange
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. The Russian stock market declined at the start of the main trading session on Tuesday, according to Moscow Exchange data. Meanwhile, the yuan exchange rate reversed its early gains to trade lower.
At the opening of the main trading session, the MOEX and RTS indices fell by 0.3% to 2,330.32 and 858.79 points, respectively, according to trading data as of 09:00 Moscow time. The yuan-to-ruble exchange rate initially rose by 0.95 kopecks from the previous close to 12.759 rubles.
By 09:15 a.m. Moscow time, the MOEX index accelerated its decline to 2,328.58 points (-0.38%), while the RTS index stood at 858.15 points (-0.38%). At the same time, the yuan turned downward, dropping by 1.95 kopecks to 12.73 rubles.
Earlier, at the opening of the morning trading session, the Moscow Exchange index fell by 0.73% to 2,320.44 points, according to trading data as of 07:00 a.m. Moscow time.

title: FSB detains two residents of Trans-Baikal over election provocation plot
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) has detained two residents of the Trans-Baikal Region who prepared provocations during the recent parliamentary elections, the FSB said in a statement.
"The Federal Security Service in the Trans-Baikal Region has foiled the illegal activities of two Russian citizens who, acting on instructions from Ukrainian intelligence agencies, were involved in preparing a series of provocations aimed at destabilizing the social and political situation in the region during the State Duma elections. FSB officers detained the suspects on the eve of the Single Election Day during operational and search activities," the statement reads.
One of the suspects is a woman who was a member of a precinct election commission. "It has been established that a member of the Freedom of Russia Legion terrorist organization, controlled by the Ukrainian Security Service and outlawed in Russia, instructed a local woman to join one of the region’s precinct election commissions," the FSB said. The handler tasked her with "obtaining some ballots and promotional materials, collecting and providing information on preparations for the vote by political parties and candidates, as well as rigging the outcome of the election process," the statement added.
The second detainee is a resident of the city of Krasnokamensk. According to the FSB, he was recruited by the Ukrainian Security Service to gather information on the election campaign and take photos of regional government buildings and the recruitment office. "In addition, he was ordered to set the city office of one of the political parties on fire during the vote, using an improvised incendiary device," the FSB said.
Investigative and operational activities are underway to establish all circumstances of their illegal activities, as well as their possible contacts.
The FSB reiterated that all individuals who agreed to assist the enemy would be established, prosecuted and duly punished.

title: Three injured in shelling across Kyiv region in past 24 hours – official
body:
Three people were injured as a result of enemy attacks across Kyiv region over the past 24 hours, Head of the Kyiv Regional Military Administration Tymur Tkachenko reported.

"Bucha district. Two people were injured. Ten objects were damaged: three warehouse premises, an infrastructure facility, and four vehicles—three cars and a tractor. Brovary district. One person was injured. A private household was damaged," Tkachenko wrote on his Telegram channel.

All of the casualties have been hospitalized.

In addition, five objects were damaged in Fastiv district, including three private households, a warehouse, and a car.

"Russia continues to strike civilian targets, infrastructure, and people's homes. All operational services are working to eliminate the aftermath of the attack and help those affected," Tkachenko summarized.

title: Minna Miners’ Deaths: Probe panel cites institutional breakdown, training gaps
body:
The federal government’s Independent Investigative Committee probing the deaths of 37 persons in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps ( NSCDC ) in Minna, Niger State, has identified institutional breakdown, overzealousness and inadequate training as issues emerging from its investigation.
The committee’s Chairman, Jonathan Kure, disclosed this on Tuesday during a press briefing in Abuja, while stressing that the panel had not concluded the circumstances surrounding the deaths.
“There are elements of institutional breakdown. There are elements of overzealousness. Some elements that will require more personnel training,” Mr Kure said.
He said the committee had requested a two-week extension to complete its investigation and submit what he described as a “thorough and credible” report.
The committee was initially expected to submit its report on 7 October but has requested an extension until 21 October.
Mr Kure said the extension was necessary because of the volume of evidence gathered and the need to obtain forensic and pathology reports.
He said the committee had inspected the NSCDC custody facility, conducted autopsies, interviewed survivors and bereaved families, and taken statements from NSCDC personnel and other witnesses.
The panel also visited the mining site and the Niger State Command headquarters of the NSCDC, where members examined locations connected with the incident.
According to Mr Kure, the committee had interacted with officers and personnel who were directly or indirectly involved in the incident but was still engaging some of them.
“Because of the peculiar nature of this investigation, it involves a large volume of testimonies and evidence which require our meticulous review and collation,” he said.
He added that the committee was still awaiting forensic and pathology reports considered critical to determining the cause of the deaths.
The chairman said the panel would give persons implicated in the incident, including suspended NSCDC officers, an opportunity to respond before reaching its conclusions.
He said the committee was determined to ensure its findings were evidence-based and could withstand scrutiny.
“We promised Nigerians a thorough job,” Mr Kure said.
He added that the panel would use the additional two weeks to review documentary and forensic evidence, receive outstanding medical reports and hear from people whose conduct or actions may be relevant to the investigation.
The 37 people died after they were arrested during enforcement operations around the M.I. Wushishi and Lukoto areas of Minna on 15 and 16 September.
The deaths were initially reported as 33 before the Niger State Government confirmed that 37 people had died.
The cause of the deaths has not been officially established.
The incident prompted the federal government to establish an independent committee to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths, including the arrests and detention of the victims and possible responsibility, negligence or misconduct.
The committee has also visited the affected communities, met the families of the deceased and interacted with survivors as part of efforts to reconstruct the events.
Mr Kure said the panel was conscious of the grief experienced by the families and would avoid speculation in reaching its conclusions.
The final report is expected to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths, determine responsibility where applicable and recommend measures to prevent a recurrence.
Meanwhile, the Nigerian Bar Association Section on Public Interest and Development Law (NBA-SPIDEL) has called for measures to prevent avoidable deaths in detention facilities across Nigeria.
The chair of NBA-SPIDEL, Uju Agomoh, made the call on Tuesday while briefing journalists ahead of the section’s annual conference scheduled for 10 to 13 November in Abia State.
Mrs Agomoh referred to the recent deaths in NSCDC custody in Minna. She stressed the need for detention facilities to operate in accordance with Nigerian law and internationally recognised human rights standards.
“In particular, NBA-SPIDEL will continue to draw attention to the urgent need to prevent avoidable deaths and abuses in places of detention and to ensure that detention facilities operate in accordance with Nigerian law and internationally recognised human rights standards,” she said.
She said the conference, themed “In Public Interest: Advancing Justice, Democracy and Development,” would examine structural and institutional barriers to access to justice, including delays in the administration of justice, inadequate legal representation and weaknesses in justice-sector institutions.
Mrs Agomoh also called for stronger legal aid, alternative and non-custodial measures, improved detention oversight and a justice system that responds to vulnerable and marginalised Nigerians.
She said meaningful reform required collaboration among lawyers, judges, government institutions, justice-sector agencies, civil society organisations, academics, development partners, the media and citizens.
“We are not gathering in Umuahia merely to discuss problems. We are gathering to identify solutions, responsibilities and pathways for action,” she said.
She also urged the media to scrutinise proposals from the conference and sustain public attention on reforms needed to strengthen Nigeria’s justice and democratic institutions.

title: Japan Launches Seventh Taigei-Class Submarine as Nuclear Propulsion Debate Grows
body: On October 8, Japan’s Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) launched the seventh Taigei-class diesel-electric attack submarine, “Shogei” (しょうげい), for the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF), as Japan considers nuclear propulsion as a possible option for its future submarines. The new 3,000-tonne submarine, with pennant number SS-519, entered the water during a naming and launching ceremony at MHI’s shipyard in Kobe City, Hyogo Prefecture. Like the fourth Taigei-class submarine, “Raigei,” and its successors, “Chogei” and “Sogei,” “Shogei” will be equipped with the new, higher-output Kawasaki 12V 25/31 diesel engines. The submarine, which has a construction cost of about 80.5 billion yen ($509 million), is scheduled to be delivered to the JMSDF in March 2028. The name “Shogei,” written as 翔鯨 in Chinese characters, can be translated as “Soaring Whale.” This is the first time that the JMSDF has named a vessel “Shogei,” and the former Imperial Japanese Navy had no vessel with this name. According to the JMSDF, the submarine has an overall length of 84 meters, a beam of 9.1 meters, and a standard displacement of about 3,000 tonnes. Taigei-class SSK weapons The Taigei-class employs the same torpedo countermeasures system incorporated into the last four Soryu-class submarines. It uses Japan’s newest Type 18 torpedo, which succeeds the Type 89. The new torpedo features improvements in propulsion, target detection, and processing. The class is also capable of launching the UGM-84L Harpoon Block II anti-ship missile against surface targets. The missile has a reported range of 248 kilometers. The seventh Taigei-class submarine, “Shogei” (Credit: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries) Why Japan is considering nuclear-powered submarines The Taigei-class submarines use large-capacity lithium-ion batteries to improve their underwater endurance and operational capabilities. However, conventional diesel-electric submarines must operate their diesel engines to recharge their batteries, requiring them to rise to a shallow depth and use a snorkel for air intake and exhaust. This increases the risk of detection. Their batteries also drain more rapidly during sustained high-speed operations. As a result, conventional submarines cannot match nuclear-powered submarines in combining sustained high speed, long-distance transit and extended submerged operations. As the Chinese Navy expands its activities in the Western Pacific, the ability to deploy rapidly over long distances and remain submerged for extended periods is becoming increasingly important for Japan. Under Japan’s three national security documents adopted in December 2022, the Ministry of Defense (MoD) in Tokyo is pursuing the development and eventual acquisition of submarines equipped with vertical launching systems (VLS) capable of launching long-range stand-off missiles. On July 6, 2026, Japan’s Acquisition, Technology & Logistics Agency (ATLA) awarded Mitsubishi Heavy Industries a 3.9 billion yen (about $24.6 million) contract for research into the total ship optimization design of the next-generation VLS-equipped submarine. The research is scheduled to run from fiscal 2026 through fiscal 2029. Illustration of the next-generation VLS-equipped submarine under study by Japan’s Acquisition, Technology & Logistics Agency (ATLA). (Credit: ATLA) Integrating VLS could require significant changes to submarine design, potentially including a larger hull. More advanced sonar systems and the operation of unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs) could also increase onboard power requirements. However, the amount of energy available to conventional submarines while submerged remains limited by their battery capacity. In September 2025, a panel of experts advising the MoD recommended further research and technological development on VLS-equipped submarines, including consideration of what it described as “next-generation propulsion.” The recommendation did not explicitly call for nuclear propulsion, and Japan has not decided whether its future VLS-equipped submarines will be nuclear-powered. On September 11, 2026, Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi reiterated that Japan would not rule out nuclear-powered submarines as it considers revisions to its three national security documents by year-end. Speaking at a press conference, Koizumi said nuclear-powered submarines can remain submerged and operate for extended periods while maintaining much higher speeds than conventional submarines. He emphasized that these characteristics could allow submarines to carry out their missions while ensuring a higher level of safety for their crews. Such capabilities could give submarine commanders greater operational flexibility and improve crew survivability when attempting to evade enemy anti-submarine warfare operations. However, Koizumi also acknowledged significant disadvantages, including higher costs, the need for larger hulls, specialized expertise for nuclear propulsion systems, and potentially greater underwater acoustic signatures than conventional submarines. Introducing nuclear-powered submarines would also require Tokyo to address issues involving nuclear safety, personnel training, maintenance infrastructure and the long-term operation of naval reactors. For now, Japan has made no decision to acquire nuclear-powered submarines. The central question is what missions its future submarine force will be expected to perform, and which propulsion system would best meet those requirements while protecting the safety of its crews. title: 'He should be ashamed': Liberman condemns Chikli for mocking his Russian accent
body: Diaspora Affairs and Combating Antisemitism Minister Amichai Chikli faced accusations of racism after mocking Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman's Russian accent during a Tuesday 104.5FM interview.Liberman condemned the imitation in posts on X/Twitter, accusing Chikli of ridiculing Russian-speaking Israelis.איפה הגינויים במערכת הפוליטית? איפה התקשורת? איך ייתכן שכולם שותקים? השר שיקלי, שמציג את עצמו כ״איש חינוך״, מחקה בשידור חי מבטא רוסי ומגחיך למעלה ממיליון דוברי רוסית בישראל - ודממה. כן, יש לי מבטא ואני לא מתבייש בו. הוא זה שצריך להתבייש. כך נראה היחס של ביבי וצמרת הליכוד לציבור דוברי הרוסית בישראל. אחר כך הם עוד מתפלאים כשילדים מותקפים בבתי הספר. זו גזענות נטו.— אביגדור ליברמן (@AvigdorLiberman) October 6, 2026Chikli imitated Liberman while referring to his past promise to eliminate Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh within 48 hours. The minister also disparaged Liberman's suitability for political office.Liberman argued that the imitation targeted more than a political opponent, saying it demeaned more than a million Russian speakers in Israel.Liberman condemns mockery of Russian speakers“Where are the condemnations in the political system? Where is the media?” Liberman asked in his post, criticizing what he described as silence over the incident.“Yes, I have an accent, and I am not ashamed of it. He is the one who should be ashamed,” he wrote.Liberman accused Netanyahu and Likud's leadership of displaying contempt for Russian-speaking Israelis and described the imitation as “pure racism.”He subsequently posted a video response. Liberman said Chikli owed an apology to the Russian-speaking community rather than to him personally, citing its members' military service, reserve duty, work, and tax contributions.Politicians, Israeli Olympian denounce Chikli's apparent racismRussian-born MK Vladimir Beliak (Yesh Atid) released a video on X denouncing Chikli's apparent racism."Hey Chikli, what's up? title: FG, Niger plan to organise artisanal mining, Bago says
body:
Niger State Governor Mohammed Bago says the federal government is working with the Niger State Government to establish a responsible mining policy and organise artisanal miners in the state.
Mr Bago disclosed this when he received members of the Niger State Inter-Tribal Association, who visited him to condole with the government over the deaths of 37 artisanal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC).
The development was disclosed in a statement issued on Wednesday by Bologi Ibrahim, the governor’s Chief Press Secretary.
Mr Bago said the government would organise artisanal miners into cooperatives and ensure they have the necessary tools and safety measures to operate.
He also warned against exposing children to dangerous mining activities, saying many had abandoned school for menial jobs, particularly artisanal mining.
“I want to call on you to continue to talk to your wards and children, to desist from illegal activities and also thuggery and rascality,” Mr Bago said.
“A lot of our children have abandoned school for some menial jobs, most especially artisanal mining. The children should not be exposed to these very dangerous operations,” he added.
The governor said numerous illegal activities occur around mining sites and urged parents to monitor their children closely.
The governor’s comments came weeks after 37 suspected illegal miners died in NSCDC custody in Minna.
The victims were arrested during enforcement operations around the M.I. Wushishi and Lukoto areas of Minna on 15 and 16 September.
The deaths were initially reported as 33 before the Niger State Government confirmed that 37 people had died.
The circumstances and cause of the deaths are currently being investigated by an independent committee constituted by the Federal Government.
The committee has inspected the NSCDC custody facility and mining site, conducted autopsies, interviewed survivors and families of the deceased, and taken statements from NSCDC personnel and other witnesses.
The committee has also requested a two-week extension to complete its investigation and submit its report.
The committee’s chairman, Jonathan Kure, said on Tuesday that its findings had pointed to possible institutional breakdown, overzealousness and training deficiencies within the security agency. However, the panel had not concluded its work.
Speaking during the visit, the leader of the Niger State Inter-Tribal Association, George Dike, described the deaths as tragic and unfortunate.
He commended Mr Bago for how he handled the incident and the measures taken to support affected families.
“The Niger State Inter-Tribal Association believes that moments such as this remind us of our common humanity and the need for unity, compassion and collective responsibility,” Mr Dike said.
“Irrespective of tribe, religion or place of origin, a life lost in Niger State is a loss to all of us. We therefore stand united in mourning with the affected families and communities,” he added.

title: Saudi Arabia confirms Ansarullah strikes on two airports
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 08 (MNA) – Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority confirmed Ansarullah attacks on Abha and King Khalid airports, claiming one person was killed and eight wounded at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.
Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority on Wednesday confirmed Ansarullah's attacks on two of the country's airports, claiming that one person was killed and eight others wounded in the attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the capital.
The authority also claimed that in another attack targeting facilities at Abha airport, two people were killed and 28 others were wounded.
Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority announced that one of the two attacks occurred on Wednesday and the other the previous day, but provided no further details about the attacks.

title: ASUSS rejects NUT strike, directs FCT teachers to work
body: The Academic Staff Union of Secondary Schools (ASUSS), Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Chapter, has rejected the indefinite strike declared by the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), FCT Wing, directing secondary school teachers and education officers to report to work and continue their normal duties. The directive followed an emergency meeting of the ASUSS State Executive Council (SEC) to review the NUT’s decision to withdraw services across the territory. In a statement issued on Wednesday, ASUSS described the strike as premature, warning that it could disrupt academic activities and negatively affect students. The union urged its members to disregard the stay-at-home directive, stressing that the academic future of students should not be sacrificed over an industrial dispute. ASUSS also addressed the issues raised by the NUT, including vacancies, promotion and the redeployment of directors in education agencies. On vacancies, the union said the requirement remained part of the Public Service Rules governing establishment control and financial planning. It argued that any changes to career structures should be addressed through dialogue and administrative engagement rather than industrial action. On promotion, ASUSS said the administrative arrangements had already been resolved, explaining that the 2025 promotion exercise would run alongside the 2026 promotion cycle under the FCT Civil Service Commission, in line with circulars issued in September 2026. The union also maintained that the redeployment of directors in education agencies to classrooms was within the statutory powers of management and intended to ensure administrative efficiency. ASUSS further alleged that the strike could disrupt the scheduled 2025/2026 promotion examinations for FCT Education Officers. It therefore directed all eligible education officers to participate in the examinations according to the published timetable. The union appealed to parents and guardians to send their children to school, assuring them that academic activities would continue. ASUSS directed principals, vice-principals and education officers to keep secondary schools open, ensure teachers report to their classrooms and maintain normal academic and administrative activities. It also instructed school authorities to disregard directives from what it described as unauthorised bodies where such instructions could disrupt the academic calendar. The union urged school administrators to monitor attendance and maintain a safe and conducive learning environment, stressing that students should not bear the consequences of industrial disagreements. ASUSS called for dialogue among stakeholders, insisting that the interests of students should remain the priority in resolving disputes within the FCT education sector. title: Lithuanian government extends temporary protection for Ukrainian refugees until March 2028 – Interior Ministry
body:
The Government of the Republic of Lithuania has decided to extend temporary protection for Ukrainian citizens who fled the full-scale Russian aggression until March 4, 2028, the Ministry of the Interior of Lithuania reported on Wednesday.
The decision aligns national legislation with the European Union Council's decree prolonging the temporary protection mechanism for an additional year.
"The war in Ukraine continues, so we need to ensure clarity and stability for the people who have fled it and currently live in Lithuania. The extension of temporary protection allows them to continue legally living, working, and building their lives in Lithuania until it is safe to return to Ukraine," Minister of the Interior Martynas Katelynas stated.
The ministry reported that the Migration Department has already begun the process of replacing digital temporary residence permits for Ukrainians with documents valid until March 4, 2028, starting October 5. The procedure remains standard, is carried out free of charge, and entails no additional requirements.
Applications are submitted through the MIGRIS electronic migration system, after which applicants must visit any convenient customer service branch of the Migration Department by prior appointment to present their original documents.
According to the Lithuanian migration authority, more than 52,000 Ukrainian refugees currently hold valid temporary residence permits in the country under temporary protection, and nearly 109,000 Ukrainians have registered in the MIGRIS system since the beginning of the Russian full-scale invasion.

title: Gov’t will not curb free speech under Mahama – Kwakye Ofosu
body: Minister for Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, has dismissed claims that the government is restricting freedom of expression, insisting that legitimate criticism must be distinguished from criminal conduct. His comments come amid concerns about Ghana’s democratic freedoms, including criticism surrounding the recent arrest of nurse Salomey Baffoe Awiti in Techiman. Speaking at the launch of the 30th GJA Media Awards, Mr Kwakye Ofosu said the government had no intention of interfering with legitimate free expression, but argued that law enforcement must act where social media activity crosses into conduct that threatens public peace. He said some individuals had previously used social media to spread hate speech and commentary capable of worsening conflicts in parts of the country. “Africa is littered with examples of how speech like that led to serious genocide and conflict. And it will be derelict on the part of law enforcement to sit and not do anything about people who abuse the space of social media to engage in these sorts of activities,” he said. Mr Kwakye Ofosu said law enforcement had used available technology to identify and address such activities, but stressed that such interventions should not be interpreted as a crackdown on free speech. “Also, a clear distinction must be struck between free speech and criminal conduct. Under no circumstances will the government of President John Dramani Mahama curb free speech,” he said.

title: Trump proposes Camp David-style presidential retreat at his private Florida golf club
body:
FILE - The motorcade for President Donald Trump arrives at Trump International Golf Club, Jan. 2, 2026, in West Palm Beach, Fla. Alex Brandon/AP hide caption
FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. — President Donald Trump on Wednesday said he wants to develop one of his Florida golf courses into a presidential retreat where his successors can spend quiet weekends on the greens, describing it as "sort of a Camp David " that he says would already have many of the security features needed to host presidents and world leaders.
The proposal for the retreat on Trump's private golf course in West Palm Beach would comingle the presidency with Trump's business ventures beyond his time in office, and is the the latest example of Trump seeking ways to leave his imprint on the presidency.
"It's a great idea, and it'll be used a lot," Trump said, claiming it was suggested by the United States Secret Service. "It seems that all presidents play golf."
The plan has already been submitted to local officials. Trump, an avid golfer, rattled off the benefits of the property a short drive from his Mar-a-Lago home during an unrelated event in the Oval Office, noting that it's close to an airport and has some distance from residential homes and tall buildings, which pose security risks.
He did not mention that the golf course was the site of an unsuccessful attempt on his life in 2024. Trump was playing at the Trump International Golf Club during a break from the campaign trail when a Secret Service agent spotted an armed man in the trees lining the club's perimeter fence. The man was arrested after a chase and later convicted of trying to kill Trump, and was sentenced to life in prison.
Past presidents have used Camp David, a rustic compound in Maryland, as a weekend retreat and a place to host presidential meetings. Trump has spent less time there, often opting for his own properties, including golf clubs in Florida, New Jersey and Virginia.
Trump's proposal follows other projects by the lifelong real estate developer to build a White House ballroom, gild the Oval Office, erect a triumphal arch, renovate the Kennedy Center, refurbish the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and rebuild a golf course in East Potomac Park. He has also begun planning a future presidential library in a Miami skyscraper.
In a letter to Palm Beach County commissioners last month, first reported by the Palm Beach Post, an attorney who represents the golf course said Trump is offering to designate it as a "U.S. Presidential Golf Course."
"Just as Camp David, Windsor Castle, or the Elysée Palace are known worldwide, so too will the Presidential Golf Course in Palm Beach County," Harvey Oyer said in the letter.
Palm Beach County Administrator Joseph Abruzzo said in a statement that local officials are eager to explore what this "historic opportunity" could mean to the community. "This likely would further cement Palm Beach County's place on the national and international stage for generations to come," Abruzzo said.
Oyer's letter said the West Palm Beach golf course could be used by current and former presidents, along with visiting foreign heads of state. The Trump Organization owns the golf club but leases the land from the county, which would need to approve any changes.
Under the proposal, the club would pay to build a new presidential lodging and then work with the Secret Service and other agencies to provide free access to the federal government. The retreat would have a separate entrance from the private club, which earned Trump nearly $37 million during his first year back in office, according to his financial disclosure.
"This is a gift that the President would like to share with his successors, the people of America, and his fellow Palm Beach County residents," Oyer wrote. "It should be noted that President Trump will be out of office before this proposed project could be completed so this is a gift to his successors."
Oyer highlighted past U.S. presidents who turned over land for public use. Dwight Eisenhower donated his Gettysburg Farm in Pennsylvania to the National Park Service, and Franklin D. Roosevelt donated part of his estate in Hyde Park, New York.
Years before it was bought by Trump, Mar-a-Lago itself was proposed as a "Winter White House."
Businesswoman and socialite Marjorie Merriweather Post left the home to the National Park Service when she died in 1973, but the agency returned the home to her estate in 1980 because of high maintenance costs. Trump bought the property in 1985, and it later became his primary residence.
