title: Maricarmen, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction shook Spain, has died
body:
Protesters gather after the reported death of María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction sparked nationwide protests, in Puerta del Sol square in Madrid, Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026. Bernat Armangue/AP hide caption
MADRID — María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her longtime Madrid home sparked nationwide protests across Spain and unleashed a political crisis, died on Wednesday while hospitalized.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez led the way on social media offering his condolences after housing activists and Abascal's lawyer announced her death. Known widely as "Maricarmen," she had become a symbol for renters struggling with Spain's housing affordability crisis.
"All my love to Maricarmen's family and loved ones," Sánchez said in a post on X. "A hug as well to all of us who feel this loss as our own today. Rest in peace."
The emotions ran into anger on the street among the protesters gathered near Spain's Parliament who chanted "Maricarmen lives, the fight goes on!"
Iciar López, a 32-year-old psychologist, shared her feelings with The Associated Press at the protest in Madrid.
"A great deal of sorrow. And above all, the thought that she is the cause, the head of this whole revolution that has happened, and that she can't see it," she said. "It makes me very sad that she can't see if anything comes of it ... That's what angers me the most, honestly."
Spaniards increasingly frustrated by housing costs periodically march in major cities demanding action from lawmakers. But a fresh wave of indignation has swept Spain since Sept. 23, when Maricarmen, who used a wheelchair, was carried on a stretcher from her home of seven decades after police cordoned off the street and removed protesters. She was taken to a hospital because of her fragile health.
Televised images of the eviction prompted thousands of people to protest in Madrid and other cities across the country.
Maricarmen's lawyer, Beatriz Duro, did not disclose the cause of death when she confirmed it to Cadena Ser radio. Duro said that she and the activists were all devastated.
"Maricarmen's case, which captured media attention and traveled around the world, leaves us the image of the shameful violence of these types of evictions and the impact they can have on people's health," Duro said.
She had been expected to return home after leaving the hospital. The real estate company that evicted her in order to rent the property at a much higher price eventually caved in under immense public pressure and agreed to let her return to the apartment.
"Although a historic agreement was reached that would have allowed her to return home, this solution came too late," the Madrid Tenants' Union said in a statement Wednesday. "It was an entirely avoidable situation following a harrowing ordeal."
Maricarmen, 87, waits at home for police to arrive before being evicted from the home where she lived in Madrid, Spain, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. Fernando Sánchez/Europa Press via AP hide caption
The average rent for Spain has almost doubled in the last 10 years, according to the real estate website Idealista. Spain's government said that 26% of Spaniards who rent housing spend an average of 40% of their income on rent and utilities, compared with the European Union average of 18% of renters who do so.
Protesters camped in Madrid's central Puerta del Sol square held a minute of silence after learning of her death.
Maricarmen spent almost her entire life in her apartment, where she first lived with her parents and brother. She later worked as a secretary for the board of a pharmaceutical company, Spanish daily El País reported. She said both her parents died in the apartment.
After retiring in 1998, she spent her days walking around the neighborhood, doing errands and taking care of the precious items in her home. The paper reported that black-and-white family photographs were among the only things she had brought with her to the hospital.
"Maricarmen only wanted to die in her home. She wasn't asking for anything else," Eugenio Melchor, 22, said at the protest in Madrid. "She was dying in her home and she almost did. They have killed her. I mean, there's no other word for it, and I hope those responsible for this pay and go to trial."
Maricarmen's plight galvanized a social movement, prompted Spain's unions to announce a general strike next month and intensified pressure on political leaders. Sánchez called an early election Monday after his government failed last week to push emergency housing measures through Parliament. He now hopes the issue will reinvigorate his Socialist Party and help him form a new government after the Nov. 29 election.
Housing Minister Isabel Rodríguez also expressed condolences, writing on X: "I deeply lament the death of Maricarmen. My condolences to those who accompanied her and fought by her side until the end."
Conservative opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo, who hopes to unseat Sánchez and his left-wing coalition, also offered condolences.
"I want to express my condolences to Maricarmen's family and loved ones. No campaign, no party, no use for political advantage," the Popular Party leader wrote. "When faced with the death of a person, we must only show respect."

title: UAVOS Adds Real-Time Visualization to NAVAI Navigation for GNSS-Degraded Operations
body:
UAVOS has developed a visualization application for its NAVAI vision-based navigation system for use with the portable ground control station. When a communication link with the UAV is available, the system allows the operator to visualize how NAVAI and the autopilot work, including the logic used to select navigation data sources. In this way, the visualization app turns NAVAI’s algorithmic process into an operator-friendly monitoring tool: the user sees not only the resulting position estimate, but also a clear representation of how the system matches onboard images with terrain data.
The application lets the operator follow how NAVAI and the autopilot arrive at the UAV’s position estimate in real time: which reference imagery is being matched, the confidence level of the match, and when the system accepts or rejects a visual fix. Based on what they see, operators can adjust NAVAI parameters directly from the ground control station. For example, operators can adjust the match-confidence threshold or the weighting between visual and inertial sources and immediately observe the effect on the estimated track.
In the portable ground control station interface, the operator can observe:  the estimated flight path of the unmanned aircraft over the orthophoto map;  areas of the satellite map used by the system for image matching;  the results of the visual positioning algorithms;  the confirmed onboard position, when the matching quality and other conditions allow the system to determine the UAV’s coordinates with the required level of confidence.
NAVAI is a vision-based navigation module for unmanned aerial systems, designed to improve flight resilience during beyond-visual-line-of-sight operations under conditions of GNSS spoofing and jamming . NAVAI uses neural networks to match images captured by onboard cameras in real time with preloaded terrain maps, helping unmanned aerial vehicles determine their position when satellite navigation cannot be relied upon. Its operation can complement standard navigation sources and provide an additional layer of situational awareness regarding the UAV’s position.
“The NAVAI visualization application is driven by one goal: giving operators greater confidence, flexibility, and capability,” said Aliaksei Stratsilatau, Founder and CEO of UAVOS. “The recent application is a great example of how we are constantly evolving our platforms to ensure they are at the forefront of technology while providing best-in-class capabilities to operators.”

title: Yemen strikes Riyadh airport with ballistic missile
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 08 (MNA) – Yemen's armed forces announced a ballistic missile strike on Riyadh's King Khalid airport, saying it hit its target precisely and disrupted operations.
In his latest press statement, Yahya Saree, spokesman for Yemen's armed forces, said a Saudi enemy aircraft was downed with an appropriate weapon while carrying out hostile actions in the skies over Taiz province.
The statement also said that King Khalid airport in Riyadh was targeted with a ballistic missile, in continuation of the retaliatory responses of Yemen's armed forces to Saudi aggressors' attacks on Yemeni territory. The missile struck its target precisely and led to disruption of activity at the airport.
Saree said, "For the last time, we warn all international airline companies about the consequences of continuing their flights in Saudi Arabia's airspace."
Yemen's armed forces stressed that the Saudi enemy's airspace, with the exception of the skies over the holy areas of Mecca and Medina, has become a scene of military operations.

title: Ghana to champion ECOWAS adoption of Accra Convention on cargo documents – Trade Minister
body: Ghana is positioning itself to lead efforts within ECOWAS to adopt and implement a new international framework aimed at making trade finance and cross-border movement of goods easier through negotiable cargo documents. The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, said Ghana is committed to signing and ratifying the United Nations Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents, which is expected to provide a common legal framework for the use of cargo documents in financing and trading goods transported by road, rail and air. She made the commitment on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, when she opened a virtual sensitisation programme organised for ECOWAS Member States on the Convention. The programme was intended to help countries examine the implications of the instrument and assess its compatibility with their respective national legal systems. The Convention was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on December 15, 2025, through Resolution 80/162, and is recommended to be known as the Accra Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents. It is scheduled to be opened for signature in Accra on October 26, 2026, giving Ghana an opportunity to host the next stage of efforts towards its adoption. Ms Ofosu-Adjare urged participating ECOWAS countries to use the sensitisation programme to deepen their understanding of the Convention and submit clear recommendations to their respective governments on the way forward. She said Ghana was ready to welcome ECOWAS Member States and stakeholders from across the world to Accra for the signing ceremony. The Secretary of the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL), Anna Joubin-Bret, and ECOWAS Commission Director of Trade, Kolawole Sofola, also encouraged Member States and other stakeholders to participate actively in the process and support the Convention’s signature, ratification and implementation.

title: NHIS coverage rises from 57% to about 70% in less than two years under Mahama — Health Minister
body: Coverage under Ghana’s National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) has increased from 57 per cent to about 70 per cent in less than two years, Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh has said. He attributed the increase to measures aimed at strengthening the scheme’s finances, including the uncapping of the National Health Insurance Levy. Mr Akandoh said the additional resources had improved the NHIS’s ability to meet its obligations to healthcare providers. “We’re strengthening what we have come to meet. We took the NHIS from 57%; as I speak to you now, it’s about 70%. In a matter of less than two years,” he said at the Ministry of Health’s Sector Update Engagement in Accra on Wednesday, October 7. The Minister said funding for the scheme had risen from about GH¢6.5 billion in 2024 to GH¢9.8 billion in 2025, allowing government to increase payments to healthcare providers by an average of 50 per cent. He said the higher payments were intended to reduce delays in settling claims owed to healthcare facilities and improve their capacity to continue providing services to NHIS beneficiaries. Mr Akandoh maintained that improving the scheme’s financial position and ensuring timely reimbursement to service providers were critical to sustaining access to healthcare and reducing financial pressure on beneficiaries.

title: BRICS membership could give Ghana more options in global diplomacy — analyst
body: Ghana could gain greater room to manoeuvre in an increasingly fragmented global order if it joins the BRICS grouping, International Relations Analyst Dr Nana Yaw Mireku has said. He said membership would give Ghana an opportunity to widen its diplomatic and economic engagements beyond its traditional Western partners, while allowing the country to pursue its interests across a broader range of international relationships. “One card that you are likely to score from being a member of BRICS is options,” Dr Mireku said on Citi FM on Wednesday, October 7, 2026. “What it means is that in these changing geopolitical dynamics, if you are a member of BRICS, it gives you options to interact, to negotiate globally beyond looking at a Western corridor or the Western window.” His comments followed Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa’s indication that Ghana intends to submit an application to join BRICS as the government explores ways to diversify its international partnerships, expand economic opportunities and deepen cooperation with countries in the Global South. Dr Mireku said Ghana’s foreign policy should remain anchored in national interest rather than exclusive alignment with any geopolitical bloc. “In the pursuit of our national interest, we do not have to be tied to a particular geopolitical block,” he said. He noted that BRICS includes major emerging economies such as China, India, Brazil and South Africa, which could provide Ghana with additional avenues for diplomatic and economic engagement. The analyst, however, cautioned against viewing membership as an automatic guarantee of access to new markets or financial opportunities. “It does not mean that once you are a member of BRICS, automatically these countries open their markets up to you,” he said.

title: Nellis Air Force Base Renews UNIFY.C2 Contract Following Successful Year-Long Counter-UAS Evaluation
body:
Renewed contract reinforces the value of vendor-neutral sensor integration and a unified common operating picture for Counter-UAS operations.
UNIFY.C2 announced today that Nellis Air Force Base has renewed its contract for the UNIFY.C2 Counter-small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Mission Command Platform following a successful year-long evaluation.
The renewal marks an important transition from evaluation to continued operational use and signals Nellis Air Force Base’s confidence in UNIFY.C2’s ability to support a complex and evolving Counter-sUAS mission.
During the initial contract period, UNIFY.C2 provided operators with a unified common operating picture that brought together data from multiple sources, technologies, and manufacturers. Building on capabilities already in place, UNIFY.C2 streamlined the operator’s workflow, consolidating sensor interface displays, tracks, alerts, and decision-relevant information into a single operational environment.
The renewed effort will continue supporting a collaborative Counter-sUAS approach involving Nellis Air Force Base, Creech Air Force Base, and the Nevada Test and Training Range. Together, the organizations continue to strengthen a coordinated approach that supports installation defense, flight-line security, training operations, range activities, and other mission requirements across the Las Vegas valley.
“We are proud to continue supporting Nellis, Creech, and the Nevada Test and Training Range,” said Jerry McGee, chief executive officer of UNIFY.C2. “The decision to renew after a year of hands-on use reflects confidence in the platform and in our team, and in UNIFY.C2’s ability to bring different systems and different vendors together without creating additional complexity for the operator.”
Nellis Air Force Base serves as a central hub for advanced training, testing, tactics development, and operational readiness. Creech Air Force Base and the Nevada Test and Training Range add distinct mission environments, operational requirements, and geographic considerations that require a flexible and coordinated airspace-security architecture.
By working collaboratively, the organizations are enhancing shared situational awareness across the Counter-sUAS mission and establishing an adaptable foundation that can evolve as threats, technologies, and mission requirements change.
UNIFY.C2’s vendor-neutral architecture allows government customers to select the sensors and technologies best suited for each mission instead of being restricted to a single manufacturer or proprietary ecosystem. The platform can integrate multiple detection modalities—including radar, radio frequency, Remote ID, electro-optical and infrared, acoustic, cooperative surveillance, and other emerging capabilities—into one common operating picture. This approach allows Nellis, Creech, and the Nevada Test and Training Range to retain existing investments, incorporate new technologies as they become available, and configure different combinations of sensors based on the operational environment.
“Counter-sUAS cannot be solved with a single sensor, a single modality, or a single vendor,” McGee said. “Different missions require different technologies. UNIFY.C2 provides the connective layer that allows those systems to operate together and gives defenders one place to understand what is happening, assess potential threats, and coordinate an appropriate response.”
The renewal also reflects a broader shift toward sustained, operationally relevant Counter-sUAS capability. Through continuous modernization and agile integration, Nellis, Creech, and the Nevada Test and Training Range are actively evaluating available technologies, optimizing existing capabilities, integrating complementary systems, and streamlining operator workflows to maximize operational efficiency.
That proactive approach helps reduce risk, improves operator familiarity, and creates a scalable framework for introducing future sensors, data sources, and authorized response capabilities.
UNIFY.C2 is designed to reduce operator workload by correlating information from distributed defense networks and presenting it within a single command environment. The platform supports real-time sensor fusion, track management, operational coordination, alerting, and operational reporting while allowing each organization to maintain visibility appropriate to its responsibilities.
The continued collaboration among Nellis Air Force Base, Creech Air Force Base, and the Nevada Test and Training Range represents a forward-looking model for addressing Counter-sUAS requirements across interconnected installations and mission areas.
“Mission needs evolve quickly,” McGee said. “We are proud to continue supporting this mission and to deliver an operational picture that can adapt at the speed of changing requirements.”
About UNIFY.C2 UNIFY.C2, developed by Spatial Persistent Software, is a vendor-neutral Counter-sUAS Mission Command Platform that coordinates detection, assessment, decision-making, and response across sensors, agencies, and effectors. The platform provides real-time sensor and data fusion, multi-vendor integration, track correlation, mission management, and a unified common operating picture for defense, public safety, law enforcement, and critical infrastructure missions.

title: GoldBod sells $125m to commercial banks in maiden FX sale
body: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) has sold approximately US$125 million to commercial banks in its maiden foreign exchange sale under its new spot FX sales and intermediation framework. JOYBUSINESS understands that the auction was conducted on Tuesday as part of efforts to strengthen transparency, fairness and regulatory compliance in the foreign exchange market. The auction forms part of GoldBod’s plan to provide commercial banks with more predictable and transparent access to US dollars through its GoldBod GoFX platform. $1bn FX Sales to Banks GoldBod earlier announced plans to sell US$1 billion to commercial banks during the month to support stability in the foreign exchange market. The GoldBod programme is expected to generate about US$1.5 billion in total. Of this amount, US$1 billion will be sold to commercial banks, while the remaining US$500 million will be advanced to the Bank of Ghana to support the accumulation of foreign exchange reserves. Twice-Weekly FX Sales Under the new framework, GoldBod will conduct foreign exchange sales twice a week, on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Participating banks will submit their requests during a designated sales window. Where demand exceeds the available FX tranche, GoldBod said allocations will be made on a pro-rata basis to ensure a transparent and equitable distribution of the available foreign exchange. Transactions will be settled on the same day. The US dollar leg will be completed by 3:00pm, while the Ghana cedi leg will be completed by 4:00pm. Measures to Prevent Speculation GoldBod said participating banks will be required to declare that their requests are backed by actual unmet foreign exchange demand or evidence of a short position. The banks will also be required to comply with Bank of Ghana regulations and directives. The measures are intended to ensure that the facility responds to genuine market demand and is not used for speculative purposes. BoG to Provide Regulatory Oversight The programme will operate under the regulatory oversight of the Bank of Ghana. GoldBod said the central bank will have real-time access to the GoldBod GoFX platform. GoldBod will also submit transaction reports to the Bank of Ghana after each sale. The GoFX platform provides electronic submission and allocation processing, as well as time-stamping, transaction histories and audit trails. According to GoldBod, these features are designed to strengthen transparency, accountability and post-trade verification. The details were provided at a meeting between GoldBod and commercial banks ahead of the rollout of the new Spot FX Sales and Intermediation Framework. The framework is expected to provide authorised commercial banks with predictable and transparent access to US dollars through the GoldBod GoFX platform.

JOYBUSINESS understands that the auction was conducted on Tuesday as part of efforts to strengthen transparency, fairness and regulatory compliance in the foreign exchange market. The auction forms part of GoldBod’s plan to provide commercial banks with more predictable and transparent access to US dollars through its GoldBod GoFX platform. $1bn FX Sales to Banks GoldBod earlier announced plans to sell US$1 billion to commercial banks during the month to support stability in the foreign exchange market. The GoldBod programme is expected to generate about US$1.5 billion in total. Of this amount, US$1 billion will be sold to commercial banks, while the remaining US$500 million will be advanced to the Bank of Ghana to support the accumulation of foreign exchange reserves. Twice-Weekly FX Sales Under the new framework, GoldBod will conduct foreign exchange sales twice a week, on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Participating banks will submit their requests during a designated sales window. Where demand exceeds the available FX tranche, GoldBod said allocations will be made on a pro-rata basis to ensure a transparent and equitable distribution of the available foreign exchange. Transactions will be settled on the same day. The US dollar leg will be completed by 3:00pm, while the Ghana cedi leg will be completed by 4:00pm. Measures to Prevent Speculation GoldBod said participating banks will be required to declare that their requests are backed by actual unmet foreign exchange demand or evidence of a short position. The banks will also be required to comply with Bank of Ghana regulations and directives. The measures are intended to ensure that the facility responds to genuine market demand and is not used for speculative purposes. BoG to Provide Regulatory Oversight The programme will operate under the regulatory oversight of the Bank of Ghana. GoldBod said the central bank will have real-time access to the GoldBod GoFX platform. GoldBod will also submit transaction reports to the Bank of Ghana after each sale. The GoFX platform provides electronic submission and allocation processing, as well as time-stamping, transaction histories and audit trails. According to GoldBod, these features are designed to strengthen transparency, accountability and post-trade verification. The details were provided at a meeting between GoldBod and commercial banks ahead of the rollout of the new Spot FX Sales and Intermediation Framework. The framework is expected to provide authorised commercial banks with predictable and transparent access to US dollars through the GoldBod GoFX platform.

title: Why does affordable connectivity modernization matter for integrated resorts (IRs)?
body: Editor’s note: This press release is sponsored by Trends and Technologies and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece. Technology-enabled business services and solutions provider Trends & Technologies, Inc. (Trends), together with global connectivity technology leader ReadyLinks, recently hosted a joint event, “Modernizing Networks Without Rebuilding Infrastructure: Smarter Connectivity for High-Demand Environments,” held last September 10 at Solaire in Parañaque City. The forum introduced Trends and ReadyLinks’s Smart Integrated Resort Solution, an integrated methodology toward modernizing network capabilities for integrated resorts (IRs) and hospitality businesses with a strong emphasis on connectivity, visibility and management, and operational intelligence, and without the need for expensive overhauls. The Smart Integrated Resort Solution instead focuses on building around existing infrastructure investments, on long-term scalability and ease of deployment with minimal disruption for accommodating growing connectivity requirements. “The underlying outcome s we’re trying to achieve for IR organizations, in this modernization thrust [with Smart Integrated Resort], is stronger connectivity, more manageable operations, and of course, serviceability for future technologies, without the need overhauls that clients may not be ready for, currently,” said ReadyLinks CEO Larry Synstelien. Synstelien added that IR organizations often move toward having these key improvements: Better visibility across properties More consistent connectivity across environments, including gaming environments Simplified management and operations Support for future technologies and services And all the above modernization goals should be achieved with reduced disruption during transformation. According to Trends’ converged access infrastructure group head Mark Anthony Castillo, disruption is a key consideration in the Smart Integrated Resort approach. “Disruption and downtime are crucial consideration s in this approach, as an organization could lose up to $15,000 a minute – that is the average in 2026 for the Global 2000, but the loss is much greater for integrated resorts, especially during peak operational windows. With this threat in mind, our approach should be subtle and most cost-effective,” said Castillo. “We’re glad we’ve found a strong partner in Trends for the implementation of this approach, which we have developed for the unique needs of the sector, zeroing in on their networks. With our technology, experience in this sector, along with the breadth of expertise of Trends, we’re confident we could achieve these goals for our clients, while also achieving lower costs,” Synstelien said. The joint forum attests to Trends and ReadyLinks’ commitment to bringing stronger network capabilities to IR operators in the country. In an environment where connectivity is supporting more needs, modernization is crucial for improving hotel and guest services, surveillance and security, retail, dining and event spaces, and gaming and facility operations. – Rappler.com

title: Bawumia mourns former NPP chairman Odoi-Sykes
body: Former Vice President and New Patriotic Party (NPP) presidential candidate Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has paid tribute to former NPP National Chairman and Minority Leader Samuel Arthur Odoi-Sykes, who died on Monday, October 5, 2026. Dr Bawumia described the late politician as a founding member of the NPP whose contribution to the party extended to one of its defining moments in the Fourth Republic — its victory in the 2000 presidential and parliamentary elections. “I am deeply saddened by the passing of H.E. Samuel Odoi Sykes, a founding member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP: Development in Freedom) who served as National Chairman and Ghana’s High Commissioner to Canada,” Dr Bawumia wrote in a tribute. Mr Odoi-Sykes served as NPP National Chairman from 1998 to 2001, a period during which the party secured its first presidential victory in the Fourth Republic. He was also the Member of Parliament for Ashiedu Keteke and subsequently served as Minority Leader after winning the constituency in the 1979 elections. Beyond his political career, he held several public and diplomatic positions. He began his career as a teacher before joining the Ministry of Information and later entered Ghana’s Foreign Service in 1961, serving in India, the United States, the Soviet Union and the United Kingdom. His diplomatic career included positions as First Secretary, Press Attaché, Minister-Counsellor, Deputy Ambassador to the Soviet Union and Deputy High Commissioner to the United Kingdom. He was also a Barrister-at-Law, having been called to the Bar at the Inner Temple in the United Kingdom before being admitted to the Ghana Bar. Dr Bawumia said the former chairman had earned an honoured place in the history of the NPP and Ghana through his service to both the party and the country. “His service to Party and country will long be remembered,” he said. Born in Accra, Mr Odoi-Sykes attended Accra Academy, the University of Ghana, the University of London and Johns Hopkins University. His family remembered him as a man of principle, courage and firm leadership who devoted his life to public service and intellectual independence. He is survived by his wife, Edith Amorkor Sykes, and four children — Cynthia Omaboe, Mavis Amoa, Vincent Sykes and Frank Sykes. Dr Bawumia extended his condolences to the bereaved family and loved ones, concluding his tribute: “Farewell, Chairman. May your soul rest in perfect peace.” Funeral arrangements are expected to be announced by the family.

title: Sesame Solar, Target Arm and AG3 Labs Partner to Launch the First Made-in-USA Persistent Drone Operations Nanogrid
body:
Sesame Solar , Target Arm and AG3 Labs are launching the Persistent Drone Operations Nanogrid , the first integrated solution that combines Sesame Solar’s self-generating mobile power, Target Arm’s robotic arm and drone magazines for autonomous drone launch and recovery, and AG3 Labs’ attritable, unmanned aircraft into a single system for training and forward expeditionary use. This solution will enable continuous drone operations with no fuel resupply. Operators can remotely monitor the Nanogrid’s energy performance and control the robotic arm and drones.
A drone is only as good as its next charge. The U.S. Army has documented this gap, citing that there is no standard procedure to get backup power out to a drone launch team. In remote, contested or austere environments, an autonomous solution that can transport, charge and safely store in a wide range of temperatures, launch, recover and recharge drones with minimal signatures can save lives while improving mission outcomes.
“Mobile electric power is a critical fifth supply requirement along with food, water, munitions, and fuel. If a forward expeditionary team can’t power its drones, or their batteries fail from heat or cold, warfighters lose one of their most valuable assets,” said Lauren Flanagan, CEO and co-founder of Sesame Solar. “Together with Target Arm and AG3 Labs, we’ve built a comprehensive solution that eliminates the fuel supply chain while keeping drones in the air for extended durations.”
The Persistent Drone Operations Nanogrid removes bottlenecks by combining:
The launch comes as federal policy moves decisively toward domestic production. Executive Order 14307 directs agencies to expand U.S. UAS manufacturing and reduce reliance on foreign-made drones, and the Department of Defense has moved this year to arm units with small, U.S.-sourced drones at scale. As a domestically manufactured solution, the Persistent Drone Operations Nanogrid meets these requirements, while providing a comprehensive solution that improves operational readiness and supply chain security.
“Every system we build at Target Arm starts with the same question: does this bring someone home safe?” said Jeffrey A. McChesney, CEO & Founder of Target Arm. “The launch and the recovery are two of the most exposed moments of a drone mission -— someone standing in the open, waiting on an aircraft. Ralar takes a person out of that moment entirely. What makes our system even more unique is that drones can be launched from a moving vehicle or a boat, so warfighters never need to stop to complete their mission.”
Potential applications for the integrated solution include:
The Persistent Drone Operations Nanogrid is available as a standalone solution or in a series of two to twelve Nanogrids, creating a turnkey MIL-STD mobile microgrid, which can also charge man-portable batteries and forward expeditionary equipment.

title: Sierra Leonean President Bio, Elumelu rally West African private sector to turn regional potential into investment, jobs
body:
The President of Sierra Leone and immediate past Chair of the ECOWAS Authority of Heads of State and Government, Julius Maada Bio, and leading African investor and Chairman of Heirs Holdings, Tony Elumelu, have called on West Africa’s private sector to move decisively from the promise of regional integration to its delivery.
They both called for support to mobilise capital, build competitive industries, create jobs, and transform the region’s vast economic potential into shared prosperity.
Hosting President Bio in Lagos ahead of the inaugural West Africa Integration and Investment Summit (WAIIS), Mr Elumelu brought together leading private sector and financial institution leaders for the inaugural physical meeting of the WAIIS Private Sector Advisory Board.
The meeting focused on four strategic areas with the potential to reshape West Africa’s economic future: energy trade and industrialisation, strategic minerals, agribusiness, and digital transformation.
President Bio set out an ambitious vision for WAIIS to consolidate a regional market of more than 400 million people and mobilise businesses from within West Africa and across the world to deepen trade, investment and economic cooperation.
“We are partners in execution — let us transform ideas into partnerships, partnerships into investments, and investments into lasting prosperity for our continent,” Mr Bio told members of the Advisory Board.
He added: “But potential is not prosperity. Our task is to convert these advantages into productive enterprises, competitive industries, regional value chains, jobs and wealth.”
Mr Elumelu welcomed President Bio’s initiative to place private capital and enterprise at the heart of the regional agenda, reaffirming his commitment to mobilising African and international investment alongside leading African financial institutions, including the Africa Finance Corporation, Afreximbank, United Bank for Africa (UBA), Ecobank, etc., to support the execution of priority projects.
The approach reflects Mr Elumelu’s philosophy of Africapitalism—the belief that the African private sector has a defining role to play in catalysing the continent’s economic transformation through long-term investment in critical sectors.
Mr Elumelu stressed that Africa’s businesses must increasingly look beyond national borders and combine capital, expertise and capabilities to build enterprises and industries capable of competing at scale, while creating jobs and expanding opportunity across the sub-region.
“This is consistent with our aspirations to create jobs for our young people,” Mr Elumelu said. “We have all it takes to be prosperous.”
But private sector ambition, he noted, must be matched by decisive government action.
“Governments must provide the policy certainty, regulatory efficiency and security required to give investors the confidence to commit capital for the long term.”
Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu , underscored the importance of industrialisation and the free movement of goods and services in building a truly integrated West African market. He stressed that political leaders must provide the enabling environment, certainty and assurances required for businesses to invest, produce and trade across borders.
At the centre of the discussion was a shared conviction that West Africa has the scale, resources, talent and entrepreneurial capacity to become one of the world’s most dynamic economic regions.
With the Summit now less than two months away, Mr Bio called on members of the Advisory Board to move from advocacy to active mobilisation: engaging prospective investors directly, matching them with viable projects, and identifying the financing gaps, policy decisions and other interventions required to move transactions forward.
WAIIS will take place on 17–18 November 2026 at the Julius Maada Bio International Conference Centre in Lungi, Sierra Leone, bringing heads of state, investors and business leaders together to advance investment across energy, strategic minerals, agribusiness and digital transformation.
Notable names on the WAIIS Private Sector Advisory Board are Tony Elumelu — Chairman, Heirs Holdings; Aliko Dangote— Group President/Chief Executive, Dangote Group; Folorunso Alakija — Executive Vice Chairman, FA Limited; Samuel Dossou-Aworet — Founding Chairman, Petrolin Group; George Elombi — President & Chairman of the Board of Directors, Afreximbank; and Abdul Samad Rabiu, Chairman/CEO, BUA Group.
Others are Wale Tinubu — Group Chief Executive, Oando PLC; Samaila Zubairu — President & Chief Executive Officer, Africa Finance Corporation; Alain Ebobissé — Chief Executive Officer, Africa50; Jean-Claude Kassi Brou — Governor, Central Bank of West African States; Paulo Gomes — Founder and Chairman, Orango Investment Corporation; Benedict Okey Oramah — Chairman, Africa Trading Minerals (ATMIN); and Habib Yérim Sow — Group Chairman & CEO, Teyliom Group.

title: Perplexity AI Releases pplx-embed-v2-late: A 0.6B Edge Model and a 9B Model Scoring 92.4% on MADQA
body: Perplexity has released pplx-embed-v2-late , a pair of ColBERT-style multimodal embedding models. They come in 2 sizes: 0.6B for fast, cheap queries and 9B for maximum quality. Both models retrieve text, images and rendered PDF pages, and they share one embedding space. Is it deployable? Yes, if you host it yourself. Both models are on Hugging Face under the MIT license. A hosted Perplexity API endpoint is planned but not live. TL;DR The best The 0.6B model uses about 340M active parameters for images and stays close to 8B rivals. A 9B index can be searched with 0.6B queries, recovering about half the 9B quality gap on text at 0.6B query cost. Its 128-dim token vectors are 16x to 32x narrower than rivals at 2,048 to 4,096 dims. MIT license, with commercial use allowed. The worst It stores 1 vector per token, so index size grows with document length. It is not #1 on ViDoRe v3 image retrieval; Tencent’s EVIE scores higher. A single input cannot mix text and images. All scores are self-reported, and the technical report is not out yet. Model Size and What It Runs On Metrics pplx-embed-v2-late-0.6b pplx-embed-v2-late-9b Total parameters 594M 9B (Hugging Face lists 8B) Active parameters ~240M text, 340M image 7.4B Base model Qwen3.5-0.8B, pruned to 12 text layers Qwen3.5 Output 128 dims per token 128 dims per token Weights in memory (bf16, our estimate) ~1.2 GB ~16 to 18 GB Intended machine Laptop, edge device or small GPU Datacenter or high-memory GPU Perplexity’s suggested role Live query encoder, 100% local Building the document index Perplexity designed the 0.6B model as a lightweight query encoder that can also run on edge devices. Both model cards show CUDA GPU usage. They need sentence-transformers >= 6.0.0 and transformers >= 5.4.0 . The memory figures are our estimate at 2 bytes per parameter, for weights only. The published checkpoints are stored in F32, which doubles the download size. How Well It Performs: Best and Worst Scores All numbers below are from Perplexity’s announcement : Benchmark 0.6B 9B Where it stands MADQA (agentic PDF QA, accuracy) 90.1% 92.4% (best) Beats Mixedbread’s retriever (88.9%); trails Mixedbread Agentic Search (93.4%) Domain-specific text (72 tasks, nDCG@10) 78.0% 81.3% 9B leads all tested models by 1.6pp; 0.6B is 0.3pp behind gemini-embedding-2 Q2D-Web (Recall@1000) 73.6% 74.8% Both beat the previous best of 69.3% ViDoRe v3 image (nDCG@10) 62.3% 65.2% 0.6B is within 1.2pp of nemotron-colembed-v2-8b; EVIE leads ViDoRe v3 Markdown (nDCG@10) 61.2% (worst) 64.7% Both beat every external model tested BrowseComp+ (accuracy) Not given 64.0% (lowest) Still 4.9pp above the next ColBERT model The strongest result: 92.4% on MADQA, set by the 9B model. The biggest margin is on BrowseComp+, at 8.7pp over the best dense model. The weakest result: 61.2% on ViDoRe v3 Markdown, from the 0.6B model. It is still the 2nd-best score on that benchmark. Image search is the real gap: Gemini Embedding 2 beats the 9B model on MIRACL-Vision and by 2pp on PPLX-Q2I. Mixing sizes: a 9B index queried by the 0.6B model scored 63.5% on ViDoRe v3 image retrieval. That beats 62.3% with 0.6B on both sides, at the same query cost. How It Works Dense models compress a document into 1 vector. pplx-embed-v2-late instead keeps a 128-dim vector for every token. It scores with MaxSim: each query token finds its best document token, and those maxima are summed. Pages are encoded as images, so no OCR step is needed. Perplexity distilled both models from an 18B teacher using LEAF -style token-level training. That training is what creates the shared space. Best Use Cases The best fit is visual document search over PDFs, slides and scanned reports. Low-latency search: index in the cloud with 9B, then query on-device with 0.6B. Agentic RAG over large PDF or web collections. Interactive Explainer window.addEventListener('message',function(e){if(e.data&&e.data.pplxLateH){var f=document.getElementById('pplx-late-frame');if(f){f.style.height=e.data.pplxLateH+'px';}}}); How It Compares Feature pplx-embed-v2-late NVIDIA nemotron-colembed-vl-8b-v2 TopK topk-embed-v1 Google Gemini Embedding 2 Size 0.6B, 9B ~8.8B 0.8B, 2B open Not disclosed Vector width 128 per token 4,096 per token 2,048 per token ( small ) 128 to 3,072, 1 vector Inputs Text, images, page renders Text queries, page images Text, page images Text, image, video, audio, PDF Runs on Your GPU; 0.6B on edge NVIDIA A100/H100, Linux CUDA GPU (Ampere+) Google API Shared space across sizes Yes Not stated Not stated Not applicable License MIT CC-BY-NC-4.0 Apache 2.0 (small) Proprietary Key Takeaways The 0.6B model fits edge devices; the 9B model is built for index-time quality. Best score: 92.4% on MADQA. Weakest: 61.2% on ViDoRe v3 Markdown. 0.6B queries over a 9B index beat 0.6B on both sides. Storage growth and self-reported scores are the main caveats. Check out the Model weights on HF and Technical details . All credit goes to the researcher of this project. Also, feel free to follow us on Twitter and don’t forget to join our 150k+ML SubReddit and Subscribe to our Newsletter . Wait! are you on telegram? now you can join us on telegram as well. title: Land Forces 2026: Thales displays next-gen Bushmaster and logistics UGV
body:
On 6 October 2026, Thales Australia unveiled an extra-large unmanned ground vehicle (UGV), as well as a Bushmaster dual-cab variant optimised for the counter-drone role, at the Land Forces exhibition in Perth, Western Australia.
The heavy-duty UGV, christened the BladeHaul, is designed for contested logistics, and it is large enough to carry a 20-foot container or an alternative payload weighing 10 tonnes.
The BladeHaul is based on the chassis and driveline of Thales Australia’s well-known Bushmaster 4×4 protected mobility vehicle. However, its mechanicals have been completely revamped by 3ME Technology, which installed a hybrid engine and battery storage solution.
3ME previously developed a hybrid-engined Bushmaster, but this time it has gone much further and created a 660V power system offering 110kWh of power. This propulsion choice means the BladeHaul could act as a standalone generator or be a power source for a field hospital or command post, for instance. It offers 1MW of power, enough to simultaneously power 1,000 homes!
Serving as an external power source is one envisaged use of the BladeHaul, alongside contested logistics, or a mobile platform for sensors and effectors. Indeed, potential roles mentioned by Thales Australia are launching coastal anti-ship missiles, carrying a counter-drone system, air surveillance radar, reloading munitions or detecting/clearing mines.
The BladeHaul is not yet ready for action, however, as its autonomy package still needs to be developed and integrated. This will be done by Deakin University, with Thales Australia signing a memorandum of understanding (MoU) at Land Forces 2026. The vehicle will be capable of remote, fully autonomous or follow-me operations.
According to Thales Australia, this UGV “is engineered to outperform all existing and planned counterparts in payload capacity and operational flexibility”. Certainly, there is a market gap for such a large UGV with a significant payload capacity. The BladeHaul is aimed at the Australian Army as well as export markets.
Turning to Thales Australia’s other vehicle showcased at Land Forces 2026, this was a dual-cab variant of the Bushmaster fitted with a RapidStriker counter-unmanned aerial system (C-UAS) suite.
Thales has modernised the successful Bushmaster into this 5.6.2 version featuring a four-door cab and a rear cargo deck. It represents the manufacturer’s efforts to keep the Bushmaster relevant to modern warfare, specifically as a sensor and effector platform rather than a mere troop transporter.
The RapidStriker C-UAS suite, debuting at Eurosatory 2026, features an EOS R400 remote weapon station armed with Thales 70mm laser-guided and unguided rockets, a Robin 3D Iris radar and a Thales electro-optical/infrared sensor.
On 7 October 2026, Thales Australia also signed an MoU with German firm Stark to integrate the latter’s new 100km-range Cascade loitering munition. It has a 4.5kg warhead, and it joins other loitering munitions from Stark that have seen combat in Ukraine.
The two partners will develop a multi-cell launcher that can go on the Bushmaster. Initially, this will have six canisters, but the intent is to add more launcher cells.
The complete Bushmaster as exhibited is capable of defending against drones and also despatching its own precision strike munitions. It is clearly intended to meet Australian Army requirements. The dual cab also has a C-rail system that allows seats to be moved and the compartment reconfigured for different missions.
Of interest, Australia’s order of 268 new vehicles announced in April this year might comprise the Bushmaster 5.6.2, but this has not yet been confirmed.

title: Oguaa Omanhene endorses GMTF, says ‘there is hope for the future’
body: The Omanhene of the Oguaa Traditional Area, Osbarima Kwasi Atta II, has thrown his weight behind the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF), describing its interventions as a powerful source of hope for the future of healthcare delivery in Ghana. The Omanhene said the establishment of the Fund and the work it was undertaking to expand access to specialised healthcare represented some of the most encouraging developments he had heard about in a long time. “There is hope for the future,” Osbarima Kwasi Atta II declared when the Administrator of the GMTF, Adjoa Obuobia Darko-Opoku, paid a courtesy call on him in Cape Coast. The meeting formed part of the second day of the Fund’s sensitisation tour of the Central Region, which is aimed at taking the GMTF’s mandate, interventions and message to communities and key stakeholders across the country. ‘I will help spread the message’ The Oguaa Omanhene pledged the support of traditional authorities in promoting awareness of the GMTF and ensuring that information about its interventions reached people who needed help. He said traditional leaders had a critical role to play in connecting communities to initiatives capable of improving their lives, particularly vulnerable families who might not know where to turn when confronted with serious medical conditions. “I will help spread the message,” Osbarima Kwasi Atta II assured the Administrator, adding that he was ready to support efforts to ensure that more people became aware of the Fund and its interventions. He also urged the management of the GMTF not to be distracted by criticism or opposition, but to remain focused on its mandate and the lives it had been established to improve. He said initiatives designed to bring relief to Ghanaians facing difficult circumstances deserved support and encouragement. Praise for President Mahama The Omanhene expressed appreciation to President John Dramani Mahama for the vision behind the establishment of the GMTF, saying the initiative had the potential to make a significant difference in the lives of families struggling with serious illnesses and the financial burden of specialised treatment. He said the Fund offered renewed hope to people who might otherwise be overwhelmed by the cost of accessing critical healthcare. The endorsement by the Oguaa Omanhene adds the voice of traditional leadership to the GMTF’s growing stakeholder support as the Fund intensifies its nationwide sensitisation campaign. The campaign seeks to deepen public understanding of the Fund’s mandate and interventions while ensuring that Ghanaians, particularly those living with chronic and serious diseases, know where and how to seek support. The courtesy call on the Oguaa Omanhene was one of several stakeholder engagements undertaken by the GMTF Administrator and her team during the Central Regional leg of the tour.

title: DR Congo Ineligible Player: NFF sent petition to wrong email – FIFA
body: One of the technical grounds on which FIFA dismissed Nigeria’s protest against DR Congo for fielding an ineligible player in the world cup qualifiers was that the mail which they used in sending the petition wasn’t the right one. DR Congo pipped Nigeria to book a place in the intercontinental playoff with a 4-3 win on penalties after both teams stayed locked at 1-1 after extra time. According to the New York Times, FIFA discovered that Nigeria’s petition against Lionel Mpasi who was in goal in the playoff final didn’t fulfill the requirements of his nationality switch from France to Congo, before taking part in the game. However they dismissed the appeal by Nigeria on what they term as technical grounds following the late filing of the case by Nigeria. A bogus claim which has now put them under intense scrutiny from the world at large. According to a highly placed source at the National Sports Commission (NSC), FIFA cited the fact that the petition was sent to the General Secretary (GS) rather than the legal portal as part of the technical ground on which it was dismissed. A laughable claim because all petitions and correspondence are first and foremost routed to the GS, who most times reply nations and give directions on where complaints should be forwarded to. Another ground was that it was filed late. A lame excuse because doing the right thing after an infraction of such magnitude shouldn’t be time barred. The post DR Congo Ineligible Player: NFF sent petition to wrong email – FIFA appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Dryad Wins International XPRIZE Wildfire Award for Autonomous Wildfire Detection and Suppression
body:
Dryad Networks, a leader in ultra-early wildfire detection, today announced it has been awarded $800,000 in the XPRIZE Wildfire competition for its performance in the Autonomous Wildfire Response finals in Alaska.
Dryad advanced from an original field of approximately 300 entrants in the four-year competition. In June 2026, three finalists were challenged to autonomously detect and completely suppress a high-risk wildfire within 10 minutes of ignition across 1,000 km² of Alaskan wilderness, leaving any decoy fires untouched. It was the most demanding live test to date of what it will take to stop a destructive fire before it grows out of control.
During the tests, the Dryad’s Silvanet sensor network successfully detected and verified target fire in 12 minutes or less and autonomously launched a response, ignoring any decoy fires. The autonomous Silvaguard Observation Drone provided situational awareness and the Suppression Drone accurately hit the fire with suppressant – providing a strong proof of concept for the competition end goal.
The XPRIZE Wildfire Judging Panel awarded $2.5 million across three Track B Finalist teams, recognizing distinct breakthroughs across the autonomous wildfire response cycle. Together, this demonstrates meaningful advances toward the competition’s ambitious goal and provided a clearer picture of what is possible today — and where further innovation is still needed.
With the award, XPRIZE recognized in particular Dryad’s 170-sensor persistent Silvanet field network combined with Silvaguard drones for demonstrating end-to-end autonomy.
“This award is a tremendous external validation of our technology and vision,” said Carsten Brinkschulte, CEO and Co-Founder of Dryad Networks. “Our vision is fully aligned with XPRIZE Wildfire: detect and extinguish fires within 10 minutes of ignition. To achieve this, fires must be detected within minutes, ideally during the smoldering phase before open flames appear and spread rapidly.”
“Ultra-early detection is a prerequisite for autonomous suppression. Drones can suppress a small ignition, but their limited payload makes them largely ineffective once a wildfire has grown out of control. Silvanet detects the fire when it is still tiny, and Silvaguard can verify, locate and suppress it autonomously.”
Silvanet uses solar-powered, AI-enabled gas sensors as an “electronic nose” to detect wildfire signatures within minutes of ignition. Its solar-powered mesh network enables sensors to communicate deep inside forests, off-grid and independently of mobile networks. The fully industrialized system has more than 40,000 sensors manufactured, including recent deliveries of 10,000 sensors to France and more than 7,000 to Italy.
Silvaguard extends Silvanet from detection to autonomous response. When a sensor triggers an alert, a Silvaguard Observation Drone autonomously launches, verifies and precisely geolocates the fire using infrared and optical cameras. A Suppression Drone then deploys up to 100 liters of suppressant on the fire. Both operate autonomously with no human operator in the loop and are designed to be stationed in forests in solar-powered protective hangars, continuously charged and ready to respond.
Dryad will now invest significantly in productizing Silvaguard, with real-world operational pilots planned for 2027 and commercial availability targeted for 2028 .
“Wildfires are a race against time,” Brinkschulte concluded. “Instead of building bigger machines to fight bigger fires, our goal is to prevent fires from becoming big in the first place. XPRIZE has provided powerful validation that autonomous wildfire response can make that vision a reality.”
For XPRIZE, the end of the competition is not the end of the work. XPRIZE Wildfire will move into an Impact Phase focused on helping translate promising technologies into durable, deployable solutions for real-world wildfire management.
XPRIZE is the recognized global leader in designing and executing large-scale competitions to solve humanity’s greatest challenges. For over 30 years, our unique model has democratized crowd-sourced innovation and scientifically scalable solutions that accelerate a more equitable and abundant future. Donate, learn more, and co-architect a world of abundance with us at xprize.org.
More info: https://www.xprize.org/wildfire
Dryad Networks mission is to detect wildfires in their earliest stages and enable autonomous suppression before they become catastrophic. Dryad’s solutions protect forests, communities, critical infrastructure, and the climate from the growing threat of wildfires.

title: Bandits kill 3 in Kebbi community
body: An attack by bandits on Kasabo, a community in Saminaka, Yauri Local Government Area of Kebbi State, has left three people dead. The community was reportedly attacked in the early hours of Monday this week. A local, Aminu Salisu, who spoke to our correspondent, said the attackers came in large numbers but luckily, many residents were able to escape through the bush. “However, they succeeded in killing three people before they retreated to their hideout,” he said. During a condolence visit to the community on Tuesday, Governor Nasir Idris described the incident as a tragic and unacceptable act of violence against innocent citizens. While donating the sum of N116m to the families of the victims and the people of the community, he assured that his administration would continue to strengthen collaboration with security agencies and take all necessary measures to protect the lives and property of the people. Responding, Dan Masani of Saminaka, Alhaji Mohammed Bashir, said that the killing was a great loss to the community.

title: S’Court judgement: Erring parties will not field candidates – INEC
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has said political parties found to be fielding candidates whose names were not on the registers it submitted to the commission will not be allowed to participate in the 2027 elections. The Supreme Court, in its September 24, 2026 judgement, affirmed the constitutionality of Sections 77(5), 77(6) and 77(7) of the Electoral Act 2026 and upheld INEC’s revised timetable and schedule of activities for the 2027 elections. INEC National Commissioner in charge of information and voter education, Malam Mohammed Haruna, made the point clear while speaking on Trust TV programme, Daily Politics on Wednesday evening. He said parties will not be allowed to substitute such candidates because defaulters will not be allowed to benefit from an offence they committed. He said the commission should be able to make a definite pronouncement on the Supreme Court jugdmemt by Tuesday next week. “It’s like you committed an offence. And then, you come and benefit from it. You remember cases that we had of some in Zamfara, you remember Plateau? The same thing. The parties, because they did the wrong thing, they thought they could now steal through the candidates. “And the law was very clear. Once you do that kind of thing, you cannot benefit from it. You are benefiting from it, if you are able to substitute a candidate.” He said by implication depending on when INEC finally concludes, “some parties may not be able to finish with even governorship candidates. “All the candidates, all the way to the houses of assembly, we interviewed them. If their names are not on the party register, they were not members of the party at the time that they contested for those tickets.” Haruna acknowledged that a lot of people are anxious to know what will happen but that the delay is because INEC has to get advise of its legal expert after getting the Certified True Copy of the judgement. “You can’t be too careful with these things because even when you see copies and they tell you it’s a CTC, it may be forged. We’ve seen instances where people have even gone, have the audacity to forge a Supreme Court judgment. So, we have to be very careful to make sure that when you took us, we did put a lot of pressure and we were able to get it yesterday (Tuesday). The INEC commissioner said the commission is equally worried by the manner of campaigns where threats are deployed by various players but added that; “Those kind of things, even if it’s a minority, it’s a cause for concern, because nobody should be threatened at all. All those talks, they are not reassuring at all. There are things, there are talks, actions, that really is a cause for worry, not just for us, but it should be a cause of worry for everybody, including the ruling party.” He said the commission is doing everything to secure the funds needed to conduct the elections as it doesn’t have the luxury of time any more.

title: Opportunities in agriculture are enormous – Young entrepreneur tells fellow youth
body: When Bernice Agboada completed school, she was unsure what would come next. Like many young people, she had finished her education with hopes for the future but without a clear path to pursue. Yet, the agriculture and food systems sector offered a potential avenue. It’s a sector that research increasingly identifies as a significant source of jobs and livelihoods for Africa’s growing youth population. World Bank analysis suggests that money invested in agribusiness generates more jobs than an equivalent amount spent in manufacturing or services. Agriculture, it argues, is a sleeping giant for inclusive growth. Bernice was introduced to agriculture as a potential source of job creation by colleagues and decided to explore that opportunity. Today, her experience in agriculture has paid off, giving her practical skills, employment, a growing business and a renewed sense of what is possible. Under the brand name Mushroom General, she grows, packages, and sells mushrooms, creating jobs for herself and other young people. “I got introduced to the Youth Entrepreneurship for the Future of Food and Agriculture (YEFFA) programme through the Ghana Federation of Disability. Then, I had completed school and wasn’t sure what to do next. So, I tried, and it turns out that I have a job and good skills now,” Bernice told Adom TV’s Afia Amankwaah Tamakloe on the Badwam TV show. Before joining the programme, Bernice had little knowledge of mushroom production. Through training and mentorship over the past three years, however, she developed the technical and entrepreneurial skills needed to establish and grow her business, Mushroom General. “YEFFA, Mastercard and AGRA trained me. I am a proud alumna,” she said, adding that the training also equipped her with skills in packaging and presentation that have helped her improve her products. Today, Bernice is not only producing mushrooms but also creating employment opportunities for other young people. Her business currently employs three youth, and she is looking to expand. Bernice believes agriculture offers opportunities because food is an essential part of everyone’s life. “Everybody is eating. No one can go a day without eating. So, this is a venture that is very good, and I encourage a lot of people to take part, especially persons with disabilities.” Her own experience, as a person living with albinism, has strengthened her belief that living with disability should not prevent anyone from becoming an entrepreneur. “PWDs can do something with the right support,” she said. Mushroom General, which is dedicated to sustainable practices and innovative mushroom products, reflects that vision. The business seeks to promote healthy living, support local communities and contribute to a more sustainable future through mushroom production. For Bernice, however, the biggest transformation has been the realisation that her business can become much larger than she ever imagined. The young woman who finished school without knowing what to do next now sees possibilities in production, processing, financing, export and regional markets. “I feel like the small mushroom business is not small. It has big potential,” she said. That growing sense of possibility has also shaped her ambitions for Mushroom General. Bernice wants to move beyond cultivating and selling fresh mushrooms into value-added processing. She envisions producing mushroom-based snacks, mushroom powder for health-conscious consumers and other packaged products that could eventually reach markets beyond Ghana. Her experience has also convinced her that Africa needs more opportunities for entrepreneurs to develop and process agricultural products. She believes “opportunities in agriculture are enormous for young people.” Sach Avudzi, Programs and Safeguarding Officer at AGRA Ghana, reiterated the need to support young people in pursuing business ventures in food systems. “Some people have the impression youth aren’t interested in agribusiness. But when you put out programs, you will be amazed by the number of youth who come. They just need support,” he explained. He said the YEFFA program is exposing young people to a range of opportunities so they can take advantage of them. “We expose them to technologies. We take them on factory tours. We go for international exhibitions and programs… In Ghana, currently, AGRA has worked with not less than 300 youth enterprises,” he added. The YEFFA program is a $350 million initiative running from 2023 to 2028. Implemented by the Mastercard Foundation and AGRA across multiple African countries, the program aims to create 1.5 million work opportunities for young people within agri-food systems by strengthening ecosystems and mobilising support from both the public and private sectors. YEFFA operates through continental and country-specific pillars to address systemic barriers and foster national value chains, ultimately accelerating youth employment and agricultural transformation.

title: Can Edo gov deliver 2.5m votes for Tinubu?
body: Governor Monday Okpebholo’s pledge to deliver 2.5 million votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Edo State in the 2027 presidential election has set an ambitious projection for the All Progressives Congress (APC), but the state’s voter statistics suggest it is a tall order. Okpebholo has repeatedly vowed that Edo would deliver 2.5 million votes for Tinubu, arguing that the “one man, one vote” principle and the impact of the Federal Government’s economic reforms would help the APC achieve the target. He restated the position in Benin City recently, during a one-million-youth march organised by the City Boy Movement in support of his administration and Tinubu’s re-election. “We are paying so much on salaries and at the same time, development is ongoing, projects are ongoing. Look at our flyover, if not for the reforms of the president, where will we get money for all this?” Okpebholo said. The governor also cited his administration’s projects in healthcare and education as evidence of the benefits of the reforms. He said the state had built more than 108 primary healthcare centres, renovated over 87 primary and secondary schools and increased subvention to higher institutions from N41 million to more than N700 million. “How could we have gotten this money, if not [for] the man (President Bola Tinubu) that is courageous enough to have removed the fuel subsidy,” he said. Edo’s voting strength Edo had 2,501,081 registered voters on the final register used for the 2023 general elections. The latest figures provided by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for the 2027 elections put the state’s registered voters at 2,865,263, representing an increase of 364,182 voters, or about 14.6 per cent in four years. The new register means Edo now has 2.865 million registered voters, making it the 14th-largest electorate among Nigeria’s 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. However, Okpebholo’s 2.5 million target would account for about 87.3 per cent of the entire 2027 registered electorate in the state. Put differently, for Tinubu to receive 2.5 million votes, nearly 87 out of every 100 registered voters in Edo would have to vote for him. That is where the difference between voter registration and actual voting becomes important. The 2023 presidential election provides the most recent voting benchmark. In Edo, Peter Obi who was the presidential candidate for the Labour Party, secured 331,163 votes to win the state in 2023, while Tinubu of the APC received 144,471 votes. Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party polled 89,585 votes, while former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party received 2,743 votes. Tinubu’s 144,471 votes represented about 5.8 per cent of the 2,501,081 people registered to vote in Edo at the time. His tally was also less than half of Obi’s 331,163 votes. The APC would therefore need to move from 144,471 presidential votes in Edo in 2023 to 2.5 million in 2027 to meet Okpebholo’s target. That would mean an additional 2,355,529 votes, or roughly 17 times the number of votes Tinubu secured in the state in 2023. The picture becomes clearer when voter turnout is considered. Nationally, about 24.9 million votes were cast from a final register of 93.47 million voters in the 2023 presidential election, representing a turnout of roughly 26.7 per cent. While Edo’s turnout cannot simply be assumed to mirror the national figure, the national experience demonstrates why the number of registered voters should not be treated as the number of people who will necessarily vote. If only half of Edo’s 2,865,263 registered voters turned out in 2027, for example, the total number of voters would be about 1.43 million, far below the governor’s 2.5 million target. Even at 70 per cent turnout, the state would produce only about 2 million voters. For 2.5 million people to actually vote for Tinubu, turnout would have to be extraordinarily high, with the overwhelming majority of those who participate voting for the APC candidate. ‘It was political rhetoric ’ Professor Atah Pine, a political scientist in the Department of Political Science, Benue State University, Makurdi, said the governor’s statement should be understood primarily as political rhetoric rather than a scientific projection of the number of votes that will be cast. Pine said Okpebholo was likely using the figure to communicate his intention to deliver Edo to Tinubu by a wide margin. “I think the idea was to say that he is going to deliver the state with high margins. I want to believe that is the intentionality of that statement, that he is going to deliver Edo with landslides,” Pine said. “Because to sit and say he is going to give the president over 2 million is a little bit politically hyperbolic.” According to him, several factors that influence voter participation cannot be determined ahead of the election. “Because issues of voter aparthy may even come in. These are some of the issues. Voter aparthy may come in and then the citizens may have a distrust in the system and are unwilling to go and vote. “Or generally other anti-electoral issues may come up that may even inhibit people from coming out to vote,” he said. Prof Pine said developments between now and the election could also alter voter behaviour. “So from now to that time for the election, whether the next 60 days or 90 days, you cannot concretely establish the factors,” he said. He described Okpebholo’s statement as a mere political speech intended to project confidence in the APC’s electoral prospects. “What Okpebholo said was a political speech. The underlying idea behind what he said was that he was going to deliver Edo State to the president with a landslide victory,” he said. The political scientist also cautioned against assigning a fixed percentage to the number of votes the governor can deliver, arguing that voters ultimately make individual choices. “Now it is wrong to put a percentage on the vote because he is not going to commandeer the voters to vote for the president,” he said. “It’s a political behavior and people’s behavior will be influenced. Voting is a political behavior.” He added that the factors influencing voters would remain outside the governor’s control. “And so it’s going to be influenced by a number of factors which are outside his control,” he said.

title: Double nomination: Court dismisses suit against Kwara APC gov’ship candidate
body: A Federal High Court has dismissed a suit seeking to invalidate the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidacy of Yakubu Danladi Salihu in Kwara State. It ruled that the claimant lacked the legal standing to challenge his nomination. The court also dismissed the case on its merits, rejecting the allegation that Danladi’s participation in the party’s House of Assembly and governorship primaries amounted to double nomination. Justice Emeka Nwite, who presided over Court 9 of the Federal High Court in Abuja, further awarded N10 million costs against the claimant, Citizens Awareness Against Corruption and Social Vices Initiative. The suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1112/2026, was filed against the APC, Danladi and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). The claimant had alleged that Danladi was unlawfully involved in both the APC’s House of Assembly and governorship primaries and consequently asked the court to nullify his participation, screening, nomination and sponsorship. It also sought an order setting aside his emergence as the APC governorship candidate and directing INEC to reject his nomination. But the defendants challenged the competence of the suit, arguing that the claimant lacked locus standi and that the court lacked jurisdiction to entertain the action. Justice Nwite held that locus standi was fundamental to the competence of an action, while jurisdiction remained the threshold issue that must be established before a court could validly determine the substantive claims. Relying on Section 285(14) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the judge said the law restricts who can institute pre-election actions to specified categories of aspirants and political parties. He said Section 88(2) of the Electoral Act 2026 similarly limits complaints over non-compliance in the selection or nomination of candidates to aspirants who participated in the relevant primaries. Justice Nwite consequently held that the claimant, being a civil society organisation rather than an aspirant who participated in the primaries or a political party, had no locus standi to bring the action. The court said it examined the central allegation that Danladi had been doubly nominated and found that the claimant’s interpretation of the law was flawed. The court noted that a person who participates in different categories of primaries conducted by the same party, but whose name is ultimately submitted to INEC for only one position, cannot be regarded as having been doubly nominated explaining that a person becomes a candidate for the purpose of the relevant statutory provisions when the political party submits the person’s name to INEC. Justice Nwite therefore rejected the argument that Danladi’s participation in the APC’s House of Assembly and governorship primaries automatically invalidated his governorship candidacy. The court held that double nomination, as contemplated by the Electoral Act 2026, was not established merely by taking part in two primary elections conducted by the same political party. It further found that the allegations made by the claimant were not supported by sufficient evidence. The case was one of the legal challenges that followed the APC’s governorship primary, which produced Danladi as the party’s candidate after the contest. A Special Adviser to the Kwara State Governor on Legal Matters, Sambo Muritala, observed the proceedings. Justice Nwite resolved the issues in favour of the APC, Danladi and INEC and consequently dismissed the suit. He also ordered the claimant to pay N10 million in costs to the defendants.

title: Iran sets terms for ending war, Hormuz deal with Oman
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 08 (MNA) – Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman announced Iran's conditions for ending the war and a deal with Oman on the security of the Strait of Hormuz, saying Iran's terms have been clearly and firmly explained.
Esmail Baghaei, speaking about the latest developments in Iran-US negotiations, said, "The considerations and conditions of the Islamic Republic of Iran for ending the imposed war on all fronts and restoring security to the Persian Gulf region and the Strait of Hormuz have been clearly and firmly explained, and the necessary response to the other side's proposals will be provided through the mediators."
"The process of consultations between Iran and Oman has been carried out well, and the two sides, while agreeing on the geographical coordinates of safe inbound and outbound routes in the Strait of Hormuz, have also reached an understanding on how to reflect the matter at the relevant international body, which, God willing, will be done soon," he added.

title: Vietnam police arrest 12 over theft of 2,700 cats for slaughter
body: HANOI, Vietnam – Police in Vietnam have arrested 12 people accused of stealing 2,700 cats and selling them for slaughter in Ho Chi Minh City, the Ministry of Public Security said this week. The suspects, aged between 16 and 39, were arrested on suspicion of stealing the cats with the intention of selling them for food. The men were found with cat traps, cages and fur-removal equipment, according to a ministry statement. Police rescued dozens of cats during the raid. Cat meat dishes are still served in some parts of Vietnam, particularly in rural areas, where they are sometimes marketed as “mini tiger” and believed by some consumers to have medicinal properties The arrests followed complaints from residents about the nighttime disappearance of their pet cats, the statement said. Authorities identified Luu Thanh Binh, 39, as the alleged ringleader and distributor. Investigators said he also bought live cats and resold them to customers seeking cat meat. To supply the operation, Binh allegedly worked with several accomplices who recruited younger people to capture cats in residential neighborhoods. Police said he also supplied traps used in the thefts. The group operated mainly between 11 pm and 4 am, using fish bait and traps placed outside homes with pet cats. Captured animals were quickly collected and transported for sale, police said. Police have returned 13 of the cats to their owners and said the remaining animals were being cared for by animal welfare group HavePaws while authorities continued efforts to identify their owners. – Rappler.com

title: ADC will resist rigging in 2027 – Mark
body: National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Senator David Mark, has declared that the party will not allow itself to be rigged out in the coming elections.
