title: Ukraine Opens Gas Exports for Private Producers for First Time Since 2022
body:
Ukraine’s government on Oct. 7 approved the partial opening of natural gas exports, lifting a ban that had been in force since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022, according to ExPro, citing its own sources.
Private producers will be allowed to sell up to 15% of the gas they extracted in the previous month to foreign buyers. The mechanism excludes the state-controlled majors.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Discussions on whether to open exports intensified in the summer, and the government returned to the issue in September after initially postponing it until spring 2027, ExPro reported. Market participants tied the need to restart exports to a gas surplus in the commercial segment, a wide gap between Ukrainian and European prices, and producers’ need for funds to restore and protect their facilities.
A plan of priority actions for 2026, adopted by Cabinet order No. 999-r on Sept. 30 and published on the government portal , instructs the Ministry of Energy to create the legal and organizational conditions for a controlled export mechanism covering 15% of domestically produced gas.
The plan argues this would help the gas production sector by drawing in investment, and it set September 2026 as the target for opening exports. The order replaces an earlier version of the plan, adopted on March 30 under order No. 306.
Gas consumption by industrial users fell by almost half after the full-scale war in Ukraine began, ExPro reported, while output by private companies, the main gas suppliers to industry, has held relatively steady despite Russian attacks. According to ExPro, private companies produced more than 370 million cubic meters of natural gas in August 2026.
European prices jumped after the war in the Middle East began, while Ukrainian prices remained stable. By mid-September, gas in Ukraine was 2.5 times cheaper than in Europe.
Ukraine’s underground storage facilities have been holding more than 15.8 billion cubic meters of gas, according to ExPro’s calculations based on data from Gas Infrastructure Europe (GIE). That is 1.2 billion cubic meters more than the government’s plan required by Nov. 1.
The resolution takes effect on the day of its publication, and the mechanism will apply each year from March 1 to Nov. 30.
It does not cover gas produced under production sharing agreements, which are governed by separate legislation. It also does not apply to market participants with special obligations under Cabinet Resolution No. 222: Ukrgasvydobuvannia, Ukrnafta and Chornomornaftogaz.
The Ministry of Energy will approve a list of eligible companies and the volume each may sell by the 12th day of every month, based on data from the Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine (GTSOU) on actual gas supplied to the system the previous month.
Gas will be sold at specialized sessions of a commodity exchange, likely the Ukrainian Energy Exchange, according to ExPro. Only companies on the ministry’s list can sell, and only non-resident companies can buy. The highest bidder wins. Sellers must state the volume, a starting price in euros per megawatt-hour and a delivery point, defined as an exit point on Ukraine’s border with EU countries or Moldova.
A producer’s unused monthly limit will not carry over. Gas already sold on the exchange can be exported in the month of the auction or during the following two months. GTSOU will report each seller’s actual export volumes to the ministry by the 15th of every month.
In a crisis, exports can be suspended temporarily by a decision of the Crisis Committee under the Ministry of Energy, taken on the ministry’s initiative or at the request of Naftogaz or GTSOU. The ministry must then approve the decision.
Unless it says otherwise, the decision takes effect on the day it is adopted and halts specialized exchange trading. Gas sold for export before that date can still be shipped, provided the established procedure is followed.
Olena Hrazhdan is the Business Reporter at Kyiv Post, covering Ukraine’s markets, business, and economic policy. While she reports broadly on economic issues, her core focus is banking, finance, monetary and fiscal policy. Olena previously wrote for leading Ukrainian business media and became a Fellow of the International Monetary Fund’s Journalism Fellowship in 2024.

title: 450 suspected yellow fever cases recorded across Ghana since June – Health Minister
body: Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh says health authorities have recorded about 450 suspected yellow fever cases across Ghana between June and September 2026, with the Upper West Region accounting for 74 of them. Of the 74 cases recorded in the Upper West Region, three have so far been confirmed as yellow fever, Mr Akandoh said, stressing that suspected cases must undergo laboratory confirmation before deaths or illnesses can conclusively be attributed to the disease. “As of yesterday, the suspected cases were around 450 from June to September. Of those, 74 were from the Upper West, and 3 were confirmed from the Upper West. You see, sometimes the health professionals have a way of determining whether or not a death is attributable to a particular disease, but not until it’s confirmed,” he said. Speaking at the Ministry of Health’s Health Sector Update Engagement in Accra, the Minister said government had stepped up surveillance and response efforts, particularly in northern Ghana, with laboratories supplied with the necessary reagents to facilitate the testing and confirmation of suspected cases. He said a National Rapid Response Team had been deployed to the Upper West Region following the confirmation of cases, while designated areas at district hospitals had been isolated to support the management of suspected and confirmed patients. Mr Akandoh appealed to the public and media organisations to remain calm and support the health authorities’ response, assuring that measures had been put in place to contain the situation. “We don’t have to press the panic buttons. So the media, please, let’s handle it well; there are a lot of things that have been deployed,” he said.

title: Mahama Ayariga backs long-term capital mobilisation to address Ghana’s housing financing gap
body: Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has called for stronger and more sustainable financing mechanisms to support Ghana’s housing needs, highlighting the importance of mobilising long-term capital for the sector. Mr Ayariga said the country’s housing challenge requires more than increasing the supply of buildings, arguing that the availability and affordability of financing must form part of efforts to expand access to adequate housing. He made the observation in a Facebook post on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, following his participation in the National Conference on Housing Finance 2026. The conference brought stakeholders together to consider practical approaches to improving housing finance in Ghana. The Minister said participants examined issues including long-term capital mobilisation, affordable mortgage financing and sustainable housing solutions. He indicated that the conversations would continue as stakeholders work towards financing models capable of supporting a more inclusive housing sector. Mr Ayariga said sustained engagement among government, financial institutions and other stakeholders would be necessary to develop practical solutions that can make adequate housing more accessible to Ghanaians.

title: Some GBA members have gone quiet over dissatisfaction — Dafeamekpor
body: Some members of the Ghana Bar Association (GBA) have withdrawn from active participation in the association’s programmes and decision-making processes amid concerns about its perceived political posture, Majority Chief Whip Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor has said. According to him, the apparent disengagement should not necessarily be interpreted as a lack of interest in the association, but rather as a form of protest by lawyers who are unhappy with how some matters are being handled. He said the situation was evident in the disparity between the number of lawyers affiliated with the GBA and those who regularly attend its programmes or take part in its decision-making processes. Mr Dafeamekpor said some lawyers had over the years perceived the GBA as being partisan, a perception he said had persisted despite expectations that the association would move away from such concerns. “When we joined in our formative years, we were hoping that they would shed some of these perceptions or misperceptions or whatever it is,” he said. He argued that the association’s leadership had a responsibility to examine such concerns and make use of its existing internal mechanisms to address grievances raised by members. “If the people who get to positions of decision-making on behalf of the association continue to perpetuate that tradition, so to speak, then you advise yourself. Either you decide not to be an active member,” he said. Speaking in an interview with Channel One TV on Wednesday, October 7, Mr Dafeamekpor said the quiet withdrawal of some lawyers amounted to a form of protest against the GBA. “People revolt by being quiet. They are not fewer. They’ve taken a backstage. Check the number of lawyers who are members of the GBA, and check the number of lawyers who attend their programmes and participate in decision-making,” he said. He added that he and other lawyers had previously raised concerns about the GBA’s perceived political posture during meetings, including a longstanding perception that the association’s level of activism could vary depending on which political party was in power.

title: 66 years on, Nigeria must escape the fragility trap, by Olu Fasan
body: How fragile is Nigeria? That is one question Nigerian leaders don’t want to confront. Indeed, it irks them when anyone says that Nigeria is a fragile state. What’s more, some Nigerians, out of sheer romantic or sentimental patriotism hate it when the word “fragility” is used to describe Nigeria. It is unpatriotic, they reckon, for anyone to suggest that Nigeria is a fragile state. But this is not a subjective matter, rather it is an objective reality, based on rigorous assessment of key political, economic and social indicators. Nigeria may choose to be the judge and the jury in its own matter and declare itself strong and stable, the world simply does not see it that way, and the evidence points to a deeply fragile state. In their seminal report on state fragility, published in 2018, Professor Sir Paul Collier, from Oxford University, and Professor Sir Tim Besley, from the London School of Economics, provided a useful analytical framework for understanding state fragility. They came up with what they called the Six Symptoms of State Fragility. They are 1) the prevalence of organised non-state violence; 2) a government lacks legitimacy in the eyes of many citizens; 3) a state has a weak capacity for essential functions; 4) the environment for private investment is unattractive; 5) the economy is exposed to shocks with little resilience; and 6) deep divisions in the society. Anyone who examines these symptoms carefully would admit that they perfectly describe Nigeria. Think about it. Is there anyone who would say there is no prevalence of organised non-state violence in Nigeria when, according to media reports, there were at least 4,326 civilian deaths between January to March in this alone? Or can anyone say that the Nigerian government has the capacity to provide essential amenities for its citizens? Or is the environment attractive private investment when several long-term foreign investors are deserting Nigeria and the country is only attracting volatile portfolio investment? What about cohesion? Is Nigeria united? The truth, except for the self-deluded, is that Nigeria is a deeply fragile state. Indeed, international indexes show it. For instance, in the 2024 Fragile States Index, published by The Fund for Peace, Nigeria was ranked the 15th most fragile state out of 179 countries. Nigeria has also been ranked the 15th most fragile state in the 2026 Fragile States Index, published by the World Population Review. In both indexes, Nigeria is more fragile than other African countries except six: Democratic Republic of Congo, Central African Republic, Chad, Ethiopia, Mali and Libya. This is a deeply depressing picture for Nigeria, Africa’s third largest economy and its most populous and most endowed nation. Now, how could a country that is so blessed with abundant human and natural resources be the world 15th most fragile state? How could a country whose citizens provide global leadership, running major international organisations, be unable to govern itself well? How could a so-called “Giant of Africa” be more fragile than most African countries? But what happened? Well, while some see Nigeria’s problems as economic in nature, I see them as political and institutional, because Nigeria’s economic and social challenges have their roots in the failure of politics and political institutions. One of the greatest insights came from the famous book Why Nations Fail, written by Daron Acemoglu and James Robinson, both economics Nobel laureates. In the book, the authors said: “While economic institutions are crucial for determining whether a country is poor or prosperous, it is politics and political institutions that determine what economic institutions a country has.” For instance, it is politics and the political process that produce leaders that Nigeria has had and thus their economic and social policies. If President Goodluck Jonathan had been re-elected in 2015, he would not have implemented the misguided economic policies and the divisive political and social policies that his successor, President Muhammadu Buhari, implemented. Similar, if President Bola Tinubu loses his re-election bid next year, his successor will almost likely reverse some of his economic policies. Furthermore, it is Nigeria’s political institution, or, if you like, its Constitution that allows someone to become president with only 36 per cent of the popular vote, gained by deploying the wedge issues of ethnicity and religion, and yet control 100 per cent political power under a “winner-takes-all” political process. What about the 64 per cent that did not vote for him? Such a perverse political system causes a government to lack legitimacy in the eyes of many citizens. Let’s face it, Nigeria’s deeply flawed political and governance structure is the root cause of its fragility, characterised by political instability, economic inequality, ethnic tensions, religious intolerance and social divisions. No country that faces those multiple challenges can be described as anything but fragile because such a country cannot achieve the unity and stability needed to transition from poverty to prosperity, from chaos to order, and from extractive political and economic systems to inclusive ones. Yet, Nigeria is too structurally fragile that it cannot achieve any meaningful progress unless it breaks free from its deeply flawed Constitution, governance structure and democratic practice. For instance, the Nigerian Constitution tells three lies. First, the Constitution starts with the declaration that “We the people … Do hereby make, enact and give to ourselves the following Constitution.” But the people of Nigeria did not enact the Constitution, the military did, and they did not, as with most constitutions, submit it to the people for popular ratification. Unfortunately, thanks to path-dependent institutional development, the civilian leaders have refused to give Nigerians a genuine people’s Constitution. Until Nigeria gets a people’s Constitution, the words “We the people” in the 1999 Constitution are oxymoron. Then, the Constitution describes Nigeria as a “Federal Republic”. But Nigeria is neither a true federal state nor a true republic. According to the Encyclopaedia Britanica, a true federal system must have three essential features: non-centralisation, local autonomy and elements that promote common nationality. But Nigeria has one of the most centralised political systems in the world, with a constitution that has an “Exclusive Legislative List” that reserves 67 items and “any matter incidental or supplementary to them” to the centre. Most constitutional lawyers say that no other federal constitution has such many items concentrated at the centre. Second, there is no genuine local autonomy in Nigeria, the kind that exists in genuine federal systems where the subnational units can pursue policies that are completely different from those of the centre. But even in the Concurrent Legislative List, which contains matters on which both federal and state governments can legislate, federal laws trump state laws in the event of a clash. That’s not true federalism; it’s a unitary system! What about the third characteristic: elements that promote common nationality. Tell me, how can the mismanagement of Nigeria’s diversity promote common nationality. President Buhari was accused of a Fulanisation agenda because he put his fellow Fulanis in virtually all critical security positions, completely excluding Igbos. Bola Tinubu ran for president on a Muslim-Muslim ticket, and, in power, he has been accused of a Yorubanisation agenda by putting his fellow Yorubas is virtually all economic, security and justice positions. It’s as if people from other ethnic groups are not smart enough to hold such pivotal roles. Now, let’s come to republicanism. Is Nigeria a true republic. Of course not. In his book The State We’re In, Will Hutton argues that, in a true republic, “political power and authority are firmly rooted in the people, with the state ruling for the people rather than over them”. But in Nigeria, power flows from the top down, not bottom up. Elections are frequently rigged, and governments never act as the agent of the people. Nigeria is not a true representative democracy because it does not have a social contract. What’s more, Nigeria’s president is one of the most powerful and yet most unaccountable in the world. He rules like an absolute monarch. Truth is, with such deeply flawed political and governance structure, Nigeria risks being trapped in fragility. Only root-and-branch restructuring can help it escape the fragility trap and unlock its potential. The post 66 years on, Nigeria must escape the fragility trap, by Olu Fasan appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: ‘Floating’ money: Did the Dutertes use manager’s checks to hide wealth off bank balances?
body: A mischievously simple theory put forward by the prosecution: Could you move tens of millions of pesos out of a bank account through manager’s checks before year-end, leave the checks unused, and make the account balance look smaller without actually letting go of your wealth? That is why P96 million in “floating” manager’s checks drew so much attention during the lengthy examination of Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) records involving Vice President Sara Duterte and her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, on Wednesday, October 7. BPI division head for central Metro Manila branches Marwin Galvez confirmed that two joint time deposits worth around P41 million and P55 million were later converted into manager’s checks. “A similar time deposit that became a manager’s check in the amount of P55 million was also running during the same years, simultaneously with this P41 million. It’s a total of P96 million,” private prosecutor James Bryan Ibrahim Alih said. Manager’s checks for ‘reverse window dressing’ A quick refresher on how manager’s checks (MCs) work. Once a manager’s check is issued, the amount is taken out of the customer’s deposit account and moved to the bank’s settlement account to ensure the check is funded. While that check remains outstanding, the money won’t be reflected in the customer’s bank balance anymore. If it goes unused, the purchaser may later return the unutilized check and get the money back. Alih called the money “floating,” and when asked by Senator-judge Panfilo Lacson if the prosection was trying to establish a “pattern aimed at proving concealment,” Alih said yes. Senator-judge Tito Sotto even had a more colorful name for the financial sleight of hand. Citing a banker friend, he said the supposed scheme was called “ tinikling ” a Philippine folk dance where a dancer goes in and out of moving bamboo poles, although the BPI division head himself said he had never heard the term used in banking. Play Video But is it actually normal for wealthy clients to buy large manager’s checks and then leave them unused? Reverse window dressing? Rappler asked a senior executive in the wealth management sector about the practice generally. The executive said clients have different reasons for getting manager’s checks, but “usually it’s deposited or paid immediately.” Rappler has also asked a high-ranking Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas official about safeguards for manager’s checks that remain outstanding for long periods. The official said they were willing to comment, but Rappler had not received a response as of writing. Must Read LIST: Duterte-Carpio bank accounts, balances detailed in impeachment trial Global tax policy expert Mon Abrea was even clearer. “No, it is not common practice. Manager’s checks are generally issued for specific payments, not to temporarily park funds,” he told Rappler. From an accounting perspective, if an outstanding check has not actually paid anyone and the purchaser still retains ownership or a recoverable claim, Abrea said the amount remains an asset even though the deposit account has already been debited. “Repeatedly issuing and cancelling manager’s checks around year-end could therefore raise red flags of reverse window dressing, making bank balances appear smaller without actually reducing wealth,” he said. If a manager’s check paid a loan, it should reflect in the reduced amount of liability. If it bought an investment, the asset changes form. So what happens if a manager’s check remains unencashed? “Substance over form – it is still cash to be added back to bank balance so sa (in the) total cash, it should still be there,” he told Rappler. All this goes back to the discussion of the Vice President’s Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN). Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said he checked Sara Duterte’s 2010 and 2011 SALNs – back when she was still vice mayor and then mayor of Davao City – and could not find the P96 million in joint time deposits reflected there. Play Video The defense, however, stressed that the documents presented in court carried Rodrigo Duterte’s signature, not Sara’s. Her lawyer Michael Poa said the Vice President did not recall the account, while BPI testimony showed her father could transact on the joint account without her participation. (READ: Is Sara Duterte unaware of BPI accounts with father Rodrigo? ) This was actually not the first time manager’s checks came up in the BPI money trail. Several MCs also appeared in records tied to a separate controversy involving BPI’s request for the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) to delete 13 transaction reports after what the bank called a “system bug” inflated transaction records involving Sara Duterte’s husband, Manases Carpio. The inaccurate amounts triggered covered transaction reports. – Rappler.com Must Read Why BPI asked AMLC to delete P2-B worth of transactions from Duterte-Carpio records

title: Finns Party pulls ahead of NCP in new Yle poll
body:
The last time the Finns Party was more popular than the NCP was at the beginning of this decade, when both were in opposition.
Parts of the article content might not be accessible, for example, with a screen reader.
The opposition Social Democrats retained their healthy lead ahead of the pack in Yle's latest party support poll, but the Finns Party leapfrogged Prime Minister Petteri Orpo 's NCP in the standings, taking second place.
However, the difference in support between the National Coalition Party and Finns Party is negligible and well within the margin of error.
"It was not surprising that support for the biggest governmental party declined. The government's saving measures are now fully showing at this stage of the mandate," said Tuomo Turja , research chief at polling firm Taloustutkimus.
The ruling NCP has not received such low support in Yle's survey since the end of 2020.
"The party isn't managing to keep its old voters. Voters are particularly drifting to the Finns Party. A fairly large proportion do not know who they should vote for," Turja explained.
The last time the Finns Party was more popular than the NCP was at the beginning of this decade, when both were sitting in the opposition benches.
The survey also suggests that the NCP's problem with drawing support from women is becoming increasingly serious. If only women's votes were counted, the NCP would no longer be a major party, but would fall into the middle tier. Based on the background data for the poll, the National Coalition's support among women is 12.1 percent.
"This time too, support for the National Coalition Party has decreased, especially among women," Turja noted.
He added that the SDP's position is still good, but it has lost some support to the Left Alliance in particular.
The Left Alliance reached its highest level in the survey's history last month, as it has gained visibility by distinguishing itself as the only party to opt out of the cross-party 'debt brake', while other parties agreed.
The debt brake , also known as a balanced budget amendment, is a fiscal rule that aims to keep government expenditure in line with revenue — limiting the need to borrow and keeping state debt from spiralling out of control.
According to Turja, the party is gaining new supporters from within the red-green bloc — former supporters of the SDP and the Greens.
While the National Coalition Party is having problems with a loss of female supporters, the Social Democratic Party is clearly the most popular party among women, with just over 27 percent support. The Left Alliance holds second place among women with just over 16 percent.
The opposition Centre Party ranked third in an Yle poll last spring, and at their best were four percentage points ahead of the Finns Party, but in recent months the Centre's support seems to have stagnated to around 13 percent, clearly behind the Finns Party.
The Centre has been pressuring the government, including the Finns Party, about high fuel prices, but considering the survey results, that does not seem to have increased their support.
Taloustutkimus interviewed 2,807 people. 2,089 people (74.4%) stated their party affiliation. Interviewees were asked which party candidate they would vote for if the parliamentary elections were held now. The interviews were conducted as computer-assisted telephone interviews and in an online panel from 7 September to 5 October 2026. Respondents were adult Finns in mainland Finland. The margin of error was a maximum 1.8 percentage points in either direction.

title: GLS focused on members’ welfare, not rivalry with GBA — Dafeamekpor
body: The Ghana Law Society (GLS) says its emergence is intended to provide an additional platform for lawyers, particularly in addressing members’ welfare, rather than to compete with the Ghana Bar Association (GBA). The society is developing a welfare package under which 20 per cent of members’ dues would be set aside to finance a life insurance policy. The initiative is part of what the GLS sees as a stronger focus on the professional and personal welfare needs of its members. The development comes as Majority Chief Whip Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor pursues a Supreme Court case challenging the legal basis of the GBA’s claim to exclusive representation on certain statutory bodies. He has stressed that the case does not seek to question the existence or relevance of the GBA, but rather the interpretation of constitutional provisions that specifically refer to the association. Mr Dafeamekpor has argued that references to the GBA in the 1992 Constitution should not be interpreted as giving the association exclusive representation, saying such provisions should also be read alongside the constitutional guarantee of freedom of association. Speaking in an interview with Channel One TV on Wednesday, October 7, Mr Dafeamekpor said the GLS was not positioning itself as a rival to the GBA, insisting that its priority was the welfare of its members. “We’re not in competition with the Ghana Bar Association. I’m saying that as a law society, our focus has been on the welfare of our members, which the GBA doesn’t do,” he said. He also called for tolerance of differing political views among lawyers, saying the GLS would not adopt an anti-NPP posture simply because some of its members belong to the party. “We are lawyers. We should be tolerant of opposing views. That’s our training,” he said. The Ghana Law Society was inaugurated on September 30, 2026, during its maiden bar conference.

title: 2027 election cases: Your conduct will be monitored, CJN warns tribunal judges
body: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA—Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, yesterday warned that judges appointed to election tribunals would be closely monitored. Speaking during the flag-off ceremony of the 2026/2027 legal year of the National Industrial Court of Nigeria, NICN, the CJN, who noted that some judges of the court could be called upon to serve as members of election petition tribunals, said the nature of such an assignment demanded a great degree of impartiality and restraint. She equally implored lawyers to avoid duplicating court actions, which could lead to conflicting judgments capable of not only damaging public confidence but also exposing the judiciary to disrepute. The CJN maintained that the court must remain intellectually prepared to meet modern-day challenges, while ensuring that its decisions remained firmly anchored in the Constitution, applicable legislation, binding precedent and established principles of judicial reasoning. She said: “As we approach another electoral season, these responsibilities assume even greater importance. “Some of Your Lordships may, in accordance with the applicable constitutional and legal framework, be called upon to serve as members of Election Petition Tribunals. “In that capacity, Your Lordships will be called upon to decide politically sensitive disputes which attract considerable public attention. “The nature of such assignments therefore demands an even greater degree of impartiality, restraint and detachment. “Whether sitting in this Court or performing a Tribunal assignment, you must remain conscious that your conduct will be closely scrutinized. “You must ensure that nothing in your associations, public engagements or other conduct creates a reasonable perception of political alignment or predisposition. “The Bar must never become an instrument through which the judicial process is manipulated for partisan or strategic purposes. “The proper forum is determined by law, not by the perceived likelihood of success before a particular Judge or court. “There is also a need for restraint in public commentary. The right to criticise a judgment or judicial process does not extend to personal attacks on Judges, deliberate misrepresentation of proceedings or attempts to bring pressure to bear on the Court through public opinion. “Where there are genuine concerns about judicial conduct, the appropriate institutional channels remain available and should be used,” the CJN added. She also cautioned lawyers on the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), noting that although it could be a handy research tool, it should not, however, displace their professional responsibility. “An AI system may produce an answer that appears authoritative, complete with names of parties, citations, quotations and even a seemingly convincing account of the decision. “That does not make the authority genuine. A non-existent case, an incorrectly stated decision or a quotation attributed to a judgment in which it does not appear has no place in a court process “For counsel, the consequences can be serious,” the CJN warned. In his address, the President of the NICN, Justice Benedict Kanyip, disclosed that the court was inundated with cases in the past legal year. According to him, over the past twelve months, a total of 2,236 cases were disposed of across the Judicial Divisions of the court, significantly cutting down its historical backlog. “Despite the pressure occasioned by this, my colleagues, in their characteristic manner, demonstrated unwavering commitment to duty and concluded significant numbers of these cases. “I am pleased to report that through the dedication of our judges, we achieved a significant increase in case disposal rates compared to previous years.” However, he decried the poor utilisation of the court’s Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Centre by litigants and their counsel. He noted that only 31 cases were referred to the ADR Centre across the various Judicial Divisions of the court in the last year. “We must note that ADR is a valid and special component of, especially, labour justice delivery. Judicial efficiency cannot rely on litigation alone. “Despite our efforts to promote ADR in the Court, we have not received any reciprocity in that regard from litigants and their counsel,” the NICN President stated. While the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, pledged the continued support of the Federal Government to the court, the President of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Mrs. Oyinkansola Badejo-Okusanya, SAN, stressed that Nigerian labour jurisprudence must remain dynamic but firmly rooted in the rule of law. Dignitaries at the legal year ceremony, which was preceded by the official commissioning of the court’s headquarters building, included former CJNs, Justices Mahmud Mohammed and Walter Onnoghen; the President of the Court of Appeal, Justice Monica Dongbam-Mensen; and several Senior Advocates of Nigeria and lawyers. The post 2027 election cases: Your conduct will be monitored, CJN warns tribunal judges appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: More than 34,000 civilians, including 436 children, remain in Sumy region's mandatory evacuation zone
body:
Oleh Hryhorov, head of the Sumy Regional Military Administration, reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
"I understand how difficult it is to leave your home, your farm, and everything you’ve built over the years. But today, life is what matters most. We ask families with children, the elderly, and those who have difficulty leaving on their own to reach out for help.
If necessary, we will help you leave, transport your essential belongings, and find a place to stay," he said.
According to Hryhorov, since the beginning of the year, 121 people have been killed as a result of Russian attacks in communities in the Sumy region where evacuations have been ordered.
According to him, the enemy has claimed the most civilian lives in the border communities of the Shostka and Sumy districts: the Seredyno-Buda, Krasnopilia, Velykopysariv, Mykolaivska Rural, Bilopilia, and Hlukhiv communities.
Hryhorov also reported that the body of a person who had died the previous day as a result of a Russian strike was evacuated from the Sveska community in the Shostka district.
“The settlements closest to the border are the areas with the highest risk to life. Unfortunately, people are still there. In some settlements, the security situation is so dire that even the evacuation of the deceased poses a risk to police officers, rescue workers, military personnel, and other emergency services who enter the area,” Hryhorov added.
Earlier, Ukrinform reported that yesterday evening in the Kovpakivskyi district of the city, a Russian drone attacked people near a shopping center—there were fatalities and injuries.

title: At least 32 killed in Ukraine, Zelenskyy condemns one of Russia’s most ‘vile strikes’
body: KYIV, Ukraine – Russia pounded Ukraine with waves of missiles and drones in one of its most “vile strikes” on Wednesday, October 7, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, killing at least 32 people, including children, and damaging industrial facilities and energy infrastructure. The heaviest losses were in Pryluky in Ukraine’s northern Chernihiv region, where a Russian missile destroyed a five-story residential building. Ukraine’s emergency service said on Telegram that the death toll in Pryluky has risen to 22 as of Thursday morning and two more bodies were discovered following a Russian air strike on an apartment building in the capital Kyiv, taking the toll there to four dead. Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi has earlier put the country-wide death toll at 28, including 20 people who died in the Pryluky attack, including five children. On Wednesday evening, prosecutors in Kyiv said falling debris from a drone killed two people in a suburb. Zelenskyy said that 100 people had been injured throughout the country. The President noted that the attacks coincided with Russian President Vladimir Putin ‘s birthday. “This is the kind of birthday present that Putin gave himself: the killing of children, the killing of people,” Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address. In earlier online comments, Zelenskyy said civilians had also been killed in the capital Kyiv and in the central cities of Oleksandria and Kremenchuk during the massive attack. In total, Russia fired 70 missiles at Ukraine overnight — many of them high-velocity ballistic munitions — and dozens of Shahed attack drones, he said. “The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively. This was one of the most vile strikes.” In Pryluky, an excavator and dozens of rescuers with shovels sifted through rubble at the site where several sections of the apartment block had collapsed. Emergency workers used ladders to get to the upper floors of what remained of the building, and brought out 15 survivors as they worked their way down through the rubble. Around 55 people were wounded in the town, regional officials said. “There’s a lot of destruction, especially in the town center,” said Danylo Savenko, deputy mayor of Pryluky, who said he had run to an air raid shelter with his wife as soon as he heard the missiles flying. Big jump in reported drone interceptions Russia’s defense ministry said its forces had carried out a “massive strike” on military-industrial facilities in Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions, using high-precision land-, sea- and air-launched weapons, as well as drones. Ukraine’s air force said it had downed just over 80% of the 46 jet-powered drones launched by Russia — an increase from recent weeks when air defenses took down 50% to 60%. Since the summer, Russia has used increasing numbers of the new high-velocity drones in round-the-clock attacks on Kyiv and other cities, with Ukraine’s air defenses struggling to cope. The air force did not explain the jump in the interception rate and did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Zelenskyy said the Russian ballistic missiles remained the major challenge for Ukraine, adding that he and his team were “every day looking for Patriot (missile interception) systems that can and must protect people’s lives.” Ukraine received a new €1.2 billion ($1.34 billion) tranche from the European Union on Wednesday and will channel the funds towards defense needs, Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said. The US-made Patriot system is the only weapon in Ukraine’s arsenal capable of stopping high-velocity ballistic missiles. Global supplies have been drained by the Iran war and the Ukraine conflict. Russia’s defense ministry said its targets included sites where Ukrainian defense company Fire Point manufactures and stores its Flamingo cruise missiles and medium- and long-range drones in Kyiv as well as regions of Kyiv, Chernihiv, Kirovohrad, Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava and Kharkiv. Last week Zelenskyy said Ukraine had fired its first domestically made ballistic missile in combat, produced by Fire Point. In an interview with Reuters, he said he expected the company to have a longer-range FP-9 missile ready by the autumn. Fire Point has said that weapon will be able to reach Moscow. People shelter overnight in Kyiv metro Zelenskyy said Ukrainian troops hit four targets in Russia over the past 24 hours, including two Russian oil facilities and a training ground in the Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions. In the Reuters interview, Zelenskyy said Ukraine would hit Russia’s energy assets in response to Moscow’s escalating strikes on civilian infrastructure. Ukrainian officials and military intelligence shared warnings of the upcoming attacks on Wednesday, and many Kyiv residents took shelter in the city’s underground metro stations. Several loud explosions reverberated through the capital during the night. In the part of Ukraine’s southern Kherson region under Russian control, the regional Russia-installed governor said a Ukrainian drone killed two civilians in a car. And Russia-installed officials in Moscow-held parts of eastern Donetsk Region said three people died in Ukrainian attacks. – Rappler.com ($1 = 0.8947 euros)

title: Killings: Drop your ambition now, northern Islamic clerics tell Tinubu
body: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—No fewer than 1,000 northern Islamic clerics have told President Bola Tinubu to drop his 2027 re-election ambition, citing killings, kidnappings and acts of terrorism across the country, particularly in the North-West. The demand was contained in a communiqué issued at the end of a national conference on “An Assessment of the State of the Nation under President Tinubu and the 2027 General Elections,” held in Kano State on Sunday. The conference was organised by the clerics under the umbrella of “Ko Da Naka”, an organisation which says it is dedicated to “the Struggle to Promote Good Governance and Community Development”, in collaboration with AFAQ Educational Foundation. Some of the clerics who presented papers at the conference included Dr Abdulmuɗɗalib Ahmad Giɗaɗo, Prof. Muhd Muslim Ibrahim, Sheikh Kabir Bashir Abdulhamid, Dr Aminu Isma’il Sagagi, Dr Najibullah Abdallah Nuhu and Sheikh Abdurrazaq Uba Musa. Others were Sheikh Musa Muhd Ɗan Kwano, Barr. El-Zubair, Dr Yahuza Getso, Prof. Ibrahim Siraj Adhama, Dr Umar Dokaji and Sheikh Muhd Sani Khamis (Abu Haisam). “Alternatively, the President should refrain from contesting the 2027 election. If he refuses to do so, it is incumbent upon citizens to reject his candidacy and allow those whom they believe can provide better leadership,” the communiqué said. The communiqué noted that following lectures and extensive deliberations on security, the economy, migration of skilled professionals from the country, the role of religious scholars in standing for truth and the 2027 general elections, the approximately 1,000 participants at the conference reached the conclusion. The clerics called on the government to take urgent action to address insecurity in the North-West and other affected parts of the country. They said if the administration failed to do so, citizens should reject Tinubu’s candidacy and give an opportunity to leaders they believe can provide better leadership. They also faulted the government’s economic policies, which they said had deepened the hardship of ordinary Nigerians. The policies they named included the removal of the fuel subsidy, changes to the naira exchange-rate system, increases in electricity tariffs and tax reforms. “It is unfortunate that the government has continued to insist on pursuing these policies, which are increasing hardship among the people, rather than reviewing and correcting them. “The government prioritised the growth of its revenue at a time when the rising cost of living and unemployment are threatening the lives and well-being of citizens,” they said. According to the clerics, participants at the conference “unanimously agreed that it would be inappropriate to re-elect this government in the forthcoming 2027 general elections if it does not change its harmful economic policies.” The clerics also expressed grave concern over the continuing departure of Nigerian doctors, teachers, engineers and other skilled professionals. They linked the exodus to unemployment, inadequate facilities, poor working conditions and the country’s difficult economic situation. They urged the government to improve salaries, working conditions and professional development, and create opportunities that would encourage skilled Nigerians abroad to return home. The clerics urged religious scholars to speak truth to power, defend justice and refuse to become political instruments. According to them, scholars should praise what is good and criticise what is wrong, regardless of the party, tribe or religion of the person in power. They asked Nigerians to put the country’s future above party, ethnic and regional interests, and assess candidates by their experience, integrity, competence and policies. “Nigerians should not be asked to endure another term of the same policies while families struggle to meet basic needs and the promised relief remains out of reach,” the communiqué said. title: Footage sheds light on Iranian attacks that drove US troops from Kuwait base - report
body: A group of US soldiers who remained at Kuwait's Camp Buehring after a prewar evacuation eventually left the installation amid repeated Iranian attacks and ammunition shortages, CBS News reported Wednesday.The network's investigation combines newly obtained footage of strikes and damage with accounts from personnel who served at the base during the opening stages of the war.Most of the approximately 7,000 troops stationed there had been moved before fighting began, sources told CBS.More than 100 stayed behind, with service members describing fears that they lacked the resources to manage an attack causing large numbers of casualties.“We had to abandon the base,” one source told CBS anonymously, citing military restrictions on speaking to the media.Soldiers moved to remote desert positionsAccording to CBS, the remaining troops took equipment with them in vehicles and departed at night for the Kuwaiti desert, where they established forward operating bases.Their departure followed attacks involving ballistic missiles and drones, as well as what three service members identified as Iranian F-5 aircraft. NBC News had reported the accounts of fighter jets in April.CBS also reported a critical shortage of .50-caliber ammunition at Camp Buehring. An Army logistics official working elsewhere in Kuwait corroborated concerns about ammunition supplies and other defensive resources.The footage provides a visual record of the attacks and their consequences for the installation. CBS said it checked the recordings' metadata and compared them with photographs of damage to establish their authenticity.CENTCOM declines comment on soldiers' accountsCENTCOM declined to comment to CBS. The Pentagon referred the network to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's March 4 explanation of the military's efforts to move personnel away from vulnerable locations.Hegseth said more than 90% of Americans previously stationed at US bases had been moved beyond the range of Iranian fire while the military built up its offensive forces.The soldiers interviewed by CBS nevertheless described continued risks after leaving Camp Buehring. Two were struck by lightning during desert sandstorms in late April, suffering burns and a ruptured eardrum, respectively, officials told the network.CBS reported that commanders had sought to relocate the troops before those incidents but had not completed the move in time. The personnel transferred to Camp Arifjan in May before receiving further assignments inside and outside the Middle East.No soldiers were killed by enemy fire at Camp Buehring or the desert positions, according to CBS, although several were injured.Damage and supply shortages across US basesCamp Buehring has supported US military deployments across the Middle East for more than two decades. The CBS investigation adds detail to earlier reporting about the vulnerability of American installations during the war.The Jerusalem Post reported in September that a Pentagon inspector general assessment documented damage to hundreds of buildings and structures at US bases across the region, including Kuwait.The assessment covered February 28 through June 30, estimated equipment losses at $3.7 billion and identified ammunition shortfalls and supply-chain bottlenecks.The Pentagon disputed those findings in a response to the Post, saying the inspector general lacked access to all relevant information and rejecting claims that US munitions were depleted.

title: Drone vessel firm Syos takes outside investment
body: SYOS Aerospace has raised institutional money for the first time after five years funding its growth entirely from customer contracts, the company stated . The round drew investment from NZVC, Outset Ventures, Altered Capital and strategic funds the company has not named. SYOS says the money will go on expanding its global footprint, its research and development work and its production capacity. The firm operates across the United Kingdom and New Zealand, develops autonomous vehicles in the air, land, sea and underwater domains, and runs all of them on a common autonomy software called AAIMS. It employs almost 200 people, with research and manufacturing at Fareham in Hampshire and in New Zealand, and a presence in Ukraine. Sam Vye, the founder and chief executive, said: “This capital will accelerate our next phase of growth: to expand our global footprint, invest further in our already very strong R&D capacity, and increase production capacity to meet growing customer demand.” The company says it has delivered more than 150 uncrewed surface vessels to allied nations, and that its growth to this point was funded through contracts rather than capital, including a £30 million agreement with the Ministry of Defence last year. Growing on customer money rather than investor money is unusual in a sector where most entrants burn through several rounds before delivering anything, and it is the detail that gives the announcement its interest. A firm that has already shipped 150 boats and holds an eight-figure departmental contract is raising from a different position than one selling a prototype. SYOS has also been working on autonomous rotary wing aircraft, and its heavy-lift helicopter cleared serial production earlier this year under work connected to Project NYX. The spread across domains, from drone boats to helicopters, is held together by the common autonomy stack. The post Drone vessel firm Syos takes outside investment first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Attacks on British mosques intensify in wave of 'sustained harassment'
body: Attacks on British mosques are becoming more severe, while reports of lower-level types of intimidation of Muslims has decreased, a report has found. There were 78 attacks and incidents against mosques in the UK and Channel Islands from the year ending in July 2026, amounting to an incident every five days, according to the campaign group British Muslim Trust. The research found a reduction in lower-level threats to mosques and buildings owned by Muslim organisations, such as the drawing of crosses, flags and hateful slogans on mosque walls, desecrating objects left outside mosques and property damage. But more severe incidents involving arson, weapons, threats to kill and violence have increased. This includes foiled plots for mass casualties, of which there were none the previous year. The report included “sustained harassment” and online campaigns in its assessment of more severe threats. The attacks took place across 64 mosques and buildings on their premises, with almost one fifth of those premises experiencing multiple attacks in the same year. The BMT, which was set up last year as the government’s watchdog for anti-Muslim hatred and threats, said the fluctuations showed “unchecked” low-level incidents had paved the way for more serious crimes. “This data tells an incredibly sombre story about the rise in anti-Muslim hostility that British Muslims are living with. Today, a mosque is vulnerable purely because it’s a mosque,” said the BMT’s chief executive Akeela Ahmed . “Security needs are increasing as a direct response to the severity of attacks that mosques are under. British Muslims are under attack due to the polarisation that is building and many Muslims are scared to go about their everyday lives.” The Home Office has allocated £40 million ($52.8 million) of funding to protect mosques and Muslim community organisations in the UK. The BMT had previously reported some mosques had experienced delays of up to 18 months in obtaining that official funding. The trust campaigns for a wider effort to tackle the underlying issues behind the security threats. “If we want to bring down the costs for protecting British Muslims in the UK, then we need to reduce the need for protection and address the root causes of hate against Muslim communities,” Ms Ahmed said. “The rise in hate that we are witnessing is showing no signs of slowing down and until it does we need to make mosques a safe place for Muslim communities.” There was an increase of attacks on mosques during Ramadan, with a man in Ayr, Scotland, repeated using a heavy object to hit a window in a room where women and children had gathered to break their fast. A man was charged with terrorism-related crimes after allegedly stabbing worshippers outside a mosque in Edinburgh . Last year, a mosque was set on fire in Peacehaven, East Sussex. Twelve people were arrested for plotting an “extreme right wing terrorism-related” attack directed at an Islamic event in Ipswich in July, according to Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) London. The report's authors faced questions over the inclusion of an attack on the former buildings of the East London Central Synagogue as one of the 78 attacks. The BMT said the attack followed an online hate campaign towards the local Somali community, members of which had announced their intention to buy the building and turn it into a mosque. The cause of the attack has not been identified, while two men were arrested on suspicion of involvement. “The community received a significant amount of online hate. When the arson attack happened, many local Muslim communities felt affected, alongside Jewish communities,” the BMT report said.

title: High-rise building in Istanbul partially collapses, trapping people under rubble — TV
body:
ISTANBUL, October 8. /TASS/. A six-story building partially collapsed in Istanbul, trapping people under the rubble, the TRT TV channel reported.
According to its information, the incident occurred Thursday morning in Istanbul Province's Maltepe district. For unknown reasons, two floors collapsed. Rescue teams and ambulances have been dispatched to the scene. No information on casualties or injuries has been reported yet, TRT pointed out.
The TV channel specified that the collapse occurred on the first two floors of the building, which house commercial stores. The stores were closed around 7 a.m. local time, and rescue workers are evacuating residents. According to TRT, a child was pulled alive from under the rubble and hospitalized.

title: Takoradi NPP members welcome new executives, call for unity and hard work
body: Members of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) in Takoradi have welcomed the outcome of the party’s National Delegates Conference held at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi on Saturday, October 3, 2026. They described it as a renewed opportunity to rebuild and recapture power in 2028. The members also called on the national leadership to strengthen party structures at the polling station and constituency levels, reconcile aggrieved members, and present a clear alternative message to Ghanaians ahead of the 2028 polls. Meanwhile, others stressed that the real work begins now. The delegates elected former General Secretary, John Boadu, as National Chairman with 2,888 votes, while Justin Frimpong Koduah was re-elected as General Secretary. Others elected were Henry Nana Boakye, Nana Akomea, and Kojo Fosu Boadu as Vice Chairpersons; Daniel Nii Kwartei Titus-Glover as National Organiser; and Alfred Kojo Thompson as National Treasurer. The NPP’s new executives have a four-year mandate and are expected to lead the party’s reorganisation and campaign as the main opposition party after losing power to the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in 2024. Speaking with the GNA in separate interviews in Takoradi, some party faithful said the elections were generally peaceful and reflected the will of the grassroots. Mr. Kwame Mensah, a polling station executive from Takoradi Constituency, congratulated Chairman John Boadu and all the newly elected national officers. According to him, what happened in Kumasi showed that the NPP believed in internal democracy. Madam Efua Aidoo, a women’s organiser in the Effia Constituency, said, “The election is over. What we need now is unity. Whether you supported Boadu, Boakye Agyarko or Paul Afoko, we are one NPP family.” Mr. Kojo Acquah, an NPP communicator, added, “Ghanaians are watching. If we want to win back power in 2028, the new executives must work hard, listen to the base, and address the concerns that cost us the 2024 elections. No more complacency.”

title: Imo Kidnap: Relief, jubilation as prospective corps members regain freedom
body: •Parents seek psychosocial support for victims By Adeola Badru and Chidi Nkwopara Parents of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, members abducted en route to their orientation camps in Imo State have expressed profound relief following news of their release, though their joy remains shadowed by anxiety as they await direct contact with their children. Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma and the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, confirmed the release yesterday afternoon during a telephone conversation between the monarch and the governor, as stated by Ladoja’s media aide, Adeola Oloko. The Olubadan, who had closely monitored developments concerning the abducted prospective corps members, also expressed relief following the confirmation of their release. However, family relations revealed that the released prospective corps members are currently in the custody of the Department of State Services, DSS, as of press time, leaving parents unable to speak with or verify the physical condition of their children. Parents speak One of the affected parents and spokesperson for the families, Alimot Akande, confirmed the release in an interview with Vanguard yesterday, saying the development had brought considerable relief to families who had spent days in anguish over the fate of their children. Akande, who has been at the forefront of efforts by the affected families to secure the release of the prospective corps members, said the parents were grateful that their children had regained their freedom, but stressed that the ordeal had taken a heavy emotional and financial toll on the families. She said, “We are happy that they have been released. This is what every parent has been waiting and praying for. For days, we have been living in fear and uncertainty because we did not know what could happen to our children. “Now that we have heard that they have been released, we thank God for preserving their lives. But our joy is not yet complete because we have not been able to speak with them ourselves.“ “What we have heard is that they are still with the DSS. So, we are waiting for the authorities to allow us have contact with them and, most importantly, to reunite them with their families.” Akande, however, said the release did not come without a financial burden, explaining that the individual families had to make separate arrangements after the abductors communicated their ransom demands. “The release did not come for free. The individual parents were responsible for the release in their separate ways because the abductors had given their words on the amount of ransom involved. “Each family had to find a way of dealing with its own situation. We were all desperate to see our children come back alive, and that was the priority for every parent. “No government gave us anything to support the families towards the release of our children. We had to do what we could as individual families.“ “Everybody was looking for a way to bring their child back safely. It was not an easy thing for any of us, but we were prepared to do whatever was necessary within our means to ensure that our children returned alive,” she said. According to her, the families had endured sleepless nights and emotional distress throughout the period of the abduction, particularly because they were constantly uncertain about the condition of their children. “The psychological trauma has been enormous. Imagine having your child travelling to report for NYSC and then you suddenly hear that the vehicle they were travelling in had been attacked and the occupants abducted.“ “You cannot sleep properly. You cannot eat properly. You are constantly thinking about where your child is, and whether the child is still alive.“ “We have parents who have been under tremendous pressure. Some had to look for money to meet the demands made by the abductors. “Now that they have been released, our appeal is that the government and security agencies should ensure that these children are properly attended to. “They need medical attention, psychological support and every necessary assistance because they have gone through a traumatic experience. They should not simply be released and left to deal with the experience on their own. “These are young Nigerians who were simply going to serve their country. They should not be exposed to this kind of danger while travelling to their orientation camps. “We hope that the authorities will learn from what has happened and put measures in place to prevent a recurrence. The safety of prospective corps members should be taken seriously,” she said. One of the affected parents, Mr Femi Adewale, 53, a public servant and father of Feyisayo, one of the abducted prospective corps members, also expressed relief over the development. Adewale said, “We are very happy and relieved that our children have been released. It has been a very difficult period for us as parents because we did not know what would happen to them. “The most important thing for us now is to see our children, speak with them and know that they are safe. We thank God for preserving their lives.” Similarly, Mrs Sade Oyeyemi, whose only daughter, Kemisola, was among those abducted, said the confirmation of the release had brought immense relief to her family after days of intense anxiety. Oyeyemi said, “I am very happy that she has been released. As a mother, especially when the child involved is your only daughter, you cannot explain the kind of fear and pain you go through when you do not know where she is or what is happening to her. “We have been praying and hoping that they would be released alive. Now that we have heard that they have been released, we are grateful to God. We only want to see her, hear her voice and know that she is truly safe.” A 55-year-old mother, Janet Oladosu, another affected parent, also expressed gratitude over the development, saying the confirmation had brought relief after days of fear and sleepless nights. Oladosu said, “The news of their release is a great relief to us. We have been living in fear and praying for our children. Nobody wants to hear that their child has been abducted, especially when the child was simply travelling to begin the National Youth Service. “We thank God that they are alive and have been released. What we need now is for them to be brought back safely to their families.” Meanwhile, the rescued victims are currently receiving medical attention at a DSS facility, according to security sources, while efforts are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the abduction and apprehend any remaining suspects. Similarly, the NYSC Director-General, Brigadier General Olakunle Oluseye Nafiu, is presently at the DSS Clinic in Owerri addressing the rescued victims. The source said: “The NYSC-DG is in the company of the Imo State Commissioner of Police, Director DSS and Brigade Commander, 34 Artillery Brigade, Obinze, Imo State.” Uzodimma reacts Reacting, Governor Uzodimma applauded the security agencies for their quick intervention in securing the release of the 20 corps members kidnapped along the Onitsha-Owerri Road a few days ago. Uzodimma also expressed satisfaction with the collaborative efforts of both the Oyo and Imo State Governments towards the quick release of all 20 captives. He said he was particularly pleased with the security agencies for their sound collaboration and patriotism in ensuring that the corps members were rescued unharmed. Uzodimma said that “since the issue involved the security of lives, the government was cautious about releasing too much information to the public, hence the discreet manner in which it was handled.” While saying that he “is particularly grateful to the security agencies for the discreet and collaborative manner in which they tackled the challenge, the Governor equally praised the parents for “their patience during the trying period and urged Nigerians to always have faith in the Federal Government to overcome the current security challenges in the country. Police confirm rescue Confirming the rescue, the police in a statement signed by Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, said the victims were rescued following sustained search-and-rescue operations and have since been taken for medical assessment and necessary care. It reads, ‘”he Nigeria Police Force, in collaboration with sister security agencies, has rescued the 20 prospective NYSC corps members abducted in Imo State on 1st October 2026. “The victims were rescued on 7th October 2026 at Amakohia Ubi Village, Imo State, following sustained search-and-rescue operations. They have since been taken for medical assessment and necessary care. “Efforts are ongoing to apprehend those responsible for the abduction, as the Police and other security agencies sustain coordinated operations towards bringing all culpable persons to justice.” The post Imo Kidnap: Relief, jubilation as prospective corps members regain freedom appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Greek Coast Guard Rescues 40 Illegal Immigrants Off Crete
body: A Greek Coast Guard patrol vessel rescued around 40 migrants from a boat 18 nautical miles southeast of Kali Limenes, Crete. According to the Hellenic Coast Guard, a FRONTEX unmanned aerial vehicle first spotted the boat carrying the migrants. The patrol vessel then located the boat and brought the migrants safely to the port of Kali Limenes. Weather conditions in the area remained favourable.
